title: Eleven Madison Park
history:
Eleven Madison Park embodies an urbane sophistication serving Chef Daniel Humm's modern, sophisticated French cuisine that emphasizes purity, simplicity and seasonal flavors and ingredients.  Daniel's delicate and precise cooking style is experienced through a constantly evolving menu. The restaurant's dramatically high ceilings and magnificent art deco dining room offer guests lush views of historic Madison Square Park and the Flatiron building. In addition to the main dining room, guests may also enjoy wine, beer, and cocktails, as well as an extensive bar menu in the restaurant's bar and Flatiron Lounge.
In November 2008, Eleven Madison Park was designated Grand Chef Relais & Châteaux, joining the ranks of one of the world's most exclusive associations of hotels and gourmet restaurants. In 2009, Eleven Madison Park received a Four Star Review from The New York Times. The restaurant was also awarded one Michelin star.

reviews.review:
I honestly don't even know where to start...

I definitely felt under dressed...showed up in  sweatsuit  so maybe wear something nice, like a nice date out. The guy at the front said I'm fine as long as I'm comfortable, and I was totally comfortable but still felt a bit underdressed. 

Now the service is some of the best I've ever received. Well trained and super professional yet friendly. It's a beautiful thing. 

The food. It's really too much to describe. You have to experience it for yourself. And don't let the price deter you. Ball out lmao I mean, be financially responsible, but plan for it. It's well worth it. 

Literally everything tastes amazing, and that's what was disturbing. I really thought at least one dish would be bad or mid, but everything was delicious and unique and a whole culinary experience. 

To top it off, we were celebrating our honeymoon and got to do a tour of the kitchen! We experienced one last bite, which was a snowy experience that I'll never forget. This was such an amazing experience. I can't wait to come back during a different season to see what's on the menu!

Food, service, ambiance all stellar. A bit pricey but worth every penny. This was an experience- they even brought us into the kitchen after we ate for a tour. Highly recommend for a celebratory dinner.

I wasn't sure if the price point would be worth it and let me just say it was. Menu rotate seasonally and while I don't drink and you normally get alcohol at the end, they had a wonderful non alcoholic option. I would dare to say this is one of the best places I've ever eaten at this. Soba noodles were my fav and the take home gifts are cute and yummy

The food is unique, tasteful, and light yet robust flavor. The service is an 11 out of 10. And it's in one of the most beautiful settings. Take note of how all the staff move about the room. It's poetry in motion.

It was ranked the world's best restaurant a few years ago. It has converted to a vegan restaurant a few years ago. I was both excited and nervous to try it. It ended up being an exceptional experience. 

Since 2012, it has maintained three Michelin stars, a testament to its culinary excellence, which is an amazing accomplishment. You can see why once you visit it. Every detail was exquisitely planned and executed. The dishes were beautiful, surprising and delicious. Service was top notch, casual and comfortable but professional.

A fabulous meal at Eleven Madison Park; all the staff were friendly and attentive, every interaction was meticulous,  but never felt pretentious.

The food was amazing, each dish well presented, introduced and devoured.

This is definitely a once in a life time experience for most people but if you get the chance go for it. You will not be disappointed.

Okay, here it is...After spending the money we did, I would love to say we loved it, but that's not the case. The hospitality is wonderful. The food is good but the level of salt made it very difficult to enjoy it. We wish we knew ahead of time that the salt was the main ingredient we would have asked to hold it 1/2 way. We loved many dishes but could not enjoy them fully due to that. It mad us sad. We waited a long time to go due to $$$$. I wish I could go back and ask to hold the salt to actually enjoy it. Unfortunately, I will not be recommending.

This was a beautiful experience for a special occasion. Food was so good (yup, vegan! Go figure). Had with wine pairing, so amazing. Staff was very helpful. If reservations are gone on Resy, CALL! The person I spoke to was very helpful and we got a time slot on a Saturday night! When I have another big event, we will be coming here!

Let me start by saying I am a carnivore. It was only after I made the reservation that I found out that this restaurant serves plant based food. Spoiler - it is delicious. The service is superior, the sommelier nailed every bottle and the atmosphere was great. The evening was made even more special by the maitre d' who allowed us a behind the scenes peek at the kitchen. Thank you - we will be back!!!

Here's a polished version of your review:

Eleven Madison Park has been at the top of my bucket list for years, and dining here for my birthday was truly one of the best meals and experiences of my life. From the moment I arrived, the team made me feel incredibly special, even taking me on a tour of the kitchen towards the end of our dinner --an unforgettable highlight. I was lucky enough to see Chef Daniel in person, and my only regret is not getting up from my table to shake his hand and express my admiration.

Having read multiple books from those associated with the restaurant, I had high expectations, and they exceeded every single one. Seeing firsthand how the staff flawlessly executes the details that make this place so special was inspiring--especially as someone in the hospitality industry. Every element of the experience, from the service to the artistry of the dishes, was impeccable. Eleven Madison Park is more than a restaurant; it's a masterclass in hospitality and culinary excellence. I'm already dreaming of the next visit!

This place is beyond great! The service is impeccable and the staff very impressive. My partner is vegan and all of the dishes prepared were perfectly delicious. Prepared to perfection with stunning presentations. I would absolutely recommend this savorous dining experience to anyone.

The food was delicious. I was left with a bit of wanting a meaty bite, but many of the dishes flew close enough to the sun to satisfy that urge. The flavor profiles were all across the gamut. 

The service was exceptional; the staff is on top of anything you need. The ambiance was exactly what one would expect. Classy, quiet, and dimly lit.

it does live up to it's name, beautiful restaurant, beautiful atmosphere, feels classic luxury and the food is delicious.  worthy of the stars and the top lists simply because as a whole package this is pretty exquisite.  The food is delicate and out of this world.  an experience like no other this is definitely worth experienceing at least once.

Decided to celebrate my birthday here and it was exquisite.
The service was top notch and the food was in a different level, every bite was better than the last.
Is my second time here and the menu was completely different and that's something I appreciate. Can't wait to be back

Incredible food in an incredible elegant space with incredible service.

5 star food:  almost unbelievably good food.  This place has been famous for a long time for good reason.... The food is amazing

5 star service:  on a trip back to NYC, the service was still excellent as always.  It's like a smoothly choreographed ballet

5 star ambience:  located in the first floor street level of Credit Suisse First Boston, I used to come here for business meetings all the time.  The space is unbelievably elegant inside, with huge windows onto Madison Square Park.
The food was excellent, the service was exceptional, the experience was magical. We will definitely be back.
I fall in love in life every time I eat here. If you can, visit Eleven Madison Park. Enjoy the entire adventure.
All the food has a delicate balance between salt, acidity and flavor - all coming from the plants. Great service and creativity with the dishes!
Food was salty minimalist vegan. Croissant bread was very good. The rest of the meal was a disappointment.

We went to EMP  for our 35th anniversary.  Hard to believe.  
This was my 2nd time at EMP (the 1st was pre-vegan).  This was my wife's first time.   This time in the bar area - and I tend to favor this over the main restaurant for groups of less than 7 or 8.  We still had too many courses to remember all clearly in a 3 hour meal.

It is really difficult to find flaws.   It was a wonderful meal suitable for the occasion.  And I don't generally like meat. 

The service was as good as one ever sees.  This is possibly the best restaurant space in NYC - unless one wants a view.  

But, I can add a few very small quibbles.  

1). The wine list.  It is impressive, but not well balanced.  We have spent a great deal of time in Toulouse and have some affinity for regional wines - which tend to be good wines and great value.  They are almost totally missing from the list.  
 A shorter wine list with broader coverage may be preferable - unless EMP wants to build up to a large cellar (such as Bern's in Tampa). 

2). The grapes in the picture were good, but I have had significantly better ones.  At these prices, the grapes should be the best quality and these were not.

3). I don't like coconut oil as a base.  There was a bit too much of it for my taste.   

EMP is expensive, but the price is justified.

I am a vegan, and the food at Eleven Madison Park is fantastic.  The squash butter is the best I have ever tasted, and the bread is so good, I bought a loaf to take home.  Ice cream eaten by hand is a wonderful delicacy,  The service was extraordinary.  This restaurant, the servers' attention to detail, and the food is the best I have ever experienced, and I have eaten at hundreds of places.

I'm baffled by the hype EMP receives from restaurant goers.  While our evening got off to an excellent starts (the sticky rice first course, and the leek dishes were truly outstanding) it went quickly downhill from there.  We were served a stream of forgettable, and sometimes inedible (the bizarre fried mushroom dish that was somehow gooey and awful tasting) courses that were simply unpleasing to my palate. Why mask the taste of otherwise lovely vegetables to an extent that the underlying ingregient is hidden? The flavor profile, at least in its December 2024 iteration, is baffling at best with various on an Asian theme. The dessert was disappointing at best. The mochi ice cream sandwich was encased in a gummy wrapper. One nibble was all I could manage (and I can tell you that in my near 7 decades on this earth I have never found myself spitting out food  in a restaurant until now).  Probably the tastiest dish we were served was the handfull of grapes which were presented on a grape leaf. At least I left with a good taste in my mouth, with a simple fruit left untouched by the chef's overly heavy hands. 
I give the restaurant stars only for its ambiance and the attentive service.  

For a far superior fine dining experience I would recommend the exquisite vegetarian tasting menu at Le Bernadin.

Back in NY visiting (12/24) about 10 months after this amazing experience. The food was spectacular when I visited. I've shared that the Manhattan cart is one of the most remarkable experiences I've enjoyed in a restaurant since visiting France is 1995 and they wheeled out a 4 level cheese cart. Highly recommend visiting Eleven Madison.

Great food, attentive service, super knowledgeable and passionate sommelier (a young man- didn't catch his name, was able to share interesting information about the wine we were drinking), beautiful, historic art deco building lobby...

We have been here twice, once not long after it opened with the new vegan menu as well as recently for Thanksgiving 2024.

$365?? For plant food!?? Damn straight, and it's worth every nickel. This is the only Michelin 3-starred vegan restaurant in the world, and probably the only restaurant at this level that either my wife (she HATES fish) or I (vegan) can go to. Our experience here was perfect. The chef worked sheer magic with ordinary ingredients like mushrooms, squash, leeks, and even collard greens. The vegan ice cream sandwich and fudgy sesame "pretzel" were fantastic. Even the bread was amazing. The abundant staff functioned like a well-managed ballet troupe, and were incredibly nice too. One of our best meals ever, vegan or not, and we would come back again even at this price.

We went here for our one year wedding anniversary and it was nothing short of spectacular. We are both meat eaters but this is an incredible vegan menu. Their bread and butter is truly the star, I can't even imagine the butter had no dairy. We also got to tour the kitchen and have their take of a caramel apple.

We did the wine pairing but if you do not, try their yuzu cocktails! They're delicious.

Last but certainly not least I must commend the service. They are attentive, friendly, knowledgeable, and great overall. I will definitely be going back!
If i can eat these vegan dishes everyday, i will be gladly convert!  Service and ambiance are expected top notch for a three star Michelin restaurant.

Returned here after having come several years ago prior to its change to a vegan restaurant. We met the chef which was pretty cool, but if I'm being honest I much preferred the previous restaurant. I love what he's doing and think it is important but for the price, it's just not worth returning though fine to experience. My favorite thing was the onion "butter", but none of the other dishes really stood out to me.

We went here for our anniversary dinner, and unfortunately, the experience didn't live up to our expectations. The service was not very friendly, and the drinks were quite disappointing. We had to wait a long time between courses, and the food lacked flavor. The courses ware tasteless, almost like eating a bland book. The rice was overly salty, though the onions and avocado were okay. Overall, we were hoping for a more memorable meal. Super overpriced!!! Not worth it.

The meal is a pricey but so good. I find their whole story fascinating. It is cool to see how they have reimagined the restaurant and switched everything up. 

I don't eat plant-based on the day to day, but still absolutely enjoyed the meal. They are so creative with their dishes. It is fun to see the flavor combinations they create purely with plant-based ingredients. Highly recommended.

Eleven Madison Park is a restaurant I like very much. You can enjoy distinguished service here! You can also taste delicious food here! Although the price here is a bit expensive, it is worth it. If you have a date to fulfill with your lover, then I would recommend this place!

This is an amazing dining experience and lives up to the restaurant's mission of making fine dining friendly. If you're not aware, the food is all plant-based, so don't go expecting meat or animal products. That shouldn't prevent you from going. The food is delicious, fresh, and satisfying. The service is exactly what you should expect from a 3-Michelin Star restaurant. The dining room is clean and simple. The food is the star. Is it worth the cost? Definitely at least once!

My first Michelin weight restaurant experience.

We were in town visiting and planned our first and probably only Michelin rated restaurant experience at 11 Madison.

There's not a lot of Michelin restaurants that are fully vegan but there are a few. As a vegan, I decided to go here for my special experience to also celebrate 12 years with my partner.

we dined in September so it was the end of the summer seasonal menu. The theme was tomatoes.

The restaurant is fine. I wasn't really sure what to expect. Basic but exactly what it probably needs to look, clean, white, dark, and intimate.

Service is fine everybody's professional very well organized. Have answer questions walk to the bathroom do anything you need or ask of them.

We opted for the 11 courses for a full experience, which was basically $400 a person.


Some of the dishes that really impressed us were the tomato tart not only was it beautiful visually, but it was delicious. It is very fresh and creative.  

Another item that I would have loved to just take a loaf home was the brioche croissant bread loaf. It was so good. Maybe our favorite dish? if they had this to go, I would've bought a loaf to take home. 

Dessert was really good as well. It was perfect for summer very refreshing strawberries on ice with a cool airy cream to dip it in mochi plum tart was also a refreshing way to end the night. One thing we didn't take a photo of was our chocolate covered pretzels, which were delightful, crisp and tasty.

The reason for the three stars is because I was very disappointed with two of the dishes that seemed very basic for Michelin restaurant at several hundred dollars a person. That would be the tofu dish and the udon noodles. There was nothing unique about them. In fact I thought they were rather bland. We were off to such amazing wonderful creative dishes, and, confused by these dishes. I don't think I'm being too critical, if I would've known that was going to be our dishes, I would've opted for à la carte. It's not that they were horrendous, but they just weren't at a level of what I would've expected from Eleven Madison, therefore three stars.
Food, Service, the Vibe it's simply amazing, so clean and quiet you are able to have conversations without yelling

So disappointing, had been waiting to come here after reading unreasonable hospitality.. the food is beyond mediocre. With such amazing vegan options everywhere, what they offer for the price that they offer it is beyond disappointing. 
Our waitress also had the sniffles which isn't ideal when you are eating. She was great but definitely needed a day off to rest and feel better.

Had a delectable experience at the Bar. Glad to be able to walk in. Every dish was Delicius, Meticulously prepared & executed, along w/ the wine pairing. Sam at the Bar was great, the ambiance refined and welcoming, a place to really treat yourself...
We came here for our anniversary. We aren't vegetarian and were a bit unsure on what to expect. The service was very good and the food was amazing.

1000% worth all the hype and more. Truly a once in a lifetime experience. Not only are the dishes absolutely stunning, but some of them tasted like nothing I've had before (in the best way). A true adventure. My friend isn't vegan and she truly couldn't believe the ricotta filled pasta wasn't made with "actual" ricotta (it was made out of almonds). 
As expected, the service was incredible and our waiter was able to tell us every little detail about the dishes which truly enhanced the experience. 
I am only in NYC a few times a year and I cannot wait to go back one day as I know they regularly update their menu.

The creativity of the chef with plant based food is truly mind blowing. This is the best vegan food I've ever had in my life. Their Michelin stars are truly well earned. As the service was also the best I've experienced in a long time. The servers are so warm and attentive, there was always someone there to pull my chain when I got up or pick up anything that dropped on the floor. They even walk you to the bathroom! 
The dining area has high ceilings which creates a very large space feel while the service and food adds a dimension of warmth to the experience. 
I would highly recommend doing the tasting as well as the wine pairing. You won't regret it. :)

The food , service and ambience all deserve five stars. Was blown away by everything. The staff was the absolute star of the show. Without getting long winded I'm just going to say it's one of the finest dining experiences in NYC. I'm a vegan so I can appreciate it all but that really doesn't matter here. Will be back for all 4 seasonal menus going forward.

To be honest this was one of my favorite restaurants that I have been to, and for sure my favorite vegan dinner! I am not vegan and I was thoroughly impressed and satisfied. The taste of everything was absolutely wonderful. The service was impeccable. It was the perfect balance between fun and elegant so that everyone had a wonderful time. The decor is absolutely beautiful, also a wonderful balance between fancy/elegant without being stuffy. I can't wait to go back next time I am in New York!

EMP takes dining out to a whole new stratosphere. We were a party of seven on business in New York. We left with memories to last a lifetime. We are fortunate to enjoy Michelin Star restaurants around the world and this is the epitome of world class dining. The food and atmosphere were on point and truly exceptional. But the people are what made it so memorable. Chef/Proprietor Daniel Humm came out to greet us, the Master Sommelier Mark chose reasonably priced wines (we were on business trip :))  that paired beautifully with our courses. Our team which consisted of the Captain, servers and the people who greeted us at the door all- every single one of them created the very best experience for us. I am not sure on spelling but our Captain for the evening Alizay and her right hands Matt and Eli were professional & on point but approachable; attentive and fun but not intrusive. Yes, the tours of behind the scenes were amazing and fun, but the hospitality and food is what will bring me back time and time again. It was the perfect sweet spot in amazing hospitality. I am not sure I would be able to return to New York and not dine at Eleven Madison Park. Our team of seven will be forever grateful to have experienced this amazing evening together. Cheers to the people at Eleven Madison Park and thank you! See you next year.

There is once again a lot of hype behind ELM as Will G's book has become a best seller. It is easy to see the remnants of Will's hospitality culture but the service has also relaxed a bit. The vibe is relaxed and not the least bit stuffy with the service staff being every day people ready to engage you in any conversation you so choose. 

This is a traditional pairing experience with the dining time being 2.5 to 3 hours. I was greeted immediately upon arrival where they took my bag to hold for me and then escorted me to my table. It was a team style service experimente so I never had one dedicated server. 

I wasn't drinking so I asked them to take me on a tea flight, both hot and iced. It was masterfully managed as the barista paid me frequent visits and explained what and how she was serving my teas along with how they paired with each dish. 

The food is as advertised, quality in taste and brilliant art in creation. With the spacing and quantity you won't leave hungry. 

Favorite dishes were the tofu and the tempura eggplant. 

Looking forward to going back for their fall menu.

Jumped the shark on fine dining after our anniversary dinner experience here.  Dishes seemed to be more about concept and presentation than about flavors.  The sommelier's recommendation of a Monthelie with our meal was literally awful sour grapes.  The 4 hour dinner left me desperate to just get the check.  And even after 12+ courses, I was still starving and immediately stopped by Grays Papaya for a second dinner.  (FWIW went back in 2011 when EMP was ranked #1 on the World Top 50)

I had one of the most exceptional meals of my life. The staff was courteous, and the ambiance was delightful. I was even gifted some granola to take home, a thoughtful gesture. Looking forward to my next visit.

This is a review based on a 3 hour lunch. 
Despite being late, the staff graciously took us in and gave us an experience of a lifetime. Attentive without being pretentious, Eleven Madison Park offered numerous dishes that delivered in both presentation and flavor. Notable dishes include the tomato tart filled with a tomato purée and topped with a fresh tomato and Thai basil, the fried eggplant,  the zucchini prepared two ways, and the best rice and beans (fancy style) you've ever had. 

The place was quintessential New York with high ceilings and white tablecloths. Dress code is truly casual but I would recommend dressing up because it's a special occasion! We will be back.

"People can feel perfection," said by Walt Disney and referenced by Will Guidara in his book Unreasonable Hospitality.  

EMP is perfection. 

We've been here three times now, first in July 2022 for the full menu, and second in May 2023 for the bar menu, and third in August 2024 for the 5-course menu. We were impressed all three times and this is now one of our favorite Michelin-rated restaurants in the world. Each time we came back, the experience was just as good or better, versus at other restaurants our repeat experiences have gotten worse. 

The food is superb. Our minds were blown every time we were here, at how good EMP made their food with only vegan ingredients. We aren't vegan but we would eat vegan if things could be prepared like this all the time. There really is some great food science and innovation happening behind the scenes. 

The ambiance is awesome at well - the high ceilings in the art deco building is timeless and full of class without even trying, and it's not loud in the building because there is so much space. 

In terms of the experience, the service was consistently good every time. For that extra touch, the first two times we weren't really celebrating anything so there wasn't anything special done aside from a consistently great meal and service - totally fair, we can't expect "magic" every time. But the third time we were celebrating my wife's new job at her dream company, and everyone who came by our table made sure to congratulate her and we also received a short tour of the kitchen towards the end of our meal. LOVED the extra touch and a view of the very clean kitchen, including the "Make It Nice" plaque. 

Every time we're in NYC, we will make an effort to go to EMP. You have not tried fine dining until you've tried EMP - don't miss out!

Actually the best meal I've ever had. We obviously had very high expectations and had hesitations with the new plant based menu but wow we get it now! You are met right as you enter through the revolving doors who takes you to your seat. The service was top tier (probably the best I've experienced). They're there right when you need and take care of everything before you can even think of something.

Food was incredible! We got the full tasting menu (summer season) and everything was so flavorful and unique. I've tried plant based restaurants before and many have been underwhelming but this place was so good it probably is number one in my books.

The ambiance is great too. Very high ceilings and large windows. Whoever designed this place is master class. One thing I will note is that they utilize lots of natural lighting so it got quite dark - though actually found it intimate in a way.

If you're thinking about coming - definitely and highly recommend you do!

Dining at Eleven Madison Park was a true privilege--an unforgettable, once-in-a-lifetime experience!

Ambiance & Service: The interior is modern and slightly moody, with incredibly friendly and attentive service, as expected.

Food: Every dish was fresh and flavorful, with Chef Humm allowing the vegetables to shine. I left satisfied but not overly full. Highlights included the pineapple cocktail, the tomato courses (possibly the best tomato ever), fresh bread with sunflower butter, the rice and beans course, and the strawberries and cream dessert. The chocolate/sesame pretzel treat at the end was perfection! 

TL;DR: A remarkable dining experience with exceptional service and standout dishes. A must-visit if you have the chance!

Our family has eaten at fine dining restaurants all over the world - Noma, Central & Mil, Gaggan, French Laundry, Pujol, Alinea, among many others. I commend Eleven Madison Park for their commitment to a plant-based gastronomy. 

In general, I believe their back of house achieved a B+ or A- effort but their front of house failed miserably, beyond comprehension for what we are used for a restaurant with this general level of prestige and caliber. We waited over an hour in order to be served our first course, at least 45 minutes until our first drink. Eventually, we had to request that we receive our first course which arrived after 70 minutes. 

At many times, it felt like our servers didn't know what they were serving. We heard anecdotes including 'I'm not really sure what this is but it's a food-sciency version of butter' and 'these are some kind of strawberries...'. When my wife was in the restroom, they proceeded to plate one of the dishes, which proceeded to cool over the next several minutes until my wife returned (for those familiar with fine dining FOH etiquette, a faux-pas). At the end of the night, the gave us a faulty bill with numbers that did not add up. We had to request a new bill. 

While there were a few dishes that underlined my understanding of Eleven Madison Park's reputation, with excellent wine pairings, when you are paying top-dollar for the experience, it's more than just the food, it's the experience. And there were a few dishes that just seemed lackluster in my opinion - whole grains with peppers felt like I put whole grains in the microwave that didn't cook all the way and 'crunched'. The cooking innovation didn't compare to other experiences we've had in other plant-based or similar farm to table meals such as at Noma, Kadeau, Willows Inn (now closed).

The ambience was typical for a New York restaurant: loud, mildly energetic, dim lighting, and nothing overtly special. To revert to our primary complaint on FOH service - the team just seemed disinterested, inattentive, and unengaged compared to equivalent dining experiences. I think the dining philosophy at EMP is smart, but I'd give them a few years to iron out the kinks. Take your money to Atomix, Le Bernadin, Blue Hill or elsewhere, for now. Or alternatively, I hope EMP had a really bad, one-off, night.
Have been there twice (March 24 and August 24). The food was exceptional both times and the service was as well. It's very expensive but that's clear up front. The flavors are amazing.
Overpriced vegetarian restaurant.  Bad food & horrible taste.   Service is fine.  Not recommended
Amazing! Came here for my bday last week! Great service, delicious food, no animal cruelty  What an experience!
Worth every penny. Phenomenal service, absolutely delicious and unique food, large space. Amazing cocktails, Would highly recommend trying this place!

Best meal of my life. The food, wine, service and ambiance were exquisite in every respect.  

The service may have made the biggest impression - no detail is spared, the staff is knowledgeable, professional, and attentive, but always warm, sociable and authentic. Not too chic or uppity, but always appropriately proper. Every staff member we interacted with looked happy. This may best exhibition of quintessential American hospitality. 

We didn't do the wine pairing, but had a few glasses, all recommended by the som. Im sure the wine pairing would have been unreal, but I didn't even feel like we needed it. The som precisely understood my taste and made delicious recommendations. 

The food was on another level. Calling the menu imaginative doesn't do it justice. It feels like every dish was a version of fresh, seasonal fruits and vegetables elevated to a level I would have never believed possible. Each element was perfectly cooked and never over-seasoned, allowing the essence of the ingredients to shine through. The starting tomato tart and "tomato water", complete use of the sunflower (in butters and leaves and the roasted heart), and the cherry-smoked smoked zucchini and stuffed blossom were perfect examples. The food was hearty, refined and perfectly portioned.

Absolutely delicious and incredible experience. Good for dates, special occasions, or a place to take your parents.

Amazing experience. The service is incredible beyond compare. There is a team of skilled waiters, waitresses, and sommeliers that ensure every need is met. The interior is very spacious and bright with a comfortable ambiance. 
   The food was excellent. Our first course, the tomato tart was my favorite, but all the food was incredible. Everything is so fresh and masterfully prepared where each bite is crafted with so much flavor. It truly is like art in edible form. I will say, with the seven courses we left the restaurant all feeling sickly full, so you have to come in starving. Each course is larger than a typical tasting menu, and don't be fooled by plant based; it is still extremely filling. Clearly, this is a very expensive meal, but if you have the opportunity to dine at Eleven Madison Park, I do think the experience is once in a lifetime.

I used to frequent EMP in the early 2000s when it was more "accessible" and the menu (a la carte) seemed reasonably priced for special occasions. For some time now the menu is prix-fixe and vegan. 

I have no dietary preferences or restrictions; and I appreciate and respect all cuisines. My vegan friend suggested to celebrate our birthdays together here. As a foodie who likes to try new foods and enjoys cooking at home, I was wary on justifying the cost of dining here. But it was a special occasion with a very good friend so I went along. I was thoroughly impressed start to finish with each dish. The textures,  combinations, and flavors of ingredients were exceptional. Very creative and well-executed. It was a very positive and eye-opening experience. To learn about the creations using plant-based ingredients was mind-blowing to me. We were satisfied and grateful to celebrate here.

i thought it was just okay but people love it for some reason so i came here and got one of the fixed meals

the ambiance was great and they had pillows in the booth i was sitting in which was really nice. it was dark-ish in the restaurant but the food was still visible

some of the dishes were just let downs. they honestly slipped my memory but the cold soup they give you as one of the first dishes was kind of weird and dare i say unpleasant? 

my favorite thing was the cut peas. how in the world, i thought, would they be able to slice such tiny peas in halves? 

my other favorite thing was the chocolate covered pretzel dessert. not just how they tasted (a good mix of bitter, savory, and sweet as well as soft and crunchy).

my other other favorite thing was the breakfast they give you to go. the BEST granola i've ever had in my life (balanced mix of dried fruit and oats and nuts and rice and the exture of each very edible and gentle on the teeth while still being exciting) and a brilliant souvenir :)

What a gastronomical experience! 

I've dined here four times--spring, summer, fall, and winter--and each visit has been unforgettable. The service was impeccable, and the flavors in each dish stood out remarkably. I was also fortunate enough to walk through the kitchen, an experience I will never forget.

Amazing experience.  It is hard to evaluate a three Michelin star restaurant unless you constantly dine at multiple star restaurants, which is not me. So, this review will be from the perspective of a person who just wanted to see if the hype was lived up to: it was. 

I really could not find any flaws. The food was fantastic, the staff was polite and professional, and the ambiance was intimate and inviting.  We felt welcomed  right away and the front of house was sure to consistently check in.  The second my glass of wine was empty, it was filled (and if I was still on the paired course, it was filled with the same wine). We were also provided a second serving of our favorite dish simply because we said we liked it. 

Also, from a non-vegitarian perspective, I can tell you that I did not miss the meat, so anyone in the same boat should not be concerned. 

We took a cool photo of the table in front of us: strong After The Party FS II vibes.

We decided to visit the place after watching the documentary on Netflix "You are what you eat" - the selection of dishes is amazing, all of them are well paired with a variety of local and international wines. Overall great service and unique experience
O.m.g. This place is AMAZING!! I'm not vegan but HOLY this vegan food ...I LOVED! The service is top tier. We sat in the lounge/bar area and the ambiance was amazing. Would love to go again!

Food good and creative. Noise was unacceptable due to the restaurant's  choice of disco instrumental music. 
This is not relaxing. Dinner should be relaxing.
Choose "Chill jazz" instrumentals, or something similar, but not that obnoxious noisy loud invasive tension-inducing cacophany.

There are culinary experiences that you hear and read about and they make you so curious that you will put anything in motion just to experience it first hand. That is exactly how I felt about EMP and why I booked two tickets to take my mom to NYC to see for ourselves.

I opted for the 12 course lunch reservation. Serendipitously, Daniel Humm just released his new book and they had a small Christmas market just outside. I was able to snag a book and proceeded to say hello to the Chef who was graciously signing copies. We had a lovely conversation and meeting my favorite chef is now on video.

Walking into the restaurant you feel immediately like your known and old friends, as you are taken to your table. We had one of the best tables in my opinion as we were able to see the entire restaurant and be mesmerized by the flow and service of the staff. My mom even joked that she wanted to be sure she followed the format and walk the right direction as not to interrupt.

What stood out to me were obviously the flavors and the composition of each dish. To be able to think them up and the meticulous detail - awe inspiring.

Service was impeccable and when we were invited to a kitchen tour, it was the icing on the cake to see my moms expression as the whole lunch, touched her and reminded her of my grandfather who was a professional waiter in Budapest. He would have loved the art deco design of the restaurant along with the service and despite not being pescatarian like his granddaughter, he would have enjoyed the flavors.

Thank you to the entire staff and especially Chef Daniel for a truly unforgettable experience!! I can't wait to go back.

Ambiance - 4 stars

Food- 4.5 stars

Service- 5 Stars


Everything was superb and thought out and like most Michelin restaurants at this caliber, I did't have a lot of complaints. However, this review  might be moot as I was there back when they were still serving meat and everything that was buttery goodness!

11 courses of gastronomical plant perfection!  My mouth experienced flavors here that I have never tasted before and won't soon forget.  

Bravo for dropping meat without dropping those stars!

Beautiful place 
Stunning creative menu 
Polite and very qualified staff 
Price is very high and however interesting menu... I've had better

So, if you are already vegan, I would probably say that you would have more of an appreciation for the courses here since it is tailored for it. As I am not vegan, the food here wasn't bad, but it was either average or pretty good, with most being average. Adding to this the cost of the dinner here, it was not worth it. Outside of the courses where we had finger foods and dessert, which were my favorites, all the others were either too tangy, too salty, or too bitter.

The service and staff were all very friendly.

I really wanted to like this restaurant, especially bc I saw the Netflix documentary, and bc it costs so much. I am gluten free. They made accommodations for that, which was mainly gluten free bread instead of the regular. Most of the courses were already apparently gluten free. The drink they gave us first was okay and very high fiber and tangy taste. The second course was actually the best. It was finger food and it was the corn toastada and the lettuce/salad wrap. They brought out a few things that's taste was plain or tangy. Desert was pretty good. This was the bar fare which I enjoyed the experience of. The vibes were  laborious WASPy vibes, iykyk.

Eleven Madison Park (EMP) in NYC:

Exquisite, world-class fine dining with incredible service, precisely as would be expected. 

We had the tasting menu available in May '24, which is expertly crafted and 100% plant-based. 

Prepare yourself and your friends. This isn't just fine dining, it's the finest in the world of it's kind (well actually there is nothing else of this kind)

Each magical dish at EMP orchestrates a blend of aromatic indulgences, visually stunning presentations, and flavors that dance exquisitely on the palate." 

prepare for a harmonious engagement of taste, smell, and sight in this magnificent sensory experience.

enjoy

Eleven Madison Park is a vegan Michelin star restaurant in Flatiron. There is a huge dining room and side bar room with jazzy music playing in the background. For two people, Bar tasting is about $500. I enjoyed the tostada, udon noodle soup, and asparagus. I found several of the plates to be too salty. Also, not a fan of savory drinks as first course. I also went to their Bake It Nice pop up last weekend and waited 4 hours for 2 vegan pastries. The pastries were enjoyable but not worth the wait. I likely will not return but glad that I finally experienced dining here. At least the service was on point!
Wow front top to bottom!!!  Food amazing, service is a show in itself.  Never would have thought Vegan was this good and better than steaks.

I dragged my boyfriend here for the full course tasting menu after seeing it featured in the Netflix documentary "You Are What You Eat." I love vegetables, but I wasn't sure if it could be a 3 Michelin star meal.

Service was great for the most part, there were a ton of wait staff. Someone takes your coat at the door and they just remember who you are and return your stuff to you at the end of your meal. I did feel like sometimes they were a bit slow to refill our water glasses. Bathrooms were really dark but nice.

When discussing the food, I do want to firstly point out that at the very least, I left Eleven Madison Park with a very full stomach, which is the bare minimum requirement for a restaurant. Their bread and iconic almond butter was obviously very good, and presentation of everything was on point. The thing is, the dish that my boyfriend and I enjoyed was the mushrooms, which was the thing that most resembled meat. Dessert was very yummy though! Anywho, for me personally, this meal didn't blow me away so I probably won't be back and I probably wouldn't recommend it to my friends. I don't regret coming here though, because I probably would have always been curious if I would have liked it or not, so I'm glad I went just once to see what's up. It's really nice that they give a gift to each diner at the end, in my case it was granola. I regifted it to some colleagues and they said it was really good granola though lol!

Shame on 11 Madison Park. We had a bad time at your 3 star restaurant. In the last year my wife and I have eaten at 3 star restaurants Le Bernadin and Per Se. How we looked forward to our indulgence at 11 Madison Park--so much so we prepaid $700 a month in advance. 

We arrived at 6:15 and all went well. We were attentively served excellent food. Then sometime around 7:00 the time between courses expanded to the point that we were feeling overlooked ignored. The chef was taking bows in the restaurant and we wondered if his absence from the kitchen was slowing things down. 

Then we learned the restaurant was also taking care of a large private party. Now we understood the reason for the delays. 

At 8:15 with two more dishes to go and nobody sure when they would be ready, we left. One of the waitstaff apologized for the slow service. 

Conclusion: not worthy of its stars. Overpriced, underperformed . We left angry, upset and disappointed. 

Andrew Goldman

Not worth it. The service was excellent and the venue was very nice, but the food was just ok. The 1/2 cracker, bread and dessert were very good, but the soba noodles and peas with rice were just ok. I expected much more from a 3 Michelin star restaurant. In fact, for vegan food, I would clearly take Dirt Candy over this place. I now understand why 11 Madison was dropped from the Times top 100 NYC restaurant's list.

On Wednesday night, we gathered with friends and supporters for a special dinner at Eleven Madison Park benefiting Rethink Food.
My entire menu was vegetarian and pairing of wine  or cocktails. I ate delicious vegan dishes that I normally don't eat that tastes so delicious. I took some pictures below, all so delicious. Love the sherbet strawberry dessert happened to have paired it with the fruity wine. From a beets with quinoa looking like a sunflower. . To some sort of Romain with a huge cracker and green paste. 
What made it even a rewarding dish was the staff. From the time you come thru the doors. So welcoming and inviting. Helps you make great pairing drinks either every dish you have.

Innovative Cuisine: Eleven Madison Park is celebrated for its inventive and imaginative cuisine, which pushes the boundaries of traditional fine dining. Each dish is meticulously crafted with a focus on flavor, presentation, and technique.

Seasonal Ingredients: The restaurant emphasizes the use of seasonal and locally-sourced ingredients, ensuring that each dish reflects the flavors of the moment and supports sustainable farming practices.

Impeccable Service: Guests often praise the restaurant's attentive and knowledgeable staff who provide a seamless dining experience from start to finish. The service at Eleven Madison Park is known for its warmth, professionalism, and attention to detail.

Easily one of the most interesting experiences I've ever had at a restaurant. 

We dined at the bar which is more laid back than the main dining room. Every course was delicious with very unique, prominent flavors quite unlike anything I've ever had. 

Service was on point and staff went the extra mile to make sure everything was taken care of. No complaints at all. 

The only reason I'm not giving this place a full 5 stars is because I've read the complaints about some staff members not being compensated well enough considering what level of restaurant we are talking about here. The head chef/owner and whomever else is involved really need to work on that issue and not just try to sweep it under the rug.

We spent a total of more than $3000 for 4 people at this 3 Michelin Star restaurant. I felt so bad for my group for choosing this restaurant over the other amazing restaurants in Manhattan just cause it had 3 stars, now I have learned my lesson. Even for the menu to be fully vegan, I can't say that they perfected the Fine dining vegan experience. I was vegan for a while and had amazing vegan food when i lived in California so that is what I was comparing this too and I have to say I was extremely disappointed. 

1. Food: For being vegan, they have to makeup meatless dishes by creating complex flavors but most everything we had was bland. The dishes didn't seem "cooked" but rather ingredients sliced/mashed together if that makes sense. Our favorite dish was the last desert (which was great but 3 star great? idk). They served us a "truffle pizza" which was just overkill of truffles on crisps.

2. Service was the only reason I put 2 stars, they were attentive and kind, even though they could see that we were visibly disappointed with the food.

3. Ambiance was not really excitant, clean tables but no real "vibe" other than servers running around. 
 
All in all, I'm not entirely sure how one could rate this restaurant 5 stars, considering they are probably spending almost $1000 a person. Also, YOU WILL BE HERE FOR MORE THAN 3 HOURS!! Which is a long time, and more than likely leave still hungry.

Michelin 3 stars - what is to quibble?  EXCELLENT service and a memorable 4-hour, plant-based tasting menu. You will be amazed by  the offerings - no need to spoil it for you...

Damages for 4 with tip and 2 bottles of wine (both under $200 each) was about $2500.

Go, enjoy!

Note I was overdressed in a sport coat and no tie!

Dining at Eleven Madison Park is stepping into a culinary Broadway show, where the servers pirouette around your table with the grace of seasoned ballerinas and the precision of Swiss watches--case in point, a server gracefully rescuing my napkin before it barely kissed the floor, making me wonder if they're part-time mind readers. Taking my daughter here felt like gifting her a golden ticket to Willy Wonka's, but for the gastronomically adventurous. Nestled in the heart of New York City, with Madison Square Park as its verdant backdrop, this Art Deco gem has been wowing patrons since 1998, undergoing a magical transformation in 2017 that would put Cinderella's makeover to shame. Under the watchful eye of Chef Daniel Humm since 2011, the menu has evolved like a Pokémon, now boasting an all-plant-based lineup that could easily convert a carnivore with a single bite. Whether you're here for the full tasting menu experience or just popping by the bar to sample the culinary equivalent of a teaser trailer, Eleven Madison Park is where you come to feast like royalty without needing to pawn the family jewels. And yes, they serve cocktails and wine, because what's a royal feast without a little libation to toast your kingdom?

A fun and delicious experience on this visit to EMP. The service was impeccable, the food - despite early hesitations that it would be too "onions and leeks" - was delightful, filled with a rich palette of flavors without being too "in your face". Who would've thought that an alliums-based soup would feature among the top 3 of my favorite dishes of the evening?.. As someone who used to dispose in the most creative ways possible [aka whatever it takes] of the dishes featuring these ingredients as a child, and never quite favoring them since, I consider myself newly converted. And  getting a glimpse of the inner workings of the restaurant was a great way to finish off a great evening. Thank you for a memorable dinner, the EMP team.

When you go to Eleven Madison Park, you go with the highest expectations.  And despite everyone's high expectations to experience the best meal of their life, they still maintain nearly a perfect score on Yelp.  That really says all you need to know.

I think their adoption of vegan menu was brilliant.  I'm not vegan, but I enjoyed the meal immensely and I'm so impressed that instead of just doing what people expect they are adventuring boldly into new frontiers of culinary experimentation.  They are leading from the top, showing the world that vegan food can be excellent.  While I'm not personally vegan I know the planet needs us all to embrace more plants in our diet.  Another perfectly cooked steak from a top tier restaurant is fine, but go to Eleven Madison Park if you want to experience food at a level of excellence and innovation you won't find anywhere else.

I rarely find restaurants live up to the hype so high expectations can be a curse, Eleven Madison Park exceeds them.

This weekend was the first time I've been there since they went vegan. Overall the food was very good, the staff was friendly, but there were some inconsistencies. 

Some servers who would explain the dishes were not as thorough as other servers serving the same dish to nearby tables. 

The service started off very good but we felt like as we came to the end, the service fell off significantly to where we felt like we were forgotten about - the table next to us started after us but ended up finishing before us.

one of the best meals of my entire life.  just book it...lunch, dinner, at the bar, whatever you can get.  absolutely amazing.  

the service was also out of the world and they bent over backwards to accommodate my sister, who suffers from Celiac.  

I hope one day to return.

perfection!

What an maxing experience here! From the staff, to the attention to detail, to the descriptions of the food. I truly enjoyed my time here. My reservation was at 9:15 so I do have to admit, staff did get a little lax once we got closer to closing time but overall I truly enjoyed my time here. The chef's here are doing an awesome job of making plant based dining a delicious journey.

I made a reservation for Saturday lunch, and it was a 6 course meal for the bar tasting menu. We were stuffed by the end - they offer their bread (onion this time around with onion butter topped with garlic confit) repeatedly, I think partly to make sure you are full. We got two orders of those.

ONION: the food was so cozy, and a nice start to the meal with food that tasted familiar in some way.
Tea with Roasted Leeks and Brown Rice
Marinated Leek Salad
Rice with Onion and Thai Basil

SWEET POTATO: this was my favorite. A well contrived balance of sweet/savory as well as crunchy/soft textures. I could've eaten 6 of these.
Fried with Plantain and Sea Fennel

GAI LAN: there was some pasta wrapped around the vegetable, which added to the flavor. Not my favorite but still liked it.
Steamed with Black Truffle and Myoga

MAITAKE: My 2nd favorite. I haven't had too much seitan before but again the textures and flavors of this were nice, although more familiar with the dark soy sauce/sweeter taste.
With Pine, Seitan and Juniper

MANGO: the white one was my favorite, which was wrapped in white chocolate. The saffron was a bit too tart?
With Kulfi and Pistachio

SESAME: nice end to the meal with housemade vermouth. They even had a nonalcoholic version for my wife that was sweeter and grape-forward.
Pretzel with Chocolate 

Cocktails: I ordered the Sansho, which was strong and refreshing, but not as nuanced with other flavors as I expected. Tried a sip of the Squash which had more flavors to it I think and a sip of the Cashew which was very creamy.

My wife ordered a coffee and they kept refilling the cup, without any rush to get us off the table. Really quality service all throughout.

They also gave us Granola to take home, a bit on the sweeter side for my taste but I really like the texture.

Forgot to ask for a menu to print out but I asked through email so I knew what I got. All in all, a little under $300 a person with tax and tip. The most expensive meal I've had but worth the experience.

We came here after seeing it on Netflix's the "Twin Study". It's apparently one of the top restaurants in the world, I think maybe #3. It used to have an omnivorous menu however, the chef Daniel Humm decided to go all vegetarian. It's easily one of the best restaurants we have ever been to. If you're willing to shell out the money, go. 
We have eaten at some pretty nice restaurants here and there throughout the city and my husband said this was the best he ever had. This is high praise coming from him because everything else is just "alright". 
You can probably see each course in the pictures attached but it starts with a tea/consumme thingy and then moves into the solid foods and finally ends with a sorbet dessert thing. The best dish? The bread lol. Their rolls are completely vegan and their butter is made out of sunflowers and coconuts and the 2 together are a match made in vegan heaven. I think we had about 2 or 3 orders of the bread (they offer it to you so if you want more you can have more). It was that good. It's warm and flaky, almost like a croissant. The rest of the dishes were very good, flavorful and each had their own unique texture and flavor profile. For some reason, I found the sorbet at the end a bit strange, or maybe I was just really full. 
The interior is beautiful, service was great and ambiance was wonderful. Very quiet and the wait staff are very orderly. A wonderful restaurant that you should try at least once in your life.

This restaurant is an absolute disgrace. I have no words. They had plenty of reservations available and would not let us reschedule so they could keep our $700 payment. The staff is rude and unintelligent. NEVER MAKE A RESERVATION HERE. Run far away!

friday, march 1st special black truffle  dinner event approx $1,000/guest was a major disappointment.   having experienced the dinning room at least a dozen times and a private dinner  upstairs, the event friday evening was a major letdown.  it was akin to a quiet reception at a budget hotel minus carpet stains and scuffs on the wall.  the atmosphere and service screamed impersonal.   the up charge for the better wines was not worth the two sips of each pairing served.  the cocktail reception area had exactly four tables...not at all welcoming for the attendees lining the walls .   personally, we enjoy both white and black  truffles...even go hunting for white truffles in italy. sadly, the black truffles served friday did not "dance" on selections served. all truffles "dance."  it was a very expensive sterile event that made me wonder if dinner was being served by unenthusiastic off duty flight attendants.the personal connection  between the guest and serving staff in the main dining room was missing.  sorry, but i have loved every dining experience at eleven madison park until march 1st. what happened?????  still a  patron

TLDR: Disappointing for a 3 Michelin Star Restaurant

I want to start off by highlighting that the presentation, ambiance, and service were all impeccable. The tasting menu of 11 courses came out to $400+ per person. For this price tag I was expecting a way better flavor profile from each dish. Sadly, most of the dishes fell flat. The presentation and style were all there but at the end of the day, no savory dish made me feel like I have to return for this bite. The desserts however were standouts for me. I particularly enjoyed the Chocolate pretzels.
To die for! Whether vegan or vegetarian or any meat eater would appreciate this amazing restaurant! LOVE it! Will be back when in NYC..

What can I say that has not already been said. They care. It's delicious. Now Vegetarian and possibly eeven more delicious. It's also expensive, but you know that. Plan for $500 a head. But it's worth it
They served me the wrong food and gave me the wrong bill. I didn't receive the level of service that I anticipated.

author.name: Rick C.
author.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: BUYER BEWARE If you are thinking of going to this NYC restaurant, before you hit the Book button BEWARE.  I am someone who has been to this restaurant many times in the past.  Everyone needs to be aware of their present booking policy.  Once you hit Book you are immediately charged the full amount.  No Cancellations and No Refunds under any circumstances.  I was recently looking at a very expensive truffle and wine tasting, while trying to see what was available I accidentally hit book.  Seconds later I cancelled my reservations.  Resy sent me a confirmation of the cancellation.  Several weeks later, one day after the scheduled event, I received my credit card statement and I was still charged the full amount for the dinner.  I called the restaurant and even though they admitted seeing the cancellation they said there was nothing they could do.  I asked why they didn't call me after seeing the cancellation and knowing I would be charged, so I could attend or send someone in my place.  The only response I got was unless it was fraud there was nothing they could do.  They said that someone from accounting would call me.  That was seven days ago, I have not heard from anyone.  I go to expensive restaurants all over the world and no one has this type of cancellation policy.  I don't know how they get away with it.  But judging how easy it is to get a reservation on almost any day maybe they don't.  If you book here make sure to have no potential emergencies, make sure you don't get sick and make sure the weather will not be an issue because once you book there is no recourse or concern for you whatsoever.

Great food and drinks. Service was great as well along with ambiance. Went on a week night and it was cozy and relaxed. Vegan dishes were excellent and the granola after was amazing. Winter treats really. 4 stars because it was a bit out of the price range for what it was. Still nice experience.
The first Michelin three star restaurant I tasted in my life. The overall quality of the dishes is excellent and they are constantly moving forward on the road of innovation.
Lovely ambiance, best plant-based food around, incredible service. What's there not to like? Treat yourself and see just how scrumptious plant-based foods are!

We loved the idea of this restaurant. The service was wonderful. We had a wine pairing and that was spectacular The courses were a lot to be desired. The first course with onion soup was wonderful. The remaining courses consisted of sweet potato, broccoli, and cabbage....which was ok but not amazing and not on point with the price point. We kept wondering where the potato, rice, pesto, or truffle dishes were....so many options for a Vegan restaurant.  I enjoyed the bread and butter (vegan butter that was amazing) but we kept waiting to be blown away. As someone who has experience with Michelin restaurants, this one, unfortunately, did disappoint.
The service, the 5000 plus wine list & an amazing 6 course meal with pairing made for such a wonderful experience & something that we will never forget.

There are many things to enjoy about Eleven Madison Park. 

The service at Eleven Madison Park is exemplary. All of the staff seem well-equipped to answer just about any question you might have about the menu, including the beverages.

The food will take you on a food adventure that you've never imagined. For example, the onion prepared three ways really opened my eyes to ways that ingredients that I myself take for granted, like onions, can really become the tasty star of a dish. Specifically, the fragrant and homey smell of the onion broth is a food memory that I hope to hold onto for a long, long time.

In addition to tasting good, the presentation of the food was fun. This isn't a restaurant where I worried about using the wrong fork, for example. Several of the courses were meant to be eaten with your hands. Oh, the bread rolls with butter were delicious. Wish I could have taken a few of these to-go! The dessert course was fun to eat and I loved the selection of creative NA beverages.

If you're wondering what vegetables can do for you, visit Eleven Madison Park! The answer is...A LOT!

Here's a secret that will serve you well, wannabe-foodies: Michelin 3-star restaurants ain't shit. 

Credentials? I've eaten at Michelin-starred restaurants in NYC, SF, London, and Barcelona for over 15 years now as well as having been a frequent diner at the James Beard House when it was still running events there. In NYC alone I've dined at Per Se x2, Le Bernadin x2, Masa x1, and this review is for my 2nd time at Eleven Madison. The 1st time was before they went plant-based, and we enjoyed it.

See, the thing is - the 3-star restaurants have plateaued and are fine to coast, whereas the 2-star and 1-star ones are still hungry and striving for another star. Spend your money at those restaurants instead. It's harder to take a star away from a restaurant that already has them, than for restaurants to gain stars. I'd recommend Dirt Candy (1 star, vegan) or Blue Hill (2 stars, farm-to-table, plant-forward) instead.

This review is not really about the food, which was passable for this level. (We've had equal or better, often) And I'm happy to eat plant-based. My husband and I booked an early New Year's Eve dinner here earlier this month before another event we were supposed to attend that evening, and most of our meal was great.

The savory offerings were delicious - you can see from the menu I posted. I especially enjoyed the offerings with mushroom (either truffle or maitake) or tofu, as those ingredients really sang. The downfall really came when it was time for dessert, and the coat check service. 

The desserts were disjointed - they didn't meld together well. The Mango with Kulfi and Pistachio sounds like a natural combination with South Asian influences, but look at it. There was no thought put into the 4 spheres and 1 puddle of sauce. There was no finesse in its composition. How do you mess that up? And even worse was the Sesame Chocolate Pretzel. Though it looked delightful and intriguing, the flavor was off-putting. I'd rather have some chocolate halva instead.

But the worst part was the coat check service. Never in my life have I experienced such incompetent service from *any* establishment - even hole-in-the-wall clubs. You'd expect more from a Michelin 3-star restaurant. Basically, they LOST my husband's beloved scarf that he was gifted from the UK, and they wouldn't even let him go back and look for it - as if we were some riffraff that would steal from other customers or something??? As if they couldn't supervise us as we looked? Sorry, I thought Michelin was supposed to take SERVICE into account when issuing their ratings?

They must have let it fall into some other guest's bag or given it to someone else by accident, and sent my husband out into the cold without a scarf, and with only an email address to complain to for our troubles. For this alone, we will never return to Eleven Madison, especially when there are better and cheaper options in this city who actually still care about providing excellent food & hospitality.

We had a great evening at Eleven Madison Park. The service was excellent. The staff were friendly, informative, and attentive. The food was really interesting--beautifully plated and very delicious. Great flavor combinations that were fresh and interesting.

Unfortunately, about 6 hours after we left, my wife had the chills, was nauseous, threw up, and had diarrhea. After 8-10 hours of that, she was feeling better. Not sure what she had, but something at dinner was not right.

Exquisite experience, like being immersed into a Monet painting. Delicate, vibrant, delightful surprises at every turn.  Amazing service, watching the processes, like a performance, is magical.  My partner is a big meat eater and said not only did he not miss the meat, but the plant-based aspect enhanced the entire experience.  I agree.  What they've created is truly amazing.  Highly recommend. Will be back.

Awesome place , fabulous food ; healthy and obviously super vegan , actúale I learn more then  the real food, you change your mind when try something from the menu, everyone is nice people ; is a wornderfully place

Wow. This restaurant was absolutely amazing!!!!! 

From the moment you walk in, you feel welcome like you came into your friend's home. 

We sat in the bar and had a lovely server, Alize, who was wonderful in describing the dishes to us. Later in the evening, she had Isabell the Maiître D' come to our table and we were invited to have a tour of the kitchen! We were absolutely thrilled with this and we were amazed at the cleanliness and professionalism we witnessed.  

Every single dish we tried was so delicious! I think my favorite was the carrot tartare. I love how they send you home with breakfast for the next day which is an amazing granola mix. 

We will definitely come back here every single time we are in NYC.

Of course the food, service and ambiance were all incredible. My only suggestion for improvement is that almost all of the dishes in the full tasting menu are dominated by Asian-inspired flavors. This makes sense since many Asian dishes are naturally vegan / vegetable based and have been for centuries. But being Asian myself, a lot of the dishes (albeit refined) tasted like things I could have made at home. It was very soulful Asian-inspired flavors. Unfortunately to me this is not creative enough for the price point. I was hoping for more innovative dishes. The highlights of the tasting menu were: bread and squash "butter" (soooo amazing!), carrot tartare, the creative ball-shaped desserts, the chocolate, and the house-made vermouth at the end. These creations were so imaginative, delicious and beyond impressive.

DO NOT TRUST THEIR COAT CHECK.

Went here for NYE. Savory courses were fine. Desserts quite bad (I had chocolate covered tahini 'pretzel' stuck to every part of my gums, leaving an utterly vile taste in my mouth for the rest of the night). Free granola was decent, mocktails made us feel quite sick. Venue seemed nice, but... 

The coat check lost my favourite scarf. They sent me away without it and refused to let me look for it, citing the 'safety of other customer's belongings'. A real slap in the face when my own belonging has gone missing after I left it with them for safekeeping.

I was told I would get a call back, I didn't. I tried emailing, no response. it took me two days of calling to get through to them, where they finally confirmed that my scarf had been given away to another guest. They said they would look into it, it has now been five days. 

Never in my life has a coat check lost any of my belongings. I can't see how a place can justify charging these kinds of prices while being this cavalier with peoples' things. Had I known there was a risk of this, I wouldn't have checked anything in with them in the first place. 

If you're thinking 'big deal, it's just a scarf,' well... It was *my* scarf. It was a gift from a loved one from a place that doesn't exist any more and it meant a lot to me. Even if I could replace it, it was expensive and had to be imported. The fact that it probably ended up getting tossed in a stranger's trash really boils my blood. 

I was told they'd comp us some snacks or cocktails, but I honestly don't want to go back into that place. I found this process incredibly offensive and left feeling utterly robbed. I now hate this restaurant and never want to return. 

Incidentally, do NOT drink the 'coffee' mocktail. It tasted like there was something seriously wrong with it. We can't be entirely sure, but believe it to be the source of some stomach problems we both experienced after our visit.

Edit: Around two weeks ago, they offered to send me a check for the scarf. I've not received any check and while I've attempted to contact them three times since then, I have not received any response or update.

Edit 2: finally got a response after updating this review the other day, making me think that maybe they pay more attention to Yelp than customer service emails. 

I also received a separate message on Yelp from somebody I suspect works for Eleven Madison using a sock account, in which they questioned my palette and cited the restaurant's three Michelin Stars. While I don't outsource my personal fine dining opinions to a tire company, I sincerely doubt that 11 Mad would still have its stars if the Michelin reviewers had the same experience that we did. Service is part of the package and losing a guest's belongings is as bad as service gets.

Edit 3: Finally received a check covering my lost belongings, after a constantly following up for 27 days.  I will never, ever return and I doubt I would be welcomed if I did.
The food is STUNNING - it's like eating a work or art . The service is impeccable and the wine paring was perfect. It's pricey but well worth the experience.

We were super excited to come here as we are "weekday vegetarian's" 

My wife read the book from the original owner and has been enamored with the high level of customer service that he wrote about, so we had to come and experience it for ourselves. 

The food was fantastic. It is a tasting menu. We enjoyed all of the courses.  The inside of the restaurant is beautiful and the bar area is very chic.

Stop reading now if you don't want to have anything ruined for your experience. 

.........


Okay here are a few nuggets:

When you arrive, there is no host stand. When you give them your name, they know exactly who you are and they walk you immediately to your table. 

The coat check is a gentleman who takes your coat when you arrive and he will be waiting for you with your jacket open and ready to put on at the front door as you walk out.  It is at that point you'll realize they never gave you a ticket to claim your coat. That is incredible service. 

If you're paying attention, you will notice that they use an electric iron to iron all of the table linens before the tables are set. 

You will receive fresh silverware for each course. 

Should you need to use the restroom, they won't just point out the direction, someone will escort you and speak to you like a long lost friend. 

If you really want to spoil the surprise, look at all the photos that I took of each course.

Service was good and menu and presentation was very interesting. We really enjoyed most of the evening and were pretty sure that we'll be coming back. What tarnished the whole experience was the "exit strategy." 
At the end of the dinner, when we were still enjoying our drinks, we were approached by one of the hostesses and offered a tour of the kitchen. She did not mention that we won't be returning back. After the "tour" the hostess took us out of the back kitchen exit and all of our things were already packed up and waiting by the exit. We felt misled and almost deceived since we thought that we're coming back to our table, where we were still enjoying drinks.  We must have stayed past our seating time, but there are many more professional ways to let us know that our seating time is over. Offering a "tour of the kitchen" and then discretely walking us out to the exit and bringing our things out definitely ruined the whole experience. Will not be coming back.
food was unreal ... a little overpriced but you pay for what you get nothing that is good in life comes for free

This restaurant served food that simply tailored very well to my idiosyncratic palate. Most noteworthy for me was the avocado, the friggin bread and butter, which was just really outstanding to me, the variety of mushrooms served throughout the dinner, and the unforgettable dessert sequence. 
The cocktails were also pretty remarkable, but it's Manhattan so be ready to drop a buck or two on these. They are worth it though. 

The staff are very attentive and as you'd expect, the service overall is very on-point. They noticed I went through the bread like a madman, and I probably had like 4-5 servings of it before the end of the dinner lol but they kept my bread plate full, so props to them for that (in addition to everything else they do)

The dining room is beautiful, in addition to what you'd expect from a Michelin 3-star dining room.

This was the greatest dining experience of my life. The food was unreal. Everything tasted and looked spectacular, but that isn't what makes this restaurant so special. The service was the best experience I have ever had. The man working with us, Nick, was friendly, charming, funny, knowledgable, and had plenty of ways to entertain. He made a special game for us where we described the person next to us and they brought out a drink that suits them. Touring the kitchen was very fun as well. They explained the transition from a meat heavy menu to one that's entirely vegan. This restaurant is outstanding.

This place is unbelievable. The service is unmatched and the venue is so unique. I love the tall ceilings and architectural feel with beautiful art.  The food is worth every penny. They do things with plants I didn't know possible while maintaining their natural magic.

Look, this is still an amazing restaurant. It will likely be one of the best meals you've had. But I've been here twice before the switch to a vegan menu and twice since the change. It's good but it's just not worth the cost anymore. I give them credit for having the courage to make the switch but, for real, it's just not that good anymore, especially for the price.

I've dreamed of eating at EMP since reading Unreasonable Hospitality, a book that has proved monumental in my professional and personal life. 

The restaurant Will describes as EMP cannot possibly be the place I ate last night. I've had the pleasure of enjoying hundreds of Michelin meals, and have absolutely no idea how EMP is still operational. A dinner at a place like EMP should feel theatrical and whimsical, something off of Broadway. EMP is a middle school play, at best (and the waiters are faker than a group of middle school girls who all "love" but really hate each other). 

The food is uninspired, bland, and boring. You can't help but feel as if you're being pranked as you eat. If I dedicated my career to cooking plant based, and created a menu of dishes considerably worse than those served as sides at other restaurants, I'd consider other professional routes. 

The best part of the meal, outside of the sheer pleasure I felt when I was able to leave after a laborious 4.5 hours, was not enjoying the food, but bonding with my table-mates at how much room there is for improvement here. Every employee should read Unreasonable Hospitality, twice, and pay a visit to a tailor to fix the way their uniforms fit. 

I don't mean to be so negative, but please do not come to this version of EMP - let the old one live in your head as a treasure. They say "never meet your heroes" and I should have listened.

Wow. I am having a difficult time understanding all the positive reviews here. There were 2 good things about the dinner: the presentation of the food, and the architecture // interior design of the restaurant. The food was rly rly subpar, which would've maybe been ok if the service was also great, but the service was shockingly bad too. After reading Unreasonable Hospitality, I was expecting top notch service. But little things like having to ask for something as simple as another Diet Coke and a paper napkin 3?????!! times before finally getting them 5 min later are unacceptable given the restaurants reputation. The dinner lasted 4.5 hours which would've been ok if the food and service made the time feel like it was flying. But with each course, we were dreading the next course because we knew we would be stuck at our table for what felt like another eternity. The amount of food we got was equivalent to probably a singular salad. I feel bad saying this because I could tell a tremendous amount of work and thought went into each dish, but it rly didn't show at all. This was definitely a once in a lifetime experience... meaning, we will never be returning. Glad to be able to say I've been tho... I guess? 
(Also everyone who worked there felt like bots. I felt like I was in an episode of Westworld)

There's a lot that can be said about Eleven Madison Park, none of which is negative. 

We were treated to top notch service from the moment we walked in. Without introducing ourselves, we were greeted by name, and had our coats taken to their checking stations. Our table cloth was pressed and ironed; something we saw the staff repeat throughout our dinner when guests departed. They would also brush away any excess crumbs between courses, ensuring we always had a clean space.

The artwork presented is something I can rave about all day -- please keep a lookout for their subtle $250,000 art piece. If you can spot it during your visit, I'm proud of you. Otherwise I can't clue you in to what the piece is, lest I give it away. Just think "celebration".
