We were also thankful for their willingness to show us around the restaurant when we showed interest in these pieces; it was nice to be given context as to what we were looking at, and to learn more about the artists.

Lastly the food was almost impossible to describe. As a former vegan, it's difficult not to be inspired by their plant based menu, to make an effort and better my diet; it's always nice to be reminded that going back to my vegetarian lifestyle wouldn't mean substituting favor and quality. I kid you not, their cabbage w/ white truffle and tofu made me tear up. It was, what I described in the moment, "a religious experience". Also, their wine pairing was perfect.

We enjoyed every single moment of our 4+ hour experience. We left full, tipsy, and smiling and are eagerly awaiting our next adventure to NYC so we can try a new seasons menu. Bravo, Eleven Madison Park, for what could be the best restaurant/food experience of our lives.

I'm a vegan and how can this restaurant get anything but a five star! Outstanding creativity with foods - excellent acoustics - wonderful staff - always presentable and everyone is uniformed and reflects their motto! Clean bathrooms - and the only thing that can use improvement is the hostess . Not kind, slightly have attitudes - and not pleasant to interact with. Otherwise Delic!
Very memorable meal with intricate presentation. We did the tasting menu and the experience lasted a full 3 hours.  The night ran a bit long, but it was a very unique experience.

What a cool and fab experience!  This was my first 3 Michelin star restaurant and was definitely a memorable one. The service, presentation, attention to detail... it was all done in perfection. Though I had a great time here, I wouldn't be rushing to go back any time soon. 

There is no menu and the whole experience felt like a show. There's this excitement and suspense for what is to come next. Each dish was inventive and creative. They contained some ingredients I've never had before (such as finger lime) and flavors I've never tasted before. Everything was so fresh! 

Love all the soups that I tried especially the first one. It was divine. The highlight was definitely the carrot tartare. They brought out the meat grinder to our table along with some incredibly fresh and the most orange carrots I've ever seen and then started grinding the carrots in front of us. We got to play with different flavors and spices mixing them into the ground carrot. 

The bread and the desserts were disappointing though. Not a fan of sorbet and the other dessert was mediocre I already forgot about it. The little game we played at end with the chocolates was cute but taste-wise, they weren't anything special.

Just had the chance to dine here again since they went vegan & every dish was extremely creative, unique,& delicious. They really focus on seasonal vegetables & this time around it was squash. I had a squash cocktail & even tried their butter made out of squash! It's so nice to see fine dining become more conscious & expose others to veganism. The service was also great as usual, you're welcomed right away & greeted with a smile. I also really appreciate the option to try bar items a la carte, vs bar tasting menu or the regular tasting menu. I really hope EMP leads the way for other restaurants & continues to elevate the bar!

All in all, well worth the time (4 hours) and money ($$$) for a truly memorable experience (made even more memorable by the special tour of the kitchen and bonus glass of plant-based Egg Cream! Wow!!!

Going to a restaurant of this caliber is to understand it is a performance. It is presenting their newfound veganism at the level of fine dining it has been known for. To this end, they succeed in that the atmosphere of the space has remained the same and the delivery of their plates still brings a sense of wonderment and often times slight confusion, similar to how it did before this transition. Personally, I am not a practicing vegan and do have an occasional craving for dairy, eggs, and honey (Call me cruel). Relying on seed oils, nuts, and beans will only get you so far with me. For this reason though I did enjoy the lentil "caviar" and the chocolate covered pretzel, the rest of my meal left me feeling like I had not even finished the last bite of a tasting menu. 

I would have given 3 stars based on the above plus the high price, but then again, I knew what I was getting into and what my expectations of service and ambiance were. They did not fail to provide a sense of elegance to every dish, even the sunflower butter was molded perfectly. I just wish there was a way to elevate their vegan meals even further, be that portion wise or by using even more distinct ingredients you may not find at another vegan restaurant. Maybe spare me the halved avocado next time...
As good as it gets.  The food, the wine, the service.... It all comes with a price but worth every dime.  Just go and enjoy.

We were accommodated as walk-ins to the bar area and had some delicious post dinner drinks and snacks. The cocktails were delightfully complex and beautifully presented. The sweet potato bar snacks were delicious and not too heavy. Our server Alize was incredibly accommodating and provided top notch service during our visit. Fantastic time at the bar we were lucky they had space available when they walked in! The ambiance is very warm and relaxing.

I have been to my fair share of Michelin experiences across all star ranges, and while I am no critic I absolutely have some criticisms. 

Why on Gods green earth did a 7 course experience take over 5 hours. I am all about soaking in the ambiance and enjoying ones time but JFC we were sitting around till 1:30 am (starving - more on that later) begging to leave. Comparing this to other 3 star experiences I have had where I distinctly remember saying "I would like to live in this restaurant".

Lets talk food. So I knew going into this it was a vegan menu. Great! Love that! Went to a vegan tasting a few days prior and it was fantastic. We were served our first course (a radish tea) and all looked at each other and knew we were deeply screwed. The tea was incredible, with so many flavours packed into a tiny (TINY) cup. We then progressed through more little plates consisting of a single dumpling, a DIY carrot tartare (best part of the meal) and different shapes blobs and cakes all covered with "veils" of thinly shaved fruit and veg. We did all nearly cry after they brought out the bread (after we asked to have that course moved up), which at that point we could tell the servers thought we were classless swine.

We probably wouldn't have asked for bread early if we weren't hammered. This was NOT our own doing. We opted for the wine pairing as one does and while the food was not at all free flowing - the wine was. At least two pourings per course. That + a bevy of broths and veils = A MESS. 

In sum EMP is a beautiful restaurant with a stellar concept and some truly delicious dishes, but it did feel like we were getting punked a bit. It all seemed a bit like satire and that there was something else coming which would be the WOW course. Unfortunately the only thing that provided a WOW was the bill which regardless of how many times you pay a three star price leaves your jaw agape.

Our pizza after was phenomenal

Wow. Just wow. We went to celebrate my husband's 50th and the entire experience blew us away. We did the full tasting which is 9 courses and it was worth every penny. Exceptional service, superb dishes, and lovely ambiance. So glad we were able to get a reservation!

Most incredible experiences of my life. The atmosphere incredibly welcoming and also the food arrived in a timely manner. The ambiance was flawless. I have never felt so impressed in my life. Congrats EMP

Writing this in vegan era
Some of the entrees were surprisingly acceptable (for being vegan)
However the number of dishes were quite low
Service was good for the first hour, but dropped off precipitously and became horrible near the end. We were waiting maybe at least 30 minutes for one of the next courses. This wasn't even acknowledged by the staff. This bad service was probably the worst part.

Wow. There are almost no words to describe the nearly five hours I spent at EMP. An unreasonably hospitable experience led to Will Guidara's book, which has wildly changed my view on leadership, life, and serving others. I wish every meal could be at Eleven Madison Park.

Another amazing meal experience at EMP!  At first, I was skeptical about an all-vegan menu. Sure, some dishes would be great, but no butter? No cheese? No fish???  So what!?!?  The food is incredible!!!  Every single bite was off-the-charts delicious!  And, as usual, the service was impeccable!  Special shout out to the waiter from Italy with a lot of hair (I wish I remembered his name) and our enchanting Sommelier Erica Lauer, who made the experience much more enjoyable with carefully paired wine pourings with each food course.  Erica really knows her stuff, and when I watched her use heated tongs to remove the top of a bottle of wine from the table next to us, I knew she is the real deal!  Deep knowledge of the wines and she explained everything very clearly.

All in all, well worth the time (4 hours) and money ($$$) for a truly memorable experience (made even more memorable by the special tour of the kitchen and bonus glass of plant-based Egg Cream!  Wow!!!

Can't comment on what this top pick is like now.  In the past classic.  Lovely atmosphere and superb service.  With both unique yet traditional apps and entrees.  Heard it's lacking luster, however, since the new chef has taken the reigns!

Spectacular! Going in I wasn't sure if I would enjoy a complete vegan evening but boy did they do a wonderful job in explaining what was to come. From the minute we sat down it was interesting and intriguing! 
A must try if you love food and interested to see how vegetables can be prepared in a way that meat is not missed!

I only had time to stop by for a cocktail, but the incredible level of service and hospitality warrants a few words.  

Everyone from the door greeter, host, bartender, and back bar were so genuinely attentive and friendly!  There was nothing ostentatious or pretentious, just friendliness and service.

I cant wait to come back for dinner!!!
Smoked Sturgeon was absolutely fantastic, Service was great as well, Will definitely come back.

Wow, this experience is one of the best I've had in my entire life. I booked before realizing they were vegan and that caused some concern, but I'm so glad it was. What a perfect way to try a new thing. I don't have the words to describe the meal, it was so far beyond anything I've ever tried before. And every aspect of the dining experience met that level. The staff was professional and courteous. No pretension, I felt very comfortable. The ambiance was spectacular. Also, the most amazing was the drink. I don't imbibe, but I was able to enjoy Na mock tails that had every bit of enjoyment as a top shelf libation. I will return at every opportunity and no trip to New York will be without.

EMP was my "must go" restaurant every time when I visited NYC. This time is the first time I visited EMP since the pandemic, but more importantly, since they changed their menu to a plant base cuisine. I'm not a vegan but a 3 stars Michelin restaurant commands me to keep an open mind. 
Service was excellent and no details was overlooked. Dishes are very tasty and we can actually taste the freshness of every vegetable. Plating was very original and creative. I expected nothing less. 
My only beef was when I compared to the old EMP, I missed the backgrounds of each dish. In the past, when the server presented a dish, he or she would tell you a story behind the dish, the origin of the dish. This captured our attention. Our taste buds were constantly searching for the flavor that the server described and our noses were seeking for the aroma. Through out the evening, there were magics, card tricks and games associated with different dishes. It was a wonderful experience and we were 100% engaging. But this time around, no story telling, no games, no magic. Don't get me wrong, taste, service, visual presentation were still top notch. But this is not the same EMP!

The ambience is phenomenal 10/10 and initial service which is evident throughout 10/10. The staff know what they are offering and serving. 
We started off with a Hibiscus soft tail drink which I wished had more hibiscus tone taste to it than the lemony I got. Than they served us an asparagus appetizer and dumpling soup, which I thoroughly enjoyed 8/10. Light and tasty. 

Truth is as much as it is a classy join i did not find the food to be memorable nor will I book another reservation here. It's excellent to show off to your friends how gourmet vegan food can be served but that's about it. Did not enjoy the Gnnochi at all. Too light of taste and I could have gotten better at a local. The tofu ( I have been having it since I was 2 ) 50 years later, at Eleven Madison it did not hit any spot in on my palate, my brain matter nor memorable. It came in a sweetish soupy liquid and other than the fact of how it was made and locally produced there was nothing in it that shouted out "have another bite it's good" 

Like I say. Food is ok.  Not something I'll go back to but the service and ambience is priceless. Mehhhhh is all o could muster

This was better than I expected, but I still would not pay to come back for this meal. 

I came into this meal with low expectations. Many friends had expressed disdain at the chef's efforts of an entirely vegan fine dining menu. And I agree - the "meat" dish was a zucchini that was smoked and flavored to an inch of its life, but it just could not replace the heartiness of a real meat dish. The meal hence felt incomplete. 

But I learned about the existence of tonburi (land caviar) that grows in the Akita prefecture in Japan. They tried to transform it into real caviar by infusing it with the flavor of the ocean using nori and coloring it black. 

The thing about vegetarian/vegan meals sometimes, is that they try so hard to make a dish resemble the non-vegetarian version. But why?? I like mushrooms because they're mushrooms, and I like carrots because they're carrots... and not because they're trying to be something else.

What I was genuinely impressed by, though, was the clear gazpacho they served at the beginning of the meal. It was a beautiful introduction to the meal on a sweltering summer day in New York City.


1. TOMATO (In variations with Shiso and Sansho Leaf)
2. TOFU (With Tomato and Lemon Verbena)
3. TONBURI (With Baby Lettuce, Horseradish and Radish Tostada)
4. SUNFLOWER (With Summer Beans, Epazote and Savory Pinot Grigio Grapes, Green Rooibos, Gentian, Verjus, Epazote)
5. BROWN RICE (Roasted with Seaweed and Celtuce Chardonnay Grapes, Mt Olympus, Juniper, Mint, White Balsamic)
6. FAIRYTALE EGGPLANT (Fried with Panisse and Thai Bird Chili Grenache Grapes, Bitter Melon, Thai Basil, Blueberry, Koji)
7. SQUASH (Grilled with Poblano Pepper, Seitan and Coriander Merlot Grapes, Pu-Erh Tea, Lapsang Souchong, Verjus, Coriander)
8. MELON (With Honeysuckle and Mint)
9. STRAWBERRY (With Cherry Blossom and Rose Chamomile, Elderflower, Yuzu Star Anise, Grapefruit)
10. SESAME (Pretzel with Chocolate)

I decided to give it 5 stars because I really appreciated the warm attentive service and some of the dishes were very inventive. Not to mention the reserve wine pairing definitely enhanced the flavors of the meal. There just  aren't too many places that can do what they're doing. Let's be clear about something, this was not the same 11 Madison experience of 2016, the previous two times my wife and I came here it was nothing short of magical and ethereal. The art deco setting was stunning and the kitchen was in full view which gave you a sense of being really connected to the experience. There was also an intimacy that was lacking from its previous incarnation, the last two times we attended in 2016 and 2013, we were invited to visit the kitchen and they gave us a small drink creation that made us feel special. At one point my wife told the server that she loved chrysanthemum tea, she doesn't drink alcohol so they brought her alcohol free pairings consisting mostly of different teas. I am pretty sure prior to 2017 someone would have brought out a drink for her containing chrysanthemum tea, that didn't happen last night. With every Michelin Star restaurant experience I've had, the tasting menu came out with its own unique tempo and rhythm, much like music in a symphony. This tempo felt purposeless, like one singular motion, think of a fireworks display with no finale. I love meat and I'd be lying if I said I didn't miss it last night, however, I've also been to other Vegan restaurants like Candle 79 where the dishes were so extraordinary you never missed the beef or chicken. Again, I respect what they're trying to do so much I wouldn't dare give it less than 5 stars. Would I go back? I can't answer that at the moment.

This is a 3 star Michelin restaurant that is 100% vegan. It was also voted best restaurant in the world. 

First time visiting this restaurant. We reserved a six course meal and had to prepay for this reservation. We also added a wine pairing for each course. 

The restaurant itself is beautiful with high ceilings and almost feels like your in a museum but with great ambiance. The food and each course were small portions however the food was excellent. 

I'm not a vegan but every course had great flavor and texture and the presentation and descriptions of each course were well prepared.

I believe one of the main reasons this place is so highly rated is the level of service that every person in the restaurant displays. The preparation and effort that everyone delivers is unbelievable. I had at least 8 different people serving my table and as I looked around the restaurant every table was treated the same with the detail of serving every table at the highest level. Overall the best service I've ever experienced at a restaurant from the moment I walked into the restaurant to when I left.

Their plant based menu is AMAZING! Wow. I am generally not a fan of fine dining because I don't like cream, fish eggs, or exotic meats. I LOVED every single dish. If I lived in NYC, this would be an every weekend type of dining experience for me. The service is also too notch, seriously. Water glasses always full and someone always walking by to silently check on the table. Very comfortable feel and the staff is well trained on the food. I had a question on how something was prepared and got an answer without hesitation. Bravo!! I will be back!

I'd give it a four star but for the price a it's three star. I had modest expectations for it being the considered one of the best of the best in NYC and it fell short. I did the 9-10 course meal with a wine pairing.

The food was alright (for a three Michelin star), not the best not the worst. I've been to a few other restaurants that are three star Michelins and this was the worst one.

The avocado was my favorite dish. The rest was nothing special. I love meat too much. This place reassures me that even the best vegan food sucks.

I felt like the wine pairings was a bit too much drinking (8 drinks) and mixing alcohol made me a bit sick. Less alcohol would have been better.

I liked idea of the gift to go (see pic), although I haven't tried it yet. The service overall was good. The venue was boring although I went on a Wednesday night.

The place is majestic. Got the chance to check out the newly revamped Eleven Madison Park, and wow, the new interior design is an absolute showstopper. It's now rocking a mix of classic charm and modern swank that takes your dining experience up a notch.

If you are dying to go, just to brag you went, do the six course meal with no wine pairings. Don't over spend, it's not worth. If you are a carnivore, you'll be disappointed but that's expected for a vegan place.

I would never give this place 3 stars. I wonder if they paid for it. The food is a 1 star and service is a 2 star. I wonder if they paid for ratings.

It was $1.5k for two with 10 course meal, wine pairing, and standard tip.

If you're a vegan like myself- its the place to DINE! My hubby and I go often and we love it. All fresh and ingredients are superb.
Highly recommend for all to try. Can't go wrong !

author.name: Tracy B.
author.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

reviews.review:
I've been here many times, but not since they've gone fully plant based. The food was always good and thoughtfully planned but the service is what always stood out and kept me coming back. While sitting in the giant immaculate dining room, you might assume the staff will be very stuffy, but oh boy do they have jokes, some of my best memories have been made in this restaurant. 
I also did the "EMP at Home" during covid and that food was fantastic, and their serving instructions could not have been easier to follow.

Absolutely incredible! The food explored taste in unique ways - each dish was tasty, surprising, and interesting. Service was impeccable, and the atmosphere was fun, somewhat upbeat, encouraged conversation. Would come here again on special occasions.

If you can afford it, it's actually worth it. (Or sit at the bar for less.) By now it's old school, one of the original chefs gone and the recent (two years?) shift to all veg. But tho not as good food as pre-veg still good mainly because of the great service, consistent across the many pre-fixe courses, one of the only places in town that outdoes Danny's many. You'll feel royal in this place. The setting - the big ground floor of the Metropolitan - is impressive. An experience at least once in your foodie life!

Ok... so it's ALL VEGETARIAN... yes , not ONE piece of meat. For 2 with extra cocktails and 1 wine tasting with tip was 1000$. Pretty steep for just tomatoes, zucchini, tofu, and sun flower!! But it was GOOD. It innovate, unique and well thought out! We did the 6 course tasting. If they had just a bit of animal protein this place would be a 5-star. It's not
clear why they started going vegetarian? To challenge the chefs that work there? It's not a political statement.  Service was impeccable. The venue was really nice! Not stuffy or unapproachable. The wine paring was MEH! They did pick some unique wines but it fell short of the food! Charge me more.... BUT GIVE ME BETTER wine! Life is too short to drink SO SO wine. Question is ... will I be back?? Probably not, not unless they add some fish or lobster!! Sorry, I won't recommend this place!

This restaurant is totally a scam!!! I don't understand how it's a 3 star Michelin. I've been dining in multiple 2 star and 3 star Michelin restaurant and all of them are amazing and truly deserved the title of Michelin. However, Eleven Madison Park does not. Not even 1 star for this restaurant. No creativity in food even the servers sounded bored. First 3 dishes are literally tomato and salt. Then random fried rice that I can definitely make better at home and then overcooked half zucchini. Their ingredients are nothing special hidding behind "sustainability" but in fact a random farm belongs to a used-to-be photographer. Don't even put effort in gathering best ingredients around the world. Ambiance is so so, servers all look so bored and not passionate about what they serve. But how could they be? The food sucks so much!!! And guess what they make you pay up front and no refund for cancellation. Really??? Eleven Madison, does your food is so so bad that you are afraid once potential customer read your review they will run away ?? And very disappointed in this Michelin rating!!! How on earth this can be 3-star Michelin. Definitely a Scam!

The experience here is top-notch from service to ambiance to food and creativity. 

We especially loved the Manhattan bar cart. They come table side to mix a variety of Manhattans with an explanation of each and tips on how to mix the perfect Manhattan. Each of the Manhattans we tried were expertly mixed.

We did the 9 course tasing menu. All of the dishes were creative and flavorful. They were very accommodating with a couple of allergy/restrictions we had. Everyone in our party, even the meat eaters, thoroughly enjoyed their meals. As we left we each were given granola to take home, which was a really nice touch. 

I would definitely recommend going here for the experience and creativity of the food (and the Manhattans!).

NOT A 3 MICHELIN STAR EXPERIENCE!
My boyfriend made a reservation to celebrate my birthday. The food was simply ok . The service was unacceptable. My boyfriend let them know about his onion allergy and they brought a course made only with onion ! They didn't do nothing to fix the mistake . 
At the moment of the check they brought us someone's else check .
We will never came back again
Service. Impecable. Food. Disappointing and underwhelming. We've been to over a dozen restaurants with stars. This menu is so marginal we didn't even take a pic. Go to Daniel.

I don't ever write reviews but when I do, it's only because the experience was not great. I also hate to be writing a negative review for this restaurant but it really is just not worth coming here (especially given the price).

For context, I've been to multiple 3 Michelin Star restaurants (French Laundry, Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare, Le Bernardin). I'm also a vegetarian so was extra excited to try a full vegetarian experience here. My wife, on the other hand, is a huge carnivore (she had low expectations coming into it). 

We had the Spring 2023 menu in July. There are about 8-9 courses. While the presentation and service were all impeccable (as you would expect for a 3-star restaurant), the food just didn't come anywhere close to blowing us away. I was particularly disappointed in that the flavor profiles were extremely narrow - it felt like everything had a green color and tart/cucumber-ish flavor. I get that it's a vegetarian menu but there's a wide spectrum of ingredients available that were entirely missing. There were no warm colors/flavors like tomatoes or mushrooms. 

Also I'm a huge sweet tooth and love the desserts at michelin restaurants because there are usually multiple courses and they usually have some macarons or other small bites to top everything off. Here though, the dessert  was just a small strawberry panne cotta-like thing followed by two chocolate pretzels, which was also quite disappointing. 

Maybe the best thing that came out of the food experience here was that the restaurant gives you homemade granola in a can to take home. My wife and I joked that this was the best part of the meal (sorry that's harsh but that's really how we felt). 

I hope the chef can be a bit more creative and add more depth to the menu going forward.

Good. They are very friendly and good food!..
Took my boyfriend here for our anniversary. This place is so romantic. There is a great view of the city and it is very pretty to look at when the sun is setting. It is a little pricy, but the service wad great and we did get a few complimentary items for our anniversary. It was a great place to go and feel semi-fancy for a day, but we were still able to dress pretty casually.

Amazing experience!!! Just WOW. I came here for my anniversary and i was immediately greeted by 2 people who congratulated me as well as our waiters. The service was impeccable and waiters were observant, friendly, and social. Food was all vegetarian and so well thought out! We got the wine tasting as well should I highly recommend. They really do give you your moneys worth. Ambiance was incredible as well. 1000% will be back! Thank you for such a great experience
Simply perfect. One of the best fine dining experiences in NYC. My food was inventive yet satisfying. We can't wait to go back!
Great service and very tasty food! Me and my family really enjoyed it! We will definitely come again to have a good time.

The place was elegant and peaceful. We enjoyed the food and the atmosphere. The service was impeccable as always. The added surprise was a tour of the kitchen. A special treat! The dessert, beautiful bread and vegan butter, everything - we didn't miss the meat!

Returning after Covid, last year, the restaurant reimagined itself into plant-based-only menus, and quite a few patrons, including myself, were not sure what to expect.  There are so very few Michelin vegetarian or vegan restaurants, especially here in America.  So I was quite pleased that I stopped in for a no-reservation lunch recently.  

The main dining area is still very open with 7m ceilings, which (intentionally?) makes the bar seating area seem claustrophobic and dark.  While waiting for my table, I watched one of the servers use a classic flat-iron to smooth out the tablecloth at one of the tables.  Yeah, if you've never been, it's that kind of place.

During a quick tour through the enormous kitchen, I made the pleasant discovery that women now comprised about 40% of the kitchen staff - highly unusual in the industry at this level.

But the first, and last, reason to visit is the excellent food.  I enjoyed the tofu with peas and anise hyssop (lavender) and the asparagus with rice, nepitella (calamint - mint/oregano flavors) and ginger.  Of course, their presentation skills have not diminished, demonstrated with the steamed-at-the-table stuffed morel with baby lettuce.

I'll have to return.

2023 06 10. M3.

I hate to write 1 star reviews, but ... I also hate to have an experience like we did here. I had looked forward to it for a long time. Of course I knew it was vegan but that didn't matter. But service was 1 star. Took forever to get started and then lagged the whole time, we felt forgotten about, and oh yes - they brought the birthday dessert twice, because they forgot they did the first time and we waited 30 minutes for it the second time when it was literally well past time to go. We had mocktails and they realized things were off so they comped those at the end. But they honestly should have done more. The manage said they would comp our menus but they are paid in advance -- and it's been over a month and no refund. I honestly don't even care about that anymore, I just wish they we hadn't wasted over 3.5 hours and a meal here. 

The food was about 2 stars. It wasn't awful but no where near ANY of the other Michelin three stars we have been to, and not even most of the two stars or other good places, and it was really a boring menu overall. The artichoke tart was probably my favorites. That is a stretch to find a favorite.

The ambiance was okay and not awful, but 2 stars there as well since it was not a relaxing classy vibe like a meal at Per Se and was more like a busy dining room where you could be forgotten. 

Most people would do this as a special night out and I really think they could do a lot better to earn that place at this price point. It just didn't deliver.

I visited Eleven Madison Park prior to the pandemic and had an incredible experience. Unfortunately after it decided to go vegan, I had not heard the best things about this place. I didn't really want to taint my original experience and did not intend to visit again until my good friend asked if I would be interested in visiting together with him and his wife. I was a bit hesitant about going but my friend said that he wanted to see what the highest quality vegan food was like, and his comment piqued my interest about what Eleven Madison Park's take on it would be like. Unfortunately, it was exactly how I thought it would be. 

The service and ambiance was perfect - just as you would expect in a place like this. My only complaint is that they had us waiting up to 25 minutes between courses and that the restaurant temperature was too cold.

Unfortunately, the food was a complete miss in my opinion. As you can see in my other reviews, I am just not a fan of vegan food. I love vegetarian food, but I just think vegan food misses a lot from not being able to take richness from animal derived sources such as milk and butter.

My experience here solidified my opinion about vegan food. To be frank, I did not think any of the courses were good. After my first bite of the first course with Celtus, I knew I would not like this meal. Nothing stood out.. everything was incredibly bland and felt like it was missing something. The first few courses were raw and because it was so cold in the dining room, they felt very unpleasant to eat. Even the vegan bread was subpar in my opinion. I found the mushroom "butter" accompaniment inedible. 

Sad to say, my experience here was not great. I don't think I will be back and I would not recommend going here to anyone based on my experience. It's really a shame, because I loved Eleven Madison Park before this change.

Phenomenal!! This was our first time and everything was exquisite! They lived up to their Michelin star rating. Staff was incredible, going above and beyond. The cocktails were unique and tasty. The tasting menu with vintage wine pairings were amazing. The creativity and flavors throughout were delicious. Note that this is completely plant based, but absolutely wonderful! The lighting was a bit dim but overall the ambiance is lovely. This dinner will cost a bit but it's a nice experience!

I came to this restaurant on a dare from my cousin who's no longer with us. The environment was lively, but I could hardly contribute, due to my extremely emotional state.

Great date spot, but the foie gras tasted old.

RIP, Murphy.

So my review of a restaurant will cover 3 elements:
1. Atmosphere : 10/10
2. Service: 11/10
3. Food: Negative 1 if possible. 

The food is weighted at the highest value, and therefore brings the overall rating down to the lowest possible 1 star. 
I believe I have a sophisticated palette and have experienced food from across the globe. I also enjoy plant-based cuisine very much, and therefore was extremely excited for delicious vegan food. 
The main course was steamed lettuce and mushrooms. It was not the ingredients which were not high quality, it is what was done with them. These beautiful ingredients were done a disservice in how they were prepared. So much potential and we were served unflavored steamed vegetables. I felt like baby food had been plated and served to us. It was that unappetizing. Everything looked so beautiful and I wanted to love it. I am not super wealthy and had saved up especially for this meal. I am not certain how it has 3 Michelin stars and am appalled anyone gives this place such a high rating. I will never get these 3 hours of my life or my hundreds of dollars back and I am offended at how the chef thinks it is ok to serve such flavorless food.

It's easy to see why this place has frequently been voted best restaurant in the world. We book a reservation well in advance of our visits to New York, and we are never disappointed.

Owned by world-renowned chef Daniel Humm, this jewel of Manhattan features a gorgeous Art Deco ambience, and the menu offers some of the finest and most creative and decadently delicious takes on plant-based versions of various foods.

At $365 for a 8-to-10 course tasting, it truly is an amazing deal, as food this great should actually cost far more. We never cease to be amazed at what this innovative kitchen concocts, and we will always return.

Thank you, EMP.
This place never disappoints.  We've been coming here for years and so glad it survived the pandemic.  The food, service and atmosphere always exceed our expectations.
Amazing service amazing food great taste and great location very beautiful restaurant love the ambiance and people who goes here is an excellent place
The most disappointing food experience I've had in a long time. I was hoping they could make Vegan food three star quality. Not even close. Bummer.
Consistently one of the best meals you will ever have - and now taking vegan cuisine to the same level EMP has reached for years.

This place is a very expensive joke. A grand for 2 people. That is with overpriced wine as well as over priced everything else. We
left completely hungry and went to other veggie place to get some real food.  

Its a place for suckers and fools. 

Enjoy!!!
Simply put its fancy but lacks substance and flavor looks aren't everything. So good luck:)

We were excited to eat here and flew over 3k miles to do it, but unfortunately, it was not worth the hype. The restaurant was running 30-40 minutes late, but we were able to get some cocktails, so it was not a deal breaker. Once we were seated, it was clear that service and experience were inconsistent depending on who you were with, the size of your party, or how many bottles of wine you ordered. My wife is vegan, and some of the courses were good, but not what would you expect from a 3 michelin star restaurant, but what would you expect from a 3 star restaurant on Yelp.

Had their 9 course tasting menu and loved every bite.  You have to be a vegetable fan, but no course was underwhelming and many were so exceptional in the balance of texture and flavors that I will definitely be back next time I am in NY.  The courses clearly reflect an obsessive attention to detail. I tried and enjoyed their up and coming producer wine pairing.

I had no idea what to expect coming to Eleven Madison Park, all I knew is that it is a vegan restaurant now since the pandemic. So coming here was a black box for me as I have also never tried it pre-pandemic either. We had a company dinner event in the private room upstairs. First the decor of the location is beautiful with high ceilings. The room of our private event was very nice and overlooked the entire restaurant. 

We started with passed hors d'Oeuvres. I was completely blown away by the creativity. Such as a lightly fried asparagus with seaweed, carrot tart and onion tart with a slice of shaved black truffle. Starting with these, I was already looking forward to the rest of the meal. 

For the sit down portion, we had fried chickpeas and morels tarte to share. Both were good, not blown away. However I do love morels and mushrooms in general so the tarte with huge morels were right up my alley! Followed by one of my favorite, morels butter! Wow! This butter had such a strong flavor, truly remarkable and innovative. 

Followed by salad and asparagus with shaved truffles. Both also were good, loved the asparagus. Then I opted for the fried king oyster mushroom. I am not sure how to respond to this dish. I was not taken away at all. In fact, I could not even finish the fried mushroom portion because it was so bland, with no mushroom taste whatsoever. The fried mushroom reminded of a dull potato. Very sad of this option. 

While I appreciated eleven Madison stayed true to the vegetable as the main ingredient and did not try and hide it as a "mock meat". I was expecting all of the dishes to be innovative like the morels mushroom butter, however some of the dishes were a huge hit and others were a miss. Overall an experience that should not be missed but hopefully you can dodge some of the dishes I had.

I heard mixed reviews from my foodie friends before coming in so I didn't have high expectations, but this experience was still a letdown. 

There were a couple of dishes that wowed me, but overall the meal was just not satisfying. And not because it was vegan - I had vegan meals that were completely flavorful and filling. But here at most of the dishes were quite watery and thin, and portions were just insanely small. The main course was literally a few lettuce leaves with a flavorful but insanely small chunk of mushroom. 

The dessert wasn't that good too. I typically have high hopes for desserts at fine dining restaurants because most of them do it well, but this one was again watery and thin. 

Maybe I just don't get it. Won't be back.

I went and had the vegan tasting menu. It was with a group of coworkers and we were treated by a vendor with whom we do business. 

The entire meal takes 3+ hours. 
It's not as stuffy/formal as you might think which is nice.
It's plant based so if you are not vegan it will not really be that amazing.
The initial soup dishes were amazing. The rest were meh. 

I would never come back with this menu. Shrug.

This was the best vegan restaurant I've ever eaten at. Service is impeccable, and the staff is very knowledgeable about the food - and the point of view the chef is taking when designing this completely plant-based menu. There's a lot of talk about the pivot to vegan cuisine, and it mostly works. I didn't miss the meat, but I did leave the restaurant wondering if I had missed something truly spectacular by not coming before. I definitely enjoyed the meal, even though three Michelin stars seems a little high (this is a good two-star restaurant, similar to Saison in San Francisco in its impact). I know the technique is impressive, but I'm not eating for technique and culinary skill. There's only so much you can do with a potato. It's the best potato I'll ever eat, but end of day, it's a potato.

I would probably go back if they pivoted back to the omnivore option. But it seems unlikely. As it stands, it's a wonderful experience that just lacked what it once likely was. Other New York restaurants blew me away. This was just impressed.

This restaurant is worth the wait.  If you can't get reservations, wait early and sit at the small bar.  You can also receive food in the lounge.  We got several of the mushroom dishes, they were all delicious.  The cocktails were even better, but I can't believe how incredible the service was.  10/10

This was a spectacular dinning experience, one my wife and I will not forget. The food, drinks, service, ambiance are all phenomenal. I'm sure most reviews talked about the amazing food. I would highly recommend the kitchen tour and the non-alcoholic cocktail pairing.

The service here is incredible. The food was pretty good but the most remarkable part was the dessert. The overall pricing per person here is too high for the a month of food you're getting IMO. It's great but not worth $400. The decor here was pretty modern and chic.

I've been to many michelin restaurants in nyc and this place was a huge disappointment. They are vegan but expected more than just raw veggies like salad. Most of them were no cooking but just ingredients. Taste was sub par, service was highly questionable, the workers seemed rather rude, not a serving way but like you are here at our restaurants type of vibe. The timing of food was the worst. Waited 1hr for the first course, then the next course would come out 5 minutes later and the next would be another 40 minutes wait. They kept on offering bread and honestly even eating a lot of bread we walked out hungry. This was $400 per person dinner and it was not worth it at all. A common "nice" ingredient truffle wasn't even a part. All greens, didnt see unique cooking and if you are here to have a good time with your date, go somewhere else. I had the worst bday dinner. Even if your partner is vegan, go somewhere else. Took 3 hrs for some lettuce and celtuce. Every new dish was a disappointment.

No words. This is the absolute best meal I have ever tasted and experienced. It's everything you expect from a 3 star Michelin restaurant and more. Don't lose hope with the vegan menu either. The food doesn't attempt to mock meat or any other non vegan ingredients. It is an entirely new and outstandingly enjoyable menu that will shock u with every bite.

Good service, beautiful classic high ceiling dining area plus very quite yet intimately set private rooms.  The food was fresh and presented in artistry forms.  The drawback and a concerning one was I was left a bit hungry.  It was a work event so I can't really ask for more (don't want them to know they are working with a secret competitive eater).  Also it is a vegan restaurant, so come with expectations that you won't get the meat high.

We went there today for the first time for lunch. They had a debut of their spring menu. Every dish we had was amazing! The flavors were exquisite and every vegetable shown through. It definitely felt like a labor of love. All the servers and staff were friendly, thoughtful and knowledgeable about the menu and what's involved in the preparation. The Maitre de was so kind and full of hospitality. She gave us a tour of the kitchen which was really special and fantastic to see. Everyone was in the flow working like clockwork and it was impressively impeccable. 

I really loved all the dishes. They use the most modern food preparation process that keeps all the vegetables full body and flavor. 

I would highly recommend this restaurant especially for special occasions. It made our special occasion memorable for life.

Thank you everyone at Eleven Madison Park! We look forward to being able to come back. You're the best 

PS even KuKu loved everything and the special treats

One of the most incredible restaurants I've been to ever. There's a reason it's a Michelin THREE stars, it is top quality and service. My husband for our 1st year wedding anniversary took us here. It was a 10 course meal and everything tasted amazing. The best was the baked Alaska for dessert it was divine. All the dishes were intricate and I believe the menu is constantly changing too but the one time we went was amazing and I want to go back the next time I'm in New York badly. Superb experience

Eleven Madison Park exceeded all expectations. It lived up to the name!

From the very moment we walked in, the service was absolutely impeccable. Every restaurant in NYC should take notes on the hospitality here. 

Our waiter was also a wine sommelier and knew exactly what to recommend. She was very well versed in cocktails as well.

Every dish from start to finish was packed with flavor and was so unique. Definitely the best meal I've ever had in my entire life and I've been to several Michelin star restaurants over the years. 

A lot of people doubted Eleven Madison Park when they decided to go plant based but they have proven that fine dining does not need meat to have flavor. 

Hats off to this fine establishment. Highly recommend.

Eleven does NOT provide a 3 Star dining experience.  In a true 3 Star, the food should be exceptional, with several courses providing a powerful "that is amazing" sensation.   Also the service should be impeccable and typically the ambience adds to the experience.  Eleven does not even come close to any of those expectations.  My experience at other 3 Stars has been truly memorable and I've been to plenty of 2 Stars that are certainly better.

I'll start with the food.  Most of the courses were basically fine/interesting - but a 3 Star should be well above "fine".  Not one course was memorable; none of them delivered that "wow, this is amazing" flavor/sensation.  And the truly disappointing one was a "signature" truffle dish - which included significant truffle shavings, but only the tiniest hint of truffle flavor.  When we asked the waiter what type of truffle was used and explained that it had almost no flavor, he said their early season truffles were extremely flavorful, but since it is now apparently late in the season, they've lost their flavor!  The waiter offered to provide another course, but we were already having 10+ courses;  we didn't want another course.  We just wanted the courses served to be delightful.  And the 2 desserts courses - totally forgettable.  We also ordered the wine pairing.  We understand that you don't normally get exceptional wines in a pairing, but you still expect a few to work exceptionally well with the course - nothing in Eleven's wine pairings delivered this sensation.  

Next the service.  We arrived about 5 minutes ahead of our reservation.  The greeter asked my name.  After 3 attempts, I had to spell it out; it's 5 letters/2 syllables, not very complicated.  But that still didn't satisfy her.  "What's the full name it's under?"  I said "Tom".  Still not good enough.  I tried "Thomas" and finally broke the code.   She already had our name on the reservation list, so why make it so hard?  I've had warmer receptions from immigration control agents in a non-US country!  Then she asked, "are we celebrating anything tonight?" "Yes" I replied, "my wife's birthday" -  then there was absolutely no recognition of the birthday during the entire evening!  The waitress at a local diner will at least wish you a happy birthday - but not at Eleven.  The service during the deal was very inconsistent.  There were a couple of occasions where my course came, and we were told my wife's would be "out from the kitchen shortly". She does have some food allergies that required a couple of courses to be prepared differently from mine, but surely a top-level restaurant should be able to ensure that each person's dish arrives at the same time.  Finally throughout the evening the servers did a poor job of explaining each course/each wine paring.

Finally the ambience.  Eleven is in the former lobby of the building with an art deco design.  Totally very nice with lots of potential.  Have they done anything to "warm it up/make for an intimate dining experience" - again sadly NO.  For example if there was one living plant/flower in the place, it was pretty well hidden.   Nothing in the setting that made you feel, "this is a special experience."

We had high expectations for our evening and were totally disappointed.  Eleven is so overrated and totally underwhelming.  Yes, it is interesting to create some unique plant-based courses.  But how they merit a 3 Star rating with such forgettable food and service is a mystery.  If you want a really great dining experience, go somewhere else!
Service great but food was not to my liking.   Changed menu.  Hope it improves. I won't be back for a while.

Eleven Madison Park located near Madison Square Park is a michelin 3 star restaurant in New York City.
I remember this restaurant was ranked no.1 several years ago. 
Food: Eleven Madison Park used to be non-vegan but now it only serves vegan dishes. Overall each dish was unique and tasty. Wine pairings were great as well. Food presentation was fun. 
Service: Service was attentive. They also gave me a birthday candle and a goodie bag at the end of the meal. But we forgot to get kitchen tour.
Ambiance: Spacious and elegant vibes. 
Would come back sometime!

Service was absolutely amazing and we especially want to highlight Eugene who was very knowledgeable about the dishes and ingredients and made us feel welcome. 

Ambiance is impressive though I do regret the loss of the original art deco colors in the interior. 

The food was very good, but sometimes left us yearning for more. And two potato courses were probably a bit of an overkill. Also sometimes we were just hoping to be dazzled by some unique ingredients that we never heard of and there was less of that. For example the mushroom course used shiitake mushrooms when there are many other more unique options. We did enjoy the vegan menu, but I have to admit that in our prior visit with menu inclusive of some animal product it was a bit more interesting. This also leads to us questioning if the vegan menu should be offered at the same price point as it probably is cheaper to source the plant based ingredients. Overall, no regrets and great experience, but wanted to share some observations.

THIS PLACE IS A YES FROM BEGINNING TO END! A truly amazing dining experience at Eleven Madison, which is now fully vegan! 

First, it is a beautiful setting and the every staff member was so sweet and welcoming. No stuffiness here folks!  We did the eight course tasting menu with wine pairing. I can't say enough about how beautifully presented and delicious every dish was! Our waiter and sommelier were delightful and very experienced.
They specifically inquired about allergies and accommodated them. 

My favorite dish and it was difficult to decide, was the Shiitake Mushrooms over rice with pesto and finger lime. I would never imagine that combination, but when eaten together was just wow! It sent me in search of purchasing finger limes, just loved them!

The potato and truffle was decadent, look at all those truffles! The onion 'butter' was so unique and the bread was much needed with all that wine lol. We will be back for sure!

I included a photo of the Winter menu (it changes seasonally), we can't wait to see you in the Spring!
Everyone should experience this once, you may just go vegan! Reservations are a must, months in advance, but if you're lucky you can walk in and grab a spot at the bar, I believe there are six seats for walk ins and they have their own tasting menu there. Just GO :-)
I have always enjoyed dinners at Eleven Madison. Their Manhattan cocktail service is unmatched. The food and service are unparalleled. I can't wait to try the new plant-based menu.

A delightful way to end a New York weekend. Exquisite and delicate flavors made the vegan menu exceptional. Service was informally formal, everything was done correctly with a lite, friendly touch. Our waiter, Brandon, was terrific.

Sorry, this place is nice and the service is great but really not worth the money. 9 course dinner (plant based) was about $400/pp. I did feel full but only one of the dishes was out of this world, the rest were just tasty. I've been to Le Bernardin and Daniel so far and this place is always on my bucket list. Kind of disappointed, they didn't even do anything for our anniversary (like i don't know candle and nice plating of dessert?? At least that's what we got at Le Bernardin and Daniel) anyway, it was a good experience, at least I can say I've been there once. Won't be coming back anytime soon though. Maybe if they have wagyu or some lobster back on the menu.

Really Bad. Do not let the Michelin stars fool you, that was from 6 years ago when this was a different restaurant. Service people here seem miserable. 20 mins to get our first drink. 10 mins of silence to even get a hello from a waiter. Food is literally just salt. Every dish we had my wife could've easily made herself at home. The dessert is literally a scoop of sherbert ice cream. We could not help but just laugh at that point. All the tables around us were also complaining and just like wtf is this a joke. Do not fool yourself I promise you will be thoroughly disappointed

I'll be honest, I wasn't super impressed. Obviously, the food, atmosphere, cocktails, service, etc. are all great. But for what you are getting for your money you can do far better. I guess it'll work if you have a client that needs to be impressed but for the most part it's for people that want to impress themselves.

3 visits since plant based.  I am mostly vegetarian and have eaten very well at Jean George, Daniel, Nobu ordering from their vegan and vegetarian tasting menus.  there is nothing i like at Eleven Madison Park.  It feels like a over -posed altar to plant based food which has the same basic musky undertone in all the sauces, even the mocktails (seedlip like in smell).  Mr Humm will have to try harder to understand the extraordinary depth and breath to plant based cuisine and not keep feeding us pickled musky food and tell us this is what plant based is about.  A tasting menu has to be exciting and delicious.  you have failed, Mr Humm.

Without trying to sound repetitive, EMP delivers exquisite food and service. Their winter menu was radish-heavy but tasted and looked delightful nonetheless. Everything from ambiance to the service choreography was truly deserving of its Michelin stars. My vegan husband was truly blown away that one of our servers noticed he was left-handed early on and repositioned his silverware. We couldn't have been happier to have been fortunate enough to celebrate our wedding anniversary and my birthday at the only 3-Michelin stars, plant-based restaurant in the entire world!

What an amazing dinner at Eleven Madison Park, a definite highlight to my trip for sure. 

Eleven Madison Park is the only restaurant in the world that is fully vegan and has 3 michelin stars when they recently pivoted to a full plant-based menu after reopening after their pandemic closure. 

Walking in, I told them my name & they immediately took my winter coat to hang and sat me down at my table. 

The ambiance here is very calming with dim lights and tables spaced well apart but not too far apart. 

Food:
The restaurant has a few different menus to select when you make your reservations. There is the full course (8 to 10 courses), a bar setting with less courses and they recently announced a shorter dining room set. The menu changes with the seasons so it is always different.

I had booked myself for the full experience. Every course was centered around a certain vegetable or flavor. The shiitake mushroom course was definitely my favorite as well as the tofu course. 

They also provided some bread and spread in the middle of the dinner set that was absolutely amazing. 

Service:
Service here was top-tier as to be expected. I was called earlier in the day to ask if I wanted to move my reservation earlier since they had some openings. When I originally made my reservation, only the 915pm slot was open. I chose to keep my time though, but I appreciated the call. Every course was carefully brought out to me and explained what it was. Servers were quick to clear off my table once the course was done. The pacing of the courses was also nice. 

TL;DR - well worth the trip to Eleven Madison Park and I'm sure I'll return in the future.

Wonderful restaurant, delicious food, love that it is 100% plant based. The staff are amazing and service was exceptional. They take allergies and dietary needs serious. The food was all delicious and well thought out--just a glitch with the dessert (ice cream in winter...but the taste was pleasant). They offer a kitchen tour, which should be the standard across restaurants. They also give a little gift bag to each guest and that is a nice touch. They are overpriced, no question about it, but they know that and make the experience worth it including a little gift bag (with something delicious and useful--not just branded nonsense). This place is just the right amount of bougie and casual. (Le Bernardin could learn a thing or ten from here!) Looking forward to the Spring menu.

I actually enjoyed the plant based menu way more than I thought I would. Probably the best plant based meal I have had. Service was great, as always. Ambiance was nice, but just like any other fine dining spots - nothing to write home about I guess. I had a nice time but the meal (with wine pairing) was a little more than what I would like to pay for. Worth trying though.

Absolutely amazing. Who knew radishes can be so tasty! Mind blowing flavors and interesting natural ingredients that makes you appreciate the gifts of the earth. There a strong zen influence to the presentation and reminded me of the Kaiseki we had in Kyoto. But the focus on vegetarian ingredients and elevated natural flavors were truly unique. What a treat! Found out the menu changes every season. I heard my wallet sighed...

I visited Eleven Madison Park about a year ago for my birthday, and I was excited to try their new vegan menu. While the food was innovative and creative, the flavors didn't live up to my expectations, especially for the extremely high price. I will say that the service and showmanship was truly exceptional. The staff provided the best service I've ever had in a restaurant, and the menu provided unique experiences like making tofu at the table in front of you.  But the flavors themselves were lacking. I recall loving a mushroom/truffle tart, but I thought everything else was just okay. I wish I could say otherwise, but I prefer the food at the $105pp vegan tasting menu at Miss Rachel's Pantry in Philadelphia, and the $43pp vegan tasting menu at Somebody People in Denver, even though the service doesn't even compare.

Heard to be the best restaurant in the world. What I can say is it is a very unique experience. We had the 8 course menu. I didn't find out that this place was vegetarian until about an hour before the reservation time bc a friend made the arrangement for us to celebrate her birthday. The food and service were phenomenal. We were invited into the kitchen which was really a treat. We laughed all night and really enjoy everything out before us including the very unexpected mock tail menu. We also received a bag of hits before we left. Not sure if that's something done for everyone. The check was about 850 for two then we tipped 20%.

It was a beautiful time. If I had to think of any negatives I'll say the lighting could have been more decorative. It was super simple.

Experience culinary perfection at Eleven Madison Park.

From the moment you step into the elegant dining room with the tall ceilings, to the last bite of dessert, every detail is carefully crafted to create a truly unforgettable meal.

The only plant based menu with 3 Michelin stars, the menu is innovative and delicious.

We started with a hot pot of sweet potato with lemongrass, followed by a celery root with rice porridge, 3rd course was white turnip and horseradish, followed by a tofu course, 5th course was squash with fried shiso pepper, then bok choy with white truffle and finally grilled celery root with juniper and pine.

The palate cleanser was one of the best I've ever had, a grape sorbet and consommé, the flavors were perfect and so balanced.

Dessert was an apple with birch and cinnamon and ended with a pretzel with sesame and chocolate.

EMP is not to be missed.

This was a huge part of our food tour in NYC along with Le Bernardin,Per Se, and River Cafe. For starters, I think it is way too trendy now in the culinary and art industry to write negative reviews. Plain and simple this is one of the greatest meals you will ever have. If you don't like it at all I would just assume you don't like vegetables. Forgive me but I can't remember our servers name but he was from North Carolina and he did a great job. I'm a huge Ravens fan and I went to the game earlier that day and they lost to the Giants. I won't lie I wasn't in the best mood after being up all day, fighting Jersey traffic for 2 hours to make this reservation, and just being tired overall. His service was outstanding though and I think he deserves a lot of credit for the success of the meal. My favorite course was probably the "fondue pots" if you would call them that. The chef definitely tells a story with each course and everything was very different. This is a very long meal even by fine dining standards but I doubt anything else in North America even compares. Lastly the bar deserves huge recognition here. My girlfriend did the juice pairing and I doubt anywhere in the city can offer as much variety. Alcohol wise the cocktails are gorgeous and a very ample selection to choose from.

Amazing place..great food very unique taste 
Highly recommended..chef Daniel humm is amazing
What a night! The food is exquisite. The setting is marvelous. Not only is it a perfect dining experience they also make it really fun.

Overall, I was pretty impressed. The food exceeded my expectations and was very delicious. Everything was very flavorful and unique. The presentation of the food was very cool and extra. The service is obviously very good. Is it worth the money? Definitely not. I can't imagine any meal being worth this much but it was a fun experience and if you're looking for a really expensive, cool place to eat, I'd recommend. You also get granola at the end to take home and it's exceptionally good!

This was one of the most amazing dining experiences I have ever been apart of. It was four hours of my mind being blown every 10 minutes. I know this place is expensive, but I definitely consider it worth the splurge at some point.

The menu changes every season so the main ingredient of each dish is a vegetable that is fresh with the season. Even though they have gone fully vegetarian, it is incredibly impressive how you don't miss the meat at all because each dish is insanely tasty and something innovative has been done.

My boyfriend and I were greeted right when we walked in and escorted right to our table. The ambiance is really nice here. We sat in a corner booth that was very comfortable. Even the pillow looked perfectly plumped. The staff was so kind throughout. Understanding of my allergies and extremely accommodating. I asked a bunch of questions about the food and they were patient with how they responded. They have so much knowledge! They share about each dish in detail when presented. We even requested something special and was able to see the kitchen. We left and were given a gift bag - I'll keep the contents a surprise - but you could see that incredible attention to detail. This is truly a place for a special event and unique experience.

I had a drink that had chutney in it, mushrooms that looked like a steak, and a broth that tasted like my childhood. Each dish is a surprise and a wonderful one at that. Thank you eleven Madison staff! I fully intend to return in another season and can't wait!

Chef Daniel Humm has create the best plant base fine dining in New York City and probably all around the world. With 3 Michellin Stars, ranked the #1 World 50 Best restaurants in 2017, 4 stars in The New York Times, tasteful ingredients, colorful textures, great service & ambiance I am gonna say they have what I called real FooddPpoetry!!

My wife and I went to Eleven Madison Park for the first-time last night and, overall, it was a very good experience. I would give 4.5 stars if that were an option and have rounded it up. However, there were some definite opportunities for improvement. 

We arrived early and were sat adjacent to the bar and given a cocktail menu to peruse. It took a little longer than I would have expected at a Michelin 3-star restaurant for a server to come and take our order for cocktails. Almost immediately after ordering, we were escorted to our table and our drinks were delivered there. The cocktails, themselves, were delicious. I had the "Pear" cocktail and my wife had the "Cumin". Her's was fantastic. 

The food overall was impressive. I am neither vegan nor vegetarian and the plant-based menu was both interesting and flavorful. The fact that they also emphasize seasonality makes their job even more challenging in January, but I have no complaints about the flavor or interest of what was presented. The opening radish courses presented with a delicious radish broth and the mitsutake mushroom "steak" were probably the most memorable. I also loved the collard green course. The pumpkin skin butter served with a vegan croissant was also a wonderful surprise. 

We opted for sharing both a higher end wine pairing and the non-alcoholic pairing. We have found in other Michelin-starred restaurants that these non-alcoholic pairings can be every bit as interesting as the wine pairing. So, by sharing both of these we have been able to enhance our experience, and not end up drinking so much alcohol that we do not fully appreciate the later courses. In this case, the wine pairings were clearly superior and complemented the food incredibly well. The highlight was a glass of 1989 St. Julien. The finish went on and on. I think that they need to work on their non-alcoholic pairings a little more. Almost all of them had as a base a mixture of a wine-grape juice and a tea. Individually, they were interesting and tasty. However, with a similar base in almost every drink, the group was monotonous. Other high-end restaurants, which I have visited, provide a lot more variety in this regard, offering a wider array of vegetable and fruit juices at base of their pairings.

Overall, the service was excellent, as one would expect; however, I do concur with some reviewers that the constant circling of the servers around the dining room can become distracting over the course of a three-hour dinner.

Overall, we had a wonderful experience. We would certainly recommend it to our vegetarian and vegan friends. Meat eaters need to go with a very open mind, but we do appreciate what chef is trying to achieve here. We would be interested to return during the late spring or summer and see how fresh local produce would be incorporated into the menu.

Overpriced for a vegan restaurant..guess because it's a 3 Michelin star (it should be lowered in my opinion). Every course was good and tasty but almost felt like eating 'meat', but why was I even bothered with that? So much easier just to go to shake shack right cross the street..Overall it was good experience given its decent service but def would not come back again.

Amazing. I was so impressed by the vegan menu. I left extremely full and satisfied and the service and performance of every course was incredible. I honestly enjoyed it better than the pre-vegan menu. My favorites were the veggie hot pot (first course) and the sliced mushrooms at the end that were styled almost like a steak. What an incredible experience!

Needless to say, the service at Eleven Madison Park was impeccable. We opted to sit in the bar area rather than the main dining room, which was perfect for a lunch date. The seat we had looked right into the main dining room, so we felt like we were getting the experience at a fraction of the cost.
All I can say, is this establishment represents NYC at the highest culinary level ever imagined ! We stopped in for some drinks, nibbles and ambience. Did not disappoint.

Tip: It's a FOOD CON. DO NOT WASTE your time or money. We saw this restaurant on Netflix and it looked incredible in the movie.  We excitedly made a reservation and flew to NYC for a trip that included dinner there as the highlight. They changed from what seemed like an incredible menu offering in the movie to a all plant based menu that bordered on the idiotic.  I was a vegetarian for 15 years so plants are not the problem.   The menu sucked !!!!! The food was not even pretentious it was just BAD.  It also followed a flavor pallet of fermentation, mush porridge, and steamed plant leaves.  You can't say it was inedible although I didn't eat the slime in two of the courses after one bite.  The rest was manageable but WHY ???? Bother it was underwhelming and I wasn't inspired I was pist as I realized the Chef doesn't care about the customer experience.  The waiters surely feel either embarrassed or curious about the fools who would part with a 1000 for a sliver of kombucha squash And a bite size morsel of bok choy steamed in a clay volcano for drama.  If you want a stunning artful tasting menu go to Jean George at least their options are delicious and respectful of their clients who want an incredible meal and a memorable experience.
Lovely space and caring service but overpriced for a vegan menu- I did enjoy most of the courses but not worth a repeat in near future
Flawless dishes,remarkable environment.Tasting menu is superb! Thoroughly enjoy this michelin star restaurant

This review is pre-menu change, but I don't imagine things have really changed all that much with their style of service. Here goes nothing (pre-pandemic style):

Surprisingly not great. From the entry through a nondescript revolving door, directly to a hostess in view of the dining room, we didn't really get a feel for the uniqueness of Eleven Madison Park. However, I don't think time was the problem since the dinner lasted 5+ hours. On all standard fronts, environment, culinary, service - there were major issues.

On service - I was served still water after asking for sparkling, the servers hastily refilled cups throughout the night, spilling every time. Bread was served to fill the gaps of our experience and nothing was cleaned up after each course. The bread course was especially bad with crumbs littered about well into 2-3 courses beyond. They forgot my order and I had to speak up to correct them.

I'm fine with having a mostly impersonal relationship with servers, but there ended up being only a handful of interactions with us over the course of five hours, two of which were to ask what food we'd like out of a list of 3 options. The only time we were asked if we needed anything or were doing alright was after the bread course - which I'd asked for a cocktail after and also an additional bun. Neither came for about an hour so I had to ask again. If service was good I could forgive the lack of personality. Nothing was prompt, or choreographed.

I really didn't like being asked to curate a meal (only 2 courses, the amuse bouche "platter" and a dessert dish were anything of a surprise) and why should someone paying this much not try everything recommended by the chef. If you're giving this much control to the customer you may as well be a Hillstone restaurant - most of which have more mindful service than here.

All in all, a long 5 hour dinner with a low amount of courses, limited ingenuity or intrigue in each dish, poor service, poor environment, poor choreography - and I'm not the only one in my party to believe these things. All 5 of us had gripes, and really that shouldn't happen at "the best restaurant in the world".

Also, wtf was with the bottle of apple schnapps we were left alone with for the remainder of our experience? Awful closer. The gift granola came in lovely little glass jars, so 1 star for that.

Extremely inflexible for a top restaurant that is supposed to be all about customer experience.  I made a reservation for 4 at Eleven Madison Park as soon as my preferred date was available online for my wife's birthday, and the restaurant charged my credit card the full $1,755 immediately almost 2 months ahead of the reservation date.  The day before my reservation (tomorrow), my wife and I tested positive for Covid.  When I called the restaurant in hope of pushing out our reservation for a few days, I was given the "friendly" reminder that all reservations are final and non-refundable.  My only option was to transfer my reservation to someone else.  The "guest relations" person did not sound a bit concerned or apologetic about this unfriendly policy.  I guess if one wants to have the full experience at a place like Eleven Madison Park, one must be prepared to handle the snooty and uncaring attitude that comes with it.  Just don't make a reservation unless you are 100% sure you will not be sick on the date of the reservation.  And please let me know if you have figured out how to do that.

I was most excited for this experience during my visit to NYC and I was not disappointed.  Completely plant-based menu in very creative ways.

We started out with a few cocktails from their seasonal menu.  I had the pear, and pumpkin seed cocktail.  Very unique and I appreciate them using seasonal ingredients.

The hot pot broth was so flavor possibly one of my favorites.  Other dishes were Rice porridge, Tonburi with chia seed and potato, and Bok Choy with white truffle.  The mushroom 'steak' was charred and was very well seasoned.  We were also served pumpkin seed bread.  It was so flaky and warm.  We were also able to get a second serving.

For dessert, we had apple and apple cider donuts and chocolate pretzels.  Nothing too impressive but I was also very full at that point.

The dinner took about 3 hours and included a kitchen tour!  Service was outstanding and very well trained on the food.  All in all, the dinner cost a pretty penny but was a once in a lifetime experience!

I was so excited when I snagged a reservation here this weekend!  I was a little nervous it would be a waste of money based on some of the reviews but I can confidently say it was one of my favorite experiences ever.  The food was amazing for the most part and the team that works there went above and beyond; I even got to tour the kitchen!!  Here's a rundown on the meal, which took about 3 hours and filled me up.  I also had the wine pairing which I highly recommend, the pours are heavy. 

Hot Pot: 5/5 the skewers were really fun and the cup of broth that came with it was so unique and tasty

Rice porridge: 4/5 the rice and broth had a great mushroom flavor although I didn't love the mushrooms on top

Tonburi: 5/5 I'd never had this before and it has a chia mouth feel. The potato and smoked almond broth made the dish

Tofu: 3/5 the texture was a little funky for me although the taste was great 

Kabocha Squash: 5/5 this didn't even taste like squash and it was nice and crispy on the outside 

Bok choy: 4/5 I think I started to get really full about this point. The truffle was a great addition. 

Maitake mushroom: 2/5 this was only only course I didn't like. They offered to get me something different but I was getting so full that I declined 

Grape: 5/5 a palate cleanser with multiple textures that went really well together 

Apple: 4/5 I was so full by this point. This course included a couple items and all were great although I couldn't finish the donut 

Pretzel: 5/5 this came with a whole bottle of vermouth which was a fun surprise. I was only able to have half a glass and half the pretzel though, I felt like I was going to explode. 

There was also a bread course somewhere in there and while I was touring the kitchen I got a wonderful glass of mushroom tea; not sure if everyone gets that or not. All in all, I think this meal was worth the money ($700 for 1 person after wine and top) for a once in a lifetime experience!

This restaurant does not deserve its Michelin star(s) or reputation. 

My wife and I spent a total of nearly $1000 for dinner for two and drinks. If that seems like a lot, read on to understand my 2 star rating. 

The decor is bland. You enter and the space is well lit. The ceiling is high. The space is otherwise nothing special. No great art. No beautiful flowers. The serving ware is fine, but nothing to remark on. It's just not star-worthy. 

The service is bizarre and distracting. For some reason, the proprietor has determined that having staff in constant motion is, what?  Entertaining?  It is not. The many servers rotate around a figure eight track. If the soup course is interrupted on its way to table, that server makes another rotation. It is akin to watching roller derby or like the Broadway show Starlight Express. And it also meant it was very hard to connect with any one server as they did not have time to stop and chat. 

The odd service was not universal. We noticed there were two tables where the servers stopped routinely and for long stretches. Customers at one of the tables appeared to be athletes, while at the other they appeared to be Wall Street types.  Maybe they were just better and longer term customers than we. But for the same cost we would have hoped for equal service. 

Both of the special tables received parting gifts and one was invited into the kitchen. 

The food .... Yes we knew it had gone vegan. Plants are multi-colored and can be very flavorful. If this meal was a book it would have been called "Fifty Shades of Beige," or "How Many Ways Can You Cook Squash?"  The exception was the final course that included skewered, smoked slices of mushroom. It was delicious. 

The sommelier was lovely. He was one of the few people to take the time to speak with us. The water server was also personable. 

At the end, a new person approached. Captain?  Don't know. She asked how everything was. We said it was "ok."  We were happy to leave it at that and chalk the experience up to our own eagerness to try something that did not turn out to suit.
