But she pressed and so we shared thoughts about the blah surroundings, the VIP tables, the lack of personal touch, and the relatively disappointing food variety. We also complimented the two servers mentioned above who were great. 

This individual then invited us to view the kitchen. There we were given the parting chocolate bar that had been presented to the VIPs next to us. I appreciated this gesture, although if was clearly an attempt to mollify as opposed to it having been part of what might have been perceived as a gracious evening. 

This restaurant is not: (a) worth the price; or (b) really good at all. There are so many fabulous places in Manhattan; including many with a Michelin star. Try those.

I've contemplated this review on Eleven Madison Park for a few weeks now. I wanted to make sure that I was giving this an appropriate review after letting the experience completely soak in. Now that I've had time to think, I can tell you that this is the best dining service and ambiance you will ever have. And it should be based off the prices and the fact EMP is a 3 Michelin star restaurant. So why only a 3 star Yelp review then? The food. This is only the best dining experience because the service & ambiance are out of this world. It's a best-in-class experience and it probably will never be beat. But the food? I could find 50 places easily that has better food. Chef Daniel Humm went plant based last year and was still able to retain his 3 Michelin stars at EMP so I was hopeful that the food was still going to knock my socks off despite not having animal products in the preparations. Unfortunately the taste of the food really fell short. Now don't get me wrong, the presentation was exquisite so EMP gets points for that but the taste of the food was just average. Nothing blew my mind from a taste standpoint so after dining here, I was surprised EMP retained it's 3 Michelin Stars. The biggest thought I had after dining there was that EMP over salted certain dishes to make up for the fact there isn't meat. I've tried vegan restaurants that were actually better than this because their identity had always been vegan and I feel like they didn't try and to over compensate.  Daniel Humm made a comment in an interview with Jimmy Fallon when talking about EMP's return from the pandemic that 'the world doesn't need another preparation of butter poached lobster or crispy skin duck'. I disagree..Eleven Madison Park was named number 1 in the world in 2017 because of that type of cuisine. It's not another preparation when you are the best at it. While I can appreciate the shift in trying to be innovative, they've tried to change the identity completely and have failed miserably. I'm hoping the change of identity truly was for the purpose of veganism and what it stands for and not to cut costs but keep dining prices the same because of the fact that Humm has been a notorious cheap skate (in my opinion...do your own research). Luckily, they've continued to focus on providing a 3 Michelin star restaurant experience with service & ambiance but ultimately provided sub Michelin bib gourmand food quality.

I can't even express the disappointment and confusion after spending 3 hours eating a meal that was neither enjoyable or frankly edible. putting aside the cost of the meal I was one of the worst meals I have had ever. if the hope was to entice people to a plant based lifestyle I will sure it did completely the opposite. I have had many great vegan meals and sadly this is definitely not one of them.

This place is just beyond imagination. So extremely creative. I LOVED LOVED the plant based menu. I had such an amazing evening with their 10 course menu, supreme hospitality and amazing selection of wine pairing. The entire menu was heavenly!!! I cannot wait to go back.

I have attached a picture of the menu they provided for us with the description of each course we ate - I will comment on every dish.

Cocktails - we ordered the apple and pear cocktails. Personally, I enjoy sweet drinks, and neither of these drinks did it for me. The apple cocktail had horseradish in it which had a very sour taste that was too overpowering for me. Also, the aftertaste of the brown liquor in the pear cocktail was too heavy for me, but that's a personal preference - my boyfriend liked it which is all that matters. After our waiter noticed I had barely touched my drink, he brought me a margarita that ended up being much better!

Sumac - if you are Indian or Asian, then this dish will not surprise you in terms of its flavor. It was technically called a "tea," but I think "broth" or "soup" would have been a more appropriate name. This dish heavily drew on the flavors of a common Indian lentil soup called "dal," to the extent that I felt like I was back home eating my mom's food. While I love my mom's cooking, I'm not sure it was worth the $ to eat a dish inspired by foods I commonly eat at home.

Matsutake - this was a delicious mushroom and ginger porridge and one of my favorite courses. The consistency of the porridge was creamy and thick, but similar to the previous dish, was heavily reminiscent of Indian flavors. However, this one gets extra points because of the unique blend of vegetables, texture, and flavors that I haven't had the pleasure to try before.

Tonburi - This was probably in my top 3 favorite courses. The turnip, potato, and horseradish were each separate, bite-sized pieces and were full of flavor. I was afraid that the horseradish would be too overpowering, but the flavor was just right. Each piece also had a different texture--I believe it was the turnip that had a caviar-like texture that worked really well.

Tofu - The only downside with this one was the harsh presence of the collard greens. Due to its relatively hard exterior, the greens weren't able to absorb enough of the flavor of the broth, and as a result felt like an unpleasant and stark contrast from the soft, gooey texture of the tofu and pool of broth. However, the tofu and broth were to die for and made up for this downside.

Bok choy - this course also makes top 3 for me. The texture of the bok choy was softer than the collard greens and was able to absorb more of the surrounding flavors, and the truffle mushroom shavings complemented the bok choy perfectly.

Sunflower seed bread + (vinaigrette?) butter - this wasn't included on the menu they provided but oh man, I had to add it in my review because it was so delicious. Easily one of the best bread + butter experiences of my life. The butter contains a center portion filled with (I'm guessing) vinaigrette, olive oil, and various spices; it's a party in the mouth.

Maitake mushroom - this was by far my favorite course and maybe one of the best foods that has ever touched my taste buds. I mean, the grilled mushroom was perfectly seared and crusted on the outer edges, and buttery soft on the inside. Not to mention a scrumptious purée served alongside it that gave it an extra tang from the juniper, and slightly sweet flavor from the maple. This course alone bumped my entire experience up by a star.

Apple - this dessert was a dollop of apple-caramel-cinnamon flavored vanilla ice cream surrounded by a glaze, with a donut hole on the side. I loved the ice cream itself, but the glaze was way too sour (it might have been the birch flavor), to the extent that I couldn't enjoy the ice cream with it. I enjoyed the donut hole, although the chunks of apple in the center were a bit to large for my taste.

Pretzel - this was probably the most disappointing course. The "pretzel" was basically just a Reese's-flavored chocolate with absolutely no texture. We were also served a non-alcoholic vermouth with it, and this may just be my personal preference since I had never tried vermouth before this, but let's just say I will never be having that again.

Granola - they included a jar of granola for us to take home with us. I haven't tried it yet, but thought that was a nice touch. I have also attached a picture of that.

Overall, if you are Asian, especially Indian, you might find some very familiar flavors and combinations. In terms of ambiance and service: 10/10 - no complaints in that department. Everyone was extremely kind and went out of their way to make our experience a pleasant one. However, I have to knock off a star for some of the courses that just didn't really hit the spot given its reputation. With a few modifications I think this could have quite easily been a 5 star meal.

Plant-based/vegan meals are so difficult to execute on a high level and make them not only tasty, but look amazing as well--and EMP does it on an exceptional level! The restaurant itself is gorgeous with its ridiculously (in a good way) high ceiling and lovely ambiance. Lively, but not loud. High class, but not stuffy. I wouldn't say this meal was in the top tier of my absolute favorite meals of all time, but it was a great experience nonetheless. Service was on point and all the bites that went in my mouth were flavorful and interesting. Nothing made me cringe, that's for sure! The take-home gift of their freshly made (that day!) granola for breakfast the next morning was a nice touch!

I have been blessed to dine at a few Michelin star restaurants before. Having said that, there is such an exponential difference in everything between the one, two and three star ratings. 

The service, food, presentation and finer details that enhance the dining experience are top-notch here and very befitting of three stars. 

Our 10 course menu was superb from start to finish. The deserts and starter dishes were my favorite, especially the porridge/vegetable hotpot & grape sorbet. The maitake mushroom entree had a great texture and contrast to the seitan. 

I am looking forward to the spring menu if I am available and nearby.

Wow! I don't even know where to start. The experience from start to finish was phenomenal! 

From the moment we were sat we watched the servers dancing around the room in the most amazing flow! I cannot even explain how incredible it was just to see the flow of the servers walking around like a dance! 

The service was of course 100/10 and each dish was created to perfection! 

We haven't been since the restaurant went vegan but we cannot wait to try it! 

Our absolute favorite dishes was the incredible "New York bagel / cheesecake inspired dish" everything bagel crust, New York cheesecake and a thin layer of fish on top with caviar.. I've honestly never dreamt of a dish more after this! Another old classic we absolutely loved was of course the famous duck! My palette is forever ruined and I can't have duck anywhere else after this incredible experience. 

We love that the dining experience doesn't end at the restaurant but that they send you home with delicious granola to help with your digestion in the morning. 

This is such an incredibly special place to us and we cannot wait for our next visit. They made my birthday so special by giving us a private tasting and viewing of the kitchen, which by the way is sparkling clean! 

Truly an incredible place!

Came to NY to try Michelin restaurants and this came as very interesting given it is plant based. Restaurant is easy to find... at 11 Madison with entrance right in front of the building. Friendly staff, service is superb 

For the food, we were told that we got the last menu for the summer as they are switching to fall menu. I initially was not a big fan of an all veggie course and thought i'd leave still feeling hungry but was pleasantly surprised that this was not the case. My husband and i find the food well thought of, flavorful, and satisfying.

Our favorite was the dumpling. We also liked the tofu tomato dish, fried okra and corn. The take home granola is also so good! 

Was not the biggest fan of the drinks shiso and the house made vermouth but it was something unique and adds to the experience.

I don't think I'd ever be able to afford to dine at this restaurant but, I had the honor of trying their food as there was a food truck in my sister's neighborhood and it was the best Jerk Chicken I've ever had!!!!  it was absolutely delicious.  I hope that my sister and I will be blessed to receive another lunch from their food truck in the near and or far future.  Thank you so very much Eleven Madison Park and I wish you longevity in your establishment.

This place is an experience. Go in with an open mind and prepare for your taste buds to explode. Every course is unique, well thought theme that moves you to the next course. I'd highly recommend pairing it with the wine option but if you're not a wine person you can buy a la cart cocktails. The Rice and the Peach are my personal favorites. If I could give this place six stars out of five I would. It's great from start to finish and it's not surprising why this restaurant has multiple Michelin stars.

Let me put it this way...thank goodness for Shake Shack in Madison Square Park. We left our dinner still hungry, and with the clear feeling of having been completely ripped off. The new vegan menu has many bland and boring dishes as well as some unnecessarily pretentious ones. Overall a far cry from the pre-vegan times. Have been here before in 2015 with the original menu, and it was an amazing experience, really worth the special trip that the Michelin guide recommends. I'm shocked they retained the 3 stars - do yourself a favor and go to Dirt Candy, they just got 1 star and is a far better taste experience.

I definitely think this place is worth a try especially since there aren't many vegan Michelin star places. This was our first time & I was actually expecting more food/flavor. I've had better food taste wise at non Michelin places. The presentation was great. Portion was great as well. For the price that's being paid, I would want more quantity & different flavors.

I'll get out of the way that service and ambiance are absolutely 5 stars - hands down the best service I've ever had. I'm trying my best to take price out of the equation, but after having 7 okay courses and spending over $500 for that, plus 2 drinks and gratuity, and still leaving hungry, all I started thinking by about course 4 is "this is not worth it."

Here's my course ratings (though it's hard to tell what anything is because they're rather obscure food items):
Celtuce - 3.5/5
Tonburi - 4/5
Bread & Butter - 2.5/5
Sunflower - 1.5/5
Corn - 1/5
Grilled Squash - 1.5/5
Peach (Dessert) - 4.5/5
Pretzel (Dessert) - 4/5

I honestly don't know how the corn dish got to the point of being served. I'd go as far as to call it bad. The granola they gave as a gift at the end was great and a nice touch, I will say. Overall though, these are some of the lowest food scores I've ever given and my wife felt similarly on all of these. This is in general too, not deducting points for price.

I feel this is doing a disservice to veganism. There were so many misses here, it's incredible. The dishes are creative, yes, it definitely takes serious skill and effort to cook and present these dishes, but what about flavor and texture? I.e., the main reason to eat? It just wasn't there. You need a pretty high tolerance for bitterness and rather foreign (not other cultures foreign, as in "I've never tasted something like this before" flavor... and for good reason it seems). flavor profiles. Dirt Candy, abcV, Blossom, Candle 79 (when it existed) and even Cinnamon Snail (also when it existed) made far, far better food.

I'd say if you have the disposable income, maybe, maybe give it a shot, but certainly don't make this an aspirational place you save up for if you really don't have it like that, because it's just not worth it at all, in my opinion.

Is EMP good? Yes. Is it worth its $400 price tag? Hmmm, not quite.

Given a few of my teammates are vegetarian, we opted to go to EMP and try this 1-Michelin star plant-based restaurant. The theme of the menu this time is "Spring", a welcome departure from one of its previous themes, "Onions". My colleague who tried both said she much preferred this one!

We start off with a white asparagus dish. Dandelion is served with fried asparagus and wrapped in a shiso leaf, with a Japanese tempura take. Asparagus dumplings accompanied - this was good and cozy, albeit a bit too salty.

Next came a radish tostada dish with horseradish crema. It was a touch spicy but really flavourful and delicious! It came with some lettuce served with cypress tree seeds to mimic caviar. The vegan caviar stole the show! It was so unique and yummy.

We then had vegan butter made of morel mushroom with garlic oil glaze, meant to accompany a laminated bread. I have no idea how they do it, but the bread was so soft and croissant like! I will never look down on vegan butter and bread again. My party enjoyed this so much that we asked for more (you can do that!).

A spring pea salad with fava beans was served - this was just okay. A bit salty but nicely tangy. It came just before another pea dish, made of English and sweet peas, served warm with some rice from New Jersey amidst a flower broth. It had an interesting curry flavour to it, with some brightness added from the dill. The wild rice was at both times chewy and crispy. 

A large pot was brought to the table, and the servers showed us some fresh tofu made from soy milk (made 5 minutes before it was served). It was garnished with shaved artichoke, arugula bloom (the flowering part with peppery notes) and some spicyness from roasted artichoke with Calabrian chili. This was okay but nothing too memorable.

Braised seitan with morel mushrooms and roasted spinach was served next with a salty, cornstarch-based glaze. I was instantly reminded of the cornstarch glaze used in Chinese vegetable dishes, but found it to be a touch on the salty side.

White asparagus made a return in the last savoury dish. A large clay box came to the table, with smoke and steam wafting after opening. A smoked asparagus served with asparagus crema and topped with ginger powder was served. I didn't particularly enjoy this dish; it reminded me of Mexican tamales but I found it quite dry.

A variety of desserts came next. Chamomile ice cream arrived first, in a rectangular block. Then came a strawberry in a syrup - my colleague was shocked at this and had to be reassured that it was merely a palette cleanser - followed by a more substantial pastry consisting of strawberry-cherry blossom mousse and rose ice cream. Finally, we ended the meal with a dark chocolate salted peanut butter pretzel served with sweet vermouth. 

Overall, was a theatrical meal but some dishes were misses. My favourites were the fake caviar, dumplings, and tostada.

As a place that has been hailed as the Mecca of dining and previously the best restaurant in the world, I was so disappointed by my experience here. Some of the courses were delicious but others way too salty. And the salt issue seemed to not be something specific for my own palate as evinced from other reviews. The white asparagus dish was served with soggy bread and questionable seasoning. Service was polite but the servers felt cold and aloof. They seemed to be machines carrying out mechanical tasks rather than passionate people always ready for a friendly chat as suggested by the "casual atmosphere" EMP is so desperately trying to promote. 

Overall the experience was decent but underwhelming and I will not be coming back again given how overpriced it is for this level of service.
I had an amazing time here with my best friend. Every course was very thoughtfully put together and delicious. We have decided to make it this an annual treat for ourselves.

I had wanted to try this restaurant for years, and I was in NYC last month, so I reserved a table for my brother and myself (you have to pay for the entire dinner upon reservation, and there are no refunds - not unusual for this tier of restaurant). Unfortunately after reserving the table, I saw online that they had recently converted to a vegan restaurant...that was definitely disappointing news, but I had already booked the table and I saw that the restaurant had still maintained its 3 Michelin stars after going vegan, so we decided to give it a try anyway. Even though I'm not vegan, I had an open mind going in. Unfortunately, each dish became more and more disappointing. I paid roughly $1,100 for 2 of us and we basically just got a bunch of pickled vegetables and some wine...there were a few courses that I couldn't even stomach. It was honestly the most disgusting dinner I've ever had in my life...we went to get some real food afterwards...yikes! Really not sure how this place still has 3 Michelin stars...or any for that matter...The service and presentation were up to par for that level of restaurant, but the food was absolutely terrible. The price is also completely unjustifiable for what you get. I heard a bunch of other people saying similar things about this restaurant after it went vegan. I'd be surprised if it's around much longer. It was really easy to get a table here, which should have been my first clue...

I don't write many reviews but after eating at Eleven Madison last week and Dirt Candy last night, I felt a review might be helpful for someone in the future - go to Eleven Madison if you want to pay a lot for a fancy experience and mediocre food . As a vegetarian, I thought all the combinations of the summer menu dishes sounded fairly unique but in taste, most dishes were a 6 or 7/10. My boyfriend's and my favorite dish was one not even on the menu - the bread and sunflower butter. The bread was extremely flaky and soft and the sunflower butter was so creamy and great.. Way better than regular butter. The dessert was also very good along with the granola they send you home with... but in my opinion bread, butter, dessert and granola are not worth nearly $300 per person

Dirt Candy on the other hand was incredible through and through. It was 1/3-1/2 of the price and every dish was truly amazing and unique. The corn, the tomato, the eggplant, the off menu carrot tacos, everything. The service was also perfect but the restaurant overall had a more laid back, hip vibe than Eleven Madison. 

If you're deciding if Eleven Madison is worth it, I would strongly recommend Dirt Candy instead - cheaper, way better food and better atmosphere.

Everything was amazing, greetings, presentation of food, taste, tour of the kitchen,
Two Of those special cocktails and also the wine pairing details and explaination.
Not to forget that gift with granola
No wonder why they got 3 michelin star restaurant.
The tasting menu is absolutely mind blowing. This restaurant delivers eastern and western flavors in a beautiful plant based show of colors. Everything is just right.

I was fortunate to have dinner at Eleven Madison Park as part of a work occasion several months ago - and the experience was divine! (Because we were in the private room upstairs, our menu was not entirely plant based - not sure if that policy has changed since then.) Highlights: a delicious and flavorful beef tenderloin au jus with truffled beets, butter poached lobster tail with thinly sliced butternut squash, and handcrafted ganache truffles that made a delicate pop in your mouth. I can see why EMP has earned so many culinary accolades and has such a loyal following around the world. The ambiance, service, decor, and experience was all so seamless - efficient, attentive, yet unhurried - remarkable, memorable and tasteful, yet subtle and unforced.  

I only wish I took more photos but after all, it was an executive dinner :)
One of the  best of the best.  It cost a lot but worth it.    And we brought our own wines.  Extraordinary.

My boyfriend and I came out for dinner on his birthday. The service was just impeccable and the food was so well thought through with flavors melting together in such unique ways. They also had a little goody bag for each of us at the end of our dinner to take home and who doesn't love that??Highly recommend for a special night!

This place is absurdly expensive but it is truly fantastic. If you go to a vegan place expecting foie and wagyu, and you expect them to magically conjure plant based foods that taste like these, you're going to be disappointed. But, if you go expecting the most intricate and tasty plant based foods, with impeccable service, that is what you get. I don't know how well this business model will work for long term. But the comparisons to Dirt Candy, Vedge, and other exceptional plant based places are a little silly. The food here is far more fussy, complex, and intricate. Really fun and exciting and well worth going.

Way too much salt on most of the dishes. Not what you expect from a 3 Michelin star restaurant. 

Ambience, service and wine were the standouts. Also the presentation of each dish was done nicely.
Such a special experience. Each course was inventive and delicious and the wine pairing really put things over the top.

I have mixed feelings about Eleven Madison Park... 

After having heard a lot of great reviews and its prestigious reputations, I was initially very looking forward to my first experience at EMP (I was fully aware of its vegan menu; though I am not vegan, still, given its fame, I was very excited and willing to give a try)

However, I want to say that it was a huge (if not gigantic) disappointment. 
1) given its 3-star, I would expect more of its service. But it's not. There is a lot of staff. But it seems like they never really pay attention. At least two times, we were served with our next course with our previous empty dish/glass not collecting away.
2) I am not against vegan menu and I applaud the chef for choosing it. However, I am sure there is other vegan material than just ASPARAGUS! And one course was just tasting like plain salad lettuce! If you're craving about EMP and you're not vegan, give a second thought about it before going!!!!!
3) The first dessert was too sour and last dessert was just chocolate plus alcohol, which was not so good either.

Overall I gave it two stars because I was quite fond of the environment and the hospitality was impressive. But that's it.

I recently decided to come back to eleven Madison park to try the vegan menu after going in 2019. However the day of the reservation I tested positive for covid, calling the restaurant to reschedule they said "we are unable to reschedule the reservation since they are non refundable and final" it felt like the worst customer service experience I've ever had. Especially considering it is a three Michelin star restaurant. This caused me to basically lose my $700 deposit. 

Once I found someone to take my spot, my girlfriend left a explained all of the dishes. She felt as if it was bland, flavorless, and overcooked. With only 2 of the 9 courses where good, but no where close to mind blowing. Most of which could be topped by going to any other vegan or vegetarian place. 

Knowing this and how the customer service treated the situation, I do not plan on returning to eleven Madison park ever and would recommend anyone who has thoughts about going here to go somewhere else.

This was the most expensive waste of money. Most of dishes was unexpectable salty , mostly uneatable. They are using asparagus in 2 dishes out of 5 it is boring for 3 Michelin stars restaurant. Most dishes was tasteless. 
If you are using radish, fava beans etc, it should be evaluated to the highest level of 3 Michelin stars, they didn't. White asparagus was overcooked. Desert was so sour that can not be eating. We brought with as our cup with our special medicine tea. After second meal the Indian water started annoying asking what is inside of your cup which destroyed my wife mud for the rest of the dining, It unacceptable was this level of establishment.  Think twice before get rip off. Don't go

And so there I stood: 12AM in the morning, dressed in my Sunday finery and brandishing my Eleven Madison Park ("EMP") tote bag. I *needed* McNuggies, but as I banged on the windows of my local McNuggie dispensary, it dawned on me that my cries were falling upon deaf ears. 

I was excited at the prospect of dining at EMP. The impeccable, attentive service by the dining room staff and the venue's grandeur reinforced my high expectations. As it turns out, though, the best part about the venue was not the views of the adjacent park from which the restaurant derives its name, but rather, its strategic location across the street from Shake Shack and Popeye's. 

Whereas a Chicken McNugget consists of many animals, Chef Daniel Humm's bold new menu contains none. On this night, the EMP menu's overarching theme was asparagus and I doubt even another vegan chef would conceptualize an entire menu around the smelly step-child of the vegetable kingdom. Yes, each course was technically brilliant and produced textures that I didn't think were possible to extract from an asparagus (one even replicated the feel of a white fish).  That said, there's no getting around the fact that one course was literally a stalk of asparagus and a leaf. I found that the courses tasted similar, notably sharing a strong acidic/citrus-y note to wake up the inherently bland flavor of the asparagus. The courses ended up blending together with nothing standing out as particularly memorable. It was like eating a salad all night, with no rich or decadent flavors to add variety to an otherwise unspectacular experience. The drinks were ok though, if you want to deaden to senses a bit. I recommend this, given the size of the bill. 

Which gets me back to where this review started -- alone, in the rain and looking for food like a modern-day Oliver Twist (if Oliver Twist had just put $520 per person on his platinum card). My appetite was unfulfilled, my taste buds were slightly confused and my pee smelled funny. 

In NYC, there are innumerable vegan mainstays where those suffering crises of either morality or cardiovascular health can be reminded that life isn't that bad. EMP is not quite there yet.

author.name: Chad C.
author.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: This place is absolutely INCREDIBLE! I've eaten at so many vegan restaurants in my life but this one takes the cake (vegan of course). Service was amazing, presentation and ambience fantastic. Worth every penny! Do yourself a favor and go here no matter what!

If you want to get ripped off,  spend $1000 on dinner for 2 people and walk away hungry, then this place is for you.
I have been to many expensive high-end restaurants and this was the worst! There is a sucker born every minute and I was one of them! PS it's a Vegan Restaurant. It's healthy because you walk away hungry.
Absolutely excellent! The service was impeccable,  incredibly attentive, the dishes were very tasty and they built in a few extra surprises along the way. Really enjoyed the experience.

Our daughter, who has worked for many years in fine restaurants, dreamed of having dinner at Eleven Madison Park.  On the occasion of her 34th birthday, we squeezed our way from the wait list into a table for four.  What a delight that proved to be.

Naturally, we knew, and also were forewarned by the restaurant, that the menu is now fully plant-based.  That caution is entirely unnecessary.  The presentations, from beginning to end, do not suffer a whit from the absence of animal product.  Indeed, we all agreed about two-thirds of the way through our wonderfully elegant dinner that if someone only then announced, "Everything you have had is plant based," we would have answered, "Who cares. It is magnificent."

Asparagus was the featured item that evening, but anything could have been highlighted.  I hesitate to pick favorites.  Still, I give a special shout out to to the tonburi and morel courses. 

I have been to several Michelin star restaurants.  They are terrific.  Eleven Madison deserves its status, plant-based and all.  The service and food are impeccable.

I read earlier reviews, some of which complained about saltiness that our party did not find, and others of which evidently struggle with the plant-based "limits."  I am a committed omnivore, but I state without hesitation that dinner at Eleven Madison Park is a three star Michelin experience.  Now, if they can just stop "cautioning" that they are plant based.

Spoiler alert. STOP reading immediately if you don't want to know anything about the food or restaurant. Well, I guess you are on Yelp, so what else would you be here for except for review or photos? So here goes...Chef Humm's plant based menu is as amazing as his previous menu! The following sums it up: My meat loving husband declared he "doesn't even miss the meat."

We are not taking about your typical caesar salad or lettuce wrap. Chef brings bold flavors to bright fresh ingredients. I can't even begin to explain the components giving these dishes flavor. The ingredients are beautifully composed and bursts of freshness with each bite without the 'grassy' flavor you might associate with plant based food. The dish may look simple but the char of a delicate white asparagus or the brûlée flavor of seitan lets you know alot of work went into the dish. My favorite is a simple bread with morel butter. 

EMP is an experience of fresh food and amazing technique. It's ironic that the same Michelin star restaurant you're paying big bucks for is also making meals for essentially a mobile soup kitchen. I love the message Chef inspires with his food truck--that food is for everyone. There is no pretentiousness, we all need to eat, simple as that. 

On our last visit, EMP's homemade granola inspired me to make my own granola & yogurt. The past year I have spent learning to garden hydroponically so my family can have fresh salads & fruit with minimal waste. People who question why pay so much for a vegan menu vs one with meat have probably never grown their own food. It's why some Japanese melons cost hundreds of dollars--you're paying for the science, dedication, and time spent growing the perfect specimen. 

Most meals, when the last bite of dessert is eaten and the check is paid, the experience is over. EMP is special--the experience inspires you to ask where does my food come from? Can I try this at home? And in the words of my husband, "if i can cook like this, I wouldn't mind being vegan."

I wish I could give this restaurant 0 stars.  I have a reservation a week out and tested positive for covid.  The options I have are beyond limited since you have to prepay ($700+).  You can transfer it to someone or allow them to try to fulfill it by contacting their waitlist. They won't allow me to reschedule  and to top it off, they just told me I would have to forfeit my reservation today, a week prior to dinner, and won't know if they can fulfill it until the day of the reservation. Which means I can't try to transfer it this week without forfeiting it.  This is beyond frustrating. Be careful booking this restaurant!

Update - the GM reached out to me directly to help me reschedule when we are over Covid.  Thanks for the quick response and looking forward to enjoying dinner in the next few weeks

I honestly tried to be open to the idea . Initial couple dishes inspired my interest and got me excited about the meal. It was mostly downhill from there on.

I ordered a simple dirty martini, how can a major NYC restaurant not make exceptional martini is hard to believe.

Pretty much every dish is truffle heavy, go to a nearby store get black truffle and out it on any carb of your choice to get the same taste but obviously less salty. To make matters worse each dish was loaded up on salt as noted by other reviewers.

Would have been nice for the owners to highlight with same marketing might to announce they have brought back gratuity on top of the expensive tasting menu.

After an hour we just wanted this experience to be done with.

Dining at Eleven Madison Park was a colossal treat. I am not accustomed to fine dining, so everything was exciting - the new flavors, the presentation, the  professionalism, and choreography of the servers (they appeared to be moving through the dining room in unison). It's not just a meal; it's an interactive performance. I walked in thinking that $340 was far too much to spend on a meal, and I walked out feeling like it was good value.  (Note: I was there for the summer menu, which, based on the other reviews, is different from the current menu. Also, these photos don't do the meal justice.

**Dine Here At Your Own Risk**

This review is my experience with how the management/staff handles the health safety while dining in their establishment today (April 2022).

We had friends staying with us from abroad and we've been in close proximity with them for several days.  Our friend's spouse tested positive for COVID on Easter Sunday morning.

As soon as we found out their COVID test result, we emailed Eleven Madison Park regarding our situation on Sunday.  Upon speaking with them (Monday afternoon), these were the options provided:

A) Transfer reservation to someone else

B) Cancel reservations and get back 50% refund

C) Keep the reservation and go dine at their establishment
Note: we informed EMP that 1 out of 4 tested positive for COVID.
Rest of us were awaiting results and was feeling a bit off already.
To keep the reservations, the 3 questionable parties would be a
potential health risk to the Staff and other Guest

We asked to reschedule for any time later this year, they said NO.

I am surprised that after two years (post-COVID life), these are the options provided, especially option C.   EMP were willing to take that risk and welcome us with open arms.

We opted to cancel our reservation for the sake of everyone's safety
(Note: we already prepaid for 4 tasting menu meals).

You're lucky we are more conscious of potential health risk during these times.  

You're welcome Eleven Madison Park.

I mean...... wow. The service was phenomenal. From the moment we entered the restaurant to the second we stepped out the doors, we were floored at how exceptional the service and overall experience was. Every server knew the details of every dish and we had multiple people come over to wish me a happy birthday! They gave us a private kitchen tour and made us a special little course while we were in the kitchen. When it was time to leave, they got our jackets without us having to say our names or anything, and left us with some extra bread that we loved from the meal. Absolutely unrivaled. 

The new vegan menu was also very tasty - not the best tasting menu I've tried, but very innovative and unique and overall a very positive experience

Too salty. They use the techniques of cooking meat to treat veggies, u can't taste the original ingredients . They use mushrooms to simulate meat which is fine.
Too much fried stuff , 2 of us feel really uncomfortable after our dinner.
The dessert is good, very citrusy , just to be fair.
Ended up paying around $500 each, I feel we learned a lesson booking this restaurant .
The service is top notch. The food I found to be very salty and lacking. I didn't finish most of my dishes. It was very disappointing especially considering the cost.

It's been a lifelong dream to have a vegan fine dining option of this caliber, and Eleven Madison Park certainly delivered. Every detail of dinner and service was impeccable and the portions were very filling. 

Even the drink options such as the house made vermouth were incredible. I had the Cacao cocktail which was smooth with just the right amount of bitterness. Cacao seemed to describe the movement of flavors from sweet to bitter more than the actual taste of chocolate. 

I'm not a food critic but I would consider this worth every dollar for both the service and the inventive usage of vegetables. The only course that fell short for me was the onion tea, which felt like a standard broth. 

There was a large mix of masked and unmasked staff now that the mandates have been lifted. We were sent home with branded jars of granola, which was a nice memento. 

We'll be back, and I do hope they're still making tableside tofu when we are.

I had high hopes for this place and it was just okay - and if you know what it costs ($600pp), then you know that just okay is not okay for this price tag.

The ambiance is gorgeous, the service was attentive, polite, and knowledgable. However, our courses were paced out incorrectly and we ended up being here for 4.5 hours.

This was a 3 michelin star restaurant in 2017, but has since gone downhill. I was keeping an open mind since hearing that the chef adjusted the menu to vegan. 

My fiance and I love vegan food - we've dined at several vegan restaurants in the city and frankly, all of them were better than this.

While there we had several varieties of onion (overwhelming), a soy cup cooked tableside (probably the best dish), a vegan tamale (okay), a fried mushroom bar (greasy and stale), a fruit popsicle (good), and a sesame pretzel (probably the most enjoyable dish).

Because it was an all vegan menu, we should have known better than to order the wine pairings - all white, bland, and nothing to them. They could have been serving me Kim Crawford and I would have been happier. The sommelier was amazing and I truly believe this would be a hard task trying to pair wine to balance out the palate for food that was overall either overwhelming, salty or bland.

I really wanted to love this place as much as I love other places in this city catering to diners who love food & wine, but it fell so far below my expectations that I don't think I'll be back or recommend that people go.

Value per dollar was just lacking - very disappointing to be out $1200+ for a birthday dinner that was just meh.

For context, Michelin Starred restaurants I've dined at include Alinea (Chicago), Smyth (Chicago), Mako (Chicago), Boka (Chicago), Oriole (Chicago), Topolobampo (Chicago), Galit (Chicago), Sushi Nakazawa (NYC), Gramercy Tavern (NYC), Carbone (NYC), Don Angie (NYC), Peter Luger (NYC), and Comice (Paris).

We were looking forward to this high end dining experience finally for vegans! And the fact that it is all vegan AND a Michelin restaurant is amazing. 

We decided to go for our anniversary.

Food ****

We chose to give this 4 stars as we thought it was a 5 star experience due to inventiveness of the food, but after the meal we felt it was heavy on the salt and it wasn't a meal you said, oh wow I need to come back here and eat this again asap! 

We got the 9 course meal. PRO TIP if you haven't experienced one of these before you really want to have a very open stomach because it is a lot of food! 

To start we had the Onion - a broth of delicious savory liquid almost tasted similar to miso soup. 

Next course was the Tofu course- this was super exciting as they actually harden the tofu right in front of you from a liquid! You let it sit and it's turns into a gel like tofu substance, it also had sunchokes and black truffle.

Turnip dish was next with white sweet potato, finger lime and wasabi - this was light and refreshing with some tang to it. A little heavy on the salt here.

Next was Tonburi with cauliflower, Za'atar, and pita. This was very good.
They also had some bread with a special butter and offered refills 

Next was brown rice - roasted with sweet potato and Meyer lemon - this was also done right in front of you with locally sourced rice.

King oyster mushroom with fried lemongrass and ginger - this was a beautifully served dish with interesting textures and tastes 

Celery root with chestnut Masa - had a spectacular presentation with a volcano to help cook part of the dish and was delicious 

And finally, our favorite - Dessert!
This was honestly 5 star: 

Parsnip with apple shrub - a popsicle of yumminess

Citrus with coconut and meringue - the best dessert we ever have had - so light and tangy and refreshing and creamy and inventive with so many aspects of pop and taste - this was amazing

Pretzel with sesame and chocolate 
A little treat we weren't expecting but tastes like a Reese's pretzel 

They also give you some granola to take home for the next morning which is super cute! 

We did get one drink as well, I believe it was called Cacao and had absinthe and smelled like chocolate but definitely did not taste like it. 

Service *****
Amazing service - they knew who we were, everyone from the hostess to the bar server knew it was our anniversary and wished us well.

Atmosphere****
Light piano music playing in the background, high ceilings and pretty artwork. Very nice atmosphere but was missing a little bit of the WOW factor you might expect from this caliber of a restaurant. 

Price $$$$
She's expensive but you do get a lot of inventive food and you definitely leave full which is good when spending that much even though some dishes are small.

When I decided to plan our wedding Anniversary in NYC.  The first restaurant i checked was Eleven Madison Park.  Since I'm vegan, I crossed my fingers to secure a dinner reservation 30 days out.  To my surprise, they had a 10pm time slot available,  I picked that time slot right away and paid the money up front.  I have to say, the experience my wife and I had from the plant base courses to the exceptional service was elegant and worth the price.  Theirs no seitan to substitute any type of meat, every course including the the sun butter bread (kudos to the pastry chef) w/ nut butter spread topped with a black miso glazed was absolutely delicious.  The onion tea and tart with truffles was magnificent.  To have a fine dining experience that is plant base from a 3 star michelin restaurant to celebrate our wedding anniversary was absolutely an epic experience.  We couldn't have chosen  a better  establishment.  We will definitely make this restaurant a priority whenever we visit NYC.

Outstanding experience. The taste and textures of the food was incredible. I came here because this restaurant finds itself regularly as a three starred restaurant in the michelin guide and as one of 50 restaurants featured in San pellegrinos worlds 50 best restaurants. To be honest it is expensive and in my opinion not worth the money, however if cost was not a factor by all means come in and enjoy yourself.

2.5-3 stars takes into account what was delivered for the price. I had heard people rave about this place before it went vegan and loved the owner's rationale for changing it. Individually, each dish in the winter menu (went 3/29) was delicately prepared with impressive technique and tasteful, unique ingredients, though higher in salt content than seemed necessary. The wine pairings went very well with the dishes. The bread texture was incredible (though flavor was salty), the turnip and white potato dish was the one big relief until dessert. The two small desserts were fantastic and the bright flavors were more than welcome. Together as a meal however, the salt accumulation was overpowering and decreasingly enjoyable.  By the end, my tongue was nearly raw from all the salt and our tastebuds were pretty bored of mushrooms (and we love mushrooms). One dessert would have been nice as a palette cleanser mid-meal (though I'd rather have more ingredient variety and less salt overall as well). For the price, I was disappointed as we were really looking forward to it and it's rare to be able splurge on an experience like this. Overall, appreciate what the chef is doing here but would not recommend the winter menu.

This is the kind of place I can only recommend if you 1. Are down to drop some serious coin and 2. Truly love food, are delighted by pomp and presentation. Price aside--Eleven Madison Park is an experience. As a self proclaimed Meat Queen, I can honestly say that I've never been so satisfied with a meal that contained zero meat. All the dishes tasty and insanely presented. Went here for my buddy's bday and it was definitely a night we won't forget. The sommelier was particularly lovely, one of the highlights was for sure just talking to him, hearing him describe different wines / their history.

I loved visiting Eleven Madison and truly enjoyed the experience the most! We went for our anniversary dinner and were immediately greeted by the host who knew it was our anniversary too. I know the menu has changed since moving to all plant-based vegan and I'm vegetarian myself and enjoyed almost every dish but overall, the experience was EXCPETIONAL and so very unique and enjoyable.

Out of the dishes, my favorites were the Onion tea to start (super delicious) King Oyster Mushrooms, the Turnip with white sweet potatoes and wasabi, and their warm, crisp bread!

The servers and service was all impeccable and hands-down the best experience I've ever had at a restaurant. Our server answered all questions about all our wine selections and dishes and most of their food is locally sourced. They also give back to the local NYC communities which is amazing! I enjoyed almost every dish but I can see the food not appealing to all, especially meat lovers or those less adventurous. However, personally, it was a 5-star experience and we had the most memorable evening. We even left with a goodie bag that has a keepsake printout of our menu wishing us a happy anniversary and a homemade local granola.

Love all the attention to the fine detail!!

I have been here a back in 2018 before they became plant based, and came back recently to try out the new menu. Both times had been amazing. 
Service was always great, nothing pretentious. We all know that Eleven Madison Park has mastered the omnivore dishes such as foie gras, lobster, and duck. But I did not know what to expect this time since they have gone completely plant based, and I was really impressed and surprised by the dishes and their presentation. 
The dinner consisted of many different kind of mushrooms, and you can see the creativity by the different preparation of it. A lot of dishes had Asian cuisine influence as well. The preparation and flavor of the dishes were really diverse. Even though everything was vegan there were smokiness, earthiness and deep umami flavor. It was also amazing to learn about new ingredients that I didn't know before such as Tonburi - a land caviar. 
The vegan croissant rolls were my favorite as  they were light and fluffy and buttery, and the vegan sunflower butter that came with the croissants was creamy and rich. 
My friend also ordered Manhattan and the staff made the cocktail by our table with a Manhattan Cart, which was fun to watch. And of course, the wine list was incredible.

Excellent service and amazing preparations.  I didn't know the restaurant was plant-based until I was seated at the table.  The presentation was great, but some plates were a little too spicy or too onion-y.  Still, overall it was worth the time.

I feel bad leaving a three star review - because of the chef's incredible attention to detail, kindness to animals and charitable nature, as well as the restaurant staff's impeccable service, and lovely atmosphere - but boy was I disappointed in the food.  I am definitely a carnivore, not vegan by any means, and I just couldn't appreciate the vegan dishes.  I'm not a fan of tofu.  I'm not a fan of the caviar-wanna be vegan substance we were served.  Wasn't a fan of the celery root that tasted like a tamale.  I recently went to per se and had delicious wagyu.  Just before that went to Le Bernadin and had the most delicious fish dishes you can imagine.   Sadly, I didn't enjoy any dish I had at Eleven Madison Park, except the bread.  To me, the food was definitely not worth the price tag, and I wouldn't return unless the restaurant goes back to the pre-vegan days.

It's a great place. A bit precious, but that comes with the territory. Those who live and work in NY, this is a spot that makes this city special. The strange thing is that while I recall the food being good, I remember more wait staff pouring the wine and cleaning the tip with their fingers. Not sure what that is, some sort an "organic" ritual? I don't know, but being used to the wine dribble being dealt with by a quick swipe of a napkin, I guess a new thing?

Still love the place though. But philistine as I am, I remember the experience of going to this place than the actual food.

Uppity, pretentious, and extremely bland soulless food. This place is like the hermes of luxury goods and everyone goes here for the brand. Hence, all the reviewers who constantly name drops, lmao. As if we care who/what/where you dined with that one time in France with your fancy wine. The other reviews here are just as obnoxious as the entire staff and honestly it only makes for a great social media or braggy experience at best. "Oh my boyfriend -insert random name here- took me to the BEST place to eat over priced duck. 5 stars". 

I have never in my life felt so underwhelmed and uncomfortable at a Michelin restaurant. I generally don't post anything if it's a fine experience but this restaurant in particular is just... way too tasteless. 

Honestly folks, I understand that this place was made to impress and make others jealous when you post your tiny dessert. But it is not a justifiable experience. Rather take my $1,500 and fly to bora bora to eat fresh caught lobster.

I mean, just WOW! My husband took me here for my 30th birthday and I was so impressed! We were greeted by the host who was very welcoming! They make sure they know you before you even enter the place. Every person we met inside the restaurant greeted me for my birthday! Everyone is just so nice! The service was also phenomenal! 

Let's talk food! Normally, at a place with tasting menus with multiple courses the food is not enough or is just that - for "tasting" but here, the food was actually filling and very much enough! I wont give away the menu exactly with pictures because I feel the surprise element behind every dish was the true essence of the experience. We had 3 courses of appetizers, 2 mains and 2 desserts and every course was more flavorful than the other. Each dish was super unique and just a burst of flavor in your mouth. I am totally in awe of the food here. 

They even gave us breakfast for the next day which kept taking me back there for days! (ofcourse I was devouring the breakfast for as long as I could!)   They also gave me a special customized birthday chocolate! 

Overall, I would definitely recommend spending your special day with Eleven Madison! I will go again soon!

After my experience with the customer service side of this restaurant, I do NOT support them in the slightest. Yelp does not let me leave 0 stars...

End result: Eleven Madison Park gleefully collects $1,400 from me while ultimately offering no option to refund or reschedule our reservation, despite Covid limiting our ability to travel (from out of state) or attend the reservation.

A few weeks ago my friends and I made reservations. Having been vegetarian/vegan for nearly 10 years, we were very excited to try the menu. While it had received mixed reviews, including one scathing piece from the New York Times, we are generally very supportive of the mission to expand vegan cuising into the echelons of fine dining, and we were eager to see what they had to offer.

Two of us were flying in from Seattle, WA and two from Austin, TX for a work conference in NYC. Unfortunately, 3 of our group caught Covid and were no longer allowed to fly or attend our reservation at the resaurant.

I'm not sure where all of the earnings from this restaurant go, but I can promise you that they are not invested in advancing their customer service competencies and policies.

They refused to fully refund our money, at best offering a 50%. They said l they could rebook the reservation once within the very next month as long as I knew my exact future reservation date. That wasn't the least bit helpful as it would require that the four of us immediately fly cross-country back to NYC, while hardly having had enough time to recover from Covid.

I begged and pleaded over with them over multiple phone calls to give me a 12-month period to rebook (similar to many other establishments), or to issue a complete refund. Truthfully I would have settled for 6 months or even 3 months

They were intractible on all of these points.

I asked them to see if they could fill from their waitlist. They said that the moment they would try to do that, I also be negating my option of rescheduling the reservation altogether.

I asked them how likely they would be to be able to fill from their waitlist? They said they had no idea, and that it was really 100% on me to roll the dice.

I asked if they would try to fill from the wait list, and if this didn't work, let me know so that I could make some attempt to reschedule. They refused, citing that it was not their job to make this kind of effort.

They would not even offer enough flexibility to fill the original four-person reservation with 2x two-person reservations rather than 1x four-person reservation.

Every step of the way they were obstinant and accommodating in only the most superficial sense.

While restaurants like this can have a bit of a snobbish reputation, I'd really never directly experienced it myself -- on the contrary, I've found that similarly positioned restaurants prioritize the experience of the customer above their own operational conveneniences. Logically, they reason that this is a meaningful investment for anybody, and that they should step up to be accommodating in service of this virtue.

Not Eleven Madison Park. I highly recommend that they get their heads out of their you know whats and get to work on building a customer service program commensurate with the prices they're pedaling.

To affirm the end result: They have $1,400 from me, and I have no recourse to either obtain a refund or try their food.

I guess I can take solace in knowing that the New York Times didn't think too much of the menu, but still I'd like to get my money back.

Buyer beware.

It was a let down. This wasn't the experience we were expecting after spending the kind of money we spent. The man who checked us in seemed kind of racist. I guess they're not liking the increase in non-white folks with their transition to vegetables. The service felt very rushed. Wine pairing was ok. Wine from Greece was awful. The only good thing was food. It was innovative and delicious. With rest of the experience gone wrong, I'm not sure if it's worth it just for food.

While the experience was extraordinary both times I've had the Eleven Madison Park tasting menus, both omnivore in 2012 and Plant Based in 2022, there is no doubt the food was more enjoying, interesting, and satisfying in this latest incarnation...and there was another pleasant surprise, too.

What was consistently remarkable both times was the theater/pageantry.  And they do a lot of fun things at the table, without it being too gimmicky--great example was the box they brought to the table to cook(?) the tofu in, right on our table.  The table side Manhattan cocktail cart is another element I love.  (The Brooklyn iterations of the Manhattans were awesome; I think I enjoyed the Brooklyn Heights more, but the Carroll Gardens was also outstanding.)  

Service was very good, but not great.  Last night, everyone was super attentive without being overbearing.  And very nice, with no elements of snootiness.  But the descriptions of the food were confusing and I think bumbled in a few cases.  I think the scripts need work and the presenters needed more practice.  But this didn't take away much from the overall experience.

The food was a major improvement over my previous visit.  One of the things that stands out most about my previous visit was the duck, which was definitively below average for duck I have eaten previously...and I thought that was reflective of the food in general.  It wasn't bad, it was just mediocre, and fell far below expectations for quality.

Now I may be biased towards the new menu, because I enjoy vegetables more than the average person, and also more unusual preparations, but I simply thought the food was more flavorful.  Any while I couldn't say necessarily more interesting--some of the old preps, like the tableside carrot tartare, were so fun--the food seemed elevated and more elegant.  And there was something I had never tried before, Tonburi seeds, which were just incredible.

Other highlights?  Well, everything was really outstanding, but the Tofu, Tonburi, and Celery Root Tamale were all favorites.  Easier to call out what didn't rise to the same level: the parsnip popsicle didn't work for me and the if anything was a disappointment, and felt like trying to hard, it was the bread and butter service...I was hoping for a fresh, crusty roll and some outstanding olive oil. 

Important to note that we left perfectly full too.  Not stuffed, but not hungry.  Though you could be stuffed if you ate faster; we were at our table about 4 and a half hours!  We did see other people move through the menu more quickly.

The other thing that seemed like an improvement, the aforementioned pleasant surprise, was the wine by the glass menu.  On my last visit, I found the selections a little unapproachable, and the prices even more so!  I thought the glasses were much more reasonable priced this time...it's nice not to feel gouged on wine when paying for a big ticket dinner.  

Whereas when I last went to EMP I had no intention of returning, I expect that I will go back probably in the next year; ideally to enjoy another season of the tasting menu!

PS-I was a little apprehensive about Peter Wells' "Daniel Humm does strange things to vegetables" New York Times review.  That absolutely wasn't the case last night.

Lucky me!!! As a beyond generous thank you for helping me get a job, a dear friend took me to Eleven Madison Park to celebrate.  I had been to the old incarnations of Eleven Madison Park, even dating back to the Danny Meyer days, and the master piece theater of Daniel Hume.  Fast forward to a post pandemic world, I became plant based and I was dying to try the new WFPB Eleven Mad.   Now here's the positives... The service was unbelievable.  So many plates, so many dishes, so much art and so much care in every dish.  I LOVED this part of the meal.  In a world where service has gone down the toilet, Eleven Madison is at the height of delivering incredible service and incredible artistry to plant based food.  

I am definitely going to bring back the boyfriend here who is WFPB, but I'm afraid those carnivores out there aren't going to see the incredible intricacy in creating these dishes and to the point of one of servers... He's not WFPB but its way more labor intensive than the former restaurant.  I also don't know if it was the season. But our meal generally lacked color.  It was a lot of beige and neutrals and less lively than I would like to see in a plant based meal. When the novelty wears off of trying Eleven Madison Park, I am keep my fingers crossed that people will still think that this restaurant deserves the crown of one of  NY's few 3 Michelin stars.

The review is to their bar menu, so the experience could be different than their full experience.

The food was just ok and nothing that I'd like to try again.  The steak was not cooked up to the standard of a 3-star restaurant.

Let's start out with the best part of the restaurant. THE SERVICE IS PHENOMENAL! I felt like an emperor being treated by the court eunuchs. If this was a service only review they would get five stars. The maître d' was very polite and helpful. The chef came out and explained the first course and the waiters explained everything else. They even gave us a gift bag with the menu and some granola. We paid $220 per person which is very fair for a three Michelin star. No alcohol, but the bar room seating is very nice. Molecular gastronomy lives up to its reputation and the food captured certain fallacies that are hard to replicate. There is a YouTube video where Eleven Madison advertises that they provided a dirty water hot dog to someone who asked for one. I did email the maître d' before we went there and asked for a bagel. They didn't provide it, but that could've been a one time thing. It isn't a big deal all things considered. What is a big deal is the vegan menu. The chef de cuisine boasts that they can provide three Michelin star quality with a vegan menu. Maybe for a vegan palate this is true, but for normal palates this is not. The taste of the seeds and truffles where very nice. But the potatoes left a lot to be desired. My friend said he could get better potatoes at McDonald's. This is slightly exaggerated, but molecular gastronomy should allow them to bring out the unami of the potatoes. Furthermore, the mushrooms over powered the flavors of the food and they should balance the flavors better. I feel going back to old menu, but allow them to have a five star review.

I know people had concerns regarding this being a completely plant based establishment and I am going to tell you forget about it! This place was phenomenal! It has a very classic old luxury feel from the moment you walk in. Everyone is so hospitable from the greeter to the hostess to the waiters and sommelier. There were like 11 courses I think. Yes, the portions are small but it's a tasting menu and with all those courses you need to have room to finish! With each course you keep wanting more! Each item is so flavorful it's like a party in your mouth. Trust me, the flavors and textures are so well crafted you won't miss meat for second. They have an incredible drink selection and a bartender that can make craft cocktails just based on flavors and spirits. The way the servers walk through also is like a well coordinated dance. I have to give a shout out to Brandon from PA, who took care of us and did a fabulous job! He was very attentive and incredibly knowledge about the menu and the alcohols. And at the very end they had a little gift for us which had a personalized message! So if you haven't tried it you absolutely must!

For years now the wife and I have always wanted to come to Eleven Madison so when we finally planned a trip to NYC last year, we immediately booked a reservation.  One disappointment was that we didn't realize the tasting menu had changed to a all vegetarian menu.  Once we did realize this fact, unfortunately we were not able to cancel.  Although food and service was good, we just didn't feel as fulfilled  as we normally would with this type of meal.   In addition my wife is allergic to coconut and melons and the restaurant was able to accommodate but it appeared that by eliminating this one ingredient it did take away from the richness of some of the dishes.  Once again, not the restaurants fault, just one of the factors that diminished her dining experience.  Overall we were impressed with the artistry of a vegetarian tasting menu which highlighted and showcased unique ingredients that you normally wouldnt get in a tasting menu but just didnt think this was the  right menu for us, we love our seafood.

I feel scammed. Nobody gives 3 Michelin stars for this oversalted overpriced multicourse meal. Every single dish was either heavily oversalted or just simply not eatable. Deserts were uneatable too ... made with salt. We have managed to drink a few large bottles of water just to get away from that saltiness. People who read this, don't go there. Pass this message to everyone. Stay away from that place. Horrible experience

Service 5 stars, food less so. 
The environment is tastefully decorated and airy. Great suggestions on champagne(s) and particularly the matching wine. Impressed by the promptness, accuracy and being awaited on with our respective coats on our way out. The only complain is sharing a single half squash by the three of us, while watching a single customer on another table having his own - same portion (size, shape, color) as ours! and that's our favorite dish...

We had a lovely experience. Service was great, despite the lag between dishes but everyone was very attentive, professional and friendly. Som was fantastic and really connected each wine option to the dish and was very informative and knowledgeable about each pour. Decor is beautiful and the restaurant is elegant-- make sure to look up and check out the balloon on the ceiling. Now the food, that's the reason for a 4 v 5 star, while I did enjoy trying the variety of options from dish to dish, I did find some ingredients repetitive. I think adding in some more earthy vegetables with ingredient twists and removing some of the Asian flare almost each course offers , will really boost this to a 5 star plant based spot. Otherwise, we enjoyed ourselves and would go back when the menu switches up again.

One of the most beautiful dining rooms in the city. The bar is superb; bartenders are kind and very friendly. The new vegetarian menu did not disappoint for sure, but I have to say I did miss the duck and the foie dishes.

One of the ultimate dining experiences. The food was AMAZING. The service was IMPECCABLE. The entire staff top to bottom deserves applause. Of course, the shining star here are the complex and dynamic vegan dishes. Each course is an adventure. Complements to the chef.

Sadly giving 3 stars to match Michelin. My first experience at EMP was absolutely mind blowing in May of 2019. I was smitten by the level of service, their attention to detail, and their efforts to make our evening as fun as possible. Matching our vibe and trying to make the evening grand. The food was incredible, intricate, and delicious.

On my revisit in September of 2021 I was let down. The staff was rushed, seemed confused, and maybe inattentive. The new menu was a resounding disappointment with the table. Visually appealing, sure, but just bland, or not in some cases not delicious. 

I left somewhat shocked and hope that these were just growing pains from coming out of hibernation and with the new menu.

The wine list is still incredible, but very high markups.

Visited for the bar tasting menu on December 2nd. Really this place is a 4.5 star but not quite five stars, mainly because of the food. 

Service is excellent and all the staff is very knowledgeable and has the whole aurora of the restaurant on them. The whole experience was fun, interior being super aesthetically pleasing. 

Starting off with the first course being the matsutake, if you ever had congee, this tasted like that. Very heavy on the umami flavor, daishi stock included. Strong asian influence in the dish considering the ginger. 

Golden beet was refreshing alternative in between before and whats to come. Also again, the daishi flavor comes back in, but it has a tangy taste and the layers grapefruit and beet makes it appetizing. 

Next the Tonburi, throws off the caviar vibe. Very creamy, and it was served with some pumpkin naan. 

Next it was a warm soup Kohlrabi, with tofu and white truffle slices on it. Another daishi flavored stock. Quite salty for my taste and the sesame tofu was definitely an interesting texture. 

Next we had the cabbage dish that drifted away from the asian theme and sort of thrown in the middle eastern direction mimicking the falafel taste. 

Last was the dessert grape, all 3 was a different texture which helped ended the meal with a seasonal note. 

Missing half a star for me since the flavors in the first few dishes were kind of repetitive. However, throughly enjoyed the use of seasonal vegetables in all the dishes. Thank you for having us!
My husband took us here for our date night, this restaurant will make you feel special. The food and presentation is out of this world..... 5 stars easily!

Yumm vegan Thanksgiving! Maybe there will be a tasting notes souvenir booklet the next year, but until then, I have to say we loved every plate and bite of the multi-course vegan tribute. Lol. There were a lot of mushrooms and pumpkin....and maybe I ordered a mixed pear drink....anyways happy Thanksgiving! I'd love to see more plant based protein included next year (if you guys don't end up sticking with the meat based menu...). Ommm.
This restaurant needs no introduction with all its Michelin stars.  I wanted to give big thanks to the sommelier, who was very friendly and helpful, and made our meal so much more special

I really wanted to love this restaurant.  There were memorable courses including the best Gnocchi I have ever tasted (may my Italian grandmother forgive me) light as air with shaved white truffles (of course shaved white truffles in anything makes the dish special).  

Unfortunately many of the dishes and especially desserts were uninspired.  Outside of the deserts nothing was sub par, but little was outstanding.  

And I found the service lacking.  The waiter took our first drink order. (The Manhattan cart was fun).  Then no one asked if we were interested in wine pairings or the non-alcoholic pairing, which I wanted to order but by the time I got someone's attention we were into our third course.

We did go on Thanksgiving day and the menu certainly reflected the occasion.  But there was very little that I wouldn't be able to very nearly replicate in my own vegan kitchen.  Maybe it was just the day, but despite wanting to love this restaurant, I'd have to give it a miss.

When I compare this to the vegetable menu at the venerable Charlie Trotters in its finest period this was nowhere near the experience.  Sophisticated vegetarian/ vegan meals are absolutely possible.  Eleven Madison Park has some work to do and since I love vegetable based meals, I hope they manage to get it right.

This all new plant based (all plant menu) will deter some folks. I welcome this because most tasting menus require you eat all the meats and in this day and age that's not so hip to the earth anymore. Realizing that, Eleven Madison has changed their menu to focus on elevating the plants they curate with care.

My favorite part of this is that they tend to truffle up everything. This is almost as good as when I went to an all truffle based restaurant in Rome and indulged in pasta and everything truffled. The con of the plant based tasting menu is that some of the options are not so desirable. Example: their obsession with this cabbage dish (which comes inside a ceramic pot that looks like the Chiquita banana woman's headdress). They serve the cabbage like they're about to carve a hunk of animal meat, on a rolling cart with the fun of smashing into the headdress to reveal...cabbage. The joy of smashing ceramic counterbalanced by the disappointment of a cabbage main.

Despite the cabbage everything else was quite scrumptious and flavorful to a degree. I know for a fact a meat heavy person will most likely hate this meal. I also know that you really are missing out if you are allergic to mushrooms or nuts. I would abstain from shelling out a couple $$$ for this type of meal because I honestly don't know what you're going to eat! 

There is so much to learn about, from land caviar to rare mushrooms. I went for my birthday and even without I think the staff is well trained to cater to your dining experience. They have a style of coming out of the kitchen that seems almost Broadway-esque. They're definitely pros. And the finishing touch of a take home gift is so nice.

Pleasantly surprised by the vegan options at EMP's dinner. The key is coming with zero expectations. Loved the texture of the seed substitute caviar. Flavors were a bit monotonous throughout the courses, mostly "Asian inspired", Japanese adjacent products like vegetarian dashi. Was not a fan of the falafel. But still worth a try. Service, of course, is top notch and atmosphere is intimate without being overbearing. Would come again when there's a menu change.

Something I don't do is read reviews before I write one but after my experience at EMP I had to.  I ego made me think I was the only special person in the world.  But that is how I felt last night.

I have a few pictures.  But they don't do it justice.  The food is like artwork and the flavor is up for interpretation based on your pallet.  So unless you are one of the many personalities in my head read other reviews but try EMP anyway.  

I want to talk about the service.  Just the experience they make you feel about being there.  

I was with a few people and whispered to someone what I was eating.  And a waiter, I don't think mine came by and not only told me what it was, and what was everything they used to make this wonderful dish.  But he explained how the foraged the mushrooms and how unique they were to this dish and the importance of the texture.  Insanely brilliant, but his hearing was impossibly great.  

The overwhelming, very complex and impressive wine list comes with what I can only image is the person that invented grapes.  The explanations and the time they took to tell us everything we needed to know was as if the rest of the restaurant was populated by cardboard cutouts of people that were just there to make me feel like this was a busy place.  

But to top it off, the coat check girl would would not take a tip.  Gave her my ticket, which was interesting in itself. Not paper but some soft material I found myself touching most of the night.   But made sure my jacket was on and pulled her hand away when I tried to give her a tip.  You would think it was only a dollar by her reaction.  I only had a $10.  She said we don't do that here.  What???

As I walked home and thought of a restaurant without meat, being this full, and having this type of service, I can see why the price point is where it is at.  Yes it is expensive.  But it is fair and worthy of 5 stars.

What sets EMP apart from the other 3-Michelin star restaurants in NYC is that despite its grandeur, it's actually a really warm and welcoming environment!  Of note, you do not need dress for the opera here.  Although I would not show up in shorts and a t-shirt, jackets for men are not required, which is incredibly refreshing for a restaurant of EMP's caliber.  But if you're like me, dinner at EMP is not an everyday occurrence and dressing up for the occasion is part of the fun.  So feel free to dress to the nines if it moves you!

From the moment you set foot inside, you are met with smiles and warm greetings by all of the staff.  We were asked to sit briefly in the small lounge area by the front doors while they prepped our table, and then led to a larger-than-expected table for 2 people, which I loved because it gave us a bit of distance from the patrons on either side of us.  Multiple waitstaff members checked in on us during the meal, including a lovely woman who took us to see the kitchen.

The food and cocktails were very, very delicious.  I am not a vegetarian, and I left feeling very satisfied with my meal.  My favorite dish was the tonburi seed "caviar" and roast squash - the perfect balance of sweet and savory, and beautifully presented!  Also, at the end of your meal, you're given a small gift to take home (we each got a container of their housemade granola, and my friend also got some chocolates bc it was his birthday).  Lovely!
Did not meat expectations. Many better plant based meals in the city and for a price of almost $400 a plate I would not recommend. They have a lot of work to do to return to what they once were.

I finally went to try their new all plant based, vegan menu.

TL;DR: If you're not vegan, it's not worth it. If you're vegan, it's also not worth it.
