There wasn't a bad bite, and some were really good, but others I would never serve at a fine dining restaurant. There was a lot of repetition in the flavor palate, and in any case, the price can't be justified.


For $365 we got:
Mushroom pine tea - Strong unique mushroom flavors. A great start. I've never tasted some a strong mushroom tea/broth.

Mushroom salad - Nothing special

Mushroom tart - The best dish on the menu. Crispy perfect tart base, with a strong mushroom cream and flakes. I wish I could just get this throughout the night.

Matsutake rice porridge - The rice porridge by itself is very nice, and I enjoyed the matsutake bites. The ginger flavor was overbearing.

Croissants and sunflower butter - the croissants themselves were fantastic. I made sure to ask for them throughout the meal. The butter, even to my vegan friends, albeit pretty, was subpar to other vegan butters.

Golden beets - Very light beet dish, with, you guessed it, more ginger. 

Squash, with plenty of Tonburi (land caviar), pieces of naan, and vegan Kohlrabi labne - Again, Eleven Madison Park shows that they know their breads. The naan is great. The labne too btw, and I don't even like labne usually. Now for the tonburi and squash: The tonburi is fun, and of course oven baked squash is delicious, but your can just as well make one at home - somewhat of an Eyal Shani move.

Celery root taco - A fun presentation with celery root, turning it into a taco with small condiments on the side. 

Cabbage baked in clay, with pistachios and mint - Aside from the show of breaking the clay, after all said and done, this is baked cabbage with nuts (premium nuts, sure). A weird entree if I ever had one.

Desserts:
Pear with Sarsaparilla - Such a fun bite! Obviously only if you're a fan of sarsaparilla (root beer flavor if you never tried it).

Grape with coconut kulfi - you get 3 little balls with different textures and flavors. I remember one being better than the others, but overall I've had way better vegan desserts.

Sesame chocolate pretzel - Doesn't pass the "make it yourself" test. Guaranteed, take some pretzels, cover them with dark chocolate, and voila, you'll have a better dessert.

Sorry Eleven Madison Park, but this dinner should have cost less than a third of what it did.

I would give it 3.5 stars in its current state. The whole vegetable menu needs some work I would say. I wish had gone before it turned vegan as I'm sure it would have been spectacular. 

We had high hopes from a 3 star Michelin restaurant that was once ranked no 1 in the world. It was one of the main reasons for our trip to NY and my wife had wanted to go for a long time. Managed to snag a late reservation. The service was excellent as expected, however could also have been better compared to some 3 star restaurants I've been to. The vegetable based dishes were good for the most part some of were great. However nothing really mind blowing. 

The ones that were not so great - bread and sunflower oil butter. Both bread and butter tasted a bit weird, did not really go well together. Also the final dish and also the most complex- multi layer cabbage cooked in a reclaimed clay encasement. Very creative dish but also heavy tasting and sort of like falafel, which both my wife and I don't really like. My wife did not finish this. 

I think the whole vegetable menu needs some work to make it perfect.

We got last minute reservations here in July.  Each course was so perfectly planned and presented.   The rolls were actually one of my favorite parts, definitely ask for extra.  And the dosa course with the pine nut cream was also great.  The service was a little stilted, but generally really good as well.  This place was on my list of places to try for a long time, but once they went vegan, I really made it a priority to go.  I think the work they're doing is amazing. If you get the chance to go, definitely do.

Was really excited for this meal as a long-time vegetarian after the announcement that EMP went plant-based. It was terrible, not just in the context of one's expectations for a 3 Michelin star restaurant, but terrible compared to any regular 'ole meal. 

It was boring, repetitive (half the dishes are mushroom) and they were so focused on a dish being fancy and trying to not make someone feel meat was missing, that they forgot to make it actually taste good. The first 3-4 courses were basically salty mushroom broth. The only dish where you thought "wow, that's insane" was a pear dessert they brought out. 

Service was awesome, but explanation of dishes was lackluster and muffled. 

We hoped the Pete Wells review would be wrong or at worst, dramatic, since we already had the reservation, but it was extremely accurate. Do not go here- not because of the almost $1,000 price tag per couple after drinks ... it's that the food was so terrible I couldn't even eat the mushy tofu dish at a 3 Michelin star restaurant. 

If you want actual delicious vegetarian food, go literally anywhere else with a veggie forward menu - Dirt Candy, Avante Garden, 232 Bleecker, Shukette, Ladybird,  etc.

This review is based off of my wife's and I's experience at this restaurant from our dinner back on December 19, 2014. The staff or manager at this restaurant may or may not presently work here, as a considerable time has passed. This review is mainly being written as a result of a recent realization after speaking with friends about their dining adventures, what they've experienced here at EMP, and thoughts/critics shared about this establishment. I wrote a great review about our experience back in 2014, but  deleted it and I'm now replacing it with this review. 

It was a long time since we dined at this restaurant, but I still vividly remember the details. After reading countless reviews, and hearing about the respect Eleven Madison Park has in the culinary world, my wife and I decided to make a reservation and were extremely blessed to land one in a short span of time. 

Mind you; I'm not writing this review to slander this restaurant, and have nothing personal against the staff or the manager that served us. I am writing this as a direct recollection of my experience. Personally, I am glad they survived the pandemic and changed their direction towards veganism, which I believe is the sustainable, long-term approach to dining in an age where we will probably all perish from our own climate destroying greed and impatience. 

It was a fun, festive, beautiful Christmas season in NY, and my wife and I were extremely grateful to have the opportunity to dine here. We were seated by our server, Cody. He had a great, cheerful, and enthusiastic personality. Upon being seated, we were shown the menu option: a card with four icons representing a different type of protein. The protein you choose dictates the course of your meal. Neat! 

My wife saw someone else's dish being served, and asked Cody what that dish was, mentioning it looked really delicious. Cody's response to us was, "No no no no...that's cheating! We don't do that here." We weren't really sure if he was joking or not, but after a couple of seconds, we realized he wasn't. I understood that fine dining establishments have their standards, but this was questionably excessive, however, we decided not to make an issue with this, and stuck with the plan and picked our proteins without complaint.

I will fast forward to the moment in our experience during this night in 2014 that has now (keyword, now) left my wife and I enraged about our dinner.

Dessert time. We were served lemon meringue. Upon digging into the lemon meringue, we discovered a hair baked inside its center. Of all the irrational weaknesses the human brain may contain, my wife's weakness is hair inside of food. We quietly waved Cody over to share our discovery. He was visibly shocked at how this could have happened, and brought the manager to our table in a prompt and concise manner. The manager, whose name I can't remember, was approximately 5'10", medium in stature, had neatly trimmed salt & pepper facial hair, wore glasses, and wore a suit with a blue shirt underneath. 

The manager calmly listened to our complaint regarding the hair. His behavior was professional, but had an air of condescension and slight impatience. He apologized about the hair and informed us the meal was going to be compensated on behalf of the restaurant. I told the manager that that was unnecessary. He looked at me with a slight glare of "You're not gonna finagle your way out of a free meal!" and informed me that it was only my wife's meal that was going to be compensated for. 

We received the bill. I paid it. It was close to four-digit territory, but not quite. The bottle of Cab I purchased was approximately $150.00. If you know the per-person dining price of this restaurant, and you're still reading this, you know where I'm going. 

Fast forward to today. We shared our experience with a few of our friends (who have been to EMP a number of times) last weekend. It was brought to us by our friends that the manager who "compensated" half of our bill never actually did so. On top of that, (unanimously determined by our fellow friends in the food service industry [Hillstone Group]), if a manager offers to compensate a meal for a bad experience, who in the hell only comps half the meal? And on top of that on top, a Michelin starred restaurant of all places? 

I did my research and looked up dining prices from back then. It was apparent the manger, although offering us a "50% off the bill" gesture, never did so. Recollecting his behavior, I would not be surprised if he assumed we planted the hair inside the meringue in order to score a free meal. The treatment at this restaurant always somewhat bothered me, but now, I'm pretty upset. 

I know the hiring process for an establishment such as this must be arduous, and I know managers can make mistakes here and there. We're all human and no one is perfect, but this experience we've had falls far below that.

A long standing recipient of 3 Michelin Stars, Eleven Madison Park is widely recognized as one of the best restaurants in the world. The stunning interior offers unbeatable views of Madison Square Park as you enjoy your multi-course tasting. The cuisine can be categorized as New American, and as of this year, is entirely vegan. 

During the pandemic, chef Daniel Humm decided that his animal-heavy menu staples were unsustainable, and that the future of fine dining is plant based. After being closed for 14 months, Eleven Madison Park re-opened in June 2021 with a very different menu. No signature duck, no caviar, no foie gras. What you can expect now is 10 courses, made primarily of vegetables, priced at $335 per person. 

Reservations become available at 9am EST on the first of every month, for the following month. For example, on October 1st, all of November will be made available. They generally sell out within 10 seconds (seriously), so be ready the moment they are released. I recommend creating a Tock account beforehand to save time at checkout. 

Upon arrival, we were warmly greeted, and asked to present our vaccine cards. As of September 2021, patrons are required to be fully vaccinated to dine here. I appreciated this, and felt safe throughout the evening. It should also be noted that every dinner purchased at EMP provides five meals to food-insecure New Yorkers. 

We were not up for a full wine pairing, but ordered a few perfectly paired glasses, on the sommelier's recommendation. I was dazzled by the creative cocktail list, whose drinks are named after vegetables. I opted for "Carrot", an exotic shaken mix of Caribbean rum, Batavia Arrack, mezcal, hazelnut orgeat, lime, and cinnamon. It tasted like a sophisticated version of a Zombie, but somehow smelled like fresh carrot. Incredible. 

Nearly every dish throughout the 3 hour meal was delicious, and thoughtful in concept and execution. The Tea with Lemon Verbena was water-thin yet deeply savory, tasting of layers of herbs. Heirloom tomatoes were bursting with flavor in what appeared to be a simple salad, but was so much more. Delicate Yellow Tomato Dosas were served with a variety of unique sauces. 

Tonburi, an edible seed resembling caviar, was served as such, with blinis and tofu creme fraiche. While I appreciated the creativity, it was disappointing to eat something that looked like caviar, but did not taste as good. Additionally, the laminated bread rolls were impressive, but I disliked the sunflower seed butter, which did not melt well, and had a bitter aftertaste. 

Fortunately, the main courses made up for it. I loved the nuanced textures in the obviously labor intensive Cucumber with Melon and Smoked Daikon. Minutely chopped cucumber and melon are layered atop avocado cream, and studded with smoky daikon. The Eggplant with Tomato and Coriander was the best preparation of eggplant I have ever consumed. 

The Beet with Horseradish and Herbs arrived with a table side presentation involving breaking a ceramic pot to reveal beets, which have been dehydrated, then rehydrated, smoked, cured, and treated over the course of three days to achieve a meat-like texture. Wrapped in fermented greens and topped with a red wine jus, this dish was simply outstanding. 

The dessert courses were simple, yet satisfying. Creamy slices of charentais sat atop a bed of ice, topped with tiny cubes of smoked melon, to start. Next, a Blueberry Semifreddo with Elderflower made from coconut yogurt concealed soft bites of mochi beneath its frozen surface. To conclude, a Sesame Chocolate Pretzel was artfully hung alongside a chilled vessel of sweet vermouth.

Overall, a memorable, one of a kind experience. My omnivorous fiancé enjoyed the meal just as much as I did. Whether or not you are vegan or vegetarian, I highly recommend trying the new Eleven Madison Park.

The food exceeded all expectations and I've been vegan for three years now. Really proud of the direction the restaurant is going in food wise. Some of the courses I couldn't even eat because it tasted just like meat!!! My carnivore husband happily devoured every bit for me. 

Issues arose when it came to service and consistency. Some courses took 10 to 15 minutes between each, while others took 30 to 40 minutes between courses. Empty, dirty dishes were left on our table for 15 minutes at a time. It seemed like the servers were still learning while on the job. 


We did the wine pairing with the meal as well and they accidentally charged us for the $375 wine pairing instead of the $185 pairing, which is an insanely expensive mistake.

FIrst time at EMP and obviously had high standards.

The place had great service and the chef was kind enough to come meet us. 

The reason for the lower rating is mainly for the food. Although the quality of the ingredients was good, I found several dishes too salty. Most of the items were cold foods, and more than half of them had mushrooms. Dessert was nice but it was just a few balls. Nothing like Per Se for example, where it looks very artistic with a bigger variety. Also, this was a looong meal (we were there for four hours). I was getting sleepy lol.

Of course, I still recommend if you've never tried EMP before.

My God! That should be the review but I will go on...

From the moment we entered the space to the moment we left it, we felt special... welcomed, from the Maitre d' to the corps of servers, runners, hosts - a ballet of service that was breathtaking to witness. The courses were stunning. Being vegan, we get a little tired of vegetables, and to be honest, we were hoping for some kind of new protein or carb that might fill us up for once. But this was a celebration of vegetables and it did not disappoint on any level. I have never tasted a broth so delicious as the first-course tomato broda. The layers of flavors... I can still go back there in my mind. I will...forever. The moment we were taken back to the kitchen to have a cocktail while watching the well-oiled machine that is Eleven Madison Park, was unexpected and made us feel like celebrities. The Sommelier, Brady, took us on a wine journey to be remembered - we loved his style, his manner. In fact, everyone who spoke to us was down-to-earth - not stuffy or pretentious. Money well spent. Can't wait to do it in another season.

Visited in Sept 2021 and had the vegan menu. Impressive food and drinks, great service, but overall we found the experience underwhelming and not a good value. 

Pros: The food is good, but not craveable. The dishes are made in a unique way that is impressive, beautiful craftsmanship. Cocktails were awesome, among the best in the city. 

Cons: Booking is a terrible pain. Without meat it left us feeling like something was lacking. It's really expensive and doesn't feel like you get your money's worth.

I can't even begin to describe how great an experience I had from this restaurant. I was a little reluctant at first when I found out that they're only serving plant based food. But that hesitation went away from the moment they served me their first plate. How can you even create such delicious foods by using only vegetables and plant based ingredients? Mind blown. I highly recommend this place! It was a truly fantastic experience and I would go again in a heart beat if I ever visit NY again, and lucky enough to get a reservation!

Vegan menu is very one note and poorly conceived, at least the summer menu. They kept coming back to the same flavors, which was overbearing acid and salt. Yet somehow also tried to suggest it was a celebration of veggies. But how does that make sense when you are overpowering the veggies with the same acrid flavor. Dessert was banging though and the cocktails are pretty good.

We had an amazing time. It's one thing to have great food, but it's another thing entirely to have a culinary experience. After a lucky break getting reservations, my friends and I enjoyed a belated birthday dinner here and had some crazy interesting food that was both full of flavor and also totally unique from anything we've had before -- tomato tea, grilled squash, smoked beets, etc. 

If you're concerned about the vegan menu in any way, don't be -- the food is great, coming from a hardcore carnivore, and you won't regret a visit to one of the best restaurants in the world doing its very best to give you a great evening to remember.

I recently went for my third EMP experience, the first two being pre-COVID.  The service remains as good as it gets.  The presentations of the plates were all stunning.  But unfortunately, the vegan food itself ranges from just ok ... to very unpleasant.  Our party of four left feeling unfulfilled, and ripped off.

I am a huge foodie and had long heard amazing reviews of Eleven Madison Park, however, as someone who does not eat animals, the menu was not my cup of tea.  All that changed post-COVID when the chef decided to go plant-based.  Literally all my friends blew up my phone when the news came out so I somehow managed to finagle myself a reservation (it's hard and the wait can be really, really long so do this faaaar in advance) and it was everything I had hoped for and more.  One of my favorite things was the melding of different types of cuisines from around the globe into the best of each one, celebrating the beauty of the complex, yet simple, flavors of fruits, vegetables and grains.  None of the dishes tries to be meat; instead they celebrated the incredible delectableness of the fruit, veggie, herb, spice, grain, etc.  The only one that I thought was a bit "meat-y" was the beet - the multi-process cooking the beets went through is too much for me to describe here, however, they end up thick, meaty, smoking with flavor and absolutely incredible.  I would be remiss if I did not also give a shout out to the fabulous cocktail menu and the yummy bread with sunflower seed vegan butter.  How joyful to see the epitome of luxurious dining is now ethical, sustainable and compassionate without losing any of its decadence!

first time here to try the new vegan menu and wow, it knocked me off my feet it was so incredible. the tomato tea was just the jolt my taste buds needed, as was everything else! the cucumber with smoked daikon tasted so intricately flavorful and refreshing. i was fully not prepared for such an amazing dinner and impeccable hospitality. the menu was inspiring and fresh. looking forward to my next food adventure here!

What can I say, what a beautiful, creative journey. I was truly blown away by the amazing experience. I had waited over 1.5 years to go to a 3-Michelin star restaurant in NYC to celebrate a milestone occasion. When I heard Chef Humm was taking Eleven Madison completely plant-based, there was no other option for me as a vegetarian. We went in mid/late August 2021 for the summer menu. The meal was to die for, I especially appreciated techniques and world cuisines that were incorporated into our meal (like the mini tomato-filled dosas and pine nut chutney - yay India!). I presumed the place would be super stuffy, given high-class clientele who can afford these meals, but the staff and most guests seemed very down-to-Earth and the service was superb, everyone was kind. Loved that we left with some treats as well - a bag with a signature tin containing the details of our menu and blueberry granola, again in a signature, reusable container. So cute & sweet! Chef Humm even comes out and rounds all the tables and says hello to all the guests - he really knows how to #makeitnice! I hope I can come back one day and try a winter vegan menu! Thank you to Chef Humm & everyone at Eleven Madison for making the night super "nice," (especially for the bold choice of going vegan and helping our environment & future)!

I had dinner at 11 with my two good vegan friends in august '21! What a beautiful and memorable event. From ambiance to service to each and every dish we were served everything exceeded our expectations. Since becoming vegan I had stopped going to fine dining establishments because in the event Plantbased dishes are available they often felt like an afterthought. 
Chef Humm delivers more than beautiful executed dishes. He brings us hope. Hope that this planet can indeed be a better place. Fine dining at eleven Madison has been elevated to a new level.

If you enjoy food, you're curious about how they can transform ingredients into culinary wonders, and if you want to have an absolutely fantastic night - go here.

There's no doubt why Eleven Madison Park is one of the best restaurants in the world. We were fortunate to get a reservation when they opened up at 9am on the 1st of the month. This is one of my NY bucket list items and I'm so glad we came here to celebrate an anniversary.

We already wanted to go but when the restaurant went fully plant based, that just shot my curiosity through the roof. I personally believe in the ability to elevate plant-based dishes to fine dining, but was really curious and skeptical as to how they would execute.

And execute they did. From the first course to the last, we enjoyed every bite, every scent, every texture, and every sight we saw. You get to see the different sides to an ingredient, from a tomato infused tea to salad to dosa. The meal was light and refreshing and then slowly becomes savoury and decadent. The sunflower butter with miso and bread was an absolute highlight!! It felt like a ramen combined with decadent baked goods. We were offered seconds and even thirds (I controlled myself and only got seconds, and then ate the rest of my partner's serving).

My partner got the wine pairing and thoroughly enjoyed every sip and every story. I did a non-alcoholic pairing and really enjoyed the fruit and then tea based drinks as the courses got heavier. There's a lot of volume in the non-alcoholic pairings that it was hard to finish though.

We got a brief but great kitchen tour where one of the Maitre D's helped us learn a bit more about the history of the restaurant. Service in general is impeccable. The only nit that I could give is that because it's so efficient that it felt a rushed - but that could also easily be how long we were taking to eat since we were savouring every course at a much slower pace than others who came at the same time.

I'm so glad we got to experience the Summer Tasting menu and would absolutely come back again when they rotate their menu. Even two days after the dinner, I'm riding in a high of just how wonderful it was and recommending it to all my friends. Hi

A success. Returning to EMP for its plant-based menu was such a pleasure. Humm's return to the fine dining scene is a smashing delight and a beacon to all those who hope to embrace plant-based lifestyles. The menu, we were told, would be ever changing, seasonal and locally sourced. The summer menu was a concoction of all things light and refreshing - the verbena tea that starts the meal blows your senses. I won't give away more than that. The atmosphere now felt friendlier, more casual and the banter with servers was informative and fun. Oh what joy!

The new menu is absolutely delicious, and the service is top notch. In comparison to Alinea, I found EMP to be much more laid back (in a good way). Interactions with the staff were fun and engaging. We also tried two different cocktails, and both were made exactly to our taste.

Was there last night for a friend's 40th. Menu was inventive and while not a fan of certain vegetables -- tomatoes, in particular -- I could still appreciate the story Daniel Humm and his staff were trying to tell with each dish (even the ones that didn't appeal to me). Only criticism: drinks a tad slow to arrive. But service on the whole was fantastic and ambience was just right. Highly recommend.
Taste-wise it's probably 4 stars, but given the hype and notoriety, I'm bumping it down a star since I left a little disappointed.

Plant-based fine dining! Eleven Madison Park has unfortunately set the bar EXTREMELY high for not only dining in general but for sure plant-based dining. Every single dish was delicious, so thought out and so creative. The staff makes you feel like you are the only person in the restaurant. We got a last minute walkthrough of the kitchen and it was impeccable, so zen. I can't say enough about our experience, I only know that we will be back SOON. For anyone that enjoys dining as a whole experience, look nowhere else than Eleven Madison Park.

This experience was so much fun and everything tasted delicious. Each meal was unique and each course did a great job showcasing the featured vegetable or fruit.

I admit,  I was a skeptic. I thought that we would enjoy this treat just once in our lifetime and never again.  We were celebrating our first wedding anniversary and my husband finishing up his second comic book, DISHOOM. Despite all the accolades, I couldn't see how any meal could be worth that much. However, this was truly a Culinary Art Experience at its highest level. We spent 3 hours in bliss, lost in the moments brought to us by this meal. Imagine going to a museum and enjoying one Matisse Masterpiece after another. This experience was about admiring the beauty of the flavors provided by nature and scupted into art by Chef Humm and the Eleven Madison Park Team.

SPOILER ALERT SPOILER ALERT SPOILER ALERT
Summer 2021

*1st and 2nd Course: A Triumph of Tomatoes.*
I didn't want this to ever stop. How did Chef Humm and the EMP Team manage to capture the essence of the tomato in this Lemon Verbena Tea? This was an incredible starter, soothing to the soul on a midsummer night. The only downside to the Dosa was that I couldn't steal my husband's. The Tomato Salad with Strawberry and Shiso did a great job  highlighting the flavor profile. 

*3rd Course: A Perfect Porridge with Celtuce.*
 This was such a minimalist dish in the sense that it tasted like it only had a maximum of 5 to 7 ingredients (isn't that a trick that the best artists have... making what they showcase seem so simple and effortless when it's anything but that). This dish was one of the highlights of our day. I would be content to eat this once a day for the rest of my life. This really demonstrates that simple isn't the same as easy. 

4th Course: Peas and Tonburi
The presentation was amazing.  What was more impressive was the baby lettuce with a stripe of dressing that served a dual purpose of seasoning and decor for application of the meticulously placed heart shaped red sorrel leaves. The delicious side Pea-Miso and Almond-Lemon Paste was marbled like a Starry Night painting.  

5th Course: Cool as a Cucumber.
How did the EMP team so precisely cut the cucumbers for this dish?!? I love how each dish really highlighted the main vegetable and at the same time the natural flavor was enhanced by the what the team did. 

*Surprise Sunflower Side *
The most amazing sunflower bread you'll get...I could not believe that there was no butter in this. It was perfectly warm and moist... the outside crisp reminded me of a croissant. This was  heaven on earth. I should have said yes when they asked if I wanted seconds but I was starting to get full and wanted to properly enjoy the second half of the meal! 

6th Course: Summer Squash.
I loved the lemongrass taste of the broth and the slightly sweet flavor of little Squash Petals.  The tofu was transformed from the tofu that I have grown up with. The EMP team did a gorgeous job carving and painting a beautiful leaf on top of the meal. This dish looked beautiful. 

7th Course: Sweet Pepper Swiss Chard Taco.
This pepper mixture-fried crumble popper was delicious completely by itself but it was also fun to experiment with the various pickled toppings. I thoroughly enjoyed eating with surgical Bayonet Forceps...and now I'm going to think of this meal ever time I operate. 

8th Course: Bountiful Beet.
This was a very cool presentation including cracking a clay pot with a hammer...the beets were cooked in various ways across 3 days. 

*9th Course: Eggplant Magnum Opus*
This was the best eggplant dish I have ever had. I've been a vegetarian for many years now and I've sampled the best eggplant meals from around the world to my mom's amazing home kitchen.  This main course was definitely a highlight- from the corn grits to the flavor intense eggplant. How did Chef Humm and the EMP team create this 9th Wonder of the World? How did they infuse the eggplant and still manage to keep its skin and inside whole? I could have sworn there was even a hint of tamarind in this dish.  Everything down to the pickled radish atop the eggplant was delicious. 

*10th Course: Dynamite Desserts*
The best strawberry you'll have: infused with yogurt and thyme followed by an extremely innovative blueberry elderflower dish with a variety of flavors from tangy to salty and a variety of textures from cold ice to chewy. You end with a sesame chocolate pretzel alongside a house made sweet and bitter non-alcoholic apricot vermouth. The vermouth tastes even better as the ice (molded with the EMP logo) melts. 

We were given a cute parting gift of a "record" of the meal along with granola to take home for breakfast. 

My husband said his highlight was seeing the huge grin on my face during the entire time we were there. 

Final Summary: I thought this would be (literally) a once in a lifetime experience but I can't wait to go back.

Time to sweep up some of the reviews I failed to write during the covid-pandemic. As a preface, we only did the delivery meal here- the roast chicken dinner with a cocktail or two. We still haven't actually been to the restaurant to have the real experience.

It was pretty good. I mean a roast chicken dinner for two that costs more than $300 better be pretty good. It better be damned excellent. I'd say this one was between pretty good and excellent. We appreciated the ability to order fine dining and get it "to go" (only in NYC, by the way), but ultimately we know we way overpaid for the priviledge.

We're try to get to the restaurant soon (but not while they're doing the veggy-only thing- I would absolutely hate that), so to be continued...

After hearing about the Plant Based menu at 11 Madison Park, I decided to give this establishment another shot.  My wife has been a decade long vegan and we both enjoy high quality plant based meals.  So despite the prior experience i had there (great ambience, service and Food Theater, but not that amazing food), I was eager to give it another try.

As you will likely find out, securing  a reservation is hard for this establishment.  The monthly reservations booked out in 15 minutes or so after opening the website, so you have to be quick!  

The ambience wasn't what i remembered.  The restaurant seemed tired.  It may be that we arrived on time for a 5:45 seating and were one of the first patrons in the restaurant.  Things Definitely improved, however as the restaurant filled out.  

The service at 11 Madison Park is amazing.  It is priced to be amazing and yes it was amazing.  No complaints.

The menu was definitely innovative.  There were many different courses and they manage to pull off things that not even an accomplished home chef could do.  That's the type of meal I don't mind paying for.  The Riff on "caviar" was mind blowing.  It looked like Caviar, but was made from Chia seeds, and paired with delightful baby peas.  The dessert was also amazing.  However there were several other items that we just OK.  

My issue is that when you are paying $450/person (including a simple bottle of wine) for a meal, you should have high standards.  I have had much better, tastier plant based meals in different restaurants at much lower price points.  My issue may be that i am generally not that fan of French Cuisine, so perhaps not in the best position to judge.  However there were certain uses of Thyme, Rosemary, Smoke that overwhelmed the flavor profiles of the dishes and made them in mind not that awesome.  

My wife loved it, and I love her, so that made the evening special.  I definitely prefer the new plant based 11 Madison Park to the old version, so am bumping it up a star.  Chef Humm also paid a special visit to our table, which was amazing.  However I would prefer to return to different restaurants before I return back to 11 Madison Park.

I am absolutely blown away by EMP's new vegan menu. As an omnivore, I was worried about missing the protein, but I was not just physically satiated but also intellectually titillated. Nothing was pretending to be a plant-based version of an animal protein, yet the progression of each the ten courses still evoked the textures and flavors you expect from a more traditional tasting menu, going from lighter to heavier. Every dish was playful and whimsical, and made subtle nods to flavor profiles from other cuisines without outright appropriating them. The timing of its launch also was an ode to the seasonal produce in the summer.

1. tomato tea with lemon verbena, yellow tomato dosa, tomato salad with strawberry and shiso: The tomato tea distilled tomato soup into its mere essence - it was a clarified broth that looked nondescript but was so fragrant and tasted so pure.
2. The celtuce on broken rice porridge reminded me very much of the flavors of congee and Hainanese chicken rice - ginger, garlic, soy sauce perhaps.
3. Tonburi: Where the previous dishes were a play on flavor, this was a play on texture. We assembled the crisp and chilled baby lettuce leaves to cup tonburi seeds and the youngest of spring peas that had a caviar-like texture.
4. cucumber with melon and smoked daikon: this was probably my least favorite dish - the cucumber was very finely minced, and while I liked the chewy smoked daikon buried in the center, overall this was the most mushy and baby-food like dish to me.
5. summer squash with lemongrass and marinated tofu: this resembled a fish course in texture and flavor. There was a distinct tom yum soup flavor, probably from the lemongrass. This was one of my favorites.
6. sweet pepper with swiss chard tacos: We were served a stuffed pepper popper in a swiss chard wrap, and invited to apply toppings like pickled onion, a spicy creamy sauce, and chili crisp. It was a messy handheld dish, but I loved all of the flavors and sauces.
7. beets with horseradish and herbs: By this point we were moving onto the heavier courses. The beet was slightly dehydrated and had a candied and stiffer texture, and it was smoked and reminded me very much of a smoked ham.
8. eggplant: the final savory course was my favorite of favorites. The grilled eggplant was had a sweet, luscious, and creamy interior, with caramelized edges. These were served with sides of sugar snap peas/haricot verts and what looked like creamed corn - this is summer grilling on a plate.
9. blueberry dessert: wow, this tasted like froyo. Buried under the disc of creamy frozen yogurt, there were fresh blueberries, a scoop of blueberry sorbet, and the best part: bites of mochi. It was such a delight.
10. chocolate pretzel with apricot aperitif: The pretzel was a gluten-free sesame-based, halva-like dish, and the apricot flavors were a perfect complement to nibbling the pretzel.

Service was impeccable. The dining room felt like there were as many patrons as there were service staff, and our 3-hour meal was paced very well and no one missed a beat when guests had to leave or return to our table. Daniel Humm stopped by and said hi too.

We had the pleasure of enjoying Eleven Madison Park on Thursday evening, 6/17/21 one week into Chef Humm's new menu. In short, it was Fabulous! Service was impeccable as you would expect from a Michelin 3-star restaurant, however  the 11 course plant based meal was one for the ages. If you are fortunate to hold one of the "golden reservations", get excited for a real treat! Chef is passionate about his food, staff, guests and sustainable supply chain which shines through even in the humility he exudes during a visit to our table. He even surprised us with "inducting" my wife to the Chef's "Clean Plate Club" after a passing comment she made to a server about how much she enjoyed every course. Attention to Detail, Bravo!
I had a wonderful dinner...Can't say anything bad about this place. I'm on keto diet, but felt safe having dinner here.

they have really good gluten free options and I like the cereal and cookies they gave as a gift when we left（also gluten free). Among all the Michelin 3 star I have had before, this is still the top one. It is not too sweet or creamy, the flavor got balanced well
This place never disappoints me. Can't wait for reopening and try new plant-based menu!!

Honestly if I'm paying this much I'd expect to have bigger portions and for the waiters not to be snobby. Terrible place the food tasted good for the one bite that it was lol. And the service was shit. Definitely need to work on your service and the people who work here are just complete snobs. I sat down and these two people were laughing at my children so disrespectful to my kids because they are innocent and did nothing wrong. The people even told me that I need to tame my daughters hair in an "establishment like this". Never coming back.

Overall great.
Duck- The best
Roast chicken- 4stars
It's a little bit expensive compare to the taste of the food hhhh (just my thought)
Amazing vegan food can't wait to go again when they reopen!! Beautiful decor and service as well. Worth the splurge in my humble opinion.

Eleven Madison Park--if you ever get a chance to try it, don't hesitate!!!

While it is no longer recognized as the best restaurant in the United States, it's quality and creativity has not suffered a single bit. During COVID, takeaway options are available and well-packed. Can't wait to experience Eleven Madison Park again in person. 10/10!!!!!

The Taj Mahal of dining in New York City. I've been closely following Danny Meyer and Chef Daniel Humm  on social media and after seeing his Netflix show, we knew we had to come!

The ceilings are like the Sistine chapel (with some exaggeration). There's no need to dissect the pricing, because no one comes to Eleven Madison Park for a value packed affordable meal. This type of dining is excellent if you've just accomplished a small or large goal or just had a milestone. 

You are able to select the course you would like to participate in. What I loved was that we never felt rushed and the staff was there to celebrate with us, not rush us out, cough cough Carbone! The dining experience at Eleven Madison Park is unforgettable. 

Feel free to snap away at your food, but I was out with clients, so I couldn't really go all foodporn here.

EMP offers Valentine's Day take out in 2021 due to the pandemic. With every Valentine's Day dinner sold, they can donate 10 meals to Rethink, a non profit organization, to help the people in need.  It is praiseworthy.  You can now also order their roast chicken dinner meals for take out on their website.

It was a mix of hits and misses - we went a couple years ago for my birthday in Feb, and maybe because it was winter the ingredients they had weren't all that interesting and the flavors felt underwhelming. What really stuck with me even to this day was how one of servers really didn't do a good job sharing the menu with us - he looked bored and was just reciting a bunch of memorized words rolling his eyes a bit as if we wouldn't care (when in fact it showed that he didn't care). Had a great time visiting the kitchen and the chef's crew though.

We went last year actually. It's expensive. I knew. But the food is  amazing, excellent and a forever wonderful dining experience. 
The decorations or atmosphere honestly is not fancy fancy by New York standard. But that may show that there focus is the food. 
I recommend it for special event especially if you all love food.

It's great to be back home. After I moved back to NY, this is my go to place. It never disappoints!. I highly recommend duck breast and chocolate mousse but pretty much everything on the menu is amazing and the service meets the expectations

I adore the small things about Eleven Madison Park. The minimalistic space contrasts incredibly against the pure creativity that is no doubt happening in the kitchen. My favorite place to spend time with an intimate group. 5/5

Some tasting menu restaurants serve you half the portions on twice the plates for three times the price, but here you can expect a beautiful meal with quality creative dishes. The staff are beyond excellent. The first time I had dinner here and it started out as just drinks, but we decided to stay for dinner when they happen to be able to accommodate us and we ended up being the last table to leave that night. They never made any attempt to rush us out in fact they gave us some great cordials once we were done. It was memorable enough to keep me coming back not just for drinks and it does not feel like Christmas without a Manhattan at EMP. 


On the top of my list for a proper indoor dining experience when we are able to again.

We ordered the pick up box for my birthday. The presentation of food is very good! However, the mushroom, pie and soup are too salty, especially the mushroom. We ended up throwing them because they are not edible! Very surprising though. I hope the chef is healthy and didn't lost taste

I think we made it to Eleven Madison Park's last dinner service before the first shutdown in March this year. Not knowing when we'd be back out again, I'm so glad that our trip to NYC ended at this iconic spot! Dinner was predictably good and had some really outstanding tastes. I wouldn't say that anything we had was avant-garde or innovative. Just a lot of crowd pleasing hits that would probably satisfy anyone who prefers a more conventional set of tastes on a prefix menu. In any case, I'm really glad we went here. Their non-alcoholic beverage menu is one of the best, and I think I ordered almost every drink on that menu!

Living in the San Francisco Bay Area with access and availability to so many Michelin restaurants including French Laundry, Meadowood, etc....Eleven Madison Park experience alone is worth a trip to NYC!

There are so many excellent reviews already.  I agree with all of them.  No need to say more.

It's a culinary and life experience!

Menu is seasonal ish. They treat you like royalty and the food is very experimental. If you enjoy the creative process of combining ingredients in an unconventional way and want to open your taste buds to a variety of choices then I recommend checking them out!

This place doesn't need my five star review but I have some extra time tonight so I'm trying to do my due diligence and write some reviews.
This is hands down one of the top few places I've ever eaten but all that says about me is that I need to do a bit more fine dining. 
I like this restaurant both for brunch and for dinner. I have been on two occasions.
Reason I would prefer the brunch over the dinner is because it was a lot of fun. Our waiters really enhanced the experience immensely. They seemed genuinely interested in our dining experience and at one point I wondered whether they were professional actors. They were all so adorable, well spoken and well groomed.
We got a tour of the kitchen which was really fun. My dinner was a lot more sophisticated which was also very nice. One of the things I remember the most is that they took our jackets and never gave us a coat check ticket. Somehow they have a system of whose jacket is whose. It's all about the details here and they got that down pat.

Came here last year for a birthday dinner and had the most amazing duck dish. We had the tasting menu but the peppercorn duck entree stole the show. It's expensive but so worth it. Usually have to book months in advance so plan ahead!

The Bread:
Before Covid-19, I had the chance to pop into Eleven Madison for lunch.
Once upon a time, the restaurant was open for lunch on Saturdays from 12 pm-2 pm.
I walked in. I sat at the bar and order a la carte. No reservation. I was given an absolutely wonderful champagne to start. This went so well with the bread I given at the start of the meal. It was a beautiful snail shape roll that tasted between a croissant and crusty soft white bread. I found out later it was a laminated dough similar to a croissant. The butter was French. The smell of the bread was intoxicating--the butter-soft and salty. The silverware was heavy and regal. I felt regal as I sipped my champagne and buttered my bun with a silver bread knife. As I touched my face to the perfectly starched linen, I thought of wanting always to have crumbs on my shirt to remind me of how real and yet surreal that experience of a warm buttered bun was.
The service was warm and approachable as that bread.
It doesn't matter what the rest of the meal was.
You really should go just for the bread.

This review is long overdue, but we had such a great time at Eleven Madison Park celebrating our 5 year wedding anniversary. I was 9 months pregnant at the time and the restaurant was so accommodating. Many of the dishes had less common ingredients/bases and it seems like they had a better idea of what I could/couldn't eat than I did (we did let them know ahead of time). We were treated so well throughout the whole experience, the staff were so welcoming, and our palettes were challenged/expanded as a result of the experience here.

This restaurant was good, but considering the price I did not think it was worth it. The ambience is great and met my expectations, and the customer service is pretty good. Overall though, I should have just saved the money on this one :(

Our last visit was February 28, 2014. Just stumbled across the menu (photos attached). 

We do hope EMP recovers and flourishes once again as it's our favorite dining experience in all of the US. They need to lead us all back from take-out hell. 

One day soon we hope to come back to NYC when this has all passed by and enjoy the gold standard for service, decor and the simple pleasure of being spoiled in the Big Apple. 

Please say it will be so!

This was the most expensive waste of money. The menu I had was just basically assembled items. Grilled bundled lettuce with snails fed mint? Why? Bagel flavored cheesecake? Another why? It was pretentiousness at its best and left me uninspired after waiting so long to eat here. I enjoyed the drinks and the dessert was ok but not enough for them to save the dinner for me.

The most unbelievable experience I've ever had thus far. Made the reservation a month in advance. Being #4 best restaurant in the world is a big deal and I was so happy to be able to experience this restaurant. From the amazing food to the Somm to the impeccable service to Claire that was super accommodating  to making this dinner experience a great one. We had the best table in house ( or at least it sure was to us ) to all the flavors. A must try experience. The goodie bag at the end is a great touch. (This was a draft on my yelp that never got posted when I thought it did- dinner was two years ago and still till this day it has been the best dinning experience we've had).

We were here to celebrate my mom's birthday and it was a memorable night. My mom is a cat lover and Chinese-speaking only. I initially requested for a Chinese-speaking staff and unfortunately they didn't have one on duties, but that didn't stop them from satisfying the customers. 

The moment we entered we were greeted with a warm welcome. They placed a birthday card with a drawing of my cat on our table and my mom received countless happy birthday throughout the night. They also prepared a translated menu for my mom so she can enjoy the full experience. Everyone received a jar of their infamous granola, tasty, at the end of the meal, and they didn't forget about my cat. They prepared a little toy box for my fur baby which I found it super sweet. 

If you are going to EMP, don't forget to use their personalized services.

I was lucky to be able to dine here this past February. One of the best meals of my life. The  potato caviar soufflé was out of this world. The service was absolute insanity. Book ahead and expect a big check. Enjoy

Ate here back in november, absolutely amazing, dinner was really long, but it went by pretty fast, because you're having fun lol, very inspired cookery with a "sense of self", like any other restaurant at this caliber

My absolute favorite restaurant in NYC.  Sadly I've lost the photos I took of the gorgeous courses I had there.  I love how much thought and care the chef puts into the meal.  Not surprised it's considered one of the best restaurants in the US (and the world).  Someone needs to build a museum dedicated to the art via the medium of food.  Hope these guys can re-emerge in the post covid world.

If you're wondering whether it's "worth the money", I just want to say, each person has a different utility function.  IMO no one can tell you if it's worth it FOR YOU.  Some people spend $$$$$ on Hamilton tickets, some spend on experiential food.  I will say for me each meal I've had here was memorable, for me, for my dining companions.  Personally I can't say the same for ANY of the other Michelin three star restaurants in NYC.  How would I price a unique experience like that?  No idea, to be completely honest.

I'll keep this simple.

If you're coming to EMP as Barbie's first Michelin-starred restaurant (e.g. a 24yo first-time Yelp Elite just stepping out into the world like a baby chick), you'll probably be blown away. You'll probably be wowed from top to bottom, left to right, and side to side by the service, decor, presentation, flavors, ingredients, etc. You'll be equally floored by the fact that they hand-selected YOU to do a tour of the kitchen, even letting you sample some new items in the works.

If you're coming to EMP as a somewhat experienced fine diner (been to a handful within the US, maybe some abroad), you'll appreciate that EMP lives up to its reputation for flawless service, creative cocktails and beautifully plated dishes. The kitchen tour will be the standout part of the experience, since few acclaimed restaurants do that.

If you're a Michelin/World's 50 Best dining veteran, EMP will satisfy but not wow. It hits all the marks but never really delivers a course worth blogging about. The plates will get their dutiful Instagram due, but those photos--along with your Yelp review--will be the only way you'll remember them five years from now. Though the kitchen tour might still stand out.

Guess which group I'm in?
Super fancy but really such an experience. The place has everything and you'll feel so decadent but in the best wayz

The general atmosphere and ambiance at eleven Madison is incredible when compared to other restaurants of the same caliber. There isn't a stuffy attitude at all and the waitstaff are all happy to help you understand the nuanced cuisine on the menu. The food itself is otherworldly and lives up to all of the hype. I enjoyed the 8-course tasting menu which included a varied selection of choice meats and vegetables melded together in an array of unique preparations. The highlight, however, was the veal which was decadent. The portion sizes also, while not that large aide in your ability to try all the foods presented to you.

This is one of the best Michelin 3 star restaurants I've ever been to. It truly deserves its title as the worlds best restaurant in 2017. Came here with on a double date and we all enjoyed every course. This caviar soufflé was the best I've ever had in my life; the sweet and savory combine perfectly in this appetizing course. This is a must-try!!

As I eat my granola from EMP, I must take a moment to give them a sincere THANK YOU. I had such a special time meeting a friend at the bar and spending the afternoon. The quality of everything is otherworldly. The drinks, the hospitality, the beauty of the restaurant. It was an experience I will always remember fondly. I'm happy that places like this exist. 

I wish they sold the granola and chocolate pretzels to take home. They were sooooooooo gooooooooood.

When people talk about Eleven Madison Park, you could think of the World 50 best Hall of Fame, 3-star Michelin, and everyone's dream restaurant to go. If you conceive this idea and dine at EMP, congratulations, you're going to be disappointed. 

I honestly expected so much more from EMP. I chose this place to celebrate my anniversary. There are two things that I love the most from EMP. 
1. Service was undoubtedly flawless. I was contacted by email to ask for some requests that I might have. I requested to have a kitchen tour, and they happily arranged that for me. When I got there, all the staff knew my partner and I were celebrating our anniversary, and this was warm-hearted. 
2. The wine list is top-notched. We ordered a bottle of Domaine du Collier 'La Charpentrie' Saumur Blanc 2015 from Loire Valley and it's amazing. Thanks to the wine sommelier for the recommendation!

Ok, so here comes the food. It was an 8-course dinner for $400+. To be honest, I couldn't recall any dish from my memory because nothing, literally NOTHING, had impressed me. I'm not saying that the flavor is bad. Instead, the flavor is well-balanced; the texture also shows the skill of the chef. The real problem is that every dish is lacking the kick that gives diners the wow moment. There is no surprise to it. The taste is without layer, and it's single-dimensional - in other words, boring. Like you're looking at an empty beautiful ceramic vase without flowers in it. 

I had been to so many different Michelin-starred restaurants before, and Eleven Madison Park might be the most overrated restaurant among the list. 

#Makeitnice? highly questionable.

Great food, great wine, great service, great companionship.
The 4K tab was well worth it.

Wow! Incredible experience from the second we walked in right up until we finished. We arrived early for our reservation, so we sat at the bar for a few minutes. I asked the bartender to make something up for me and she gave me possible the best cocktail I've ever tasted! Now, the food. It was almost indescribably good - I couldn't get enough! We started with an oyster broth reduction that was so intensely flavorful, I couldn't believe it. The next several courses were outstanding, from oysters to cured trout to braised veal... incredible. They had a beer bread pudding with cheese fondue on a later course that was maybe the best thing I've ever tasted. 

So grateful I finally got to experience this place! Deserving of their #1 reputation! Amazing service, good, and we felt so welcomed. Thank you!!

Fabulous evening in the upstairs private room with our own bartender. 
The food was perfectly prepared, incredible wine list and cocktail list. 
The service was perfection and everything went smoothly.

I went last night with my three children and out-of-town guests whom I wanted to honor with an over-the-top experience. EMP did not disappoint! The attention was exquisite from the moment we walked in the door; and at table, Laura and Rebecca handled everything with a smiling amiability that had none of the obsequiousness or pretentiousness you can find in very highfaluting restaurants. And yet, ELM meets all the highfaluting markers in the very best way: creative, delicious dishes presented gorgeously by choreographed servers. And the dishes keep coming; there were supposed to be 8 but it left like more. Oyster broth; oysters cold and hot; savory cheesecake with smoked sturgeon, caviar, and sea urchin cream; choice of how you'd like your foie gras; poached lobster tail; tofu custard with truffles, choice of duck breast or veal cheeks;  choice of desserts; cheese tarte served with beer....I think I'm forgetting a few but you get the idea. Every new course was met with  oohs, aahs, and yums by us. And then, a visit to the wine cellar and kitchen was the icing on the cake, plus gifts to take home. Wow, what I night! I highly recommend that you put EMP at the top of your list.

Would give 6 stars if I could. It truly was the best dining experience we have ever had - from the very beginning to the end. The service was outstanding!!! We sat at the bar for a cocktail before our dinner, and was immediately impressed with our bartender's knowledge (especially so during our conversation on bitters). That really set the tone for the evening. Once we were seated, our server was fantastic, our sommelier was wonderful. And the FOOD! Amazing. I have food allergies, and they accommodated everything with ease. They listened, they made us feel welcome and they truly went above and beyond in every way. If you have the opportunity to dine here...do it!

Everything and more!!! I will say, Eleven Madison Park is absolutely the most amazing culinary experience that I've ever had the honour to venture. 
It started with friendly staff welcoming us in a genuine manner. We decided to try out the bar tasting meal, which included the Caviar Benedict with Smoked Sturgeon and Ham, Brook Trout with Radish and Sesame, Lobster with Razor Clam and Sea Urchin, Duck Honey and Lavender Glazed with Cabbage and Pear, and for dessert, Pear with Caramelized White Chocolate and a Chocolate covered Pretzel. The creative presentation of the foods, the personal touches with the service, and cocktails (please try the "Yogurt"...loved it!!) !It was definitely the best I've ever had experienced. We were also surprised by Eleven Madison Park when they invited us to the kitchen, where we enjoyed watching the chefs and sous chef preparing dishes, while enjoying a treat that was specially made for two of us.
One of the finest restaurants around the globe. 
Thank you Eleven Madison Park so much for the most memorable meal experience.
We don't live in New York , but we will definitely return again.

This review is long overdue. Had reservations for my birthday and had high expectations. There were a few mediocre courses like their version of a seafood boil. However, the caviar was phenomenal - can't go wrong with caviar. Also enjoyed the duck, they seasoned it very well.

Full disclosure.  I was actually at Eleven Madison Park a couple of years ago,  before I was doing Yelp reviews but just ran across my pictures and thought I had to do it now.  Time does not change the fact that it was definitely a memorable evening!

I was there for a private party in the room upstairs that overlooks the main dining area.  We had about 40 guest and I swear it seemed like at least 20 people taking care of us.  We were offered a drink when entering the room.  After that your glass was refilled without asking unless you said no or changed what you wanted. Not sure how they kept track of everyone's choices since the first hour was a cocktail hour with everyone walking around the room.  There were several appetizers being circulated, I'd say 6 or 7. Each one better than the one before.  Scallops on a shell, pureed carrots and my favorite was a smoked sturgeon savione in an egg shell.

The meal itself was an abbreviated 6 course tasting menu. It was all great but I really enjoyed the foie gras terrine with mushrooms and grapes and the beef tenderloin roasted with beets and onion which melted in my mouth.  I couldn't wait for each dish to arrive to see the presentation.  It absolutely was a big part of the whole experience!

We received a gift box at the end which held 2 of their delicious savory black and white cookies.  

Overall an outstanding dining experience! Best I've ever had.

I been wanting to try emp for awhile because they were named number 1 restaurant. The food, atmosphere and service was top notch. Each dish was unique and delicious. Something so simple such as their bread croissant had me wanting to ask for seconds. One of their stand out dishes was their cheesecake with everything bagel seasoning top with caviar. I'm so used to eating traditional cheesecake that I enjoyed their innovative take on a savory cheesecake. The only dish that I didn't take a liking to was the beer/cheese with bread pudding and mustard . It was little heavy for me . Food proportions might look small but don't be fooled. Me and my significant other were full by the time dessert came out .At the end of the meal, they gifted us their home-made granola . They are more casual here and aren't strict about dress code . No suit jackets required.

We did the bar tasting menu and it was more than sufficient amount of food .  And the service was still amazing.  So if you don't want to spend that much on the full experience (or would just like a preview) I'd definitely recommend trying the bar tasting menu just to see.  And at the end of the night you get sent home with a little bag of goodies (granola) and the menu for the night.  Love it when restaurants do that (just had that experience at another restaurant, in Vancouver, and by far the cutest ever...  A heart shaped brioche!  Yes, it was for Valentine's.)

I went here with my husband to celebrate his birthday. Overall experience was amazing which deserves its reputation of the number 1 restaurant in the world in 2017. The service was excellent I can't say anything that I dislike. All food are great and delicious expect the dessert part (compare to the other ones I tried) But so far is the best of all other michelinstar restaurants. Highly recommended.

author.name: Flora T.
author.location: Long Island City, New York, NY

reviews.review: I couldn't get a reservation for the full tasting menu so I sat in the bar area where they serve the reduced price four course meal instead of the 8-10 course one. (Judging by the other reviews I don't feel I missed out on anything special) I went here several months ago, and sadly I cannot remember a single thing I ate, none of the dishes stood out. All that I can remember thinking was that the sauces were tasty, nothing mind blowing though. I've eaten at a number of nice restaurants in NY. Atera, definitely my vote for the best in the city though there are a number I have still yet to try, The Modern, which was superb and where I had one of the most incredible dishes I will be thinking about for years, Crown Shy, where everything was delicious and the free bread was the best I've ever eaten, even Perry Street which ludicrously does not even have a single Michelin Star and where I went for restaurant week and had a chicken dish in a sauce that completely blew my mind. Here's the thing, when you are universally praised, it certainly affects the expectations of your customers. A place with this kind of reputation should have at minimum one dish to remember, but the most memorable part was when we got up the leave all our bags and coats were waiting by the door for us, that was a first so shout out to the person running the house side!. I regret not making it to this place before they remodelled in 2017. I would like to give them another shot and go for the kitchen tour which I failed to request in advance and maybe even try the Baked Alaska

Amazing! This was the best dinner ever. 

My husband made a reservation in January for a February dinner. Reservations open January 1 for all February reservations so plan ahead! 

This was my first time going to a 3 Michelin Star restaurant so I didn't know what to expect but it truly was an incredible experience. 

Each meal was presented beautifully and explained well to us. We got the wine pairing as well and we could really tell the quality of the wines. The dishes were unique- flavors that unexpectedly worked well together and surprised us! 

The service was great as well. We walked in and our coats and bags were taken away. Whenever we needed to step out, someone would help move the table out and guide us back when we returned. 

We also got to tour the kitchen which is part of the meal experience. The staff were professional and worked so diligently. We even got a fun snack - maple syrup with apple snow ice popsicles! Yum! 

At the end of the meal - we got to take home homemade granola and key chains :) it was a nice touch to conclude the best meal!

I went here for my wedding celebration and then later for my anniversary this year.  LOVE this place. The atmosphere is perfect, and the staff provides a Japan-level quality of service. They are extremely pleasant and anticipates your needs like nowhere else I have eaten in the U.S. I love that the meal is slowly paced and you are not rushed through. Frankly, you pay so much that you really want this to last, but more than that, you want it to last because it is such an excellent dining experience. An experience, not just a meal.

We had the tasting menu and ordered a separate bottle of wine. Although it was 8 courses, they added certain items for us to try. The dishes were all expertly prepared. Some do run on the saltier side, but not over salted. I loved everything, but especially the savory cheesecake and the pretzel.  The granola parting gift was unexpected and absolutely nice touch at the end of the meal. We most definitely will return.

We have been talking about eating at this restaurant for years. We literally flew into NYC just to eat here. The experience was absolutely the most lovely I've ever had.

We had several email correspondence with the hostess and the sommelier which really showed that personal touch. From the moment we walked in, I felt like we had been given a big hug. The restaurant itself is stately and beautiful, but what was even more beautiful was the perfect choreography of all the servers. The sommelier had put aside a birthday year bottle of Diamond Creek for my friend and the sommelier of the night (someone different) chose an absolutely stunning starter bottle that complimented the Diamond Creek perfectly. We had never seen a bottle opened using hot tongs. My friend asked to keep the bottles and they even put the top portion of the bottle in a small glass case. 

We were given several food choices. The bread itself surpassed any bread I have eaten (sorry to Husk in Charleston, but EMP topped yours). All of the dishes were superb. My favorite was the beautiful foie gras pate. The presentation was perfection.

Did you know that they have three dreamweavers on staff? I didn't either. Essentially what they did for my friend was to create an art piece of a favorite deceased pet. After giving us a view of the kitchen and taking a picture next to their sign "Make it Nice", we returned to the table with a drawing of his beloved pet in a frame. We both teared up a little. It was a touching moment.

We sat and finished our wine and were given a bottle of apple brandy to sip for dessert, as well as a glass container of their homemade granola (hands off kids) and their menu presentation was in a small decorated tin. It was superbly presented.

I never want to compare experiences because they are all different. But this experience at EMP was the best I've had (I dare to say even over Per Se). It is the small details, the warm atmosphere of the servers and staff, the fluidity and ease with which the staff were able to accommodate their patrons, and of course, the amazing menu. Their saying "make it nice" is felt throughout the entire meal. I will look back on this dinner so fondly and will be bringing my husband back soon I hope!

Seriously one of the best experiences from start to finish. The ambiance, service and food are impeccable. My husband and I went to celebrate and checking our phones was a great idea! Every course melts in your mouth and the staff make you feel grand. Every detail is thought out from the ice cubes in your glass to your departure menu keepsake and take home snack.

We checked our phones so unfortunately I didn't get pictures but it made the 4.5 hour evening more special. We even got to do a kitchen tour, one of the most immaculate and staffed kitchens I've ever seen. A top dining experience and wonderful NYC staple, highly recommend coming here, you will not be disappointed and it's worth every penny!!!

This is a very belated but much-deserved Yelp review for Eleven Madison Park.  Work, travel, and forgetfulness are to blame. 

On December 6th, 2019 at 5:30 PM I entered the finest restaurant in the world, Eleven Madison Park.  I say that with confidence because in 2017 Eleven Madison Park was voted the finest restaurant in the world and I have no doubt that if the award could be given consecutively, (rules) Eleven Madison Park would be repeat champions.  Yeah--they are kind of like the New England Patriots of fine dining. 

My experience started a couple of weeks before my visit with the attentive Reservations Supervisor, Melinda.  Melinda made sure that I was all set with my reservation and locked me in.  

Upon my arrival, I was greeted at the door as if I was an old friend to the establishment.  Eleven Madison Park is known for doing a bit of intel on their guests before they arrive but it's not too overbearing.  

"Mr. Flanders, welcome to Eleven Madison Park".  Very cool. 

Because I made reservations late in the game the main dining area was totally booked.  So, I grabbed the next best thing.  Bar seating.  

I'll call bar seating the Jr. version of dining at Eleven Madison Park.  1/2 the price, and not as many courses. With that said, Eleven Madison Parks bar seating experience should be granted 3-stars on their own.  No difference in service, no difference in the quality of food, and no difference with your experience.

Immediately after being escorted to my bar table,  my Captain (Ben) appeared and began mesmerizing me with what I was about to encounter.  He smoothly informed me of the prix fixe menu and then summoned the Sommelier to my table. 

My Sommelier was not an entry-level Somm, a Certified Somm, or an Advanced Somm, nope my Sommelier was a Master Sommelier. This-blew-my-mind.  Her name was Mia and I proceeded to pepper her with every wine question I could think of.  Come on---how often does a Master Somm uncork your bottle during a dining experience. Wow!

Everything from that point on was magical.  Friends have asked me why I would spend that kind of money at a restaurant.  My reply is simple. 

Would you spend that kind of money on a Broadway show?  Dining at Eleven Madison Park is like experiencing a wonderfully choreographed Broadway musical.  

The Captain, the Somms, the Servers, Assistant Servers, the Kitchen Servers the Bartender, all working in perfect unison to put on an extraordinary show.  Oh yeah---and---you're eating out of this world food and drinking great wine during the show.

You leave a Broadway show with a memorable experience---you leave Eleven Madison Park with one as well.  

Even watching the Kitchen Servers deliver food to your table is artistry.  I still want to know how my Kitchen Server (Truman) was able to pour the sauce onto my plate from what seemed to be shoulder-distance without spilling a drop.  That's attention to detail.  

There are so many excellent superlatives that I could add regarding my amazing experience but reviews should not end up becoming War and Peace.  You'll lose the audience. I cannot wait to come back to the Big Apple and do it again at Eleven Madison Park.  Next time though I'm going for the full dining experience.

One of the most memorable dining experiences ever.  Creatively prepared, wonderfully executed and oh so damn delicious without being ponderous.  On top of the food, the service was stellar.  I suspect that the menu changes somewhat regularly but here's a brief rundown of our 5 course tasting menu.

The first course was 11MP's homage to eggs Benedict, a poached quail egg served in a caviar tin, with the egg nestled in a ring of aspic dotted with ham, with a dollop of smoked caviar and topped with a Hollandaise foam.  Accompanied by quarter-sized toasted English muffins, it was in a word ... wow!

I selected the foie gras studded with pumpkin seeds as my second course; my wife opted for the brook trout with radish and sesame.  The combination of the foie gras and the pumpkin seeds was an expected marriage of fatty goodness and nutty umami-ness (is that even a word?).  It was undeniably rich.  The brook trout was equally good but completely different; the fish was lightly smoked and the radish had been marinated with what we thought was ginger juice.  It was light and airy.  The contrast between the flavor directions of the two dishes couldn't have been better; they were like yin to the other's yang - equal but opposite.    

Lobster with razor clam and sea urchin was another flavor and texture surprise.  Razor clams with their salty crunchy bite provided a perfect counter point to the sweetness of the poached lobster tail and the richness of the sea urchin sauce provided a delicate liaison that tied everything together.

Duck breast with honey and lavender and veal cheeks with onion and mustard were each superlative and completely different in flavor and texture.  Both were excellent. The desserts of pear with caramelized white chocolate and maple ice cream with sweet potato and chestnuts were the perfect end to the meal. (But, you can't forget the homemade chocolate pretzel!)   

Like the amplifiers in the movie Spinal Tap, when all others go up to 10, this goes to 11, because 11 is more than 10.  Go to 11 at least once.

The best restaurant for anything. The dinner was like 5 hrs, but every millisecond was worth the time. The prices could nave gone down a bit, but the rest is good. BEST RESTURANT EVER FOOD IS THE BEST

Our meal was just plain dreamy at Eleven Madison Park. We did the smaller menu for lunch, but it was still a looooong, beautiful lunch and definitely felt like a good value. There were several small touches along the way (including individual menus and housemade granola at the end), and we were stuffed. The duck was by far the best dish, and I am dying to come back already!

When my Uncle took me here during his recent visit over the holidays I was pretty thrilled. Legenedary restaurant I have always wanted to try but have been trepidatious about spending my own money to come here. The feedback I've gotten about this restaurant has always been very, very good or very, very bad.  The good feedback always comes from restaurant amateurs that don't really know what actually makes a great restaurant. These people are wowed by tableside stuff and gimmicks.  The very, very bad feedback is always from my friends and colleagues in the industry that know what good food is. These guys are more likely to be found at an unknown neighborhood joint or a dirty ethnic spot off the beaten path. Well, I knew better the entire time.  Although everything was pretty and tasty here, it was so pedestrian it hurts. Its like they are relying on magic tricks here.  Bait and switch. Deceive us with gimmicks and fancy aesthetics so we dont really realize that the food just isnt that good... and expensive as hell.  Lobster dish was well-cooked but so freaking simple and boring I'm shocked it made it on the menu of a restaurant of this caliber. Again, I think the strategy is to deceive with pretty presentation.  Worked on my uncle who was blown away by the silly spiral on the plate.  Desserts hardly qualify as desserts and are unfulfilling. Oh yes, my coffee also took 20 minutes to arrive. I had already finished my not dessert dessert by this point.  The best part about the meal? That my uncle paid the bill so it was basically free

I hardly ever write reviews unless it's for getting a coupon or discount. This is not the case here. Despite what I heard about the service from friends, I had an amazing night at EMP and want to express my gratitude since they do not accept tips at the restaurant. We went there to  celebrate my boyfriend's birthday and the staff planned an extraordinarily unforgettable night for us. The service was truly above and beyond. My boyfriend was pleasantly  surprised and had a wonderful time.

For being worlds best restaurant I expected more. Not sure if my party wants to write their experience  but I have been there before couple of times and this was my least favorite.  My party understands  and knows they are 11 Madison, I expected more also our server did her thing which was expected but, can I say her other helper over shadowed and towered her! Andrew J, I think Jenson, he listened and was really sweet. As a minority we felt heard by Andrew, thiS place has a certain stature and it was nice for what it was.!  I gave it a 4 star because this time it wasn't as memorable as previous trips, could be due already having their title and not caring as much. Be prepared to spend about 500$ per person and could have had the same experience as another location such as River Cafe or Marea.

We went to Eleven Madison Park for my  dad's birthday. We had a great time! The dinner took almost 4 hours, but it really feels more like dinner and a show than just dinner. The waiters have a presentation whether it be the preparation or the explanation of the dish every time they serve you. 

Although I did not find each and every dish as tasty as I might expect for such a high price point, I think you're also paying for the impeccable service and performance. The service was the best of any high-end restaurant I've been too, they literallly walked me all the way to the bathroom door just to ensure I found my way. They offered a woman who looked cold a pashmina to keep warm!

Pretty much universally, our favorite dish was the foie gras. The oysters came in warm and cold preparations and were also amazing. Amazingly, neither of these foods are typically something I love!
