The croissant-like bread was great as were the desserts. I ordered the sweet potato brown sugar and my boyfriend the chocolate and we shared both. I found the dessert courses to be a little small though. At the end they serve a delicious white chocolate pretzel but only 1 per person, which I thought was a tad strange as most places serve an array of petit fours.

We had a tour of the pristine kitchen which felt special and is not an option at most restaurants - the night really felt like a performance! Unlike some other high-end restaurants (ex. Gramercy Tavern and Le Bernardin), I do not think I will return for a while (given the prices and the food is not the type I crave often), but we were all glad we chose it!

Was brought here for my birthday, the food was amazing. But the highlight of my night was the attention and service I got from Andrew J. He wasn't the server. But delivered in my point of view better service. Attentive and always with a gracious smile. Made me feel very welcomed. Olivia was also extremely friendly and gave my party and  I a kitchen tour. Purpose of my review I expect more from the server but overall an awesome experience.

The staff at EMP invited us to the kitchen, which was a pleasant surprise , where we enjoyed watching their beautiful harmonious rhythm of cooking /preparing dishes , while enjoying a cake that was specially made for two of us. What an experience. The ambiance, artful presentation of the foods, the service, & delicious cocktails. 
One of the finest restaurants around the globe. 
Thank you for coordinating this fun evening for us, Kelsey, the wonderful concierge staff at EMP.  
We will return.

Eleven Madison Park has always been about nuance and subtlety. Lost in the accolades and sky high expectations is an actual sense of how difficult it is to pull a meal like this off. And to deliver an experience that validates its claim as 2017's world's best restaurant is borderline impossible.

At face value, it might seem underwhelming. Sure, the classic Daniel Humm dishes are sure to excite. But when you're expecting transcendence across the board, there's a chance you might be disappointed.

Except if you take a step back. Much is actually pretty transcendent. Actually, very transcendent. But not in the ways you'd expect. Leek souffle topped with caviar was a masterclass of souffle texture. Shit, if you've ever tried to make even a decent souffle, you know what I mean. Great caviar is great caviar (and the caviar is indeed great), but the real star is the souffle itself.

The same rules apply across the board. Oysters were insanely fresh, but the chowder served alongside was the star of the show. Seared fois gras is always incredible, but the pickled radish rounded the dish out. The uni foam is what highlighted the perfect poach of the lobster. The always present truffle dish, in this case a roasted mushroom with truffle glaze and cream, was more a showcase of roasted mushroom finesse. Humm's duck needs no description of its greatness so I won't delve in. One bite and you'll know what I mean. And the cheese course's highlight was the pickled onions that added a subtle yet necessary scallion-esque bite.

This was my second time at EMP. And I continue to love it. It honestly makes me think about my own cooking more than any other restaurant I've been to.  It is sometimes difficult to approach food of this caliber. Especially with the aforementioned expectations. And I get it.  But take a few moments to soak it in.  

Approachability matters.  I think this is often lost in restaurants like this. Eleven Madison gives a rare impression that showcases food that seems possible to make on your own. But then you realize you can't. In the best way.  It combines familiar flavors in innovative ways that makes you reinterpret your foundational food knowledge and makes what you think what is possible.  But you have to take a minute to digest it.  Take that minute.  I promise you its worth it.

It's been over a year since I attended a small wedding reception at this location and it was truly unforgettable, thanks to the care and attention and thoughtfulness lavished on the wedding party by the staff. The decor and beautiful details placed in the room, overlooking the main floor of the restaurant, were tasteful and elegant and perfectly in tune with the style of the couple. The food was truly amazing (in the full sense of the word!); every course was a lovely surprise and absolutely delicious. The servers anticipated every guests' need and they were very attentive to some of the elder guests present in the room. The pace of the dinner was perfect, from appetizers to the wedding cake. I hope to return for the tasting menu (or for anything, really!). I wanted to thank the staff for making my sister and brother-in-law so happy, and for delivering in such a beautiful way in every expectation.

Location: very convenient, the restaurant is on the first floor. 

Decor: plain, but love the high ceiling, seating is comfortable 

Food: what can I said, everything exceed my expectations. I did the dinner 8 course tasting menu, my favorite dish are the golden oyster mushroom with truffle sauce, that was the best. The golden oyster mushroom was grown by A farm in PA only for Eleven Madison. 

Foie Gra, serve both cold and hot. The hot want one was tender juicy and flavorful. The cold one we got was decorating with nuts outside,
Like a hedgehog, I think that is very creative,. 

Service was first class. 

Price: it is Michelin 3 Star and one of the best restaurant in the world, it is pricey but can't complaint. 

Reservation: hard to get reservation, and paid when you make the reservation.

Another absolutely fabulous, near perfect meal at Eleven Madison.  I was sitting with superstar Chef Masa (one of the best chefs in the world), and we both gave it a ten out of ten.  Virtually perfect execution (the food was way up to the quality of wines we had) and perfect service.  It's one of the top restaurants in the world currently firing on all cylinders.  When I get back to Los Angeles I will post menu and photos at www.acmefoodwine.com

Overcooked rubbery lobster, unimaginative simple dishes with a basic combination of Protein + sauce (kombu, mushroom, etc.). My husband's duck was doused in cumin and you could barely taste the duck. Food was unfortunately extremely expected, had zero innovation, boring and underwhelming. I had to give away my main course, dessert, and overly sweet chocolate covered pretzel.  Last time we were here we had the best meal of our lives and this time we couldn't believe how bad everything was. Only highlight we enjoyed were the hot and cold oysters. 

Service was mind boggling bad too. I am a messy eater and breadcrumbs sat on the table for 20m. They gave us the wrong check for our wine at the end of the evening, undercharging us until we corrected them without much of an apology. To make matters worse, they then handed me back an umbrella that belonged to someone else, and I had describe mine before they could find it -"it's Burberry, long, and has viewing holes". Not sure how they managed to misplace that. 

Emp used to care and work hard for its food and service. Now it's a cash cow milking establishment resting on quality from years ago and undeserved stars. I hope they improve because they used to be sensational.

3 of us went last night. DO NOT RECOMMEND. Waste of time and money. The food was actually sub par. Desserts were...not even real desserts. This place pretends to be all that...the only people truly enjoying this is the owners who are most definitely laughing every day that they've fooled so many people. It's not special. Food was actually not even good. We didn't enjoy a single course. And we eat out at least 2-3x a week. Room lacked any warmth and felt like you were eating in the lobby of a building. Food presentation was waaaay better than the actual taste. Staff didn't know not to interrupt conversations in order to clear crumbs. Everyone was on auto pilot and following a rehearsed script. No one smiled. My overall assessment? I felt like if you're someone who doesn't get out much, you could be fooled into thinking this is an amazing place. If you like good food and know great service, you're going to be scratching your head. #truth

Have wanted to eat here since reading about how creative the menu was. I think we've come 2 years too late. Nothing creative here. 
Made a reservation on Tock at 10am for 7:30 same day. 
 We paid $729.46 (670 plus $59.46 in tax) for 2 people. 
The room is nice but bare. No flowers on the table. Just a box that we wondered about. The server asked if we wanted to put our cell phones in the box to get away from distractions. If we opted to do so she would remove the box from the table. What????  We said no thank you.  Hahahaha. 
The front of house staff  need to relax a bit.  Being friendly and smiling costs nothing. When you approach a table, make eye contact, smile and say good evening or hello. Take notes from the runners.  Really do.  We both thought the staff should be as casual as the restaurants' dress code. We observed many diners wearing jeans.  Thankfully the gentleman clearing our dishes and refilling our water glasses smiled the entire evening.  
There is a 10 course tasting menu. The time between each course is 20 minutes which is way too long.  
Of the ten courses, I really liked 4. I thought 1 was fair. I didn't like 5. 
Hot and cold oysters  Very good. 
 Potato  souffle with caviar. Fantastic course. 
Seared fois gras. Fair
Poached lobster. Excellent
Oyster mushroom was very good. Loved the presentation. 
Duck.  He loved it. I didn't. Waited (you guessed it) 20 minutes for the swapped out sea bass. The fish was cooked perfectly. I didn't like the sauce.  
We chose to skip the cheese course and were offered  an extra dessert. We waited 20 minutes for the first dessert. Then we waited for the second dessert (20 minutes). When we saw we would be waiting 20 minutes for the chocolate pretzel (chocolate shaped like a pretzel, not a chocolate covered pretzel) we asked the server to bring it immediately.......with the check.  We didn't want to wait 20 minutes for the check. 
If you want to get a tour of the kitchen be sure to put in your request when you make your reservation. We didnt know that so we were refused one. 
Glad we tried EMP.

Why 4 stars? Frankly I wish I could give 3.5. On the 31st we dined at Per Se, a Thomas Keller property. On the 2nd we dined at Daniel. Neither ever missed a beat. I am completely baffled by the catastrophe that plagues 11 Madison Park. Yes the oysters are placed on relatively hot stones and although hot, it did not scorch our tongues and were delicious. The service is crisp and relatively professional. The floor managers, who walk about had to inform the wait staff that we had dirty dishes, and needed removal. The timing between dishes was also haphazard, sometimes slow other times brought to the table while dishes needed removing. We witnessed the pressing of the linen and everyone was relatively attentive. Things went relatively well, in spite of missteps, however the attitudinal response by sommelier Alex (apologies if spelling is off) when I informed her that a madeira wine was not to our liking, was totally unbecoming a restaurant of this caliber. A floor manager heard our displeasure and was very attentive and seemed genuinely interested. Our other complaint was the presentation of the staff. Most were dressed with pressed shirts and groomed hair. However this was not standard throughout the staff. Some had poor grooming, others with wrinkled shirts. It was a hodgepodge unbecoming a former best in world restaurant. Perhaps the owners should visit Per Se and Daniel and get a reset. As for the food itself it was very good, however compared to Daniel and Per Se it was second-tier. The food was good but certainly not great.

This has honestly been the best restaurant I have ever been to. We did the bar tasting menu and it was perfect for my husband and I.

It took a minute for us to find the actual entrance, but that was part of the fun. We got into the restaurant and I was a bit devastated at first, because they couldn't find our reservation. I was SO happy when they found it with my confirmation information. The hostesses were fantastic and so sweet. We sat down and had THE BEST meal of our lives.

My menu:
*Caviar, soufflé with clam leek and potato 10/10
*Foie Gras, marinated with maple and apple 10/10
*Lobster, with pumpkin and citrus 10/10
*Duck, honey and lavender glazed with shiitake mushroom 10/10
*Beer & Cheese, with bread pudding and mustard 10/10 (this was my favorite. I was not expecting a savory dessert but honestly this was MY perfect ending to a perfect meal)

I hope to visit again. This was a fantastic experience.

We went here for our anniversary. Generally, the experience was great. The tasting menu was delicate and delicious. The kitchen tour is educated and enjoyable. However, there is one thing we felt a little uncomfortable. The  wait between each course was way too long sometimes even as long as half an hour. It took us 4 hours for one meal. There were less than 10 courses in all. We had several tasting menu before but never had that long. It was a little pitty we were not satisfied.
I'm attending a dinner here with family as a Christmas gift. The service here as top notch and the food is absolutely to die for. I would love to come back soon.

Definitely one of the top dining experiences. Several things are still some of my favorite dishes to date (especially that black truffle tea). 

The reserve wine pairing, although extremely expensive, was definitely worth it in my book. 

One knock on them is service was great up until the very end, where it took us 15-20 minutes to get a cappuccino after ordering it (while not waiting for anything else).. For a place with a reputation like this, you expect service to be on it a little better.

I couldn't have picked a better place to celebrate graduation than at Eleven Madison Park! It was truly a wonderful experience!!! 

We had the 9 course tasting menu and everything was beyond tasty! After watching the "7 days out" episode on Netflix, I was so excited to try their famous aged duck! I definitely savored that honey and lavender glazed duck. Everything was just so tasty! Great balanced flavors and very unique spins on dishes. I LOVED their celebration of NYC; amazing cheesecake with smoked sturgeon and caviar on an everything bagel crust. And their customized drinks were beyond delicious! I typically don't like Old Fashions, but the drink they customized for my boyfriend was so good that I almost wanted to trade drinks! 

The service and meticulous attention to detail really made this one of my most special dining experiences! When my brother made the reservation, he had mentioned we were coming to celebrate graduation. When we arrived everyone congratulated me and they had a beautiful card at our table. At the end of the meal, we got to tour the kitchen where the magic happens and the rows and rows of their aged ducks. 

But that's not all!!! At the end of the meal, there were some surprise goodies to top off the night! We really enjoyed the chocolate covered pretzels and Laird's apple brandy. They even gave us a little goodie box to take some extra pretzels home in addition to the cute little jar of blueberry coconut granola. 

This was definitely one of my favorite dining experiences! Highly recommend if you ever get the chance to celebrate a special occasion in NY!

All Michelin-starred restaurants have tasty food. But not all of them have great service. And not all of them have enough food portion size to fill you. Eleven Madison Park has all three -- great food, great service, and generous enough portions to leave satisfyingly filled. I love the decor and the vaulted ceiling. Every dish is memorable, from the first course consisting of oysters two ways -- raw on ice, and warm on hot stones -- to the grilled wild mushrooms, the venison Wellington with Foie gras center, the signature duck breast with crackling crispy skin, the lobster with razor clams, the caviar soufflé, to the variety of house-made soft cocktails, etc., etc. I have gone to many Michelin-starred restaurant. Eleven Madison Park is one of the few that I will be returning to.

Man, I sure do miss the days when my coworker and I used her corporate credit card to go to these kinds of posh, high-end restaurants and spent hundreds and hundreds of dollars on our meals in the name of "research." I knew the food was going to be amazing but I was suprised and beyond thrilled with our treatment. Yes we were dropping cash on the table like it was going out of style but the staff at EMP were some of the nicest and most personable staff I have ever encountered! Everything felt personalized and as if it was the extra mile. We had full on conversations and laughed repeatedly! Our amazing sommelier is even brought out a pack of EMP edition Cards Against Humanity for us to have after overhearing my conversation with my colleague about the game. How often does one say that after visiting a fancy-pants restaurant? 

Four hours later, we were stuffed beyond belief but had to pretend we didn't just willingly put ourselves into a gluttonous stupor. My favorite part of the experience was the kitchen tour we were invited to partake in. It's amazing to see the nuts and bolts of a high quality establishment. They definitely took their time with us as it was clear they loved our company... or our corporate card? Hell who cares. At the end we both got a big hug from Cody and I took my chocolate covered pretzel and black-and-white cookie to go as I could not fit anything else in my stomach.

Overall a fantastic meal and I can still remember all the happy fuzzy feelings I had during our dinner there. I would love to go back again someday for a special event whether it's with colleagues, family or friends!

No pictures because I put my phone in the box.  I really recommend it to fully enjoy the company of who you're dining with and the experience of being here.  And you get a special treat when the box is returned!  The food is superb, service A+. If you're unsure what to drink (and the drinks menu is extensive) definitely take up their recommendations.  Tour the kitchen when offered, you get another treat there!  My favorites were the lobster, creamed kale, beer & cheese bread pudding, the Ginger cocktail, and the Laird's apple brandy. And the bread! They'll bring more to the table too.  Ahhhh!

I'm sorry to say I'm in the "what am I missing" category.  My husband and I are self proclaimed foodies who seek exceptional dining experiences wherever we travel.  Perhaps the expectations were too high? The space is beautiful, the acoustics allow for easy conversation, and the service was outstanding.  The presentation of the meal started out with a BANG with gift boxes full of the first course delights.  From there on however, the meal itself was lacking.  My husband and I like to order different things so we can try each other's dishes,and pretty much across the board, the response was "meh!"  The squid was flavorless, the lobster itself was masked by the accompanying bisque, and both the duck and the venison were tasty, but uninspired. My husband loved his granita desert, but my chocolate sesame thing was underwhelming.  Thankfully, the service was excellent, accommodating and unpretentious.  The atmosphere was minimalist, yet comfortable.  I only wish the menu and the food had lived up to the hype.  After waiting so long to finally get a reservation, it was just so disappointing.

Finally. A couple of slight misses in the dining room had me scratching my head a bit. What was I missing? This time around I tried dining at the bar, and suddenly everything clicked. It's no secret that the EMP bar has its own dining menu, including an abbreviated $175 5-course, one that now holds my regards as the finest overall meal one can have in New York.

Let's start with the cocktails, in themselves an achievement. Pricey ($20-30) but worthy, each named after a core ingredient such as Concord Grape or Ginger yet wrapped in a perfect balance of flavor.

EMP has always struck me as starkly minimal in the preparation of its dishes, and this meal was no exception. The shorter nature of the meal, however, made each element that much more memorable. Standouts included the squid (marinated in juniper, chopped and layered with a dash of garlic aioli) and a venison en croute entrée which blew me away with a sublime slow-cooked tenderness. I was absolutely convinced the meat was somehow cooked sous vide before being baked in pastry (it wasn't). The poached pear and parsnip dessert was a brilliant finish to the evening, in addition to the classic post-meal bonuses.

The reason why the bar worked for me where the dining room didn't is the drastically different level of service. In the dining room, the courses are brought out with somewhat detached fanfare, and seemingly by design a different member of staff each time. On the other hand, the bartenders add a constant and personal touch to the meal that felt missing, or at the least a passive observer to confirm that - yes - the food really is that good.

With gratuity included, $175 for the meal I had felt utterly fair. My previous visits to the dining room left me strangely unsatisfied, but I couldn't bear to write a review because I couldn't shake the feeling that I was missing something. Now, I think I finally found it.

Food was really good! We had the 7 course tasting menu. The whole experience was like watching a show - they had a fancy way of opening wine bottle. They also brought a whole marinated mushroom in front of us and told story about it and then served. It was really fun. Among all the thoughtfully presented courses, the duck breast and venison were amazing. 

However, I felt that there could be more courses in the tasting menu (compared to other top fine dining restaurants). The dessert could also be improved. Also this place does not allow any change / cancellation of reservation once you made it (even a month in advance). That made me quite unhappy because I had something on the next day and due to this strict reservation policy I have to travel super early on the next day. Anyway, the food experience really exceeded my expectation. I just wish they can change their reservation policy a bit.

Terrible menu and terrible food. Service was good. But a good service can only do so much. 

The pastry chef should be fired. The bread was too salty and the texture felt in between that of a croissant and a cream puff. It was too salty. The butter felt like cheap hydrogenated vegetable oil. The dessert - poached pear, was extremely underwhelming. 

Coming to the main course -  we had venison which was served inside a puffed pastry. The pastry was soggy and the meat itself felt raw and undercooked. 

 The only highlight was the service. Overall an experience I would like to forget. I wish they somehow magically run out of business and disappear from the face of Manhattan. Not sure how they still retain 3 Michelin stars, let alone stay in business. 

For take home souvenirs, EMP presented a caviar box with a printout of all the items we had ordered for dinner alongside a box of granola! Yes. A box of granola. Sigh. 

I won't be going back here at all.

Not my favorite three star restaurant (fat duck) but worth nothing less than five. Definitely worth a visit with people you want to make special memories with. They let us tour the kitchen where I had my super-tasting suspicion confirmed. It was a magical night. One tip: skip the signature duck. My whole table ordered it and nobody was a big fan.

Really disappointed.  Expect so much more from a restaurant billed as"one of the best in the world."   While the food was solidly good; it lacked presentation.  Even the servers seemed bored and disinterested in what they put in front of you. Many times had little of any description of what was pt in front of us.   Service was mediocre at best.  Several times had empty water glasses on table and had to wait for it to be filled.  Would expect so much more from a Michelin 3. Wouldn't you?
WB

Absolute perfection from start to finish. The experience was amazing - confirmation that this is the best restaurant in the world. I don't want to spoil any of the surprises so I won't say give a lot of detail but you know this is an incredible place, so go and you'll have an wonderful time. It's rare to be surprised by a restaurant these days and were were surprised a few times by creative dishes and presentations. Service was impeccable and that's often what pushes a restaurant into 3 Michelin Star territory.

Absolutely beautiful experience. 

The first night we went to EMP we got cocktails at the bar because we were unable to get reservations. My husband and I got several cocktails, all impeccable. His favorite was The Chestnut and mine was the Collaborative Cocktail. We are on the lookout for the best cocktail in every city we visit and he thinks he's found it in The Chestnut. So many layers of flavor, worth every penny. 

I think what made our experience the first night so incredible was our server, Katherine. She was so very attentive and sweet. She surprised us at the end with a kitchen tour and we were so grateful. 

By a crazy turn of events, we were able to get reservations and two nights later were able to return to EMP to eat at the bar (this turn of events is also thanks to EMP staff, who made even getting reservations epic). 

I'm vegan, so per usual I just expect my meal not to be so great  I was so wrong. They knew I was vegan beforehand. Every course was absolutely beautiful, I just don't even know another word for it. I'm not even a bread girl and have been dreaming about the bread every day. The salad with date paste was to die. My husbands meal was insane. 

Honestly I just don't have words for the whole experience. If you are in NY and can get reservations, run!  

Special thanks to every person who made this night so amazing. Without yalls amazing service it would have just been a nice meal. We will never forget it- 
Madison, thank you for putting in the extra work outside of work to make sure we got reservations. 
Ben, you are incredible! Service was 10/10 and we loved meeting you. Katherine, we can't thank you enough. You are clearly in your sweet spot.
Great way to celebrate a birthday. Thank you so much for everything!

I've been wanting to come here for forever and I finally had my anniversary dinner at EMP! I loved every part of the tasting, and the staff's service made the night that much more amazing. We opted to store our phones away during the meal, so we didn't get to take any photos. I also wish we could've done the kitchen tour, but maybe next time.
My expectation may be too high. I am quite disappointed. Food materials are not good enough and tastes bad. We waited for long time for each course. Look at photos, they even don't look good enough.

I had an amazing experience eating at the bar today. 
The bar is just to the side of the main dining room and not isolated so you don't feel like you are missing out at all.
The service was amazing. The 5 course tasting menu was more than enough and each and every dish was superb. 
I asked for a kitchen tour and it was really impressive. 
I was also happy to realize the tip and tax was included in the $175 for the 5 course tasting.

ONE ENCHANTED EVENING 

Celebrated Thanksgiving Dinner there with a party of six. It was a wonderful gorgeous experience.

Four course meal was truly incredible.

Setting gorgeous.

Service amazing.

EMP is one of those places you go to for a special occasion because you want to make it special. You want the people who greet you the moment you step through those revolving doors and who hold up your jackets for you by the doors when you're ready to leave. You want the staff to wish you Happy Birthday no less than 10 times throughout the meal. You want them to print custom menus for you to take home and give you a gift after dinner. You want all of that and more.

The food here is excellent. It's rich, decadent and beautifully plated. Is it worth $365 (post-tax)? No probably not. But you're paying for the whole experience - the service, the ambiance and the food. 

I wish I had read more about EMP before I came as I probably would've: (1) requested a tour of the kitchen via email, (2) put my phone in the box to get a gift of chocolate at the end (3) opted for the bar menu which has all the best parts of the full tasting menu for half the price. 

The tasting menu changes seasonally but we got:

Scallop with bread, butter and broth - Bread is a hybrid between a croissant and brioche, in the shape of a dinner roll, and it's flaky buttery perfection. The butter is unique thanks to the savory scallop gelée on top. Scallop soup had a strong, punchy flavor, which may or may not be your thing (I liked it with the bread). Finally there's a dish of scallop, pickled apples and sea urchin. Unfortunately I didn't even notice the sea urchin as it was hidden under the pickled apple, which was by far the dominant flavor. 

Caviar + Soufflé with clam, leek and potato - Standout course of the dinner. I'm not a soufflé person but something about the combination of the light, savory mini soufflé and the briny caviar blew away those reservations.

Foie Gras - You get a choice between bitter greens, squid and foie gras. But just when you think you've made the choice of foie gras (because let's be real, that's probably what you'll pick), you're presented another choice of how to prepare the foie gras - terrine vs seared. And the two preparations result in two very different dishes. The terrine is deliciously smooth and paired with apple, while the seared version is prepared with a sweet potato on top. Both are good and rich in different ways (though I personally found the sweet potato cooked bit too al dente).

Lobster charred with pumpkin and citrus / Halibut with black shallot and mushroom - Only two choices here, so as long as you're not dining alone, you can get a taste of both. Halibut has a uniquely citrusy broth surrounding the fish, adding a nice twist to the dish. Lobster itself was very tender and the sauce had an almost nutty taste. 

Golden Oyster Mushroom with pine and black truffle - My other fav dish of the night. Just mushroomy goodness on top of mushroomy goodness. The golden oyster mushroom is apparently grown on a farm in PA and it was perfectly roasted, with the sauce over it offering the most amazing fragrance of black truffle.

Duck, honey and lavender glazed with shiitake mushrooms - This dish is apparently iconic and I found the crusted skin fairly unique in terms of the spicing (cumin and Sichuan peppercorns), but I just don't think I like the French duck preparation. Duck is always a bit more chewy than I'd like. The sauce is a mix of sweet and savory, but the highlight for me was again the shiitake mushroom on the side. So umami. 

Creamed kale with parmesan and pickled egg yolk - Egg yolk added a nice creaminess to the kale. Good but not my jam since I'm not a fan of creamed veggies.

Brussels sprouts with blood sausage and garlic - Well executed dish of Brussels sprouts. 

Beer and cheese with bread pudding and mustard - The cheese taste is pretty strong for this dish, and honestly a bit off-putting for me. Perhaps the only dish that was a dud for my entire table. 

Chocolate with maple and sesame / Grape with mulled wine and apple - You get a choice between chocolate, grape and apple, and pear with bread pudding. Unfortunately wasn't a huge fan of the chocolate as despite it being super photogenic, it's too dense for me, and an odd mix of sweet and almost savory flavors. The grape was a tad too tart for me but others at my table enjoyed it.

The meal ends with a chocolate covered pretzel, which was only like a pretzel in shape (taste wise it's very different), and a bottle of apple brandy that you're allowed to keep pouring until you've had your fill. 

They didn't do anything special for the birthday (other than a candle on your dessert plate and some singing) but I don't blame them since everyone seemed to be celebrating a birthday. The service was good in the attentive but non-obtrusive way that seems effortless but is in fact very hard to achieve, although we were at one point served the cold scallop dish and not told anything about it, which threw us for a loop. 

All in all, EMP is an experience, which is exactly what it strives to me.

So I can understand why this place was rated the number 1 restaurant in the world overall...but it's important to understand that it is for "overall." The setting and service were incredible. I wanted to be friends with my waiters...not in that hipster millennial way where everyone just bonds but in a "I knew I could count on them to destroy my search history way."

But the food....meh. Certainly an interesting menu that was creative but was it the best food I've ever had? Absolutely not. Compared to places like Cellar con roca or fujiya, this place was lackluster when it came to the food. I mean, nothing was bad and I'm glad I tried it once but I'm not aching to go back again anytime soon. Where as I'll go to roca everyday if I could.

With that being said...the first course I had was scallops. Prepared well. The broth had amazing umami and was the highlight of the course. The apples with the scallops didn't really add to the dish in my opinion. The scallops were super fresh but I had 2 bites with grit or sand on it so the attention to detail there was a miss. 

The marinated foie gras was overpowered by all the other flavors and sweetness. The flavors were a little chaotic. But I was really looking for more foie flavor. The pan seared version was much better. The sweet potato on top was amazingly smoky. 

The soufflé and caviar....ok this was a revelation. Eggs in an egg theme was very whimsical. The flavor was also very intense and really well balanced.

The lobster was well cooked but that's it. The halibut...not fair because I don't like halibut.

The venison was tender. The puff pastry en croute didn't really puff. My mouth was confused by the flavors and texture of the duck. I thought the duck could have used 30 seconds less cooking.

The mushroomn dish was ok. 

The prezel cheese course was pretty good and super rich. There was this odd back end that makes me think of a White Castle burger 

The desserts over all was a weak point. I didn't feel the finality. Or the satisfaction from dessert.

Was it worth over $300? Maybe once. I'm glad I went but I don't think that food wise, it is number one in the world

My wife and I are epic savers. So had you told us that one day we'd spend a mortgage payment on dinner for three...without alcohol...and we'd consider it a bargain...we would've avoided your crazy ass forevermore.
But you would've been right. I'm old and have had my share of experiences. Nothing like this. 
I never share specifics because I don't want people's good deeds to go punished via others reading/expecting the same...but kitchen tours are a known thing, and what they did for us during...and after..will probably be the classiest (and most unexpected) consideration we ever encounter. Maybe it's a movie they've played 1,000/more times and it's part of a system...but it felt like an ad hoc thing that can only come when the culture and people are magical. EMP will extract future mortgage payments from us and others...deservedly so.

They are pretty chill with the dress code which I really liked! Once you walk in, you're greeted instantly by a hostess (there's about 3) and the staff is super friendly, quick, helpful, accommodating and always smiling. You definitely pay for the service because they were on point with everything and the food was awesome! We had an overall great experience.
Long dinner but amazing food/presentation/ and wasn't rushed during dinner. They did forget our coffee during our dessert and had to call someone over to remind them.

A wonderful experience all around. The 8 course tasting menu was varied and executed beautifully. The ambience is simple but refined. Staff were very attentive and our glasses for the wine pairing were refilled immediately. Highly recommended for a nice evening out.

I will start by saying I have been coming to eleven Madison every time I visit NYC (typically once a year) for the last five years. I have never been disappointed. Everything from the ambiance to the food to the service is impeccable. The attention to detail and creativity are second to non. Last time I was there I was sad to see two of my favorite dishes are no longer on the menu which changes regularity. It was nevertheless an amazing experience. I highly recommend this for everyone who enjoys an amazing dining experience. I suggest the duck and the fois gras from the option dishes and for drinks, do yourself a favor and order the Manhattan cart!
What a wonderful experience. My husband and I have been twice, and without fail- it's the best evening. Everything is thought out, the ambience is insane and very flattering. We loved every minute.

Visited for the second time in summer 2018 (yes, overdue review).  let's just say everything was seamless and did not disappoint! I went with high expectations already, since it was my second visit.  I was amazed and pleasantly surprised.  They even baked a jar of treats for my dog, customized jar with a hand drawing portrait and his name (they got the breed wrong, drew a pug instead of french bulldog, definitely my pet peeve but I forgave them.).   I look forward to visit again.

Great experience at one of top ranked restaurants. 

My husband and I picked this place to celebrate our anniversary and my birthday.  We loved the food, drinks and service - everything!  We asked them to downgrade $175 wine pairing to $100 and we were satisfied with their selection. 

We also had a chance to see their kitchen - we felt great energy from a great team work.

11MP is what I call surpassing the bar of other NYC restaurants. I have experienced 11MP a few times in the last couple of years and thought with a few menu changes my opinion would subside. Fortunately, this did not happen and I am still a fan. The service is Great, Food is Amazing and the Ambiance is Top Notch. THIS IS MY FAVORITE RESTAURANT IN NYC.

11MP speaks for its self. Good luck snagging a reservation.

Ugh. I hate having to leave this review. I've been itching to try this place for several years now. After trying other Michelin Star places in the city like Per Se, Le Bernadine, Jean Georges (which were all AMAZING and reasonably priced for the quality and service), we finally caved and decided it was worth it to put in the cash for a meal at the "number one restaurant in the world".

We were highly disappointed. The food was average. Several of the dishes were just downright gross (weird minced squid dish- unsure if there was actually squid in there, chewy lobster). Not to mention they messed up our dessert orders. Then, At the end of the evening they brought us someone else's bill. While these all sound forgiving and I'd normally turn my head away for these, we paid over $2k for 4 people (and might I mention you have to pay in advance when you make your reservation!) so mistakes like these should not be happening. 

Maybe we just had higher expectations.. not sure. But I would definitely not recommend this place to anyone. Really not sure how they get these raving reviews/awards. Save your money. There is much better high end dining experiences in the city for a fraction of this price!

If you are a vegetarian, I would highly recommend avoiding Eleven Madison. Having had remarkable dining experiences at places like Per Se and several Michelin-starred restaurants around the world, Eleven Madison was one of the most underwhelming  experiences I have had.

Most courses felt unimaginative and plain (e.g., here's some ground mushroom with truffles). One course was literally just roasted cauliflower. Eleven Madison did not meet the expectations that we had from what was apparently the best restaurant in the world a few years ago. Service was too slow at times, unlike at other places of similar caliber where it seems choreographed to perfection.

Cocktails were good, the wine list is incredible, and the regular (i.e., non-vegetarian) menu is probably all that it is made out to be, but I would not recommend this place based on my experience.

My girlfriend took me to 11MP for a surprise 21st birthday dinner! From the moment we walked in we were greeted graciously and taken care of. All of the staff were super friendly. This was our first fine-dining experience ever, so we had no idea what to expect. Our server kindly guided us through the 10 course meal and made me feel really comfortable in such a formal setting. It was awesome to try all of these different foods that I've never had before. The black truffle tea to begin with was a great, savory way to start off the meal (the definition of umami). The foie gras was very rich, and according to my girlfriend, the herb crusted duck was one of the best things she's ever eaten. The whole experience went so smoothly. Atmosphere was great and if you're lucky, you can watch what others order and see how the dishes are presented. At the end of the meal, they gave us parting gifts to end the night: personalized menus and their handcrafted granola made from that very morning. Overall, this place was my first fine dining experience, and one that I won't forget (in a good way LOL)! After watching so many episodes of Chef's Table on Netflix, I was able to experience one of the best restaurants in the world, and I'd have to say it lives up to the hype. I would definitely come back.

Overall a solid but completely forgettable meal. Had the five course bar tasting menu; each dish ranged from below average to above average. Nothing evoked a wow response or would make me want to come back, even if the meal were 1/4th of the price. I exaggerate not when I say the table bread was the best part of the meal (I had three pieces). The sweetness of the souffle didn't work well w/ the caviar. The foie gras was a bit too chilled and sweet for me. The lobster was solid (but almost all lobsters are) and the duck didn't pack much flavor. Even the dessert (ice cream with chocolate and peanuts) didn't do much for me... which is rare.

While Eleven Madison Park (or EMP) is undoubtedly a five-star, unforgettable restaurant, after my most recent experience, I have some reservations.  I'm compelled to post a five star review because of the lasting and formative impression my first visit, in 2014, left on me (I never reviewed that visit publicly), but would leave a 3 star review based on my visit for my birthday earlier this month (hence the average, 4).  EMP is, without a doubt, for the vast majority of people, the best restaurant they will ever experience (unless they are an absolute fine dining fanatic).  However, when compared against other stellar dining institutions, EMP now seems comfortable to rest on its laurels, relying primarily on its exclusivity rather than its creativity to drive interest. 

My initial experience with making the reservation was fantastic; the day of my 30th birthday was booked, so I emailed to inquire about a waiting list or any other available tables. I received a quick response that a 9:30pm table would be available on that day.  I grabbed my credit card and paid for my table, as is required by EMP's reservation system Tock (a little over $800 at $335 for two plus tax, inclusive of service).  I was also asked if we were celebrating anything special, so I of course mentioned my birthday.  

Months pass and the day arrives, though little did EMP know just two weeks prior I had dined at Frantzen and Gastrologik, a 3-star and 2-star in Stockholm.  Rarely do I have the opportunity to compare 3-stars side by side, but I was excited to measure the newly experienced Swedish restaurants against my all time favorite EMP.  My first experience with EMP was magical; the host knew your name when you arrived, servers would show you the original Waldorf cookbook and explain the history of the Waldorf salad while tricking you with the fun plating, you got to pick your flavor at the beginning of the meal, and experience the "picnic basket" course (for just a few examples).  The recent experience at EMP, while undoubtedly good, lacked every bit of the flare and creativity the restaurant once had.  It was back to being a standard, well-executed, luxury dining restaurant with careful, attentive, and friendly service.  

After waiting slightly beyond my 9:30pm reservation (which on a Thursday, for a 4+ hour meal, was already towards the end of my night) we were seated at a table just beyond the server station, so we got to listen to the servers as they carefully monitored their tables (which is good to know they are paying close attention, but somewhat awkward to listen to constantly).  We were not offered any cocktails/wine/champagne while waiting. Once seated, you get approximately 12 different tastes (9 courses, three bites), with larger portions than their original 20+ course tasting menu.  All were beautifully plated and most were perfectly executed (lobster was overcooked and felt rubbery and tough to cut through).  Starting the meal with a unique sparkling wine made only for EMP was fun, but this became a recurring theme throughout the dinner.  The participatory aspect of the caviar taco situation was fun. Seeing the oyster mushroom (specifically grown for EMP) was akin to the Nomad's chicken presentation before you get your dish.  Finishing the meal with the apple brandy (again, only for EMP) was a pleasant ending.  But if you want something more experiential, say, a coffee made with the siphon, wine that has been "tonged", similar to those experiences that used to be just part of dinner....you're paying extra ($30+ for the coffee; min. 15-20 year old bottle of wine).  One highlight is the goodie bag with unbelievably tasty granola (so good it can be eaten without yogurt) and your menu which has been printed while you were sitting there, along with some fantastic chocolate with a unique spice.  Be sure to ask for a kitchen tour, as get to play a little tasting game, guessing the link between the flavors of the herbs before you and the juice you're drinking. Interestingly, beyond a candle on my dessert course and every single staff member quietly saying "happy birthday," (which was a bit odd in and of itself) nothing out of the ordinary was done for my 30th.  

Ultimately, it felt like the magic had gone and EMP no longer wanted to affirmatively impress the guest.  The guest was lucky to partake in the exclusive experience of EMP; the guest was not a person to be impressed, but a person to be impressed upon.  Both Stockholm restaurants still felt the need to try, as they aren't located in NYC and haven't been named the best restaurant in the world (yet).  EMP knows it is on top of the world and I can tell it knows this too (not always an enviable quality).  I sincerely hope the spark returns.  EMP made me fall in love with fine dining (in 2014), but it also revealed that it is incredibly difficult to maintain that level of brilliance without getting comfortable (a la 2019).

I really enjoyed eleven Madison. My fiancé took us here for my birthday. We actually watched the Netflix documentary prior to coming. The service was impeccable and the staff were super nice. We also tried the Japanese whiskey (hibiki 21 if u are looking for Japanese whiskey). The dining room was bustling and the staff worked like an orchestra, anytime someone got up, immediately staff folded their napkin back on the table. The food was delicious as I expected nothing less from eleven Madison. This was the first 3 star we tried in the USA and although it didn't compare to Gordon Ramsay in London, it was worth the price for the experience.

In NYC visiting mini-me at college and he wanted to have dinner at ELM. We were all excited about the once world number one ranked restaurant with 3 Michelin stars. 

Perhaps because our expectations were set so high but we were all a little disappointed. While the dishes were all decent, none really blew us away. We also found some of the dishes were overly salty. In addition, it seemed that chef Humm was attempting to incorporate some Asian herbs and flavors in several of the dishes; as examples, we tasted ginger and perhaps fermented black bean paste. Unfortunately, I personally was not sure that it always worked. 

The service on the other hand was superb. Everything thing seemed well choreographed. 

Another one of my complaints was that the bench seats were quite uncomfortable. I felt like I was in a unreclinable seat on a Southwest flight for 3 hours.

You've probably heard about all the accolades or seen the Eleven Madison Park episode on the '7 days out' series on Netflix. It's only natural that the 3 Michelin star restaurant has been on my foodie bucket list for awhile.  

I finally got to cross it off the list when I came to celebrate a special occasion here. It is truly an unforgettable experience that definitely lives up to the hype and it's only appropriate to save my 100th review for one of the most special dining experiences I've been fortunate to have.

FOOD - They offer two types of tasting menus: The dining room (8-10 courses) and the bar tasting menu (5 courses) which you prepay for when you secure your reservation on Tock. The tasting menu rotates regularly so I won't get into the specifics, but everything was fantastic. 

SERVICE - I think what really stood out from any other restaurant I've ever been to was the meticulous attention to detail and the impeccable service we received from the staff all night. Service was not overbearing and the vibe from the waitstaff seemed casual, yet formal and I did not get that stuffy feeling at all. Keep in mind that gratuity is already included in the menu pricing.

SURPRISES - The apple brandy and the chocolate pretzels at the end of our tasting menu were a nice touch. They also sent us home with several keepsake menus and their homemade granola.

EMP represents the quintessential NYC dining experience that is perfect for celebrating a special occasion!

An incredible special occasion restaurant that lives up to the hype.  This is one of those meals that is an experience that sticks with you.  I love how the vibe was quintessential New York - fancy but not too stuffy, inventive cooking using local ingredients, and classy but a lot of fun.  The service was incredible as well - and everything was incredible memorable.  My one complaint is that we were not offered a tour of the kitchen, which I had heard was something others had the chance to do.

I feel honored I got to eat here. I'd go again and again if I could. I am still processing how incredible this experience was.

Like for real, right now I feel like the part of my brain that processed the sensory data associated with tasting the meal has been transported to the same realm a large hit of DMT transports you to. It is busy communicating with Aztec deities, trying to convincing them to incarnate in the 3rd dimension as an earth primate so they can this food.  So it's too busy to give me the words to write a proper interview.

I'll update when that part of my brain returns from the 16nth dimensional time space reality continuum EMP transported it to.

We finally got to try another Three Michelin Starred Restaurant in New York beside Per Se. It seems more casual here compared to the ones we've been to in San Francisco and Napa.
We didn't find it as an unforgettable experience after all but just a casual tasting dinner. 

All the dishes tasted okay. Nothing is so special in my opinion. The seasonings were too rich and heavy that it overpowers the taste of meat and seafood even though everything was well cooked.

In the end, we ordered one more drink (Jameson whiskey on the rock) but it took a while for them to bring it to us. It seemed like they had forgotten about it because we had to ask the server to check on it again...
 
Well I'm glad that we got to try it anyway. Thanks again!

This was definitely a one of a kind experience! It's hard to make reservation as they're usually booked out and since we were flying in from Seattle we had made advance reservations. Due to our flight being delayed and with the time zone differences I had called the restaurant and the hospitality was amazing! 

Understanding and very accommodating saying that they will still accommodate our party by the time we arrived and that there was no dress code and so we didn't have to stress about not being able to make it to dinner. 

When we arrived the owner had greeted us and said that it's delighted to see how dedicated we were. The service and ambience was top notch it was like having your own VIP services per person per table! The storytelling to every dish is an add on and due to my fungi allergy everything was accommodated! 

This place strives in customer service and taking care of their customers first with a great catered menu. Will be back and try other locations but definitely this is the reason why they're Michelin rated.

My first time to a fine dining and had an amazing experience with great companies!! Great interior and love the artistic presentations of the food, most importantly great food!! And yes, I loved all the food that I chose. I loved the bread (we had three rounds of breads), the scallop with unagi, souffle with caviar (my favorite), the duck, the lobster, and so many more I forgot already. I didn't use my phone to take pictures, but took one of the interior before leaving. It was a great night and a great experience to have.

A friend and I were able to get a table in the bar area through EMP's waiting list. I was so excited to finally eat at the famous EMP but ended up disappointed. Staff were friendly and attentive and the ambiance was nice but the food - which is really why you come - was only OK. The bar area offers a smaller tasting menu than the dining room, so maybe you would have a different experience with the larger tasting menu in the dining room, but at this point I wouldn't pay the money to test that theory. Dishes were hit or miss with some courses really good and others mediocre. Even with the good courses there was no "wow" moment, and at that price point and Michelin rating I expected at least one dish to really impress. We ate at a nearby 1 star restaurant the following night and had a better meal for less money.

I can't believe I'm giving "The Best Restaurant in the World" a 4 star rating. Completely missing the WOW factor you expect as far as food is concerned. And I'm usually extremely generous with 5 star ratings. But if you're going to be #1 you have to really be #1. Honestly the ambiance, service, and attention to detail is top top. It's why they're rated what they are. But the food was only good! It's so disappointing! I expected flavors, dishes I'd wish I could try again but wouldn't be able to until I somehow came back here. Not 1. If it wasn't for the service I'd say my rating would be a 3, maybe even a 2 because of price. I think the missing factor was that the food was bland. In fact the newly renovated venue was pretty bland and underwhelming as well.

Now for the positives! Did a tour of the kitchen, it's totally calm and huge and clean and beautiful. Real masterpiece back there since the renovations. There's a real relaxing vibe to the place, that was great. You also get about 10 different servers come to you throughout the night, felt like we were hosted by the whole kitchen - staff really cares about what they do and take it super seriously. That was nice. I think they also do a great job of accommodating. If I had an allergy, or didn't like a certain type of food, you get the impression they'll drive over to McDonald's to get you a burger if that's what they think you really want and to accommodate you. Unfortunately I eat everything and I'm not a picky difficult person so I couldn't benefit personally from that level of accommodation they definitely excel at. 

Bottom line: they need to rethink their tasting menu because if you're #1, you can't have ok dishes. The dishes were just ok. Nothing amazing. Everyone I was with agreed. I've ate at many Michelin star rated restaurants and high end restaurants in general. EMP you have to really please introduce some WOW factor into the menu because everything was just OK.

Several months ago while planning for the trip to NYC, I had the idea to try a Manhattan in Manhattan. The search was on for a place to try it and I found Eleven Madison Park. The article mentioned that 6 different types of Manhattan are available to be served tableside in the dining area then I realized that EMP is a 3 star Michelin restaurant that's been rated as one of the best restaurants in the world.

As soon as I could make reservations online, I did and it was to treat my nephew for his belated birthday celebration. I had gotten the Bar Tasting Menu for us. I tried the more citrusy version of the Manhattan which was called Brooklyn and my nephew had the Beet. Their bread was incredibly soft and the butter with seaweed went well together. We started with a spoonful of caviar which we stirred into the souffle. Great flavors! We both had the foie gras which had maple oozing out of the middle. Also, had the lobster tail. I had the duck with mushrooms. Chocolate with maple and sesame. Chocolate pretzels with apple brandy.

To end the night, we toured the kitchen and got a little extra bite as a birthday surprise.

They sent us home with a jar of granola!
Best experience within a restaurant I ever had. Food was delicious they brought back there most popular courses and it was delicious. The staff was perfect. Highly recommend.

What additional insight could I possibly add to the thousands of glowing reviews about 11 madison park?? We celebrated my birthday here and I was very happy with this choice! I was a bit worried because we celebrated my birthday last year at Alinea and that experience is hard to beat (i know, i know, first world problems). 11 Madison did not disappoint! Every course here tasted great. Compared to Alinea - there were some flavors that did not mesh well together.  

I was especially surprised by the non-dairy croissant. They were able to achieve a flakey texture without any butter and I loved it so much I ate 2! This caused a lot of pain throughout the rest of the meal (since I was full by course 3), but it was so worth it! I will dream about this bread for the next many birthdays until I get another chance to go back to 11 Madison :) 

Thank you for an unforgettable birthday dinner!

Not that a yelp review is even needed for this place but just in case you are even questioning it still, make your reservation already! We did the tasting menu in the bar area and had them pair it with tequila cocktails. What an incredible experience! The attention to detail and service here is next level. The food was phenomenal and the drinks were SO amazing! Worth every penny! Make sure to get a tour of the kitchen!

I have been meaning to write this Review for almost 2 years now but the experience is still fresh in my mind. We flew into New York in January 2018, to find out the reason why Eleven was Voted Best Restaurant in the World 2017, The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Michelin Guide, 2018. 

From the moment you walk through the door the staff has to be the friendliest we have ever encountered in a restaurant of this stature. We were greeted at our table by almost a dozen staff members throughout the course of our meal (not in an intrusive way). They were each friendly and knowledgeable about food and wine of course... but also about art and architecture. I almost wanted to invite some of them to sit and join us because they felt like old friends. 

Now for the food...The preparation, presentation, texture and taste of each individual dish was unique and exquisite. Some of the best flavors in the world that we have had the pleasure to enjoy. They were also extremely generous with the wine pairing, my glass was never empty and each wine was a perfect choice for each dish. If I could rate them 10 stars I would, the enter experience was unparalleled.

We all know the accolades that this restaurant has - 3 Michelin Stars, World's best restaurant (2017), James Beard Chef, etc. 

Like other restaurants, they've adopted the Tock reservation system. Essentially, you'll be spending time refreshing on the first of every month at 9AM Est trying to snag a reservation at this coveted restaurant. 

And this is all part of the build-up (at least for me). The anticipation and count down, the excitement of going to one of the world's best restaurants - and paying that premium price tag to go along with it ($350+ a person). And of course, the fame of Eleven Madison Park - a restaurant that employs a "dreamweaver" that attempts to make your experience as unique as possible. 

So needless, to say, I had pretty high expectations coming here... and that's part of my disappointment. Perhaps my expectations were too high, but I do think they should be at least comparable to their peers (other 3 Michelin star restaurants such as Alinea). And that's where they really fall flat for me. 

I'm usually not one to care for service, but after hearing the legendary tales of EMP, this is one category they fell sort in. Did they rush to push a chair in for us? Yes. Was our water cups ever empty? No. But the service wasn't perfect by any means. We had servers mess up on explaining the dishes, making faces when they did and overall did not feel warm and welcoming. In fact, they never mention that they charge for simple things such as tea or coffee - we learned that later when we were handled a bill for "beverage" at the end of the meal. This bill came with our chocolate pretzels at the end, and it seems to me that they were so focused on giving us this bill that they even forgot to bring us a bottle of their infamous apple brandy with the pretzels. I now only know about the apple brandy bottle after seeing it on their instagram with a caption of "Verified
At the end of each meal, we serve our signature apple brandy for the entire table to share." Missing something that's suppose to be a component of the meal is a CRUCIAL miss. Something I wouldn't expect a 3 Michelin star restaurant to fumble on. Then there were the little things - like giving a spoon to someone in my party when it was meant for my dish. 

Anyhow, onto the food itself. In general, I am of the belief that tasting menus won't always WOW the eater. There were some dishes which I did not really care for but there are some stand out dishes at EMP. These would include the infamous duck breast, the caviar souffle, and the mushroom dish. I would say these were the most memorable dishes of the night. Overall, the food is good - but is it worth its price point? I'm not too sure. 

I came here because it was a bucket list item (I imagine to every foodie, trying a restaurant that was once deemed the best restaurant in the world, would be). Maybe I came with expectations that were too high, but no one in my party seemed wowed. And after learning about not even being served the apple brandy...I am even less wow'd.  

Overall - would I recommend this restaurant to my friends? No. Would I come here again? No.

We actually planned our trip to New York from Canada because we had heard great things about Eleven Madison Park. We wanted to dine at this magnificent restaurant we had heard about through television, social media, and friends of friends. We flew here to celebrate my girlfriend's 30th birthday, which would end with dinner here. 

I should prefix this by saying that the important part was that my girlfriend had a great time. She enjoyed her meal and the experience; that alone made the trip to New York worth it. They were always wishing her happy birthday, and never made her feel anything less than special. I value and thank them for that service. 

But I would be remiss if I didn't comment on how it feels to be on the receiving end of a restaurant trying to adapt for food allergies. Essentially, I have a severe nut allergy and a moderate dairy allergy: one that I've grown up throughout my life having to apologize for to the various places I visit to eat. I gave them the generic, "hey, I have a food allergy so I'll probably not be that fun" speech I have been used to giving me entire life. Despite that, I feel like they don't quite understand what it's like to be fearful of the unknown that comes with allergies. 

I only ended up being able to eat 1/3rd of the dishes they presented, and the more audacious part was they never bothered asking why. There was never a question or concern about why one could not finish a dish; why someone possibly could not even start to eat their dishes. Not even a question of concern about how things are tasting so far. Just on to the next course; hope you like that. I've been to other Michelin star restaurant that go above and beyond to accommodate for their patrons; this stop just fell flat. 

For a restaurant that goes for the little details (things such as the orientation of plates so that flipping them over demonstrates a right-side-up logo), they don't go in depth enough to understand the concerns of their patrons. I gave them the heads-up about everything weeks in advance, yet everything fell flat on execution. At the end of the day, I can't scold them because thats just how I was born; it's not their job to accommodate for my faults. But I certainly shouldn't feel like they didn't care about it either. 

What I could eat was fantastic. Highly recommend you go. But if you have food allergies, I'd recommend you skip them all together.

We spent April in Paris and had the pleasure of dining at Taillevent, Guy Savoy and Tour d'Argent. We had dined previously, in January, at EMP, and for once Michelin got it right--this place is right up there with those luminaries, but distinctly and uniquely American. It was magnificent without being stuffy, the staff engaging and friendly without being fawning or obsequious.

Top of my list for nyc restaurants that I wanted to try and it was great. No surprise it's hard to get a reservation and use a concierge to help you here.

One of the things that surprised me the most here were all the dishes that had Asian influence. There was a duck breast with Sichuan peppercorns and cumin.

There's no point in naming all the dishes because it rotates so often. You come here, and I think ingredients are what you appreciate the most. There was a tomato dish with nothing done to it other than some olive oil was added and it was blanched, but the taste was so memorable and delicious. Same with a lobster, never had it so tender before, normally lobster is a bit more tough, but this one had the firmness of crab, but the satisfaction of a lobster. There was a corn dish that I can't imagine that they did much to it, but it was the sweetest corn I've ever had and would've been happy to have that for dessert.

What I was most surprised about and what prevents me from giving it a 5* was the amount of courses. I felt like it wasn't enough to make me feel really full. Like I could go home and in 3 hours feel like I need to munch on something.
The price tag is worth it. One of the most memorable culinary experiences I have had. We went on November 2018 and he best dishes had truffle on them.

This is more of bar / service review. Walked in hoping for a table .... alas as expected, no luck. Stayed for a couple of drinks. Tried the Watermelon soft tail. It was excellent. Service very attentive. Will be returning armed with a reservation next time

ElevenMadisonPark is the former "Best Restaurant in The World for 2017" and continue to be 3 Star Michelin. I was lucky to get reservation through the wait list even though it's been sold out for months. Thanks to my coworker Jon.
The ambience is A rating with elegant decoration and jazzy background music. 
The service is A+ rating with waiters/waitresses walking in one direction every 30 seconds in sync. They are knowledgeable and know when I need service before I even raise my hand.
The food is A+ rating because every dish is unique and incomparable. My favorite is the cream corn which was the best of the best I've ever had. The only way is to understand it is to experience it.

This is definitely my French restaurant benchmark. I'm sure there's always better, but for now this is definitely the pinnacle of my fine dining experience.

For 3 Michelin stars and ranked one of the top restaurants in the world, the staff at Eleven Madison Park is one of the friendliest and approachable.  My friend and I ordered the Bar Tasting menu, which was a 5 course meal.  

Course 1: Cavier Benedict with corn and ham.  This was salty, briny, buttery delicious.  It was like a deconstructed eggs Benedict in the best way possible.  It also came with miniature homemade English muffins. 

Then came the bread with butter.  This was butter on top of more butter and even MORE butter (if that's even possible).  The bread was crispy with layers of flaky goodness.

Course 2 was Crab with Sunflower and Cardamom.  Honestly, this was my least favorite dish.  The sunflower tasted pickled.  This was a bit unmemorable.  I also learned I don't really like sunflower :)  

Course 3 -- lobster with summer beans and savory.  The butter poached lobster.  This was sweet, tender, and the sauce was absolutely to die for. Then you add the crunchiness of the summer beans (best beans I've ever had-- I think they were green beans, honestly) The best way to describe this dish is literally "melt in your mouth" sweetness and tenderness.

Course 4 - main entree, I ordered the Dry aged beef w/ lettuce and Anise Hyssop.  This dish took a surprising turn.  It was fatty, but tasted very lean.  It came with some grilled lettuce, which was better than the meat, itself.  But what surprised me the most of the asian flavors that were utilized in this dish.  While it was good, it didn't really go all that well w/ the rest of the menu.

Course 5 - dessert.  For dessert, I had the Cherry and Corn w/ Vanilla.  This was one of the best desserts I've never had.  You really can't judge a book by its cover.  Purely based on appearance, this was a simple plate of 5 spheres -- 1 white, 1 orange, 2 red, and 1 yellowish.  But... when I started digging into this, it was honestly one surprise after another.  Each sphere had at least one additional layer.  It honestly brought me so much joy! :)

Dinner wrapped up with some chocolate covered pretzels and a little gift of delicious granola to go.  

Highlight for me were the Cavier, Lobster, and Dessert.

It's quite an experience to eat at a restaurant like this. The attention to detail is unsurpassed. I loved a majority of the dishes but some felt like they tried to hard to make it different and forgot to make it delicious. But the DUCK was superb. I would like to go back and have just the duck and skip the regalia.

Truly the biggest waste of money on my part in years. The same amount would have been much better spent on a new iPhone because for 2 expect to drop $1k+ here.

Started off badly with the incompetent reservation staff, who made our booking on an incorrect date. Apparently correcting it to the right date meant we used up our one "change reservation" free pass even though their staff were at fault. Keep in mind this is a $400/pp PREPAID experience that we're being told is immutable. We had to change our flight to eat this meal.

Upon arrival, the space is airy and tranquil. Everything else pretty much sucked. The velvet seats they went on about in Netflix are incredibly itchy. The meal itself was unremarkable and insulting, even I (a petite female) left feeling hungry. "9-10 courses" is definitely not true when they consider bread and a cup of soup to be courses. We also came during a mushroom theme and when a server was cutting a chunk off a large mushroom branch she dropped it on the serving cart but gave it to us anyways. Duck was the only memorable food item, it was delightfully crisp and juicy but you'll be served about two mouthfuls of it. The small jar of granola they send you home with is really good, but it's not worth $1000. FYI the recipe is on NY times and it really does taste identical.

The only thing I got out of this was a lesson learned and a good granola recipe.

Three and a half stars. It's ok. It's "meh". Is it worth the nearly $800 for the price of admission for two people?  No. No it's not. 

Service was great. Cocktails took a lot longer than expected.  

We had the 8 course tasting menu. It was a good meal with good food.  High quality food with creative ingredients that was innovative you prepared. 

Was it mind blowing?  No.  But I love the fact that they use local ingredients and try to use the whole plant/ animal when preparing each dish. I was satisfied rather than being blown away. 

The only thing that was a major let down was the deserts. Frankly, they were some of the worst deserts I've ever tried. I did not want to finish them. 

That's about it.

Our experience at EMP was pure magic.  Every Michelin Star well deserved.  I am still raving about it to everyone that will listen to me.  Staff absolutely humble and incredible.  Food insanely gorgeous and delicious.  If I had a larger wallet, I would insist on making this an annual occasion.  Thank you team for an UNFORGETTABLE experience.

I came here for my first anniversary and could not have been more disappointed. The food was mediocre (I could've cooked and made all myself) and we didn't eat a single bite of food until an hour after our reservation (10PM). We have been to a ton of top 50 world wide restaurants and this was by far the worst. As a native New Yorker I could've gotten to all the great restaurants that around me in Greenwich village abd this place is 10x over priced. They claim to purchase with in the season; I came September 21st and they were still cooking "New Jersey corn, rice, zucchini, peaches, and tomatoes",seems like summer is over and purchase what's in union square farmers market. I don't want to eat your month old zucchini's. I will absolutely never be back. Blue hill I go or even Vic's. This was made for tourists.

I don't care what people say, this place is worth the trip and the splurge. The menu is always extremely well thought out and portions are well balanced within a tasting menu format. My wife and I love going out to eat and experiencing all aspects of dining, regardless or pricepoint and ambiance. The staff here are super friendly and the way in which your food is served is like a symphony. We would recommend EMP to all and are looking into going again in November.

TLDR - 5 stars if just for food -2 stars for service.  Food is unique and innovative, but not substantial.  Service is mediocre and on a downward trajectory.

At first I really hated this restaurant, but after thinking about it a bit more I think this is a restaurant for people who have been to too many other good restaurants.  Would you pay $300 a person to be served a tomato even if it was the most delicious umami infused tomato you've ever had?  I guess it depends if you're bored of eating other things or not.

Personally this was the first 3 michelin meal I've had where I left unsatisfied in terms of food quantity.  Crazy things have been done to the ingredients which led to some stand out dishes with new flavors and textures I haven't experienced before such as the aforementioned tomato dish, the brown rice course (by far the most unique and interesting), and the aged duck.

For the drinks my wife and I opted to split the pricier reserve pairing since we were told it's about a full bottle of wine in volume and this is where the service kind of went downhill.  Our drinks attendant, the sommelier was nowhere in sight, got the impression that we were a bunch of cheap asses trying to split a wine pairing instead of just getting our own and kept pushing us to go for individual ones.  There was a miscommunication when I asked her to bring 2 glasses instead of 1 so we could split the pairing for the next round and she thought I was trying to finagle extra wine out of the current one.  She went to discuss with the sommelier if this was ok came back and rolled her eyes at us as she poured out a second glass.  I had to double check with my wife if I imagined that or not, but I didn't have to as she already had a "wtf was that" look on her face.

The strange part is my coworkers had raved about coming here in the past.  After talking to them it turns out before the renovation and the change in ownership you used to get tours of the kitchen midway through your meal.  Additionally stories of service staff going above and beyond to make each meal personal are all over the place online.  Sadly this doesn't exist anymore so don't expect much from the service.  Shoutout to Bridget the maitre d though, she memorized everyone's special events who were coming.

Also a lesson learned after visiting a couple fancy restaurants including this one: always request better seats.  Everyone is celebrating something special, if you don't you'll end up with some spectacular views of the toilet, the exit, or the service entrance to the kitchen.

I think there are two important questions to ask when writing a review. Namely (1) would I do it again and (2) would I recommend a friend. 

Considering both of my answers are no this will be a short review. Level of service and quality/creativity of menu was disappointing. There isn't really a nice way to say this but it felt like a slightly older and more tired version of how it was shown on Netflix. I did not see the exacting attention to detail that one expects and to be honest was a bit bored by our dishes. There were a few triumphs but in general I felt like they were very much playing safe. Minor things in execution with the odd erant crumb and the like were very telling. This is the first  restaurant if this caliber that I have been to where something so basic was missed in plating. 

At this level one is expecting perfection. This did not happen and there were a lot of awkward misses. 

Based on our experience not sure how long they are going to be keeping all those stars. 

Disappointing for what looked like an amazing experience. Bunch of kinks to work out on the service and food side. 

My recommendation you can do better.
The food was great but the service was AWFUL.  I had to ask 4x before potentially getting served and still did not usually get what I asked for.  Completely unprofessional wait staff.

Last night I ate at The Yeatman in Portugal and was super impressed with their service and wine pairing that it made me think of a negative experience I had at Eleven Madison Park for my birthday last year. I never had a chance to write a review about this but the opportunity has risen and it was such a basic mistake that I have to write about it. 

While the food and experience at Eleven Madison was great, i was disappointed with the service I experience with wine pairing. The most rookie mistake occurred.
