Instead of switching out my wine glass for a new glass to pour out a new wine, the waiter poured a new wine into a glass that I previously had a different wine in. Very basic mistake and was disappointing to see from one of the top restaurants in the world. 

Dining at The Yeatman made me think of this because their attention to detail was impeccable and we had 6-7 different wines and each time, the glass was switched out.

The food and service overall was good (but not overwhelmingly amazing) and I probably won't be back to EMP and I wouldn't highly recommend it to friends. I don't think it holds up to the cost and expectations that one should have from the #1 restaurant in the world.
The duck here was the best.  Crispy and very flavorful.

Underwhelming food given the price.

Top notch service! Honestly the only reason I would come back.

The food overall was heavy and rich, not balanced. Only the duck dish did I feel that it was lighter since there was some acidic elements. This was for the summer lunch menu. Maybe their next menu will be better I dunno.

Everything is awesome!  We got there (there are 52 tables) half an hour earlier and the moment we got to the door one lady called me by my last name and I was shocked she knew who I was.  She escorted us to our table.  We booked the tasting menu and everything is awesome. They have a nice wine pairing and I'm glad we did that to save us time deciding what to get.  At the conclusion of our meal we were given a tour of the kitchen per my request (as suggested by a friend who did the same thing).  There's even a take away jar of granola and the menu we had for dinner.  Truly a 3-star michelin.
The best restaurant ever. Its pricey but skip ten dinners out and experience the best dining experience you can ever have. On every level they succeed.

Service for sure is 5/5. Food was 4/5. Worth it? Maybe the bar tasting menu. 

Service: absolutely wonderful. Our cups were constantly being refilled. Everyone was attentive and not intrusive. Legit ninja skills as someone was always pushing my chair in for me even though I saw no one close to me when I tried to sit down. Everyone was very knowledgeable about the menu and what we were being served. We had a good kitchen tour at the end as well. 

Food: we had a party of 5. We didnt have fast enough fingers to get a table for 5. Instead we did a table for 3 and 2 at the bar. So as a whole we had both the dinner and bar tasting menu. The dinner tasting menu included the bar one plus 5 more courses. I absolutely loved the foie gras, lobster, and duck. The caviar was decent. Bread and butter was delicious. Dessert was good but not amazing. The other courses were every day ingredients or foods with a twist including a congee, tomato dish, creamed corn, and greens. 

Worth it? Maybe the bar tasting menu. It had all the best foods and excluded the more creative but less delicious courses. If you have a ton of money to spend on dinner, then go for the dining tasting menu. There was just too much tomato for my liking. If you want to have an amazing service experience, the dining room will hit that spot. But if you wanna try fancy food without breaking the bank, the bar is my recommendation.

An amazing meal for a special occasion!

3 Michelin stars and #1 restaurant in the world in 2017 - this place deserves all the praise it has gotten. The craftsmanship and creativity in each dish is a culinary work of art. You can see, feel, and taste "Make It Nice" in every perfect dish. The experience is whimsical and captures the feel of New York.

The menu changes according to the season but the staple is the duck. Chef Humm has perfected this duck and while the flavors change slightly according to the season, the dish is always stunning.

THE EXPERIENCE

We went during the winter holiday season so we sat down to a box of presents. We were curious of course so we opened the boxes to find our first caviar course with potato and sturgeon cream.

Our next course was foie gras with pear and mushroom laid out precisely and beautifully. Then, we had lobster poached with kale. She had the halibut which was so delicate.

My favorite dish aside from the duck was the braised mushroom tart with a crisp baked on top. They shaved a truffle on top of mushroom cream. The braised mushroom was so simple yet so good!

The cheddar tart with apple at the end was surprising and delicious.

At the end of the meal, you get to help yourself to an apple brandy made especially for Eleven Madison Park! And of course, the chocolate pretzel.

I also had a beet cocktail that was probably the best cocktail I've ever had!

Overall, an experience like none other! So delicious and so meticulous

Amazing food in an amazing space with amazing service. We got we paid for here, and if there was anything to complain about, it's that we were left wanting a bit more time there.

This was our second EMP visit, the first being six years ago and extremely different from this trip. That one lasted almost four hours, featured sixteen total courses, and each one seemed to have a story and/or kitschy presentation to it. This trip was more businesslike -- almost exactly two hours from start to finish, ten total courses, and much less storytelling with each one. 

We found ourselves somewhat conflicted on those changes. Four hours was probably a bit too long, but two hours felt a bit too short. We were definitely full at the end, but not to the point of being uncomfortable, and while eating to the point of being uncomfortable is dumb, it does feel like the volume of food should be borderline excessive when you're paying this much for it. I did appreciate the elimination of the stories, picnic baskets, etc, although I'm sure there were others who appreciated those things more than me.

Anyway, the food itself was as incredible as you'd expect. The rice porridge, roasted tomato with tuna and seaweed, their signature duck, and the chocolate with coffee and cocoa nibs were a few of my favorites, although the caviar/okra taco was probably my favorite bite of the night. (That corn tortilla....) That in itself probably says a lot about the food from this visit -- it felt like there was more of a not-strictly-French vibe, which I liked a lot given how rarely you get incredibly fancy non-French food.

Overall, an amazing experience which lived up to the billing, while also leaving us wanting more.

Superb service.  Elegant decor in a Art Deco building. The most memorable dish was surprisingly the bread.  We went there long ago before they increased the price.  We would definitely check out the restaurant again.

Service is god as expected...

Caviar app was good then it went downhill for the next two courses .. foie gras was a funky flavor and the replacement app or the crab salad has really mayonnaisey flavor..

Lobster dish...the lobster wasn't too fresh... I am from Boston so I do get great lobster and may be biased...

The duck meat was excellent after I scraped off excessive coriander seeds off the skin ... will attach the image...

And finally the dessert was actually pretty good. Nothing to dream about but good.

Satisfied my curiosity but would not recommend highly...

It's Eleven Madison Park. In case you weren't aware, it was ranked the best restaurant on the planet in 2017, and it's been in the global top 5 for years. Evidently, the meal is absolutely, positively incredible. The tasting menu changes out on a pretty regular basis, but some of the highlights from my experience were the snails and foie gras. For one of the entrees, they'll likely give you a choice. Pick the duck; it's what they're known for. I'll say two key points for you to keep in mind moving forward:
1. If EMP is within the realm of affordability for you, I'd highly recommend going because it's truly a world-class experience.
2. If you can further afford it, the wine pairing works wonders with the tasting menu and honestly added a great deal of enjoyment (and tipsiness) to the meal.

The service is excellent but besides that everything is average at best .The food was a joke , nothing special .I travel around the world and no way this restaurant should not have rating of number one .

Excellent but disappointing. 

First of all, every dish was perfectly prepared and the service was flawless. But the 4 of us left thinking it was an interesting experience that we wouldn't repeat or recommend it. We also left hungry!  

The dishes are very good, but almost Saturday Night Live skit small. My wife and I decided to share the duck and beef options. The beef was about the size of 3 Vegas dice, which when you cut it in half to share with your spouse is almost comical. And the two vegetable side dishes they give the table to share take it to a new level. We could barely get 4 teaspoons out of each to share. And my wife pointed out that she's had shrimp larger than her lobster tail. 

The Pretentious Dish of the Night Award goes to the tomato dish. They roll out a carving table and present a single standard-sized, but farm raised, cooked tomato. The server then meticulously carves the tomato into 4 pieces, applies some fairy dust with tweezers and serves it. We all ooh and ahh about it until we realize ... it's a tomato. Actually it's a quarter of a tomato. 

All the dishes were perfectly prepared with interesting seasoning, but there were very few if any wow moments where you say, how did they think of that - it's amazing. 

The service was very efficient but also very cold. Maybe that's the objective so as to not distract from the food. There are so many servers but no one person is lead for your table. Different people serve different things. What we've experienced at other 3 star restaurants is the same level of service but with a point person who acts as your guide through a 3 hour adventure. Someone who gets to know you a little. Someone you form a bond with and let's you form a bond with the restaurant. That doesn't happen here. 

We just went to St. Hubertus last month in the Italy, another Michelin 3 star restaurant. We had their smaller 10 course tasting menu. When we asked if we could substitute an item from the larger tasting menu, they just added it to our menu. We had one waiter leading the team, who described each dish with passion, and many of the dishes were just amazing in their creativity. We left after several hours feeling delighted and full, and with a New York Restaurant recommendation from our server. It was a memorable experience, and we've spent the last month describing our favorite dishes to our foodie friends. To me, that's what defines a 3 star Michelin restaurant.

With all of the hype it's hard not to come to this place with the highest expectations. Although the dishes were beautifully presented and highlighted the flavors of the ingredients there was no wow-factor and in fact, there were a few misses in my book. Misses? Maybe I mean that EMP helped me better define what I really enjoy about a culinary experience. 

Some observations:

How many service staff do you need? - The updated room is gorgeous and the service was genuinely friendly but when you have so many service staff constantly walking around in a circle (clockwise I believe), then the experience can be literally dizzying with no sense of peace. More importantly, you lose the personal touch of the consistent figure that guides you through the experience. For example, our initial waitress who welcomed us, took our order and who we made conversation with was quickly replaced by someone else for a better portion of the meal. A variety of people came by to present dishes and along with that descriptions also varied with respect depth and clarity of explanations. So, not sure what I ate on a couple of occasions. When our original waitress came back later, it felt disjointed and awkward. Was she coming along for the journey or just stopping by?  This is where an experienced maitre d can make all of the difference because they can help maintain a consistent feel for the entire meal. 

The box on the table - yes there is a unusual ugly box on the table when you arrive. It's a conversation starter. What is it? What do we do with it? Is there something inside? Well, you find out that its a box to put your phone away during the meal. I found this a bit off-putting because it makes a false assumption about the customer. Although it may be the restaurant's way of letting the customer know that they value a meal away from the screen, it also assumes that you have a 'problem' with your phone and offers a solution before getting to know who you are first. This left a bad taste in my mouth before the dinner ever began and also made me feel bad about taking pictures of my food. Why make the food so beautiful and then give me the option not to make a memory out of it? And do you want me to put my phone in a box that was full of everyone else's bacteria-infesested phones? No thanks. My recommendation is to have something on the table that is unusual and unique to promote conversation but is also actually a part of the meal later on. That would be cool. 

Decisions Decisions - So you pay for the tasting menu ahead of time without knowing what you are going to eat. That's fine, it's a culinary journey and I'm game for whatever the chefs decide to make. However, upon arrival, our waitress asked us to select between different dishes with minimal explanation and there was no menu to consult. This put me in a difficult position of making a decision about what I was going to eat rather impulsively with little information. Lobster or bass? Foie gras or crab? Duck or ribeye? I don't know, I'd like to try everything please. Perhaps the choices provide some flexibility for multiple people at the table, but I was expecting that I would just eat what was prepared for me and not have worry about deciding whether I made the right choice or not. Again, just my preference but well highlighted by my experience at EMP. 

Food to drink ratio - I've been to plenty of fine dining establishments and I know tasting menus have small portions. In fact, I like that because you get to try a lot of different dishes without feeling uncomfortably stuffed. However, I feel that I drank more than I ate at EMP, which is not a good feeling either, especially since many of the dishes were really light. For example, one entire dish was half of a tomato. At that point I already drank a few glasses of wine and I really wish I hadn't because I definitely needed something to soak up the booze. Also, there was noticeably long pause before the final meat dish. I think they do that so that you don't feel too full when you get to that part of the meal. However, they poured a very deep rich red wine for the meat dish right after they cleared the plates for the previous dish. So I sat their for about 20 minutes with sipping on the wine and having a conversation with my wife. By the time the meat dish came our glasses were empty. Was that a mistake? Maybe. Although they did refill our glasses, I felt like I was done drinking and just wanted to eat something. In fact, I couldn't even stomach the apple brandy that was served with the dessert. 

The solution? In true movie-style fashion my wife and I followed up our EMP experience with an epic midnight burger and lobster spaghetti from the Lamb's Club back at the Chatwal hotel, where we were staying. Dare I say that Geoffery Zakarian saved our meal?

My husband and I regularly travel to New York from San Francisco, our hometown. With each visit, we excitedly anticipate an excellent and unique culinary experience that only select destinations like New York can offer.
 
We've dined at almost every New York "upscale" restaurant including Per Se, Masa, La Bernadine, Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare, Jungsik, The Modern and too many others to list. As San Franciscans, we're spoiled by numerous Bay Area/Napa Valley/Sonoma Valley establishments and chefs celebrated by the Michelin Guide and James Beard Foundation. After consuming countless calories in New York, San Francisco, Las Vegas, Chicago, Paris, Dubai, Hong Kong and Tokyo (as well as in remote eateries of Argentina, Italy, Lebanon, Peru, South Africa, South Australia, Spain, Sweden, Thailand and Vietnam), we hopefully earned enough stripes to consider ourselves legitimate foodies.
 
During a trip to the Big Apple just last month, we finally had dinner at Eleven Madison - a hot spot that has long been on our bucket list. Given its accolades and glowing reviews, my husband and I were sure that Eleven Madison would easily justify its place among the degustation elite. We ignored several friends who cautioned us that Eleven Madison's menu is now overheated (pun intended). But they were right. Our high expectations were crushed at first bite.
 
For example - rather than providing fine toast points or blinis or even a simple spoon (for roe purists), the introductory course was mismatched with dense corn flatbread, aggressively okra-infused, that overpowered any semblance of caviar flavor. The escargot was pungent and inedible. Never have I thought that caviar and escargot could be unpalatable, if not repelling. There truly is a first for everything. The remaining courses were either too salty or unbearably tart. Dessert was underwhelming and I recall only the last item, a chocolate-covered pretzel that imposed a lingering sour aftertaste.
 
The above assessment is my first Yelp restaurant review. I am compelled to share my thoughts because of respect for the culinary arts. Awarding three Michelin Stars to Eleven Madison dilutes the peerless value of truly exceptional restaurants in that class. Perhaps it was an aberrantly bad night for Eleven Madison, or maybe the pending dissolution of its owners' partnership (https://www.foodandwine.com/news/will-guidara-daniel-humm-eleven-madison-park-end-partnership) has diverted focus away from food to finances. Whatever the reason, I hope Eleven Madison finds its way back to the kitchen. Until then, I implore industry influencers of public perception to offer reviews with integrity. Please remember that your credibility is at stake.

Waking in, you appreciate the High ceilings and well appointed space. We were greeted right away and Bridget recognized our names from our reservations, came over and warmly welcomed us. You are treated like royalty from the moment you step in and until you leave. Everyone who attended to us greeted us for our anniversary and made us feel relaxed as we settled in for the evening. They are not stuffy and were very friendly, sharing stories with us when we asked questions. There was a little box on the table to start: it was an optional box to send away your cell phones for the duration of the meal to truly enjoy the experience. My water glass was never empty, the wine choices immense and the food presentation and quality amazing. Most surprising dish was the smoked tomato: wow. We also had to stop ourselves from consuming those buttery layered rolls: perfect for taking up any remaining sauce on the dish. The little "to go" bag with granola and keepsake menu in the tin was a nice touch. It was perfect from beginning to end!

Life changing! We did the prefixed menu (too many courses to count) with the wine pairings and it was all spectacular. Loved the atmosphere as it wasn't too "stuffy"...truly amazing staff as well! Would highly recommend to anyone visiting NYC and wanting a fine dining experience.

The service was impeccable, as was the space. 


As a tasting menu, there was 3 courses where you chose between 3 items. In my experience, usually they just keep bringing you food. 

The chefs were able to not only accommodate our religious dietary restrictions, but also my wife's personal dietary preferences. 

For these reasons, my wife and I had varying dishes with many courses, which works out because I got the chance to taste more items. 

The attention to detail is pretty incredible - they go as far as stamping the ice with their logos - pretty cool. 

There wasn't a course the entire night I didn't care for. My favorites were the duck, which they are known for, and the sheep's milk cheese cake with berries. The chocolate pretzel at the end is pretty amazing too. 

Excellent meal overall.

Came here on a Thursday night for post work drinks with colleagues. Impeccable service. Cocktails are approximately $20-24. A glass of white wines range from $15-25. Bar snacks were provided with drinks. Ended up staying there for 4 hours and we weren't rushed out at all, nor pressured/asked to dine there. Great bar for intimate drinks providing you are able to get seats. The bar has great selection of drinks too, would love that at my house.

Went here before for our anniversary celebration and the food did not disappoint. It is expensive because it's fine dining. We got a 12 course meal which are all small portions that are uniquely made. The whole experience and service was outstanding. My bf loves the venison butter. We got to bring home a jar of their granola for free which was good. =) i believe their menu changes depending on the season and they don't do the 12 course now (it's now 8-10 i believe). Definitely worth it but be prepared to spend $400 or more per person.

11 Madison Park is a very popular 3 Michelin Star restaurant featuring a multiple course tasting menu , wine pairings, as well as nonalcoholic beverage pairings. In addition they feature an extensive sophisticated wine list and cocktails. The space is elegantly beautiful, allowing the classic architecture and giant windows overlooking Madison Square Park to be the decor. We very much enjoyed our meal, which was seasonably summery and light. The Foie Gras, the Duck wIth Lavender, the Sea Bass, and the Eggplant were standouts and absolutely delicious. I was impressed with number of vegetable dishes offered as part of the menu or as a side dish, as vegetable dishes are often underrepresented or absent on tasting menus. All of these offerings were delicious. The wine pairings were lovely, and the juice/tea pairings were not only tasty but extremely creative. Service is very attentive, although in several cases so rushed in describing what we were eating or drinking the explanation went over our heads. This was particularly true with the beverage pairings. Further, there was an unending parade of waitstaff circling in front of our table (a system devised apparently so staff doesn't collide), that was ultimately distracting and slightly annoying. Overall we really enjoyed the meal, but if I go back, I will try the Bar menu and experience and not the dining room.

What an experience!
Me and my husband went there for the summer menu....no word to express the combinations of flavors and quality of this food.
I really enjoyed also the Peach cocktail

The 3 Michelin stars only serve to validate and quantify why your taste buds are dancing with unabashed joy.  

A truly fine dining experience.   Not just the fancy food or the fancy beautiful setting but the level of service is what makes you feel like a fancy lad or fancy lass.
Top notch quality.  Non-intrusive attention is a skill not many staff have but this place has it in spades.  The general manager looks young but it is clear that this lady has loads of experience running a smooth operation. 

Bread and butter are fantastic.   The wine list has only winners.  The food presentation makes you reflexively reach for your cell phone so you can attempt to capture the beauty of each carefully crafted plate.  
So snap away you amateur blogger, everyone else is doing it.

We ate at Eleven Madison Park last night for my birthday. The new summer menu came out earlier this week...it was delicious! EMP serves a set tasting menu, but we were given a choice of two or three menu items to select for some of the courses. 

The service at EMP was unmatched. We were greeted by name upon entering. Wow! The restaurant employs a "dreamweaver" to customize your experience so I encourage you to be forthcoming when they email you prior to your reservation so they have something to work with. Our server was much more friendly than at some other three star Michelin restaurants I have tried. In fact, she was the best waiter I've ever had!

At the start of our meal she asked if we would like to put our cellphones into a box to be returned at the end. I recommend putting at least one phone in the box because it's was rewarded with a treat to take home at the end of the meal.

We asked for a tour of the kitchen and I'm glad we did because they happily obliged and it was a great experience. 

Overall the food and service was incredible and I highly recommend the restaurant for a special occasion.

This was a very disappointing experience all around.  I had never eaten at a three star Michelin restaurant before, so I was so excited to eat at what is supposed to be one of the best restaurants in the world.  My brother and me had watched the seven days show in Netflix, as well as multiple  YouTube videos about this restaurant, in advance, to get us excited for the big night.

We arrived on 07-26-19.  The hostess was very nice and since we were early, she directed us to a two top table at the bar.  No one came up to this table for about ten minutes until finally I waived a sever down and he took our drink order.  This was already very surprising to me.  I would expect at a restaurant of this caliber that the moment you sit down, a waiter would be there welcoming you.

Our drinks did not come in time, so they were brought to our table in the main dining room.  The hot towels to begin with were a nice touch.  The first few dishes were great and came out as soon as we were done with the others.  Once the bread came out, things took a turn for the worst.  Crumbs were on our table for at least 30 minutes as well as dirty bread plates.  I had to ask the waitress (who was nice but not the caliber I was expecting) to crumb our table and clear our plates.  We waited..and waited for our next course.  The server even came over to apologize for the wait on our food. Normally I would appreciate the server apologizing, but this is eleven Madison, there should be no apologies.

Food was all good, but nothing mind blowing.  It was the service that truly surprised me.  I was expecting that as soon as we were done, plates would be cleared and the next course would arrive.  After about the fourth course, there was a big lag between courses.  There was even a table next to ours that was complaining to management about the poor food and service


I normally don't leave bad reviews, but I feel like upper management would be ashamed with the service we received tonight.  They seemed short staffed and you could feel it.  We looked forward to this all week, but unfortunately it was not the mind blowing experience we were expecting.

I have wanted to try Eleven Madison Park since 2017 when they won the best in the world resturant. Turning 60 in 2019 I decided it was going to be my Birthday present. 
I read the amazing review written by Brittany T,  and decided to try the bar menu. I had an appointment in NYC in July and decided to stay over and celebrate my birthday a month early. I waited for the first day of June and  went on the reservation site and was able to get my reservation for 6 pm in the bar on July 23rd.
I was blown away by far the best dinning experience I have ever had. I am still on cloud nine. Please read the review by Brittany T it is perfectly written and at point. Everyone should feel this way after an amazing food experience. Thank you to the amazing staff at Eleven Madison Park.

Just finished up my fifth trip to Eleven Madison Park. EMP never disappointed prior but after our last experience we will not be coming back to EMP. This saddens me since I've been such a loyal fan and patron to EMP for several years now. It's been about 7 months since our last trip and something drastic has changed with the restaurant. The food was just off, there were no "wow that was incredible" dishes. There was no flavor and each dish tasted the same as the prior dish. There were some issues with the service as well. Sauces were spilled while pouring and not cleaned up, the waiter spilled the apple brandy on my hand, and silverware wasn't cleared from prior serving. 

These may sound like little issues but when you're charging the money you charge for dinner things like this should not happen. In the four prior dining experiences this was never an issue and the service and food was incredible. 

Even our trip to the kitchen was not memorable. We had dined with friends who have not seen the remodeled kitchen. Prior kitchen tours would provide a nice little appetizer in the kitchen along with a little drink. It may not seem like a lot but the little details mean a lot. This time around we got a 2 minute quick kitchen tour with no appetizer.

Again, it hurts to type this review about such an amazing restaurant but something has changed at EMP. We will not be going back to EMP after our dining experience last night.

Had a wonderfully indulgent dinner with a group of close girlfriends. It's everything you expect and then much more.

Service is impeccable.  Food is beyond words. 

Such an experience and one you won't regret.

Outstanding food with a very unique blend of tastes and textures. The service is impeccable. The cocktails are truly unique and also incredible. The only reason I dropped them 1 Star is that the portions are too small. Having not eaten all day, we left a bit hungry after the 5 course tasting menu.
5-course tasting menu at bar areas. Arrive at 12pm. Several choices for each dish. Great places, nice good, wonderful experiences!

We were able to get a reservation at the number 1 restaurant on the World's 50 Best, at the time, and decided to go with the lunch option.  

Our reservations experience wasn't the best as we had a large group of 11 and had to take 2 reservation at different time slots about 45 minutes apart.... We weren't sure why they weren't able to move the tables together and join our groups as the dining experience does take 3+ hours which means there probably wouldn't be someone before our 11:30am reservations.  This doesn't take away from the amazing dining experience as it was made up from the service we received and food when we arrived.

From the moment you walk in to the way the dining room moved and how the kitchen was conducted, you can see how Eleven Madison Park won best restaurant in the world.  

I won't go through all the dishes as there was far too many to list.  My favorites were the Caviar dish, Duck breast, and Pate with Pumpkin Seeds.  These dishes were not only visually stunning, but tasted fantastic!  I felt like we were eating art with most of the dishes.

One of the best thing about dining at Eleven Madison Park was, we got to take a tour of the kitchen.  We contacted them ahead of time and requested this and they allowed us access to the kitchen which was very beautiful.  It was recently remodeled and everything was brand new.

Definitely worth the experience and something I would absolutely come back to in the future when visiting NYC.

You can't afford to miss this place. They have one of the most spectacular tasting menus and pair it with a massive wine list. An over the top culinary adventure that's perfectly served in a magnificent art deco space on Madison Square Park. It doesn't get any better than this. A brilliant standout amongst all the restaurants in Nyc.

This was the best food experience that I've ever had.  Unsurprisingly, the food is incredible.  Expect a healthy mix of playfulness in flavors and presentation (delicious in each case).

What differentiates EMP from other highly-rated restaurants, for me, is the service.  The staff all had a casual professionalism that came off as positively unpretentious.  As someone who didn't grow up with fine dining as a staple experience, I found this to refreshing.  I am absolutely looking forward to going again.

too much daikon dishes for this tasting round
messed up our order 
the service is 5 star
plating is not as impressive as michelin 3

Recently had lunch at EMP.  We had the 5 course bar menu.

The presentation was creative, flavors unique, and service was impeccable. 

However I would say thar IMO Le Bernardin is superior to EMP, but EMP is definitely worth a visit.

As a student of the Culinary Institute, I know how admired and respected this restaurant is in the food community. I get it. The food is excellent bc it looks fancy and complicated. But when I went with with one of my girlfriends, I had the most demeaning and utterly contradictory "service" experience. 

We were sat in the lounge area next to the bar, and during our second drinks, my girlfriend found out that a group of her friends were also coming to Eleven Madison to have drinks. When they arrived, they were sat at a bigger lounge table across from us, so we waved hello and acknowledged their arrival. We then asked the waitress if we could transfer to their table, when we were rudely rejected with a flat-out "No" and some conceited explanation of why we weren't allowed to move. Are we, the customers, supposed to serve your operational front of the house needs? Will such rearrangements make your receptionist's touch screen suddenly crack and explode with the changes that you make? There was plenty of room on the couch chairs for people to join. Sadly, we explained to our friends the situation, finished our second drink, and dipped without being able to hang. What's the point of a great restaurant if it's so sterile and self-regarded to the point they can't allow customers to join their friends?

Went to dinner at Eleven Madison Park on Saturday evening. An experience I was excited to be a part of, but one that did not live up to its billing. The exorbitant price tag does not leave any room for flaws, and unfortunately it was far from perfection.

Quality: Eleven Madison Park has been bestowed with about every honor a restaurant can achieve, including reaching the pinnacle as #1 on the S. Pellegrino World's 50 Best Restaurants in 2017. And while there is no doubt the meal I had was innovative and tasty, it did not come close to my lofty expectations. No dish left the impression that I would never eat something this delicious again. And while every course is beautifully conceived and plated perfectly, I just did not come away amazed. The Smoked-Sturgeon Cheesecake With Caviar is the star of the show, with the Seared Foie Gras, Spring Lamb, and the Duck as excellent dishes as well. But there were uneven bumps with the Crab, Snails, and Lobster. And without a truly transcendent dish or a flawless mix, it is difficult to rave too highly of the quality.
Quantity: Without the generous Wine Pairing, I think I would have left still hungry. The tasting has a good number of dishes, but nothing particularly substantial.
Value: $335 for the Dining Room Tasting Menu. $175 for the Wine Pairing.
Ambiance: Eleven Madison Park is located in the Flatiron District of Manhattan, across the street from Madison Square Park. It is found in the art deco Metropolitan Life North Building. Walking in feels a bit like walking into a bank, which is appropriate for the money you will be depositing. During the daylight it is not the most appealing looking space, but as it grows darker outside and the lights start to glow inside it becomes a bit more magical. Everything is perfectly in place, and a waiter will rush over the moment something changes. And while I only walked through the bar area, it was the design here that really was more awe-inspiring.
Crowd: If you are planning a visit, make sure you are sitting at your computer when the reservations first come online. This is a sold out experience every night of the week. Though I think you may want to consider the bar tasting for a more affordable option to experience Eleven Madison Park.
Service: Over the course of the meal you interact with a lot of staff. And while some were absolutely fantastic others were less so. I was amazed by the hostess and the sommeliers, but the waiters were very inconsistent. Some were incredible at describing the dishes and their inspiration, others barely said a word. Sitting between two other tables, I felt I heard three different descriptions of each dish and they varied wildly, which just seemed wrong.
Parking: No easily identifiable parking. Car service or subway seemed to be the options.

With the best fiancé in the world...she brought me here for my 31st birthday and I can't say enough about my experience. Later finding out it's been rated one of the best restaurants in the world, I'm glad I experienced my meal here unknowingly so I could approach this experience with no expectations. 

I haven't really experienced much fine dining, or have been to too many Michelin star restaurants but compared to the ones I've had, this was probably in the top 3 amongst dining experience, service, timing and of course the food.  Very unique tasting menu and sufficient staff. 

Couldn't have asked for a perfect dining experience and birthday gift, shout out to the best TT!

So disappointing. I've been to hundreds of michelin star rated restaurants. I would tell you to skip this one.  It took three hours to dine and the 6 of us couldn't wait for it to end. The chef must have gotten a special on trout. The cheese dish was a muffin pastry with only one type of cheese inside. They put 18 of the exact same muffins on the table. They could have been bought at Costco. Not like going to Gary Dankos in San Francisco or Le Cinq in Paris where the presentation of cheeses and desserts is out of this world.

There's a reason this place is always on the list of best restaurants.  The food presentation and flavor is amazing, however, I personally think the portions run small but typical for a fine dining place.  The wine selection is diverse and extensive.  The bar area is nice and relaxed.  This is one of my favorite places to go for a fine dining experience since they always make you feel welcomed (ie no jacker required, etc) and do not come across as pretentious.  The servers are always attentive but not overbearing.

I can't say enough about our experience at EMP. First off I am not a "fine diner" so I was a little nervous about feeling out of place at the worlds #1 restaurant. The staff could not have made me feel more comfortable and at "home". 

The reason for my visit was to surprise my girlfriend with a proposal (she said yes btw). The whole process was super personal, generous and thoughtful. Big thanks to Jennifer and Annelisa for going ABOVE AND BEYOND in helping me plan and execute a perfect surprise!

Eleven Madison is literally on everyone's list, be it a professional recommendation or yelp bookmarks. To make my virgin visit special, I decided to go big or go home. THIS IS A PRIVATE DINING REVIEW.
Pre Event: I started out by contacting them via email. The coordinator Maggie was professional and very detailed. I scheduled a visit with her a week before my event and she showed me around the rooms before I put down a deposit. As expected from a respectable restaurant, you sign a contract electronically when you put down the deposit, and then they send you additional forms to complete for the details of your party. They cover everything from decor to menu. They will follow up with you for confirmation.
Event: Sufficient staff was ready when the event began. They helped put up some balloons that we had, and offered space and hangers for bags, coats and other items that you may have. Professional and polite, all waiters and staff was patient and thorough. We had lunch there and we stayed for more time after dessert. They had one waiter in the room with us the whole time so we are definitely taken care of. 
Post Event: I received a follow up and thank you email the day after my event and I really felt like they took care of me.
It was easy, no-stress, no-surprise to plan and arrange with them. If you are looking for a space for a special occasion, I highly recommend Eleven Madison!

I am so happy my girlfriend and I decided to celebrate our anniversary here at Eleven Madison Park. Everything, and I mean everything could not have been more perfect. Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted and told happy anniversary! They really take the extra time to go through and make sure they study every reservation and the occasion just to make your entrance that much more special. Right when we got in, we were whisked away to our table where one of our many wonderful waiters and waitresses, Steve, came and congratulated us on our anniversary and also offered us our choice of drinks. Upon choosing still water and being offered their vast drink selection (really, the wine menu has an INDEX) we decided that the best and easiest route was to trust our Sommelier and get the "younger" wine pairing. After that, Steve expertly walked us through our dinner courses and even asked us to select 3 of our courses (which I truly enjoyed.)
And after that it was all a perfect if not magical show. Throughout the dinner not a single glass was left empty. Every course that was brought out made sense. The wine that went with every course made just as much sense. The explanations that went along with each course made our mouths water before even having our first bites. And of course, the service. The service is just bar none best service you can ever get at a restaurant. I kept complimenting the staff throughout our dinner because truly they deserved the highest praises. We had eaten at a neighboring 3 star Michelin restaurant the night prior and quite frankly, Eleven Madison Park absolutely destroyed them in all aspects (food, staff, atmosphere.) I was telling my girlfriend that the inviting atmosphere of the space alongside the perfect staff and the just as perfect food made me tear up just a little bit as I was so happy that a place like Eleven Madison Park even existed. If any of the staff chance upon reading this review, thank you thank you thank you. Keep up the amazing work.

Also! If you are deciding upon whether to put your phone in the box and taken away through the course of the dinner, please take this tip and do it!

Did the tasting menu. The food didn't blow me away compared to other three Michelin's in New York. But the food was still good. The waitstaff was excellent. The wine was amazing. I did the wine pairing. The staff was friendly. The atmosphere was great it was open and bright.

Second time here because I didn't remember much from first time and my foodie friend told me she really likes here so came here again. Good service and beautiful double height space. However food was good but not exciting. Maybe that's why I don't remember much from my first time here. I liked black truffle tea, foie gras with Brussels sprouts. The rest, caviar, lobster, golden mushroom and duck were rather mediocre.

Major disappointment. Went there for 60th  birthday with my wife. Started out great with a friendly greeting and we were immediately seated. Offered menu and wine and drink list. We chose a bottle of wine and ordered 2 cocktails. We were finished with our first course before either the cocktails or the wine were brought to our table.  A service mistake that could be overlooked at most places but this restaurant is currently #3 in the world and will probably soon be #1 again. 

The food was very inconsistent with some fantastic dishes like the sturgeon tart with caviar and some were just odd like the snails in steamed greens with a lettuce sauce. This was bitter and chewy. One of the best parts of our meal was the delicious granola which we were driven as we left the restaurant. 

I love good food and I'm willing to pay for it but I expected more from the likes of Eleven Madison Avenue.
I am hoping and praying I can spend my 60th birthday here, ten years after the most special meal of my life!

I was lucky to go here with my family on my birthday, but the restaurant did not live up to the hype. (This was in Feb). Every course was grey or brown and over salted. There was nothing exceptional or memorable about the flavors or presentation. The service was poor, multiple mistakes were made and the server did not know what was in each dish. Even the chocolate had way too much salt in it. Extremely disappointed. No where near as novel and memorable as le Bernardin.

We really loved EMP. Our menu included the following dishes:
- Trout custard 
- Steelhead trout served with bread and the best butter ever
- "Cheesecake" made of asparagus and cream cheese, with a everything bagel crust, topped with smoked sturgeon and caviar
- Seared Foie Gras 
- Lobster wrapped in green tomato
- Snails (brought out first in their shell, then sent back without)
- Duck* with peppercorn and lavender honey glaze
- Lamb*
*mains mentioned above came with snow pea and spring greens to share
- Cheese course with warm brioche buns with butter inside plus a whipped cream cheese and rhubarb 
- Dessert of a chocolate dish and a lemon dish with sesame (very unique)

We added the wine pairing to the tasting outlined above and were happy about it.

Also, if you hand your phone into their box at the beginning of the meal, you'll receive a very delicious chocolate with bee pollen and honeycomb!
Everything you want it to be. Perfect.
This place, the service, just amazing. Kevin, if you're reading this, thank you.

Updating based on my more recent experience.  Service is 5 stars, presentation is 5 stars.  but WHAT IS THIS SPRING 2019 MENU?? We had to force ourselves to eat many of the courses. I was so sorely disappointed to be out so much money for what was a pretty bad meal to be honest.  Barely passable to say it was even slightly good.. If I could describe this meal in a word it would be "mush" ..

1st course - mush (morel custard with trout roe. It was separated, super fishy, we had to force ourselves to eat it. so bad), followed by a pretty decent steelhead trout tartar (one of the only good dishes).  
2nd course - mush (fish cheesecake. It was not good.  They tried way to hard to be creative, and instead of saying hey, this tastes pretty bad, let's not serve this, they just soldiered on with confidence.)
3rd course - mush (a mushy crab dish, how they messed up crab I don't even know).  We also had the asparagus which was pretty okay, better than whatever the hell that crab dish was.
Let's pause here - did the chef not try his menu in succession and realize  that the textures for his first courses were all mushy? Or that most of it tasted weird?
4th course - delicious (we tried both the lobster and the striped bass, and both were really good.  The lobster was good but not mind blowing, the bass was really great).
5th course - snails .. biggest letdown ever.  We love snails, the flavors for this dish were not on point.  They present the snails so beautifully only to disappoint.  Also, more mush.
6th course - Probably the best of all.  We had both the duck and the lamb and they were both really good.  But you don't pay $335pp for just really good.
7th course - triple cream cheese in brioche with rhubarb and sorrel dips.  The dips were bad and the brioches were ok.  I think we were mushed out at this point and this was just more mush.
Dessert - We had both the strawberries and the ice cream and they were both good.  The chocolate covered pretzel was the highlight though, really delicious.

So overall, my 1st experience at EMP was near perfect, but unfortunately this 2nd experience was really bad.  If I were you I would wait a few months and hopefully they change the menu to food that actually tastes delicious and focus less on theatrics.  I wish I could get a refund for whatever that meal was.

Most expensive/high class restaurant i've been to! The food was an 11 course meal so it was quite fulfilling.

The service was exceptional and meticulous and so attentive. Every time we finished a course, they would come after an acceptable time to rotate the silverware and clean off the tablecloth for the next dish.

The food itself was good, but nothing exceptional. I loved the playing of the food and the running theme of wooden and simple presentation.

As for my favorite dishes, was definitely the appetizer with cream cheese. However, the rest of the courses were all quite heavy and hard to finish, especially the cheese dish. The halibut was great, the fish was so light and soaked up the sauce flavor. I loved the roasted duck, it was very fatty and had a bit of crunch on it. However, the rest of the courses focused one dimensional flavors that were heavily savory or acidic. The desserts were also very heavy aswell, i enjoyed the chocolate however it was very subpar.

Overall, an amazing experience and the food was always a presentation

Me and my mom had lunch here for Mother's Day and it was well worth it! The food is of course amazing. We expected a great meal, and it far surpassed our expectations! The staff was nothing short of amazing. Very nice, answered all our questions, and very personable. Felt VERY down to earth! Beautiful restaurant with amazing lighting. And my favorite part was the granola they give you to take home! Loved this experience, and will definitely be going back!

This is one of the top restaurants in the world. It's a four star Michelin restaurant and while I enjoyed the experience, I found it too upscale to fully enjoy. We booked a month before heading to the city, and so we were only able to get a 10pm reservation. That was a really late dinner, but since we were coming from West Coast time it was fine.

We did the chef's tasting and the service was amazing. They welcomed us at the door and knew our names and greeted us immediately. While it was amazing, you knew you had to be very proper as it was a fine dining establishment. The food was very much prepared and presented in a delicate and artistic way. Delicious but with all fine dining, portions were quite small so it was more for sampling than fully indulging into each dish. 


Book way in advance!

Food: 5*
Service: 5*

Food was impeccable and though dinner lasted 3 hours, it went very quickly.

My favorite dishes of the night were the savory sturgeon cheesecake, foie gras, and cheese course. 

For the main, duck or lamb were the options. I was going to have lamb because it was easter, but ultimately chose the duck and I'm glad I did. Tender, crisp skin, and the sauce that went with it was rich.

The chocolate dessert with ice cream was good, but I treated the apple brandy as my dessert. The granola they provided was some of the best I've had, but I've never made it myself, so I don't have a baseline to compare it to. 

Overall service was spot on. They were attentive the entire meal yet not stuffy, and very down to earth which I like. The worse is when a staff acts all high and mighty because of the setting you are in and this wasn't the case at all despite the high accolades it has received.

Yes, it isn't a cheap meal, but the my experience was top notch from walking through the door to leaving the rotating doors with my goodie bag of granola. If I can't replicate the duck at home, I would come back for it, and the apple brandy...and the granola.

This was the best meal of my life. The service was seamless and gracious. My SO and I felt transported to another world. The food was amazing and each course was better than the previous one.

Reservations - You pay in advance, which is great because you don't have to worry about the restaurant cancelling on you or calling to confirm your reservation. And your meal is paid for.

Drinks - I don't drink much but I really enjoyed my cocktails. I got the "soft" Chocolate one and I still dream about it. I also had one "collaborative" cocktail.

Entrees - I like the surprises you get with a tasting menu. My favorite dishes were the oyster mushroom (both the flavors and the table-side preparation) and the famous duck.

Dessert - I loved the donut and ice cream.

Souvenirs - They gave us a printout of our menu and a jar of granola to take home.

For what was once the top restaurant in the world, my trip to Eleven Madison Park was incredibly disappointing. The only thing I can think of when the foie gras comes to mind is salt. The "famous" duck was rubbery and the dessert was ruined by a grainy shortbread. All in all, not worth the heartbreak! You spend money only to get your image of fine dining completely and utterly destroyed. My only thought was 'What standards were used to judge this as the finest restaurant in the world?'. Thankfully I have had good experiences elsewhere. Otherwise I would be of the opinion that fine dining is just a sham.

Yes of course food & wine were perfectly paired, but considering the hype for this place , I didn't find it special at all. Everything tasted on the same pallet, kind of same taste fore 7 dishes we had. I guess I'm not very sophisticated. Good food. 1000 waiters. But Nothing outstanding

I've been wanting to go to Eleven Madison Park for a very long time, and my interest was elevated when they topped the Pellegrino World's 50 Best Restaurant List in 2017. Now that my time on the east coast is coming to an end and I'm moving back to California, I figured what better way to celebrate my time here than visit EMP!

I came here with 3 other diners and our overall impression was that while the food was good, it unfortunately did not live up to the high expectations. 

Overall, I enjoyed the beginning of the tasting menu more than the end. My favorites included the morel custard, steelhead trout, and the duck, and the caviar cheesecake was definitely the most interesting/creative. Underwhelming dishes included the lobster and chocolate dessert, and everything else fell in between. 

The spacing of the courses was excellent at the beginning, but then began to drag on near the end of the evening. Service was professional, friendly, and knowledgable, as expected of a restaurant of this caliber. The interior was not my favorite - the cavernous ceilings and dim lighting made for a weird clash between grandeur and coziness. 

Overall, I think had I entered the experience with lower expectations, I would have enjoyed the food more. However, 3 michelin stars + #1 restaurant in the world in 2017 made for extremely high expectations, which were unfortunately not met. Glad I gave EMP a try, but don't think I'll be back anytime soon.

4.5 stars but decided to round up.

After hearing it was the number 1 restaurant in the world back in 2017, getting 3 Michelin stars and seeing the Netflix episode of 7 Days Out, my husband and I decided to bite the bullet and go to Eleven Madison before we leave New York for good

RESERVATIONS: You can make reservations on Tock (online reservation website).  They open reservations at 9AM (Eastern Time) on the first of every month for the following month. So if you want to make reservations in April, you should make them on the Feb 1.  I would suggest making a Tock profile ahead of time, setting an alarm and doing it right away. You do have to pay for the meal upfront so have your credit card information saved and at least 2 back up dates in case yours is not available.  Otherwise, when I checked back around 9:15 to see what else was available there were still spots left so it's not horrible.

ATMOSPHERE: We got the bar menu, which I'll describe below but that means you sit at the bar area instead of the main dining room.  It's not as nice because it's darker and not as airy but it's still a nice area.  You get an actual table with chairs instead of a bar stool or a low bar table with chairs.  Those are for walk ins, but for reservations you are pretty much dining as if you are in a regular restaurant.  The atmosphere is semi-formal, clean, modern etc.  It doesn't have a super trendy vibe but not stuffy or old either.

BAR MENU - because we weren't willing to drop $300+ for a dinner per person we opted for the bar menu and I think it was a great decision.  It comes out to about $175/person and this includes tax and tip! It's 5 courses plus you also get unlimited bread, a special second treat at the end and a take home item.  Their menu changes seasonally so I won't go into specifics but you basically get to choose 3 of the 5 courses and then the other courses are set.  When you choose, they give you 3 or so options to choose from.  Order of food:
1. Caviar
2. Fois Gras, Crab or Asparagus option
3. Lobster
4. Duck, Lamb or Veggie option
5. Lemon or Chocolate dessert

My favorites were the lobster and my lamb.  The food is really good.  It's kind of your typical fancy, new-american food but usually each one has a twist or unique presentation about it.  It's not going to be like Alinea, but for example, the Caviar was served in these tins and had little English muffins and it was their take on a caviar eggs Benedict.  Everything had good flavor but I will say it didn't blow me out of the water.  

The courses go by quickly so we finished everything in about 1 hr and 45 minutes.  They don't rush you but the portions aren't huge so you finish them pretty quickly and they don't make you wait around for the next course like some restaurants.  It didn't feel drawn out.

SPOILERS - you do get a special "dessert pretzel" at the end one for each person and they also give you a jar of granola per person to take home including a personalized menu with the date and what you ordered as well as a little saying if you're celebrating something.

KITCHEN TOUR - about a week beforehand, someone will email you asking if you are celebrating anything special (might as well tell them you are to get extra special treatment) and if they can do anything for your stay.  Request a kitchen tour in that email and also remind the waiter when you come in because they put in the request as well.  It's not guaranteed but they say if there is space and availability they'll give it to you.  For us, it was the highlight of the meal because you get to see behind the scenes and someone personally escorts and shows you the kitchen.  They also take plenty of pictures of you inside the kitchen.

SPOILERS - you also get to play a little game where we sipped on 3 sodas and tried to guess which spices were in the sodas.  It might change per person but it was really fun and a nice interactive way to end the night.

SERVICE - I don't normally talk about the service but this was one to be mentioned and why Eleven Madison is also 5 stars.  Their servers, wait staff, hostesses, etc. are all very attentive and basically know what you need or want before you even say or ask.  They are mindful of how they place things on the table, how they serve your food, how they describe your food, folding your napkin, pulling out your chair etc.  I felt very cared for although they weren't overbearing and knew how to be in the background and not interrupt our dinner.  Our waiter was very knowledgeable AND...they asked to refill our bread twice without us even asking!

Overall, Eleven Madison is an investment but for the bar menu price, it's worth it because you feel full and satisfied and get most of the same perks except you eat less and don't dine in the main dining room.  The person who showed us the kitchen even said the courses/food is pretty much the same just with a few added extras (for example, more things served table side etc.).

I have 4 AVAILABLE SEATS on:
4/29/19 MON at 5:30pm BAR SEATING 

Reservation cancellation experience was terrible so far. My cousin has canceled her wedding, so we are no longer flying into New York. Found on their website that they do manage a wait list for any cancellation. Called the restaurant more than a month ago and said never had a problem filling the seats to those on wait list. So I count on their words and has changed my air tickets to go somewhere else instead. Called them again 1 week before and now they said no promise and no guaranteed and will just try their best to fill the seats. What they meant by filling the seats is just if someone does ask for the exact day and exact time, then they will give them a call, otherwise they are not going to put any extra effort to ask the rest on wait list.  Apparently that is not going to be guaranteed which I understand. But since they sounded very promising at first, and now turned around and said something totally different, I would not trust their words ever again.

Amazing restaurant, we sat in the bar room and had the 5 course option. The granola that you are given at the end is amazing!
I loved every moment of the experience!
Wonderful food. Wonderful service. A unique experience worth the hype. It's a place one never forgets.

Eleven Madison Park is on every foodies bucket list. Is it the best restaurant in the world. Hell no. Is it amazing...yes. The flavors are those you have had before just sophisticated with accompanying service that treats you like royalty. Forget about the number one in the world factor and come enjoy an exemplary experience. Bartender is great. Crowd is sophisticated. The beef tartare with foie gras was phenomenal as was the lamb. Your taste buds will thank you.

One of my friends who has worked as a cook at Michelin restaurants on two continents warned me that I would be disappointed, and he was right. At this point in my life I am really looking for a wow factor, something unexpected in taste or presentation at this price point. 

EMP serves European food mostly in a classic style with unique and high quality ingredients. All of the dishes were expertly made, but none tasted different than I would imagine to the point that I though anyone with enough time could find similar ingredients and execute close enough. My cousin asked me which was my favorite dish and it was the first, dosa,  which was simply black truffle in like a thin eggroll batter and fried. I also enjoyed the caviar and souffle dish even though I have definitely had better caviar.

Fantastic service. Wish they comped coffee and tea like Alinea. Bathrooms seemed minimalistic for a 3 star...

Love the service at this restaurant, great attention to detail. The staff is very well-trained, and making sure you are having the best experience. That's why I keep coming back to this place. Every dinner is unique and tastes amazing.

Seriously was like 3 hour meal and at the end I needed to be rolled out of the restaurant. Many dishes were great! I loved the mushroom and potato dishes the most! The potato was light and great for starter dish. The mushroom was crispy on the ends from roasting. The earthy taste of everything mushroom was amazing. The donut dessert was the best. You seriously get full. 

I opted for collaborative cocktail and I loved my drink. Tasted like the old fashion popsicle.

They were quite attentive and always slide the table when I had to get up. 

Requested for the kitchen tour it was awesome! Got to see all the people working and had fun sodas to taste. 

Definitely a place to try at least once if you're in the area. RSVP early though! Tips included in the reservation online. 

Came here for my fiancé's bday and they even made him a card! They give you a gift to take home at the end (for everyone, home made granola).

Eleven Madison Park has been an interesting ride....  When first enjoying the experience about three years ago, the evening was fantastic (a show in and of itself)!  Then came the revised menu style about two years ago with fewer dishes / not as much presentation and there was a huge drop off in the quality of the experience which made me sad that I'd never again enjoy an experience equivalent to the first (likely when they were receiving votes to move to #1). Went last night and had a lovely time!  Though still a bit of a dip from EMP of three years past, the dishes last night were delicious and we had a great time!  The staff was lovely as well.

Wow... 

EMP is ON POINT & then some!
It definitely deserves all the hype.

Attention to Detail.
Exceptional Service.
Beautiful Restaurant.

The Bar Tasting Menu was PERFECT for us!
Everything was INCREDIBLE!

Well worth it!

I won't add to all the well-deserved kudos, dining there was an ethereal experience.  I simply wanted to comment on the wine flights.  They come in the 170 and the 350 ranges, so my wife and I tried one of each.  The 170 version did not offer much that was special, and while the 350 version had a couple of extraordinary things on it (a perfectly balanced Sauternes, a 2004 Châteauneuf and a wonderfully weird thick sherry from Andalucia), it was disappointing.  To begin, you are given more white than red wine (I'm a red drinker mainly), and lots of champagne at the beginning, a wine I've never quite seen the point of (so sue me).  Moreover, since we were there early, at 6, many of the bottles were just opened and took time to develop in the glass; and since you're only getting a few sips, your experience with the best of each one is limited.  This was especially true of the Chassagne-Montrachet, which only tasted like the wonderful wine I know in the last sip.  Perhaps it would be a good idea to uncork some bottles early and let them breathe a little in the bottle.  In any case, if you know something about wine and rely on the wait staff (which knows them well) you are probably better off getting your own bottle or two half-bottles. For $500+  you could really indulge in something special.

I'm at a loss for words, and feel as though words wouldn't do this meal any justice anyway. 

From being met at the front door by the hosts who took my luggage and comforted my anxiety because I had a boatload of stuff, to being escorted to the restroom, my experience was impeccable. I arrived right at noon which was just in time to hear the staff say their daily "Oui!" during preshift. Needless to say it gave me the chills. The tables are moved and swiveled around every time you sit down and get up, and your napkin is replaced with a new one. There's never a crumb on the table, and my water  glass was never empty. 

I was greeted with a glass of champagne, and I feel as though whenever this happens unexpectedly at a restaurant you feel extra special. Each dish was explained and presented so beautifully and cleared just as elegantly once you're through. I had the extreme pleasure of going back to the kitchen and seeing where the magic happens--It's so neat and quiet you could hear a pin drop. The chef introduced himself and I thanked him over and over for having me and treating me like royalty. Everything tasted just how it looked, amazing. As a send off, the mignardise you're given is container filled with granola along with the menu of everything you ate. 

I feel so lucky to have been able to experience the #4 restaurant in the world, and I implore you to not pass it up if you're ever in New York City.

What can I say, this place is an experience and truly 5 stars. From the bartenders that'll mix whatever is to your liking, to the amazing courses, the superb staff, this place is an extremely strong recommend. It's no wonder it's consistently in the top ten restaurants in the world.

Didn't live up to expectations of previous meals (pre-remodel) and EMP Beach House (East Hampton pop-up). An air of arrogance that at some points was overly pungent by staff. Or, entirely the opposite with our server saying "amazing" over and over.  Champagne chocolate cocktail was unique and delicious. The menu I felt was trying too hard. Caviar souffle was superb. Fresh scallop was unique, it's flattened to almost resemble pasta - kind of rubbery which wasn't so great. Beet dish was meh. Next, lobster course, lovely, but not mind blowing. The dry aged veal was good, the duck was good as well. Dessert this is where the presentation should blow your mind - mrrr, mrrrr - it's April - they were offering a gingerbread chocolate dish, cheese course that was a bread pudding, pumpkin and squash cake. What?! "We haven't changed to Spring menu". What?! We enjoyed the wine pairing. I'd say it's a skip, if on your must have restaurant tries -  it's a sprinkle in the bucket at best.

EMP deserves to be on every foodie's bucket list.  Definitely a special occasion restaurant where you will pay top dollar to be blown away.  Service is outstanding.  Attention to detail is unmatched.  And though it is expensive and Michelin starred, does not feel overly stuffy.

Definitely make reservations far in advanced if you want dinner service.  The bar area serves some small bites and reservations are much easier to make here.  Great if you do not want the full tasting experience and just want to try a few dishes.

Wtf this place was good. The service was PHENOMENAL. The food was amazing! Just don't think about the price. The wine pairing is a must do. The somms do a great job of pairing and it's overall an amazing experience. Questioning whether or not I should just come here every time I come to New York or not.

This is a restaurant that inside has been ranked in the top five in the world for a long time, and it is still the fourth in the world until today.  I don't need to say much about the taste of the dish and the dish itself. I specially ordered a Medium rare for the fried duck meat for the main course. I wanted to see the level of the three Michelin star chefs. as I expected, the color of the cross section of the duck meat was perfect. every layer from fully cooked to bloody was very obvious, but for the main course, I think there was a problem in the amount of food.  A gentleman next to me ordered the same duck, but his piece was at least twice as big as mine. I don't know why.  The service in the restaurant is very good. Although my English is not bad, it is not enough to order dishes. They provide waiters who can speak Chinese, which allows me to perfectly express my demand for dishes to the restaurant.  I ordered a cup of very fresh red wine, which was very comfortable with duck meat. My whole mouth was full of the fragrance of spring.  Generally speaking, this is a very good dining experience, and I would recommend my friends to come here to eat.

I celebrated my boyfriends birthday here. It was an amazing experience and completely worth the money spent. It is 3 hours long where you are welcomed with genuine enthusiasm and treated to a great culinary journey. The staff are well trained, amicable, enthusiastic about their job and truly there to make this an all rounded experience. It is not just about the food that makes this place stand out, and that's why the five stars. I cannot wait to go back. There's no point talking about food here cos with 3 Michelin stars it's all the same- great quality and taste that is to be expected with this caliber. The service is what MAKES the DIFFERENCE and is why eleven Madison park is amongst the top 5 restaurants in the world. Again, shout out to the staff - you guys really are appreciated.

I'm only sad that my boyfriend left the very nice jars of muesli in the Uber ride home. It's been on my mind for days. It would have been such a great souvenir for an amazing time at this restaurant.

I'm struggling between giving this a 3 star or 4 star review. Don't get me wrong, it's a really good restaurant and you will not be disappointed. But I think most people come here to be blown away, and it just won't happen. The first dish, the caviar soufflé was probably my favorite. And they have really great bread. Everything else was okay, nothing to really rave about. The duck was certainly interesting and tasty with the lavender and peppercorn crust, but I had a hard time cutting it with my knife. The veal was good but not super memorable. Same with the lobster, good but not great. I think the scallop was my least favorite and the husband agreed, salty and a little fishy. And the chocolate dessert kind of sucked, the pumpkin squash one is way better. Also, prepare for the pour of a $40 glass of Pinot noir to be light. A good restaurant for sure, but not my favorite. I will be generous today.

This has been on my restaurant dream / bucket list for some time.  The meal was good but left me wanting something more.  It is hard to put a finger on it, but we didn't find the food to be as good as at world class peers (other Michelin two or three stars), the service was competent but didn't feel as special as at some others.  There were awkwardly long waits at the start of the meal, and I felt the wine pairing was a bit skimpy.

Some nice touches like a trip to the kitchen and tasting game, along with a very cute keepsake photo.  

All the food was good, but felt out of step.  We dined the first week of spring and almost every dish featured mushrooms - a very fall and winter ingredient heavy menu (even "winter squash"). It didn't seem to reflect the bright spring day I would expect at a top restaurant with a seasonal menu.

I'm glad I went, but may have enjoyed the Netflix version ("7 Days Out") more.

Mission accomplished! Special Thank to Laura,Lisa @lizalouwnyc and @elevenmadisonpark  3-Michelin Starred and No.1 50's Worlds best restaurants2017.This restaurant was on my bucket list :The Worlds 50 Best Restaurants and Michelin Guide After last year I've been Gaggan (Progressive Indian Cuisine),Bangkok ...It's challenging to get a reservation :Me from LA to New York - Basically you need to set aside sometime at the beginning of the month to catch a date for the following month to reserve on their website- Miss it by a half-hour and you will likely be out of luck ...Eleven Madison Park is very long meal however be prepared to sit and slowly pace through each course for 3 hours in total. My seasonal tasting menu :11 courses had dishes with Black Truffle ,Caviar, Foie Gras,Lobster,Veal Dry-aged14 days,Duck honey and lavender Glazed ,Golden oyster mushroom and more. Service was outstanding and Food is amazing - Except cheese fondue and desserts.

This place was wonderful, don't get me wrong -- however, I don't understand why it's rated #4 in the world. I've had many dinners at better restaurant. I just expect more out of a restaurant that's supposed to be "the best".

Everything was cooked wonderfully and the presentation was top notch. The service was wonderful too. I found it really funny how when the wait staff comes around to clear plates, they do it almost synchronized at each table- collecting plates at the same time, with the same motion. 

There are a lot of table side preparations. They were really fun and unique. My favorite was definitely the old fashioned way of opening a bottle of port. The woman heated up the neck of the bottle and then broke it off by brushing cold water on it. The broken part of the bottle was sealed with the restaurant's symbols and was packaged up in a cute box to take home as a souvenir. Oh yes, they have phenomenal mocktails here too :)

The food is great. I'm not going to do a run down of all the food I ate but, the memorable ones were the black truffle dosa and the duck. The duck was cooked the perfection and the skin was so crispy and crackly. I loved it!!

I'd recommend this place if you're curious however, please don't go into this restaurant expecting the best meal you'll ever eat (you may be disappointed).

This was truly an amazing experience. You can taste the labor of love the chefs put into the food . The staff is very attentive and my water glass was never empty and they pre-empted our every need. The mushroom course was AMAZING!!! It is one of the most delicious things I've ever tasted in my life. The food was creatively plated and ambiance was lively.  I'm gluten-free and I felt my meal was not at all compromised to accommodate my dietary needs. My courses were very similar to my husband's courses, which were not GF. They even gave us goodie bags to go for us and our 4 children! The granola they give you for "breakfast" is delicious and allows you to reminisce about the delicious dinner you had the night before. We stayed across the street at the EDITION and we enjoyed our dining experience so much that we went to the bar to have cocktails on the other days we were in NYC. The bartenders definitely know how to craft a delicious libation. If you are planning to visit NYC, make a reservation at Eleven Madison. You will not be disappointed.

My wife and celebrated our 26th anniversary here last night and it lived up to its reputation.

Even before we got there, someone emailed to ask if we had any special requirements which was a really nice touch.  When we got there, they asked again about special requirements but also about things we didn't like and then adjusted the menu accordingly (mostly).  At every step, the service really stood out (and you aren't allowed to tip).  The people were beyond competent but also really friendly.  For a three Michelin-starred restaurant, the people were really not stuffy.

Each of our nine (or was it 10) courses was amazing and very imaginative.  While they were each amazing, I would call out the golden oyster mushroom roasted with pine and coriander and the harbison washed rind cheese fondue with mustard and pear.  Maybe even better than the food was the bread.  AMAZING!

We also went with the wine pairing. I think its actually a pretty good value since you get more than half a bottle of wine per person.  They did a great job pairing each course with an appropriate wine.  We had two champagnes, a couple of Italian reds, a couple of French wines and finally a Spanish sherry that was out of this world.

I had two smallish negatives about the experience.  First, I think some of the wines were a too bit "off the beaten path."  To their credit, they offered other wines when we said we didn't like what they offered.  I think they should consider having the somm first inquire about what you like/don't like and then recommend the pairings rather than offering up a pre-chosen list.  Also, and sorry to be a snob, the wines they offered for the pairings were B+ wines at best.  I get that they aren't going to pour DRC or Chateau Lafite but I thought the wines were just good, not great.  If (or when) I go back, I would probably order wines myself and worry less about how they pair with the food.

Celebrated my 6 year anniversary here and it was truly a top notch experience. This 3-Michelin Starred and once #1 on World's 50 Best Restaurants actually met my expectations after being on my bookmarks for so long... we all know how disappointing expensive and highly raved about fine dining can be a let down sometimes. Eleven Madison Park is a very long meal however, be prepared to sit and slowly pace through each course for 3 hours in total.

I highly recommend that if you're already here, go for the full experience ride and opt for the wine pairing. I don't find myself usually enjoying a lot of wine nor am I a wine connoisseur by any means, but their wine pairing was absolutely GENIUS. Every glass was fantastic and paired seamlessly well with the dishes. High warning that you will leave out of here really tipsy from it too! On our seasonal tasting menu we both had dishes with black truffle components and black truffle tea, soufflé with clams and caviar, roasted oyster mushrooms, leeks, and a cheese fondue dish. Some of my highlights of the meal were the seared foie gras... so amazing and perfect especially the wine accompanying this. As a big fan of duck meat, the duck breast with honey and lavender glazed was spectacular. My boyfriend had scallop with sea urchin, halibut, and dry aged veal which were all delicious. Each dish truly had so many depths of layers in elements and flavor from top to bottom. Not a single dish that we were served fell short.
