I don't think I would return to Eleven Madison Park, simply because if someone asks me which 3 Michelin Star restaurants in NYC I would I recommend, the answer would be "I've only been to four, and so far my favorite is Per Se."

We're looking to try Le Bernardin and Masa later this year and that will conclude our list of the current 3 Michelin Star restaurants in NYC.  No, I didn't forget Chef's Table; it's in Brooklyn, not my thing (no offense to Brooklyn).  Will gladly await its Manhattan opening in 2017.

When you get invited to join a group of 5 to dine at one of the best restaurants in the country, you say yes and grab your prettiest dress for the closest. My dinner went on for 4.5 hours and included wine pairings for all of our 10+ courses, one of which was in the kitchen (dessert). Look, to be honest, not everything was perfection but most of it was. The least impressive thing was the carrot tartare that was shaved table side. It was cute to watch though. Some of the wine bottles went back decades and the wait staff and hosts were phenomenal. My hats off to them for such a wonderful experience. My favorite part aside from the simple pleasure of experiencing that with a group of amazing people was the foie gras dish that melted in your mouth. We kept raving about it so they sent out a second plate, so we had 2 of the same course, lol. I'll go back any day.

Ate here two days ago and the food was good and the service was very friendly and helped to make us and other consumers relaxed. There was only really one major gripe with the whole experience which was when we were near the main course the pace of the food started to slow considerably where we literally started to fall asleep. 

However the table next to us had a stable flow of dishes coming in (and he even came in after us and finished quite a bit before our table of two while he was by himself). Although he was probably some important figure (checked out his Instagram and he seemed to be a food blogger/chef) or someone associated with someone important as the waiters and other staff kept coming to greet him and saying how they're so honored to meet him and showed him round the kitchen. 

I don't mind the special treatment that the VIP received however for a meal that costs a base of 300 the pacing of the food shouldn't fall too far behind. Apart from that however the whole experience was good and I would definitely come again. On a side note for those who are not familiar with the restaurant the menu changes every 3 months according to the waiter (overheard the conversation with the VIP next to us).

If you eat a dinner in this restaurant, you are gonna be undergone 'Real Innovation.'
 Jun/16/2016, I felt, saw, tasted, smelled awesome cuisines. Before this restaurant, I even tried almost Michelin 3stars restaurants, at that moment, I felt marvelous experience.

This is a very late review... we had an extraordinary, quintessential NYC, and bluntly put - a freaking expensive AF 16 (18?? Lost count after 9) course lunch last July.   I had a bit of a reviewer's block bc 1) what value could I add that hasn't been said about the amazing EMP? 2) how do I go about critiquing the food w/o offending the die hard fans of this beloved 3M stars haven? And finally 3)  can anyone really justify paying $8 Benjamins for lunch more than once? 

I'll start with this... I love love love the entire experience, from stepping into what used to be a bank with high ceilings, white glove services (each employee has a job - including Miss Universe (her posture puts me to shame! Ugh...) carrying a tray of forks/spoons/knives for every setting) to the often "over the top" presentation and ending with a child's dream in the form of a popsicle! (Serve to you by a little old man at his cart! Talk about paying forward! - nicely done EMP!)

As for food, the most memorable in my mind was the delicious individual tin can of caviar serve using a mother of pearl spoon! How expensive!?!  (Probably unnecessary...) and the asparagus cooked in a pigs' bladder (don't hold your breath, it's just 1 stalk!) and the dessert course that reminded me of some science lab!  So why wouldn't this magical place get the rightful 5 stars?!?! 

OK - now I will share my experience on why I took a star away.  There was an organic carrot course, where the sous chef comes out and demonstrates with a table top grinder. It's what some have called "adults playing w/ food" - presented with fixing such as nuts, seeds, cream.  I am NOT a huge fan of carrots and I've mentioned that to our server. So needless to say, I had left over.  Apparently that must be a "frown upon" thing at these type of establishment (ur a freak if u don't lick ur plate...)  I was "ASKED" not once, twice but 4x as to why I didn't finish my carrots?!?!  Server, sous chef assistant, the guy who manages our table, & the water server... Seriously?!  It's carrots... It was tasteless, boring, and not very pleasing.  Was I beyond annoyed? Eff yes!  Bottomline, no one should ever force you to eat uninteresting of anything or "food shame you"! Especially for $8 Big Ben!  Ugh...

Listen, if you have $$$$, go wild! Reservation takes a few tries and only goes up to 30 days at a time, good luck & happy feasting!

I went to this place last month. The ambience was great and seat was arranged to have a very spacious view. The price is very reasonable as a Michelin three star restaurants. The food is awesome as well ! The Caviar Benedict as a appetizer is my favorite. It is very flavory with creamy taste. I had steak and fish as my main dish. Honestly , the appetizer is more creative and impressive. We had a kitchen tour after our dinner and had a small ice treat. It was an amazing experience with the service and food ! If you really want to have some Michelin three star restaurant experience in Nyc . I would recommend this one as a first choice!

When you are going to a three Michelin-star restaurant, expectations are of course high. So high I would say, that the experience is always a bit disappointing. Everything is so relative. This is why I most often really applaud for two- or one-star places, or restaurants that have no star what-so-ever. They are the challengers and in that group I find restaurants that really make me feel that my expectations were exceeded. They are often more reasonably priced as well. However, 11 Madison Park is the probably the best three-star I have ever visited. No, not the best restaurant, there are a few dinners I rate higher. A three star is always slightly stiff. However, food, wine, service and ambiance, they were all awesome.

I will start with the wines in this review. The list at 11 Madison was great and the sommelier did a super job. We always prefer to try some local wines when we travel. Perhaps not always in Asia, but for sure in the US and Europe. New York state wines were quite new to me, so the friendly sommelier picked a few from the wine list that represented the style of different wine regions in the area. He even opened a few bottles that we not on the by-the-glass list, so that we could taste them. And everything we were able to get in half glasses. That's pretty great service.

There was only one six course menu. We were asked for any specific food-allergies, so I assume they accommodate special diets (even Ms "no oysters" diet), however no specific selection can be made in the start. During the dinner, we were able to, however, make some individual choices on courses. The six courses was also a bit of an illusion, as there were so many small extra tasters, that one kind of lost track on what was a course and what was not. It was just a four hour food festival with continuous snacking. I will not write the whole list of courses we had here, but I can mention a few favorites: eggs Benedict with mini muffins perhaps being my favorite. We also had really great lamb (three different pieces) and our dessert was a baked Alaska that was flambéed at the table. There was also a fun chocolate tasting at the end of the dinner. We got four chocolate bars that were all made with different milk (cow, goat, lamb and buffalo), and we were supposed to guess which is which. It was actually quite hard even though each chocolate bar tasted distinctly different.

All in all the damage was around 400$ per person. Around 300$ of that accounted for food and service was included (yay! I hate tipping). And yes, that is a lot of money. However, for a three star meal including a flight of sommelier picked wines, I did not feel all weak in the legs when pulling out the Amex. We have had significantly worse value for money meals, and this felt more like an investment into the memory bank. The meal was worth every penny.

Cyndy's Bottom Line:  A magnificent dining experience!

I was so excited when my hubby got the reservation at Eleven Madison Park (EMP).  EMP is rated as the 5th best restaurant in the world for outstanding service.  So we were ecstatic.

We were early at EMP and the staff meeting was being held in the beautiful dining room.  They were so nice to let us in to sit and have drinks in the bar area.  Off to an excellent start!  The structure and interior of the restaurant is in art deco.  The high wall to ceiling windows are magnificent in casting a natural, serene light into the dining room.

We sat in the bar and had cocktails.  I love the bar snacks.  Hand made potato chips, olives and nuts.  Hubby had a black Manhattan and I had a prosecco.

This is what we ate/drank:
Black & White Savory cookie with apple and cheddar

Whitefish Salad - Morel with rye crisp well fleet oyster with caviar

Caviar Benedict with spring onion and ham

Foie Gras Seared with sorrel and fava beans

Lobster butter poached with dandelion and ginger

Asparagus braised with potato and black truffle

Title fish
Roasted with carrots and nettle and broth
New Potatoes variations with flowers
Morel custard with spring garlic

Strawberries poached with vanilla and elderflower.

Chocolate "Name that Milk"
Chocolate Pretzel with sea salt and Apple Brandy.
Def a stuffy feeling upon entering here. Food is great, drinks even better. But it's a very corporate environment, be prepared.

I'll keep this short since this is EMP. Everybody already knows all about this place. I flew in from Chicago for the weekend and set up a reservation through a concierge service. It's much less pretentious than you expect. In fact, a lot of the 1 star Michelin places I've eaten at have had stricter dress codes. 

Truly, eating at EMP is about the food. Be prepared to spend 2 hours hear. We actually had plans afterwards so they managed to squeeze the final desert/game into a shorter time span for us. I came away satisfied completely and we even got little gift bags. 

If you can swing the money, just do it. It's hard to get a reservation, but it's well worth it.
A unique dining experience with impeccable service. The drinks are fabulous and the ambiance is perfect. A younger clientele compared to other restaurants of this caliber.

I mean when you first walked in and was greeted w a birthday wish, you know this place is on top of their game!  We haven't been back for nearly 10 years and they have become much more creative and innovative with the dishes and presentation! There's an element of surprise for each dish!  And they had sparking pointe champagne!

"Unlikey Suspect Turned Chef" We got dropped at the park out front, wanted to take it all in, from the outside in. It was a bit chilly but the sky was clear and the building had a certain glow to it. The architecture was charming and inspiring to me. I had to pull out my camera, go into complete tourist mode and take photos. I back up, slouch down to get the just the right angles. The clock on the building was mesmerizing to me. This went on for a good solid 5 minutes. My gracious significant other waits patiently as I do my thing. He didn't have the heart to tell me that I was photographing the wrong building! At any rate, the building next door to the restaurant, is gorgeous...Eleven Madison itself, from the outside was nice. Understated, which I should have known and expected.
Greeted at the front door by the maître d, he knew exactly who we were. Greeted us by name, inquired about our professions, and really made us feel at home. The inside of the restaurant is much more inspiring than the outside. A grand art deco design and eccentric floral arrangements as far as the eye could see, wide and tall. The staff moved strategically like notes to a song by a grand composer such as Beethoven. Strong, intentional and purposefully placed. Nothing was out of place, no detail over looked, the owners clearly maintain an unreasonable demeanor which demands perfection.
It began...eleven plus courses (get it? "Eleven") with wine pairings. We had arrived with complete intentions of leaving in a food induced coma, and of course a nice little buzz, hence, the Uber. Our reserved tabled was meticulously set with our place seating's and a crisp white box wrapped in a blue and white bakers twine. Yes, I recall those details. Keep up, the details will start to get foggy as we get deeper into the courses, ok, ok the wine pairings are more of the culprit. I'll cover a few that stuck out to me. Inside, an amuse bouche. A play on a black and white cookie using cheddar and apple. It was adorable, it was scrumptious, and for me, really set the tone of what I was about to experience. 
First course, what I call the yin and yang of oysters. Mind you, I do not like oysters. I will be polite. I will try them, I will eat them, and I will even pretend to enjoy them...but I don't. Out of pure culinary respect I will take one for the team and try them. However, these oysters I feel like I could eat for days and not be sick of the taste or the texture (which is huge for me, I'm a texture girl). The cold oyster was topped with a liquid nitrogen shaved apple. The perfect balance of tart and flavor. The warm option, a shaved fermented chestnut. Looked almost as a toasted shaved cheese on the verge of becoming a frico. 
Another favored course was a play on an eggs benedict. Served in a caviar tin, was a whipped fingerling potato, perfectly poached quail egg, surrounded by caviar, crisp panko-esque crumbs and a sphere of hollandaise sauce. Perched alongside were the tiniest little English muffins that were almost too cute to indulge in. Delectable, Delicious, and Devoured.
Later on our head server wheels over a cooking apparatus with cooper pots. He proceeds to finish off cooking a celery root, cooked and basted inside a pig bladder. Cut open and removed just as it was placed on our plate caressed in a black truffle concoction of goodness. Although so simple, the taste was so rich it read like a protein and left me wanting more.
The dessert that stuck with me was the baked Alaska. An olive oil cake base, grapefruit sorbet, nestled inside a meringue that was so perfectly piped and laid you would think it came from a pottery mold. It was ignited at our table, we were provided a brief history of the baked Alaska and then it was hustled away to be cut for us.
There were many other stars of the meal with fantastic pairings, pairings that were decided just for us during the meal, but I am only highlighting a few, hopefully no hard feelings. The restaurant staff was so accommodating. I had requested a kitchen tour and they did more than just deliver. After a few courses we were invited into the kitchen. We stood behind a hostess stand type podium watched as the kitchen operated with as much smoothness as a well-oiled machine. We watched in awe. A chef came and greeted us, performed a technique in front of us and made us a sweet treat of apple and syrup (from Vermont, go figure). Our night, we thought, was made. Nothing could top this. We were in the kitchen of an unlikely suspect, turned chef, turned culinary genius without any formal training. And then, it happened. Yes, my smart mouth asked for it, but I didn't think it would actually occur. An oddly tall, lanky man, in unlettered chef whites, bright white sneakers approaches us, leans in, shakes our hands and introduces himself. The man, the myth, a true legend, Chef Daniel Humm (Hallelujah! Hallelujah!) Let that simmer for a bit...

The entire experience was beyond my expectations.

I was so excited when I got a reservation here back in August 2015, but it didn't amaze me as much as I expected (or maybe my expectations were too high). The food was definitely delicious, but it was one of the least filling tasting menus I've ever had. 

Pros:
- The duck is probably one of the single most phenomenal things I've ever eaten. Ever. There really is no question about it.
- The foie gras and their interpretation of eggs benedict stood out to me as well.
- Good variety of bread, which was fresh and warm as well. The butter was silky smooth and perfectly rich.
- The waiter was very attentive to my requests, specifically for my food to be lightly salted since I found the earlier dishes a bit heavy. 

Cons:
- I was incredibly disappointed by one of the courses, the "whey sorbet". It honestly tasted so disgusting and I could barely choke down half of it. My waiter noticed and didn't offer a replacement dish or anything. 
- Tiny, tiny portions. I know fine dining focuses on quality over quantity, but compared to other 3 star restaurants, it still paled in comparison. While 11 courses sounds like a lot, they count the amuse bouche and palette cleansers as well. 

Takeaway:
Definitely, definitely recommend going for their a la carte menu, which includes the duck! I wouldn't go back for the tasting menu unless I saw it beforehand and liked enough of the courses.

Absolutely LOVE this restaurant and the entire waitstaff made it a point to make sure I had the best graduation dinner ever (I did!). IMPORTANT: The bill is shocking, yes but the service charge is already included in it and you pay for what you get. 

At the end of the dinner, everyone at the table was given a jar of homemade granola and a small menu detailing the dishes each of us had that night, which I thought was a nice and memorable touch to end the night.

Such an enjoyable experience from the moment we were greeted through 10 beautiful and delectable courses with thoughtfully cheeky nods to New York culinary heritage, expertly paired wine, and down-to-earth, extremely knowledgeable service. Without question, one of the best meals I've ever had.

Disappointed- I get what they are trying to do, but if I wanted to taste the essence of one stalk of asparagus- I could get it at the grocery store for way cheaper. I'm only writing this review to say
" the emperor has no clothes"! Seriously, I have been to other 3 Michelin starred restaurants- Per Se was phenomenal- Arzak in Spain- best food in the world. But this was an awful experience- I left hungry and scratching my head as most courses were under flavored and under cooked. Save your money for the guys who actually take raw food and make it into a dish.... I could have had better at Babbo for half the price. Extremely awful experience- won't be back.  Don't drink the kool-aid! If I could put no stars- I would.

Just held my wife's Alice,75th birthday at 11 Madison.  We where here 5 or 6 yrs ago. Had a great time then and even better time this time. Megan was a a delight.  As the Mgr of the day, she set the tone and the staff delivered. Thanks from all of us. Peter S.

The place is one of the most memorable dining experiences. Each dish had its own presentation. The progression of flavors from dish to dish made you excited to see what was next. I usually bring a book when I am dining alone but I spent my time watching all the faces of everyone around me experiencing their dish. I had one table a couple dishes ahead of me and another that was a couple back so I got to see the faces of enjoyment to see if it matched mine. The staff was very friendly and great conservationist. It was fun learning about  the history of some of the dishes. The Maitre D' Zach was great. I was able to see the kitchen and meet the chef which was a moment of wonder and awe. I am a big foodie and the whole experience was AMAZING. Thanks Zach and staff!

One star for the bread and one for the duck and one star for the service. 
The food is way too salty even after we told the waitress.
The bread is really good and the duck dish too. 
I just don't understand why they put so much salt in everything. 
Now I think Michelin three star does not necessarily equal to good taste.

The manager came over to apologize for the salt level and they gave us 50% off.

5 is not enough stars for this place. The service is impeccable, the food is outstanding, and it's the only bar I've ever been to that makes bar food so classy. We enjoyed the tasting menu last spring and now come to at least the bar every single time we visit NYC.

my friend and i couldn't get reservations, so we decided to do a walk in and sit by the bar instead. the service and experience is fantastic, even at the bar!

of course we couldn't try the set menu at the bar, but we were able to pick and choose a few items for that night. the only thing i remembered was the duck which i thought was cooked very well.

ok, so this is where the 5 star service comes in. we were talking to the bartender, saying how we tried getting reservations and it was so hard. moments later, the bartender comes back and says he wants to invite us to the kitchen.

we got a really cool tour of the kitchen and they made us a dessert in front of us ON THE HOUSE. this alone would make me come back.

Foie gras - superb, and I'm not usually a foie gras person

Spring lamb - okay, some pieces overcooked. Some were rare/ just right. Wish I got something else 

Snapper - alright, standard entree at fancy restaurant

Strawberry poached - alright, nothing new here 

Chocolate orange - good, fresh intense orange flavor I've not had elsewhere. 

Service - great.

3 story high vaulted ceiling with an amazing pink tiled design up there. A bit boring ambiance overall though.  

Service was right up there with Alinea as being the best in the business. They are super nice, quick, and seem totally genuine.  Service was a great addition to the experience.

The creativity of the food was great, lots of really fun dishes like the pig bladder asparagus and caviar dish.  Every food item was amazing.  The pace of the meal was perfect. However, I do have some issues.  The portion sizes were really small and there was only 3 really savory courses, and the sizes were small. Bottom line I wasn't very full.  The price for the amount of food was ridiculous.  I've been to a lot of these places and this was the worst value of many I've had for amount of food/courses vs cost.  

I had a really good time, probably a top 10 meal I've had.  However, I can't say I'd be back because for the roughly $800-$1000 you're going to spend for 2 people, you can go twice to most of its peers across the country.

I've been coming to EMP since the early 2000s.  I first learned about EMP while watching an episode of Sexy in the City - Carrie fell in EMP when trying to rush out after learning that Big was marrying Natasha, lol!) It was good back in the day, but over the past 5 years when Chef Daniel Humm purchased the restaurant from Danny Meyer, this place reached unbelievable levels!! Now, its on my repeat list for special occasions (birthdays, anniversaries, NYE, Saturday nights, anytime I can get a reservation makes it "special" and a reason to go). 

Food: The menu changes often.  It's based on the best seasonal ingredients available.  On our most recent visit in April 2016:
Black and White Savory Cookie with Apple and Cheddar - so good and simple, yet amazing. Great start to the meal.  You know you made the right decision to come after eating this.
Whitefish Salad, Fava Bean Croquette (very good), Morel with Rye Crisp and Wellfleet Oyster with Caviar.
Caviar Benedict with Spring Onion and Ham - My favorite dish of the tasting menu. A nice portion of caviar, egg yolk and small English muffins.  Words can't describe the joy this dish brought me.  
Foie Gras (Seared) with Sorrel and Fava Beans - I'm not a huge Foie Gras fan, so I didn't get this dish.  My husband got this and we were both blown away by how good it was. It was cooked to perfection.
Fluke and Peas - My least favorite dish of the night.  The texture of this dish and that it was served cold didn't work for me.  
Snapper 
Lobster course - My second favorite of the evening.  I large portion of lobster for a tasting menu and the flavors were phenomenal! 
Asparagus - braised with potato and black truffle - was very good, but very small. This dish was all about the presentation.  The Asparagus was cooked tableside.
Spring Lamb - was good
Duck - was good, but slightly over cooked.  I was very full at this point, so I didn't mind as much. 
New Potatoes and Morel (two separate dishes - served as sides with the Spring Lamb and Duck) - very delicious.
Strawberries Poached with Vanilla and Elderflower - very refreshing.
Chocolate and Salted Caramel dessert - very good, just enough at the end of the meal
Chocolate "Name that Milk" Pretzel with Sea Salt - cute game of matching up 4 different chocolate and milk (cow, sheep, buffalo and goat).  I was not successful, I think I got 1 or 2 right.

Wine: Excellent wine list, but this is expected.  Great prices points to choose from.

Atmosphere:  I always loved this room, even back in the early 2000s.  It feels special but not stuffy.  It's classy and elegant.  I love the floral arrangements in the front (right when you walk in).  We always take a picture here.  

Service: Is very attentive and more than meets my expectations for a 3 star Michelin restaurant.  

This restaurant was the highest listed restaurant in North America on the San Pellegrino the last few years.  It deserves all the accolades that they have received in recent years.

Can't say anything against this place. I've been a couple times now, once at the bar ordering off the a la carte menu, and once with the tasting. Both were brilliant. Incredible service (to be expected) and really creative presentation. It's really awesome for special events and celebrations. Be prepared for an epically long tasting.

Came for a chase sapphire preferred event hosted in the private dining room. After an hour of hors d'oeuvres (which were incredible), chef humm made an appearance to give a small speech on his journey to 11mp and what we'd be tasting that night. The sommelier then added his bit on the wine pairing for each plate.

Long story short it was a incredible experience, bite after bite. They offered more than the tasting menu lists, and the staff is extremely courteous and knowledgeable. The wine pairings were surprising but impressive as well. Overall the food was a tad too salty to everyone's taste (the unanimous comments around our table are the only reason there is a star missing), but at the very least they kept the wine flowing to wash it away. We had a wonderful time meeting those around our table, and left with a signed menu to help us remember our incredible night.

I went here for my birthday recently, and it was by far the best experience. It is 100% worth the wait and the price. The service and food is to die for. It doesn't get any better, and they have earned every one of those 3 Michelin stars.

Though the food portions may seem small, everything is delicious, and by the end of your many courses you a full. The wine menu they have is extensive, and there is something for everyone.

The atmosphere is also a joy. I had the pleasure to go take a tour of the kitchen as well, and even that was amazing. The service, the food, the parting menus all make EMP one of the best restaurants I've ever dined at.
They should open a Eleven Madison Park bakery or something. The breads and granola taste amazing.

I wanted to celebrate my Girlfriend's birthday here, so I booked this fine restaurant once I discovered it on yelp. It came highly recommended with its Michelins. 

We went all out with their Tasting Menu. Problem was, she thought I was going to pop the question :-D - The food was nothing but superb!!! With an excellently paired wine. 

 By the way, they wouldn't accept my tip, even though our waiter deserved one. He was nice enough to allow us to try 3 different wines, where the 3rd was perfect.

 Interested to try their Private Dining Room, which gives you a birds-eye view of the dining area. I just need to get my friends in on such a grand venture. 

This is one of my top 3 restaurant picks for special dinners.
My girlfriend and I were very happy with all the dishes. With the spacious dinner settings, fantastic presentation and the Chef's flavor profiles, I highly recommend it.

I'm not gonna repeat the previous 1387 reviews. 

However EMP is one of the best. Everything was perfectly cooked and tasted amazing. Service was exceptional. It's very difficult to make a reservation and you need a lot of patience. Don't forget to request the kitchen tour!

Well worth every penny. Me and my wife enjoyed the amusing experience very much. If you want to try a Michelin 3 stars restaurant in NYC, this is the one you should try.  

EMP well deserves Michelin 3 stars.

what a nice experience! this unique testing menu! we tried a lot and we were not overeat!i liked it! it supposed to be close 11 pm but we we sitting there like till 12:30 . amazing service. That special salad from apple they make in front of you really quick. Interesting to watch. Loved their amarone wine. our( me and my friend) bill (including tips) was $1200 but because we bought good wine. definitely recommend it . I read that this is considered one of the best restaurants in the world. and in the end they ll give you little presents: granola and chocolates made from different milk an you have to take a guess what milk its made from.:) pretty interesting.

This is our 5th Michelin star restaurant and possibly the best! No doubt it is ranked as the best restaurant in USA! The attention to detail is impressive! The staff is very very friendly and warm and since my wife wanted to celebrate my promotion, every staff made it a point to congratulate me! Starting from the huge wine selection to the oysters, caviars, crab, bass and lobster everything was just uniquely tasty. We were trying the lunch tasting menu for 3 hours and it is every bit worth the price tag.

My best dining experience ever. Everything was near perfect if I can't say it's perfect! 

Oyster poached and raw with chestnut and veloute was my favorite. The raw oyster with apple meat and vinegar like sauce was my one-bite organismic wonder! It's refreshing with the slightly sour dressing and fruity apple aroma. Everything together taste amazing, icy fresh with a fruity finish. The warm oyster is on the other hand, rich, creamy and delicious.

Caviar - mini Benedict with egg, potato, and ham. Very cute, mint bite size muffins. We need to assemble them ourselves which was another fun part of the meal! 

EMP def masters the cooking of seafood - no matter it's the crab or the lobster, the meat is juicy, super tender and soft (mind-blowing)! I can't imagine the lobster can be as tender as this! 

Celery root - never had celery this flavorful before.

Duck - another my favorite dish. Two weeks old honey and lavender glazed duck coated in cumin spices with Juicy meat and fatty skin. Duck soup - salty and rich.

Cheese plate was extraordinary too. Amazing presentation - tarte with Apple skin that filled with cheddar.

After our cheese plate, we were invited to the famous kitchen tour! it was mind blowing to walk into the world classic restaurant's kitchen!! There we shaked hands Chef Will!! We were also greeted by other chefs and got our complimentary maple syrup refreshment coated with Apple meat. The waitress kindly offered to take photo for us. I mentioned that my cell was running out of battery so we used my friends'. When we returned to our table 5 minutes later, I found a wireless charger on the table!! I didn't even notice when she mentioned this to another staff! The service was absolutely impeccable.

Baked Alaska was a great show!

Lastly, we had a lot of fun in the "name the milk" chocolate milk guessing game. And deeply enjoyed the last bites of chocolate pretzel with sea salt.

To end the will-never-end-memory-creating night, everything was perfect. EMP - thanks very much for the absolutely fun, amazing, delicious and inspiring dining experience.

Summary: Amazing experience. Great food and service. Presentation is exquisite and atmosphere is elegance without stuffiness. The walk-in al a carte dinner via the bar is an excellent bargain for the quality that this establishment provides. 3 well earned Michelin stars and no tips accepted. Hope to come back again. Recommend the Grog for a cocktail and mushroom or foie gras.

My wife and I wanted to hit up a Michelin start restaurant on our recent visit to the city, but we didn't want to deal with a 8+ course menu or with reservations two months in advance. I stumbled upon this Thrillist and discovered the walk-in option for Eleven Madison Park (article https://www.thrillist.com/eat/new-york/michelin-star-restaurants-in-nyc-cheapest-new-york-options). It seemed like the perfect venue for what we were looking for.

We arrived around 5pm and waited for the doors to open a little before 5:30pm. The staff was still going through the pre-meal planning session as we checked our coats and bag, then made our way into the bar to a nice table near the top of the ramp. Soon we were greeted and given drink menus to peruse. I asked our server for recommendations of red wines based on my tastes and my wife did the same for cocktails. Soon my wife was delivered a glass of the Grog and I was presented with the Cab Franc to try.  Both were amazing, with my wife nearly downing the Grog in 10 minutes because it was so perfectly crafted (it even had a metal straw so that the liquid was cool the entire way). Following that she tried the English Milk Punch was surprisingly good for a whiskey drink (not my wife's typical choice) and had a massive cube-shaped ice cube with the four icon logo for the restaurant engraved into the top of it. Crazy cool!

Soon it was time to order some food. Complimentary with the meal were a bowl of mixed nuts, a bowl of green olives, and a bowl of house-made potato chips. There was something so simple, but perfect about the three items that made them a great starter for the rest of the meal. We also received some flaky rolls with butter that had ground cheddar on top and a side of sea salt. Those had a nice texture, but could have been a little warmer. Here are the other items that we ordered:

Foie Gras - Amazing. Very rich and creamy, but with a nice crust on the outside, balanced by the maple and apple roll served on the side. Such complex flavors and textures...wow.

Mushroom - Amazing. Earthy and soulful with delicious red quinoa and mushrooms. Again, the craftsmanship was incredible.

Lobster - They kindly split the dish into two plates so we could each have our own and it was delicious. The lobster was incredibly tender and flavorful with the bisque and other elements set before us.

Malt - We got this because it sounded like a chocolate cheesecake, but it was not at all what we expected, unfortunately. The cheese was very powerful, the dish was more savory than sweet, and the maltiness was really intense. Fortunately, our server was empathetic and suggested we swap it out for...

Chocolate orange ganache - Much more traditional and sweet. My wife and I enjoyed it much better along with a glass of dessert wine. A great way to finish the meal.

Don't get me wrong, the prices are high and the portions small, but 1) with the starters and sides we were definitely NOT hungry by the end of the meal, 2) the food is awesome, 3) the experience is wonderful. Our total came out to $260 (with built-in service charge, since they don't accept gratuity) and was worth every penny. We would go again in a heartbeat.

I'll be 100% honest here... Hands down the BEST meal we've ever had. Ever. The menu was so incredibly thoughtful and the food was executed to perfection. Our wait staff was attentive, explained every course, answered any questions, and provided wine suggestions for each course as well. It has always been a dream to eat at one of the best restaurants in the world. I wish I could properly put into words just how incredibly divine our meal was, but the words happily escape me...

Went there with group of 8 experienced diners.  Tasting menu took almost 4 hours, to the point of exhaustion.   14 "tasting" dishes later we were still  hungry, tired, and underwhelmed.  I mean, a single asparagus? A thimble of green peas? A piece of beef the size of a D battery?  While the quality of each dish was wonderful, the portions were simply so small and so spaced apart as to be unsatisfying, particularly for the price.  We won't be returning

I've been eating at the one top Michelin restaurant each weekend in 2016 and this one right here takes the cake.

UPDATE: As of now, I have eaten at the following competitors in the last 2 months alone: Momofoku Ko, Brooklyn Fare, and Le Bernardin. 

And now i can say this blows away ALL of them

This is the only 2+ star Michelin star place I've been that that is almost worth the price tag

One of the best meals I've ever had - both food wise and service wise - and i never give out 5 star reviews.

I walked in a total skeptic and walked out a convert.

How this place is only the #5 on Zagat's top NYC restaurants is beyond me.
Luckily, it takes its rightful place as the #5 Restaurant in the WORLD on San Pellegrino's top list.

I came here for my birthday and it was really special.

From the moment you walk in, everyone from start to finish knows and acknowledges your birthday from the reservation guy to the beverage guy, and almost every face you see during the entirety of meal.

The meal has changed since Jan 2016 so be aware.

Its now 8 courses spanning 2.5 hours instead of the old 14 courses over 4 hours, but its still magical. Its  $295 a person + tax and drinks, but tips are included, so it clocks in at one of the most expensive meals in the city.

Our main waiter was young Giovanni Ribsi look-alike and this guy did it all. He took the orders, he brought the food, he cooked food live table side, and he had a story for every dish.
The rest of the staff was awesome, and like other reviewers have said, are definitely just ordinary dudes. None of that pretentious "all french staff" some places had.. (i'm looking at you Le Bernardin)

Its the small things that really make this place excellent. For example they will always make sure your bottle of beer always has the label facing you while it sits on the table, and they will even put it on ice to keep it cold while you finish your glass.

The dishes were absolutely delicious, simple, with an amazing presentation all at the same time. Nothing pretentious like everything covered with truffles or a potato chip with something raw on top (yes EVERY restaurant is doing this stupid crap now with potato chips).

I loved the fact that many of the dishes were interactive and either featured a small show table-side, or had to be put together - especially the mini English muffins with a side of quail egg omelette that you make into tiny sandwiches. Fun and delicious. 

For a 2.5 hour meal, I was not bored at any point. There was always something going on.

Some other great tidbits was the all-you-can eat fresh croissants with butter and sea salt, the 2nd slice of dessert (once we asked why they showed us an entire pie table side but gave us only a tiny slice), and for big drinkers, a complimentary BOTTLE of liquor at the end of your meal (usually whisky or brandy, no chasers though, so not easy to drink). 

I found it a bit funny they are still doing their "guess that chocolate" with the Mast brothers Brooklyn chocolate after their scandal about how they are selling melted Hershey's at $10 a bar.

Also, the goody bags with chocolate birthday truffles and a jar of granola when you leave was an excellent touch.

Would I come here again? yes definitely for a very special occasion. The only 2 or 3 star Michelin restaurant I can say that for

Bottom line however, even after trying almost every top Michelin restaurant in NYC, I can now safely say that none of these places are REALLY worth the $300+ price tags and the Michelin rating system is a total sham.

==========
That being said here's my Ultra-High end tasting menu/Michelin Star grading sheet from Best to Worst:

- Eleven Madison Park A

- Brooklyn Fare C

- Momofoku Ko D

- Le Bernardin F

- Semilla F

I had the greatest meal of my life at Eleven Madison Park. I also had the second greatest here. I also had a disastrous one that featured lame table-side magic and a carrot grinder.

But I'm pleased to say that the restaurant has nearly returned to its past glory. Our latest meal still didm't quite include those one-bite orgasmic wonders of their first menus, but every course was a home run, and the service was impeccable--perfectly timed, efficient, flexible, welcoming and friendly.

Highlights of our most recent meal included an assortment of delicious oyster preparations (high praise since I'm not a huge oyster fan); caviar served like miniature eggs benedict that you assemble yourself; a wonderful sea bass; celery root cooked in a pig's bladder; and a chocolate guessing game for dessert.

They have started opening their older wines with port tongs, which may be a bit over the top but does provide an entertaining table-side show, and it certainly gets rid of any cruddy corks!

The biggest change is that instead of 16 or so mini courses there are now eight somewhat larger ones, and many course offer several selections. This allowed us, as a party of three, to sample nearly everything on the menu.

I like this new format, and the more professional level of the service overall. Say a happy goodbye to the magic show, and give it a fresh try.

I wish I could give 10 stars to EMP. 
I have been to all 3 star rest, this is far best!
Reason why I like this restaurant best out of all 3 stars, they allow me to bring my own wines. This is such a big part of my dining experience

Impeccable service and stellar tasting menu! Lovely staff.  Pam took care to accommodate dietary restrictions in our party which we truly appreciated.  The caviar and quail egg dish was one of the most delicious dishes this foodie has ever tasted. Everything was fresh, the presentation was incredible, food top notch! To top off an unforgettable evening, Zach took us on a tour of the kitchen and Joe offered us handmade apple syrup frozen on a stick right before our eyes! Dining experience we will never forget.  Thanks Eleven Madison Park!!

WA WA WEE WA is the only expression accurate enough to describe how amazing this meal really was. Yes it's very pricey but it is so worth it. The staff are amazing (shout out to Zach who made our meal that much more memorable). 
1) the food was spectacular. 
2) the service was amazing i swear our table had 4 different people looking after us (all of them very pleasant) 
3) you get to go to the back and check out the kitchen??? HOW AMAZING IS THAT 
4) they need to start selling those pretzels online or something (one of the desserts they had when i came) 
5) scratch number 4 cause i'll probably get morbidly obese if they do 
6) the restaurant had very nice lighting (you know if it's too dark and while you're eating you get sleepy?) 
7) i'm coming back 10000000% 

LOVE LOVE LOVE

This was my second time at Eleven Madison Park and everything was consistently excellent as anticipated. Every single dish was delicate and nicely excecuted and service was great as well. I was impressed with the number of staff that were working at a given time and helping out. Each had a specific role and they were all courteous and not pretentious at all.  We left feeling very satisfied!
My favorite Michelin start restaurant!  Every dish on the tasting menu was creative and unforgetable.  What an incredible experience.  There wasn't anything that was disappointing.
AMAZING!!!! Ask them to iron your tablecloth...that actually happens!! Definitely worth the $750 price tag for two
Only came here for drinks.  I seriously need to come back because this place is amazing just for the drinks.  I'll make sure to update once I'm back!
Food was good. Very small portions and long wait in between courses. We were asked to move after our drinks then no one ever used that table!

When the price tag for a meal is more than $300, you can't blame anyone for having high expectations. What we had, however, was nothing near perfection. At the end of the 2-hour long, much anticipated event of the month, we felt a sense of frustration rather than fulfillment.

I have been to four Michelin-starred places in the past and this one would rank at the bottom. The biggest problem with the food: salt, salt, salt. 

Most of the stuff that came after the three excellent appetizers/small plates is overly salty. The pork, the soup, most of the sauces they used, and the cheesecake which I don't know if I could still call a "dessert" are cooked with too much salt. The problem came in various forms, broth, sauce, or layer of caramel. It was so bad that we couldn't finish the cheesecake (at a much hyped 3-star Michelin place, who could have thought). A related problem is the lack of variation in flavor or presentation, which could be due to the fact that everything was overwhelmed by salt. 

Worse yet, nobody asked us how the dessert/entire meal was at the end, so I had to raise the concern of saltiness of the food with our waitress. She was dismissive and perfunctory, and it almost felt like it was our problem that we did not find the meal up to our expectation. It simply didn't occur to her that maybe she could do something to address our concerns and I might still leave thinking, hmm, maybe the chef was having a bad day. Nope, the problem was so pervasive that it couldn't have been a chance event. We got heartburn after the meal, and had to drink a lot of water to stay hydrated, possibly because we had so much sodium in the system. I don't really care if this is some locally sourced "Long Island Sea Salt" or whatever comes in big boxes in Walmart - you can ruin everything by salt, plain and simple.

Overall, a dining experience that is so bad that it took us half a day to recover from all the atrocities on our taste buds, and our wallet. This review is to give those foodies who are thinking about throw $300+ at this establishment a sense of what could go wrong, basically, a lot of things.

We were disappointed. It was so salty from the main course to the dessert and when we mentioned to the waitress, she just said thank you ... Oops, we really did expect everything perfect at price point

Not what I expected. Then again, I have very high expectations. Del Posto, Colicchio & Sons, and even Soigne in Brooklyn have much better food and service. The dining room is very dated, the background music was just horrible, staff was attentive but as it got busier they were less friendly, and the banister was broken. Yes, it was.... Both sides. For a 3 Michelin Star restaurant you would think that the details matter to them.

Also, what happened to the rest of the Baked Alaska????? A whole Baked Alaska is brought out, displayed, fired up, and they bring back 2 spoonfuls? What is up with that? Does anyone know where the rest of the Baked Alaska is? The couple next to us had it as well, and the rest of their Baked Alaska went missing, too. I would have preferred to take that home in an insulated bag instead of the dated granola. My boss went 10 years ago and also got the granola....smh.

Very disappointing. Will never go back.

Eleven Madison. What do you say when your significant other makes a reservation for your birthday and the server forgets about It, only to apologize and walk away without remorse at the end of the meal as you are leaving? I get it. You especially forgot because the guy eating by himself at the table next to these guys has an accent and is dressed like a million bucks. And the table next to them are a bunch of finance guys wearing 15k+ watches. So why not give them more attention and forget about the young couple having a birthday dinner. I'm in the industry so I kind of get it, but when an impromptu tour of the kitchen is asked of and is more like, here it is, now there's the door back to the floor without any explanation of the layout, etc. I'd have to say I'm more insulted than disappointed. Maybe it was because we only spent 1k, but I thought hospitality was supposed to be more than what we got tonight. Food was great, some staff were awesome, but cmon guys. Don't be so quick to judge because you googled these reservations in advance in order to prioritize. I've had better tours at Gramercy tavern and Del Posto despite the lack of Apple snow Popsicles and a table to observe from like a zoo. I expected more out of you guys, but unfortunately the upset gf who went through all the trouble and was dismissed as unimportant and written off as "whatevs", trumps all. And I refer to Trump before he lost his mind and started talking about exporting all immigrants and building some stupid wall.

Overrated. The service was excellent, but the restaurant itself is a bit old, seems like it needs a renovation. The food was good but not as delicate as other michelin 3 star restaurants. It was just an experience, but I wouldnt go again.

Everything was mindblowing. This has to be one of my most favorite meals EVER! 

There were so many memorable items:

 - the oysters that seems so simple, cooked 3 ways tasted so different depending on the temperature. MINDBLOWING
 - the simple bread tasted so awesome with the butter that melts on. 
 - deconstructed eggs  benedict with soft quail egg and caviar MINDBLOWING
 - seared foie gras with apple slices ALWAYS MINDBLOWING
 - lobster was super tender MINDBLOWING
 - the root cooked in a calf's stomach MINDBLOWING
 - the crispy duck skin and moist duck meat MINDBLOWING
 - black bass super moist MINDBLOWING
 - cheese inside apple skin MINDBLOWING
 - the baked alaska set on fire in front of you, with the cripsy outside and ice cream inside MINDBLOWING

The only thing that I was sad about is the dessert. Baked alaska was good but most michelin star places have multiple desserts. They did give us chocolates with different types of milk and a guessing game for us to guess the type of milk. Also they gave us chocolate pretzels and some take home granola. I wish they would've gave us a different type of dessert since I'm not a chocolate fan.

Other than that everything was perfect. Be back again next time we're in NYC!!

I'm a foodie, and a friend and I have been working our way through the NYC Michelin-star list for a couple of years (modifying our targets as the list is modified).  So far, we have enjoyed every single experience we've had - we're flexible and we approach this with a really positive attitude. Our times dining at this level have been universally fun and delicious and we are definitely not nitpickers, and we are adventurous diners, too. So, this past Friday, we finally made it to Eleven Madison Park, an experience we had been anticipating for quite some time. We were very excited and completely ready to be delighted.

Disappointed is the only feeling I left with. The service was good - but definitely less personal and thoughtful than I've experienced elsewhere (not that it was thoughtless - just not AS thoughtful); the sommelier was AMAZING - she really saved the night, in my opinion...just excellent and fun and personable; but the food is where I really felt let down.  There were three dishes - including one DESSERT - that were so salt-forward they were basically inedible. And I love salt. When our waiter asked about our main course (the first salt infraction was the side of butternut squash accompanying our main dishes), we told him about our salt issue. His response: "Oh, I'm sorry."  Nothing else. No other response at all.  The cheese course and the dessert tart - both the same issue. We returned our plates with only one or two bites of food consumed...again, no response to our response to the query about whether we'd enjoyed the dishes. To me, at a restaurant supposedly of such a high caliber, this is unconscionable.

A couple of other service "nits" - I had pre-paid for the meal as a gift to my friend, and a note explaining the gift was to be delivered at the end of the meal in lieu of the check. Instead, it was waiting on the table when we arrived. Bummer.  I'd pre-ordered a split of champagne to start us off, too - but nothing to acknowledge that this was "special" was noted. I had to explain...

The place is gorgeous - there is no question. Did I enjoy the overall experience and am I glad I went - of course! I think the ideas behind the food are strong - the descriptions of the dishes all really appealed to me. The celery root - fantastic. The foie gras - amazing. There were some standouts (although I've had equally as-delicious things at other restaurants). But, ultimately, the execution of some dishes failed us (didn't just underwhelm - FAILED), and no one responded when we brought it up. That's not what I expect from a place like this, so the entire event ended up being a little sad - especially when our level of anticipation was so great.

A year after my trip (well almost, about a month short) I return to finish this review that I never got down to writing. I went in with high expectations, and to be honest, left just a wee disappointed. Everyone says that Eleven Madison Park sets the bar for cuisine in New York City... but really, I preferred Per Se and it wasn't even close. I was even tempted to give this a four star review, but really, that wasn't fair. EMP was excellent. It was best-in-class... it's just, for me at least, Per Se was better.

I enjoyed the meal thoroughly. Service was en pointe, flawless, and welcoming. Without going into specific dishes, every dish was creative and intriguing... with their rendition of a 'eggs Benedict' being the most memorable dish I had that day. Eggs, caviar, a light Hollandaise emulsion, ham gelee... all the flavour elements of one of my favourite breakfast items, compacted into a caviar tin. Brilliant. Delicious. Unforgettable.

Some of the other dishes though... were a little off-balance for me. A touch too sour, or another a bit too salty... it felt as though the kitchen was trying to push flavours and ideas further and had gone just a little bit too far... meaning dishes were no longer balanced. And balance is so important to me... a harmonious dish with multiple flavours, that's cuisine. So it was a little... I wouldn't say disappointing, but a little surprising to find that I didn't agree with everything the kitchen put out. It might be more me, maybe I just have a conservative palate.

But overall I would recommend dining at EMP in a heartbeat. The service is perfect, and even with the dishes I didn't love, I still liked them and the meal itself was still one of the most enjoyable experiences I've ever had, in a restaurant or out. 

Deservedly five stars.

I was deciding between 3 or 4 stars... the food of course was good but it was not exceptional.  Maybe my expectation was too high but it is listed as one of the top 10 restaurants in the world so it was appropriate.

It was unfortunate because we started off really well.  We sat at the bar while we waited for the others in our party and we had really good cocktails.  The bar tender can make some special cocktails based on your liking which was very creative.

Then we were seated to our table and the service began.  The service was great as expected and the food presentation was fantastic.  They had a mini meat grinder where they pass through carrots for the tartare .. but then it didn't taste as good as it looked.

The wine pairing was good though -- creative and definitely enhanced the food.

In the end, they give you a bottle of granola for breakfast the next day.

I might go back and have cocktails at the bar -- no reservations needed.

Having eaten at numerous other Michelin 3 star and Pellegrino Top 50 restaurants, I can say, without reservation, that this was the best meal I've ever had.  With the exception of dessert, each course was the best I've had of that particular food item.  Between the 4 of us we tried just about every option available (some courses are a choice between 2 or 3 items) and I don't believe you can go wrong with any choice you make, with one notable exception.  At one point you have a choice between foie gras terrine, pan fried, or a beet salad.  It may seem obvious to most, but unless you (understandably) have a problem with the way foie gras is produced go with one of the foie gras choices.  I didn't think I could find foie gras done better than I've had at Betony or Nomad but both the pan fried and the terrine foie gras at EMP were exquisite.  The beet salad was a beet salad. 

Aside from the amazing food, the service was fantastic - everything I would expect from a restaurant of this caliber.  They were on top of everything without being overbearing.  They were friendly and helpful and not at all pretentious.  The atmosphere is elegant without being stuffy.  The beer list is impressive and the 2 Manhattans I sampled were excellent.

The one disappointment in the entire meal was the dessert.  Dessert is one of the courses with options, but the baked alaska must be chosen by the entire table.  We chose the baked alaska so I can't speak for the other dessert choices, but I was very underwhelmed by the baked alaska.  It was ok, but I've had countless far better desserts at lesser restaurants.  Following so many incredible dishes, this mediocre dessert was certainly a letdown.  

Overall, EMP was a wonderful experience.  The one misstep we encountered, though disappointing, did little to overshadow the truly exceptional food and service we experienced before dessert.  I was blown away by some of the flavors my mouth was fortunate to experience and for the first time that I can remember I consciously tried to savor each and every bite for as long as possible.  Though the price tag is quite hefty for a single meal, I would absolutely recommend EMP to anyone who can get past the price.   And trust me, it's not too difficult once you taste the food.

Rather than reprise the numerous thoughtful appreciations of Chef Humm's creations which can be found here, let me post a caveat for the benefit of those who might, for instance, stand before a Monet and mutter "But it's just a fuzzy pitcher of a haystack." If that is you, dear reader, this restaurant is not for you. You will find the cuisine, and the praise with which it is described in some quarters, as mystifying as a Christie's auction. You will be able to buy yourself a filling, toothsome, and sensibly-priced meal (or even a "pre-fixed theater menu") at any number of fine eateries throughout the city, which I hope you will consume with gusto on your way to the show.

I close with this advice: the bowl of salt at table is there so that the diner may salt his or her food to taste.

My second favorite Michelin three star restaurant that I've been to (right behind Bo Innovation in Hong Kong).  Ahead of Per Se for some food reasons, and more so holistic experience reasons.  And way ahead of peers (although diff fare) like Jean Georges, Daniels, and The Modern.

16 ingredients and no set menu with a generous corkage policy, there's just so much room for creativity and surprises.  Without listing and remembering every course, among the best experiences include some simple courses that featured (spoilers), a picnic basket with a perfect warm soft pretzel, side of artisan mustard, and local craft bottled beer, a dessert that featured a magic trick from the waiter, and a course with 4-5 different ingredients on a wooden board that lets the eater combine/flavor to liking.

11 Mad Park really isn't just about the food, it's about the experience.  It does the food very well, but it's the experience that sets itself apart from peers.  Seriously, how many fine dining restaurants trains their staff to do magic as part of waiting tables?

Let me start by saying that this was my second experience at EMP and was blown away by our "experience" (that's truly what it was!) our first time around last year. However, since Jan. 15th Daniel Humm has chosen to change their menu. It is no longer a 14 course tasting menu that can last up to 4 hrs. (That was part of the experience and I didn't mind it) It is now 7 courses and some menu items can be chosen by customers. Personally, I am more than willing to give up all control to the chef in a tasting menu... At $300  pp (not including drinks/wine pairings which can add another $350) it is now more expensive with fewer courses and more similar to a regular :( dining experience in many other restaurants. 
Gone are the explanations and theatrics that I thoroughly enjoyed previously and contributed to the overall experience. Now, the menu is simpler, with less visual and palatable appeal. 
If I had to describe this last experience at EMP in two words, I would say, underwhelming and unimaginative. 
So disappointing.

If the most memorable thing about a highly anticipated night is the service... then i guess we might have a bit of a problem

Eight courses
1) oysters (cold/hot pairing... quite solid)
2) foie gras (didn't get the apple it came wrapped in, might have been pickled apple?)
3) caviar benedict (this was the highlight, by far, nothing even close - this is one of the best things i've eaten... EVER)
4) lobster - meh, nothing to write home about
5) vegetable in pig's bladder.... OK, here's my issue - what did the pig's bladder add exactly? i mean it's nice to have it finished table-side, but am i supposed to be appetized by the thought of a pig's bladder? or taste the bladder-i-ness on the veggies? this was a typical example of bland food hiding under rich sauces (in this case, a very lovely truffle sauce)... but lets face it, you can put truffle sauce on anything and have it be delicious
6) duck - it was actually lukewarm when it arrived at the table, but worse yet, it came with something slightly more serrated than a butterknife, making the whole thing difficult to cut 
7) cheese - beautiful piece with apple on top and cheddar on the bottom, an homage to upstate NY i'm sure... 
8) cheesecake - completely unmemorable at this point

If nothing else, I recall thinking a few times - this dish could have used more salt. I mean yes, there was a dish of salt in the middle of the table, but I don't think that's the point here.

There are two wine pairing options, a lower price one with less known and more adventurous choices, and a higher price one with classical regions and more vintage stuff. We went with the higher priced one and I was surprised to see so many whites, but given the menu above, I guess that makes sense. 

But I was even more surprised to still be taken on a tour of some lesser known wine regions. Which made me wonder how "exotic" they get when you opt for the cheaper pairing?? "this is a fine producer out of Bangladesh..."

Overall, the highlights of the meal were our Waitress and the Sommelier. Definitely wouldn't go back and don't even think I wanna try NoMad after that. 

For this kind of price - there are plenty of other options in NYC.

Amazing experience!  Came here for my wife and brother-in-law's birthday.  The food was divine and the service was 100% perfect. The staff are true professionals!  They took my wife's food restrictions seriously and had wonderful alternatives.  With nothing more than a glance from our server to his assistant, we were brought new items that fit our taste. Truly unbelievable!  This restaurant really goes above and beyond and does so very skillfully!

4.5 stars.

EMP is pretty damn good, but you don't need this review to tell you that.  The service is impeccable, friendly and knowledgeable; the decor is deco and spacious; the food is terrific.  Here's what we loved:

-Oysters and especially the oyster veloute.  Rich, creamy and delicious.
-"Eggs benedict" with caviar and quail.  Just the right flavors all together.
-Braised celery root.  Who knew celery root could absorb flavors like that?
-Baked Alaska.  And a show!
-Take-home granola.  We want more.

EMP is great, and if you have a chance to go and celebrate something wonderful, you won't be disappointed.
A bit disappointed.  All the things are so so, plating, flavor, service...and not worthy of the price.  I have to say per se is far more excellent.

We had a great evening at Eleven Madison Park. The experience started with making reservations and plans with Jonathon. 

The staff was expecting us when we arrived, greeted us by name and took us directly to our table. We settled in and started with bourbon Old Fashioned, but thinking back on it...a Manhattan from their cart might have been more fitting.

-Amuse-a black and white apple and cheddar cookie. The contrasts and complements set the tone for the evening.
-Oysters-There was a raw oyster and a poached oyster served with chestnuts and veloute. I loved the continuing theme of contrasts and complements
-Caviar presented in the style of Eggs Benedict with egg, potato and ham. These classic flavour pairings worked very well.
-Foie Gras seared with maple and apple was outstanding.  It was paired with 2013 Mas de Daumas Gassac.
-Black Bass perfectly seared with black radish and sesame paired with 2011 Quinta da Muradella, 
-Celery Root braised with black truffle. This was paired with 2005 Gianfranco Bovio Barolo. It was very cool that they opened this bottle using port tongs! A bottle of this age probably didn't need to be opened with port tongs, but it added to the spirit of celebration. Rather than pouring a glass of this wine they gave us the bottle.
-Duck with honey lavender, salsify and pear. The cook on the duck was perfect! The Barolo pairing continued to work very well.
-Butternut squash roasted with thyme and an amazing potato confit.
-Cheddar tarte with apple and bacon marmalade. Another example of classic flavour pairings presented elegantly. This was paired with 2014 Domaine de la Bergerie, Clos de la Bergerie.
-We chose Baked Alaska with molasses and vanilla ice cream for dessert. It was paired 2012 Weinlaubenhof Kracher Auslese.
-They finished the service with an assortment of chocolates and challenging us to guess what type of animal milk was used for each chocolate. They gave us a bottle of St. Georges Apple Brandy to close the evening. I loved the intense apple nose on this brandy.
-As we left they gave us gift bags with more of the chocolates and copies of our particular menu and pairings.

The food and presentation was absolutely fantastic. The wine pairings were creative. The service was very professional, very friendly and attentive.

I completely understand how the restaurant has earned its Michelin stars and its reputation as one of the world's best. It was a great way to celebrate a birthday! Make sure you make your reservations early!

A tasteful choice for a special occasion. My husband and I dined here last night, on Valentine's Day (our first as a married couple!), and it was wonderful. The caviar starter was presented delightfully in gifted packaging, adding an element of surprise and fun. The staff is on point, friendly and courteous, and very knowledgeable about the flavors in everything they serve - cocktails included. While the menu constantly changes, some faves from our meal were: the foie gras (marinated with maple and apple), lobster poached with rutabaga and pear, celery root braised with black truffle, dry aged duck (with honey, lavender, and pear), the strawberry dessert roasted with buttermilk and black pepper, and the final chocolate pretzel with sea salt served with Laird's apple brandy as a digestif. We didn't love the pork cheeks braised with onion and mustard, but we would love to return to Eleven Madison at some point to give our taste buds another palette spin.

All staff there are very kid friendly ( I have 8 month old girl ), they don't have high chair , however, they are willing to help... 
Well, the food is very creative and unique.. Comparing to Other Michelin 3 star , I would come Back here and recommend my friend too... For the service and the food.. It's worth it.

We had a brilliant meal at EMP. From the moment we walked in the door, we were treated like royalty. The meal was delicious, inventive, surprising, dramatic. Every element was well-thought of and presented with care. Our sommelier was incredibly knowledgable about wine, but also a passionate coffee drinker, and throughout the meal was educational, friendly, and down to earth. The service was impeccable. This was one of the most magical nights of my life!! Totally worth it.

One of the best meals of my life. I'll be frank, and say that some of the spiel and performance pieces are a little hokey. (And the cynic in me wonders if they show everyone the same bladder.) But I digress. The food was fantastic, and we were thrilled to have a kitchen tour. Don't miss it!

Make your reservation at least a couple weeks in advance. "If you have the means, I highly recommend picking one up." If you don't know who said that quote, stop reading this review and go figure it out. Listen, this is one of the top restaurants in NYC/the world. Just Google it (or Bing, if you're a weirdo) and read the many food critic reviews that talk about where the Chef grew up or how he makes his truffled chicken reduction or celery root purée - both of which I couldn't pick out of a lineup. Here is the bottom line: 1) Expensive. 2) Great food - plus you will leave absolutely stuffed, and 3) When they drop off the check, they also drop off a full bottle of liquor (complimentary) and say "take your time". They gave us vodka, and I'm not sure if you can swap for another type, but either way it's a pretty strong move so be prepared to take advantage... or at least bring a flask or solo cup to fill up. Separately, on the way out we walked by a family who was eating dinner with their 3 children, all ages under 10yrs old. This boggled my mind. This joint is like $250 a pop, so basically this table dropped $750 on kids dinners. Like wtf? I was so confused I asked the hostess what the deal way, and she said they were regulars. Like..regulars so the kids just order a piece of chicken or something and pay $25? Nope - all pre fix menu orders and they come in a couple times a month. It felt like the hostess was just trolling me for fun. She prob made the whole thing up. Its weird how you can sit through a great 15 course experience and one of the only things you can remember is the family of 5 dropping over 1500 on grub. The brain is a mystery.

My friend who frequents NYC recommended this place. Due to short notice, we were only able to get a lunch reservation. I had a reservation for 2, and last minute, I called to see if I could add a 3rd; they were more than happy to accommodate.

The immaculate service is noticeable as soon as you walk in the door. We were sharp to our reservation and were seated promptly. My friend gave me the evil eye because I didn't have a blazer on.... I was a bit concerned because of it cause he made it seem like a big deal... I mean, if I'm going to spend this much money on lunch, I'm going to be comfortable doing so!

After looking at their menu, we decided to each have the chief's selection, an 8-course meal. We were warned it would be a 3-hour experience.... 3 hours... for lunch... OK!

The meals were all little portions, and were amazing. The sommelier came to the table right about when our first course came out and recommended a couple different bottles of wine that complimented the Chef's selection, we went with whatever he recommended, which was a dry Riesling. Perfect choice for the 3 of us, for lunch.

After each course, there was a nice lady who removed the finished plates, and silverware. She was kinda tucked away somewhere, but was always watching us somehow. It was very impressive how attentive she was. Once, I looked her way, and she walked right over to me and asked me if i needed anything. I told her, I was just getting up to use the restroom, and she pulled the table away from me to give me more room to get up (its the little things that do it for me, the attention to detail).

My friends told me they came and cleaned up my messy side of the table while I was gone, replaced silverware and gave me a clean knee cloth.

About 5 courses in, a gentleman came up to us and asked how our meal was. I thought to myself, "OMG, hes going to say something about me not wearing a blazer, or maybe I did something improper" This was not the case. He said, if we were interested,  the chef would like to invite us to the kitchen and show us how things work. We all looked at each other and I answered, "hell yeah!..., oh, i mean, "that would be splendid."

We proceed to the kitchen, and I swear, everyone in the restaurant was looking at us like we were some VIP. Nope, just little-old-me (maybe they were appalled that I wasn't wearing a blazer ;P). We went to the back, and was introduced to the Chef who just thanked us for coming and some other inspirational words before he darted off to get ready for the dinner rush, To tell you the truth, I cant exactly remember was he said cause I was too busy looking for my jaw on the floor. We were on a pedestal while the sue-chef made an edible cocktail for us, and told us about all the stations and how the kitchen works, and how it differs from a lot of restaurants. He then let us ask him questions about day to day operations and their inspiration, etc. The edible cocktail was made with liquid nitrogen, right in front of us. It was awesome!

By the time we get back to our table, all the cloth was changed out, and our next course was served. One of the meals was foie gras. I remember taking a few bites and just couldn't finish the dish. My friends LOVED it. My pallet is just not that refined, especially coming from a state which outlaws it. The lady again came to me, and asked me, "was this not to your liking?" I giggled.

After all the delicious food, my friend (being a big diva and all) asks for french pressed ice coffee... Our waiter said they had regular coffee they could put over ice, but he'll see what he can do. I kid you not, they flew to Africa and got the beans, but in 15 minutes, they had french pressed iced coffee that we all enjoyed.

I think we left there exactly 3 hours after we sat down. The bill wasn't THAT expensive for the AMAZING experience we had, around $500 including tip, with a bottle of wine for a party of 3.

Came here for an early Valentines Day dinner and it was by far the best upscale meal I've had. I could go course by course, but it's worth it to go and be surprised by it all. Though, I must say, definitely take advantage of the refills of bread and butter. Something so simple is made unbelievably good. More than the food, the service is really what impressed me the most. At some other "expensive" places, the staff tends to be cold, militaristic, and a bit pushy almost in clearing the table. It was the complete opposite here. Though the staff is trained very professionally, they will get a feel of the diners and socialize comfortably with them. We cracked jokes with the diff waiters that assisted us and got to really talk in depth about the food in a comfortable manner. I'd feel at ease coming back again and not feel so intimidated if it didn't run about a G for two people! I will definitely be taking a seat at the bar soon though.

Well all I can say is what an experience..

If you area foodie and would prefer a dining experience, versus a pair of shoes/expensive bag then this is the place for you. My husband brought me here for my xmas present and it was hands down the best dining experience I have ever had. And I have to reiterate its a culinary EXPERIENCE

From the moment you walk in to you leave, everything is so relaxed and you feel so important. The staff are just outstanding, with a special shout out to Elizabeth who helped make the experience all the better

I wont spoil the list of food and drink as I love to be surprised and hate to have preconceived expectation before eating somewhere like this. All I will say is don't even think twice about it. Get on the phone and make your reservation

My husband took me here for our wedding anniversary. What we got was delicious food beautifully presented and very attentive and courteous service...I highly recommend this place for anyone who wants to splurge for that special occasion!

Came to the fabled Eleven Madison Park for an industry networking event recently, and it was quite an experience. They had a number of passed hors d'oeuvres that we're all delicious - I think my favorite was the carrot ginger. Following that, there was a 7 course chef's tasting menu (including a cheese course and dessert) that was prefixed with an amuse bouche. Of all, I think the first course, kale with smoked pork, was my favorite - and I'm not the biggest fan of kale by a long shot. The beef was cooked and seasoned perfectly, but the lobster course was tough, and the bass was a bit fishy. 

The service was impeccable, and the space was graciously appointed. The Pinot Noir provided for the night was thin, flat, and had finish of dry pineapple. I know the wine was selected from a list by the hosting company in order to keep costs reasonable, but if you have dedicated sommeliers and cellarmasters, you surely can find a bargain wine that doesn't immediately taste like a $5.99 clearance rack special. The Cabernet Sauvignon offered, though, was excellent and paired well with much of the dinner. 

Over all, I was pleased with Eleven Madison Park, but I thought it was overpriced for what it offers. I've had other tasting menus for $200 that were tastier and prepared better, so there's one star off. Much of this is splitting hairs though, if you're interested in this place definitely go and try it out for yourself.

By far my favorite Michelin star restaurant in NYC.  

As a vegetarian, this was definitely the best prix fix menu in the city, while still having a comfortable, fun enviroment.

Well done!

This was my 21st michelin star restaurant. I can say it topped all of the other restaurants I've been to. We ate here the next night after our dinner at Le bernardin. The food , front of the house, the ambiance,the flow of the night, the cocktails and our server was amazing. Everything was just into place. Daniel Humm is a genius! My boyfriend and i enjoyed the night so much. Some of the dishes that really amazed me : Their take on eggs Benedict was absolutely scrumptious, the contrast of cold and hot oyster with the veloute was a good match, lastly the duck - the best entree iv ever had ,the texture was so perfect , the explosion of flavors and the taste was amazing . EMP is truly world class.I am glad we chose to celebrate our anniversary here. My boyfriend having been fond of michelin stars, expensive restaurants and world class cuisines was awed by EMP.Can't wait to go back on our next trip to new york.

baked alaska dessert was off the charts, the best i've ever tried!
