foie gras, crab salad with sea urchin, pork cheeks, celery root, all pretty outstanding...
The only disappointment was the cheese dish...
Beautiful presentation and delectable food! A one of a kind experience for a foodie and gourmet adventurer.

My exploration of Michelin started here. Thanks giving weekend, wanted tondo some thing special. Refreshed lots of pages, finally find a table for lunch open. 

The front gate was so hard to find. Greeting, perfect. Checked you coat and lead us to a table on the lower floor. View? I cant see any from my table. Those servers should be really good at chatting. Ours checked in with us a couple of times, and then we just watched him swung to another table. Some courses came so late, i felt like we had to wait 30mi for a dish. People came after us finished before that.

Taste. A paper board, take out the one you like. I heard some people saying their was the one you don't like. I guess Michelin raters are fond of this sort of things. Started with a black and white cookie, which was sour. I guess this is the part where they wants to surprise you and reset your palate. There were caviare in an egg white, 4 small dishes in a course. Your drink, fresh maid juice, depends on the elements you choose at the beginning. Main dish was either duck or deer. The duck one was so hard to cut with the knife. Covered with sichuan pepper. I was impressed how they can eliminate the taste of the pepper completely. Dessert, with demonstration, flaming cream cake. You get two pieces. What do you think these restaurants do with the remaining?

The whole thing took us 4.5 hours. Drove us nuts.

Of course I am giving the 5th best restaurant in the world (the #1 best restaurant in New York City) a 5-star rating....my senses were having a field day!

I took my husband here for his 29th birthday to celebrate his last year in his twenties....because it gets better right?! (as long as my salary keeps up with inflation, I say hell yeah!). I've been near the Flatiron so many times and actually didn't know this restaurant was located here....in fact we got lost and ended up walking around the block in a complete circumference around  the restaurant!

The restaurant itself is spacious with REALLY HIGH CEILINGS! It reminded me of a bank. Everyone involved in the orchestra of food presentation were GREAT and on point...hooray!

Ok onto the food: 
My favorites were the STURGEON sabayon with chive, OYSTER pie and velouté, CAVIAR Benedict with egg, cauliflower and ham, and DUCK roasted with collard greens and apples....these were so savory that I wanted to melt into my seat! I have absolutely nothing to critique!

I love coming to Michelin-star restaurants for special occasions because of the unique dining experience for your mind, eyes and mouth. And this is by far the most creative and well orchestrated restaurant that I have been to.

I went to Eleven Madison a few years ago, but wanted to relay my experience. 

I went to Del Posto earlier this year, and was a bit disappointed with the service. The air of confidence in providing diners an all around wonderful experience was not present at Del Posto. The food was good, not great, but very good. But when I think back to my memories of Del Posto, I can only remember one emotion: anger. Halfway through the meal the thought of "I can't believe I am paying $300 for this service. I feel like an idiot" crept into my mind. And it absolutely killed the meal.

When I think back to my memories of Eleven Madison, I can't remember many specific bites of food. What I do remember is one emotion as well: pure and unadulterated happiness. Don't get me wrong, the food was spectacular. The drinks were superb. 

But my memory of eating there is one of those hazy experiences that sits in the portion of your brain devoted to making you smile. I just remember every person who was working there being absolutely and confidently focused on making my experience nice. Each person I interacted with seemed to genuinely want me to enjoy my time with them. Were they being genuine? It doesn't really matter if they were. If it was an act it fooled me in the way that a great actor (Daniel Day Lewis) can fool you into thinking they are a character (Abraham Lincoln). They did their job perfectly.

Every portion of my meal was thought out. And even if I don't remember the exact taste of each bite (similar to how I remember the jelly foie gras at Momofuku Ko in 2010), I definitely remember the happiness. 

So go to Eleven Madison if you want to be happy. It is crazy expensive, but if you are into dining, it is a good investment.

We ate at Eleven Madison last night for my mother's birthday. Table of 6, with myriad of food allergies. Food was great, but more importantly service was excellent. Everyone from hosts, to our head waiter Matt, were great.

Ate here on a Saturday night with old friends.  What a memorable experience.  The last time I ate here was many years ago for lunch.  Having the new minimalistic tasting menu is quite a gastronomic experience.  14 courses of creatively prepared dishes ranging from Sturgeon Sabayon with chive to Caviar Benedict with Egg, Cauliflower and Ham.  One of my favorites was the Hen of the Woods Mushroom Roasted with Horseradish.  Each dish was beautifully prepared and plated with attention to detail.  They made sure to tailor the dishes for individual preferences-two people did not eat gluten,  one person preferred no carbs... (Yes, I know, I felt sorry for her, she missed all the delicious breads and desserts, blasphemy!)  The end of the evening was completed by playing a game with different chocolates called "Name that Milk" 
The service throughout the evening was top notch,  every employee we encountered was professional and willing to work to make it perfect. 
So if you are willing to spend the Bucks and have an unbelievable gastronomic experience without the "fussy" factor, go to EMP.

Decided to come before the menu change starting next week, and good thing I did.
The 3-hour tasting menu was very extensive, and the courses flowed beautifully from one course to the next. All the courses were amazing, utilizing many local ingredients; The tasting menu was perfectly executed.

Highest compliments to the dessert chef, as well. I hope they keep the 'Milk & Honey' on their new tasting menu.

The price for the 13-course tasting menu was very reasonable, considering that it included gratuity.

Service was impeccable (Many thanks to Matthew & Co.).

There is a reason why EMP received 3 Michelin stars and 4 stars from the NYT.
One of the best restaurants in NYC (and considered one of the best in the world by some food critics).

I really want to try the new tasting menu and visit Humm's other restaurant, The Nomad, very soon.

The highest recommendation!

: 10 calendars
Came here on November 28. Overrated and not worth the money. Place is a total sideshow. They give you no beef and really no food of substance. Lots of vegetarian types of items.
If I can give it a 10 star I would. Everything on the tasting menu was savory. The presentation, taste and service was top notch. Of course the price too, but worth every penny.

This was an incredibly amazing culinary experience. In fact I'm going to say this is the best dining experience I've ever had in my life. I'm not going to comment on the food, as it was all impeccable, as you would expect. I will comment to say that one of our party had severe allergies, which we told them of ahead of time. They prepared similar tastes for each and every course for her than the rest of us. At no point did she ever feel that her meal was less than, and what amazed all of us was how similar the feel and taste and texture of the items were. 
The staff were amazing, probably the best restaurant staff I've ever encountered and boy do they know their restaurant. You can ask any question, from the art work on the walls, to the crockery that food is served in to the history of the oyster farmer who supplies them and the staff know about it. Incredible! How wonderful is that?
It's strange as I find it hard to actually put into words how great this restaurant is, it truly was an experience. Every single sense was delighted.
We experienced the perfect dinner!  The food. (All 15 courses) was exceptional.  Every employee anticipated our expectations and both surprised and delighted us!

Nice place for a 3 Michelin experience. Went here at dinner time during xmas week. Service was great. Drinks were good. I'd say 4.5 stars on yelp.  I felt on the flavor scale the last .5 star punch was somehow missing. They had some great unique dishes. Please get the Chocolate Sundae variant of the desert and keep your camera rolling when they serve it - an experience I should have recorded but was busy getting awestruck (thank me later :)). Was definitely worth the try!

EMP definitely deserves their 3 Michelin stars and to be named #5 Restaurant in the world! 

We had Friday night reservations at 5:45pm two weeks before Christmas. The restaurant was fairly empty when we showed up but filled up quickly in the next hour. Some of the dishes looked mediocre presentation wise but the flavors were definitely present. Out of the 20+ courses, my favorites were the eggs benedict and the foie gras. The egg benedict looked plastic and unappetizing when it was first presented so I was completely blown away by the taste. 

The wait staff is extremely attentive; each time I took a sip of water or wine, someone would be back to refill it. If you had to use the bathroom, someone would always be there to walk you over. On one of the many trips I took the bathroom during this 4 hour dinner, I jokingly told a waiter I had to leave work early for the reservation and my manager wanted proof that I was indeed dining at EMP. They came back and presented me with a letter for work and excusing me from work for the next few days. It was extremely thoughtful and witty! 

My boyfriend had mentioned we were taking our first trip together to Hawaii the following week so after we were done with dinner and paid our bill, it was a complete surprise when they invited us to the kitchen for a tour. It is amazing how the kitchen of a restaurant serving 20+ courses is so clean and well organized. We were given an overview of how the kitchen is run, a tasting of apple snow and then they gifted us with lei's! All this was done after we paid and tipped, so they didn't expect anything extra for this. Job well done EMP! 
5 stars for food and 5 stars for service!

Just amazing. It's not hard to see why this restaurant is so awarded and highly regarded. Each course is expertly composed, prepared and presented. The thought that goes into the entire experience makes for...well, a completely dining experience. The sweet course of the 'deconstructed' late harvest Riesling was superb. The wait staff were excellent. My only disappointment of the evening was not receiving a kitchen tour and I believe the requests I had sent through prior to their head maitre d' were forgotten. Although we were told we could come back another day specifically for a kitchen tour and just to advise it could not be accommodated on the evening.

Came here with my wife for our anniversary. Service here is amazing - they are very attentive without being overbearing. It definitely has Danny Meyers' fingerprint in terms of customer service. Unfortunately, the food is lacking in exception for a 3 star Michelin restaurant. The food is good but not exceptional. Their menu is seasonal and definitely from the presentation of the dishes, you can see the effort that goes into the creativity and preparation of each course. Our favorite dish there was the duck - it was roasted perfectly with crispy skin and a great balance of honey, lavender and apricots. Everything else was good but we expected more from such a highly rated restaurant.

Sheer perfection worthy of 3 Michelin stars.  Playful combinations of exquisite ingredients that tastes like morsels of heaven for 13 courses.  An almost impossible feat to be creative, delightful and perfectly executed on absolutely everything.  Superfluous yet invisible service.  If I have to be very nit picky, the only imperfection is a very skinny pour on a glass of $45 burgundy.
Sadly to say the food is uneatable, there is no substance. I have been there few years back and was a memorable experience but now is like they are making fun of your intelligence. Avoid it.
One of the best meals I've ever had. So delish so fresh, go here for a special occasion and admire the beauty of the food.

About a 2-2.5: The hubs and I came here to celebrate my birthday (Dinner #2) - I was super excited, as this would be our last 3-star Michelin in NY!  Owned by Chef Daniel Humm, the menu consists of a seasonal tasting menu that focuses on local ingredients.  We were actually a little early for our reservation, and while in the process of directing us towards the bar, another employee kindly stated that if we were ready to begin our dinner experience, we could be seated at that moment - yay!  I really think we received one of the best seats in the restaurants, as instead of facing the entrance way with the 'Exit' signs, we were facing the back of the restaurant where it was open, airy, and a beautiful mosaic on the wall as our focal point.  I loved the large table, as it gives an option to couples whether to sit right next to each other or across :D  When we were seated, we noticed a little box tied with a string - contained our first bite of the evening, which was a savory black and white cookie with apple and cheddar - this was salty and savory and crumbled in your mouth! Next, with our napkin holder, there sat a little egg filled with sturgeon caviar, sabayon and chives - delicious! Afterwards, we had an oyster pie and veolute; scallops marinated with black truffle and leeks; a take on eggs Benedict with egg, caviar, cauliflower and ham, with mini biscuits that were just so addicting and oh-so-cute!!!; foie gras (they ask if you would prefer it to be seared or in mousse form; I requested mousse, but I liked the hubs' seared format, as it was delicious); a made-to-order Waldorf salad with apple, celery, grapes, and walnuts - the apples were shaved with a French shaving machine, and this salad was super refreshing; underneath the salad, the plate was lifted for the next course, a celery bisque that was creamy; we then tried lobster with poached butternut squash and chestnuts; Hen of the Woods mushroom bundle roasted with horseradish; a choice of either the restaurant's signature dish, the roasted duck with collard greens and apple or venison; I was not a fan of either of these entrees, as the duck skin was just way too touch and not flavorful, and the venison was also just not tasty; a little mini 'fondue' set with Cato Corner cheese, melted in a hollowed out squash with a side of mustard and twig-like salted pretzel rolls; Botrytis ice cream with bitter almond and ginger crumble with a spoonful of Josef Vineyard's Riesling; a scoop of milk and honey custard with bee pollen ice cream; and, finally, a cute way to end the night - a chocolate 'Name that Milk' chocolate bar game - you receive a mini card with the restaurant logos and 4 animals (bison, cow, sheep, and goat) - you taste each of the unidentified bars and do a matching game, and the server brings out an answer key - this was SO FUN (and, I WON) AHAHAHA  Just note that the bars are dark chocolate-focused. At the end, we received a little bag of their housemade granola, a little canister of the printed menu, and some sea salt chocolate truffle bars. The staff were all super accommodating, friendly, and had a great sense of humor - we really loved Dean :D I am glad I was finally able to try Eleven Madison out!

+eggs Benedict with mini biscuits!
+seared foie gras
+Waldorf salad
+cute 'Name that Milk' game at the end
+ask for Dean :D
+friendly staff

Good service. Food is ok.  I heard this restaurant from my friends.  I think everyone been to here will write the same review . But I want to say when you finish you dinner you can ask for the kitchen tour, they told you detail about how each course are make it, and chef will do a sweet candy for you.
We do our dinner about 4 hours, at the end the waiter will give you a homemade small jar. It's good

We went for the bar dining .there was no wait and service was five star. We had lobster with squash main course and foie gras as appetizer. Has the chocolate ice cream for dessert. The dessert was not that great it's too sweet for my taste. The lobster was very fresh and very good. I had a cocktail called the jungle bird under the dark spirit that was awesome. One of the best cocktails I have ever had. I would go back for the cocktails alone.

I was so excited to try EMP, and having dined at  some of the world's top, i tried to set my expectations to be lower despite EMP's 5th ranking. 

But what a disappointment it was!

No, the food was good, and a few dishes definitely memorable. Particularly, the famous eggs benedict, the truffled scallop and the duck.

But what they did with the duck made me so utterly upset and disappointed that I could not get over it for the rest of the meal! They brought out a  full duck "preview" and explained how they cooked it and then took it in the back "to carve up for you" and what came back was a tiny piece per person!! The duck was one of the best I have ever tasted, if not the best, but what a tease it was.  THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO POINT TO SHOW THE PREVIEW BECAUSE DINERS ARE BOUND TO BE DISAPPOINTED? I COULD NOT UNDERSTAND WHY THEY WOULD DO THIS!

Additionally, the restaurant felt like it had no soul nor passion, some of the dishes just felt gimmicky and the service while top notch felt contrived and robotic. There was no real kindness here. The sommelier was good, but it felt like her goal was to try to get diners to spend as much as possible, as is the restaurant's overall sole purpose. EMP is just too commercial of an establishment, with a "churning out" feel.

Compared to the top Michelin restaurants in Europe and Japan, this place is a joke.

Wow, our taste buds didn't know what hit them! What an experience!

A girlfriend and I had been wanting to check out EMP for quite some time and last night was the night!

Every course was outstanding, the service was super friendly and not pretentious at all and you definitely get what you paid for! After Per Se I must admit I was scarred from spending ridiculous amounts on food but EMP has since changed my outlook.

I'll let the photos speak for themselves as everything was delicious!

We ended up paying $345 pp for food, taxes, tip and 2 glasses of wine each. I think from Jan 1 it's $295pp from $225 but the new price includes gratuity.

I have never had a dining experience quite like this before. 11 interesting gastro-pub dishes. Each course was an adventure in culinary science. Not only was the food interesting, fantastically presented, but the taste was to die for.  The customer service was unbelievable as well.  The cocktails were interesting and refreshing. Despite my initial frustration regarding the difficulty of getting a reservation, once my wife and I sat to dinner, I was pleased to see the restaurant was not overly crowded, and the service was top notch. My only gripe is that I wish it were more affordable so that we could go back. At this point, it seems as though it was a once in a lifetime experience.

A beautiful culinary experience slightly mired by clientelle and some lackluster courses.

Four of us attended dinner at Eleven Madison Park on a late weekday evening. The service was impeccable; from start to finish every host, hostess, waiter, waitress, and sommelier was polite and genuine.

The 13 courses we ate over 3 hours were primarily decadent and delicious, some more than others. The pacing was on point due to the attentiveness of the staff; once the plates were clear, they were gone in a hurry.

Highlights of the meal included a foam dish with chive oil served in an egg-shell, a savory venison course, a caviar and cornmeal take on eggs benedict, and a custard with a ball of honey that shattered to spill honey. Relative to these standouts, some mediocre servings included a black and white cookie to start, a pretzel serving that had mixed reviews at the table, and an oyster rockefeller dish that was rather too saturated with cracker (though paired with a delicious soup). Needless to say, even these mediocre dishes would suffice as good or great in any other restaurant, but paled next to other remarkable and memorable dishes.

The sommelier was excellent, almost too good, nearly doubling our bill. A tip I would have to future diners, and some gastronomic folk may murder me for this: ignore all drinks and pairing and focus on the food, this is why you came here! Fortunately for us, her beguiling ways led us to a delicious pairing of reds and whites and doubled our bill. A sumptuous regret.

The most glaring downside was the rudeness of some of the clientelle. A table of what my Brooklyn friend described as "bridge and tunnel Jersey" folk were plain rude to the staff and even engaged in rather crude banter with another table of what I could only assume were young startup professionals. Normally we wouldn't bother or care, being New Englanders ourselves and used to boisterous behavior, but at an establishment like Eleven Madison Park you'd expect better behavior from diners. Even the staff offered their apologies for the surrounding tables and offered champagne and cavier on them next time. I could only imagine this would be rectified by a more private dining atmosphere, but only further reinforced the quality and attentiveness of their staff.

Overall, a decadent experience and one I would gladly go for again, having learned to focus on the food and maybe be more specific about where we may sit to and enjoy the delights that come from the kitchen delivered by an impeccable staff.

I always comment that good service and by that I mean attentive and anticipatory, costs little. If you're going to be on the job one may as well do it well. At Eleven they step up to the mark and then some. Every moment is calibrated perfectly but somehow it doesn't feel stilted or artificial. Yes, it's apparent that the environs are laid out with great thought and undoubtedly the staff are held to high account but the naturalness from the moment of stepping from the cold outside is what sets this restaurant apart from others. 

The food is also something too. Some say worth a special journey.

The food is outstanding and the service is even better. Even the granola gift they give you for breakfast the next day is out of this world. EMP was truly a wonderful experience.  
  
Having said that, four stars instead of five for few reasons:
  
1) The reservation process: I called at 9:00 on the dot 28 days prior to when I wanted my reservation. I was on hold for longer than a half hour. When they did answer, I was told the only reservations were 5:30, 5:45 or after 9. The 7-8 block I'd wanted was already gone (or, presumably, being held for more important people). I begrudgingly opted for the 5:45 spot. "Oops, it got booked while we were talking." I'm not kidding. That happened. Obviously they were messing with me. I didn't for one second believe that, but I figured what difference is there in 15 minutes, and booked the 5:30. It was like trying to book a table at L'Idiot. 
  
Note to EMP: for the money being spent, the goal is NOT to make your customers resent you before they've set foot in the door.   
  
2) My meal lasted two and a half hours: Everything I'd read suggested I'd be there for a lot longer and I'd prepared my night for that. While there's no doubt I left full, I feel like I ultimately missed out on some portion of the experience. Whether that feeling accurately reflects reality or is merely perception is entirely irrelevant. 
  
3) Some of the dishes were not amazing: This is self-explanatory. Most of the dishes were unreal. The EMP's take on eggs benedict was unbelievable, the sturgeon sabayon was unbelievable, the oysters were unbelievable. The lobster was believable. At a restaurant like EMP, anything less than the best is noticeable.   
  
All of the above notwithstanding, if your wallet can handle it, EMP is as good as you've been led to believe.

I went there on a Thanksgiving weekend with my friends.  It was my 3rd time there.  However, all 3 of us were very disappointed with their food this time.  Everything was just salty.  We wondered if the main chef wasn't there on that day.  Ice cream had some salt too.  Main dish duck was very unimpressive.  Eleven Madison used to be really great, but we left the restaurant wondering what went wrong there.  It was a very disappointing experience.  We went there late, so the waiters and waitresses looked tired too.

My dinner at Eleven Madisson Park was probably the best I had in my entire life. The food was just fabulous! For 4 hours, we discovered multiple flavors, textures and enjoyed the wonderful atmosphere in which we had the chance to enjoy our diner.
Go there for the tasting menu - you will be amazed!!
This dining experience was unique!

I was a big pleasure to dine in this Restaurant. I had no Reservation, but they had some space at the Bar. Very nice Ambiente and Stuff. Good Wine. And the Food of Daniel Humm and his Team is just Perfect. The foie gras with Cabagge and the Lobster with pumpkin and reduced Lobster Sauce.. Awesome.  i enjoyed at its best.

I was really looking forward to this place. I called exactly 28 days ahead of time at 9 AM and was very excited to secure a reservation.  

I guess I am what you consider a foodie. I've tried many restaurants, some very excellent restaurants around the country. Unfortunately, I have to say I was extremely disappointed in my experience. I took my parents for a very special night out to dinner. We spent $1000 without any wine. We each had a cocktail. For that, I do expect an exceptional experience. Unfortunately the courses were underwhelming.  The taste of the food was pretty good. However, I cannot say it was amazing. 

Also I was very disappointed in the presentation. Many restaurants go out of their way to make the presentation very artful are beautiful. I think they try to make the presentation somewhat artful but I wouldn't say it was beautiful.  I took pictures of each course but looking back, none were beautiful.

The positives were there was excellent service. The restaurant itself is beautiful and very comfortable. What I recommend this restaurant? I would have to say no. Next time I would try another place.

1. Why i chose this
I chose this restaurant because it ranked 5/50 in the world's top 50, which makes it number 1 in America. Also, compared to the other American restaurants on that list like Per Se and the French Laundry, I think this is an exceptional value. Theres only one meal option for both lunch and dinner, which is the $225 tasting menu which ranges from like 12-16 dishes. The other top restaurants could cost up to $325-450 per person. But keep in mind if youre on a budget that the tip will be pretty hefty on top of the base price. Also, near the end when they ask you if you want coffee/tea (which costs an extra $6-15) dont skimp on that extra cost because its going to go along well with the 4 bars of chocolate that they give you to play with lol

2. When to go
Id recommend lunch time, although most ppl including myself want a dinner time. The reason for this is that this is a long, heavy meal. It averages 3.5 hrs they tell you, but ours was 3 hrs 45 minutes. If you do lunch, this could be a whole days worth of calories. If you do dinner, the lunch you ate earlier that day might fill up your stomach and prevent you from fully enjoying the meal. Plus all the energy from the food might keep you up! Most ppl say call 28 days in advance at 9am for the day you want to go. I was able to play around with the reservation system 5 days before my lunch. PLUS if you come on daylight, your camera wont need to use flash. Imagine flashing 16 times throughout the night cus you want to take foodie pics lol. The old ppl sitting next to you might find that strange. 

3. Service
Great service overall. When you step in the head maitre'd really knows what shes doing, offering to take our coats/backpacs and moving the table aside for us to sit. When you need to use the restroom, theyll usually move the table aside unless theyre too late. Make sure to walk back in an area that they can see you if you want them to help move the table. Then 90% of the time this one waiter would not say youre welcome to my friend everytime my friend thanked him. He also had a mean face. I think he should be retrained because my friend was not happy with his service. Then none of the waiters really tried to make small talk with us, even though i clearly saw other tables receive it. Also for the second salad dish he kinda just left it there without plating it on our plates. I dont wanna pay you a $100 tip to plate my own salad. After we paid, i felt like we werent tended to any longer, no more sparkling water or helping us with the table... However in the end the head maitre 'd  did help me with my jacket so that was good. 

4. Personalization
This was amazing. I asked for a kitchen tour and to integrate popcorn into the menu since my friend LOVES popcorn. We were taken to the kitchen, met the chef, and had a tasty apple ice/maple syrup dessert! Then for the popcorn, they made it duck flavored and nicely paired it with their main duck dish! It was definitely a special experience, highly recommended to personalize the experience for your significant other. 

5. Food
Im not going to comment on this since it changes. It was great, best meal of my life! Dont try to remember each dish because theyll give you a menu (in a cute container) at the end. The only dish that was meh was this lobster dish but only because it was hard. Other than that i loved how we could personalize the meal if we wanted to (like the popcorn)

Overall this was a great experience to go to if youre into food! Kinda gimmicky at times (the history, chocolate game) but it was fun!

Took some friends here while they were in town to experience a Michelin-starred restaurant. Pretty decent place (although drinks could use some work). Loved the presentation and the staff here is very attentive. Basically what you would expect of a high-end restaurant. Not sure if I'll return, but it was worth the experience.

EMP ranks #5 on The World's 50 Best Restaurants List (#1-4 all being located internationally). Although a non-believer in any sort of ranking systems, it's hard to deny the indisputable prestige that comes with this sort of recognition.

Block out 3.5 hours for EMP. There's no printed menu, and only an opening conversation regarding allergies and preferences led by your table's captain. The generous real estate, high ceilings, 9-feet windows, and magnificently seasonal centerpieces induces feelings of royalty. A very non-Manhattan setting and I like it.

EMP wheels out tableside carts, encourages blind tasting games, and shares historical tidbits and ingredient sourcing; the 3.5 hours spent are far from being stagnant. But, at what point does an interactive dining experience begin to feel too gimmicky? As long as the experiences are meaningful and purposeful (rather than filling space to simply break up the monotony), I think we're in the clear. 

Two things that stood out: 1- Interesting treatment of ingredients 2- Unassuming yet vigilant staff facilitating the no-wait transitions in between courses.

The first 3-star Michelin we tried. Good atmosphere, greater experience compared to food itself.

The tasting menu combined with New York elements, like pretzels picnic. I would say it's closer to people, other than the elegant, cold-faced French cuisines. The total time would be around 2.5 hours, if you have special events, the server would bring you to the kitchen as a tour, make cocktails for you as well. Really cool to see the busy secret place.

Be sure to make reservations with phone call in 9:00AM exactly 28 days before your target day, highly possible you won't be able to make it on regular dinner time.

I don't mean to be pooh-pooh, but this was more restaurant experience than great food. Overall the dishes were quite good, and nothing was less than above-average. But this is a bit of old-school fine-dinery, with the fancy decor, over-the-top service, and a general feeling of, we are here to pamper you and make you feel special, and you will love us in return. I'm from a generation that cares less about that stuff, and I'd rather not remember there was service than have it imprinted in my memory how well they served me. We did a tasting menu and enjoyed it, but frankly there was nothing to rave about. Some of the veggies were very good. Compare to Momofuku Ko, where the bill is slightly higher, the stools much less comfortable, the service far less servicey, and I will take the latter every time, because the food is so much more memorable. Of course, these are really not the same thing, as you can score a reservation at Eleven Madison and it will impress your date. MfK may also impress, but it will be on a 10 pm reservation on a Tuesday that you landed on an off-cancellation on Tuesday morning.

Exceptional dining experience! 
First heard this place from my friend, and I have been dreaming of dining at this place for over a year and this place is really difficult to book... I have tried three times to book a dinner at normal dinner time like 7pm and all failed. This time, we compromised and booked for a lunch. Both lunch and dinner offer fixed price tasting menu.
Don't want to share much about what you are going to see here. Just go and experience by yourself, do not read many reviews about their dishes or services - they will never disappointment you anyway so no need to do much pre-work before you go.

Once in the lifetime experience! 

The menu was designed for you to enjoy the local foods of New York as well as their play on classic dishes such as breakfast sandwich and tartare. I love the fact that they demonstrate how they cook certain foods and they talk you through each course. 

And best of all, they give you take-home gifts for breakfast in the morning and candy.

Ok, so the food here is good.  Not amazing.  But pretty good, including some interesting and creative dishes.  Could use way less salt (and I like salt), but otherwise good.

That said, the ambiance feels sterile.  And more importantly, the service feels a bit soulless and robotic.  Everyone seemed nice, and my glass was always full, but honestly they just weren't very warm.  I expect they are intentionally trying to leave the diners alone to enjoy their meal, but I thought the result was a relatively cold and impersonal experience.

So overall, we had a good time.  But we felt like we were part of a machine.

We have celebrated special events with friends here previously (7 1/2 years ago) and planned to celebrate the birthdays of two wives (two couples) with great expectation. Unfortunately one of the wives became ill the day before our reservation and that couple was unable to attend. However we did and we reminded the receptionist of the birthday event upon entry. We have eaten at several of the top 10 restaurants in the world and thus looked forward to an exceptional experience. Unfortunately, it was not found! the food varied from mediocre to good. While we were well aware of the price of the meal, the price ($81) for the 3 glasses (in toto) of "okay" wines was exorbitant. the service was outstanding, if a little overbearing. we were disappointed not to receive any recognition of the birthday, especially in view of 2 adjacent tables who had desserts featuring a candle to celebrate theirs, when we had mentioned the birthdays when making the reservation and again upon entry. The final disappointment was the 15-20 minute wait for our coats at 10:15pm. We were very disappointed in what we expected would be the finest meal experience of our lives.I am not sure that I would rank our visit in the top 50 that we have experienced let alone the top 10.

The food was good, but honestly I didn't really fall in love with it. 
I expected it to be as good as per se, but it didn't impress me, or my friends. 
We didn't do the tasting menu but ordered everything on the menu.

The food was amazing. Many of the other reviews here offer great detail. The most memorable for me was the eggs benedict with caviar. 

As expected, the service was amazing. Went for a 30th birthday and the whole staff made the birthday boy feel very special. 

We ordered the wine pairing with our meal. The wines served were both tasty and interesting. However, our som was no more accommodating than any other non-starred restaurant in the city. When we gave her feedback, or asked for something different than what she had planned, she was very dismissive. This was an enormous disappointment. 

Would go back for a very special occasion, but would buy wine by the bottle. Likely would try or return to other three stars before emp as a result of the disappointment with the wine program.

Must try if you are into fine dining. You can read about the experience in the other reviews. I do not want to ruin your experience. Menu changes. Make a reservation early. Try to no look at other tables. Be prepared for surprised and lots of food.

I must say the food was absolutely fabulous  the chef should be commended but how I was treated by the hostess and wait staff was horrible.  I just finished a meeting next door at CS and decided to have lunch before returning to CT.   I was advised only the tasting menu was available in the restaurant and it was only by reservation only then I was seated in the bar area with my back turned to the restaurant , only patron treated this way.  I noticed the management staff noticed and approved and directed the hostess.  I decided to stay and have lunch after 3 hour meeting however I wanted to write a review and post my experience.    I will never return.

This is an old review from when I dined last year in the summer Late may. 

The service is spectacular as to be expected from a three michelin started restaurant, but that is not where I found the overall experience lacking. Winelist was not as comprehensive as I would have expected especially for bottles under 100$. They do have the big dogs of the grand cru classé and Napa valleys best, but honestly who has 8,000 bucks to drop on 7 glasses of wine. 

I found the food quite inventive, however some things were surprisingly under seasoned, I point in particular to the "clam bake" and the under salted beef course (though he beef has a massive punch of acidity from the eggplant that came along with it, which I imagine would have been dynamite with more salt). The presentation of this course was fun and interactive and the seafood itself was of top quality, but the lack of salt made every component taste quite normal. 

Of course this is not an every day meal, and having dined at a few 3 star places in North America I expected to be full at least by the time petit fours arrived. My two times at the French laundry for example were not only journeys through food, they also left me feeling satisfied, this meal was reminiscent of the fake me out 80s where people wanted to be seen at a place, pay through the nose, and not be full so hey could blow cocaine at the local yuppie spot. 

The one saving grace was the mason jar full of delicious granola. Yes I ate it in the cab on the way to pacha, but not before a stop at the nearest shake shack. 

I'd say go there if you haven't for a special occasion just for the experience and attentive, but not stuffy staff, but don't expect to be satisfied in all of your expectations, or you'll be deflated.

Learning that it was ranked by Pellegrino as the #5 restaurant in the world, I thought I owed myself a dinner there during our recent trip to NYC. While all the courses were meticulously prepared, I did not find them to be that creative or memorable. Given the number of hours the staff spent routinely on training and  preparation that I read about, the service was superlative as expected. Overall though, we were not wowed by the entire experience. 
They served only a pre-fix menu that changes regularly, so it does not do much good to name those courses that we liked and those that we didn't. In conclusion, I can name twenty one other restaurants where I had a better dinner and overall experience, so it will not be among my top 25 list. On my next visit to NYC, I shall go back to our old standbys - Le Bernardin and Per Se. While the latter do not exactly offer trail blazing, creative cuisine, history gives me the confidence that I will leave with greater satisfaction at the end of the evening.

Is it blasphemy to say I wasn't terribly impressed by what is supposed to be the #1 restaurant in NYC? The food was certainly good and there were some stand out dishes (celery root on my menu), but I just didn't experience the wow factor I was expecting. It was all very solid, just a bit underwhelming. My sister was treating me so I would probably have been even more disappointed with the experience if I had been footing the bill. 

FINAL RATING:
4

My bf took me here for my birthday and I was beyond excited. I've been a fan of Daniel Humm for a while so this was such a treat. I have absolutely nothing but praises doe this place. The food, ambiance, the staff, all impeccable. My bf spilled his wine and broke the mother of pearl spoon for the caviar lol, and the staff appeared as if out of thin air to fix the table cloth and replace the spoon. I only wish that I got to meet Daniel because that might have made me faint. So maybe a good thing that I couldn't meet him. Overall a very memorable birthday.

With high hopes and baited breath we waited to see what Eleven Madison Park had to offer. Sure we'd heard the hype and seen the pictures. However, experiencing the meal ourselves was something else entirely. As numerous others have already discovered, Chef Daniel Humm is a deft master of innovative cuisine.

Each course is precisely choreographed, meticulous in its presentation and displayed like a beautiful artwork. The menu is regularly changing, so it is hard to recommend specific dishes, but just know that whatever the chef will concoct is sure to be creative and thoughtfully plated.  Of the many courses you'll receive, every one may not be a standout, but you are guaranteed to find some that blend so harmoniously that you'll dream about them for weeks to come. Flavors meet technique, and the result is refined yet entertaining. While the cuisine was definitely upscale, it was also more comforting and accessible than some other restaurants of the same caliber. One of my favorite examples of the style would be their take on eggs benedict, a silken egg custard topped with a generous serving of caviar, and two miniature "muffins" to make your own gourmet breakfast-for-dinner.

The entire experience is a seamless production, with the servers attuned to your needs, and course after course of showmanship. For example, a miniature lobster boil is prepared tableside, and then carefully plated atop a wooden slab covered with brown paper lining. A course using sunflowers was preceded by the server bringing over a basket of blooming sunflowers, so that we could view the "before" version prior to receiving the dish and explanation of what it consisted of. The chocolate taste test at the end, was an interactive and fun opportunity for the diners to try their hand at playing milk detective, tasting and then selecting between sheep, goat, cow, and buffalo milk chocolates (as a side note, I'm still impressed my husband managed to get them all right- good job honey). Plus I was grateful for the little touches, like a box of salted caramel chocolates with a birthday wish from the restaurant, and a delightful jar of granola to take home for later (which I am trying to stretch out as long as I can since it too is fantastic).

The wine list is excellent, although the cocktails are deserving of their own accolades. I thoroughly enjoyed the smooth but potent English Milk Punch (with scotch Jamaican rum, Batavia Arrack, Darjeeling Tea, Pineapple, Battenkill Valley Milk Curd, Lemon, and Spices). The atmosphere as already described, is the epitome of elegance, with the bank-turned-restaurant boasting high ceilings, massive windows, warm uplighting, and spectacular floral displays. While EMP is definitely a dress for the girls and jacket for the men kind of establishment, it doesn't feel overly stuffy.

Be sure to anticipate that the meal will take some time and plan your evening accordingly. However, we were never waiting too long between courses, so it didn't feel overly drawn out. Also, if you would like to visit, be sure to plan ahead and check on their reservation policy since they only open spots at a precise intervals before the date. Even then, it can take a good deal of effort, luck, and concierge connections to snag a spot at this high-in-demand restaurant which keeps rising in the ranks of several top in the US and the World lists (and with good reason).

So come, savor, and enjoy one of New York's finest restaurants, Eleven Madison Park will be sure to deliver an unforgettable experience.

So we're food snobs and it's probably pretty obnoxious with how many Michelin Stars we've "collected."  I think that just gives us a better reference point.  So we took our friends here as their wedding present and they said it was their favorite gift.  The food was not the best in the world, but it was delicious and creative.  I was especially impressed with the presentation and dishes.  One salad dish with a secret soup compartment was pretty awesome.  Our main server, Elizabeth, knew EVERYTHING about the restaurant.  It became almost comical and we began testing her about random facts (ie., material and origination of the table clothes).  We couldn't stump her.  It was awesome!  My only real complaint is that other than Elizabeth, the servers spoke SO SOFTLY.  With the really high ceilings, I couldn't hear most of what we were eating because it all got lost in the acoustics.  The chocolate game at the end where you have to identify the animal source was so fun.  Really, I loved all the whimsical dishes and the relaxed demeanor of the staff.  I wouldn't go back SO fast, but we'd go back.

3 Michelin Stars ... Wow what an experience. We reserved this restaurant as a post-NYC-marathon treat and it sure lived up to the hype. The restaurant is hidden in the Credit Suisse building on Madison and easy to miss unless you are looking for it. Reservations are a must and you can only reserve 28 days in advance. They served us a 14-course tasting menu which included 3 desserts (no complaints there!). At the start of the meal we were asked to choose between venison or duck for the main course. We chose venison. 

Our menu consisted of:
*Cheddar savory black and white cookie with Apple
*Sturgeon sabayon with chive
*Oyster pie and velouté
*Scallops marinated with black truffle and leeks
*Caviar Benedict with egg, cauliflower, and ham
*Foie Gras (two ways, you choose) seared with Brussels sprouts and smoked eel -or- pickled with red cabbage (we each ordered one so we could try both)
*Waldorf salad with apple, celery, grapes, and walnuts (prepared meticulously table side)
*Lobster poached with butternut squash and chestnuts
*Hen of the woods mushroom roasted with horseradish
*Venison roasted with beets and onion
*Cato corner cheese fondue with squash and mustard (served with unlimited fresh soft pretzels)
*Bortrytis ice cream with bitter almond and ginger crumble paired with Herman J Weimer Riesling Noble Select 2012
*Milk and honey custard with bee pollen ice cream
*Chocolate "name that milk" game (we were given 4 milk chocolates to taste and had to pick which one was made of sheep/goat/bison/cow milk)
*Pretzel with sea salt paired with brandy

All the courses looked like little pieces of art and tasted as good as they looked.  They sent us home with a jar of homemade granola that was amazing. Seriously, I have never had granola that tasted that delicious. My boyfriend could not stop eating it on the plane so he finished it all in one sitting. I managed to ration it so I had some left over to mix with yogurt for the next couple of days. 

Dress code - there is no strict dress code. Although a jacket seems to be the norm for men, a tie is not required. If it is summer, you can even skip the jacket and no one would look at you twice. Women have lots of leeway. I wore my typical NYC uniform, a black dress paired with Matisse-print tights and black combat boots.   Some women were in cocktail dresses. Others were in blazers and slacks. My boyfriend wore a light blazer and his black Lululemon ABC pants and fit right in (we are runners, we like our performance fabrics). Basically, just look biz casual and you will be fine.

Service - Very attentive but not over the top. Exactly what one would expect for a restaurant of this caliber.  The sommelier was very knowledgeable and made excellent recommendations for drinks and wine. 

Last time I had a meal like this, it was in Le Mout in Taichung Taiwan (#20 of the best restaurants in Asia) and I paid $650 for it so the $225 at Eleven Madison Park was a bargain , since it is also ranked as the #5 best restaurant in the world (2015).

Service and ambiance is second to none but overall the fall 2015 tasting menu was disappointing. I came with my mom to celebrate my birthday and while the meal started out exciting, we were both cheesed/buttered and creamed out by the 5th course. The Waldorf Salad course was really subpar. Aside from the intricate preparation with a side of story telling by waiter, the salad itself was very underwhelming - honestly something anyone can make at home. The mayo soup that accompanied it was so heavy that we couldn't stomach beyond the first spoonful and we're dairy heavy eating people! The chocolate bowl desert was all presentation and an a hodgepodge of over-sweet, over-salt, and over- sour cream flavor profiles - again, couldn't stomach past 2 spoonfuls. The only dishes that stood out were the duck, oyster, and caviar eggs Benedict. I would have expected 12 out of 12 awesome courses rather than 4 out of 12 for $225 per person meal (not including tax and tip).

My SO took me here for my birthday dinner recently and honestly, we were both floored at how bad the meal was. I compared it to gloried plane food. The bill came out to be over $600 for two and it was the biggest and saddest waste of money ever. It was honestly a joke. I would have even been disappointed if we spent $100. I've been to my fair share of Michelin starred restaurants (Per Se, Alinea, Brooklyn Fare.. ) and Eleven was not even in the same stratosphere. I've asked friends who have been here back in its "glory days" and compared it to their more recent visit, and they all agreed that it has gone down hill significantly and are baffled at what happened. I honestly can't remember a single memorable item I had- every dish I tried garnered a slight gag reflex the moment I tasted it. I'm not even exaggerating. The only dish I finished was their take on the eggs Benedict (of course, bc I like all eggs Benedict, so that's easy), but for every other course I literally took one bite and didn't want to take another. These days I don't force myself to finish food I don't enjoy, why should you, sunk cost. The main course, the duck was the biggest joke. They show you this entire whole duck at your table, crispy and delicious looking... Bring it back to carve it and come back with a duck sliver the size of your finger.. And it wasn't even tasty ! The duck was dry, hard, had a thick layer of fatty skin, and seasoning was terrible- giant peppercorns that felt like I was biting on pebbles when I was eating it. I didn't even finish my sliver. The only thing that I somewhat remember as decent was my dessert at the end, but then again...I already forgot what that was.

The food here is great, and one could easily argue that NYC has other restaurants that serve better, higher-end food. However, the dinning room design is fantastic, and the staff here define professionalism. I've visited other great restaurants in NYC, but this place always stands out for their great attention to detail.

Easily, this was my best dining experience to date.

I came here with my girlfriend to celebrate our accomplishments - she got a new job, I received a promotion, and we were approved for our first apartment together. 

The exceptional service started before we got to the restaurant and continued long after our meal was complete. The maitre d emailed me days before our reservation to inquire about our visit and ensure we were personally welcomed when arriving at the restaurant. Waiters demonstrated the utmost professionalism throughout our dinner, as they were truly skilled in their craft. It was also apparent that the dining room manager (Alex) took pride in his establishment, as he took the time to walk the restaurant and speak attentively with guests.

The food quality and presentation was fantastic. Our tasting menu for the evening consisted of 14 items that were each impressive in their own right. Standout courses included caviar (benedict with egg, ham, and asparagus), carrot (tartare with rye crisps and condiments), asparagus (braised in pig's bladder with potato and black truffle), lobster (butter-poached with dandelion and ginger), and veal (dry-aged with ramps and bone marrow).

While finishing the final menu item by playing the famous "name that milk" game, Alex came to our table and handed us a key (literally) that unlocked a private experience after dinner concluded. I won't include those specifics in this review to avoid spoiling a potential surprise for future guests, but message me separately if you want to know the story.

This restaurant deserves its three-star Michelin rating in every facet, and I will be back for another meal.

Simply wow. From the minute you walk in you are astounded by the service. Rarely have I been so impressed with how a three Michelin star service can capture your attention right from the first second. We walk in and they already knew who we were, the bottles of wine we brought were taken away swiftly to be chilled to our preference. 

The food - taste, presentation and quality were all so good. Amazing.

I loved my experience so much last fall that I had to bring my boyfriend back this year. 

We started off with a couple of cocktails before moving onto wine.  Their wine list is crazy huge, with a big emphasis on French wines.  I wish we could have seen their wine cellar, but it's not open for people to see.  

Cocktails:
- Hutch: apricot and Jamaican jerk bitters stood out in the ingredients, and the cardamaro is very interesting
- Amish snap: I thought sugar snap peas sounded creative and interesting, and indeed, it does take like sugar snap peas, but in a good way. It has a very distinct type of sweetness. 
- Honi honi: this looks like a tikki drink, but it actually has a lot of character and isn't just tropical/sweet.  The coffee in this is very interesting, and this was my favorite cocktail
- Montauk: kind of like an old fashioned, but not. The best part was the most beautiful iceberg of an ice cube

Food: 
1. Their black and white cookies in a box to start.  It was a cheddar cookie with apple for the fall, coated with black and white chocolate. Loved the cheddar cookie
2. Sturgeon sabayon with chive oil served in an egg. It had a good smoked ham-like flavor to it
3. Oyster pie: the delicate shell outside of the pie was really good, and the oyster was nicely poached and topped with dehydrated celery root, which paired really well with it. 
4. Oyster veloute: acidic, rich, intense, amazing 
5. Marinated scallops: raw, served underneath fragrant charred leaks with black truffle. I'm amazed that the truffle and leaks didn't overpower the scallops, and it's impressive that they were able to balance everything so well 
6. Caviar: served in their tin, "eggs benedict" style. It had a soft poached quail egg underneath.  The "hollandaise" on top was nice and light, but there was too much creme fraiche for me. I loved the warm "mini english muffins" to accompany the caviar 
7. Bread and butter: the bread was like a cross between a croissant and a roll, and there were 3 butters: one plain, one with duck renderings, and one with venison renderings (since we ordered one duck and one venison for the main meat course)
8. Pickled kohlrabi: rounds of lightly pickled kohlrabi topped with shaved cheese and a hazelnut paste on the side. It sounds like a weird combination, but it was amazing 
9. Foie gras: you can have it seared, or marinated in cognac, and we went with the cognac version. It comes as a "red cabbage" with layers of foie in between layers of cabbage, reconstructed into a wedge (creative!)
10. Waldorf salad: made table side, with shaved granny smith apples, candied walnuts, celery roots marinated in white balsamic vinegar, plump raisins, amazing blue cheese from Middlebury, Vermont, and a lemon mayo. I usually dislike mayo, but the lemon in this one made it not even taste like mayo, and it was a great take on the Waldorf salad
11. Chilled apple and celery root soup: this sat in a bowl underneath the salad, and the two dishes complemented each other perfectly
12. Lobster: butter poached, topped with super thin sheets of butternut squash and an amazing lobster black cardamom sauce. I love lobster, so I loved this 
13. Hen of the woods mushrooms: roasted with horseradish, really good
14. Venison: I had this before but had to get it again because it's so tender and flavorful. it's cooked in ash dough, and it comes with a beet venison reduction and crispy beets. My boyfriend doesn't even like beets but thought this was amazing. 
15. Duck: his main for the meat course. The duck is dry aged in house for 14 days with coriander, lavender, and peppercorns. The duck jus with citrus was amazing. 
16. Cheese course: I was kind of sad it wasn't the cheese cart from last year, but this was a great apple based course. It was a cheddar tart with a baked apple, a jar of bacon marmalade (amazing!), and a bigger greens salad with a light apple vinaigrette. I love apples, and I love cheese, so this was great and was more unique than a cheese cart
17. Bitter almond ice cream over a ginger snap crumble, served with a spoon of riesling on the side. The wine was a bit sweet for me, but I loved the rest of the dish 
18. Milk and honey custard with bee pollen ice cream. Something about the distinct sweetness of honey always gets me, and this dish was surprisingly light but very satisfying 

Then surprise: a kitchen tour!  Jonathan led us into the kitchen, and there was actually a table awaiting us where they made us individual snow cones with apple brandy syrup and fresh cream. 

We finished with a game of name the chocolate where you get 4 chocolates (cow, bison, sheep, and goats milk) and you need to figure out which is which. They also poured us some apple brandy made especially for EMP by St. George distillery, and of course we had the chocolate pretzels and granola to go.

We weren't stuffed, and I was actually hoping for more food, but I think it was a good amount. Service was wonderful, and it was a great birthday dinner!

I'm giving it 3 stars only because I didn't like their tasting menu that evening. Everything else in terms of service, ambiance, and presentation was immaculate and impeccable, hands down 5 stars. 

Highlights:
-Cheddar Black and White Cookie
-Foie Gras 
-Farmers Cheese Sundae with honey/grape/sorrel/oats 

Lowlights:
-Ok, the first dislike is more of a personal taste and is biased. I am not a cucumber person and I'm not sure if it would have made any difference, but I should have let them aware of that. The first dish that came out was tuna marinated in this gelatin cucumber (I did not appreciate the texture and I'm still not a fan of cucumber).
-Lobster boil with clams/shrimp/beans - overall good but the portion was way too skimpy for 4 people. We must have had 2 pieces of seafood each... 
-Braised Sunflower....who wants to eat braised sunflower? It tasted like what you would think it would taste like.
-Mast Brother Chocolates - The game of guessing what type of milk the chocolate bars were made from (cow, goat, buffalo, and what was the fourth?) sounds like a fun idea but..some of those tasted absolutely disgusting...and I felt like the chef got a free pass and I got jipped on a dessert. Hey, I am afterall paying for a dining experience!

Many people prefer EMP over Per Se, so I'm sure it was just the menu I got that evening and I will have to go back and check it out again.

Definitely my favorite of the various prix fixe restaurants.  The presentation/story behind each course is fantastic, the food is great (and feel stuffed before we get to the final courses) and the wait staff is very friendly.

A great spot for a special occasion dinner!

Okay! I think most of ppl would say exactly the same thing about this place - how good it is! I totally agree! 

What I really want to mention is that we had a kitchen tour after our dinner. so make sure u ask for that when they email you what you expect from ur upcoming dinner! The waiter was nice and he introduced us to different chefs and u got to see their work stations. They also offered shaved ice, making it in front of you! 

I always believe that good restaurants can make complimentary food tasty. It is also true for EMP. Their granola I would just die for and can finish the entire jar by myself! It's a really memorable gift!

Best dining experience of my life... And I'm from New Orleans. This place is unbelievable. The service alone is out of this world... Word on the street, they google all of their guests before hand to cater their service to you (from the south? Southern waiter.. Etc.) additionally, every dining experience is completely unique. You will never have the same dinner twice there. You choose your flavor pallet out of four unique herbs and spices. Oh, speaking of pallets - literally just tell them your flavor profile for cocktails and they make you your perfect drink.. Like p-e-r-f-e-c-t. I'm partly convinced that they just had a cocktail with my exact name on it back there. Also- if your server asks you if you're down for an adventure at any point in the meal JUST SAY YES. I won't spoil the surprise and tell you what happens, but trust me on that one if you get to be one of lucky ones.

Came here for the second time. This may be the best restaurant I go to. I love how they give you a background or story for some of the dishes. Anything with caviar and eggs here is perfection. I wish I can just order 10 of these. Their menus differ so don't expect some of the things I tried to be on your tasting menu. I posted pics of all the dishes on the tasting. Check them out! 

Some notable things - Eating sunflower for the first time was very interesting. It's pretty good too. One of their desserts where you guess which animal's milk was used to make the chocolate was very entertaining. I even brought the remaining chocolate bars for my co-workers to try and guess. This is a great marketing strategy for them. You're welcome EMP!

Short review... amazing and entertaining!!! 
Not the Nappa Valley " At the meadows " , my favorite 3 Michelin Star restaurant in the world , but this one taking a close second !

What an absolutely amazing experience!  Initial impressions were of impeccable service with welcoming and extremely attentive staff. 

The food was prepared and presented with such precision and finesse. This is food, the way it was meant to taste, each course thrilled with the first bite... poetry in your mouth!

We were lucky enough to get a tour of the kitchen - the fluidity and precision of the entire operation is incredible.  

An experience to be had at least once in your life. Without a doubt the best dining experience in NYC!!

We were very lucky to be able to have our small wedding lunch here some years ago. It was just the most perfect, amazing meal ever. Even today our guests thank us for inviting them to their best meal in their lives.
Everything good that you read about them is true, and yes, it is expensive, but if you can try it at least once, do it, it is not just a meal, it is a whole culinary experience cared to the detail that´s going to stick with you forever.

Eleven Madison park, what can I say! It's off the bucket list but didn't live up to the hype. They kept it very simple food was tasty but lacked in presentation( not all) The kitchen tour is a must. Service got off to a very slow start and for so many waiters I thought could have been a lot better! Service staff were great, ambience is nice and combination of dishes was good. All in all a good experience but for as many stars as this place has and 35 chef's , 40 wait staff, I think there is room for improvement
Been here a few times over the years. It's never gotten old, the staff is incredible and the food is always out of this world. Always a special treat when I get to eat here.

Love everything about this place! Service, food, portions, ambience, quality, etc. can't say enough good things! 
Having gone to seven of nine 3 Michelin star restaurants this is my number 1. Well done 11 Madison!

Dang....3.5 hrs for so little food.  Sigh. 

Really sad to say this, but our tasting menu tonight was pretty underwhelming. There were a lot of creative pickling and small portions of veggies which were garnished n beautifully presented ....but failed to follow through in taste. The "tomato in oil" dish was too concentrated n acidic; it was pretty much like eating a fancy version tomato paste. There was a mini pickled eggplant and then another pickled sunflower heart. OMG. 

The desserts were more salty than sweet.  

There were so many courses, but each were pretty much bite size. I did not need 15 mins each to eat them. Actually, I didn't eat half of the meal. 

To their credit, the fois gras with the fried shallot crumble was AMAZING, so was the corn/cream/caviar dish. The duck was good, but we each only got a sliver of it....what happend to the rest of the duck?? The seafood boil was made well, but had a bunch of, again, seemingly pickled veggies and only a few pieces of real meat. 

The fois gras proves that they've got skills here at EMP, but their creative culinary artistry got ahead of them. Instead of presenting their diners with an ensemble of delicious and satisfying dishes, I felt we were guinea pigs here to pay A LOT to taste a food experiment. 

There were a lot of "womp womp WOMP" moments. I felt teased. And I left not full....and I am a small person. 

I apologize. I know I'm ranting. 

*the extra star is for the impeccable service and gorgeous décor.

At EMP, if you do tasting menu, you probably will only enjoy 2-3 dishes from the menu and the rest are just chef's own obsession & don't care what you feel. The food is masterpiece of cutting edge culinary techniques, yet it lacks the emotional connection or mind-blowing moments you might have eating a great fried chicken or BBQ ribs. 

The restaurant does try hard to provide you great service, not the staff --- they do what the manual told them to and nothing beyond. Sommelier knows what's on the list, but don't expect much pairing advices unless you order the pairing option. 

Speaking of experience, personally I would say it has more showmanship than any regular restaurants, however details such as course timing, table deco are average at best. Except you don't know what will be served next, it doesn't have much element of surprise nor personal touch.

For anyone open-minded and curious about modern culinary art, I still recommend them to go.  For special occasion or just want to have a great time, you might be sadly disappointed and price paid worth think twice about what you are really looking for.

If you like pickled cucumber several different ways, then this is your place.    Extremely disappointed.  Everything is sour and vinegary.  I would not pay $50 to eat this let alone $500.  But thats just me.

Amazing. One of the best dining experiences I've had. Food and service were top notch. I told management ahead of time that it was my boyfriend's birthday, and that he was a chef and they gave him an engraved knife along with a private tour of the kitchen. Kudos to EMP for making his birthday one for the books!

Seriously? Go to The Modern at MoMA or Dovetail instead. Surely a Michellin rated restaurant should have character and ambiance. The staff are disconnected and robotic - friendliness is almost frowned upon.

For beautifully constructed French flavors and chic, elegant but warm atmosphere - go to The Modern at MoMA. Soooooo much more of an experience.

Fantastic dinner, with a couple of memorable dishes (Eggs Benedict, the Pork Jowl, and the tomato) were absolutely amazing. It is a lengthy dinner, ours took about 4 hours, so just keep that in mind when making reservations.
Simply the most wonderful dining experience I've ever had. Everything from the service, food and ambiance was just perfect. Every dish was unbelievably good. Definitely worth trying it at least once!

I dined here last night and sad to say was very, very, VERY disappointed with the food. Let me give you a rundown of my experience:

Ambience:
-Similar to a brasserie/bistro with Art Deco finishing...it was nice but not what I could expect for a $225 pp (ex tax and tip FYI) place. I had expected it to be a lot more upscale.

Service:
-Plenty of wait staff (approx 2 per table). It was generally on point except that they served coffee to us when we didn't order it (which they granted to us free), and that one time where I had to order bread twice. We had a nice maitre'd called Peter who happened to also be Australian and was very friendly and accommodating. 

Food:
-This is where I subtract several stars. I don't even know where to begin here...
-Each dish was either too savory, sour or bitter for my liking. We were told the chef likes acidic food so I guess that is the reasoning behind that. It left a weird aftertaste in my mouth (not to mention I was feeling thirsty the whole meal) and there was all but one dish - the one with the corn, caviar and quail egg - which balanced the heavy acidic emphasis. 
-one of their dishes was a sunflower heart...which looked like an artichoke heart when cooked but tasted so bad I winced from the bitterness. No idea wtf they were thinking with that one. 
-weird eggplant dish - a mini eggplant filled with weird fermented beans...I can't describe it but it was less than desirable 
-one dish contained a slab of foie gras...I swear they added no seasoning or at least cut down the portions so it was edible...I had to give some away to my friend.
-the last 3 dishes were made of cheese...again, way to overkill on the savory. 
-seafood stew/gumbo. Boston does it so much better. Very underwhelming.

All in all, I do not think this restaurant deserves the top 5 in the world, or no 1 in the US. I have had cheaper meals elsewhere which were way better. I find it insulting that we're being charged almost $300 pp for substandard food like this. I won't be back and urge anyone interested to dine here to check out their menu before they attempt. Maybe I went during the wrong season or something.

Exquisite experience!  This was not just a meal, it was an "experience."  We went to celebrate a milestone and they made sure that it was a special time.  The food was great, the drinks fantastic, and the ambience perfect.  Best of all, the service is unreal.  This is one of the best restaurants in the city and you can tell by the quality of the waitstaff.  They were committed to providing a first rate experience.  Fabulous!

My favorite restaurant of all time.  A culinary, quintessential dining and taste experience. Just amazing ambiance, killer menu - the wine options and expertise, it truly is iconic NYC dining. You can arrive in jeans and take in an amazing evening, or dressed for that perfect special occasion, it just for some reason is magical in its own way... Clearly, my favorite NYC eatery.

EMP lived up to its lofty status and reputation as being a top ten restaurant in the world. The meal spanned nearly five hours and was not only a culinary adventure, but also performance art and entertainment. You will pay dearly with your wallet, but EMP represents a restaurant that you won't soon forget. 

Food: There is no menu. You are presented with two choices out of the approximately 14 course meal: How you want your foie gras prepared (seared or terrine) and your choice of duck or veal (represents the "main" course that the whole table shares. Every course was unique and included only the freshest ingredients and creative presentations. I won't go into detail into each course as the photos of the menu and each course tells the story, but we all agreed that the highlights were the caviar eggs benedict, carrot tartar, and the duck. But each and every one of the courses was exciting, interesting, and delicious! 

Drinks: You can also choose to order alcohol a la carte or opt for wine/beverage pairings that start at $150 and go up from there. We opted for the $150 pairing that included pairings for half of the courses, which ended up being more than enough as they were generous with the pourings and top-offs (more on beverages below). The sommelier was attentive and extremely knowledgeable and we enjoyed unique wines from all over the world that we would likely have not tried anywhere else. We especially enjoyed the white wine served with the pike and the red wine served with the duck (That included the sommelier melting off the neck of the bottle - super cool!). 

Service: Impeccable. A whole army of servers seamlessly integrated with the meal and were never intrusive. Appreciated their willingness to joke and have some fun. All questions and requests were answered promptly. Perfect 10. 

Ambience: Elegant, lofty space with tables spread apart and with all of the accompaniments of a 3 michelin star restaurant. The noise level become progressively higher the later it got (our reservations were at 6:30) as the restaurant steadily became more crowded. The energy in the room also grew as well.

4/5 stars calculated by giving a 1-5 rating on each of the 14 courses we had... 53/14 = 3.7 rounding up to 4/5 stars. Service was good, but a little more casual than we were expecting for the price point. We had a wonderful experience and were happy to try EMP, it was the culinary highlight of our trip to NYC over the weekend and hope to return in the future.

AMBIANCE/DECOR
Could use an update. The music was horrendous, either don't have it at all or please find a way to make this more modern. It reminded me of elevator music. The interior was similar to a courthouse, it's high ceilings and big windows would be sexy with a more modern look.  I'm sure a good designer can make this happen. Another point to mention, we called the day and the hour down to the minute of the reservation line being open and still our choices were either 5:45 or 10:00 seatings.  The restaurant was empty until 7:30-8:00.  That's kind of confusing to us.  I understand you're holding for VIPs and such, but come on.  At any given point during our four hour tour there were open tables.  I was happy though to dine in the same place Carrie and Mr. Big had lunch in the episode "Ex and the City".  Yes I am a die hard SATC fan so what.  Restrooms were nice.

SERVICE
Initially upon being seated we were a little disappointed.  It was an empty restaurant until 7:30-8ish and they had initially seated us trucker style along the wall.  No one likes to sit trucker style.  It's uncomfortable and awkward.  We requested to be moved to a table in the corner right away and they accommodated- but not without checking with the host staff first.  We had many servers throughout the evening so it was difficult to say who was the main go to guy.  The wine service was fantastic and we appreciated speaking with her, she was incredibly personable.  We were both wearing black and were not offered black napkins and had to ask for them.  As did the table next to us.  This should be a standard upon guests walking in, a minor detail but important in this caliber of restaurant.  A little bit casual on the service in my opinion.  But I get it, they're not going for stuffy here.  Note this section did not factor into our 4 star review.

CUISINE
4/5 here.  There were a few dishes we really enjoyed, the first being the Tuna marinated with cucumber (I love both of these things) and then the Caviar dish.  The caviar dish was eggs benny style and was a delectable little cup of heaven.  The Foie Gras was good too, more up my husband's alley than mine, but decadent nonetheless.  These were pretty much the shining stars of the evening.  The "mains" of the evening including the lobster boil and the duck left something be desired.  The duck was a little tough (I assume due to the dry aging process?) and the lobster boil was just ok.  Though I liked it, my husband did not, the sunflower was not a favorite at our table.  It was kind of a filler dish and was just a little boring.  We enjoyed most all of the desserts because we like tart things, I could see how if you're not a fan of the "euro tart" or sour taste how these wouldn't sit well with you as some of the other recent reviews indicate.

WINE
We opted for the pairings throughout.  My husband did the more eclectic tasting menu while I went with the traditional/Old World wine selections.  Mine was superior, his gave him a little bit of a hangover the next day. The varietals were interesting, Roses from Long Island and such, but mine was definitely better taste and quality wise.  His was also $70 less expensive to boot.

Happy to dine at this 3 star, it's certainly a standout in the Michelin establishments.  Overall happy camper here.

Left us wondering if we made the right choice. Lets start where most things start at the beginning:

The Reservation:  28 days ago at 9am and 1 second I found myself feverishly calling their number to get a reservation.  For some reason it actually doesn't open until 40 seconds later I am put on hold for 18 mins. Finally I am able to get a reservation on Labor Day Weekend at 715pm. Perfecto!

 The 28 Day Wait... I am so excited I have probably read every review looked at every photo I can not wait any longer.  A few days out I am emailed by the Matrie'd and asked if they can make out night more memorable. Lets be honest my requests were not to rent out the whole restaurant so my tiger can also eat with me or that I have a phobia of anything purple on the plate. I simply explain it is my parents 30th anniversary and also request a tour of the kitchen.  I am emailed back that they are thrilled we choose to dine at EMP and have also made a request to see the kitchen during our meal.

The Day:  Finally today is the day.  We arrive right at 715pm.  Walk in the Matrie'd greats us. And we are taken to our table.  The room is beautiful sunflowers everywhere we are seated and given the tea service list and a 160 page wine list.
