If you have never been to EMP before they also have an upstairs where a private party must have also just been getting started because all of a sudden people start to take flash photos down at us. I look up to see some guy laughing and pretending to unbuckle his pants and bending over to moon us... Great I didn't take my parents to EMP I took them to the Delta frat party at Animal House :(. My Somm was there and joked the thing off but I knew my parents seem horrified at the situation. 

The Drinks.  We decided on a bottle of Bordeaux unfortunately my bottle did not cost thousands of dollars so we were not given the hot port tong opening.  My parents since they do not drink went with the table-side tea service. My parents really enjoyed the tea service and the knowledge and presentation that came along.  Todd one of the servers even went out of his way to bring another glass of tea over for my parents to pair with their duck which they loved!  

The Food:  The food was everything you can think it would be.  The pan seared Foie Gras with Plum and Thyme and the Caviar with Benedict with egg corn and ham were my favorites.  Also my mothers father just passed away and his favorite flower was the sunflower.  So it was amazing that they had a dish that you actually eat the heart of the sunflower.  The presentation of every dish really made the night enjoyable and after 3 hours we could not believe that we had been there so long it felt like only 20 minutes.  But like anyone at a 5 hour dinner we hit a wall around our Duck course.  

Things Turn South:  During our duck course we have been there almost 4 hours and we ask about the table side coffee service. We are told usually that the SOMM will be back over during the start of our desert course to explain everything but we decided to go with table side ground coffee now.  We are tired and excited to try the coffee.  We wait... and wait... and wait...we wait so long that our cheese course comes out, our whey course comes out we ask again about the coffee and told that it takes some time to set everything up.  We wait some more...now our berry course comes out.  Still no coffee we eat our berry course which I really wish was with our coffee.  The berry course was my favorite desert.  I guess I should have licked my plate clean because when someone tried to clear my plate she split what was left literally on my head and on my jacket :(.  Now I am tired still no coffee and I am cleaning White Currant Sorbet off my head.  We ask again about the coffee and at this point wonder if there is any reason to still get the coffee.  We are told not to worry we still have two courses left and the coffee will be best paired with the name that chocolate game.  My father starts his timer after 10 minutes longer he gets up to speak with the matrie'd  I am not sure if there is only 1 coffee cart and we were just lower on the list but literally 4 courses came out and it must have been around 60 minutes of waiting endlessly for coffee.  We finally get our coffee.  Its almost the end of the meal and I wonder if we are still going to get the tour of the kitchen.  I do a quick yelp search and read about people going to the kitchen at the end of the meal so I still hold on to hope. We end our meal. Nope no kitchen tour.  

The Recap:  I guess the best way to recap my parents 30th anniversary dinner is we sit down when we get home my father looks at me and goes.  I guess no kitchen tour :(

I am sorry to say that I really did not enjoy my meal here. It really wasn't just one thing. I didn't love the menu setup or the individual courses either. There may have been one or two that I did enjoy but that's about it. I also didn't like the ambiance. I felt like it was way too loud to even concentrate on my dishes. I thought it was cool that they bring you into the kitchen for some part of the dessert. Seeing the kitchen is always great because that's the heart and soul of each restaurant. Overall, maybe someday I'll come back but not in the near future.

Having lived in NYC for a few years, my husband and I have definitely had our share of delicious meals-- and this place did not disappoint. Service was impeccable from the moment you walk through the doors. Each course built perfectly on the last, making this a most enjoyable meal.

Make sure you call for reservations as soon as those phones lines open, as this is a meal you don't want to miss.

This should be a 37-star rating, but alas I'm trapped at five. I can't even.

There is a reason that Eleven Madison Park is rated as the #5 restaurant in the world. In fact there are countless reasons...well, however many I can fit into this review!

Reservations: 28 days before the day I wanted to go (my wife's 30th birthday!), I was up at 8:45am. Phone had the number already punched in, and I waited. The SECOND it hit 9am, I dialed and prayed and prayed and waited and prayed. Lo and behold, I was able to get through to the reservation team and make a reservation for when I wanted! Amazing!!

The experience: Sheer dining bliss. From the moment we arrived, the staff were incredible. This is by far the most professional, meticulous, engaging staff at a restaurant I've ever had the pleasure to dine with; from the continual genuine "happy birthdays" my wife received to never waiting more than 30 seconds to have a dish cleared or a glass filled, to watch them circulate to every table providing the same attention to detail. Incredible! We were greeted by the host, sat at our table, and then had the experience explained by another staff. No menu, no ordering - just sit back and enjoy the show!

The food: What. the. what. I can't even. It's brilliant! 14 courses of the most exquisitie, delicious, beautiful, creative food of all time ever amen and amen. We began with a box on the table that we were instructed to open - inside contained a savory black and white cookie (cheddar and apple). A three-michelin star cheezit that was to die for! That was followed by several vegetable courses, my favorite being the tomato soup. They miraculously take puree and soft-mold it into the shape of a tomato slice. When it arrives at your table, you think "ok i'm getting a slice of tomato in a bowl" BUT WAIT it's actually delicious soup!! Then the foie gras. What. the. WHAT. Pan-seared with duck-fat renderings on top. Followed by their take on benedict with caviar, quail egg, and a corn/ham gel. At this point my wife and I are literally giggling/in awe and cannot believe this is real. Then the table-side fish boil, the perfectly prepared duck and pork jowl, and sunflower. Yup, they cook a sunflower and it is so daggone good!! Then a palate cleanser and three dessert courses, including a fun game where you are given four bars of chocolate (love this game already!) and you have to identify which animal's milk sourced the chocolate.

3.5 hours later, my wife and I simply staggared out of Eleven Madison Park, feeling absolutely elated and still in awe of the brilliance of what we had experienced. Granted for the next six weeks we are on a strict ramen and american cheese diet to pay for the whole thing, but 100000% worth it!

The Story: I would like to announce that one of my bucket list restaurants is now off my list. I've been dreaming about coming here for quite a while now so when my cousin asked if anyone is interested to go with her, my name was one of the very first on the list! 

Food: Usually I will list what I liked and what I didn't like but I feel like this place deserved a list. Luckily they provided me with a menu so I know what they served me. (I know they try to explain each dish but I'm usually too busy oogling the plate lol)

I had a total of 16 amazing bites of culinary heaven..

1. Chedder: Savory Black & White Cookie with Apple. - I wanted this cookie to be sweet but enjoyed it nevertheless. 

2. Tuna: Marinated with Cucumber - Presentation for this is lovely. It tasted like I was eating a salad. 

3. Eggplant: Slow-cooked with Shelling Beans and Mint - It tasted to me like a pickled plum and I was at first taken aback because I was expecting eggplant.

4. Squid: Poached with Peppers and Artichoke - This plate was also beautiful and you can really taste how the squid and peppers mix together.

5. Tomato: Salad with Basil and Red Onion - Presentation was great. I expected a slice of tomato but it tasted like a hearty tomato soup instead.

6. Caviar: Benedict with Egg, Corn and Ham - This is the dish that started to get me excited. The first 5 dish I've already tasted the flavor profile elsewhere. They served this with mini english muffins and the soft boiled quail egg in the middle is amazing. Gooey Goodness!

7. Foie Gras: Seared with Thyme - This is actually my first time trying Foie Gras. It's a little heavy for my taste and the portion they gave me was way too much. The flavor profile with the pickled apricot was amazing though. My brother also joked that 11 Madison Park ruined my Foie Gras experience because it's probably the best in the world.

8. Bread: Served with Cow's Milk Butter & Duck Fat Butter - I had one right away because I was still hungry at this point. I didn't eat breakfast because I was expecting 16 courses. I liked the regular butter over the duck fat. 

9. Lobster: Boile with clams, shrimp and beans -   There wasn't much in this dish but everything was cooked perfectly. I'm not a lobster girl but their bite of lobster made me second guess myself.

10. Sunflower: Braised with Green Tomato and Sunflower Sprouts - I find this dish interesting. However, I didn't really like the flavor profile for this dish. Very pretty though.

11. Duck: Roasted with Lavender, Honey, Apricots, and Fennel - I LOOOVED this dish. I was excited when they brought out the display duck to tell us Duck is going to be our next course. The skin was crispy and the meat was tender. I think I definitely spend a lot longer savoring this dish. 

12. Farmer's Cheese: Sundae with Honey, Cherry, Sorrel and Oats - I'm not a big cheese eater. The cheese by itself is extremely salty but paired with the flavors on the lazy susan...HEAVEN. 

13. Whey: Sorbet with Caramelized Milk and Yogurt - I'm a derp that ate just the whey and yogurt and complained to my cousins that its too "tart". Dug a little deeper and my opinion changed instantly. Wow! Love the balance of flavors.

14. Berry: Cheesecake with White Currant Sorbet and Raspberry Vinegar - It's like eating cake without the cake. Beautiful flavors balanced so well. 

15. Chocolate: Name That Milk - They presented us with 4 chocolate bars made with different animal milk (cow, buffalo, goat and lamb). I now know my palate works lol The goat and lamb chocolate isn't that good...

16. Chocolate 2.0: Pretzel with Sea Salt - This is by far the best chocolate pretzel I've ever had. It's white chocolate dipped into regular chocolate and has hints of pretzel in it. AMAZING!

17. Fruit Bar: with Abraham - After exiting the restaurant, we were instructed to go say "hello" to Abraham and he'll give us a gift. We got a iced fruit bar. Yum!
                       

Price: $225 per person with no wine paring. A splurge but definitely worth it. 

Decor:  Really nice high ceilings and natural lighting from huge glass windows. Sunflowers everywhere. Beautiful place. 

Service: As expected, the service was amazing! My glass of water never hit under 50% mark, all the plates were placed in-front of us at the same time. They kept our table clean even though breadcrumbs where flying all over the place. I was pretty sure we each had our own waiter/waitress, but I cannot confirm that 100%.

Parking & Finding the Place: Located at 11 Madison Avenue in New York City. My cousins thought I was joking when I said that was the address haha. It's right across from the Madison Park and you can get here either by cab, car service or the subway (6).  .

Additional Thoughts: Truly a once in a life time dream come true. I am fortunate enough to have experienced this culinary adventure and if I'm lucky, I'll be back sometime in the distant future.

WORDS CAN'T EVEN. Worth every penny. Amazing food, service, decor--there's a reason it's consistently one of the best restaurants in the world. 

Apparently this was the year of splurging on food w/ Ko + EMP but totally worth it. I won't go into detail about all the courses... I can say it didn't start out mind blowing but by the end I was sooo food happy. I LOVED their eggs benedict w/ quail egg and caviar, it was just perfect. One of two foods that have ever made me close my eyes as I just enjoyed the taste. Seafood boil and duck entree really shone as well. Best. Duck. Ever. Minus the too small of a piece because I could have gone ham on that whole duck. 

As for desserts, the whey sorbet was pretty interesting... Humm and his team do an amazing job of making combinations of flavors work and whey for dessert is a prime example. Sour and very strong flavor on its own but perfectly balanced when eaten with the caramel and toffee bits on the bottom. The milk chocolate w/ the MAST Brothers collaboration is a fun touch, but IMO goat's milk and sheep's milk chocolate are disgusting. Not my thing; couldn't get past just one bite of the sheep's milk one. The pretzels at the end were incredible--how do they get that texture?? I was about to grab the ones left over at the table beside us. Can take the girl out of the hood but can't take the hood out of the girl. Just pretending to be fancy at EMP. 

Lunch took 4 hours and rounded out with a take-home baggie w/ a jar of granola and a printout of the day's tasting menu. Sister and cousin got chocolate bars as well to celebrate their belated birthdays! Final surprise outside was also a nice touch :) Hopefully I'll be back sometime in the (maybe not so near, I can practically hear Mint scolding me) future.

Wow. Where do I start...?
Service: the best service I experienced. Ever. Some things about the service that stood out - when I asked where the restroom was, I wasn't pointed in a direction... I was escorted to the door! Also, when I get up from my seat at a table I have a habit of loosing my napkin. I hang it on the chair and it falls. Here, I got up from the table a few times and when I came back there was a fresh napkin on the table waiting for me. Oh... And when some of the people at the table were cold they were offered a basket of pashminas. 
Food: amazing. Some of us had food allergies like gluten, nuts, dairy and more. The restaurant did an amazing job accommodating. They even had gluten free chocolate covered pretzels. They were also able to whip some great dairy substitutes on demand using coconut,  soy and almond milk. The flavors were as unique as the presentation.
They made a dish out of a sunflower. Who knew one could eat that or that the dish could be this interesting?
Other notables: there was a chocolate tasting game at the end of the meal that the child in me enjoyed a lot. 
Dinner can last as long as 5 hours and they give you breakfast to go. 
The place is pricey, but for a special occasion it is worth a try!

We visited for a special occasion dinner in July.  They checked in about a week before the reservation to see if we had any special needs, and were quite accommodating.  This was a long, 3-hour dining affair that never seemed rushed.  The service was phenomenal without being stuffy (one of our waitstaff had a great sense of humor, which really put us at ease for being in such an exclusive-feeling place).  There were definitely some interesting culinary surprises, including the tomato "salad" which came looking like a slice of a beefsteak tomato but was actually created from some kind of intensely flavorful tomato puree, reminiscent of a Michel Richard trick.  Other standouts include the lobster boil (if you ask for it they will provide a shooter of the broth), the caviar with tiny english muffins and of course the post-meal granola.  The sunflower was beautiful and  creative, though not as flavorful as it looked.  Overall just an amazing experience, and comfortably paced allowing us to savor every bit.

Their service was, as expected, excellent. I have to commend the waiters. They were very pleasant and attentive, i really felt well taken care of, and they weren't pushy or annoying in any way. They gave us plenty of time to savor the menu and overall just made our dinner truly wonderful.The food was divine. I was very impressed on how they tailor the menu to your dietary specifics, like food allergies, preferences and so on. I am amazed by how good the food was. The portions weren't that big, but you come here for the experience. It's so worth it. They put in an amazing amount of imagination and ingenuity with their dishes, making them as perfect a dish can get. I highly recommend this place for any food lover!

Ate here for our son's birthday--wonderful!!  Servers were great and attentive.  Food & wine pairing was DELICIOUS!!  Enjoyed all the selections.  The sunflower presentation & dish was interesting.  Loved the gift of Granola mix in Mason jar & copy of the Menu given @ the end of our meal.  Beautiful place to celebrate a special occasion.

Came for the food, but the wine pairing stole the show.  Dustin Wilson had ostensibly moved on to other pastures before my experience but the sommelier was truly fantastic.  I had a ton of fun and learned a good deal.  

I would provide a more thorough, detailed review, but what can I add?  You're sure to have a different, equally magnificent experience, so treat yourself and have a great night.

I am afraid I have to say I am very disappointed at my experience having lunch here three days ago. 
Do not get me wrong. The dishes were super visually appealing and creative. The ambience and decor were great.  Everything seems perfect only except one fact that the food was not delicious. 

The thing I do not understand is that they put so much effort into creating beautiful dishes but they simply cannot make it delicious or tasty, which drives me crazy.
For example, the sunflower was so presentable and the dish was visually appealing but the taste was totally in the opposite. The Farmer's Cheese- sundae, was too sour as well as the sorbet served right after.  I could not even finish these two dishes. 
I believe they must had spent so much effort to make the dishes look good and interesting, but why do not they care about the taste? The most basic standard for a dish cannot even meet and it is a Michelin 3. I do not understand and really disappointed.  

Another really awful part is that I did not like the food so much and could not finish. My server did not feel a thing or ask anything and the service was intermittent. And again, it is Michelin 3. The food taste bad and the server was absent-minded. Really really disappointed...

I'm not in control of other peoples' money for a living, so unfortunately I can't afford myself the luxury of eating here on a whim. 

Luckily, I got married and took that as an occasion to finally try Eleven Madison Park. 

The servers were kind enough to ask about and accommodate everyone's preferences and allergies, and each course was altered slightly for each diner to suit this. Daniel Humm's menu was perfect, and Danny Meyer's efforts to take care of people weren't lost on us. 

Every course was beautiful. We opted for the more eclectic (and slightly less expensive) wine pairing, and it was well done, matching each course perfectly. The service was friendly, and quick, and the food was without exaggeration some of the best I've had in my entire life. 

We were given jars of granola and a copy of our menu at the end of the meal, and overall the experience was great. I will likely never be able to eat here again, but I'm glad I was able to at least once.
It was a fun meal with great friends. Dishes were creative and service was sincere.

Great Service, Great Food, Great Experience 
All the Food was great sans the Sunflower course which was frivolous and tasteless . Everything else was great . The Classic Duck Breast, the new Pork with Watermelon radish. Loved the squid course and the Clam Bake. The opening tuna course was another standout. The Caviar Eggs Benedict course stole the show. The wine service was brilliant Great parings including sake, beer & rose. John, the sommelier, is the man. Will and Chef Humm have this place firing on all cylinders and keep changing the menu to make you want to come back. Still at the top of NY fine dining.

I've been here twice with friends and every time I've been surprised. Amazing food, every detail thought out, amazing drinks/wines, this is what food heaven must feel like. If you can swing it, try to get a kitchen tour, it's well worth it to see the magic happen.

I went here in the spring and have hesitated to share my review. I am definitely a self proclaimed foodie and needed to try this place! I saved up for a number of months do that I could enjoy the tasting menu with wine pairings. My total tab with tax and tip was $510, which is what I expected so that was fine. 

The food was amazing! I loved the creativity of the courses---added a big element of fun. There was an heirloom tomato soup with lemon thyme that blew me away! The duck was PERFECTION! Everything was absolutely delicious. Very nice wine pairings as well. 

Where I was disappointed was in the service. I went with a friend for lunch at 12:30pm as it was difficult to get a dinner reservation. I felt that 12:30 was early enough that there was no need for us to feel rushed. However, our server kept bringing out the next course before we finished our 3 ounce wine "pairings." We literally had 2-3 glasses of wine a piece sitting in front of us at any time. Considering that it was a wine "pairing" this seemed strange. We felt disappointingly rushed. 

My friend mentioned to the server delivering the wine that we had a collection of wine in front of us. He was quick to inform us that it isn't an uncommon circumstance. We looked around the full dining room and only saw one other guest with several wine pours in front of him. 

I then mentioned to our head server that we felt stressed out because our courses were coming out faster than we were finishing our wine pairings (we weren't drinking THAT slowly). He was quick and defensive saying that many people don't finish their pours. Excuse me, but for that price, of COURSE I'm finishing my pour!!! I came to enjoy and savor everything to the fullest. After asking, he did slow down the courses, and miraculously we were out in plenty of time for the restaurant to prepare for the dinner crowd. 

I thoroughly enjoyed the food, but my experience was quite tainted by the fact that I felt rushed and it felt like adding insult to injury that two servers were defensive when we let them know that we weren't happy with the rushing of the courses. 

I went to the French Laundry a number of years before and both the food and the service were fantastic. Unfortunately my experience at Eleven Madison Park turned me off enough that I don't want to go back. Maybe I'll try the NoMad because Chef Daniel Humm clearly does his craft well.
Excellent service! Great place to celebrate special event, but unfortunately i have to say the food is just okay... The taste was not as impressive as the presentation...

This meal was worth the price I paid.  The service, presentation, vibe, creative cooking, etc was the best I have ever experienced.  But, would I go back there again?? Not for $1200 for two.  (tasting menu plus wine pairing plus tip) That is one hefty ticket for yours truly.  Memorable? Absolutely.  Once a lifetime? Yep.  But I keep getting back to the 'once in a lifetime' thing.  Since I am not in the 1%,  it may be a 'once in a lifetime' meal. 

I read that the chef wanted to create a legacy.  I think he succeeded.  Kudos to him and his team.  I was struck by the millennial wait staff. All around the 30 mark, obviously well educated, and had a nice groove about working in a high end place.  What a difference from other 'high end's where it's dominated by professional 'male' waiters.  It was refreshing to see smart and engaged female captains.  Also the lingo.... our captain/sommalier was about 30, and on the first introduction of our pairing simply said, 'ok, we are going to start rocking'..... love it. 

So, in conclusion GREAT food, GREAT vibe, Super cool and engaged service. Go there as if you are going to see The Beatles. Front row seats to the best show in town. THAT is what you are going to get. Memorable and great.

Next time, I'll check the bar menu.

The only thing more perfect than the presentation of the food and the taste at Eleven is the fantastic service. From the moment we entered until the time we left, 2+ hours later, our server anticipated everything. Food arrived, plates were cleared, and the table was crumbed without us even noticing.

(4.75) ~ Excellent Overall Food & Service.  Best "Tasting" Menu we've had...

OUR TALLY:
** Service = (5) Excellent!
** Food = (4.75) Very Good!
** Coffee = (4.5) Very Good
Creative presentation throughout. Excellent quality and service. I didn't give 5 star because the taste was not one of the best I've had.

Bon appetite! 3 stars Michelin food tasting there. We started with the egg and mushroom appetizer and foie gras then tried the lobster with curry granola. The wine is paired with the meals. 

It is a gastronomic restaurant; expect tiny portions and high price. For instance, just a green tea cost $11. 

Decoration is art deco space style with high 30' ceiling.

Still pinching myself that I was able to eat here last night. . Everything was fantastic from the host, the server to the decadent, thoughtful food. Highlights: foie and the pork jowl. The bread was decadent!!!  There is a reason eleven Madison repeatedly makes the "best of" lists.

We took my MIL out for her birthday and it was a great evening had by all!  My MIL and FIL were both so happy with the food and the "blind" menu and the service was simply amazing.

Their sommelier was so knowledgeable (despite not having that sommelier metal that they wear around their neck) and made AMAZING wine recommendations.  My hubs and FIL went with the wine pairing and MIL and I had about 3 different glasses per recommendation by the somm and we were all very happy!

Lastly, to cap it off, we received a kitchen tour and it was STUNNING to see how a beautiful restaurant is run from the inside out.  It is like a choreographed dance!  The waiters are all lined up so that as soon as the food hits the counter they take it to the tables...amazing!

Overall, one of our favorite 3-Michelin starred restaurants and will certainly be back!!!!!!!

Solid restaurant

Service: top notch; what one would expect at this type of restaurant and for the price

Atmosphere: got lucky and got a corner table so was able to people watch...high ceilings, spacious

Food: everything was prepared to perfection

If the price wasn't so high, would go back more often but good for a special occasion

I arrived at EMP in shorts, a t-shirt, wearing a hat and carrying a ton of luggage.   I was also drunk.   The staff didn't seem like they cared the least.   I was treated just like everyone else which was amazing.  When it comes to food this is a Michelin 3 and San Pellegrino top 10, almost everything you'll eat is phenomenal.   The difference though between here and say Le Bernardin is the atmosphere and the ridiculously attentive staff.   EMP gives off no pretenses.   My friend made a face when he didn't like a dish.   The staff saw that from across the room and immediately the head chef came out and offered another dish.   This isn't just clearing a table and refilling a drink between courses, this is otherworldly service that shows they really care.   In any case.  5 stars at every phase.   This is a place that I flew from Texas for and thought not a penny was wasted.

What can I say that everyone else hasn't already said?

I'm a foodie. Like, I live, breathe, and dream of food. I go out to eat every single day and sometimes twice or three times a day. My guilty pleasures include: (you guessed it) food.

A friend of mine had suggested that we go to 11 Madison Park for quite some time. Alas, just a few short days after they were named the 5th best restaurant in the world, we decided to make a reservation and go all out.

I will start off by saying that I truly enjoy food "experiences". I love 5+ hour meals, tasting menu's, cocktail and wine pairings, you name it! I feel that this is lost in the modern age of dining as usually people want to get in and get out. Not me and not 11 Madison Park. Don't come here if you want a quick meal or really anything less than 3 hours. Don't rush. Don't panic. Relax. Woooooosa. It's okay. Sitting down for a great length of time and trying out heavenly dishes isn't so bad, trust me!

DECOR & AMBIANCE
Art deco/former bank. To be honest, I'm not really a fan of art deco or bank "decor". I would just say that this isn't my style. However, a great deal of people LOVE the decor here so it's really just a matter of preference. The ambiance is great as it just oozes elegance. Everyone is dressed from head to toe in pure perfection. One word: Classic.

SERVICE
Top-notch. Would you expect anything less? The service was absolutely perfect (and usually poor service is my greatest pet peeve at restaurants). Bravo!

FOOD
While I've had some truly exceptional meals in my lifetime, this one was definitely in the rankings. Every dish was obviously very tasty and delicious but I was particularly surprised by the creativity behind each dish. At the very end of the meal, chocolates were presented with a little guessing game. Many different flavors were presented and one would have to match the unknown flavors to their names. Later, someone brought a cheat sheet and provided the correct answers. I really liked this as it just seemed like a really fun way to end the evening.

Will I be back? Yes. I want to come back and try their lunch actually. MMM MMMMMM MMM!

Come here expecting not just a meal but an experience.

+ Also make sure you ask for a tour of the kitchen! It's immaculate!

Great spot for fine dining. I liked that the menu was creative and whimsical. The staff was engaging without being overbearing. I will definitely go back, but the dining room is in desperate need of a face lift.

Three Michelin stars and numerous amount of awards and accolades. Three Michelin stars mean the food is so good it's worth flying for. 
I feel lucky to have gone here because first of all I don't live here in New York. Secondly you need to make a reservation way in advance and me and the hubs come to New York spontaneously which makes it harder to book. BUT FINALLY THE TIMING WAS IN THE CARDS. I couldn't hold my excitement and was oh so excited...as this restaurant is rated Number FIVE in the whole world as of 2015. If you guys had dined in at Eleven Madison during 2011 and prior, I suggest you come again as the experience will be quite different. Before 2011 they had more affordable prix fix menus but the menu as well as the food have been redefined and fined tuned to perfection under the care of Daniel Humm. SInce 2012, the restaurant has received their 3 michelin stars consecutively and have shot to the top as one of the best restaurants in New York and the entire world.

The cuisine was sophisticated, elegant and unique and the flavors danced around my palate. 
The menu changes seasonally and these are some of the things that we were served. (don't they all sound so delicious?!
-Morel with custard with Trout Roe
-English Peas glazed with Buffalo Yogurt and Garlic
-Radish Salad with Pike and Nasturtium
-Caviar Benedict with Egg, Ham, and Asparagus (interesting flavors)
-Foie Gras Seared with Sorrel and Horseradish
-Carrot Tartare with Rye Crisps and Condiment (Favorite)
-Butter Poached Lobster with Dandelion and Ginger
-Asparagus braised in Pig's Bladder with Potato and Black Truffle (absolutely delicious)
-Duck Roasted with Lavendar honey, and rhubarb (Signature Dish)

Service was also exceptional. Eleven madison was everything and MORE. Highly recommend!

Amazing service, food, and ambiance! 11 Madison is probably the best restaurant I have been to in New York. I appreciate that the staff goes extra-mile to make you have not just a good, but an excellent experience in Eleven Madison. For example, at the end of the meal they would give food gifts, and since I have been there a couple of times, I wanted to see if I could get two granola bottles instead of one and they gave me four of them without hesitation! The food changes seasonally, so if you have been there two times in the same season for whatever reason, they will change the dishes so that you can have a different experience this time. This is my favorite restaurant around! 

Food: 5/5
Ambiance: 5/5
Service: 5/5

Went here with my wife, brother-in-law and his wife. We went to the bar, and had a good talk with an informative bartender about IPAs. We were seated promptly for our reservation and had immediate attention from a friendly and supportive sommelier. Throughout the dinner (which consisted of 15-some courses), every detail received attention (including the creation of similar but separate dishes for my wife who doesn't like seafood). 

Some of the dishes were truly inspired and fun. Others were, frankly, just weird. Overall, it was hard to find a theme or an overarching story behind the meal. It felt like a bunch of interesting, but disjointed;l, inventions from a big kitchen.  

The meal was (I think) the most expensive I've ever paid for, coming out at over $750 for the two of us, after we split the bill. That included our pre dinner drinks (2) and 4 1/2 bottles of wine (2 bottles total). 

Overall, a great service experience, but the slightly disappointing food led to an unjustified high price.

Flew in to New York for the week and I thought I'd treat the missus to a very nice meal. The service was excellent. Everyone was very knowledgeable in their craft. The dishes were all over the place however. The chef has great creativity but some of the dishes didn't give me that sense of wonder with the first bite as a Michelin 3 star should and one so highly rated. The wine pairing also seemed to be a little disconnected. Don't get me wrong the wines were great but I thought the pairing could have been a bit better. My gripe with the whole experience is that, I've eaten at 1 star places that were equal to what I had here and I forked out a lot more money for this meal expecting an experience. A bit dissapointed.

I wanted to come here ever since seeing that it was New York's top rated restaurant and as part of my personal "go to all 3 Michelin star restaurants in New York" plan. 

The menu is pre set on the day but you can tell them your dietary requirements before hand and they alter it to your taste so it works out quite well. Some of the foods such as the cheese with various toppings that you can add to your preference was lovely and a great savoury desert. The salty chocolate pretzel was also very delicious and a lot better than it sounds. 

When it comes to the food here though I would think of it more of an experience than for the pure food. Its quite innovate and I would suggest going once to anyone. That being said though other top michellin restaurants such as Jean George and Daniel in my opinion have better food in terms of pure taste in my opinion. The price here was a wee bit steep, after tax and tip if you have pure food it comes to around $300 or so. 

I'd recommend going and trying if you can but if you can only go to one top posh NYC restaurant I would recommend Jean George or Daniel instead.
So my best friend took me here for my birthday and everything was just simply amazing! My favorite was the surprise at the end!

Absolutely amazing experience. 

Eleven Madison Park has been on my radar for years for various reasons. As a Seattleite I've been a fan of Jason Franey's for years. Any place he's worked is a place I want to eat. Another reason is that this restaurant has been voted amongst the top in the entire world years in a row. And finally, it's convenient because the NYC office of my company is located in the same building. So why not?!

My fiancé and I took a weeklong trip to NYC to eat and drink our way through the city. The very highlight of our 6 day trip to over 20 bars/restaurants was eating here. 

Right upon entering you're warmly greeted by staff. They ask a few questions to learn about you and help customize the experience. We were then seated along the back wall in a position so that we could watch everything going on around us. For such a gorgeous and intimate feeling space, it's amazing how busy and loud it gets. Not loud in a way that affects your meal, but loud in a way that you're there and you're part of a communal experience with tons of other people eating the city's best dishes. Even with the buzzing of the staff and the commotion of other tables it wasn't necessary for me to shout or stretch to hear what my fiancé was saying as we talked through the nearly 4 hour, 15 course meal.

Table service is exquisite. If you watch, you'll spot staff members whose job it is to just watch the floor and take action when needed. If an empty plate or glass of water has sat for 1 second too long, they jump in and come to the rescue. For many dishes the kitchen staff comes out and begins to prepare or explain the dish upon arrival. Really nice touch for people curious about the meal and specific dishes.

We also had table-side bar service! There's a bartender that makes Manhattans from a portable bar cart that he wheels right over to the table. This was another fun touch as they had about a dozen spins on the classic Manhattan for you to choose from.

After cocktails and the first course of savory black and white cookies, the meal began and we asked the sommelier to pair wines for a few courses at a time. He was absolutely excellent at his job and we tried everything from reds to whites to sherries and beyond. 

I won't go into too much detail about the menu as it changes, but the dry aged duck was incredible. As was every single other dish! Standouts include the morel custard, the English peas, the chocolate pretzels, and the interactive "guess the milk" chocolate quiz where you have to guess which animal's milk is an ingredient for a specific piece of chocolate. Choices were between cow, sheep, goat, and buffalo. 

Many people would scoff or pass out at the thought of spending major money on a meal. But this is truly a once in a lifetime experience and perfect for special occasions, vacations, or just celebrating a raise or a special event. I don't know that I'd come here every single time I'm in NYC but I will absolutely be back. It's truly worth every penny and the memories from a 4 hour dinner will last forever.

Dining guests are also gifted with a parting gift of granola and a printed copy of the menu from that evening to use as a reference if they ever want to relive the experience on paper.

Really lovely service, really lovely food, and just thoughtful and thoroughly entertaining. I had a total blast!

Before I start, let me just say that the service was excellent. The waitstaff was incredibly pleasant and helpful, and truly deserved at least 4 stars. But the food just didn't. Given that this is the number 1 restaurant in the United States, I was expecting to be wowed, yet I kept finding myself wondering what I was missing. Was I at the wrong restaurant? Was it April Fool's Day? Have Michelin stars become a charity gift? I'm 99% sure that my boss and I informed the waiter who introduced the meal to us that we had no dietary restrictions, yet somehow he seemed to interpret that to mean that we were both vegetarian. Admittedly my boss was talking about having recently completed a juice cleanse at the bar, so maybe they just wanted to ease her back into real food? Either way, the food just wasn't that exciting. Unless you really like salt, in which case, definitely give this place a shot, you'll love it.

Novelty/Uniqueness - 4/5

Taste - 3/5
None of the dishes really wowed me in terms of taste. The feeling where I would want more and more. And wouldn't mind ordering this dish as a app, main or dessert.
They are getting 3 stars because the food didn't taste bad but was ok, another star for being unique (nothing I tried before).

Value - 3/5
*The more expensive ingredients were really small portions .. the only pricey ingredient they used was the beef for the steak and the lobster and the two fishes. 
I was full.. Stuffed actually. There were like 4 courses for dessert. Too much? None of it really tasted amazing but was just cool the presentation and novelty factor. 


Service - 2/5 
The service was fine in the beginning until near the end when I asked to see the kitchen. The server never returned to say no. I asked twice. At first, I thought she was busy so i reminded her the second time and she said ok I will try. But no follow up. We waited and waited but nope.  We waited for 15 minutes? But seriously for a restaurant this calibre you would expect service to be perfect.


Side note: Did you know this restaurant was voted one of the best restaurants in the world. It is rated number 5 for 2015. Hmmm.. I will give another restaurant listed in this ranking a shot... 
http://www.theworlds50best.com/list/1-50-winners

In summary, if you are a foodie like me and have the money to splurge then go ahead. It was a good experience but would i return? No.

Overrated!! We have eaten at several high rated Michelin starred restaurants.  Food was mediocre and they tried to cover this up with gimmicks like shredding a carrot at the table.... Also portions were much smaller than other high star restaurants! Very disappointed, save your money!!

fine dining at its best.  can't say enough about this place. if you can handle the hefty price you will not be disappointed. beautiful interior, excellent service, and great food.  they give you a giant bottle of some liquor (can't remember which) after you finish eating and it's pretty much all you can drink.  staff told us some pretty funny stories about people trying to finish the bottle

Highly disappointed. Had the tasting menu on Valentine's Day. After eating at several other Michelin star ranked restaurants over the year, decided I should say something. This place is overrated. Most memorable was the last dish they served - duck. It was too tough and I know duck can be chewy but this was bad. 

Spend your money elsewhere. Don't believe the hype.

After all these years, I finally stepped foot into Eleven Madison Park. Came here for lunch which is the same menu as dinner. For what you will be paying I expected to be wowed by every single dish. Good but not sure if it was worth every penny. All I can say is I'm glad I got the experience to try this place. My favorite was the caviar on their take of a benedict. Very interesting. I love that they also spoil you at the end with the chocolate pretzels, alcohol and take home granola.

5th best restaurant in the world, #1 in the USA????? Not even close!

1) I had a good experience, not great, not excellent, not memorable.
2) Better restaurants that I've eaten at and had better experiences include: French Laundry, Le Bernadin, Gramercy Tavern.
3) Basic Summary: Service was wishy-washy (such that you had some servers that were totally  in the moment and adding value to experience and then you had another server who was cold as ice...too many servers hitting the table, didn't know who my head server was....) Execution: arguably perfect. Duck was cooked and seasoned perfectly. Lobster wasn't a second over-cooked. Many other dishes follow suite....Concept: hit and miss dishes!.....some had a great concept and many others seemed to be too far reaching. There was a Foie Gras dish that was very interesting and complicating but all the pieces didn't come together.....less is more, sometimes!

Probably wouldn't come back, not because I had a bad experience, but rather I'v had better experiences at other places at same price-points and nothing WoW'ed me about the meal. 

Would recommend a focus on refinement...Execution in the kitchen was near flawless....just needs some focus in the dining room and the composition of the dishes.

Wow.  Great place.  This is not a meal, its an event.  Great food, Great drinks.  Classy stuff.  Had reservations for our anniversary.  Has many courses and drinks, some drinks even come with courses.  Left satisfied and full.  Wife told me I had to wear a jacket, but couple next to us were in ripped jeans and t shirts.  This is worth the cash.  

Staff was great through and through.  At the end of our awesome meal they even took us on tour of kitchen.

If you're going here to taste normal, replicable food don't bother. But if you want an experience and to try dining at a different level this place is for you. The price tag is incredibly high but the quality, service and uniqueness of everything they bring out makes it worth it. I won't bother going through course by course as the menu changes per season but overall it did not disappoint and would go back, despite the price and despite having been there twice now.

The service and the wine were extraordinary.  The meal was, unfortunately, just okay overall.  There were standout dishes that were excellent (their caviar eggs benedict) but there were also a few pretty bad misses (peas).  However, by-and-large, the majority were only interesting, not amazing.  And, maybe it was wrong of me, but I was expecting amazing.

Having been to many establishments of this level, I wouldn't call it the top of the class.  I would have preferred to spend my money at Per Se.

This restaurant continues to deserve 5 stars. Everything on the plate was purposeful and delicious. The service was over the top outstanding. We were treated like royalty. I am incredibly spoiled therefore I was not blown away by each dish. I enjoyed every bite but sometimes felt like the plate could've had two more bites.  Some of the specialty items were of simple origin and I felt maybe a little contrived. Maybe it's time to mix it up a little bit because some of the dishes I felt like you've been serving for years and it wasn't giving me the special uniqueness that I was perhaps expecting. It's hard to really be critical of a place that is so special. I'm not trying to be a pain in  neck I'm just trying to give an honest review from my perspective. I was really looking forward to coming to this restaurant and experience the Michelin three-star experience... I feel like it was overpriced for what we were served in this day and age of tasting menu plethora. Maybe they needed some sort of a fancy savory fish course besides the lobster to leave us a little bit more satisfied. The parting gifts were Nice. We enjoyed nibbling on granola for many days.

Dare I give anything less than 5 stars to the reputed king of New York's dining scene.. That is the question and I suppose that's the problem with EMP, it comes with the reputation with price tags to match, although thankfully I wasn't picking up the check. With 3 stars from Michelin, the tire company known just as much for its guide than rubber products, it better be wow. It was nice but maybe I was just expecting too much.

The sturgeon was the lowest part of the meal and it just wasn't flavorsome. I've had much better at no star restaurants. The high point was definitely the baked Alaska. Perfect. If it were for service alone I would give a zillion stars. They waitstaff are amazing and so natural. I love fine dining without the silly pretentiousness that one often experiences, especially in this city. So refreshing. Hopefully next time the food will be a little better and the waitstaff exactly the same.

Excellent service!
Every one of the 14th courses served within three hours was amazing. Food was just a little overrated but definitely worth five stars on yelp!!

It really is a 2-star for food, but I give a 3-star for the service.  It should be a 1-star for cost-effectiveness for food-cost ratio. I have to honest and say that I am so disappointed with the food here.  Am I eating at the same restaurant as everyone else?  The portions were extremely tiny.  For midgets and I am only 5'2".  A couple bites maximum for each dish.  The mirage to make the dishes seem grander than life still resulted in over-seasoned under-peppered food.  They were very insulted when I asked for fresh pepper, which I had to put on myself.  Where's the beef???  What is up with the carrot tartar?  I was expecting wagyu...but instead got carrots.  Yes, amazing carrots if we were on Iron Chef with the battles of the carrots...but we are not, and I wanted some meat.  Don't come here if you are a carnivore.  While the half stalk of asparagus was edible, not sure if all the hoopla with the pig bladder orchestra made me less hungry.  To end, you get dessert (chocolate dipped pretzel hung on a metal rack) and they give you all-you-can-drink pure ethanol (is it moonshine?) to make you forget the pain of forking out $700 for 2 people.  They send you home with a menu, and a jar of granola...sorry but you can keep the granola (I tried to leave it there but the staff saw that I left it there and force me to take it).  So sad, the hype is all hype.  Don't come here if you are hungry.  If you are vegetarian with an expense account, this is a sure winner.
Hands down one of my favorite places in the city. The wait staff is always professional and kind. The food is delicious and the cocktails even better!

What can I say about this restaurant that hasn't already been said? It's one of current nine Michelin 3-Star rated restaurants in the United States! If you get the opportunity, you should most definitely dine here. I'm sure everything is wonderful, but I had the Caviar and the Poached Lobster. Simply Divine!
What can I say that hasn't been said about this place? Excellent service and food. It exceeded my expectations on many levels. Pricey but definitely a great place for a special occasion.

The vegetarian tasting menu is simply the best we've enjoyed anywhere. Service stands out as you feel at home being looked after by the most considerate friends. Each course is a delightful sensory experience. The bread rolls are an example simple yet most delicious. The use of texture, the subtle use of ingredients and the artful presentation are perhaps to be expected. The decor is tasteful and stylish but balanced. Each member of the team engages with ease and the attention to detail in the service which is beautifully synchronized, is exemplary. The humanity of the experience is what touched us. We'd mentioned how much we'd enjoyed the bread rolls over dinner. As we left four rolls and the butter sourced from a local farm was waiting for us to take home to remind us of our evening. The jar of granola is thoughtful touch and gift.

Simply put, my meal at Eleven Madison Park was no less than the best meal I ever had.  Everything was perfect, from the almost sinfully buttery bread to the pastrami/deli course.  In my opinion Eleven Madison Park is the best three michelin starred restaurant in America.

This is one of the finest restaurants in New York and that honor is very well deserved. Starting with the exceptional service by Justin, Jonathan and Matthew everything else continued in that stunning fashion.
Every course resampled was simply extraordinary. The tasting menu was well paced and just the right amount of food leaving us satiated when we were finished but not feeling gluttonous. It was my spouse's birthday so we were treated to a special visit to the kitchen followed by chocolates and Brandy in the bar. Of course Eleven Madison Park is very expensive but based on what they are delivering it is a bargain. 
We will most certainly return and can't wait!

I ate at the bar because the main dining room was full.  I had seen the restaurant at the top of NYC lists and as a foodie I wanted to try it.  I had high expectations.
I was very disappointed.  The food was tasty.  But it is the epitome of the expression tweezer food.  It's almost a joke.  Maybe if these were the portions of a tasting menu I would understand it.  But a la carte is the only option at the bar.  It's not a meal.  I was very disappointed.  I wish I read a review like this before I went, which is the only reason I am writing this.  Buyer Beware.  $325 later and you are sure to leave hungry.
Everything is great here...food isn't the best i've had, but it's really good...and and the rest of the experience is top the line

they gave me some options on tasting menu: seared vs cold foie gras and veal vs duck. I went for seared foie gras and veal. compared to other 3 stars, this one is a pass for me, probably won't come back.

==loved==
hudson valley foie gras with sorrel, amaranth, and fava beans
lobster
asparagus

==liked==
radish with pike and nasturtium
eggs benedict ham, asparagus, and caviar
carrot tartare
spring veal

==meh==
black/white savory cookie

==disliked==
morel custard w/ trout roe and mustard flowers
english peas with buffalo yogurt and spring garlic
farmers cheese
whey dessert
strawberry desert

Yes, just yes. Food is amazing, atmosphere is amazing, and service is above and beyond. Took a friend here who loves food but is price sensitive. Beyond the amazing service, the sommelier went out of his way to pick something delicious in a comfortable price point. Won't comment on the rest of the food/service since I think that's covered by the other reviews.

High expectation was given before my meal as this is probably the best restaurant in the city, and probably in Americas area. Nothing let me down and more surprises were found during my eating journey! 

In terms of comparative advantage, I'd say presentation was definitely outstanding here at EMP. Starting from the black and white cookies, to the end strawberry ice cream. Even their crisp bread with duck fat was remarkable! 

The part which surprised me the most was absolutely the guessing chocolate part. Essentially you were given four different flavors of chocolate and were to tell which one was which. Unfortunately I got zero out of four right...however this was definitely the best interactions I have ever had.

Before leaving, EMP was kind enough to provide a bottle of cereal and the menu as the departing gift. How considerate! Best experience so far!

It takes a pre-planning very well in advance to get a dinner reservation if you are not flexible on a date or time for your special occasion (especially for 2 persons).  I tried making a reservation for my birthday.  Despite 28 days in advance, with only an hour late to the reservation phone line, table for two were completely booked.  Heartbroken and panicked because I had my mind set on celebrating my birthday at EMP this year.  I noticed on Opentable that there was a table available for 3 at the time I want.  So I went ahead and booked it.  I'd just have to go drag the other friend of mine to join me for birthday dinner.  :D

The day came, I was nervous and excited as if I was going on a first date or something!  I've been waiting to dine at EMP for years!  We were about 10 mins early for 5:30 dinner reservation.  So we got to wait at the bar and witnessed a dinner service staff meeting which made me excited even more!  You get a sense that all staff members take their service seriously and they are on a mission to make your dining experience as memorable as possible.

Right on time, we were seated at our table.  Got an introduction from our caretaker and we went straight right into the first course which was already presented in front of us before we got to the table.  What could be in this small white box?  I opened ... cookies???  For first course??  I was perplexed, but as soon as I had a taste of it ... oh my .. I could not wait for the rest of the courses to come!  How can this simple looking cookies be so delicious!!??!  I won't go into detail of every course because their menu changes depend on availability of local ingredients.  You eat whatever they are going to serve you.  Except we got an option for one of our courses; duck breast or veal.  Since I was a birthday girl, I got to pick for the table and I went with the duck.  

I enjoyed most of the food from my 15 course meal with an exception of 2-3 plates.  Most courses were exceptional, fun, creative, fresh, and presentation was beautiful.  Duck breast was my least favorite of all.  It was chewy and didn't taste great.  I remember my friend told me it made him wanted to throw up.  Yikes!  Some other courses were a bit heavy in sea salt.  Overall, food was very much worth it for a special occasion.

Service ... while most staff had friendly smile on their faces and very knowledgeable about food, I sensed this rigid and awkward feelings during my dining.  At times, staff came off as insincere and trying too hard to impress.  What caused that feeling started when a lady tried to set up a new set of silverware and my hand was coincidentally in her way.  She (intentionally or coincidentally) pushed my hand out of the way and didn't acknowledge or apologized for doing so.  I thought that was slightly rude, but I ignored that.

At the end of dinner service, we all got our printed menus and goodies bags (awesome).  To me, this experience was worth the money.

We decided to go to Eleven Madison Park for a special meal, celebrating a special occasion. The service is outstanding, befitting a Michelin star rated restaurant. I admit I was truly impressed by the attentive profuse staff. 
The dining experience here is massively exceptional. Each course is extremely precious. Each item on the menu is also quite diminutive, which is an arresting cramp when thinking about the price per item, especially on the à la cart menu.
The dining experience at Eleven Madison Park is truly an enjoyment and appreciation of the culinary arts.
There is a great formality, which is customary to Michelin star rated restaurants of this caliber.  Yet, a  slightly more personalized and appreciative touch on the side of the staff in relation to the customers would felicitously be deserved.

Boyfriend took me to Eleven Madison Park for my birthday and I must say that it was more for him than for me. We were both excited to go but he was like a little girl about to get her first mani/pedi done. Eyes gleaming with excitement. But alas! With all the hype and excitement, we were disappointed :(

No doubt about it with the price point, EMP is fancy shmancy dinner fit for special occasions or if you have the dough to throw. The whole dinner will last between 3-4 hours so plan accordingly. 

Service is on point as it should be. Nothing to talk about there.

Dinner is very interactive and lots of showmanship going on. First, we were given a small sealed envelope that we have to open up with a knife we were given. Inside there are two cards,one for me and one for the bf. We then need to pick between Apple, maple, cranberry and celery for the theme of each of our dinner. Hmmmm. We wondered how that would pan out. I picked celery and he picked Apple. More on that later. 

So for show:
- celery root that was cooked in pigs bladder. So they come out to show you the pigs bladder with the celery root in it. Cooking process is explained and the chef will make the motion of basting it with whatever juice they cook it in. 
- for entree, we were to choose between duck and another protein (I forgot). If you choose the duck, they'll come out with the whole dry aged duck for show and again explain the cooking process"before" they cut you your piece. 
- For dessert, they have the baked Alaska. Fire is made through lighting up rum and basting the dessert with the fired up rum. 
- Even their cheese plate are assembled table side with the cart brought to you. Each cheese with which locale it came from and type explained. 

All that hoopla is nice but it does take away from the taste of it. We came for the food, not the entertainment. And I'm afraid to say that it didn't quite reach our expectations.

11 Madison Park stood out as the restaurant whose staff hustles the hardest to provide an outstanding three-Michelin-star experience. If you want to see what truly world-class dining service looks like, you need go no further. 11 Madison Park gave me an amazing team of people- Jane, Aurora, Ellen, and Megan- who worked together professionally, passionately, and flawlessly to create an unforgettable experience.

The courses are all presented in unforgettable fashion- from oysters served on 
beds of ice and stone, smoked sturgeon presented in a cloud of vapor... If you want to impress and be impressed, this is where you go. All for less than half the cost of Per Se, Jean Georges, or a similar competitor.

If you'd like a dorky course-by-couse description, I invite you to go here:
http://www.threestarepicure.com/blog/2015/4/19/11-madison-park

Exquisite. In every way, Eleven Madison Park is amazing. Food, service, presentation - all outstanding. They set the bar very high and exceeded on all accounts. Dining here was a dream, I don't have enough good to say about our evening here!!

My girlfriend has been hinting that she wanted to try this place for her birthday, honestly I was reluctant because I assumed it would be stuffy...and I would rather eat 1,000 singles then pay 1k and be treated like crap.

I shocked by how lovely and friendly the atmosphere and staff were. It wasn't stuffy, the food was fantastic, and we even got a tour of the kitchen.

My GF and I love it and will happily go back.

Eleven Madison Park is an event. Four of us ate there on 5/14 and agreed that the staff is extraordinary: friendly, professional and helpful. We were overwhelmed by the extensive wine list and opted to give Dev, the sommelier a $1200 budget and he selected four very nice bottles; two red and two white. The dinner was a four hour marathon of 15 small  courses, most very unusual, tasty, and pleasing. Our criticism focuses on the contrivances that, while amusing and conversation starting, were unnecessary and distracting. Two lonely asparagus poached in a pig's bladder (two of our party were vegetarians and passed on the opportunity); carrot tartar ground at the table in a small instrument that was reminiscent of my grandmother's chopped liver maker; a tasty mousse topped with caviar served in a small caviar tin, were examples of the theatrical flourishes. The restaurant is a lovely place. It is quiet despite being a full house and it is worth the price, but it is not a place that leaves one with the desire to return. Once is enough. We were glad to have experienced it but, unlike Jean George or Per Se, we will not return. Bruce R.

Had tremendously mountain-top high expectation for this restaurant. Let me start with why the four star. 

1. Kinda expecting all the beautiful plates I've seen in the pics, but where were all those colorful flowers on the plate? Where?? My asparagus looked so lonely on the plate. 

2. Service might had an off day and I might be overly critical but hey, for a 3 star Michelin restaurant, who would blame me for nitpicking the details? So, first they mistakenly put someone else's carrot tartare grinder on my table, and then my carrot tartare was missing its salt condiment (Yes, look at the pic and one bowl was empty lol). Then when I was back from the restroom, somehow my napkin was gone and one server seeing me approaching my table, ran a bit but missed his chance to move the table out of my way (I didn't need that kind of small attention but I did feel sorry for him lol). Comparatively, Gordon ramsay restaurant in london with its world class service still trump on all service aspects over EMP. 

3. Some dishes had this overpowering taste that I was not too fond of. The morel custard was too acidic, the pretzel was too salty, and the lobster was slightly overcooked and the leaves on top was really really salty. 

But here are some highlights. The seared foie gras was the best I've ever eaten in my life! The duck skin was heavenly, the meat was moist and tasty. The asparagus and potato black truffle puree was out of this world (although again, it looked a bit lonely). The carrot tartare, their unique interpretation of beef tartare, was so unique that I would choose this over a real beef tartare, anytime! Really, how could you manage to make carrot that delicious? Loved their interpretation of egg benedict too, super special.

So overall, out of  the 15 menu, there were 6-7 that I might go crazy about, but the rest were great, but not phenomenal. Also, kudos to their no dress code policy, sometimes you just want to eat a great meal without the hassle of tying a tie and donning a suit.

All it matters is that I came here & never will I forget the palate adventure I had. The ambiance,service & presentation was beyond expectation. To top it off we got kitchen tour & they demonstrated nitrogren liquor drink & we left with jar of granola and cookies. This place is food heaven, I will earn my way back some day.

To date, this is my favorite fine dining restaurant ever so it truly is the best meal I've ever had. I dined here with my brothers, both have been before. Both thought the experience was equally as great as their first time. The magic happens with the service. I assumed that I would be receiving the most pretentious, snooty service. My experience at Bouley and Jean-Gorges left me with expectations of stuffiness and sterility. And besides, how much can service really alter your enjoyment of good food anyway?

I was so, so wrong. The service at EMP was a complete contradiction to any of my preconceptions of fine dining. It was some of the most effortless, genuine, and outstanding kind I've ever experienced. The people here love what they do. They were born to do it. For example, my super foodie brother looks super young for his age, but the maitre d' treated him with so much respect without needing to be convinced the kid knows his stuff. Or when you get up from the table someone magically appears to move it out of the way if you're sitting along a bench. 

Upon arrival, a waiter who had previously and coincidentally served my brothers on separate occasions dropped by and mentioned he recognized them, recounting specific details of conversation he had with each of them. Whether or not this was staged, we'll never know, but it made for a very WOW HOLY SHT moment. I'm convinced they've either hired some of the best actors or those with everlasting memory banks. 

Additionally, we received a tour of the kitchen in which the a chef made us a few dessert beverages. It was my brother's birthday so he received chocolates compliments of EMP. You will receive your standard homemade treats like the granola I've been using with my breakfast this past month. And finally, if you ask for a doggie bag, you'll get an extra bag of treats. Ours included a really f'n good pastrami sandwich for the next morning. To top at off, as we were leaving, a cab was already waiting for us. I'm not one to go on and on about service, but the food was just so outstanding and flawless that before you know it, you've already fallen for the EMP hype.

This is the gold standard for all restaurants to date in my book (maybe Noma one day fingers crossed). It was such a treat in every way possible because the waitstaff and the patrons are the down-to-earth type (in my mind) that I prefer to dine alongside. Your money goes a long way here, and I can't help but get upset when other restaurants that charge equally as much don't measure up.

Catching up on my reviews, but I remember the dining experience at Eleven Madison to be AMAZING!!! Dishes were very original and fun! All looked and tasted great. Beautiful presentation. My go to place to entertain important guests and friends!!

I just tried to make a reservation-- exactly 28 days in advance. At 9:00 am the reservation line was not open yet. Thirty seconds later I called and was put on hold for 20 minutes. Finally I was told only 5:30 and 9:45 were left.  They said the delay was because so many people call at 9:00 and they only have 29 tables. Is it because my name is not Rockefeller ? We are previous guests but never again. It is easier to get in to Per Se. Don't waste your time on hold.

I know people are looking at this 2-star review and thinking there is something wrong with me. Let me explain. My wife and I came here after eating at Mirazur in Menton, France (number 11 in the world) and wanted to have a similar experience at Eleven Madison Park (number 4 in the world). The 2-star rating is relative to what our expectations were going into the meal (very high). 

I will start with the negatives so you don't have to scroll to the end. My wife is pescatarian and we noted this when we sat down. We came on a Sunday night, probably not the best time to come, but reservations were hard to get. The service was extremely slow. We waited for 20 minutes before someone came to help us. The fact that my wife does not eat meat was overlooked and they served her a dish that had a layer of foie gras hiding underneath a quail egg. This is simply not acceptable at the 4th best restaurant in the world. Very poor attention to detail. Too many dishes were duplicates. I love quail egg and caviar but I don't want it in back to back plates. Some dishes were "filler dishes" and simply too ordinary to warrant even serving at a place of this caliber. By the end of the meal, we were both praying for it to end (not a good sign), but the onslaught of dishes seemed endless. 

Okay, that all being said, there were flashes of brilliance. The fish that was cooked in smoke was my favorite part, but we ate here 3 months ago and that's the only positive thing I remember besides the maple soda and the granola parting gift. I know there were probably 2-3 other dishes (out of 18) that were good, but I cannot recall them. 

I really want to think that they had an off-night, that it was a Sunday night, the main chefs were not in-house, and that the staff was tired and wanted to go home. Even if all that was true, I still would not risk going back to see if they get it right. 

My next stop for a top restaurant in the world will be Alinea in Chicago.
Beautiful restaurant.  Delicious food.   Staff very attentive and friendly. Be sure you set aside plenty of time to enjoy the food and atmosphere. Looking forward to enjoying my takeaway treat.

This was, hands down, the best restaurant experience I've ever had and probably will ever have. And I'm completely OK with that. Coincidentally this is my 100th Yelp review and I could not be more pleased to use my 100th entry to review Eleven Madison Park.

I was fortunate enough to score reservations for this fantastic restaurant through my American Express concierge. Highly recommend this service if you have access to it.

Matthew (our waiter), Dev (the Sommelier) and the entire staff at Eleven Madison Park are incredibly classy and professional while still being relaxed, chill, and hilarious.

So what makes Eleven Madison Park so fantastic? Maybe it was the 15 course tasting menu. Maybe it was the personalized wine experience (note: not the standard wine pairing; Dev created a personalized wine menu based on our tastes). Maybe it was the eggs benedict with caviar. Maybe it was the croissant that came with duck fat butter. Maybe it was the duck itself. Maybe it was the kitchen tour (note: ask for this at the beginning of the meal like we did - it's a MUST). Maybe it was the stroopwafels that came with one of the courses (I go a bit nuts over stroopwafels after discovering them in Amsterdam a few years ago). Or maybe it was the part where I witnessed Dev demonstrate port tonging, which is the coolest thing I have seen in months. 

Upon leaving we were given: the top of the wine bottle from the port tonging demonstration in a box with a ribbon as a souvenir, chocolates, two printed menus of what we ate and drank throughout the evening, and two mason jars of granola to be enjoyed for breakfast.

Total time spent at Eleven Madison Park: 4.5 hours. And I enjoyed every second of it.

Perfection. Absolute perfection.

Good friends had recommended Eleven Madison Park having dined there a few years back. When planning to visit NYC with dear friends we thought this would be a fitting final evening dinner. It was that, and more. The staff from the minute we arrived were friendly but very professional. We were fixed with cocktails & given an overview of the Degustation menu, during which time our food preferences were sought, and then our journey into wonderful flavours and whimsy began. 

The food was themed around New York ingredients and dining tradition, but often with a twist. We started with Black and White cookies with apple, but these were savoury, cheesy and moreish. Widow's Hole oysters were next with the hot and cold contrast the feature. The wonderful smoked Sturgeon was next with a truly theatrical presentation but flavours befitting it's introduction to the table. 

Great advice by our sommelier saw us choose an Alsatian Reisling which was perfect for the next several courses. A delicious turnip broth was next making one reconsider this humble root vegetable as the variations in its presentation again provided an interesting contrast. Hudson Valley Foie Gras was next and can either be served seared with sun choke, hazelnuts and pear, or marinated with red cabbage and apple. Either way it was rich, creamy and superb. 

Theatre returned over the next two courses with the sauce for Lobster Newberg prepared at the table accompanied by the story of its origin in NYC. The lobster is followed by celery root braised with black truffle which is presented to the table in the hog casing in which it has been slowly cooked before being returned to the kitchen for plating. Again a wonderfully flavoured dish. 

We had selected a Bandol from Provence to accompany the Mangalista Pork braise. A great pairing, the pork was rich and delicious. 

We were invited to the kitchen to witness 'behind the scenes' and meet Dimitri Magi, Executive Sous Chef. Whilst there we were served Eleven Madison Park's version of a pastrami on rye with celery soda. The kitchen is a study in calm professionalism with most staff working 13 hour days. A privilege to see them in action. 

Returning to the table we resumed dining with Harbison Cheese served in a carnival squash with Apple jam, pretzel and a bitter leaf salad. This was a truly novel way to serve a cheese course. Following cheese was a dessert that celebrates botrytis, with a Hermann J Wiemer, 2011 Riesling Noble Select, Josef Vineyard, Seneca Lake accompanying a sorbet with bitter almond and ginger crumble. 

The second dessert was a bourbon barrel aged maple syrup with milk and shaved ice that was simple and yet striking. The texture and flavours a wonderful surprise, and yet it was as light as a feather. A chocolate covered pretzel with sea salt and a sweet black and white cookie with Apple molasses accompanied by Apple brandy finished the evening in a wonderfully symmetrical way. 

General Manager, Paul Downie, was really attentive and informative all evening and ensured that this would not only be a meal, but a night, to remember. 

If you love good food presented by knowledgable people in a splendid room you must add this to your Wishlist.

Beautiful location with an ever-changing, delightful menu that takes one on a whirlwind tour of the agricultural bounty of New York. The food courses are delicate, fun, creations that reminds one of the playful and artistic side of fine dining. 

The private event room that overlooks the main dining hall also offers lovely views of the restaurant from above.

We liked EMP better than Le Bernadin, but less than Daniel. The atmosphere is not quite your traditional fine dining - a lot more tables squished on the floor and very loud - although I guess we did come on a Saturday night and sat near the bar. Anyway, food was good, not great but there were some fun dishes where they let you mix your own ingredients. Service was very professional - Stephen was our server for the night. We enjoyed the dinner but nothing memorable enough to bring us back again.

general flavor: sea salt and tart theme from start to finish. little too salty for me and my family. few of the wines were terrible and had to be sent back, create serious pucker face when tasted. food and wine not as tasty as other Michelin 3 stars in nyc. reputation, price, and our expectations were overblown. should've been $125pps not $225. walked out unsatisfied.

The best word to describe this meal is epic. I've never enjoyed so many interesting, flavorful, complementary dishes and ingredients before as I did in our 3.5 hour, 14 course lunch at 11 Madison Park. 

Highlights:
- Eggs Benedict with asparagus and caviar
- Finger Lakes duck dry-aged, with spring onion, rhubarb and citrus duck jus
- Strawberry, poached, with vanilla and elderflower
- All of the wine pairings, with which we trusted the  host with the decisions

Although my experience at 3-star Michelin restaurants is admittedly limited, we noticed that the environment lacked the stuffiness that I expected at such places, that our host, chef and servers were casual and attentive, and that the entire experience felt effortless. In addition, the chef regularly came to our table to either perform some cooking instruction (basting the asparagus in an herb broth) or to finalize the dish (grinding a carrot at our table in the style of beef tartar), which lent a playful feeling to the day.

As lunch was coming to a close, a bottle of custom-made apple brandy (with an invitation to drink for as long as we'd like) accompanied mason jars of cacao-nib granola to make sure we have a superb subsequent meal as well. This unusual gesture epitomized the customer-centric, effortless feel of the meal. The menu changes every three months; we certainly intend to return.

PS: If you plan to go, book ahead. Reservations open 28 days prior to the date one plans to book for, and while I called 27 days prior to the day we were planning to be in the city, the only availability was for the last lunch reservation of the day; no dinner spots remained.

Everything was way too salty. 
Even the bread was salty. 
Very disappointed and cant believe how this restaurant ranked top 50.

Oh my god! This was the best meal I have ever had in my life! There is no clearer way to describe the experience of Eleven Madison Park. Their duck was so amazing that I never want to eat duck anywhere else again, just so I can always remember it this way. Impeccable service, food, and paired wines made this an outstanding culinary experience.

What an incredible expierance from start to finish!  I've recently been lucky enough to get a reservation at chefs table and also have eaten at per se and have to say that eleven madison park by far has been my favorite place yet.(all three being bucket list restaurants) the whimsical laid back approach to the food and the on point yet effortless service really put this night over the top for me.  The tasting menu in its own right is genius and flows very nicely and ties together nicely.  Memorable dishes include the raw carrot tartar done table side, sea urchin custard with apple scallop and chervil, and we chose the duck which I believe is the way to go.
