It was presented to the table beautifully and didn't disappoint! And to finish off the night a little take home gift of their famous home made granola which is delicious. Seriously it's so good ask for another!

I have nothing but high praise for this place.  This is my 4th time here.  I tried my best to frequent this place when I visit NYC.  Love the food and their impeccable service, and I do mean IMPECCABLE.  Eating here is like a great journey for food lovers everywhere.  always try to squeeze in the kitchen tour at the end of your spectacular meal.

Had my fair share of tasting menus in NYC and Eleven Madison Park for Valentine's Day was by far the worst.The only course worth touching out of all dishes was the tiny pastrami dish served on a cutting board. The last dish we were served on the tasting menu was the roasted duck. It was chewy and very rough and the most disgusting of the night. Hoped this dinner would be epic, only left extremely disappointed.

Eleven Madison Park (EMP) met and exceeded expectations.  We did the $225/person tasting menu which consisted of 13 amazing bites, 14 if you count the parting gift bag (mason jar of housemade granola).  From start to finish did take a bit over 3hrs, so plan accordingly.  Don't forget to ask about the kitchen tour,  gorgeous kitchen!

I had a fantastic meal at this restaurant.  The service and food definitely lived up to its 3 Michelin stars rating.  The staff paid attention to details that made us feel special.  The flavor of the dishes were well balanced and the presentation was enjoyable.  Thank you for a wonderful experience.

The service, oh, what a great, personal, awesome service!

When in comes to 3 Michelin star restaurants, you know what you're getting into so the food and the price shouldn't be a surprise. 

The food was absolutely awesome and the price reflected it.

But the service was above and beyond my expectations. I might even dare to say that this place has the best service I've ever experienced in a high end restaurant.

Cheers.
Service was perfection, food was divine, and everything was perfectly paired with beverages and rich flavors.

Went in February 2015.  The food was good, I guess my expectations were too high.  Service was good, some of the dishes I found a bit gimmicky.  Best dish was the celery root dish.  Worst was the cheese course in the pumpkin.  Not disappointed that I went, I just don't think that I will be returning.

Years ago I frequented this restaurant so I had high expectations for my birthday dinner on 4/4/15. I was disappointed in the food in several small ways. They added up to my giving it a low rating in contrast to the high cost. It's four star at $100 but it's three star at $500. 

It's become popular to strew chunks of salt on dishes where it conflicts with and distracts from the subtleties of flavors. Many dishes disappointed me in that regard. They offered flakey buttery whole wheat rolls, superb but big chunks of salt were affixed to the top, an overpowering taste interfering with the subtle delicious flavors of the rolls. They served a chocolate covered pretzel which had more like subtle candy than pretzel inside and again affixed chunks of salt outside. There was a delicious celery root preparation with a truffle sauce that was so salty the really wonderful flavors were overcome by the salt. The duck was superb with wonderful fatty crispy skin but affixed to the skin was all sorts of stuff that i found distracting and unnecessary. 

The smoked sturgeon, served in a covered glass with smoke inside was a problem. The look impressed like a magic trick when they whisk off the glass cover and the smoke fills the area, but when several of these were opened the restaurant smelled like there had been a fire in the kitchen, very unpleasant and distracting -- interfering with the enjoyment of all my food! Also the taste of the fish was overly smoked for me. I didn't like it.

In contrast there were great tasting dishes and the service was top notch as was the ambiance. One dessert called Botrytis included a wine I could drink all day. Superb! there was a maple dessert with frozen snow that was almost perfection. The only negative to it was that, yes, they poured salt on it! Ugh! This would have ranked among the best desserts I've ever had if not for that added salt. It had wonderful textures and tastes and was beautiful to look at, too, but they spoiled it with the salt.

It's not that I have an aversion to salt. I enjoy salted pretzels and potato chips, of course, and choose to eat them too often. But when I'm eating fine food with subtle and complex flavors, I don't want them spoiled with a heavy application of added salt. The salt on top hits your palate first, overpowering the taste buds, so the subtle complex flavors can't be fully experienced.

I'm a big fan of foie gras and I tried both their offerings. They were very good but by far not on my "best" list. No. One would have been better solid mouss-ey foie gras without the red cabbage. The other, also a little too complex. I won't forget the foie gras I had at Lutece every Friday for years. While I liked these they were just too complicated. 

On the other hand the caviar with the cream cheese, absolutely perfection! That was memorable! The Harbison hot liquid cheese dessert was also unreservedly excellent, and the honey and apple butter the best.

The wines are great and the sommelier attentive to diners' tastes. I truly wish the food was as good as I remembered. The take home treats were very good, too, but yes, again! They gift us their home made Mounds bar, but what do they sprinkle on top of it? You guessed it: salt!   

Honestly, were you ever tempted to sprinkle hot salt on your Almond Joy or Mounds chocolate bar so it would stick on top of the bar? I didn't think so. It ruins it.

But the take home granola, just wonderful, containing the best fruits and nuts and it isn't overly sweetened. 

I remember some amazing drinks in years past, and seeing them prepared in the kitchen too. Wow, I longed for that. They were delicious. And they were magical, too, in the way for which they were trying with the smoked sturgeon.

As for the menu, they are trying too hard to do something very different, but fine food just has to be a little different to rise above. I am sorry to have to cross this one off my special favorites list but I won't be back. They want to provide an extended magical experience but without the perfect food, it's bad theater for me.

Eleven Madison Park (EMP) is known among the foodie community as a Michelin 3 star restaurant.  It's one of 6 restaurants in the city that can won this accolade. 

With all the hoopla about EMP across the press, tv segments and even through films like Somm which highlight EMP's Dustin Wilson's path to achieving one of the Wine Industry's greatest honors, my dinner companions and I had extremely high hopes for both food and wine.

When expectations are high, it's often the case where humans are disappointed.  I didn't think it was possible, but 11 Madison took us to a complete different level and now ranks as all four of our's best dinner we've had to date. 

A night at EMP is both an experience and a culinary festival.  Upon our entrance, we were guided to the lounge and offered a choice of some excellent sparkling wines and champagnes.  A detailed knowledge of each wine was offered and then our palette's delighted by a recommendation uniquely made to each of us based on some of our likes.   

We were guided to our table after enjoying the wine and ran into a notable celebrity and some other faces that seemed familiar.  We were seated in a large, Art Deco hall with windows and ceilings that exceed 30 feet.  

We all chose the tasting menu and three of us went with a wine pairing.  Our meal began and throughout the three hours, we had great conversations with the team serving us.  The manager even came over to ask if our fourth guest had passed on wine due to illness or not feeling well.  Francisco explained that while wine is mother's milk, he's not drinking tonight.  

Then the meal began. As the menu changes quite often, I'll highlight only a few things that were stood out:

- Widow's Oysters - hot and cold, the hot coated in black chestnuts that were roasted.  A perfect winter treat.
- Hudson Vally Foie Gras.  By far the best I've had paired with a German Red that blew me away.  (Weingut Hexamer, Spatburgunder, Wissherbst, Nahe, Germany 2013). 
-Wine opened with Port Tongs must see video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aDKmE-Ky860)
-Lobster Newberg - a classic dish from the late 1800s, all but lost today.
-Dry aged duck - beautiful crusted with lavender and other wonderful flavors
-Celery root prepared in sous vide style

At some point the manager came by with a gift back for Francisco that had a bottle of wine a new plastic baby bottle to play on his mother's milk. He wanted Francisco to enjoy later what he could not that night. I mean, WOW this is what happens in the movies and even then, rarely so.

As the meal approached it's end, we were taken into a tour of the kitchen which is beyond big - it is one of the largest kitchens I've seen in NYC.  During the tour, we were offered a classic NY Egg Cream which was whipped up in front of us while the staff shared some stories. 

All in all, a meal we'll never forget!  Thank you Eleven Madison Park for making an evening with friends that we'll never forget.

Just straight up amazing! We truly had the 5 star Yelp and 3 star Michelin experience. From the moment we walked in the staff knew my name and that we were celebrating 4 year anniversary, pre wedding planning, and 30th birthday. From coat check to our half dozen servers, everyone was incredibly personable, knowledgable, and attentive. We were fortunate to have the director of the beer program to look after our table and make recommendations on beverages all night. Thanks again!

The food is remarkable. Each dish had its own history, presentation, and unique set of ingredients. My favorite was everything, but the roasted duck breast really stood out to me. It was cooked perfectly medium rare and the skin had great texture. The maple with shaved ice was also remarkable. Everything was well balanced.

Surprisingly I was full after the meal here and I have a big appetite. You'd think that one with a big appetite wouldn't be satisfied with the small portions, but 10 courses later you'll feel swell.

Truly an amazing restaurant - can't speak highly enough about the quality of food or service. Top notch!
Most overrated meal of my life. Hostess was beyond pompous. It was as if there were doing me a favor by allowing us to dine at their restaurant.

Damn this place is awesome! Tomato confit and lobster made a great combo for me. Service was best I can remember in some time. My boyfriend ordered the foie gras and gave it a B+ (but he's a pretty picky guy lol)

Review from my '13 experience:

Lots of hype, but it couldn't live up to it. The first third of the menu was interesting, tasty and visually appealing... the rest is another story. 

The first third of the menu included: sea urchin snow, surf clam, littleneck clam and the somewhat deconstructed 'clam chowder', the tomato confit with lobster and the foie gras (2 options here). All these dishes looked really well, the combination of flavors was interesting and the overall taste was what one could expect from a top 50 restaurant. These dishes appeal to all the senses.

The rest of the menu relied heavily on 'showmanship/presentation' --you'll even get to see a magic trick-- which compensated for the uninteresting flavors. Most of the dishes are deconstructed (carrot, malt, cheesecake and picnic basket come to mind) which is interesting and an experience I'd recommend, but it's all pointless if the end result (the dish put back together) is rather underwhelming or flavorless --The malt, though was to my liking.

The most unappealing dish was the sunflower, the taste is very odd and it's kind of a 'deviation' from the rest of the menu in terms of taste... it was served between fish and duck and it didn't really serve any purpose; it didn't clean my palate for the next dish, it didn't enhance anything, definitely the odd dish.

Onto desserts. The two dessert courses were inventive and plated beautifully. The first dessert was a sassafras sorbet with banana cake, caramel and vanilla. The taste was odd-- too herbaceous, medicinal instead of refreshing (e.g. basil, mint). It was not what I expect from a dessert (I have a sweet tooth). I experienced the same thing with the red pepper sorbet and deconstructed cheesecake. The red pepper was tangy and it overpowered all other components in the dish.

Service was intermittent, at times very attentive and other times missing in action. Heck my napkin was missing for one course, it was taken away when I went to the restroom and requested one as soon as the course started. I did check my seat and the floor just in case, but nothing... it was really gone. First time that this has happened to me anywhere and it happened on a dish that you eat with your hands (picnic basket pretzels).

I asked for a tour of the kitchen at the end of the meal. Our head waitress said she was going to ask, we waited for an answer for close to 15min. Needless to say we left, a simple 'no' would have sufficed. I wouldn't have gotten upset, but waiting without any acknowledgement... that was upsetting.

TIP: Make reservations as SOON AS YOU CAN!:)

It was the most amazing fine dining experience I have ever had. It was just good food after good food, after great food. I was so stuffed halfway through, but I couldn't stop because everything was just so exquisite. 

Walking in, the interior design just made the atmosphere of the restaurant. It was classy, and open. When I received the menu, they explained to me that their system, which was to choose the main ingredient I wanted for each main course, and that the chef would make any type of dish using that ingredient. I suppose this lets chef use his imagination and to keep every dish unique. 

Every course that came out was fantastic. In between every single course, you would get a mini little dessert. I suppose my favorite one would be what their take was on a New York Style Raspberry Cheesecake! It was delicious, and it was so cute. I wanted to snap a picture.
However, next time i'll be sure to throw my pride out the window and just snap a picture of everything.

I also tried the tea samples, my favorite would be the tomato tea with thyme. I wanted to have it with me throughout my entire meal, but once I put it aside, they took it away from me, and I didn't want to chase after them for it. :'(

After the FEAST, they gave us complimentary mini black and white cookies. They were so cute, and so good. 

Overall, it's a really nice place to go if you want to experience fine dining in a lovely little area in the middle of the city.

Holy crap is all i can say because this place is a 15 out of 10.

Service - IMPECCABLE.  Gotta love when you eat at a high-end restaurant and your searching for a server for ANYTHING.  Never the case here.  They appear like ninjas out of the shadows only when needed.  Proper balance of letting you enjoy yourself, but not overbearing.  Additionally, the humor of our table captain was spot on!

Food - Customized menu with course after course of pure works of art.  I was eagerly waiting for each course just to see what would be next.  That being said, I will warn that there is ALOT of food and you need to pace yourself both in food and booze consumption or you may not make it.

Atmosphere - Decor is bit lacking, but the staff make up for it.. Nothing pisses me off more than having to dodge staff members as i head to the restroom with perhaps bit too much wine in me... NOT HERE.... its like you walk and the staff just glide gracefully and respectful out of your way.  They immediately move to the side... every time i went to use the restroom, i felt like i was in the matrix as people just parted

Price - Yes its not cheap... but if you break down what your getting... about 225 pp for the most incredibly food/art you will ever experience, then i would say its a bargain.  You will not leave hungry... thats for sure.

Quite frankly the best overall dining experience that I have ever had.  I have dined all over the world and this is Number 1.  The food is special but the environment and hospitality is what makes this place truly unique.

We enjoyed our visit there on Feb 21, 2015.  We had a flight out later that day, and they were very aware of that, and made sure that we were done in plenty of time to make our flight.  The wait staff was very attentive, without being overbearing.  The food was amazing.  We have dined in many fine dining restaurants in NYC, Chicago, San Fransciso and Napa Valley, and we had some of the finest food we have ever had.  We did not do the wine pairings - which we would normally do, but since we were going from the restaurant to the airport, we didn't partake (maybe, in retrospect, we should have *wink*).  Not every course was a home run, but we had many memorable courses.  I tried several ingredients that I had not experienced before, and they were great.  They accommodated my husband's dislike of Foie - but I was able to experience their take on that in more than one course.  The ambiance was great -what a beautiful building!! The staff was very attentive and certainly were not overbearing - they were kind and pleasant, as well as informative.  The celery root in the pig's bladder tasted amazing and what a presentation!!  I would go again in a heartbeat!!

Went there for dinner. Probably the best Michelin restaurant in New York so far. Good service. Great food. Really like the turnips soup, lobster and duck. Dessert is also very good. Expensive but tasty.
Look I didn't eat here but LET ME JUST SAY. Wow. Everything. The cocktails are delicious and everyone is very nice and welcoming.

Here is what separates a truly great restaurant from a really good one: service. At 11MP, they understand that principle and they hew to it with an easy (but clearly well studied) elegance, grace and charm. This makes a huge world of difference and is what makes 11MP very memorable whereas restaurants that should by rights be able to call themselves its peers to me only warrant four or maybe even three stars. 

Also, ambiance can help make or break a place as well. 11MP's grand high ceilings, huge windows and tastefully modern decor all set in a charmingly Art Deco building also helps catapult it into the top tier. 

Also, I LOVE that it's one of the rare restaurants in this class wherein reservations aren't murderously difficult to come by. Thus, I came by fairly often. Mostly for lunch, but a couple of times for dinner as well. 

However, MAYBE this is actually a 3.95 rating as the food, while great, well executed, and well presented, isn't -quite- exactly at the level of a place like Per Se (which is my standard for how a restaurant of this caliber should be). It's almost there! It rises far above -most- other comparable places in NYC. There was always just one tiny something missing. But it was TINY little quibble and unless you're as particular as I am it's doubtful to make an impression at all.

The level of professionalism from the staff is amazing. Everything is beautifully coordinated and I felt like I was whisked into a place where my every whim is catered to. The food is good, as it should be at these prices but the presentation is the best part. For me the most memorable part of meal was the cheese selection. So good. The thing is though, the cheeses should not be the part of the meal that I remember the most. Not at this level at least. I will be back but I'm hoping for more wow from the food, especially the fish dishes.

It certainly was a culinary journey.  Every dish came with a story.  Service was pretty amazing.  However I will have to admit, out of the 16 course meal, I was only really in awe of 2 - the cold/hot oysters and the snow dessert.  They change their menu every quarter and I think I may have just gone for the wrong menu.  I also took one star off because we were seated next to Michael Fassbender who was on a date with some twenty-something actress making out like crazy. It was extremely awkward because of the smooching noises and I wish the restaurant would have told them to stop.

from reading the cookbook and reading the menu online, i was stoked

made last minute reservations two days prior and was able to snag a 9 pm reso

located a block from the metro

service was exceptional

i had made some notes on my allergies and when i was greeted at the door they were already asking me about them

food was visually stunning

price was a bit steep but it's to be expected for all the labor that goes into everything

will come back next time i'm in ny!

Dined here last night with my brother. It was our first experience at this restaurant. My experiences at other Michelin star restaurants never disappointed me and neither did Eleven Madison Park. 

The service and presentation of the dishes were impeccable. I ordered a Manhattan and a whole Manhattan cart was pushed over to my table to prepare my drink. We chose the off the beaten path wine pairing which was $70 less expensive than the other option. My favorite dishes were the foie gras and the lobster. The celery root cooked in a pig bladder was definitely an interesting presentation but taste-wise so so only. Loved how they prepare the lobster jous with the lobster head right at table-side. 

By the seventh course, (the salad and pumpkin one), I discovered a hair on my plate.  When I made the waitress aware of this, more than 3 people came over to apologize, including the manager, Kevin. The sommelier came over and topped our wine. I was quite impressed at the steps they took to rectify the problem and to maintain customer satisfaction. When the check came, the manager came over and told me they comped my portion of the tasting menu because of my imperfect experience. That blew me away as I did not expect that gesture at all. We ended up paying for 2 wine pairings, cocktails and only one tasting menu dinner. Now that is customer service! 

I would definitely come back to Eleven Madison Park. My favorite in terms of food is still Le Bernadin but service and presentation now goes to Eleven Madison Park! 

Looking forward to my next dining experience here.

My two visits to Eleven Madison Park were within just shy of two years; the first still stands as one of the best dining experiences I've yet to have but my second... The menu was, no doubt, considerably different and perhaps my palate had become more critical over time as well. But it's with a heavy heart that I have to revise my prior rating for EMP downwards.

What had changed? The restaurant still holds its three Michelin stars, and in the time that had passed, had moved upwards on San Pellegrino's list of "The World's 50 Best Restaurants" to fourth place, surpassing evening Chicago's esteemed Alinea. The high-ceilinged Art Deco building was just as majestic as I had remembered, although arriving in the evening gave it a subtler, less harsh appearance. The very server who had overseen my first meal back in March of 2013 was there to take care of us again this evening; he was able to even point to the very table I had sat in on my prior visit. No, it comes down to, at the very end, the food.

The beginning was the same, featuring the savory version of the Black and White Cookie with an apple filling, as well as instructions to choose one of four ingredients on a pop-out paper sheet (which later turned out to be a house-made flavored soda). It was followed by a familiar bread course, featuring the croissant-like rolls served with a lightly salted pat of butter, as well as a small cup of venison broth. The only other courses that were similar to the tasting menu I'd had years back were the final two: a chocolate covered pretzel with a sprinkling of sea salt, as well as the final ending bite, a sweet Black and White Cookie with an apple molasses filling.

There were courses that shone, of course. I fell for the Hudson Valley Foie Gras; it was seared in this iteration, and served with a blood sausage base, a dotting of cranberries, and entwined with a leaf of kale. The richness of the liver blended beautifully with the metallic tang of the blood sausage, and the textural contrast in each small bite was sublime. The quartet of Long Island Seafood was also memorable, featuring a gorgeous bite of Oyster with Yogurt and Lemon, a Scallop dotted with Pistachio and Apple, marinated Blue Crab with Pickled Radish, and a Vichyssoise with Caviar, Smoked Blue Fish, and Quail Egg. Our "main course", which took a beautiful cut of medium-rare venison, was thoughtfully composed with the accompanying braised beets and onions. The course that we found the most sublime, however, was perhaps also the simplest, one that paired a sphere of Celery Root braised with Black Truffle with a creamy celery root puree.

There were dishes that weren't quite as successful. The play on the quintessential Pastrami on Rye couldn't compare to the original "Bagel and Lox" I'd had almost two years back; while creative, the various sauces and presentations weren't as refined and intertwined as their predecessor. The sauce paired with the Atlantic Striped Bass was too overwhelming for my taste, as the clams, squid, and various other shellfish that had been cooked down for it overpowered the main protein. The Charcuterie course, with plated several miscellaneous bites (cured meats, liver on toast, jams, and the like) across a wooden board seemed haphazard, and quickly strewn together. And while I appreciated their take on the Baked Alaska, I missed the elegance and simplicity in the desserts I'd received nearly two years ago.

Eleven Madison Park is still good, make no mistake. The service is still phenomenal, welcoming and thoughtful without being invasive, with each course and transition perfectly timed. The 9-foot windows and pristine terrazo floors are still magnificent, and one of the most beautiful restaurants I've yet to step foot into. In the two visits that I've made, however, the most recent one pales in comparison to the first in terms of quality and innovation of their 16 course menu. Perhaps I've also become jaded; the last two years in New York City have been a rapid primer on fine dining for me, and perhaps even my most recent visit to Alinea has thrown off my perspective [1]. Nonetheless, honesty is always the best policy (in my book, anyway), so I'll stand by four stars for now.

--
[1] For anyone curious: Alinea is worth the trip to Chicago. Go.

We had my father's 60th birthday party here and the experience was incredible. We had a private room and did the 9 course tasting menu I believe. It was a very special evening complete with amazing service and outstanding food. The savory black and white cookies were amazing! Such an awesome way to start the meal. There is really nothing else left to say except that I hope I make it here again in my lifetime. There's really no surprise it's consistently rated one of the best restaurants in the world.

This restaurant is so dated. It's so brightly lit and you feel like you're having dinner in a hotel lobby. There's nothing fancy about this place and the decor is dreadful (sorry to say). 

Staff is so formal, and the menu needs updating. What was new and inventive 30 years ago just doesn't work nowadays. 

Dinner for 4 was over 3 hours long. Will not be going back to this place.

(12 course) multi-course tasting menu
(I think these were all the dishes)

caviar and smoked sturgeon
5/5 - the sturgeon caviar was amazing.

Sea Urchin Custard with baby squid, manilla clam and apple
4/5 - interesting mix of sweetness and fishiness.

Cranberry Gelee with smoked curds and agretti
2/5 - totally lost on the taste.

Cucumber Snow with lapsang souchong and grape
5/5

Roasted Eel with fois gras and swiss chard
4/5 - chard was a bit bitter.  fois gras was awesome... like eating butter.

Langoustine with fennel, sour cherries and clam
5/5

Potato with potato skin crisp and onion dust
5/5 - great potato dish

Poached Lobster with escarole and almond
5/5 

Glazed Sweetbreads with hazelnut, fennel and pear
5/5

Marinated Plum with jasmine and cashew
5/5

Chocolate Covered Pretzel covered with sea salt
5/5

At the end of the meal, the waiter gave a granola goody bag for the road.

Also, had a chance to meet Dustin Wilson from "Somm".  1 of 250 master sommeliers in the world.  Pretty awesome guy.  Helped with the wine selection.  Funny and entertaining.

Gave a rating of 4/5 only because not all of the food matched my taste buds... i.e. to adventurous for my palate.

I can honestly say that Eleven Madison Park provided me with the most amazing restaurant experience of my life. It will bankrupt you, but it's worth it. 

Everything we experienced was absolute perfection...the food, the service, the wine. They customize their tasting menu specific to any preference you share so don't be shy about your likes and dislikes. There might be more servers there than patrons...they literally escort you all the way to the restroom to show you where it is. The experience takes hours...we arrived at 7pm and were there past 11pm. They prepare a fair amount of the courses at your table, explain everything in detail, and you will enjoy every last bit of your meal...if you can fit it all in without bursting the seams of your clothing. And then they send you home with a lovely print out of what you ate and a jar of granola for breakfast the next morning. 

For a party of four, our bill came in at $1800 without tip)...wowzer. No, I did not pay for my dinner but after that experience, i gladly would've dished out my share. In fact, the next time I need a destination for a special occasion, I'll be calling Eleven Madison Park first.

I was so excited to finally try this place. It had nearly perfect reviews and had been sitting on the top of my list for so long. But, I was disappointed afterwards.

Food was not spectacular. They are nicely presented and I think the ingredients are pretty fresh. However, flavor is too one dimensional for me. I was hoping for the Woah moment, but throughout the whole course, the only thing that I really enjoyed was the lobster appetizer. The claw meat was cooked perfectly, very tender, and I know it takes precise timing. The rest of the meal, was just okay. Celery root and duck was good at the first bite, but after several bites, I got bored of the flavor already. It is lack of the intriguing factor that makes you want to discover more. I was hoping the chef would be more creative, combining ingredients that don't usually go together and create the harmony out of it. 

The service was below my expectation. I was holding jean-george service as the standard for michelin restaurants. But here, my main waitress was often no where to be found. I noticed she was also working on many other tables, which made it hard for her to give attention to everyone. The time between courses are sometimes long and nobody came to set expectations for what is going to be next.

Cherish the memories! Delivering world number 4 standard food & service is no easy task but the staff at Eleven Madison do this with a certain style that lingers in your memory for days on end. I certainly recommend this fine dining restaurant to every Australian foodie who is looking for innovation, artistry and something unique in presentation. The service is polished and entertaining with a story behind every dish delivered by staff who make you feel that you are a very special guest. I was delighted to be presented with a gift and a copy of the menu when leaving this magnificent restaurant by Chef Daniel Humm. Yes, I love NY and I will return to Eleven Madison Park. It is beautiful.

I went there couple times. Great environment/food! Good for groups/friends gathering. I love their foie gras and lobsters. That is the two dishes I won't miss each time I visit. Hey, did I mention their duck dish? Very juicy! Here comes the restaurant week; I m so coming back!

Reactivated my Yelp account just to praise these guys...

Food was sublime (maybe not THE best but among the best), and everything was served with a touch of fun and whimsical flair, but the biggest highlight of the evening was the service. Truly out of this world. Thank you to the EMP staff for going far above and beyond to make this a special evening for all of us.

In particular - we mentioned that we liked the wine bottle, and they brought it out all lit up like a christmas tree! My jaw dropped when they brought it over. It was also my dad's birthday, and they brought him out an autographed menu. It's the little things (and the light up wine bottles...) that matter.

Thank you, EMP, for a magical evening! We can't wait to return.

Enjoyed an amazing multi-course meal here with wine pairings.  The food was excellent and the waiters were very friendly and informative.  Unfortunately, the wine steward had the personality of a piece of cardboard and seemed annoyed when we asked him questions about the wine.  It was as if he didn't really want to be there.  Adding the pairings substantially increased the cost of this meal - so that was very disappointing.  

The room is lovely and relaxing and I also liked that they used predominantly local ingredients.  Would have been 5-stars if not for the steward.

The overall dinning experience was great. However, the desserts are not satisfying at all. Starting with the black and white cookies, ending with ice cream and Max Brenner's chocolate pretzel was not at all something that a three-star Michele restaurant should offer.

The foie gras! I'm normally not too big a fan of foie gras, but I just loved it here.

There were a few items that I wasn't a fan of but I'm not in the mood to give this place 4 stars. For example, I didn't like the black white cookie they serve both in the beginning and the end, or the oysters, or the bread, but everything else was pretty amazing.

However, their dessert selection is not very extravagant compared to many other restaurants. There was only like 3 items, which I guess is a good amount as the dessert amount doesn't actually have to be as grand as most places make it.

All in all, great experience! The restaurant is actually pretty big with high ceilings and lots of seats, so it shouldn't be too hard to get a reservation..

The restaurant was great, they did a really good job at explaining stuff, the dishes are craftily made and overall it was an interesting experience (first time I've ever done this level of haute cuisine)

Overall, I must say that I just don't think the food is worth $300; yes, it was impressive, but I also think of all the things I could have done with that money.

I really enjoyed the experience but I don't think I'll engage in this kind of dining soon

Best meal i've had in New York. Most things have already been said, so I will try to summarize. If you love inventive, intelligent food but you really don't like the environments you usually have to suffer through to eat that food, Eleven Madison Park is the answer. Casual seeming, yet 100 percent perfect food and service. You don't feel like you have to stop acting like a normal human being in order to eat and experience something transcendently good.
Just amazing.... Start to finish..... Sigh.....highly recommended, go with people you like, it's a long meal. 3-4 hours average

I'll add my 2 cents. I'm definitely no fine dining guru or expert but I can appreciate creativity, delicousness, and great service. Obviously this place is world class in pretty much all respects. I thought the service was great- not stuffy but clearly very attentive and nice. The creativity and fun of the meal was definitely there. Not quite as delightful and surprising as someplace like Alinea but still fun in its own right. The food- I would say that for me, there were some hits and then some dishes I just didn't enjoy that much (ie the cheese course and the desserts). Maybe they just weren't really my taste although I would say I love most food in general. Overall, it is definitely an enjoyable experience but from a value standpoint, perhaps not quite there for me. Anyhow, definitely worth a visit but I will say I've enjoyed my visits to restaurants like Alinea and Le Bernardin a bit more.

We came here on a very cold early afternoon yesterday. I was surprised how easily I got a reservation here, for 1 PM on a Saturday; but I digress. The space of the restaurant was expansive and more old-world styled. The service was excellent as expected in most fine dining restaurants; I appreciated the fact that some sauces and food was prepared or finished table side. 

The memorable dishes for me were the pan seared foie gras, which I would rate a 10 of 10. I have had foie gras in the past, but nothing so rich and so quick to dissolve in the mouth like this foie gras. The accoutrements with the foie gras also paired nicely with the richness of this sliver of goodness. The second memorable dish was the Lobster Newberg, whose sauce was prepared table side; our hostess stressed very much how the dish used to be named Lobster à la Wenberg. Anyways, the sauce was prepared with the innards of a lobster head, apple brandy, herbs, and a kind of lobster bisque. The lobster itself was perfectly poached and was brought in separately as the sauce was poured on top of it; the micro mushrooms complimented the dish nicely. 

The third memorable dish was the smoked sturgeon dish with it's various side platings, all very beautifully arranged and almost overwhelming. These complemented flavors included a slice of bread with ethereal thinness, caviar with crème fraîche, pickled mackerel, whitefish potato salad, pickled cucumbers with black rye and salmon, and beets with apple and trout roe. Each section had it's own distinct flavor and the thought process was executed well in this set of dishes. 

That being said, I want to explain why I gave this restaurant only a 4 star rating. It was not because of service or the environment; it was the remainder of the dishes, most notably the duck. I expected a godly piece of poultry, but I found it much more ordinary than what my expectation believed it to be. The knife given to us was dull and the skin with the flesh wasn't very forgiving to the knife, so I was initially shocked that my knife couldn't even penetrate the duck after 4-5 strokes. The skin was flavored well but not as crispy as I had imagined; the flesh was more tough than tender. The mushrooms were cooked nicely but I wasn't a fan of the thick mushroom mousse that accompanied the duck breast. Maybe this was an off day? I am not entirely sure. 

Was this a 3 star michelin meal to me? Probably not, but what do I know. I've been to many restaurants but this meal didn't blow me away. Not to say it wasn't good, but it did not exactly match my expectations, as very few restaurants actually do. Would I try Eleven Madison Park again? Yes, perhaps for a summer menu when other produce is available; many of these dishes were root based and perhaps the better weather in the surrounding area will in turn translate to better dishes for my palate? Perhaps, but the next stop on our list is Le Bernardin.

Thank you for reading this review.

There is nothing I can that hasn' t already been said or that could even do justice to this amazing restaurant. We called three days in a row at exactly 9am to be kept on hold for 45 minutes each time to finally get a reservation at 5:45 on a Tuesday. I would have been kept on hold a week though. 

From the moment you walk in, you feel like royalty. Like you were meant to be there and that every wish or desire you have would be fulfilled by there team. As you enter into the rotating doors, past the iconic EMP sign, you are greeted by the Matrie'D and several attendants. They greeted us and asked politely for our names while helping take our coats. As soon as we said our names, it was followed by "Oh yes, Mr & Mrs, please follow us this way". 

We sat in a lovely corner booth and had the iconic envelope, opener and black & white cookies awaiting us. As we sat, within a few minutes my husband needed to use the restroom and while he began excusing himself, attendants came over to move the table so that he did not have to awkwardly scoot out of the booth. They did this the entire night when we needed to get up. Service was absolutely spot on. Drank 25% of your water, well then it was time to refill it. Engulfed your delish bread and venison butter - why not get you more? It was amazing. 

The food was just astonishing. Nothing was a 'miss'. Everything was seasoned perfectly, well thought out, presented with style and tasted deep in flavor. I had several overall favorites. First, I loved the long island seafood course- four small plates of local seafood - oyster, crab, scallops and caviar. My favorite was the oyster and the scallop- served with pistachio. 

My overall favorite course of the night was the celery root, braised in the pigs bladder. This is brought out to your table and basted tableside with vegetable stock. As the bladder increased in temperature, it expands and holds in the heat and braises the celery root - which is done with black (winter) truffles. It was absolutely amazing. The celery root was perfectly shaped, and still had some bite of texture whilst losing the fiberousness of the vegetable. The stock sauce with truffles complemented it so perfectly. 

All the dishes were presented well, explained and had wonderful plating, presentation and flavor. From the baked Alaska to the slow cooked bass - all were divine. My last favorite was the wonderful assortment of cheese, served with house pretzel bread, small salads and quince. I fell in love with the simplicity and complexity of this. I love cheese courses, but they were able to pair cheeses to have individuality whilst going together- three types of each goats, cows and sheeps milk cheeses. All similar yet unique. After a very disappointing night at Momofuku Ko, this evening was absolutely perfect and shows how Daniel Humm and his team are so well renowned!!

Phenomenal dinner! There was perfect service and perfect food. We are a regular. We had always had their signature duck as our main dish. This time we tried their new alternate: pork.  Amazing flavor. I know this may be blasphemy at this place... But this pork (braised confit served with mashed potatoes accented with fois gras and red wine) may be even better! Can't wait to go back!

I didn't love Eleven Madison. :: Shock waves spread through the internet ::

It was stupid expensive. Maybe if I was part of the 1% I'd like this spot more, but leaving close to $700-$800 poorer (including only about 2 drinks per person) after what seemed to be an adequate meal is never a good thing. 

Pro-tip: Still want the Eleven Madison experience? Grab a seat at the bar (first come, first serve) and order a la carte.

Ok, so a few words about my experience and what I took away. Eleven Madison Park pays homage to New York with most food being from the local area. Salt from the Hamptons, meats from upstate, you get my drift. Very cool. I ultimately found that Eleven Madison fell short of any value leaving me loving only but a few dishes, finding others to be fine, but not really giving me the value I so look forward to when dining. I'm not cheap. I'll spend the money, but I still look for value which I have found at the likes of French Laundry, Le Bernadin, Jean Georges, Robuchon, Gramercy Tavern and so on. 
- They say this is a multi course meal (about 12) - they do include few cookie style amuse bouches. Have you been to other 3 star, even 2 star Michelin restaurants? They often give those as gifts, not courses. So in actuality, you're getting about 10 very small courses & dessert.
- There is no menu meaning you have no clue what is about to go down. They do ask you to choose your protein (in our case, duck vs venison). That's fine since I eat everything, but I do prefer to choose my own adventure.
- This restaurant is definitely more fun than other fine dining establishments. However, I think it's more gimmick than food. Yes, their pastrami on rye which was about 1 inch by 1 inch in diameter with 1 slice of pastrami was good. I appreciate they make it in house. You know who also makes really great, just as good in-house pastrami? Katz's. And for about $20 I can get a sandwich that feeds a small country.

This was a similar experience with the main dish of venison. They brought it out to the table so we could see it being prepared in an ancient method which was cool as shit. A nice hunk of meat cooked in it's own smoke and ash. What came out was a small taste of meat per person. Where is the rest?  I'm talking not even credit card size. Was it superbly cooked? Hell yes. I probably wouldn't of been so butt hurt about the size if I enjoyed the other courses as much... read on.

- Most of the courses were fish. I love raw fish. I love fish. Most of these courses were completely unmemorable. Like totally unmemorable now that I think about it. They just came and went. 

- Dessert. Ah dessert. My favorite part of the meal. Eleven Madison Park's wasn't up to snuff. The sorbet and Baked Alaska were fine. Chocolate covered pretzels were delicious, but I mean I just dropped $700.

Things I loved at Eleven Madison Park and why you should go:
The Manhattan Cart - they make your drinks tableside.
The venison broth - YES! 
I enjoyed the cheese course- nice hunks of NY made cheeses. 
They give you the most delicious granola to take home.
The service was IMPECCABLE. Less stuffy than most fine dining establishments, but completely professional.

If money ain't a thing, yes, go here, of course, d'uh. For those with a tighter wallet but still enjoy the finer things of life, I do think you can have an equally impressive if not better experience at the likes of Jean Georges, Daniel, Gramercy Tavern and get a bit more value for the money.

Peace, yo. Don't hate.

What can I say? I went for my birthday and it was amazing as always. The wine pairings were really interesting. My favorite thing? Hard but I had some parsnip noodles that were something like I never tasted ever. Second favorite part, the take home menu. I was relived, again, not to have to recall everything.

I also appreciate that I was asked about my preferences and dietary concerns, with the chef adapting and still producing amazing dishes - that is the definition of service!

Singularly best meal I've ever had. Predictably the wallet lightness reflects that. 

Memorable parts of an otherwise top-to-bottom amazing meal: wine opening (involves fire), the duck, the variety of beverage pairings with the courses, the flight of manhattans.

Easily one of the best restaurants in the country.  The food is delicious and creative without falling into the trap of being 'weird for the sake of weird' that you sometimes see these days.  Service is spot on and the wine list is first class.  The only thing I don't like about Eleven Madison Park is that I can't afford to eat there more often.

Finally I got the reservation. I was so excited so that I was doing nothing the whole day and just waiting for the dinner at the evening. But quite frankly, I was very disappointed. To me, it should be 3.5 stars, considering that they were trying so hard to impress the dinners, I rounded it up to 4 stars.

Among the 14 courses, none of them made me wow. Most of them were very forgettable. But quite a few things I knew I disliked almost right away. The striped bass was flavorless and the texture was off, the duck was so hard to cut, the desert tasted too much of rum and it was so bitter.

They really tried hard to show the dinners how the food was prepared and how it was cooked. And what were the the ingredients and where were they from. For example they carried the pig bladder to show people from table to table ( I don't  know I like that, not very sexy and a little weird). They also wanted to show the creative techniques to make the food, for example, setting the desert on fire. Sure, it was cool to watch it like a show, but I cared more about how was the flavor of the dishes, if all the ingredients went well together, if the dishes were executed perfectly so that no any small details were missed out. From this point of view, EMP really fell short.

The service was very good but I felt that it was not as professional as daniels and per se. Some people may like it, because it can feel more relaxed and more causal. That is true. I did feel the whole atmosphere was more relaxing, some guys with jackets, some guys without, one guy even starting to get a little drunk and talking so loudly.

Getting Reservations: This is difficult. I called in month in advance 15 minutes before their phone lines opened. At 9am sharp I was placed in phone queue for about 20 minutes before I finally was able to make a reservation for my girlfriend and I. And even then, I was only able to get a 10pm table. 

A Week Before The Meal: The Maitre D' sent me an email confirming the reservation and asked about any food allergies. I informed her of my girlfriend's allergies and they were very responsive and accommodating with it. I also requested a kitchen tour at this time.

The Dinner: I won't speak too much about the meal experience itself as other reviewers described it quite well. We arrived a bit before 10pm and were seated at our table. There were some empty tables but I think that was intentional. Service was wonderful and food mostly tasted great, although I was not a fan of every single dish. Towards the end of the night, around 1am it felt slightly rushed but understandable. At this time the Maitre D' gave us a very informative kitchen tour. 

Overall great experience. I would likely return to Eleven Madison, but after a few years.

I don't think I have enough words to describe  how much I enjoyed the experience of dining at Eleven Madison Park.  It is more than just having a meal; it is a true food experience.  The service is impeccable and overall the food was great.  Bring an open mind and a developed palate.  Don't come or bring someone who is only into basic simple tastes.  I found most of yhe flavors to be complex and delightful.  I won't go into a blow by blow of all the courses, but some of my favorites were the NYC flavors, you make a little sandwich and get your flavored soda and the seafood course was divine.  I have to stop because I'll start including them all; I truly enjoyed everything!  We requested a tour of the kitchen, you should rrquest this ahead of your visit, and we got our tour at the end of the meal and it was the perfect way to end our extraordinary experience.

I've been treated to this lovely restaurant twice and both times, while good, I was looking for more. I'm not sure what I feel is missing; it's a solid meal but with the talent they have in the BOH, I wonder if they could push the boundaries more.

Slightly disappointed. 

Yeah, that pretty much sums up my experience at 11 Madison Park. After planning this evening for sometime, I can't help but expect nothing but the best. Don't get me wrong, 11 Madison wins many, many points but on this particular night, something was off. 

Upon arrive, they greeted us and even said Happy Bday to the lady of the evening. After we were seated, I got up to switch sides with the Mrs.  The servers quickly came over to extend the table for me. Very on point. 

Our Maitre D' welcome us explained our courses for the evening, let us choose our preferred flavors of the evening and gave us a start off black and white cookie. Starting to look promising. 

We were served by over 10 different people during our evening. Our glass of water were not even permitted to go down by half throughout the night. Each dish was of course explained and the servers were very down to Earth. Service was world class in every which way. 

Now the food. This is where the review goes down hill just a tad. 

Bread was croissant like. Flaky and buttery... Butter with hints of duck. 

Warm salad - pickled vegetable noodles with a pistachio or two with butternut squash. Served with duck broth. Nice and hearty. Good way to begin. Wow me? No. 

Seared Foie gras with blood sausage. Tasty, creamy but I think the star of the dish may have been the blood sausage. Better than foie gras at Jean George's? No. 

Rye bread with little mini dots of mustard and mayo served with perfectly cooked Pastrami. Lasting impression? Not really. 

Long Island plates. Oyster wrapped in a vinegar gelatin. Chopped scallops. Crab with pickled Daikon. Sturgeon caviar with quail egg. This was prepared nicely and the caviar with quail egg was clearly the impressionist. 

Stripped sea bass with shellfish squid ink sauce. Tiny little fish and had very little appeal with me. 

Sea urchin with foam on a bed of mashed potatoes. This was actually very, very good. 

So 11 Madison loves to show you the plates and how they are cooked. They come by and show me the celery root that was trapped inside a pig bladder and tell me they'll go into the kitchen to serve it. They lie. It's just a show piece. The same show piece I saw at least 15 times that night at different tables. I actually felt bad for the servers that had to repeat the same thing over and over. You can see it in their face. "Stupid pig ball sack again and again". 

As for the celery root with truffle gravy. Eh. It was ok. 

Blend of liver patte and cured duck meat. Nice touch. 

Next is the duck. Another show piece they walk around tables throughout the night. It was a bit tough and hard to cut but the taste was there. 

Cheese. We had 8 types of cheese to choose from. The variety was nice but there was one potent one that smelled and tasted like concentrated fart. Once I cut into it, the aroma seared our nostril hairs. It was pretty raunchy. Other than that, pretty clean and nutty flavors. 

Baked Alaska. Only real strong complaint of the night. Yet another showpiece I was sick of seeing. Fire was cool. The taste of this thing was... Out right awful. Patrons want dessert. Real dessert. Creme brûlée with a spin. Chocolate something to blow me away. A mousse perhaps, some kind of crazy lava cake. The taste of this was gross. The rum soaked bottom was too strong it become bitter. The Apple flavors just didn't work for me. However, they did say they'll be happy to give us something to substitute. 

I will say they do whatever it takes to make you happy. If you didn't like something, they would find ways to make it up to you. Service is perfect. Gift bag was nice. Granola was really good. Fancy good. 

As for the food, it missed on a lot of marks so the experience was not as remarkable as I thought it'd be. Not for the price that was paid.

One of the best restaurants I've ever been to and here's why:

Food: amazing! My boyfriend took me here for my birthday back in September and the menu was more seafood heavy, but delicious. The food is not only delicious, but very interactive, which I really appreciated.

Service: Service was great, of course from a fine dining restaurant, it is on point. The staff is also very interactive and you get to interact with multiple servers. 

The experience is def different from the other Michelin Star restaurants. I would go here if you want to enjoy great food and have a great time!

The big name has been around for quite a few years and finally I gave a try.

I have been to other 3stars like Le Bernardin and Alinea in Chicago.  My review will be based on the comparison mainly.

In terms of food, I just want to say it's good. But among the 15 dishes, there are too many desserts and the first dish even repeats. As a matter of fact, only.

I am an Asian I don't like cheese, did not finish cheese dish. Two dessert dishes are way too sweet for me that I can't even finish a bite. Also they don't taste very special compared with dunkin donuts. The first and last chocolate dishes not surprise me either. So out of the 15 dishes I DON'T like 5 of them.

The remaining dishes including celery root or venison are pretty good though.

Next the wine pairing, I am not an expert on wine but neither the red/white wine or sparkling wine/riesling is much worse than the wine pairing from Alinea or Le Bernardin.


The overall experience is fine for a Fine Dining but it does not meet my expectation for a 3-star. Will never come back again.

Here's another 5 star review for this amazing place. 

My boyfriend and I had been eyeing Eleven Madison Park for months, wanting to indulge, but waiting for the right occasion. We finally decided to make a reservation for our one year anniversary and the experience was everything we could have hoped for. 

We were greeted by the Maitre D', who knew it was our anniversary. We then received congratulations from every other staff member we came in contact with, as if he'd told every one before we arrived. 

What I think is actually the most fun about this place besides eating, is watching the staff. The dining service is perfectly orchestrated, every staff member's movements timed and choreographed. The service is what I can only imagine is the best in the world. They are pleasant, friendly, and somehow extremely regal without coming off as stuffy. We felt immediately comfortable and like we were most definitely welcome. Our waiter was perfect, and the sommelier chose 3 types of wine for us to pair with the meal, since we didn't opt for the true wine pairing. Many other staff members swift in and out almost undetected, to clear plates, replace silverware and napkins, and refill water.

The food was delicious, with a few standouts including the fois gras, venison, and celery root. We found the seafood left something to be desired, and didn't quite work for us, but every other course was very enjoyable. 

When you go to Eleven Madison Park, if you want something, ask for it! They'll literally accommodate you in anyway they can. We were almost to our dessert courses when I decided I wanted some more bread, which had been our second course, and they brought us more warm rolls and butter. My boyfriend fell in love with the apple soda they served with the deli course, so our server gave him a bottle to take home. This on top of the two jars of granola we received, as well as a special anniversary chocolate bar for each of us.

All in all, Eleven Madison Park is totally worth the $700 bill for two. If you have an occasion to splurge for, don't hesitate. I will say, while the food is very very good, the service and ambiance were the true stars of the experience. Go into it wanting to have fun, and you will!

The experience was amazing - definitely a highlight to our trip. The food was so creative and absolutely delicious. The service was also amazing. Ask for a tour of the kitchen, it's definitely worth checking out. We got a bit carried away with doing a wine pairing which placed quite a dent to our wallets but we got over it ;)

I don't know what I can say about EMP that hasn't already been said in the previous 1,000+ reviews!

We blew in on a cold January night, several minutes before they were technically open, and they welcomed us in and invited us to have a cocktail at the bar until the dining room was ready. My husband got a scotch on the rocks, and OH MY GOD, that was the most BEAUTIFUL ice ball I had ever seen! The bartenders HAND CARVE the ice balls here! I wanted to see it in action (especially after we all raved about it), but alas, our table was ready, and we were whisked away to the dining room.

We were surprised by the details in each of our courses. I wasn't feeling all that great in my tummy, so I had to warn them that I was lactose intolerant when I would normally suck it up and pay for the pain/discomfort later! This was actually a good thing because some of my courses were SO MUCH MORE delicious than that of my friends or my husbands! 

They really knocked it out of the park with their super attentive service. This wasn't stuffy pretentious service. This was service that seemed effortless and was at times just downright playful. We were joking that we didn't know what course we were at, and made a comment that we should have boxer girls in bikini's walking through with big number signs! The next thing we knew, the server who was handling the silverware lifted up his tray that had a post-it with a number on it and walked by!! We were DYING with laughter. The guys didn't know what we were laughing about, and the next course the girls had post-it's with a number on the bottom of our plates that we then lifted up for the guys to see! It was AWESOME. And FUN. We had so much FUN here!

It was a four hour dinner that did not feel tedious or boring. Not once did we check phones (except to take enthusiastic pictures of the pig's bladder with celery root). And at the end of our glorious meal, our AMAZING server gifted us not only with the granola and printed menu, but also with individual S'More kits!! We were joking that we should have s'mores since the venison is cooked in this crazy ash/salt crust, and when they bring it out into the dining room to show you, it smells like an amazing campfire. I cannot believe they did that for us, and it really seemed like the servers were having as much fun as we were!

There were a few courses that we didn't enjoy - the seafood was weirdly fishy at times, and I really didn't like the dry sausage/charcuterie course. But there were some AMAZING highlights like their take on pastrami and rye (TO DIE FOR), and their venison (the most tender piece of meat I've ever had - I could have used like 18 pieces of those). The dessert for me wasn't that great (everyone got baked alaska and I got some cloyingly sweet sorbet I couldn't stomach). 

But the service really put this meal at one of the best we've had. The service here was even better than the outstanding service we had at Per Se. However, I personally think the food at Per Se was a half step better than EMP. 

This really is a 4-figure dinner, and one that was honestly worth every penny!

What a wonderful dining experience in addition to the presentation of every dish. The duck was delicious and beautifully presented. We loved the picnic basket course which put an intimate feel to the classic elegance with an urban spin on a restaurant with high ceilings.  The staff was very kind and our waiter was just the perfect amount of comedic and friendly.

Overall an amazing food experience and definitely one that everyone should put on their bucket list.!

Amazing. Went here for my sister's birthday. The service is impeccable and the decor is beautiful! When we walked in everyone said happy birthday and there was even a card. The meal was so delicious that I recommend everyone try this at least once to learn to appreciate really good food. As an extra treat they provided granola to take home which was the best granola I've ever had. I will definitely be returning to this amazing restaurant!

Although unlike other fine dining restaurants, emp uses food from places around nyc, they really did a good job to combine food from different origins into a big symphony with balanced harmony and engaging atmosphere. Good job. Will visit here again in the future and try other favors even though it costs a few hundreds bucks. And their servers are extremely good at handling the atmosphere and expectation of guests.

The service was amazing but most of the food was NOT good.  The presentation was good and the detail and timing of the food was great but it was not yummy.  I was so sad because this was my first Michelin star restaurant but I was genuinely shocked at the food.  I have friends who enjoyed their experience and their meal in the past.  

The service was impeccable.

The food was not worth eating and definitely not worth paying for.  

I went with 3 other gals that love food and regularly go to great restaurants and they all agreed that it was NOT worth it.  3 of us drove from Philly to NY to eat here and we enjoyed the company but not the food.

I did appreciate the granola they gave us as a gift as we left.  :)

I could see why this place got a three star Michelin. I came here through an invitation not knowing anything about what this place was and I was blown away. Don't really eat at these places but the tasting menu had me stuffed. 
My favorite that night was the steak- which was the softest steak I have ever had in my life. All the other dishes were very unique and delicious too. Maybe a little too unique for a newbie. 
Service was great though :) 
If youre a baller, go for it.

I've heard a lot of great things about EMP, so when it came time to show my father  (who lives in California) around NY I decided to bring him here over the other triple-Michelin shops here. It took quite a few days of trying to get a reservation, especially during the holiday season; we got lucky and scored a prime 6:30 reservation on a Tuesday after Christmas.

Upon arrival, we were escorted to our table and offered a selection of champagnes from a cart and introduced to the EMP experience, which begins with a ticket for each diner to select a food ingredient "theme" from apples, maple, cranberry and celery. My father and I both opted for a seasonally-appropriate apple theme.

EMP's focus is on surprises throughout the meal - their tasting menu is seasonally adjusted with the freshest ingredients sourced locally. EMP also strives to present a "New York"-themed dining experience - rather than compete with the French-style restaurants in the same category. As an example of the dishes we were served, EMP had it's own take on the "New York dirty water hot dog" with pastrami and rye, alongside an apple soda. 

Still, despite it's proclivity for creativeness, EMP did serve some more traditional dishes such as a sampling of Long Island seafood, Bass and Venison. The venison especially was amazing, as it was cooked inside of a hardened bread shell. The bread shell helped to evenly cook the venison throughout, so that the entire piece of meat (which was honestly quite thick) was the same level of tenderness and juicyness, contrasted with the typical pattern of seared on the outside, and gradually more pink as you move towards the center.

Dessert was a series of local chessses followed by sweet finishes of cakes and sorbets that delighted our palettes. Each dessert melted in our mouths, and were served with delightful presentation - as an example, our "Baked Alaska" dessert was drenched in on-fire rum in front of us at the table before it was served, which was a spectacle in itself.

The service throughout the meal was impeccable, with amazing presentations of food before final cooking preparation and detailed explanations of the local origins of each dish. 

The only reason EMP lost a star in my review was over the wine pairings. My father and I, having lived near Napa valley for most of our lives, opted for the more expensive wine pairing at $225 a person. However, we were a little disappointed that the wines were good, but not exceptionally impressive - in our previous dining experiences, we've had wines that were able to transform the taste of the meal and every dish; EMP's wine pairings did not live up to that standard unfortunately (though, it is a difficult standard to meet). The most disappointing was our final brandy pairing with dessert, in which we were offered an apple brandy that was much less than smooth in going down. Although it tasted fine, we had expected something truly exceptional for a restaurant of such pedigree, and those expectations were not met.

At the conclusion of our meal, we were presented with the traditional printed menu of the dishes we experienced that evening and their wine pairings, alongside two jars of EMP granola. I didn't have the chance to sample the two jars of granola that evening but the following morning, I noted that the granola was indeed very delicious (though, I wonder if it's "Triple-Michelin" granola, or indeed if "Triple-Michelin" granola exists).

Overall, EMP is an experience worth having because it is truly one of the best restaurants on this planet. The New York local character of EMP is unique and rewarding, and helps it stand out from the other Triple-Michelin establishments here (and from the other great restaurants around the world). I would be cautious of the wine pairing if you grew up around wine country, but otherwise EMP will meet, and likely exceed, your expectations for your dining experience. 

On a pricing note, my father and I paid a little over $1300 for the tasting menu and the higher-level wine pairing, including tax and tip.

EMP is also definitely worth repeat visits for it's seasonal dishes and varying tasting menu throughout the year. I will be visiting again soon once the right opportunity and dining partner arises.

Before I make any comments... If you've never been to this place and you're curious-stop reading and make a reservation. The idea is to surprise you, so please take my advice and don't read too many reviews before you go there. 

To make a reservation-call exact 28 days in advance, at 9am their local time; if you get a prerecorded message saying it's not open yet, hang up and call right back. Keep trying, be patient and you'll get it. Have a credit card with you because there would be a $125 penalty for no show.

For the food, the drinks, the service, the ambience-all the good things have been said and they are all true. So I prefer to share some personal thoughts here.

Spoiler alert!!!

I am lucky to have the opportunity to dine at Eleven Madison Park. Thanks goodness they were still nice even though I showed up in ski jacket and snow boots. 

It was top-notch, but not the best meal I've ever had. If you check the menu, it was overloaded with delicacies, and I believe all ingredients are best in class. At the beginning it was enjoyable experiencing different flavors, textures and expecting the next adventure, but soon the process itself became pushing. There is a concept in Chinese aesthetic called leaving blank space; "less is more" should be the equivalent. That's what I'll say- I would probably enjoy it more if it were four or five separate meals. Some guests left with satisfied and painful look on their face; obviously they were stuffed. I also saw people get drunk (on a complimentary, unlimited liquor coming with the last course). If I were the restaurateur, I don't want see these here.

Still it was a wonderful memory and worth all the $$$. I admire the chef, the manager and the crew- their pursuit of perfection is why I am willing to spend time, efforts and money to get to know what they do.

Ranked #4 in the world. 3 Michelin star restaurant. Eleven Madison Park is by far the best restaurant that I have ever eaten at and I consider myself well traveled having already eaten at D.O.M. in São Paulo  which is ranked #8 in the world. 

Reservations can only be done through opentable and the earliest that you can set the date is 28 days ahead. Reservations open at 10 am ET. I went online at 10 am 28 days ahead and the only available slot was at 10 pm which is what we chose. If you miss your appointment, you will be charged $150/person. 

I arrived with my girlfriend around 9:30 and we went to the bar to get some drinks. We saw a waiter ironing the table cloth for a new table. At 10, we were shown to our table. The interior of the restaurant is very elegant and stands to see why it was given 3 Michelin stars. The menu is always changing (my brother went there 2 months before we did and he had completely different things).

We were given 12 dishes for the tasting menu with wine pairing. Each dish was fantastic and there were absolutely no complaints. Service was impeccable and friendly. If you come here, just prepare to spend the entire night here. We didn't finish out last course until 1:45 am and didn't get back to our hotel until 2 am.

I highly recommend Eleven Madison Park and have never eaten better food than I did here.

We had dinner on Thanksgiving day. Expectations towards this restaurant were very high and we can definitely say that we were surprised by all means. Staff members were all so warm and friendly. Our server was even a little bit cheeky. 

Each dish was perfectly prepared. The dinner was 15 - 16 courses depending on how you counted it. We particularly appreciated the fact that server asked for not only food allergies, but also preferences, so that the kitchen could tailor dish for each diner. My favorite courses were the smoked sturgeon with caviar and the homemade soda and the duck. There wasn't anything that we didn't really like. We didn't do the wine pairing, but each had cocktails we were really enjoyed. 

Yes, it's expensive but it's once in a lifetime experience.

I've been fortunate to experience s lot of great Manhattan restaurants - but eleven Madison park is by far the best. Every dish was perfect. The service was as delightful as the food. The venison broth to start was great especially when paired w the squash and pear dish. My favorite was the sturgeon with quail egg caviar sable. The Hudson valley foie gras wasn't very good - so the staff was kind enough to trade it out since we didn't like it! Amazing. 

It was overall just an amazing experience.

This was the dining experience of all experiences. I've told many people that I have no problem going to extremes in search of an otherworldly food experience and Eleven Madison Park delivered on a level I don't think can be exceeded.

My wife and I dined there several years ago but I only recently started writing reviews and this place demands one. 

Made an open table reservation one month out. We were visiting NYC so we were not at all displeased with an early seating. Especially given the long dinner. We had the full tasting menu with wine pairings  - the full Monty. The pairings were both a wise and bad decision. I can't imagine the meal without them, but the aftermath wasn't pleasant. It was simply too much of a good thing.

The meal itself was mind boggling. Too many delightful courses to remember (though I did photograph many). Somewhere around 14 courses with or without the amuse bouche. A clairvoyant wait staff who anticipated every move and desire. A once in a lifetime trip to the back of the house to see the kitchen in operation and enjoy a table side drink made with liquid nitrogen pomegranate and brandy. The list of surprises and best '_____' ever went on and on.  Even the bread was delightful. I mean crazy, delicious. I'm not afraid to admit there may be some confirmation bias involved here. Oh well.

We left with the standard granola (omg it was good), two boxes of candies, our individualized (and treasured) menus...and a extraordinary hangover and a lifetime to fondly remember.

The only tragedy is that I want so badly to go back, though I can't afford many ($$$$.$$) nights like that. EMP has since been named the #1 restaurant in the U.S. and #5 in the world. How do you top that? I don't know how, but I want to try. Perhaps the best way would just to go back to EMP.

P.S. I bought the cookbook. Its fascinating, but I dare not even attempt such artistry. Certain things are best left to the masters. We will be making some granola this holiday though.

We were so looking forward to our trip to EMP based on all the glowing reviews. Boy, were we disappointed! Perhaps it had something to do with the fact that we had been to Per Se the night before (where everything was perfect), but this disappointed from the start. First, the room was boiling hot. My dining companion and I both had to remove our jackets and shoes just to keep from passing out from the heat (and I'm one who is usually always cold). Second, there were virtually no dishes, except for the final savory item, that left us saying, "Wow!" For this caliber of restaurant, I expect to be wowed. One of the dishes, a striped bass, was completely flavorless and its texture was downright unpleasant. When we mentioned this to our server, their solution was to give us a tour of the kitchen and make us a special cocktail. Nice effort, but I go to restaurants for the FOOD and EMP simply doesn't deliver on this score. They rely too much on gimmicks, which is fine if the execution meets the creativity. Sadly, it doesn't here. The service was wonderful, but that simply doesn't make up for mediocre food. The final dish of duck breast was absolutely delicious, but one dish out of 16 can't make for a good rating when you're spending that kind of money. I DO highly recommend Per Se!!!

cant complaint anything about the service. always right on point. guess thats the secret they got three stars. however. the food compare to other three stars restaruant is not that great. but wont regrat went there to try. if u ask me will i go back. maybe not. its overpriced. maybe u will give higher review if u go there without expectation.

I have been to this restaurant twice in the past year, once for dinner and once for lunch. I am writing to express how excited I am to have reservations to visit once again for dinner in a few weeks to try out their new 12-course menu that has recently replaced their revious set-up. Isdidn't think this establishment could get much more innovative while staying traditional but they have! 

Interestingly enough you will see that the chefs, kitchenstaff, waitstaff, hostesses, bartenders will all play a mojor role in your dining experience. You don't even realize they are there for the most part as they are as stealthy as they come but you notice after a while that each member of the "cast" has had a hand on your table at least once, it is absoluetly seamless.

Obviously the prices are steep but its not like they try to hide it so don't bitch when you go and your bill is through the roof... actually just don't go because you are going to waste your experiece and you money trying to save).

Please save your money and support this oh-so respected restaurant They deserve all the time they have spent in the #1 spot on every restaurant rating service around and I hope to see them stay there. Game on restaurantuers!
Amazing service!  Thank you,Matt, for making four visitors to NYC feel welcome and special. Above and beyond wonderful service.  Food was out of this world!!

Yum. Every course was amazing and the building was so beautiful and the service was perfect. Loved the mushroom course at the chef table in the kitchen. Anytime one is invited into the kitchen it's always fun . I chose celery, my beau chose maple and we did the full tasting. Definitely worth the full belly.

Did not live up to expectations. 

I came here for my birthday, extremely excited. I have been wanting to go to Eleven Madison Park ever since I heard about. It's a foodies mecca, the place that we will all eventually go as long as we eat all the vegetables on our plate and treat our enemies well and our friends better. 

The restaurant itself had a slightly more relaxed atmosphere than I was expecting and the lighting was relatively bright. Most of the folks in here dressed in suits and below the knee cocktail dresses, but there was a random cluster of diners huddled on the side at the bar wearing plaid shirts and hoodies. 

The service was phenomenal, the sommelier was exceptional, and the flaky bread was delicious. Did not expect anything less from a Relais & Chateaux establishment.
