My favorite part of the night was when you were able to choose ingredients from a punch out card, now that is ingenious and interactive.

The disappointment was the food itself. 

The Good: 
*Duck Broth. We could have had three bowls of this, it was delicious, rich, and not too salty. 
*Long Island Seafood: Delicious oyster with yogurt, scallops chopped precisely, blue crab tasted fresh, and caviar with fish foam... of course that was delicious.
*Celery Root: Well cooked with a delicious black truffle sauce
*Finger Lakes Duck: Generous portion, and the Spice rub was on point. Cooked to perfection.

The Not So Good: 
*Cheddar Cookie tasted similar to a ritz cracker cheese sandwich.
*Kabocha Squash: Presentation was beautiful, but the amount of roasted squash was too little and most of the salad tasted like raw vegetables
*Pastrami: dry.
*Charcuterie: That's simply what it was, a charcuterie board, I expected much more.

Neutral:
*Foie Gras, smooth, but I'm ambivalent about foie in general. It tasted similar to others I have sampled.
*Atlantic Striped Bass: Wish the fish had a little bit more flavor, I prefer to not depend on the sauce for that aspect.
*Cheese: Cheese is cheese, I wish instead of sampling cheeses from a cart I could have eaten something that they created from the cheese. 
*Sorbet with Caramelized Milk and Milk Foam: Unmemorable but not bad.
*Baked Alaska: Just wish there could have been something more inventive to be served as our main dessert.

A scattering of mainly neutral dishes. A couple of good dishes. And a couple of bad dishes. This was an A-OK meal. Unfortunately, for such a pricey meal, I would have preferred to splurge on a course with more amazing inventive dishes...

Went here with my girlfriends mother.  She got pretty bad food poisoning, and we ended up calling an ambulance about 3 courses in.  She's Japanese and eats some wild shit, so it's not like she didn't have the bacteria to process something that is normally edible.

And we had to pay for part of our meal - admittedly the staff was professional and it wasn't 100% clear what was going on at the time, but I feel that there were two plausible outcomes, both which are their fault and potentially very serious.

1) There should have been some follow up in the sense that it could have been a potentially life-threatening allergic reaction, so an ingredient we explicitly said to leave out was in the meal
2) [Our outcome]  Really, really bad food poisoning - she was in the hospital for 2 nights.

This is obviously not the modal probability outcome here, but I feel like this absolutely should not happen at a place like this.  Service extends beyond the time where you're at the table and your credit card is on file.

Meh, at least we got granola to go.  It was excellent despite the fiasco

This is as good as it gets. Exceptional service. The finest food. It's an experience to savor. You have to take time and enjoy this experience. The Tasting Menu generally is a 3.5-4 hour extravaganza that includes somewhere between 12-15 courses including desert.

I was here about a year ago so not sure if the menu is the same, but this was an incredible experience for me coming from little old New Zealand! I had done a lot of research into the best NYC restaurants before our trip and settled on Eleven Madison Park as where I wanted to splurge. It took me seven nights of staying up until 2am frantically refreshing open table to secure a 5.30pm reservation for my friend and I. 

Well the day finally arrived and we were running late and sprinted across the park, walking through the door looking like flustered messes - probably not the best impression! The greeter was absolutely lovely though and didn't appear phased at all. We were lead to our table right at the back and settled in. My friend debated what to do with all the cushions around us but I thought it was very comfy. The building is beautiful, I loved the whole decor. Its tastefully decorated. 

The menu was 15+ courses, and each one is a complete surprise. They don't give you a menu prior but our wonderful waitress explained that it was "New York" themed with an emphasis on transitional dishes and local ingredients. Our only option was beef or duck for the entree (known in NZ as a main!) and we went for the duck. Both of us had to have the same one. They ask before hand if there are any foods you don't like or any allergies. I said onion, banana, caramel and coffee (because I am fussy and annoying!) and they didn't seem concerned. Dishes start small and get larger and more complex. Its a long meal (over 3 hours) but all the dishes are well spaced. My favourite things would be the sweetbreads, clam dishes and the duck. Oh and the foie gras was delicious. Overall it was incredible, interesting, intriguing, innovative food. There were only maybe one or two dishes that didn't completely 100% impress me. Of note is the imagination in presentation and serving styles. We got a picnic basket, a clam bake, and carrot tartare was certainly interesting! I don't want to give to much information that might spoil your own experience. 

Service is out of this world. Impeccable impeccable impeccable. One of my favourite parts actually was walking to the toilet - everyone stands aside and nods and smiles at you. Probably the only time I'll get to feel like a celebrity haha. 

Wine service was the only letdown of the night and why I wish I could give this place 4.5 stars instead of 5. The wine list is extensive but I'll be the first to admit although I loooove wine I'm not the most educated on the topic (apart from NZ wine). My friend and I decided since the night was a splurge anyway we would opt for the wine tasting to accompany the food tasting. As with the food menu we were asked if there was anything we didn't like and I told the Sommelier that I wasn't a fan of any white wine, but especially sav blanc and resiling. He said it was mainly a white wine based tasting as that went best with the food but he would see what he could do. Well, it was all white wines, maybe two reds? I couldn't finish two of the whites as the taste really wasn't for me. I did regret not just ordering a bottle or two of something I knew I would like - no doubt between the two of us it would  have been far cheaper as well! 

To end the night we were given some muesli in a mason jar to take home for breakfast in the morning. I liked it and found it quite delicious. We were also taken out the back into the kitchen to meet the chef and have a cocktail prepared for us. We were told we were chosen as we looked like we had been enjoying ourself, which we certainly had been! We were also quite tipsy at this point. 

Overall this was a very expensive night out, close to $500USD each. Luckily we were somewhat intoxicated by the time the bill came so just laughed as we handed over the credit cards! We had planned for it and had some idea of what was forthcoming, and reasoned that it was a once-in-a-trip experience and at just under 4 hours it was like an evenings entertainment. 

Bottom line - I would definitely recommend this to anyone who is looking for an exceptional dinner experience in Manhattan.

My friends treated me for a birthday dinner here once.  It was indeed unforgettable and spectacular experience!  Explains a lot why this is the number one restaurant in NYC.  

We tried out the tasting menu.  The presentation of every single dish is so tasteful and elegant, the flavors are exquisitely balanced, and the combination of the different textures of the ingredients compliments each other in your mouth like nothing I've ever tasted before.  I think I close my eyes half of the time, that's how much I enjoyed it LOL.  

The restaurant is so grand as it is in one of those art deco buildings, which added to the ultimate dining experience.  I love all the fresh flowers everywhere.  

I also love the service here, you're treated as if you're the most important person!  I think if you own a restaurant, it may not be a bad idea to check out this place out if you haven't already.  I will definitely be back!  Also, if you happen to come by early before your reservation, check out their cocktails at the bar.  It's out of this world!

The service was fantastic, but the food didn't meet expectations.

Based on the food alone, I would probably rate this three stars. But the service really forces me to add that extra star. Everyone was very friendly, informative, and helpful. Our captain (Andrew) was very pleasant, a little stiff at first, but I think he warmed up to us! He took the time to help me choose my wines and made excellent suggestions.

They also had a card (in a sealed envelope and they provided a letter opener!) with four flavors that you can choose from. Spoiler alert: this is to choose your flavor of the soda that comes with the pastrami. They also use this flavor in the Vanilla dessert.

Don't get me wrong, the food was good -- prepared well and you can tell they take care in plating the dishes, but none of the flavors were particularly interesting or kill-me-now amazing. For $225 per person, I was expecting more. See my pic of the Nov 25th menu.
-Cheddar - tasted like a cheez-it
-They also had flaky rolls that were really good, probably my second favorite food of the night. It came with a duck butter that was pretty amazing.
-Broth - very fatty, the flavors weren't as complex as my mom's homemade chinese broths
-Squash - didn't care for this, it was a bit tart but overall kind of bland
-Kohlrabi - I actually don't even remember this dish
-Beef - probably my favorite dish of the night. The pastrami was tender but not as juicy as I'd like. The soda that comes with the dish was a very nice touch.
-Seafood - all of it was really tart. The mignonette gelee kind of ruined the oyster for me, sure it's interesting, but maybe it was better in theory. The caviar was good, but come on, it's caviar.
-Striped Bass - it tasted a bit rough, maybe it was overcooked
-Celery Root - came with black truffle sauce which was delicious, but I didn't care for the taste of the actual root. They also brought out the animal bladder that they cook this in, this was cool to see and touch (haha).
-Charcuterie - the cured, smoked duck breast was good. The sausage left something to be desired. The liver was extremely liver-tasting, stay away if you don't like that much of a liver taste.
-Duck - they brought the duck out for us to see before serving it to us and it looked like ten pounds of meat. Apparently they age the duck for 14 days so the whole duck is inedible except for the breast. They also told us to feel free to ask for more of this, so if you're still hungry (which I don't think an average person can be after all the courses that come before this, and more to come), you can ask for more. The actual duck was seasoned well with a nice herbed crust, but the tenderness wasn't there.
-Cheeses - mehhh, just some cheeses, some were especially stinky
-Whey - sorbet made with whey -- of all flavors they could use, they used whey. Not a fan.
-Vanilla - a very pretty presentation, but anti-climactic
-Pretzel - regular
-Chocolate - the black and white cookie was way too sweet for me
-Apple Brandy - omg this is killer, like a horrible moonshine

After drinks, tax, and tip, the meal was about $770 for the two of us. Was it worth the price? Based on the food, not really. But if you count it as a 3 hour experience, and have money to burn, go for it.

Overall, a great experience to have because of the service and environment (although if you look up, you just feel like you're in an old bank). Very cool to just take it all in and enjoy being treated like royalty. They space out the dishes perfectly and are very aware of what you need.

I am glad that we were able to make a reservation for 2 before arriving and this was a first class experience, I have nothing against the menu or the dishes and the atmosphere  was quite conducive for the meal. Overall it was a nice experience.

Tasting Menu.. SPECTACULAR.
The whole dinner (3 hours) was so interactive!
I absolutely loved the entire experience!
They give you the tasting menu to take home PLUS GOODIES!
Their tasting menu changes seasonally.
I hope to go back again! Someday!
A co worker took me here. WOW simply amazing. I will be booking for my next trip back to NY. This is a treat everyone should have at least once.

I have dined here twice now, for lunch and dinner - and what a phenomenal experience it was. Superb, funny, knowledgeable service and absolutely peerless food, well worth the price of admission (and then some). Be prepared to spend 4-5 hours dining.

NY, NY 

Overall:  2.75 

Value:  4
Food: 2.5
Service: 5.0
Ambiance: 3.5

The Set/Tasting menu is 10 plus courses.  If I came super hungry and ate everything offered I would be Stuffed.  

Unfortunately, 2 of the courses were pretty good while the rest were literally "just okay".

Even though the food itself fell way, way, WAY short of expectations the Kitchen gets an A for effort.

Went with the Venison and the "soup" to sip in the beginning was really fantastic.  The Venison was perfectly cooked & seasoned.

The "Celery" soda was quite refreshing and unique.

The presentation of the Venison was really cool.  Also, the "Celery root" cooked in the casing of a pigs spleen (it could be a different organ) was unique.

Apparently the Chef decided to change the menu 2 years ago.  Since then it has focused on very local ingredients with an approach of "We want you to appreciate the food eaten by folks in this state 100+ years ago to the present day".

Nice thought as some of the dishes are provided with a telling story.

From the second you walk in until you leave it is as if you are The Focal Point Of the restaurant.  Really, really great service yet unpretentious and not stuffy at all.

No hostess to speak to - just whisked directly to my table towards the very back, dead center.

This restaurant is outstanding. It's the best of the best and anyone else giving them less than five stars here in Yelp, are not worthy of visiting Eleven Madison Park. But don't just take my word for it or anyone else's on the website, rather from the experts that award Michelin Stars.

If you're deciding between per se, le Bernadin & EMP--this place wins out BIG time. 

For a mere $225 (before tax and tip) you'll have the pleasure of experiencing the glory that is EMP. 

I don't wait to spoil the menu or any of the surprises but each course is inventive, delicious and will be sure to introduce you to a new perspective on food. 

We also ponied up for a half wine pairing (companion had to drive after dinner).Their sommelier is a genius btw. The pairings lean towards white wine because the food is so delicate (but with HUGE flavors) but we also got a rosé and a red for the meat course. If your interests are more of the hoppy variety, EMP also has a great beer pairing. 

The night we were there 70 people were on staff for the 80 guests. Yup. Not a typo. Almost a one to one ratio. This makes for impeccable (& almost excessive, in a good way) service. 

PRO TIP: when making your reservation ask for a tour of the kitchen. It's a beautiful operation & they give you a little surprise once inside.

Overall Experience: 4.5
Service: 5 Excellent
Interior: 5 stars
Food: 3.5-4 stars. 
Price: 2 stars

Pretty good food, but can be very rich for some people. I wish there was a la carte menu because I did not like everything they served...food presentation was excelllent!! But I am more into the taste of the food...I like the old Eleven Madison Park menu when they had an individual choices.  I did not like the fact that everyone in my party had to order the same entrée. A few dishes can be combined as one. They served potato as a different dish because they wanted to present pig bladder...an excellent presentation but taste was okay...Overall, $225+$225 (wine tasting) was a great experience for a very special day, but definitely little over-priced. Sommelier (Dav) was excellent!! I would rather go back to Gramercy Tavern or Jungsik because better price & better food.

Before our NYC trip we knew we had to experience Eleven Madison Park at least once so a month before our arrival we were lucky enough to be able to get a reservation for 4. 

The environment was of course very formal, most of the guys were in suits and ladies were also business casual. 

Immediately after we sat down, there was a present that was waiting for us to unwrap, which was also our first course, it was the Cheddar Black and White Cookie with apple, famous NY sweet treat and let me tell you, it was the most delicious black and white cookie I've had in NY. No joke.

We initially expected about 5 to 7 courses, but wow, 15 courses including a presentation before each of them, the captain and the chef actually came out and explained the history, origin of the ingredients for each meal. 

Their wine list is out of the world, we got 4 bottles of champaign throughout the night and everything tasted wonderful. On top of that we each got a cocktail from the Manhattan Presentation which the bartender brought the entire mini bar to your table and mix your drinks there. Pretty awesome huh?

We finished with some espresso and the captain brought a whole bottle of Apple eau de vie (40%) as our "after dinner" drink. Oh my god! Crazy!

5 hours went by exceptionally, we didn't even notice. At the end of the night, we were given a little souvenir bag with a mason jar full of organic granola and the menu of the night.

It can be very, very expensive but I think it's entirely worth it, not mentioning about the food, the service you get is second to none. There's a reason why reservation is almost impossible, because you are guaranteed to get the best time out of it.

EMP truly deserves to be one of the best restaurants in the world. I highly recommend it. We surely will come back (would love to do it every season if we lived in NY) when we're in town.
It's been 40 minutes since our reservation and we have still not been seated. Not a great way to celebrate an anniversary dinner...and the baby sitter needs to go home...not coming back.

I love everything about this place. The food is perfectly cooked. The service is impeccable. The wine list first rate. Best soufflé I have ever had. I want to go back this week for a special occasion. One of my favorite restaurants in New York!

A fun take on fine dining by people who want to share their love of food.

In order...

CHEDDAR - tasted like a gourmet goldfish cracker, with the slippery coat of an actual goldfish

BROTH - fluffy-as-air roll in the broth of whichever protein you've selected as your table's main, in our case, venison. I would have eaten this for my entire lunch 

KABOCHA SQUASH - this dish's joke is less the pizzazz of making squash strings as long as spaghetti and more the endless interweaving of the strands that makes isolating a bite akin to escaping a Chinese finger trap or solving a Google hiring puzzle

HUDSON VALLEY FOIE GRAS - we opted for the terrine rather than pan-seared and thank goodness we did, since the restaurant nailed to the degree the melt-in-your-mouth temperature at which to serve it

BEEF - the second best pastrami sandwich in the city and certainly the most whimsical, with a grand reveal to satisfy your curiosity and hunger. Served with a soda of our chosen flavor, maple 

LONG ISLAND SEAFOOD -- another epic reveal, as each of four different bites (each better than the last) is unstacked before your eyes

ATLANTIC STRIPED BASS -- I though this was presented as halibut, but in any event, probably the only dish of the day that struck me as merely good

LION'S MANE MUSHROOM -- is it kosher to cook a mushroom in its own broth? Not sure, but it's tasty

CHARCUTERIE -- emphasis on the word "cute", like all the tiny savory bites on this plate. Delicious? Too small to tell

MILLBROOK VENISON -- the way this dish is teased is sensational: first, smoke wafts across the dining room, in an apparent kitchen error; then, servers bring a copper pan with a small forest smoldering in it. In the woods: your venison, to return plated shortly. 

SELECTION OF LOCAL CHEESES -- the pretzel and bitter greens bring out the best in these fromages and vice versa. 

WHEY -- lost in the shuffle 

VANILLA -- they flamed this "baked Alaska" like Vegas impresarios before our eyes and we half wished they would have told us to dig in then and there, Fire Marshall be damned. I do wonder what happened to the 80% of it that never made it back to the table -- not that we could made any use of it

PRETZEL -- because, at this point, screw it, right? Dipped in chocolate and sea salt and cut only by a glass of apple brandy dryer than calvados. We did not take the bait and finish the bottle

CHOCOLATE -- but for the need to wrap up with a mirror image to the first course, I might have said stop the insanity at the pretzel. But that wouldn't have been right.

Inventive -- don't go here for a run of the mill
Dinner -- get outside your comfort zone and be a foodie!!

I've been living in NYC since 2000 and 11 Madison Park is consistently one of the VERY best dining experiences. Service, atmosphere, and food.... All A+++.  Perfect for a special occasion or a quick cocktail at the bar. It's truly a gem!

The best restaurant I have ever eaten in and by a long way. The service and food were absolutely faultless. My wife was pregnant at the time of our visit and the maître de emailed and called me several days before to discuss the menu and make sure that anything my wife couldn't eat was substituted. Would recommend this restaurant over any other.

30 days before my meal at EMP, I asked my husband if he wanted to celebrate our 1 year anniversary at the #4 best restaurant in the world. Since reservations are accepted 28 days in advance starting at 9AM EST, I was all set and ready. 15 minutes in, I scored a lunch reservation for the exact date of our anniversary - hooray!

There is nothing that I could possibly say that hasn't already been mentioned about how amazing EMP is. The food is delicious, inventive and the theme of New York resonated throughout the meal. The staff were attentive, friendly and made you feel welcome. They even gave us a tour of the kitchen and took us on an adventure to their other restaurant NoMad. Nothing could have made our anniversary more special! This is the perfect place for a special occasion and I highly recommend coming here for lunch or an early dinner, the interior design is stunning. 

Food: 5/5
We've been to several Michelin star restaurants, and this has been the best tasting menu we've ever had. Everything was delicious and the portions were large enough to leave you very full when you are finished. 

And regarding the duck, I literally got goosebumps from how delicious it was. 

Service: 5/5
The staff went above and beyond to ensure that our anniversary was perfect. They gave us a small anniversary gift, and also took us their other restaurant NoMad and gave us free champagne. 

Atmosphere: 5/5
The interior is really beautiful, it has a very Art Deco design element to it with tall ceilings and large windows. There is also a private dining room hidden away upstairs with glass walls for amazing views. 

Value: 4/5
This is no cheap meal, but this was the best meal we've ever had at this price-point. We've paid more for meals at restaurants that don't compare to this.
The food speaks for itself. What put this experience from a perfect 100 to a 110 was Kristen who handles their events. She is the epitome of what hospitality stands for.  Amazing experience

What can I possibly add onto the over 1000 reviews that EMP already has?? It's definitely been on my list of restaurants to try. With 3 michelin stars, I expected a lot and the restaurant met all my expectations.

We had a pretty late reservation at 10PM so the meal didn't end until 1:30AM. With that said, I didn't feel like it was dragged on at all. Every course was explained thoroughly and you get to know about all the local products that New york state has to offer. 

The meal started with a savory black and white cookie which is such a staple in NYC. Practically every deli carries it. It ended on the same note with a black and white cookie filled with jam. The 13 courses in between were filled with small bites with explosive flavors. My two favorite included their version of pastrami on rye bread (DELISH) and the crusted duck. 

This is definitely the most expensive restaurant that I've been to but I viewed it as a show + food experience. I waited the full 28 days for the reservation but I'm totally happy that it's off my bucket list.

We had an AMAZING wedding reception dinner in the North Room here in December.  We worked with Kristen weeks prior to plan a perfect evening for our twenty guests.  The night of the event was seamless, and the attention to detail was impeccable.  The staff successfully balanced tending to our every need with not being too visible during our private dinner.  They made sure nothing was out of place without us even noticing!  The food presentation was perfect and tasted delicious.  They were very considerate of food allergies and other dietary restrictions.   Everyone at our reception had a wonderful time!

This restaurant is what everyone says and more.  I gorged myself in Michelin restaurants in Paris and nothing compares.  This place makes me drool just thinking about it.

The only downsides are that it is fancy schmancy and requires you to dress up and also it's expensive. One of the most expensive restaurants in the city.  I don't mind expensive but I like to be able to eat anything I want in jeans and a tshirt.

MERICA.

Celebrated our 10 year anniversary  with good friends as we were all in NYC together for the weekend. Service was perfection and if you ask them questions, the night is more interesting and fun. It was only 4 days into the new autumn tasting menu so it was a long night as they were still perfecting the courses. I was very happy we had a 6:25 dinner reservation as we got done after 11pm. We did get to experience a kitchen tour which I requested when we confirmed our reservation. That was the highlight of my night for sure so if you are a foodie, ask. It made it extra special. 

The food- Some of the courses were outstanding and made me want the lick the plate while others were just ok and I was surprised they made the menu. Two standouts in the just ok category and the outstanding one. The halibut really needed a sear of some sort as it was a very bland and boring bite. The lions head mushroom course was outstanding. If you say you don't like mushrooms you will miss out on this one and that would be a mistake since it was the most delicious plate of food I ever have eaten. The mushrooms tasted like rib eye and the broth was perfection. Yum... making me miss it right now! 

Overall the dinner was an amazing experience and I felt the waitstaff was amazing and attentive. Watching them dance around the dining room was like watching a Broadway show. One of my favorite parts was watching them pour a diet coke into a glass that was designed for the bottle. It held just the right amount of ice so that it could be poured using the whole bottle without spilling a drop. I know if sounds silly but it fascinated me to watch it! 

Great experience if you have the money to splurge but definitely a once in a lifetime one to have for sure.

I really wanted to like this place (if for no other reason than so as not to feel like I just completely wasted hundreds and hundreds of dollars on a random meal).  Everything was solid and well-prepared, but, aside from the dry-aged duck with cumin seeds, nothing struck me as particularly delicious or memorable.  My wife and I looked at each other with delight when we tasted that duck--that is the response I was hoping to have for each dish given the restaurant's reputation (and pricing).

The "whimsical" approach to some of the dishes felt forced and is something David Burke does much better.  The timing between dishes was too spaced out (dinner lasted about 4 hours) and I wanted to get out of there after about four courses.  The service was great, but overly formal for my tastes.

For me, the food is always key and, unfortunately, the food at EMP was just not worth the money and time commitment for me.  I'm sure those that take a more holistic approach to dining and enjoy the "total experience" would enjoy EMP much more than I did.  It is worth trying, but not necessarily ever repeating.

Rounded up to 4 stars

I've been to Eleven Mad 5 times over the last few years. The first time I was absolutely blown away. They only had 1 michelin star back then and the food was whimsical, surprising and absolutely perfect. 
Fast forward a few years and unfortunately I think that the food has lost a certain something and almost harbors closer to being pretentious. The last time I went a few months ago (after they changed the tasting menu) and decided that I won't be coming back. The service was decent but really not up to the same standards that it used to be and same for the food. We were a group of 4 and my friend had raved about the place to her boyfriend. Unfortunately none of us were really impressed at the end of the meal. Given the caliber of the restaurant, we wanted to be wow'ed and it just didn't deliver. I think I would rather go back to Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare for a special occasion

Have been coming here for 5-6 years now. I feel like the menu is looking its touch and the show element is over paving the food. 

Also thing the decor needs a makeover. However, Chef Mumm has an amazing selection and this is worth every penny.
The wife and I had a lunch tasting sometime ago, great experience and the wine pairing was superb, the sommelier of the restaurant was also in the documentary "Somm".

Amazing, outstanding, unbelievable - these synonyms are lacking because the truth is I am just speechless. 

There were numerous times during this meal when the food brought actual tears to my eyes. The first wine, the foie gras, the smoked sturgeon, a little bite of squash, the duck with lavender. 

Like some other review said: I'm not even sure I need to describe the experience. 

It is a 15 course tasting menu. At the beginning you are given four flavors of the season and asked to pick one - I picked apple, my companion picked celery. There were tiny bits of apples incorporated into my tasting menu in a superb way, plus I got an apple soda at one point. 

Criticisms: 

We did the pairings. It is not all wine - though on the menu it does say "drink pairings" and our waiter also let us know it was not all wine. I think we received one glass of red, which was disappointing because we love red wine and were there partly to drink some amazing reds. That said, we did not let our waiter know that we preferred red wine and had we done that I think we might have received different wines. The first wine we received, a 1989 Riesling (Hans Kramp) was probably the best wine I have tasted in my life. Those 2 oz alone might have been worth the price of the tasting pairing. 

The apple soda was sickly sweet. 

Two of the drinks were a light beer and a dark beer which we did not really touch. I took a sip of the light beer. Again, we did not let our waiter know we didn't want beer - probably would not have gotten beer had we done that. Moreover, i feel as if it is a little misguided to serve beer in the 13th course - you are SO full, beer is the last thing you would want to drink. 

We got a sherry and a sweet wine, both lovely, but again - would rather have had red. Plus I didn't finish the sherry because that plus dessert is too sweet. 

Lastly, our last pairing was a BOTTLE of bourbon - which I took about two mini sips off. This "gift" feels disingenuous because I am sure they know there is absolutely no way you will drink a bottle of bourbon after 9 drinks. On the other hand, I am glad they didn't give us a bottle of wine, which we probably would have drunk. And that would have been a terrible terrible idea. So if you like bourbon, great gift. 

Both the chef and wine director stopped by our table to say hi, service was impeccable all around. Dinner is five hours (better go with someone you really like) the bill is over four digits.

Think part of the negative review is related to price and lack of criticism for this restaurant, as well as mediocre experiences in NYC that are overly priced and don't deliver. This place characterizes that sentiment exactly.

First the wait staff was young, inexperienced and tried to interact with my table too much. There is a part of the meal where someone wearing "chef" attire comes by with a huge slab of beef, talking about how it was cured, or treated, or something stupid that was supposed to make it great. After we ate the beef (which wasn't that great) I made fun of the guy and one of the table attendants was eavesdropping and made some comments.

Regarding the wait staff also they seemed to want reinforcement for how great the meal was, which I found annoying. Also I don't care where the chicken came from, who his brother was, etc...

To be fair they were very nice and attentive, I just felt like they needed my attention more than I was happy with.

The meal was not totally awful but average. I am surprised what people write on Yelp given what my experience was. Decent courses included the sandwich (soda wasn't that great), waldorf salad, cookies at the beginning. The steak wasn't particularly remarkable and the halibut was kind of nasty. Pretzel I though would have been comparable to a microwave item you could get at any gas station. 

In any case not to be a jerk but dinner for three was about $1000. I had a reservation for theNomad for the next night, which I proceeded to cancel. I ate at Le Bernadin instead, which is really a completely flawless experience top to bottom.

Food was incredible. Service was really good and staff was incredibly friendly. Only complaint was the room felt a little sterile. All that said, experience was fantastic and well worth the reservation wait.

Experience: Incorporating different nyc components was innovative and broke up the ~5 hour meal well (picnic basket, make your own pastrami sandwich, waldorf salad). Definitely helps cement the memory as more than great food.

Choice: The punch card was a fun little 'mystery' for someone who hadn't been there before. In retrospect happy we each chose coffee, as not sure how my palate would have benefited from a celery soda or baked alaska. Meat choice was nice as well, although sounds like we would have been happy with either duck/steak.

Food: Standouts were the two-part tomato tea followed by lobster stuffed tomato. Possibly my favorite, although the szechuan peppercorn crusted duck was perfect as well. Waldorf salad was a close runner up, just ahead of the potato ice cream (although caviar part was just ok). The bad - oyster (way too acidic), baked alaska was good, not great - so a little disappointing as the primary dessert.

Great, interactive dinner. Maybe would have liked another lobster stuffed tomato but all-in pretty happy. That said, would choose blue hill stone barns almost every time just given the atmosphere. Something felt a little sterile about the room.

It was a terrific meal. There was a tremendous amount of creativity that I have not experienced ever before: The punching of the card for flavor and picnic basket course especially.

Dinner:
Black and white cookie - savory (ok)
Potato ice cream and caviar (very good)
Oyster (ok)
Tomato with lobster (good)
Sturgeon (very good)
Foie gras hot (good)
Waldorf salad (very good)
Soup (ok)
Halibut (good)
Sunflower (ok)
Duck (ok)
Cheese (good)
Whey (excellent)
Baked Alaska (ok)
Pretzel (good)
Black and white (good)

Amazing dining experience here. 

Their carrot tartare was an interesting starter -- obviously not as tasty as tuna tartare but probably the best you can do a carrot. 

The most incredible dish of the evening was an egg that had the top half cut and was filled with food cooked inside. I found the food overall to be on par with any 2 star-michelin restaurants and couldn't find anything about it that made it 3-star.

However perhaps what makes it 3-star is the service. We had lamb which was only okay but what was amazing was a dining companion accidentally knocked his piece of meat onto the floor. The head waiter immediately picked it up and without a question, just replaced the whole dish within a few minutes while apologizing for the incident that wasn't the restaurant's fault. They definitely value customer service and experience here.

I felt love, true, genuine love here as I ate their food. I am not totally convinced that I even need to describe how good everything is here. Eleven Madison Park is in the top 10 restaurants in the world, beating out French Laundry and Per Se. So enough said.

The pairings are a must. They take your meal to the next level. Superb.

The atmosphere is surprisingly light, not stuffy. The room is bright with sunlight. Everyone is dressed well but speaking at a normal decibel and not whispering.

If you have a special event like a proposal or if you just want to do something special, you can get a key and I believe that the key unlocks a room of some kind. I don't know all of the details but the table next to me had a key and the waiter said that something special was planned for them. I wanted to ask them if I could go to the room with them, but felt that I might ruin their moment so I refrained. 

I very much enjoyed the food, atmosphere, waiters, everything! However, for some reason, Le Bernardin is still a notch better. Go figure.

The only other restaurant that I'd put on the same level in terms of experience, would be Blue Hills at Stone Barns. Let me be clear, this is not your typical expensive, hard to get into, stuffy place. This restaurant offers an almost mystical experience, a journey through food and service, an interaction between patron, server and chef. This place is nothing like you'd expect. It's about the food but not about the food. It's about the service but not about the service. If you are the right person for this place and can keep you mind open, it's a rather intense and profound experience. The legendary El Bulli restaurant in Spain (now closed) had attempted to create such an experience as well. This place is worth the $$. If you are going to focus on the expense, this is not for you. It also happened to be my bday, so my husband and I got a tour of the kitchen and a complimentary cocktail made of some gassy chemical stuff that was awesome. All in all, this is a true manifestation of what NYC has to offer its residents and visitors.

we went on my bf's bday, it was a great experience and for each dish they named it "only in new york" makes me thinking that this is the first real amercian food resta i ever get (if per se is a french one)
so let me tell you how the resta impressed me! we ordered four courses with the main duck, I seldom have red meat but had to admit the confit dish was GREATEST I ever have, if for any chance I will have red meat again, I'll definitely choose this one again.

EMP is my fev place. I have been dining here for the past 4 years each time I experienced some different things. I never been disappointing about everything at the place at all. Service , food , drink was supper amazing. I rather want to give them 5 Mechilin stars if there is exist . 225$ per person for food is worth it. It's the good place for celebrating your  special day I highly recommend to  try out this place then you will know what I'm actually talking about.

We had the second room floor booked for a wedding reception at this award winning restaurant.  The staff, bartenders, audio visual personell were fabulous and the food was an amazing multiple course meal, I am actually blessed to have experienced this wonderful establishment with great friends on their amazing day! I got to visit one of the best restaurants in the world!

Being a vegan isn't always easy at restaurants. But one of the ways you can tell a great restaurant from a good restaurant is how the staff treats people who have specific requests. Here at 11MP, when informed about my vegan proclivities, the staff couldn't have been more gracious. I was with a party of 20, the rest of whom were all meat-eaters, so the appetizers and main course were not vegan friendly. Didn't matter. Within a few minutes the staff was bringing out vegan appetizers, and the entree the chef created was simply one of the best vegan meals I've ever had in my life. Ever. This is a magical place. No matter who you are (well, no matter who you are as long as you can afford it...) there is an extraordinary meal waiting for you here.

Eating at Eleven Madison Park (ranked 4th in the world with 3 Michelin stars) has been a dream of mine ever since moving to New York in the summer of 2007. From my early exposure to Shake Shack, where I learned what a real quality burger tasted like, to the venerable Gramercy Tavern where I received some of the best service in recent memory, EMP would be the crown jewel that would meld both concepts at the highest level.

Without hesitation, and with 3 empty seats to fill, I had called and confirmed the reservation with IKTC's Joshua Stern who was a pleasure to deal with. Luckily, over the next 2 hrs, I was able to find 3 of my friends willing to drop $225 for a dinner happening in a few hours.

At 7:45pm, we all arrived and marveled at the entrance tucked away just steps away from Madison Square Park's Shake Shack. We were greeted warmly by the host and as he led us to our table, I marveled at the high ceilings and the warm glow of soft light - a balance between formal and cozy.

The host saw that we had bags with us and within seconds, these hooks magically appeared out of thin air. They clamped on the tables and held our bags with ease. I've never seen anything like that before and thought it was the coolest thing in the world but my female companions assured me it was quite common. Still, bonus points for great service as most places wouldn't do anything about your bags and assume you'd leave it on the dirty floor.

After settling in, we were given an envelope and a letter opener. None of us had any clue what was going on as we opened the envelope and 4 cards tumbled forth silently on the tablecloth. Each person at the table picks one ingredient and their forthcoming dishes would be built around that ingredient in different variations.

Our earl grey tea arrived shortly in these gorgeous ceramic cups and saucers handmade by Jono Pandolfi, a dinnerware designer who plies his trade from an abandoned factory in New Jersey and supplies dinnerware to some of NYC's top restaurants such as EMP, Nomad, Atera and so on.

A gift box wrapped in twine was dropped off at our table and Sharon squealed like it was Christmas morning.

The box contained savory black and white cheddar cookies with apple which tasted like elevated Cheez-Its.

The oyster dish was not too briny and the creaminess of the vichyssoise worked hand in hand with the salinity of the caviar to produce a perfectly balanced bite. The table agreed that we could have put down a dozen more easily - what a tease to only experience one.

The next dish showcased EMP's renown whimsicality. While the scallop, covered in a scoop of apple snow and marinated with pine and water chestnut, was cooked perfectly, the star of the dish was....the actual dish; an actual scallop shell that shined like a pearl. The reason why the shell stayed put on top of Pandolfi's plate is because it was wedged on a bed of sand (which isn't edible, trust me).

The next dish was even more creative in terms of plating and flavor. What caught my attention first was the luminescent mother-of-pearl spoon wedged perfectly in the slot on the wooden block.  Next to it, a cross section cylinder of bone, perfectly smooth to the touch. As Claudine demonstrates in the photo below, simply puncture the creme fraiche disc with the spoon and scoop gently. You will be rewarded with the most tender bite of beef tartare with caviar and smoked bone marrow. 

The theme of beef continued as four heavy wooden blocks with carefully inserted waxed butcher paper landed at our table with a satisfying thud. The dish paid an homage to New York delicatessens. Set in front of us was a gourmet open faced sandwich with house cured pastrami, rye bread with mustard, and endive. The best part of this dish was clearly the tender pastrami, clearly of the highest quality and even more luxurious in marbling than Katz's Deli. Everyone took a few pieces and arranged it on top of our rye with mustard. 

To wash down our sandwich, we were given housemade sodas based on the flavor we selected at the onset of the meal (my cranberry soda was perfectly tart). 

While I understood the homage to such an important slice of New York culinary history, I couldn't help but think that I could have just gone to Katz's to get a pastrami sandwich because essentially this is what it was. It didn't seem that "elevated" to me and I was mildly disappointed.

The bread course was delicious - house rolls with the flakiness of croissants served with duck fat butter and salt. In this instance, the limited quantity of one roll per person was probably for the best.

The next dish was a miss for me due to personal preference. I like my foie seared, the hunkier the lobe the better (like Betony's). EMP's foie gras, cured with sunchokes and served with fermented mustard greens, was rolled up delicately and wasn't as foie-intense as I had hoped.

*Read the rest of the entry here: http://www.scrumphsus.com/blog/2014/9/16/elevenmadisonpark

Truly a great restaurant the location is top notch the staff were incredible friendly and welcoming
The duck with the lavender, fennel, peach and ginger purée was succulent while the foie gras brûlée was amazing 
Truly special place

I went to eleven Madison park, per Se and le Bernardin this weekend. Eventough this was fantastic I like Per Se a little bit more. 
It was my second time here in 3 months time and I liked it less than last time. The food was terrific but I give it 4 stars because it was much like last time and I would expect some more change in the menu.
Anyway, one of the best restaurants you can find in the world!

I've eaten at many top-tier places like Le Bernardin and Coi but I think this was the best meal I've ever had. The menu included lobster, caviar, oysters, foie gras, and aged ribeye. The presentation was amazing and the ribeye was unbelievable. I loved it and definitely want to come back.

People say it is the best restaurant in the United States. Listen to the people. People are right. 

I was there to celebrate my birthday. Eleven Madison Park makes sure that my special day started the first second I heard from them on the phone to confirm my reservation. They asked our names and preferences and told me who (by the name of person) would be waiting for me by the door that day. They gave us the best seat that night and everyone was greeting me with a Happy Birthday. 

I went to all the stars restaurants in New York, but Eleven Madison Park is ranked No. 4 in the best 50 restaurants in the world for a reason. It cuts down the "fancy" part but enriches the entire meal with respect to previous great chefs and historical events in the city. Unlike Le Bernardin, it doesn't have "golden leaves on rice", instead, Eleven Madison Park explains to you what Wardorf Salad is and why it is called Wardorf Salad. It educates you what is Baked Alaska and where it comes from. With respect to all the wonderful chefs who created dishes, Eleven Madison Park showed us a humble attitude towards the greats. 

I also love the picnic basket. We have four gentlemen in polish business suits sitting in front of us. When the picnic basket was there on the table, they were confused and didn't know what to do about it. They lifted the napkin to take a peak and finally after a good 10 minutes, they started placing a picnic on their table, passing around soda, cheese, plates and bread. It is like a picnic in the Central Park with friends. It brings back good memories. You forget that you are at this upscale restaurant. You are more concentrated on the food and your companies. The hesitation on how to start with a picnic basket is like a small joke between you and the chef. When you are wondering what is going on, I bet the chef is laughing in his kitchen. 

At the end of the meal, they gave us the menu for us to take home. It was like a great show, you were in it, you were curious about the next dish, you enjoyed every minute in the show. And at the end, you had some survivors to take back home for this fun memory.

700$ tomato soup for two ... We tried the tasting menu ... Everything was a joke .. Taste like nothing ... Just tomato soup was very interesting ... This place more of a tourist trap ... When we were having dinner seams like everybody's first time ... This restaurant is very beautiful but it's better just seat by the bar have a drink and get some appetizers ... We left the restaurant so hungry lol ... I've had so many tasting menus true pricy but never left hungry lol ... Jean George's and Del Posto million times amazing !!! Waist of money 100% !!! Every way !!!! My favorite Del Posto for tasting menu !!!

This place used to be the gold standard for new american when Danny Meyer still ran it and it was a la carte. The current prix fixe is totally overrated. Many dishes attempt to be clever but simply fall flat. Pseudo-intellectualism that's not very smart. The card game? Beer and pretzels? When you're paying this much you expect an interpretation of the titles, not simply... A basket with a beer bottle and pretzel inside. Incredibly mediocre. A mighty fall for a once great institution.

first tasting my companion has ever enjoyed, and i've taken her to all sorts of great restaurants in the u.s. and france.  and i'll say it was fun and a good value.  it wasn't great, though, foodwise.  the service was amazing, but it seemed like they were listening very closely to private conversations, maybe through microphones.  complaints about food = not enough protein (how did that whole duck transform into two little slivers of breast in its trip from the pan to our plates?).  also, there were food temp issues.  the chicken was room temp, and should have been warm.  same with the seared foie gras.  that's bush league ball.  it was a fun lunch, though.  great cherry soda.  food probs 3-star on its own (nothing approaching the best i've had, and not a lot that i'd be desperate to taste again or even remember in a week), but service and fun bring it to 4 overall.

It was one of the best dinners that I had. Food was fantastic,services was amazing. waiter was so helpful and had so much knowledge about food. menu was very interesting and had humor in it. Tomato  tea  with lemon Thyme salad with lobster and garlic was mind blowing! Foie Gras must be one of the best in the city!
Great for special occasions!!!!

This is a really spectacular spectacular restaurant. Perhaps my favorite restaurant in Manhattan. I was surprised every step of the way in this 4 hour dining extravaganza. It was such a colorful adventure and I never knew what could lie ahead in the rainbow whether it came in a basket, on a grill, in a box, or tied in a ribbon. And I liked that the portions were small, absolutely perfect, and savory so you could actually eat the entire 15 course without feeling overwhelmingly full. And I have to say the service was absolutely amazing. The waiter was so courteous and knowledgeable which made the experience unpretentious. If you live in NY, EMP is a must-go!!! :) Fabulous and an unforgettable experience!

One of the best dining experiences I've ever had. Food was amazing but what really stood out was their service. It was meticulous and above and beyond outstanding. Because my husband doesn't care for long drawn-out dinners like this I don't see us coming back anytime soon but I'm glad we got to try EMP.

I really wanted to give it 4.5 stars; however, since I cannot do that, I rounded up to 5 stars.  It's all about the food, so let's break it down.  I would say that all the appetizers were the best compared to the entrees and desserts. The most memorable appetizers was the seared foie gras; however, I kind of felt gypped.  My portion of the foie gras was small compare to others.    As for the entrees, we selected the duck over the lamb.  It was cooked perfectly.  Looking around the dining area, most people selected the duck.  I didn't feel the same about the picnic basket.  The picnic basket was a nice concept, but it was lacking in execution and flavors (hence the deduction of  1/2 star).  As for the desserts, I liked the Baked Alaska.  The presentation was great.  We finished the meal with an apple brandy.  Overall, it was an amazing experience.  We really feel like it was deserving of a three Michelin stars restaurant unlike Le Bernardin.

I requested a quieter table since I planned proposed to my now wife! After the proposal, everyone clapped for us. (didn't know everyone was watching) Got complimentary champaign and the cork for the occasion. Oh, and the food was delicious and they helped me throughout the proposal process.

Had an amazing meal here in 2012 but only writing about it now. Second best high end dining experience I've had in New York (Picholine was the best but my friend was dating the sous chef there and friends with the sommelier at the time, so figures we would get extras there and therefore I can't rate Picholine objectively). The presentation of all the dishes were outstanding. There wasn't anything served that I didn't like. I forget the wine I got, but it was very moderately priced and very good. Also, they put a bottle of Guillon Painturaud VSOP Grande Champagne Cognac on your table that you can drink as much of as you want.

Hands down one of the best places I have eaten in a long time. Went there with a few friends who were aquatinted with one of the chefs. The food,service and setting were all excellent. It's expensive but well worth it. Just delicious!

I'll start with that my wife and I are avid worldwide travelers, foodies and have no problem with paying for 5 star quality and service.  Having been to some of the worlds finest restaurants, in our opinion, Eleven Madison Park is overrated.  The decor is wonderful with lots of waiters and assistants running around.  During a tour of the kitchen, one of the managers mentioned that they have 1 employee for every two guest.  There was lots of attention, however, it felt impersonal, canned and rushed.  The wait staff were like robots with no personality.  Our main waiter was  snarky, impersonal and gave the impression that our paying over $1,000 for dinner for a party of two was a privilege.  The sommelier was very knowledgeable, however, initially recommended a wine that cost over $1,300.00.  In my opinion, a $1,300 bottle of wine should not be his first recommendation.  At the very least, he should have provided a range of wine.  We instead settled for a $325 bottle of wine.  The food itself were tiny bites which you could eat in one bite.  The selected surprise ingredient (i selected coffee and my wife selected celery) ended up being a cheap 6 oz coffee and celery flavored soft drink.  Some much for quality and creativity.  Eleven Madison Park has a good marketing campaign that I believe that has mastered the heard mentality and if you don't like their food - you don't know good food.  I hope this is beneficial.
Amazing, creative, surprising food, top notch non pretentious service. Had an amazing time.

Wrote a very long review, but yelp said I had to click on a confirmation email to post it, which never came. So here I am again, and I'm making it shorter this time.

Ate here twice. Both experiences were excellent.

First time was in winter. My wife and I decided it was the best meal we've had. Yes, the food it outstanding / award winning / etc. Everyone knows that. It's the service that won us over, as they made it an unpretentious, fun, and entertaining experience. Make your own tartar. Magic tricks. Smoke in a globe. I don't want to diminish the experience by reducing the meal to what (according to my narrative) sounds like cheap parlor tricks, so I'll just say that the servers are outstanding and really deserve more credit than they get.

So we decided to have our wedding rehearsal dinner here over several other venues, and rented some rooms for private dining. We hosted around 20 people, and Kristen graciously combined the private dining rooms as it was available. Had a special little ceremony, and the meal followed. Again, service was outstanding, as well as the food.

We are absolutely happy with our decision to have our wedding rehearsal meal here, and will come again in the future.
I think the best meal in NY. The service is A+++: The food Delicious, whimsical and generous. For a special occasion this is THE place.

Service and Experience is what makes this place.

Expect a 4 hour dining extravaganza.  

Great for special occasions and anniversaries.  A 15 course meal that will keep you on your toes.  This place is a well thought out experience where there are options and adjustments for different path options.  

So you might be asking why 4 stars....Although the service treated you like royalty some of the food dishes were below what I expected.  The level of difficulty in cooking asparagus inside an inflated pig bladder using broth is great and all but ultimately still asparagus.  An A for effort but I can't give it the 5 star.

Hint:  Make sure to get a reservation.  A secret is to request to get shown the kitchen where they make you a drink that will make you feel like you are back in high school science class doing an experiment.  Expect it to be expensive.

Honestly, there's not a lot that one can really say or conjure about this establishment that HASN'T been said already. The food and aura is very New-American; if you're into adventure and whimsical surprises at every corner of your courses, this is the place to go. 

With that said however, with the wine pairing for two the bill can easily just crack into the four digits if you're a generous tipper. And with that kind of burn in your wallet suffered, there are better "luxury bargains" in the city but if you're already looking at this page and thinking about it, chances are you're set to swallow the price.
Great experience. Every course was well thought out and executed to perfection. Chef Humm was Kind enough to take a picture with me and invite us in the kitchen for dessert. Great time!!!!

We've decided to downgrade our review to four from five stars for a simple reason: in retrospect, none of the dishes turned out to be truly memorable. 

I still have vivid memories of dishes I've eaten at other *** restaurants, but not so much from EMP. 

Yes, the clam bake was fun and creative, yes, the picnic basket super cute, yes, etc. etc, but I wish there was an "Oysters & Pearls" dish that I was still dreaming about.

Apart from that - top-notch.

Hands down this is the best birthday dinner for my best friend after many disappointing 2-3 Michelin star adventures in New York City. 

EMP has excellent service with great tasty food that won't make you want to eat shake shack after dinner. The service is flawless without being snobby; and has a tad of fun/sassiness while maintaining VIP classiness. The only small things that annoyed me is the fact that the staff sometimes forgot to refill our water by 5-15 minutes. 

The fact that the chef will listen to your request is a double edged sword. I told them
I love shell fish and my friend is allergic to shellfish. In the end we were served the same sea bass dish to please my birthday friend while other tables got this amazing clam dish. I gotta say the Seabass was poorly seasoned and the worst dish of the night. Further I blamed my friend for being allergic to shellfish. EMP should have served bass to my friend and amazing clam dish to me!

On the flip side, one of the chef creatively changed the summer fruit inspired dessert to a custom-made chocolate decadent dessert after my birthday friend and I got tired of eating all the summer influenced ingredients (berries, cucumber, corns, tomatoes) throughout the course. 

Wine list is flawless. They have the best wine inspired from every different region of the world. The Taiwanese table side tea service is a differentiated service that I never saw in any other 2-3 Michelin star; which made my Taiwanese friend extra happy for this surprise treatment from the tea sommelier. 

All and all, EMP is at par with Alinea or Next in Chicago but is significantly better than Noma in Copenhagen who served you moss and ants for dinner. I like how EMP is trying to use local ingredients and favorite NYC dish (pretzel, pastrami, soda) and upgraded it with their interpretation. Now I would like to challenge EMP to reinterpret halal cart and NYC pizza into a gourmet 3-Michelin star meal.

Our son and daughter-in-law recently gave my husband and I a gift card for Eleven Madison Park.
From the minute you walk in the door you are greeted by a  friendly, warm and attentive staff.  Our son met us for cocktails by the bar before our dinner where there was a reserved table waiting for us.
You won't be able to take your eyes off the design of the room and the vases filled with beautiful yellow flowers.
We had the 14 course tasting menu, which lasts about 3 hours.  There is one surprise after the other.  We were asked to choose duck or aged rib eye  for the table, as part of the main course, we chose the rib eye, which was done to perfection.
A few of my favorites were the corn custard with tuna and caviar, tomato tea with lemon thyme served with a salad of strawberries and basil. For one of the desserts you will love the apricots they grill at the table served with lemon thyme ice cream and honey. Oh, and one of the surprises - a picnic basket with fresh cheese, homemade soft pretzel, raspberry mustard and green tomatoes.  You will find that your taste buds 
will come alive!!!
They do have an extensive wine list and unusual cocktails. 
The service was beyond my expectations!! The waiters, and there are several, explain everything.  Just when you think it's all over you are handed a copy of the menu and a glass jar with granola for the next morning.
Truly an unbelievable experience.  We were truly lucky to have gone and hopefully one day we will be back!!!!!

Memorable evening to celebrate our one year wedding anniversary. Food presentation was terrific, thus 5 star rating. Clearly a lot of thought and hard work was put into each course. We had 15 (or 13?) course tasting menu and the highlight was the sunflower. Never had sunflowers before and was impressed by the novelty a bit. The center of the flower was prepared and had a texture of a potato. I had high expectations for the duck since I've heard from others how great it is - it was tasty but not the best I've had. The service was great and the staff was very attentive. In the end we didn't notice how 4 hours just flew by.

Get ready to have the best meal of your life, which is likely to be the most expensive too. The tasting menu and service was incredible! 

A tip: With drinks and tip, your bill is likely to be at-least 800 dollars, so get ready!

2nd time back.

Short Review: This place still serves ambrosia.

Pros: From the moment you step into this place, you are treated like royalty. The food, the service, the air, the ambiance, and the rest of everything have been carefully thought out to craft the perfect dining experience. 

Cons: The amount of time I have to wait to come back here yet again.

Spectacular service, food, & a playful experience. It was far from the stuffy experience that could be expected for such a highly ranked restaurant (4th best in the world!!!!).  
Make reservations ahead of time and expect a minimum 3 hour dining experience so starting as early as 6pm isn't a bad idea.
Expect it to be pricey, including the alcohol which isn't part of the $225/person. While the food, especially the smoked sturgeon which was out of this world, the homemade duck fat butter, and the caviar, were amazing, I was truly blown away with the well executed & accommodating service! They even hooked us up with the seafood stew broth and bread at my request!
I've ate at multiple michelin restaurants around the world and so far this is the best food I've ever had the pleasure to enjoy.

The best meal I have ever had. The whimsical fashion in which all the food is presented, the creativity in each of the dishes, the sheer deliciousness in each bite of every item placed in front of us, and the sheer delight in the eyes of all of the staff that served us, all came together perfectly and makes my wife and me reminisce often about our dinner there, even though it was nearly two years ago. This is as close to a "must go" as any place we have ever experienced, and we hope to make it a tradition to dine here every time we visit the city. I hope to one day visit Noma, just to see if it can even come close to knocking EMP off the pedestal my wife and I have put it on.

We can't wait to come back!

It's hard to imagine that a meal that costs a kings ransom will actually make you feel like royalty - but that's exactly what EMP did!

The best meal of my life (so far).  The service is fantastic.  I felt at all times like I was the focus of the servers attention.  Nothing was too much effort.  The showmanship was magical and it made the entire meal an unforgettable experience.  The atmosphere was in no way stuffy and the waiters seemed to be having fun revealing each new surprise for us.

I loved the little gifts we got to take with us - nibbling away at those delightful snacks, kept the EMP experience with me for at least a week.  I also was very impressed with sommelier  who kindly sent us a list of wineries to try on our visit to the Loire Valley.

This is the best dinner, meal, food, anything digestion-related I've ever had. I'm a stone-faced numbers person who's been to a range of michelin-ranked, top-tier restaurants and I've never thought I could feel this ecstatic and emotional about food. For god sakes, they managed to make me like mustard and cold tomato, five out of five on that alone. Above anything, order the tea!

Dinner spoilers below:

****

The best way I can describe this dinner is "pure happiness". 

There's a sense of playful creativity with the courses. Pastrami! Picnic! Finger-food seafood! Every dish was truly memorable and delicious with the exception of the sunflower heart, a B+ among fourteen A/A+ courses. I'm losing man points here but the picnic basket might be the most beautiful moment I've had on a date. How do you not think about pure enjoyment and the wonderfulness of being with someone more than that moment? I'd love to go on a picnic with my girlfriend with pretzel/jam/cheese/ale and, despite our work schedules and obligations that make us limit our time together, EMP made it happen. We make time and reserve money to dine at nice restaurants to make memories and EMP made the greatest one of them all.

The service acts with the knowledge that everyone is having the most special dinner they've ever had, and they are helping others reach that potential. There's a friendliness and casualness with everyone involved that few other restaurants are willing to make or execute with the delight of EMP's staff. They're perfect, the food was perfect, the interior and atmosphere itself was perfect.

Actually, ignore what I wrote before: "perfect" is the best way I can describe it.

What a neat experience! 

This is a very hands on dining experience. Our server was fantastic and at the end of dinner he send us away with a breakfast baggie and the menu of the night, so nice! 

They definitely made the experience very personal and attentive.

My experience at EMP was an experience of a lifetime.  It was so magnificent, so perfect, and so spectacular that I'll surely be telling stories of the evening I dined there with the three most important people in my life until the day I die.  I was so impressed, so taken aback, and so utterly dumbfounded by everything for the three - three and a half hours we spent there that even now it still feels fantastical and unreal.  Let me tell you something straight out - Eleven Madison Park was not named the fourth best restaurant in the world for nothing.  It doesn't have three Michelin stars for nothing.  It is a well-oiled majestic restaurant machine surely blessed to humanity by the gods.

Before I can even talk about the food, I've got to talk about the service.  Before I even arrived, the maître d wrote me a personal e-mail welcoming me to the restaurant and asking if I needed anything maybe a week or so ahead of when I drove down.  We carried on a vibrant email conversation for days and when I arrived a week later, every member of the wait staff that was at our table knew everything about our situation - that we'd arrived from upstate NY, that none of us had ever been to a restaurant of this calber before, that we were celebrating my 30th birthday, and many, many more details.  I've never felt so welcomed and cared for anywhere in my entire life to this point.  

All of the 10+ wait staff that delivered the 14 course tasting menu to us all evening long were doting, caring, extremely knowledgeable, and the best wait staff I'll probably ever enjoy.  With every dish, everything was timed absolutely stunningly, and even when they took dishes or delivered new plateware to the table, everything was perfectly synchronized.  In other words, when they were taking our plates away for example or replacing our silverware, everything came down or was removed at the same time.  When we initially sat at the table, they not only pulled the chairs out for 2 of the people with me, but pulled out the *table* so the other two could comfortably sit in the booth with ease.  Everything was explained with vivid detail and showcased brilliantly, such as the roast duck with honey and lavender, the picnic basket, or the sunflower and how it was braised, and it was truly magic for the ears.  I seriously cannot compliment the wait staff enough.  I can't imagine anyone in the world being more magnficent than this.  Did I also forget to mention they even gave us a tour of the Michelin star kitchen without me even having to ask, where we all got to see the chefs at work, and got to meet and shake hands with the Chef de Cuisine, Chris Flint?  Or perhaps the birthday gift box they gave me with a classy Michelin star twist on a homemade almond joy inside? Truly an unforgettable experience for life.

As for the food, what can I say?  With the exception of one of the dishes on the fourteen course menu (the Long Island rustic clambake), everything. was. magic.  I especially have to call out the dessert courses, the open-face pastrami sandwich, the braised sunflower heart, and the tomato-thyme tea as the 11/10 courses of the evening.  They were the most elegant, classy, and picturesque dishes I've eaten ever and I can still taste them now, literally days later.  I honestly don't know how I can ever eat normal food ever again after tasting what they served.  Everything was seasoned exactly right and each element of food was in unbelievable harmony with each other.  Every small brunoised piece of vegetable or mini-quenelled piece of caviar was simply stunning, executed beyond belief, and was just exactly where and what it needed to be on just about every dish on the menu.

People, Eleven Madison Park will change your life.  It will change your world.  It will change your universe.  If you ever have the opportunity to dine here, do so.

My girlfriend (now fiancee) and I went here this weekend to celebrate our engagement.  

What a meal, what service, and what an overall four-hour experience.

Everything is managed down to someone being prepared to pull your table out for easy entry after taking a trip to the restroom.

We loved each of the 14 vibrantly flavored course as well as our beer pairing which we chose through a collaboration with their beer expert.  To be totally honest, the courses that involved meaty proteins were the least spectacular including the lobster, shrimp, and duck.  We had to choose between duck and a 140-day dry aged sirloin.  I would love to know what that is like in retrospect.  The meat courses were still great, but the standouts included some pleasant surprises.

Dinner highlights:
Tuna wrapped custard served alongside sturgeon caviar (WOW!)
Tomato tea with lemon thyme (clear tea bursting with tomato flavor)
Clams in the seafood bake (lobster and shrimp not as spectacular)
Seared Foie Gras (we had foie gras two ways, but the seared stole the show)
Sunflower heart braised with sunchokes and sunflower seeds 
(didn't even know you could eat sunflowers)

Dessert highlights:
Picnic basket with fresh cheese (w/honey) and pretzel (w/spicy raspberry mustard) This was one of five phenomenal desserts; came with Ithaca picnic basket witbier
White chocolate pretzel covered in dark chocolate

Beer highlights:
Hanssens Olde Gueuze (eye opening tartness with a balanced finish; our fave)
Rodenbach Single Barrel 2009 (almost up to the vintage 2011 gold medal std)
Hausbrauerei Uerige Dopplesticke (Old ale paired beautifully with the duck)

Extra points for our head waiter Kevin who was great throughout the whole meal and specifically spent 10 minutes talking out my fiancee's allergies to make sure we were comfortable with everything that came out of the kitchen.  We also received a few small additions to the meal in honor of our engagement.

If any NYC dining experience is "worth" the price tag, it is this one.  Highly recommend.  I cannot imagine a better place to celebrate an engagement!

A table for 2 at 10pm. A tasting menu that takes 3.5 hours. I was sure that no chef would be staying around that late to cook me 14 courses and so had been trying to pull the reservation back into an earlier slot and failing. 

So I was really surprised when I turned up 30 minutes early to enjoy the bar and was politely ushered to the table and kick started straight into the tasting menu experience. 

And from the second I took a seat and chose a strand to run through the tasting menu (I chose cherry), Eleven Madison Park was exceptional! 

People wise, food wise, wine wise... everything about the restaurant was phenomenal! Bar staff, waiting staff, bussing staff, were all brilliant! Every single course from the cheddar, tuna and caviar through to the sunflower and onto the pretzel was masterfully created, seasoned and delivered! And the wine list which could have been daunting, was made easy by the sommelier who took our requirements and delivered something absolutely amazing - then went on to use a flaming torch, wax and tongs to create a stress fracture and snap the neck of the bottle off (avoiding any cork issues).

Of course all this isn't cheap, but in terms of the starred restaurants I've had the good fortune and pleasure to eat at, Eleven Madison Park is at the top of the pile in terms of quality and experience!

Excellent food, not the best I've ever had, but top notch paired with innovative dining.  A bit too long for me to sit still, but I'm glad I had the experience! Certainly do recommend to anyone looking for a tasteful and unique experience.
The ultimate culinary experience ever! Definitely one of the best meals I've ever had. It's very expensive but worth every penny! I can't wait to go back! Superb service, food and ambience.

What more can I say about this place that isn't already covered!! Took my husband for dinner on his birthday and loved every minute of those 3+ hours. Servers went out of their way to make the whole experience personalized.

EMP was by far one of the most memorable meals I've had in a really long time. The food is spectacular and our team of servers were just wonderful. I can't stress enough about forgetting your pre-conceived notions of what you like / dislike. At EMP - the most wonderful smells and tastes await and they'll blow you away. I'm still dreaming of that tomato tea. Deliciouso!

You know, I don't exactly understand the hype surrounding this place. Recently I had dinner with some visiting relatives at this restaurant. When the reservation was made I was asked for a credit card # to secure it, so, I assumed, this might be "special".  I received an e-mail from a concierge urging us to mention any special requests. Having an allergy to many seafoods I responded requesting an accommodation. When I arrived and was seated at the table no mention was made of the food allergy. I was simply asked the same question, again. Then sitting there watching other tables getting many seafood dishes; my guests (who enjoy seafood) were relegated to eating all the meat and very weak vegetarian bites offered to me. Mid-meal among the multitude of "courses" (if one calls cheese on a cracker a course) we were offered sautéed sunflower bottoms. After waiting and chatting for 20 or so minutes one of the staff came over and told me that they had a problem with the dish and it would be delayed (no alternative offered!! no accommodation made, just another half hour added to this painfully long meal). So, at the end of the meal, even with all the goofy hijinks (including the ridiculous picnic basket with 2 pretzel sticks to share between 4 people, lol) I felt disappointed. I certainly can't recommend this place to anyone with 1500 bucks to spend among 4 people. I just wished it would have been better. So sad.

I have dined here numerous times. Its obvious they have changed the way the run the operation. The customer no longer comes first. We were ignored for 15 minutes before we got a glass of water and menu. I think all the good reviews they have recieved has gone to their heads. The quality of service has deteriorated dramatically. The food is not what it used to be. I think its  time for management to rethink their attitude. We will not be returning after our last poor experience. For the kind of money they charge, there are dozens of finer quality establishments.
Don't Waste our Time.......

a haiku:

total decadence
the greatest meal in New York?*
am I in heaven?

*update: no, but close

I highly doubt I will ever eat another meal in my life that will top the meal dinner I had at Eleven Madison Park last night! Even though it costed an arm and a leg (around 700 dollars for two people for a wine pairing for one and two after dinner coffees) it was worth every penny.

Each and every dish was meticulously crafted to engage all of the senses particularly with sight, smell and taste in mind. There are also quite a few surprises that involve choosing flavors and opening up mysterious boxes and baskets.

To add to surreal nature of the experience, the service was impeccable. The servers are there to explain each dish and drink to you in detail, where the ingredients are from and how to best enjoy it.   

Hands down, the best meal I've ever had and I can't wait to come back and try their other seasonal menus!

Hands down the best meal I've ever had in my life.

Was able to get a table here for a Thursday night dinner. Wow is all I can say. Everything here is simply done from the shoes up. Amazing attention to detail in everything I could possibly think of and more.
