From the way they set your knives down on the table to the way they fold your napkins if you get up from the table to go to the bathroom.

The dinner tasting menu was somewhere between 15-22 courses (depending on what you count as a course) and was $225 a person. Every course built upon the previous one, so the whole experience felt like climbing some sort of perfectionist culinary ladder. Not only did the food taste utterly amazing, it was all extraordinarily unique. Highlights include a tomato tea, an open faced pastrami sandwich, a seafood boil, and of course, the duck with extra crispy skin.

I'm not going to be able to say anything new that others haven't said before, but for good reason. Honestly if you're on the fence about it and you can afford it, just go. It's definitely been one of the most amazing and unique experiences of my life. I will carry it with me and reminisce about it for years to come.

This restaurant has great customer service and food!  I have to say, at the prices, it's more of a place to go for a special occasion or just to experience the height of living in New York once or twice.  

That being said, the food was amazing and the servers were so attentive.  I absolutely recommend this place!

I'm fortunate enough to have been here twice. Once in 2013 and the other time last week. I have to admit that I was blown away with last year's menu and experience. This year, their menu was somewhat disappointing for me in that every dish seemed too fruity and sweet. I'm more of a savory type. Even the service was better last year. I'm so bummed that they even got rid of the magic trick at the end. I hyped it up to my brother in law that he wasn't impressed, and I can see why...It was subpar compared to my first time. Looks like I'll just have to go again when they change their menu again.

Oh, I had been looking forward to this meal for so SO long, and it did not disappoint. 

The meal was nothing short of an experience. I highly reccommend you just tell the bartender a type of liquor and have them mix you a signature cocktail. Our bartender was amazing, and I had some awesome tequila cucumber cocktail that was totally to die for.

My stand-outs were shockingly the tomato-tea (until you know, you don't know), the open-faced pastrami, the foie gras (go with seared!) and the seafood bake. It was all just so good though, honestly.

We were on the fence about coffee, but we ordered the siphon pot, and I highly recommend you do! Dinner wasn't complete without a bunson burner making coffee at your table. It was de-licious. 

Can't say I'll be back soon, but man, I hope I am!!! Worth every DIME. Seriously.

Eleven Madison Park is an exceptional restaurant and, if I hadn't been to Per Se or The French Laundry, would get my vote as the best restaurant I've been to.

With that said, I do have a few nits.

First, the interior is underwhelming. It's nice, but not breathtaking.

The meat dish - prime rib - was underwhelming. If you didn't tell me it was from a fancy restaurant, I wouldn't think anything of it.

The cream soda at the end is overpowering. Not exactly nuanced.

I wouldn't go back to Eleven Madison Park, but it is an exceptional restaurant nonetheless.

At this price point, the food is as perfect as their reputation would have you expect. The service is excellent, the room is kinda big and business like. I didn't give it 5 stars because the food didn't WOW me. Everything was a great version of something similar we've had before. So we were left to consider: is it 2X better than other top restaurants in the city? I don't think so.

The best dining experience of my life thus far.

I love how hospitable the service staff is. They make you feel comfortable as soon as you walk in the door and the atmosphere is not stuffy at all. The food here is nothing short of amazing, My favorite aspects of the dinner was how each course was introduced with a story and how the entire meal came full circle at the end. 

The stand out dishes include
- Lobster and Beets
- Pastrami open faced sandwich
- Foie Gras (get the seared version)

I can't wait to come back another time as I know their tasting menu changes fairly frequently. I can't think of anything negative to say about EMP. Please make reservations, you won't regret it!

Step aside French Laundry, Jean Georges, Per Se and Le Bernadine. All of you left me bored, but Eleven Madison has stolen my heart.

I'm not crazy about the room - it's a bit too much business for my taste - but the service and the food are beyond compare on this island, and possibly this continent.

From the best brioche I've ever had, the cheesecake with blood orange jelly, the tableside egg cream, the scrumptious butters, to each appetizer and entrèe, the flavors were revelatory, the presentation sublime, and the service convivial. This restaurant would garner 2 Michelin stars in Paris, and has the potential to grab a third (it's already there on food). I don't think any other US venue comes close.

It's a shame I never ate at Campton Place while Daniel was there. I stopped going after Brad Ogden left. I think Chef Humm has surpassed anything any SF chef has to offer these days. 

Absolutely impressive.

Before the start our waitress asked us to choose an ingredient in a little punch card. Turns out two courses of the meal depended on my choice of celery (celery soda and celery infused sugar in whey dessert). We also had to choose between duck and beef for the entire table.

Chef Humm is so effing creative. I cannot forget the flavors of the tomato tea, or the magnificent blend of spices lacquered to the duck breast... He may not be a fan of sugary dessert. Both desserts we had - whey and apricot - were very tart. The portion sizes were very healthy. There is no carb-heavy dish except for the bread course and the pretzels. There is no array of bread to choose from but I kind of wish there was.

At the end of the meal we had granola in a mason jar to take home. The host also told us to get a little popsicle from the hotdog stand outside. These details give the whole dining experience a leg-up from other 3 star restaurants.

Amazing taste experience. The many appetizers were sensational, very unique tastes experience. Main course was OK. Experience was certainly unusual and a delight. The price was off the charts. Wine and spirits were very over priced. Our bill for two including one $265 bottle of wine, two glasses of champagne at start and one whiskey at end plus tip came to $1,095!

I came here over a month ago, and we opted to do the wine pairing. To be completely honest, the last couple of courses (out of 16) were a bit of a blur, because the wine pairing equates to over a bottle of wine... per person. Even spread out over the 4 hour meal, this ended up being a bit of a challenge towards the end, especially given that the last course included an ENTIRE bottle of apple brandy, which you were at liberty to finish (does anyone ever finish it? I'm actually kind of curious!).

In terms of food, I'm not going to bore you with the details, given that the tasting menu changes seasonally. Yes, it was exquisite, etc etc. Eleven Madison was ranked the best restaurant in the US this year, and I can see why. Every course felt like its own self-contained meal - that is to say, an experience. Even a month later, I can still taste the baked potato ice cream + caviar melting in my mouth. I sometimes daydream about the Waldorf salad-inspired soup. And someone said this in a previous review, but the granola - what a reductive term for what this was - they give you to take home must be laced with crack. Because it is incredible! Who knew I could feel so passionately about granola?!

Also, the service was bordering on supernatural. The attendants usually appeared at the table before I even realized I was trying to get someone's attention. Are psychic abilities a requirement to work here? I wasn't enamored with the space itself, which felt so cavernous as to bring to mind a train station or a museum lobby... I did love the windows, though, which began above the outside traffic and ended just below the cathedral ceilings; all you could see was the park. This rare view compounded with the restaurant's hushed ambiance really transported me to a simpler time and place. The bill, however, was slightly more advanced, coming in at around 1k for two, including tax and tip.

Impeccable service.  From the time you enter the restaurant to the end of the meal, this isn't about just eating food.  It's a food experience.  Our waiter knew everything about our dishes, from how it was made to where the food was sourced (he could have been bullshitting, but if so, he plays it off well!)

Tasting menu plus one drink and tip came out to be about $325/person.  Would recommend trying it out once with a group of 4 people.  I hear that getting reservations for a group of 4 is much easier than a group of 2.  

At the end of dinner, you get a copy of your menu and a mason jar full of fresh granola that the chef made.  Also, for dessert, you get a bottle of apple brandy that is basically drink all you want.  It's strong... so be warned.  These nice subtle touches create a memorable experience that doesn't cost much for the restaurant, but leaves guests with an indelible memory of their trip here.

Have an open mind and have fun w/ it!
My favorite in NYC!  When I visit, this is where I eat (as long as I'm not the one paying!).  Go for the full-on tasting menu...doesn't get much better than this!

How can one put into words a mind-blowing culinary experience from beginning to end including service and ambiance? As many other Yelpers have reviewed here, the food is out of this world and so unique it is truly impossible to even try and compare! There is a reason why 11 Madison is a 3-star Michelin rated restaurant and anyone that dines here can see why.

Prepare yourself for a 16-course chef's tasting menu over a span of 5 hours time. Each dish offered homage to NYC and although each were fairly small plates (don't worry! You will be full! ), the flavors packed a punch. From the savory 'black & white' cookies that melts in your mouth to the corn pudding served with caviar and the perfectly roasted duck, my tastebuds were heightened to a whole new level. Never in my life have I ever experienced such fine dining in a welcoming, yet upscale establishment,  where the servers were top notch, friendly and beyond ready to help make your evening as spectacular as possible. I genuinely felt whisked away from the moment I entered to the time I left and if there is one thing I can say about 11 Madison (aside from salivating incessantly) is that you definitely get your money's worth here!

Kudos to Chef Daniel Humm for conjuring magic in the kitchen and management for exceeding quality service! As a wise man once said, 'YOLO!' And on that note, GO GO GO and make your reservations today!! 

PS-There was no better way to celebrate my 30th than right here. 11 Madison-Thank you for exemplifying what fine dining and service is all about!

What a treat!  Everything we had was wonderful as you might imaging, but I will tell you about my favorite course.  They brought out a picnic basket and inside there was the makings for a tiny pastrami sandwich.  It sounds simple, but the pastrami was so perfect that I wanted to eat everyone's portions!  The chocolate covered pretzels at the end of the meal were also a delight.  Of the Michelin places we have been, this was the most creative and maybe the most fun.

My favorite restaurant ever! We went for lunch on Saturday and the whole meal was such a fun experience! (I believe 3 hours) The detail and thought that goes into every course is incredible. Even if you don't love the taste it's just fun to see what surprise they bring out next. We took so many videos and pictures. The service was outstanding as well! Just can't say enough great things about EMP. My whole group loved it! I will be back for sure!

#1 restaurant in North America = #1 dining experience I've had so far. My first 3  Michelin star restaurant was amazing. Keep your mind and palette open for anything and you can experience something incredible. I don't want to sound repetitive as other recent reviews as we had the same tasting menu (although they are about to change it next week).

I have to say some of my favorites was the play on a pastrami sandwich which inspired us to go back to Katz Delicatessin the next morning. I chose the cherry flavor as my theme and the cherry soda paired with the pastrami was soooo good - no artifical flavors! The different preparations of beets was also a standout for me...love beets! We got the wine pairing and I have to warn everyone...we went there on an empty stomach...drink plenty of water too or you may not remember your amazing experience. It's bottomless wine! 

In summary, there is nothing to critique. Food...unparallel to anything I've had. Service...they will probably kiss your feet if you asked them to. Price...you get what you pay for and it is the #1 restaurant in NA. Next up....Noma.

One. Of. The. Best.

I cannot express my gratitude to EMP. They made my anniversary AMAZING. In all honesty, I was expecting it to be a little hyped up (recently disappointed by Sushi Nakazawa) and my expectations were not too high. 

We arrived Saturday afternoon for lunch. It was quite empty, few guests at tables here and there. Luckily we got a corner couch table with an amazing people watching view. Perfect! 

I got a cocktail (the Townsend) and it was very smooth and well made. It didn't seem like it was strong since it was so smooth but I knew it was a good cocktail when I started getting tipsy after a few sips! 

Every plate and utensil placed was perfectly executed. The timing of the dishes were right on and my sparkling water cup was never empty. The waiters definitely didn't judge that I was taking 10 pictures of the same dish every time...in fact they were sweet & easy going. The service was PERFECT. 

So a few of my favorite dishes were: 

1. the Apple Waldorf salad- fresh, light, & summery. The mayo was not too overwhelming. I wish they gave more cause I could have eaten a whole bowl! 

2. Lobster - the beets were cooked perfectly and the lobster was thick and juicy. Only the best part of the lobster was on the plate. 

3. Asparagus- if asparagus tasted like this all the time, I could be vegetarian ASAP. How can this vegetable be so darn delicious? What is the secret?! 

4. Lamb- the main dish and there were three cuts of it. Each piece was savory, juicy and not overwhelming. I like how it had cabbage on the side so it's not all meat.

5. Fresh cheese- this was in a picnic basket & my boyfriend was nice enough to let me open & dig through it first. God, how did EMP know I was a sucker for pretzel and cheese? Cheese was so creamy, seriously could have eaten 10 of those. 

6. Beef pastrami - this beats Katz Deli any day! First it is not overwhelming with meat and it has delicious mustard and peas. Love the NY pastrami concept. Best part was their homemade soda in the bottles. 

Those were my favorite dishes but all of them were great! Loved the fresh ingredients and how each dish was a different concept. Just amazing and it blew my mind. 

At the end, we got a kitchen tour and anniversary chocolates. It was icing on the cake. 

I wouldn't have gotten to experience this if it wasn't for my boyfriend and the lovely staff of EMP. It was literally a perfect anniversary.

One of the best food place I've ever been to in New York. The waiters are incredibly accommodating and happy. Definitely gave justice as the 4th best restaurant in the whole word. Cocktails are superb!!
Always great to dine here. Service is amazing as always and the food never disappoints.

People. Will. Judge.

Don't care. I love food, drinks, & fancy things. So naturally, coming here fit the bill.
We dressed the hell up as a group & it was nice to be super fancy for the evening.

Seeing that this restaurant is #4 in the world that makes it #1 in NYC & in the USA.

The service here was impeccable. No request went unturned or overlooked. The staff was supremely accommodating. 

I opted with cocktails to accompany my meal while two of my friends got wine pairings. Another friend was our DD so she kept it PG with water & seltzer :)

We had a total of 15 courses & imbibed for 3.5 hours, thoroughly enjoying everything. 

Favorite courses? The (1)pastrami, (2) English peas dish, & (3) lobster dish.

Our meal was finished off with black & white cookies and apple brandy that was hot fire.

Yes, I dropped over $250++ for a meal here. No, you can't judge because you dropped $500++ to see your beloved sports team/favorite singer/ first class ticket to somewhere.

I'll be coming back.

Admire their food detail, exceptional creativity and service. They truly are special place. It is definitely the most exquisite meal I have had. The variety is endless. The staff is the most knowledge nice and helpful ever. They even used a heated steel thongs to open a wine as the old day. I do enjoy every course but not all of them are necessary 5 stars. 
The most let down was "the best duck" being mediocre and on the dry side.
The best was cucumber soda, before and after cookies, the apple salad/soup and chocolate pretzel from Mast brothers was AWESOME.
So-so courses are the over cooked asparagus, dry duck, cute but not too exciting beer pretzel picnic, oyster(the condiments were too overpowering and can't Taste the oyster)

Getting a reservation is a hassle! but the upside of that is the PEOPLE WATCHING!! Lovely couples,  darling love!! Young girl with rich guys! so fun to watch especially the ones with extravagant dresses!

But i don't want to go back again. By the time the 10th course came, my lower back hurts. Sitting 3 hours for a dinner is not my style. I appreciate the artistry but it is not for me.
Did I mentioned they have the best staff? yes they are awesome!!

I've never had such wonderful experience before (money speaks, of course).

The servers were all so polite and happy and seems so knowledgable about everything, even though some waitress came across as a bit intimidating (hot chef alert)!

I don't even know where to start.

The food was of course amazing and indescribable. What caught my attention was that the spoons and plates they use are all carefully designed. Caviar was served pearl spoon and it was just so beautiful.

Even though I came here by myself and I feel kinda lonely eating alone, this was the best experience I've ever had. :)

You can read a more comprehensive review from my friend here:

http://www.yelp.com/biz/eleven-madison-park-new-york#hrid:Ak_nlfUIYoIVKGa19dlajw

It is everything you would expect from a 3-star Michelin restaurant; the service was impeccable and elaborate. For their dishes, you are encouraged to focus on your senses, but there were some hits and some misses. For that reason, I have to take out one star. 

Highlights:
- Their Malt dessrt was the single best thing I've ever had, HANDS DOWN. 
- I absolutely love love loved (!!) their take home breakfast granola. Thankfully, they provided us with their recipe.

They really set the bar for other fine dining restaurants. Eleven Madison Park is definitely an entertaining & unique dining experience. What else can I say that hasn't already been said about this fantastic restaurant?!

Check it out if you can!

We went there when I was nearly 9 months pregnant as our "last nice dinner before having baby" and it was wonderful.  They were very accommodating in providing substitutes for things I couldn't have like shellfish and alcohol.

Service was amazing.  Some things were a bit gimmicky, but it was still amazing food, and a fun experience.

I mean. 

I just. 

Without going into too much detail, because really, how necessary is that when there are over a thousand positive reviews for a place, this was, without a doubt, one of the most epic meals of my entire life. 

And I do not use the word 'epic' lightly. 

From start to finish, we were well tended to, the food was mind-blowing, we were sufficiently entertained by our waiter, I mean, all of it was fantastic. 

But here are my favorites parts:

When one of my dinner dates decided to drink the green strawberry pickle juice, and our waiter noticed that we all seemed to be wild with the idea of drinking pickle juice, and so brought out three pickle back (double) shots immediately afterward. 

When I was so full of questions that I was given an EMP notepad and pen so that I could write them all down. And then taken into the kitchen to ask the chef face to face.

Our extra course of gin shaved ice in the kitchen. 

When we told the chef how much we liked the rhubarb puree that came with our duck, and he showed back up with individual jars of it for us to take home with us.

The bottle of snaps that was discreetly left on our table, that turned us from the best guests of the night, to the most obnoxiously drunk guests of the night, in a period of about 35 minutes. 

THE TEA. You guys! ORDER THE TEA. The production involved in ordering tea is absolutely worth every penny we spent on it. Holy moly. 

When one of my dinner dates quizzed our waiter on the stats of his previous visit to EMP, and how our waiter knew everything he ate, including food aversions, by heart. 

The homemade EMP muesli I had on my yogurt every morning for a week afterward (with my rhubarb puree!), essentially reliving my experience long after walking out the door. 

Absolutely worthy of its three Michelin stars, and if not for being totally different from Noma (which is equally as epic for totally different reasons), should arguably be the best restaurant in the world.

I just held a small wedding and reception in their private rooms. The food was fantastic and the service was excellent. I only docked a star for the not cueing the recorded music properly during the processional AND the recessional.

Kristen, the private events manager was extremely cooperative and helpful as well.

From the moment you step in the door you are swept into this amazing dining experience.   The maître d' gets your name and walks you to your table without having to look at a book or computer. From then on there's snappy service: water is poured, menus are handed out and your waiter comes and takes your order. My meal was prix-fixed, with a choice of 4 different flavors that they would incorporate into the courses throughout the night. 

Every course was fantastic and modern, playing on simple dishes like a Waldorf Salad, while playing homage to NY's pastrami sandwich, and black & white cookie. Pacing for the meal was good enough for a conversation between the dinner party. With the win pairing, the meal timed to about 4 hours.

I'm sad to say that Daniel Humm, himself, came out to check on the dining room and he gave me a nod acknowledgement. I regret not going up to him and shaking his hand in fear of him finding it rude to shake the hand of some punk 26 year who doesn't know squat about food. All in all, I had a great time at EMP and will remember it as one of my best meals to for the rest of my life.

I don't think much needs to be said. Top notch location, service, and food. Very much enjoyed the 4 hour dinner. The kitchen tour at then end was a great bonus. 

They are they gold standard. Period. 

Would definitely return.

By far the best meal I have ever had.  The service, the ambiance, the food, all adds up to a once in a lifetime dining experience.  

When we first arrived, the bell captain comes to our table to introduce himself.  He tells us that he heard we came to NY to sight-see, so he presents us with 2 tickets to the Empire State Building compliments of the restaurant.  

That is not all, they have a packet with information on top sight-seeing things to do in NY.  There is directions using the cab, by car, or by subway.  After that, they present us with 2 homemade granola bottles filled with nuts, fruits, etc.  They tell me it is for my mother.  I am like, WOW!

Now the food is also spectacular.  I don't want to ruin it for anyone.  But every dish was extraordinary.  The food was delicious and it was presented in a way that made our mouths water.  The colors, the ingredients, the plating was all top shelf! 

We definitely will go back again!

This delightful restaurant has one and only one thing over every other 3-star: it's fun. The food is absurdly expensive. The wine is out of reach except for millionaires and billionaires. But oh what theatre! Each course (what, 20?) is served with perfect and brief little stories, and of course with the élan of presentation only a starred cuisine can master. The staff are bright, friendly without being cloying, and happy.

If noma is #1 (which it deservedly is in my mind), Eleven Madison Park is certainly not #4 (on the San Pellegrino World's Best Restaurants list). I can easily think of a handful of restaurants whose food tastes better, chefs are more inventive, and waitstaffs are more attentive. 

When you're sick, don't come into work. Assuming the food is actually as good as people claim it is, that's the only reason I can think of that would explain why approximately half of the dishes I had were too salty. But the more logical explanation is that the food just isn't that good.

Aside from the little flourishes in presentation (the Waldorf salad made in front of you, the soda accompanying the sandwich, the picnic basket), the menu itself is not very inventive. On paper, it's the pretty common fine dining technique of cooking standard dishes with small twists in preparation or ingredients. That can be great so long as executed well; unfortunately, Eleven Madison is more flash than substance.

The menu is still sticking to the general concept they introduced in 2012 of taking you through a tour of New York-area culinary tradition. Unfortunately, even when made with unusual or atypical ingredients, most of the dishes don't taste too much different than traditional dishes. For example, the first and last "courses" of the meal were sets of cookies. Both sets were plays on the traditional black and white cookie. The first was savory using cheddar cheese and apple, which tasted just like a cheese cracker with cheese filling. The last was sweet using chocolate and mint, which tasted just like a mint Milano. Both cookies were just standard cookies using better ingredients. Neither cookie was elevated or transformed beyond its supermarket brethren. This sense of good but ordinary pervaded the entire meal.

Even if all the dishes had come out at the right level of saltiness, the meal would still pale compared to other "world-class" restaurants. Service was also not flawless as one would expect. For example, I was offered additional bread and minutes passed by without more bread; instead, another server came by to ask if we wanted more bread. On another occasion, my napkin was removed for replacement with a new one when I went to the bathroom, but the napkin was nowhere to be found when I returned and was given to me only after I sat down. Minor issues, to be sure, but not what one would expect or accept at a restaurant of its supposed caliber. The 3 stars EMP received from Michelin is just evidence of how inflated the North American Michelin guides are compared to their counterparts across the world. On both food and service, EMP is no better than a high one to a low two on the Michelin scale.

Yes, it's expensive, but my meal yesterday was the best dining experience I've had in my life. The service was beyond perfect. I'm always worried that an upscale place such as this will have snobby waitstaff. Scott, our server, was fantastic: charming, knowledgeable, and funny. The sommelier came over to speak about the wine list and wine pairing option. He didn't treat us any differently when we turned down the $145 option and was extremely helpful when we said we wanted to go with cocktails, even if it wasn't on the menu. My husband had a refreshing Pimm's Cup that wasn't on the menu. Our meal took 3.25 hours. There was such thought and care in the composition and beautiful presentation of each course, down to the plates and bowls used. We were made to feel absolutely welcome and cared for while we were there. My cousin told Scott she wanted to get her sweater from a checked bag and he offered her a pashmina (which they had in different colors so you can coordinate with your outfit). I would love to go back again and experience EMP in the fall or winter, once my wallet recovers from this visit!

you come for the show and service rather than to be wowed by the food. It's the best service and story time you'll ever receive. 

Tips: when they ask you which foie gras you'd like, choose the one that's more like sweet breads rather than the mousse. Their home made granola as a parting gift is addictive like crack. Their baked alaska is pretty phenom.

Best restaurant in NYC.  Everything was just amazing, I don't think I even need to go into details.  You just need to get a reservation and go there to experience it for yourself.  I was impressed that I immediately bought their book and it's still one of my favorite coffee table books I have to date.   My ideal day in NYC would be: a mild fall day, bike ride around Central Park, lunch at Joes Shanghai, dinner at EMP, and finish of with a musical on Broadway.   I will have to re-create that again in the near future :)

This is by far the best dining experience I have had world over. From start to finish we were treated like a king and queen and every course kept building on the next like a carefully composed  symphony. I have been twice and cant wait to return. It is worth every penny.

Honestly, I can't say anything more about this place that hasn't already been said. The staff really is super attentive and they make huge efforts to make you feel special. I came with Brian M. in the middle of a snow storm and wore rain boots on the walk there and had to change into heels in the restaurant's foyer. Thank you EMP hostess for not making fun of me or making me feel like a total moron. They kept wishing us a happy anniversary the whole night and I swear they must have googled Brian because they remember he worked in the same building as EMP. 

We've both been to our fair share of Michelin restaurants in NYC and EMP is definitely in the top three. The amount of work the staff puts into explaining the dishes and the time they take to lay out the silverware in between each new dish is extraordinary. I accidentally moved my fork and someone immediately came over to put it back into its proper place. I kid you not! This may all sound super uppity, but the earnestness of the staff makes it feel completely casual in a way. I never once felt uncomfortable even though I'm sure I was sitting close to some crazy high roller on a date who kept ordering bottle after bottle of wine. 

At the end of the night, they gave us Mast Brothers chocolate covered pretzels to take home. I devoured mine right away and attempted to steal Brian M.'s as well. Before we left, our waiter came by with a box full of the chocolate covered pretzels for us to take home. Amazing! I put those bad boys in the freezer when I got home and had one before bed with a glass of milk and dreamed sweet dreams of the 14-course menu.

Good pretentious food to impress business associates or for personal events like anniversaries, etc.  It amazes me that places like this still exist, but I'm glad because I have a place to take my insatiable mother for her birthday.

Everyone should visit this restaurant at least once! There is no menu, at least not until it is time to go home. The tasting menu is innovative and fresh, making you focus on the flavours and the occasion. We were not disappointed. We ate things that perhaps we won't eat again, but the fun with which this menu is presented is well and truly outside the box, providing us with many happy tales to tell friends about our experience there.

It isn't cheap and it isn't for the faint hearted, but the welcome and food make this an experience you can dine out on for many months to come! Brilliant.

I came here during December and was able to grab the last seat for lunch as I called in a month ahead. The meal lasted for about 4 hours for the tasting menu, but it sure didn`t  feel that long.

I would say that this was probably the most delicious tasting menu I`ve had. Not all the dishes blew me away, but the majority of them did. Throughout the course the dishes had interaction, discovery, a sense of wonder, and just fun to play with and eat.

number one in the U.S, and number 4 in the world.

if you think your taste buds are too good for this place, you're out of your mind.

Granted some didn't shine as bright as others, others that did were incredibly bright. And in the end, everything was surreal and overall a dining experience rather than a meal. 

Can't describe the whole experience in words even if I tried. It's a hefty amount for extremely well prepared food (I'm not saying it's entirely worth it, because I'm currently broke). Definitely for a special occasion.

Let me preface this review by saying I'm a vegetarian (who eats eggs) and my fiance doesn't eat shellfish.  We did the tasting menu with wine pairing.

We've been to quite a few Michelin rated restaurants including most of the big ones in NYC and this was far and away our favorite.

One thing to really note about EMP is that it's "cool".  What I mean by that is it doesn't feel as stuffy as many other expensive restaurants do.  It's a beautiful atmosphere and you're made to feel comfortable throughout the entire dinner.  

The wine pairing was also the best I've had.  They give you full glasses but I wouldn't suggest finishing each glass.  I made that mistake in the beginning and could barely drink that last few (i know, i know... rookie mistake).  One thing to note is that many restaurants don't do custom wines for the vegetarian meal- they just pour the same wines as the standard menu calls for.  EMP, however, did an excellent job pairing different wines for my lighter plates.

The food, as you've probably heard, was perfect.  It changes often so I'm sure it'll be different by the time you go but just trust them- you'll love it as much as we did!

Was there several months ago for dinner.  Loved the duck and the "apple snow" thing. Everything else was just okay. The restaurant itself was very beautiful though, would probably go there again for lunch.

Their complimentary cereal for you to take home was pretty tasty!

This place is amazing. My family and went when we were in NY and we loved everything! This has probably one of the best tasting menus I've ever experienced. It was interactive, informative, creative, and ever course was literally better than the last! The constant reinterpretation of ingredients was smart and surprising. Before the courses were introduced, we had to select an ingredient by punching it out of small piece of card stock paper. I selected maple so this ingredient was incorporated throughout my individual tasting menu. One course involved a picnic basket where we had to unpack all of the ingredients which I thought was brilliant and really added to the interactive flair of the experience.  One of my favorite events was the flight of butters! The most glorious and flaky little croissant roles were served with three types of butters 1) butter with farro 2) butter with bacon fat 3) regular butter. I love butter in life so this was a real treat for me! There are too many lovely courses to write about individually but I'll wrap up by saying that this was one of the best dinning experiences I've had in a while. I go to Michelin rated restaurants about once a quarter and what makes Elleven Madison stand out is the level of involvement and surprise in addition to the how informative the staff was about what was being served. Not only were the dishes described, but I left with knowledge about the ingredients and how they were interpreted and incorporated. Fantastic place and I will be back!  As with Michelin star restaurants, the service was fantastic! Get there!

#1700 Review - specially reserved for Eleven Madison Park

Eleven Madison Park is one of the best restaurants that I've even been to and well deserving of its Michelin 3-star rating.  The dinner wins "most creative", original, and even whimsical presentation.  The food was unbelievable with every course being 5 stars.
+ Cheddar savory black and white cookie with apple
+ Oyster baked potato ice cream and caviar
+ Morel custard with main sea trout roe
+ English peas warmed with meyer lemon and egg yolk
+ Beef pastrami with ramps, rye, mustard, and strawberry
+ Foie gras cured with orange-chamomile, white asparagus, and bitter almond
+ Apple waldorf salad with celery, rhubarb, and walnuts
+ Lobster poached with beets, ginger, and nasturtium
+ Asparagus braised with potato and black truffle
+ Duck broth with cured duck and watercress, roasted rhubarb, shallots, and scallions
+ Fresh cheese, pretzel, parsley, and strawberries
+ Whey sorbet with caramelized milk and milk foam
+ Almond baked Alaska with rum, caramel, and strawberry
+ Pretzel chocolate covered with sea salt
+ Chocolate sweet black and white cookie with mint

This restaurant!!!!!!!! O M G!!!!!!!!!!!!!! 

I don't even know where to begin.  If you are thinking of going to Eleven Madison, stop. Just go and stop the thinking part!!!  This place is crazy good!

Let me start by saying that my wife and I decided to go on a culinary experience like no other while. We dined at Le Bernardin, Per Se, Marea and ABC KItchen to name a few.  This was my favorite together with Per Se and it was not easy choosing from this list!

The location:  Dreamy!  Do you ever wonder what a restaurant would look like if it was built inside an old bank? Wonder no more.  Absolutely, drop dead, GORGEOUS! High ceilings, gorgeous floors, big windows... so much character!

The Menu: A talking point itself.  It was a white piece of paper consisting of 16 single words, all arranged in 4 columns and 4 rows.  The concept?  Each of those words was either describing the main ingredient of what you were ordering or the general concept of the dish.  So, your order, in essence, is 4 words like... milk, lobster, chocolate, and lime.  NOTE: They do ask you if you are allergic to anything or if there's anything you absolutely won't eat.  Otherwise, you have to leave the Chef alone to do his thing. (NOTE: I believe they have recently changed their menu to a more traditional look)

The Experience: Sick!!! In a good way.  In an awesome way!!! The 4 course menu ended up being much more than that with all the little surprises along the way.  The egg amuse bouche was to die for.  A second amuse bouche, a black and white cookie, was... wait, what's this? A sweet black and white cookie before dinner? Really? Surprise! Even though it looked exactly like a white and black cookie, it didn't taste anything like.  It was salty. It was, phenomenal! I just cannot express how unbelievably awesome this restaurant is.  It seemed like every plate was accompanied by a little extra. A gift from the Chef!  

The Service: Exceptional with a capital "E".  Did I mention that they iron every tablecloth at the table before setting it up?  Not a single crease! Details!!!

As for wine, we purchased a bottle of Heitz for $90.00 which is an amazing price for a NY restaurant of this level.

I dined here in Summer 2008 with my sister. It was late afternoon / early evening, so the restaurant was actually completely empty until near the end of our meal. Between courses, my sister needed to step out for 10 minutes, and one of the waitstaff come over to my table to chat with me so I wouldn't have so sit alone in silence (this was also before I had a smart phone). It's been 6 years, and I've dined at many expensive, foodie-touted restaurants (and a few Michelin rated restaurants) around New York and the US, Europe, and Asia, and this one service experience at Eleven Madison Park may still be my favorite.

The food is also delicious.
I went for rest-week. The whole restaurant looks fancy and up class. I order the skirt wing, one of my best lunch choices.

"A 3 Michelin Star and World's Top 50 Best Restaurant (#4, 2014). Great service and comfortable seating. Food are definitely excellent and surprisingly unexpected. Make sure to make reservations months ahead"
The best meal I've ever had - everything = amazing!  Better than NOMA in my opinion.  It's been ~2years and we still talk about their mini clambake!

I came here several years ago when it first opened for Restaurant Week and it still remains one of the best meals I ever ate.  I remember it was the first time I had beef cheeks and they were phenomenal. It is so great to see this place and Daniel Humm getting all the praise they deserve.

I help pay for my son's wedding reception at Madison 11. We had 50 guests at @#150/head. This was the worst restaurant that I have eaten at in 40 years of dining. The Novelle cuisine was served very slowly and took 4 hours to serve 5 tables of 10. The food was extremely poor and was so minimal that I wish I eat at the Shake Shack in Madison Park before the "gourmet" meal. They gave 5 pieces of small appetizers about a square inch each and had absolutely no taste. The faugra tasted life i was made out of butter. The fish about 2 inch by 1 inch by .5 inches had absolutely no tasted.  The beef was better but again was minimal at 2 inch by 3 inch 1 inch. I had to ask for bread 4 times with little success and was told that it would be served at the "right" meal segment and this was after 2 hours of drinking. The wine selection was mediocre. 

The worst thing was the attitude of the major  dee who prevented us to meeting our guests in the restaurant foyer. He was so arrogant that I was tempted to cutting him into small pieces. He would not allow us to stay at the bar or go to our private room before the reception started. He refused us permission to use flash photography in the private room because it the flash would "upset" their other guests in the main eating area. When he couldn't control the flash photography, he had the blinds closed. He prevented my family from taking pictures and insisted in taking pictures in the park rather than the restaurant. I have been to this restaurant 4 times with my family when Danny Myer's first opened it and it was great. This experience will prevent me in going back. 

I would have cancelled my check if I could.

was looking forward to an exquisite dinner with an amazing tasting menu...out of the 16 courses maybe 2 were really good. i felt more like i was at a tourist attraction  like Carnegie Deli...the waiters perform as thouh they are actors on a broadway show. Whatever you were doing before this NYC experience you need to go back to that..for the money you expect perfection....and we did not experience that. I was there with an executive chef as well as a country club restaurant manager and neither was impressed...we should have gone to le bernadin instead

They spilled water on my wife, twice.  On one of those occasions the glass slipped and shattered on the table.  

You might be wondering, how does a Michelin-rated restaurant overcome drenching its patrons.  The answer is simple, they made it right without me ever having to say a word.  We were taken on a tour of the kitchen and made a stupendous cocktail by a very sweet chef while we watched the cooks work their magic.  On top of this, the restaurant completely comped our meal, including our pre-diner cocktail and our wine pairing.  Going even further, the restaurant refused to run my credit card so that I could leave gratuity for the wait staff, saying that they would take care of it themselves.  I felt guilty about this, and luckily I had enough cash on me to leave a full tip!

Ignoring the restaurant's experimental "day in the rainforest" course, the food and atmosphere were excellent.  Rather than repeat the many other complimentary reviews below, I'll simply add that I view EMP as a strong recommend to anyone that doesn't mind sitting in the splash zone at Seaworld :-D

Full 16 course tasting is HUGE--do not eat anything all day if you want to be able to get through the meal not feeling sick.  They don't allow you to take leftovers home.  Glass of wine or otherwise is $30+ each.

Plating felt gimmicky--much was useless, though great for pictures or even video.  Only 30% of the courses were tasty/amazing--others were mediocre.  Bread and smoked sturgeon dishes were fantastic.  Menu changes seasonally.  They will accommodate for allergies or dislikes, however they substitute things like uni for radishes, so from a cost/value-perspective, I recommend passing on substitutions.

Don't be startled when the waiters stalk you on your way back from the restroom to pull out your chair.

Dress code is business casual at least.  Guys might feel more comfortable with a jacket.  Cocktail dresses for ladies is standard.

Good for an experience, but you'll get a tastier meal and less pretentious service for a more reasonable price elsewhere (degustation, Jean George, etc).  If you're intent on eating here, a better option would be the smaller tasting menus that are also available at the bar.

First time I came to Eleven Mad was for my birthday. I forget which birthday, but I recall the dinner - it was phenomenal! They "only" had 1 Michelin star then. Over the years they have added two more stars, but lost the midas touch somewhat. It's now more on the gimmicky side. Food is great, but not stunning. Ingredients are great but flavors are not amazing-amazing. Service is spotless and all in it is still pretty great. But not WOW anymore.

One line summary - technically superb, but lacks soul.

What a meal!

Simply one of the best meals I have had in the world...and I have been to some of the best restaurants in France, Italy, Hong Kong.

Service was amazing, but not high pressured.  There was no rush to complete our meal..I think or meal was 4.5 hours.

Be prepared for wallet impact but it is a meal to be remembered.

Not bad, but sort of gimmicky, with dishes based on NY delis, picnic baskets, baked Alaska, pig bladders being carried around the dining room, etc.

The best dishes were the duck, the mushroom custard, and the asparagus. Good wine list.  Nothing really to complain about for other courses, but the presentation was not particularly special and the combinations of flavors not very inspired.  Service was fine, a bit rushed at times and too long a wait before other courses.

While I'm glad I tried it, once was enough.

My friend who frequents NYC recommended this place. Due to short notice, we were only able to get a lunch reservation. I had a reservation for 2, and last minute, I called to see if I could add a 3rd; they were more than happy to accommodate.

The immaculate service is noticeable as soon as you walk in the door. We were sharp to our reservation and were seated promptly. My friend gave me the evil eye because I didn't have a blazer on.... I was a bit concerned because of it cause he made it seem like a big deal... I mean, if I'm going to spend this much money on lunch, I'm going to be comfortable doing so!

After looking at their menu, we decided to each have the chief's selection, an 8-course meal. We were warned it would be a 3-hour experience.... 3 hours... for lunch... OK! 

The meals were all little portions, and were amazing. The sommelier came to the table right about when our first course came out and recommended a couple different bottles of wine that complimented the Chef's selection, we went with whatever he recommended, which was a dry Riesling. Perfect choice for the 3 of us, for lunch. 

After each course, there was a nice lady who removed the finished plates, and silverware. She was kinda tucked away somewhere, but was always watching us somehow. It was very impressive how attentive she was. Once, I looked her way, and she walked right over to me and asked me if i needed anything. I told her, I was just getting up to use the restroom, and she pulled the table away from me to give me more room to get up (its the little things that do it for me, the attention to detail). 

My friends told me they came and cleaned up my messy side of the table while I was gone, replaced silverware and gave me a clean knee cloth. 

About 5 courses in, a gentleman came up to us and asked how our meal was. I thought to myself, "OMG, hes going to say something about me not wearing a blazer, or maybe I did something improper" This was not the case. He said, if we were interested,  the chef would like to invite us to the kitchen and show us how things work. We all looked at each other and I answered, "hell yeah!..., oh, i mean, "that would be splendid."

We proceed to the kitchen, and I swear, everyone in the restaurant was looking at us like we were some VIP. Nope, just little-old-me (maybe they were appalled that I wasn't wearing a blazer ;P). We went to the back, and was introduced to the Chef who just thanked us for coming and some other inspirational words before he darted off to get ready for the dinner rush, To tell you the truth, I cant exactly remember was he said cause I was too busy looking for my jaw on the floor. We were on a pedestal while the sue-chef made an edible cocktail for us, and told us about all the stations and how the kitchen works, and how it differs from a lot of restaurants. He then let us ask him questions about day to day operations and their inspiration, etc. The edible cocktail was made with liquid nitrogen, right in front of us. It was awesome!

By the time we get back to our table, all the cloth was changed out, and our next course was served. One of the meals was foie gras. I remember taking a few bites and just couldn't finish the dish. My friends LOVED it. My pallet is just not that refined, especially coming from a state which outlaws it. The lady again came to me, and asked me, "was this not to your liking?" I giggled. 

After all the delicious food, my friend (being a big diva and all) asks for french pressed ice coffee... Our waiter said they had regular coffee they could put over ice, but he'll see what he can do. I kid you not, they flew to Africa and got the beans, but in 15 minutes, they had french pressed iced coffee that we all enjoyed.

I think we left there exactly 3 hours after we sat down. The bill wasn't THAT expensive for the AMAZING experience we had, around $500 including tip, with a bottle of wine for a party of 3. 

I would love to go here again and try out other items on the menu. Great experience.

Daniel Humm is without a doubt one of the most talented chefs in America. Unfortunately, the goal of his team was to make a restaurant that would be ranked number one in the world by San Pellegrino. What has resulted is a restaurant with astounding technical prowess and a unique point-of-view, but, alas, one that caters to tourists and that, while entertaining, leaves the customer with zero desire to ever return, having seen the "the show" before. In short, it lacks soul.

However, anyone who is into food needs to go once.

Yeah, this place is great.  We were able to obtain our dinner reservation for 830 on a Saturday night.  I'll agree with others that despite the fame and the 3 stars, the service is fairly relaxed.  They are able to walk that line of making you comfortable, yet still important.  The dining room is open, airy and of course, properly lit.  Prior to dinner, I knew I wouldn't get the wine pairing so I started with a beverage off the Manhattan Cart. A guy pulls his little cart up and you have a choice of 5 or 6 different types of Manhattans.  Man.. it was perfect. Dinner is 13 or 14 courses.. I lost track and does take 3.5 hours.  I love my GF, but am glad we went with friends who we hadn't seen in a long time.  We chatted the night away as each course was presented to us.  They made it a point to give the locally sourced products props during the presentation.  Food was perfect. No crazy molecular gastronomy, just expertly prepared food with abundant flavor.  A couple memorable dishes- the asparagus sous-vide in a pigs bladder and the dry aged duck with peppercorn honey.. amazing.  I was sad when they didn't give us the entire duck.  I asked a server what they did with the rest and his reply  "oh, we sit in back, eat the leftovers and drink beer" I chuckled and called him a bastard, but it was nice that the staff can still provide excellent service while still being "human"

The food, coupled with the service made it a great experience.  IMHO, better than Per Se, Gramercy Tavern, Inn at Little Washington ,Robuchon.

As a total money-restrained, teenage tourist in New York City I found myself forced to attend a dinner reservation made by an eager friend - where else other than New York's finest restaurant. Eleven.

Upon arrival I was dressed so badly - confused wearing the most elegant (not) dress in my suitcase paired with platform boots. Lets say I did not fit in. We were greeted and treated like kings however, I felt like Blair from Gossip Girl livin' the life in New York!!

We had the degustation, and boy were there a lot of dishes. I was more into super sized big mac meals at the time and did not appreciate the stunning presentation and rarity of each ingredient put into each dish - which drove me to make my next move of creating a sad face with the left overs of one of my dishes. As the waiter took the dish away he came back moments later and questioned me about my artistic display on my previous plate. I told him the truth - I just wasn't into the fancy food and would have rather spent all this money on 100 cheeseburgers.

The head chef proceeded to come out and within moments my friends and I found ourselves in the kitchen of Eleven! We were given a tour of where and how the food was made and the chef designed a menu to suit my taste buds for the night. It was amazing!! The amount of effort and passion put into making guests happy and comfortable at Eleven is astounding!

I wish I wasn't such a grotty teenager at the time and appreciated the food - but hey, I got an awesome experience out of it! :)

What hasn't already been said. I will just say this, I came here for lunch and it is a good alternative as they serve the same meal. It was surprisingly more 'playful' than I thought it would be (picnic dish, carrot dish,  apple brandy, showing the duck) and maybe it was because it was during the day, it felt much more inviting and less formal than some of the other places up there with this restaurant. The duck dish was the absolute standout and service is what you would expect from one of the best restaurants on the planet.

This is a special occasion restaurant (you were just promoted and got a big fat raise and have an extra 500 bucks burning a hole in your wallet), but it's wonderful.  This is also what I call a restaurant that's good for exploring new foods.  There are items on the menu I would never think of eating and every time i eaten here, I've tried something new (on someone else's dime), I've been blown away.  They even give a take-home gift. It's unforgettable.  This is a place to go when you want to impress someone special in your life.

Elegance meets grace and class with a dazzling and unforgettable delicious multi-course dinner.  This unpretentious top restaurant ascended immediately to my number one restaurant in the city. It is by far my favorite so far of all the ones I've tried which have been many.  The staff is young, friendly, knowledgeable, professional, and makes you feel important no matter who you are.  They honored our request to be seated at the corner table, which I felt was very telling of the kind of people they have working there. Unlike all the other four top restaurants in the city, this one makes you feel like you're wanted, appreciated, and a true guest at their establishment. Each course of the tasting menu was cooked to perfection, with a perfect combination of flavors, and of course a presentation to die for. My favorites were the lavender duck and the fois gras. And mind you, I am someone who is ethically against fois gras because of the force-feeding of ducks. Still, I couldn't resist it.  When we first arrived we were asked if we had any food intolerances, allergies or anything that we didn't eat. I don't eat pork, and I am intolerant to salmon, and they honored that fully. We actually got to meet the chefs and see the kitchen, and got a special dessert/drink treat over there. It was amazing! The drinks are fabulous as well, I had a really good jalapeño infused drink that was the best drink I had in my life. The wine sommelier also knew everything that we needed him to know about wine, and hooked me up with the perfect oakie full-bodied Chardonnay the brought forth the flavor of my dish.  The only part that I felt fell short and was not as great as everything else was the dessert, but with dishes as perfect as they set themselves up I think.  I would've loved some chocolate, but there wasn't any.  They do a New York theme for their dishes, and New York being the Big Apple the dessert fell into that theme. I just absolutely love everything about this place, including the granola they gave us to take home.  I love it so much I plan on making many appearances, including one very shortly for the Kentucky Derby event they're having over there.

Eleven Madison Park is more than a restaurant.  It is the ultimate culinary EXPERIENCE which takes you on an incredible journey of flavors, ingredients, presentation, & service.  This is a bucket list restaurant.  This is a once in a lifetime restaurant.  This is the epitome of a meal experience.  THIS is why we eat.

My Overall Rating - 5 Stars (Atmosphere, Service, Food, Return)

Atmosphere - Eleven Madison Park is a beautiful & elegant restaurant.  The main dining room is in a large hall, with beautiful flower centerpieces in the middle surrounded by white cloths and custom place setting.  The crowds consist of you share of couples, groups, business diners, and New York's elite.  It's a place where you feel weird (almost embarrassed) to take out your phone to snap photos.  It's upscale, classy, and everyone is dressed accordingly.  1 Star.

Service - As soon as we walked in and gave them our name, they said "Happy Anniversary" and proceeded to give us the most amazing service.  We began by choosing a flavor (strawberry for her & coffee for me).  These flavors would resonate later mysteriously in one of our courses.  It was fun, mysterious, & exciting! Each of the 15 courses has an introduction & explanation - culinary stories if you will.  After each course our table was cleared and all items reset.  There is an army of servers with specific tasks with a head captain leading the way.  1 star.

Food - You don't dine at Eleven Madison Park.  You EXPERIENCE it.  It's so hard to explain as I've never had a meal like this.  This is fine dining that combines an inventive menu with unique ingredients, textures, & cooking techniques that you've only heard or read about.  Our meal included items such as savory cookies to start, potato chip crème fresh, coffee cola, pastrami, poached lobster, & more.  To attempt to describe the dish would be an injustice to the actual experience.  The meal ends with sweet cookies, a custom menu, a full belly, and an evening you will never forget.  Make time though - the dinner lasts about 3 hours.  2 Stars.

Will I Return? - Yes (if I win the lottery).  Normally I would say no because this experience comes at a very lofty price; however, it's a place you go to experience the grand possibilities that can be created by food.  In all likelihood I will probably not make it back, but it doesn't mean I don't want too.  You may not like everything on your menu, but no doubt you'll be talking about your experience for years. 1 Star.

My Yelp Rating Scale (Sum of all parts):
1 Star - Atmosphere - Is it a cool dive?  Perhaps an upscale place?  No matter the type, atmosphere plays a big part and I'll give a star if I like it or thinks it has great charm.
1 Star - Service - You can have a great meal with bad service.  But that's also what can make a five star joint drop to four.  It's important to the dining experience that service is great and on point.
2 Stars - Food - I'll award up to two stars for the food, since this is the main reason we dine out.  Sometimes the extra star is given for value, but it's really all about the food.
1 Star - Will I come back? - If I know for a fact I'll return, I'll give this a star. A place has to make an impression for me to return. 

Each Category can be given up to 1 star except food (2 stars) because I consider all these categories important to the overall dining experience.  I will sum them up to provide my final Yelp score.

My experience here was amazing. From the food to the service, and the unique way the dishes were presented. 

When two creeps kept staring at us during our meal they happily moved us to another table out of their view. 

I don't want to spoil the experience, but its worth every penny

Thank you, Eleven Madison Park, for allowing us to have a little bit of fun while we enjoy this exquisite dining experience.

The 3 Michelin Star restaurant is located adjacent to Madison Square Park where you walk inside to a grand setting that practically shouts old school New York City feel. You literally feel like you are in a high end restaurant straight out of New York 1930s. 

The staff warmly welcomes you as you pass diners that have mysterious soda bottles on their table alongside....pastrami sandwiches??? I didn't know 3 Michelin Star Restaurants have pastrami sandwiches on their list of dishes!

As soon as you sit down, the staff gives you a punch card with four flavors - ours at the time was fennel, cranberry, maple and apple (I'm seeing on other reviews that they change frequently). From here on out, we knew we were in for an adventure (it ended up being a flavoring for our soda as well as a special dish later in the meal).

Our wine pairing wasn't that great but maybe it was just an off night. 

It turned into a 3.5 hour experience that we enjoyed to the fullest.

Nearly every one of the many courses had a creative twist to it, and I can't recommend this place enough. You really do have a fun time at a place like this, totally eliminating any pretentiousness or stuffiness. This is definitely my favorite 3 Michelin Star restaurant in New York (Chef's Table follows by just a little bit). 

Can't wait to come back here soon.

From the minute we walked in, we felt like we stepped into a harmonious past era.  Service is perfect and classic, people are well dressed, and everyone is passionate about their mission.  This is fine dining at its apex.  The level of service is unprecedented, and the spirit of Relais Chateaux is fully evident.  Without repeating others or giving away the surprises, this is a foodie's dream -- creative food and amazing wine (go with the wine pairing).  We were blown away, plain and simple.  In a word: amazing.

It's my duty to show & tell, yelp peeps, especially when I happen upon a dining experience as intriguing as Eleven Madison Park's. Read no further if you want your 3-hour dinner to remain a mystery; just know that it is worth the 3 hours of your life (so very few events are.)

Things you should know: 
1) no menu (until at the very end when they hand one to you, along with a mason jar of granola for tomorrow's breakfast.) If you're dining here, it's for the $225 16-course to-do. 
2) menu is somewhat customized to fit your preference. For instance, I instructed NO caviar, foie gras, oysters, organ meat, and no meat other than chicken or beef. Beef & seafood must be cooked all the way through. Even though my waitress was thinking, "WTF, Crazy?!," the chef happily obliged & I was thrilled with my menu.
3) the restaurant focuses on 4 major flavors each season (ours was celery, coffee, strawberry, & cherry.) You're given a card & asked to pick one flavor you'd like to see showcased. I chose coffee so I got coffee-flavored soda & coffee flavors in my baked Alaska dessert. He chose cherry.

Absolute most favorite parts of dinner:
1) one course was a picnic basket. We "unpacked" the contents, complete with checkered napkin & ceramic "paper" plates, & had a picnic in the middle of the fabulous restaurant.
2) another course focused on waldorf salad. apple was grated tableside. after eating the salad, we were instructed to lift the top portion of the bowl, revealing a soup consisting of waldorf salad ingredients. So many surprises!
3) from the very first course -- a box to be unwrapped -- we knew we were in for a fun, whimsical evening. 

So this is what it's like to have your culinary dreams come to life...

Okay, it was 3.5 hr dinner. We had the 4.7.14 rsvp. From entrance of the restaurant to leaving it was very interesting and so much food. Staffs were friendly and attentive. Awesome food . Love the little creative ideas on how foods were served. Our stomach was bulging half way through the meal. We hit food coma and revived for the next. It is a must try.

Had an amazing meal here back in December. Every bite of the savory dishes were delicious. Unfortunately, the dessert courses were not as great, which is why I am giving 4 stars, instead of 5. A friend of mine came here a few weeks afterwards and felt the same. Hopefully by now, they have improved on that and I will look forward to it the next time I go. The savory dishes alone still make it a worthwhile trip.

The only sentence I can write this time about this place "you get what you pay for". The food looks phenomenal, service is excellent.Food taste was allright for white table cloth restaurant ( if u know what I mean). The wait staff have lots of  knowledge  about food and wine. This is what I meant,  Bravo!  Definitely we will come back there soon.

Very elegant dining experience.

Service is impeccable and although they try to be friendly, it was a bit rigid.

Problem I had was the food. 

I'm rating as 3 stars for the experience, but the food wasn't to my liking. Perhaps its a bit too contemporary for my taste buds but I can't recall a dish that I liked. There were a few bad dishes: 

1. A serving that appeared to be a Pork broth, which they told us to sip like tea. My wife and I couldn't keep it down. 

2. Celery root dishes\foams\yuzus - very strong taste of celery overpowering most of the dish. Never had celery root that overpowering, last time I had a similar dish at Le Bernadin, and comparably, this was too much.

3. Pastrami - there was play of NY Deli style sandwich in a bite with Pastrami... however it had me comparing it to Katz Deli, and wasn't up to par. This is understandable considering Katz specializes in Pastrami, however creating a mental link that isn't a great idea in my opinion.

4. Overall dishes had very bitter/sour notes which others may like, but wasn't to my taste buds.

Definitely an experience, but won't be going back.

PS - Forgot to mention but after the dinner, they gave us a souvenir jar with granola which is amazing... Been savoring it for awhile. That's the best tasting serving from eleven madison...

I have been wanting to go to EMP since around 5 years ago but I couldn't get a reservation the two times I tried. Was very happy to finally get a reservation!

The service is impeccable. It seemed a little uptight at first but the food is so fun and creative that it brings out the lighter side in everyone working there.

Really enjoyed the cocktails there and they of course have a great wine selection.

I haven't been so entertained at a fine dining restaurant since a couple of years ago when I had dinner at Aronia de Takazawa in Akasaka, Japan. The concept of each course is brilliant and I especially enjoyed the cheese course. I won't write too much about these because I'm sure you want to be surprised if it's your first time going there.

The food is beautifully presented and cooked, though I prefer more simple flavors so there were some courses that I didn't exactly like that much.

Yes, it's pricey... but I would definitely recommend EMP for special occasions. I was thoroughly impressed with the service and creativity of the food and can say without hesitation that they would rank in the top three for service in New York. I love how they pay attention to every little detail and are consistently watching out for the customer's every move. 

I probably won't be returning any time soon because of the steep price tag, but I'd definitely go eat a la carte at their bar some time.

Keep in mind that I rate places based on the category it's in... I pretty much have nothing bad to say about EMP but it wasn't one of my favorite high end meals in terms of flavors... 

http://umamidiary.com/

I got to say that this place is pretty freaking good.  However, I felt like a country bumpkin coming here because I don't usually go to fancy restaurants.  My husband had made reservations for lunch here while we were visiting New York City.  I had no clue about this place before he took me here.  

Initially, I was hesitant about coming to Eleven Madison Park because I nearly fainted seeing how expensive the prices were here.  I am not going to lie, I'm pretty cheap and love a good deal. Oh well, I rationalized in my head, go big or go home right?  

When we arrived, I noticed that I saw this restaurant in a Sex and the City episode when Big broke the news that he was engaged to Carrie.  Being a SATC fan, I began to be thrilled.  My husband teased that the only reason I liked the restaurant was because of my enthusiasm for SATC.  Since we were celebrating our anniversary, the restaurant was so sweet to print out a little card congratulating us.  They gave us two delicious cookies in a box.  I really liked the truffle cookie.  Anyways, we ordered the prix fixe meal which was totally decadent and delicious.  They even offered to take us into the kitchen to see how food was prepared.  THIS WAS ABSOLUTELY MY HIGHLIGHT because I love educational experiences.

The waitress was really nice.  I had to ask her what some of the things translated to because some of the words were in French.  I told her that I wanted to avoid any organ/tissue type of protein. She chuckled at me in a nice way.  I felt really like a country bumpkin.  Haha

When the bill came, I nearly had a heart attack.  It was $500 buck.  OMG Do you know how my 99 cent cheese burgers I would get for that amount?  Even though I'm very cheap and love good deals, I have to admit that this place is very classy and offers you a five star experience.

I have made it a rule not to review restaurants where I am an invited guest.  Today I am making an exception.  Eleven Madison Park, at the southern end of the Original Madison Square Garden, is the perfect location for a New American but truly international dining establishment.  This is truly one of the best restaurants in both New York, and the country!  I have always said that it is about the food, but let me say it starts here with the atmosphere and service which is unmatched in NYC.  I love the spacious tables and the old school space worthy of Commodore Cornelius Vanderbilt himself!

This is a perfect restaurant for a romantic rendezvous or a marriage proposal.    The caviar appetizer was exquisite, and the warm salad with mushrooms, pine nut, and kale combined a wonderful presentation with a medley of fresh, rustic flavors.  My main course of roasted beef with root vegetables and black truffle was truly memorable.  It was perfectly seared retaining its flavor and cutting perfectly.  The dessert was very flavorful and subtle: Tart Tatin with Hibiscus Caramel and Creme Fraiche Ice Cream worthy of Paris, France.  Eleven Madison Park is truly a special place worthy of the Annals of Madison Square Garden!  It was a perfect place for  me to connect/reconnect with many other Double Hoyas!  If you are looking for a classy but friendly location this is the place!

Best dining experience of my life. 

However the celery root dish did not appeal to me. 

Their take on the NYC deli beef with rye was nothing short of spectacular.

The duck was fantastic... I almost didn't want to finish. 

Sort of felt sad as I donned my jacket and walked out into the blustery February night...

Second time I've had the pleasure to dine here, and lunch proved to be just as spectacular as dinner. The service staff is professional and friendly, my sister and I had a lot of fun joking with them between courses. The food, of course, is consistently excellent and delightful. Playful is easily the most accurate word to describe the food and atmosphere at EMP. 

I have nothing more to say - everything is transcendent, and the restaurant continues to be more than worthy of it's starred rating. Can't wait to come back.

I'll start off by saying that many of my friends absolutely love this restaurant and come here quite frequently, but my own experience here was not as great as I would have liked. Here is the breakdown:

- Service: Service here is great - staff was friendly and professional. Everything you'd expect from a restaurant of this style/tier
- Ambiance: Great ambiance - loved the lighting, roomy feel, everything. Very comfortable space and well laid out dining room
- Food: It really came down to the quality of the food. I had recently dined at Atera, which was probably my best dining experience ever. In comparison, EMP food seemed like it lacked texture, and flavors were just overpowering in every dish. Everything was either TOO salty, TOO sour, TOO rich, etc. Based on all the amazing reviews that this place gets, I chalk it up to having a different palate than most people. I tend to prefer more subtle flavors and interesting textures (a la Atera, in my opinion/experience). I can definitely see how those who prefer bolder/stronger taste would enjoy this place, but it was not for me.

I thought about giving this 4 stars, but it just didn't feel right. For the amount that I paid for this meal, I really didn't enjoy enough. It's definitely a restaurant worth visiting at least once in your life, and more if it's to your taste.

I'd recommend it, but I myself wouldn't return unless the menu changed drastically.
The food and the service are absolutely amazing! Every bite was delicious! It is definitely a great experience!

Absolutely exceptional in every way.  It's an experience of a lifetime, one I hope to repeat again.  From the moment you step in the door the service is warm, friendly, and gracious.  Over 15 amazing courses, some of which are creative and great fun.  4 hours and lots of wine later, they gave me a wonderful tour of the kitchen, where they made me a special dessert (dessert number 5).  A memorable experience.

If you enjoy fine dining then you must go here (remember they only take bookings 28 days in advance). The degustation was amazing and you will not be disappointed.  
Service was also fantastic and they certainly know how to make sure you are always with water, service and food of course.

So I've been to few really nice places in my long old life..u know...the 3 michelin stars, pellegrino list, and the whatnots.  And I've been trying cut down on being a so called 'foodie' and just trying to focus on cheap tasty grub.  Because for me, it seems once u done all the fancy schmancy mole schmol gas mash, it just all pretty much the same same.  And also, I need to save money for my retirement.  You cannot cash out a 16 course meal when you turn 65.  Even if you could, you won't get that much of a return on that investment. 

But my girl wanted to go for her birthday and that's how I keep her around.  Sad but true.   And it's this sadness that drives me to stuff my face.  Anyways, I really didn't have high expectations.  Thought it be excellent food but just all the same.  Well 16 courses and wine parings later,  EMP really surprised me.  I won't give away the details but it was a fun playful meal...of course until i saw the bill.   

Excellent service and very welcoming environment.   Overall it was a pleasant surprise and a great experience. And this is despite my girl and I having a big fight on the super most ridiculous thing halfway during dinner.  Well its what we do during birthdays.  We fight like little kids.  Cheap way to make us feel young again.

ps. had the best manhattan in the city yet

You're in New York for a few days in the middle of a backpacking trip, you're after your first Michelin starred restaurant, you want a transcendent dining experience and you know that one waiter side-eyeing your wrinkled dress that's been shoved at the bottom of a pack for two weeks will send you off the deep end. WHAT DO YOU DO?
You head down to 11 Madison Park because you've heard of how warm the service is compared to similar restaurants and reap the rewards. 
The food was amazing, of course, but in this review I have to gush about the service. Every staff member I encountered was bright and attentive. No one batted an eye at a lone 21 year old in hiking boots enthusiastically asking questions, tucking in to the chef's tasting menu, and furiously taking notes. 
This place runs like a well oiled machine, but is far from stuffy. I've never felt so relaxed and absolutely enchanted in any other restaurant.

Absolutely amazing.  Do yourself a favor and treat yourself to a meal at EMP.  SUCH an enjoyable experience.  First and foremost the food is delicious, yes it is whimsical, and fun, and surprising, and impressive, but it also TASTES AMAZING!  

The service is unbelievable, the staff is one step ahead of you, anticipating your needs and providing everything from information about your meal to a piece of bread at exactly the right time, all without a hit of being intrusive.  Everyone who works there seems not only knowledgeable but as though they are enjoying themselves as much as you are!

It was more than just a meal, it was an absolutely amazing experience.  I could (and I have been) talking for days about the amazing food - the cured foie gras, the savory and sweet black and white cookies, the pork consomme, the bone marrow!! - but really you should just go and experience the creativity and magic for yourself.  You will be smiling for days!
Beautiful decor and well prepared dishes. Not cheap but was one the best places I've dined in manhattan. Well worth the trip

I can't complain I think the food was very great but some of the dishes were huge misses. I had some weird carrot salad that tasted like dirt-- you basically had to assemble the whole thing yourself. I also wish I had known that some of the dishes come with cocktails as I found the flavors to be super conflicted as I was drinking a rasberry/gin concoction and then beer with a pretzel!  My reservation was a bit late for dinner-- 9:30, I didn't realize that we'd be sitting for so many hours. Towards the end I kept thinking please god no more little plates because I was so full. They play this really funny card trick too-- of course I got my favorite thing and my bf was the same. It was magical!
One of the most amazing dining experiences I've had in my life.  The food was creative, fun, and delicious.  The service was absolutely superb.

I think people are over-complicating things a bit.

This place serves delicious food. If you can afford it, you should definitely come here. Celebration? This is the place (if you can get a table).

Dont overthink it guys.
