I threw my husband a surprise party here. We reserved the North Room, which overlooks the main dining room. Kristen, the primary planner, was unbelievable with helping me plan the event - making sure the staff knew it was a surprise, allowing us to make the room our own for the evening. The service was so precise and the waitstaff was very accommodating. 

I would comment more on the food but I was so busy talking to guests at the party that I barely got a chance to eat! We had the 6 course pre fixe. My favorite courses were the fois gras and the dessert course, which was a take on cheesecake with fruit. Normally I dislike cheesecake but this was no ordinary cake. It was so smooth and not at all bitter. Pairing it with fruit and a small pastry made it incredible. 

I wish I could have this type of experience every day. Would recommend this place to anyone, especially if you want to throw a party.

Thoroughly enjoyed my experience here.  
Now when I say experience, this really was an experience.. like an interactive/hands on meal.  I came with my boyfriend and had an amazing time, but this would be equally as fun with friends as well.  I want to take everyone here!

The restaurant was easy to find, and I was surprised to find that the dining room was relatively bright for dinner and was wonderfully comfortable.  The servers are young, informative and very attentive in a friendly manner.  I loved the service and vibe here.  Relaxed while maintaining a certain elegance.  The crowd was also really assorted ranging anywhere from business people, couples to groups of friends.  Everyone seemed to be light spirited, laughing and having a good time!

When seated, we were given an envelope and a letter opener and upon being opened, there were two cards with punch outs of 4 different flavors: Fennel, Cranberry, Maple, and Apple.  We were each told to punch out the flavor that appealed to us most, and our own menu tastings would be adjusted to reflect these flavorings.  So we picked Apple and Maple.

Not going to list out everything that appeared on our tasting, but a few notable favorites of mine was the rye bread and mini grill of pastrami that appeared at our table, the table side prepared waldorf salad, the foie gras slices,  the picnic basket, the pork broth with cheese crackers, pork prepared three ways and the table side baked alaska.  I am a little disappointed that the flavors that we picked made an appearance only three times in our 16 course tasting... but the tasting menu was delicious nonetheless.  

At the end of the meal, we were sent home with a delicious jar of house made granola.  If you ever have the time, I'd definitely make EMP a place to visit in NYC at least once in your lifetime.  Worth every penny.

Beautiful experience. We came here to celebrate a big birthday of mine. The week before I had my doubts, should we really spend all this money on a meal?  But my husband persuaded me to go ahead and I am glad he did.

The service was beautiful, attentive without being intrusive. The food was exceptional.  We loved all the courses except for one. We merely "liked" that one. Some of the things that were amazing: savory black and white cookies, the marinated scallop, the pastrami with bone marrow, the waldorf salad, the pretzel with onion and dried fruit.  We got the wine pairings (of course!) and spent 4 hours in this gorgeous restaurant indulging ourselves. 

We left a little tipsy but not drunk and satisfied but not stuffed. The granola that we took home was incredible: sweet, salty, crunchy, chewy.................. An amazing place. Go if you can and just let the whole experience wash over you.

Wow, what an extraordinary dining experience. I came here with two skeptical, picky eaters and left with two more believers.  The service was attentive and warm, without even a slight rolling of the eyes as we each listed off what we don't eat.  The food was as delicious as you would expect, but the surprise was in the creativity of each course. It was like dinner and a show!

I can't wait to go back!

We came here for a "milestone" birthday!  16 courses, service was on point, felt like a well orchestrated production. Everything you hear about Eleven Madison Park is true. It is a meal that everyone should experience at some point in their lives! New York City fine dining at its finest!

I always have a great experience here, whether it be dinner or brunch.

You definitely have to try their brunch.  Especially their chocolate croissants.  They are just so scrumptious with the perfect amount of butter, crisp and flakiness.

For an upscale restaurant, they are rather friendly.  Every meal is worth every penny.

I have now had TWO bad experiences with the service at this restaurant (not with the food).  First was when I dined there a couple of years ago -- food was great but service was terrible.  They poured ALL THREE bottles of wine I ordered at once (and all before a drop of food arrived), appetizer wasn't served until almost 2 hours after we arrived, waiter gave me an argument when I asked if the dessert had milk chocolate or dark chocolate (the menu said milk, but it turned out to be dark), etc. etc.  All this and I spent almost $3K for 5 people.  Now ANOTHER bad experience with the service -- member of my party of 2 had the flu this morning and I needed to reschedule (I did not cancel, I rescheduled), they charged my AMEX card $250.  Not plausible that they can't fill the reservation, they have a waiting list.  Will NEVER go back there -- attitude is terrible, no other fine restaurant in NYC behaves this way.  No matter how good the food is, bad service not worth it, ruins the experience.

One of the best dining I have ever had. From start to finish, the service was fantastic (wait staff were quick and unpretentious) and the food was delightful (twists on classics using local ingredients). The entire dining experience is just so much fun but I will not give too many details since the surprise is half of the fun. We also appreciated the extras - serving specialty drinks with certain courses (and having a good non-alcoholic alternative for me) and the take home breakfast gift. This is definitely somewhere for a special occasion.

As a foodie who greatly enjoys eating and talking in great detail about my dining experiences, I often get asked the question - "So, what's your favorite restaurant in New York?" It's SO hard to pick just one, especially when it depends on so many different factors - mood, budget, cuisine, etc. 

EMP was definitely my favorite high-end restaurant in the city when I ate there the first time. I had the 4 course menu a few years ago and had a delightful experience. My boyfriend surprised me on my birthday this year with reservations for their new tasting menu, and I'm happy to say I had another unforgettable evening.  My second experience was equally as charming and fun, shared with excellent company ;)

Upon being seated, we were presented "flavor passports" where we selected a flavor to incorporate into our courses. I picked apple while the boyfriend went with maple. 

We chose the pork over the duck for our main course. I'm not going to lie, I always have reservations about restaurants cooking pork right. EMP did not disappoint. Our pork was cooked a variety of different ways and every bite was ever-so-tender. The pork lay in a broth with morcilla sausages and gruyere, roasted with cabbage, coco beans, and almonds. 

Other highlights of the meal included:

- Lobster poached with razor clam, sea urchin, and kale - the lobster meat was cooked perfectly and paired well with the other flavors of the sea

- Greensward with pretzel, onion, and dried fruit - this came packaged in a whimsical picnic basket that we then unwrapped and set up. I really like the makeshift picnic idea.

- Scallop marinated with apple, pine, and water chestnut - the apple sorbet was delicate and refreshing, pairing well with the scallop

- Celery root braised with black truffle - I would eat celery all the time if it tasted like this

- Beef tartare with caviar and smoked bone marrow, pastrami with pickles, rye, mustard, and apple - While the delicate square of pastrami was delicious, I think I prefer my pastrami in healthy, thick portions from Katz's or Carnegie Deli.

I love when servers prepare food table-side. One of the servers put together a delicious Waldorf Salad with apple, celery, cranberries, and walnuts. 

They also gave us "gift boxes" to unwrap throughout the meal. The first box contained cheddar cookies (savory and sweet) and the final box contained chocolate cookies (sweet). While great in concept, the cookies failed to delight.

I was also disappointed with the Baked Alaska with rum, raisin, and apple. The rum cream overpowered the dessert and it tasted too alcoholic for my taste. My boyfriend liked it though.

Service was top notch. The servers were very observant and timed the cleanup and serving of subsequent courses very well. Even though we didn't have any alcohol, we still ended up spending over 3 hours at the restaurant. We got the full immersive experience and even received a tour of the kitchen (just call in advance to arrange - they're very accommodating!)  

We wrapped up the meal with chocolate-covered pretzels and a box of peanut butter jelly chocolate. I was happy that they still gave out jars of granola to take home at the end of the meal - still think this is the best home-made granola I've ever had!

My boyfriend had one final surprise for me at the end. Our waitress came out with an Eleven Madison Park cookbook, signed by Daniel Humm, the head chef! Now I can make these fancy dishes in the comfort of my own kitchen :)
 
If Yelp offered half stars, I would give EMP a 4.5. The experience was unforgettable, but some of the courses were just OK. I still highly recommend this restaurant for a special occasion.

Great service.  Presentation was good. Experience was great.  However, I thought they failed on the proteins (there were only two - maine lobster was good but not exceptional.  I actually expected them not to use Maine lobster because imo it's nothing compared to the spinies both in flavor and texture, it's cheaper and eh, it's okay.  expected more.  Challans aged duck was tough + lukewarm).  

What was good about this meal is the way they bring out an ingredient, get you to think about it, and then say hey this will be the next course.  Then, when you eat the ingredient, your mind says hey, i seen that ingredient so your mind is constantly working backwards and forwards to give you an artificial sense of time/experience/space...whatever it is.

Wine service was an issue.  
I brought a 1990 Chateau Margaux & a 2007 scarecrow, which they decanted for us.  Unbelievable wines, but, they left 20% of the wine still inside the bottle.  It was not an issue that there was sediment.  I think that often sommeliers leave wine in the bottle so they can take it and drink it later.  Sorry, not gonna happen here.

At the end, they came by to bring a bottle of their house made apple brandy for us to drink and (so we did) and what I really liked was they say: here's our apple brandy. feel free to stay as long as you'd like.

That was sweet, but strictly on the food for a top 10 restaurant in the world I thought it was okay.

What a night!  The service was first class from the time we walked in the door until we left.  The staff was friendly and attentive without being pretentious.  Corwin Kilvert, the Sommelier, was wonderful throughout the evening as was the entire staff.  A very warm experience.

The food experience was first class.  I loved the fact that many of the courses had a theme to them.  It made for a wonderful experience.  Well balanced and a nice variety of flavors.  Our only disappointment was dessert!  We were expecting a big finish and felt a little let down.  No matter, we will be back!!!  Well done!!!

5 stars for stellar service and presentation, but about 3.5 stars for the food. 

I had been looking forward to coming to EMP for the longest time but could never justify the price tag. Then finally as a surprise my bf took me here for our anniversary. 

It's taken me a long time to write this review because of mixed feelings between my expectations and reality. Out of the 16 courses I have to say less than half really made an impression on me, however the ones that did really knocked it out of the park like the seared foie gras, the little neck clam set up which was so innovative and unique, the tomato confit with lobster salad. 

I was disappointed by the duck because I heard such great things. I felt it was a bit undercooked and the fennel didn't go well with the flavors. 

All in all, the meal was like a journey and a theatrical show which I appreciated immensely. I wish they would change the menu back to the old grid style, I would definitely give it another try!

Not even close to worth the money or time. Seriously. Can't figure out what everyone is raving about. Three Michelin stars, how? Their talent is apparently duping a lot of people into believing they serve up something unusual or special. I can understand if you don't eat out a lot but most of the people who I have heard rave, do and do so in NYC where there is a long list of places that are better to eat and well worth the money.  The food is fine, some of it even good but it is hard to understand why it needs to cost so much.  And this is from someone who has happily spent more on meals.  The "entertainment" portion including picking your preferred flavor from a punch card of four flavors so they could incorporate it during your meal (a flavor which figured in all of 3 times throughout the meal, one of those in the granola you are given to take home) and having a musty old cookbook dropped on your table and then listening to the story of the waldorf salad while it it prepared tableside was disruptive and trite and the picnic basket was just silly and not even particularly tasty. The service was lovely if a tad annoying at times.  I won't be going back until they change their format and if I can save a few people from spending the money, I will rest easier. Shame on the professional reviewers who have fallen for I don't even know what.  This place should have been skewered by the food critics of NYC.

I had eaten at EMP a couple years ago right before the menu change and I knew that EMP should be the meal that should be our finale dinner for the trip. And I was right. The experience that EMP offers is unable to be topped by anywhere in New York and the meal was one that I will remember for a long time. The greeting we received as we entered to the service throughout made us feel special and as if we were the only table at the restaurant that night. Everything is precise, but you don't notice it being "mechanical".

The new menu is very fun. Every dish is a mystery and a surprise. Every dish has multiple elements that come together and make the meal about the whole experience, not just the food. Normally I would expect the gimmicks to negatively affect the food, but here, they are confident enough about the food to be able to be more creative with the presentation.

It's been two days and we're still talking about the the oyster course and the "bone marrow" course. The oyster with the vichyssoise and the caviar was so good I could have eaten two dozen of them. The "bone marrow" with beef tartar and caviar hidden inside was fun and delicious. We chose the duck as our entree for the table and the duck breast had the most amazing spice rub. It was so aromatic and went so well with the flavor of the duck. I also really enjoyed the picnic basket as I had no idea what to expect.

The service at EMP is unparalleled. My fried is a beer drinker and they had the beer expert come chat with him. We ordered coffee without being offered a table-side presentation and, when my friend asked about that, they set up a table-side Chemex brew for the entire table. The server told us all about the coffee we would be drinking and the intricacies about brewing with Chemex. Since we showed interest in the Chemex, she also provided us with official brewing instructions from Chemex and when she learned we were from California, she recommended a few roasters in our area that she liked. Finally, I had requested a kitchen tour and the Maitre D'came to introduce himself near the end of our meal to let us know to expect the tour as we finish the meal. There is a table set up in the kitchen for this reason and one of the chefs comes over to create a frozen cocktail for you. The cocktail is made and you eat it while in the kitchen, so there is plenty of time to observe the kitchen at work and to ask questions. In case you were wondering, there are 37 people in the kitchen and another 35 people in the dining room. A total of 72 staff members for a restaurant that hits 80 diners maximum at any one time.

Not much to say. Hostess was super friendly. Our super was very knowledgable. We never had to ask for water. The food was amazing.  Our waitor recommended a great bottle of wine    Their drink selection was perfect. The dessert was to die for.

Looking for a 3-Michelin Star evening on our special NYC weekend, we thought ahead to make rezzies at Eleven Madison Park.  They only had a 10pm slot available but since we were flying in from SF that afternoon, it was really 7pm in our timezone, so we grabbed it!  And due to our 10pm rezzie, we were also able to fit in a Play beforehand - worked out so well, all around!!

As we arrived, the place was still hopping at 10pm.  We left around 1:30am & weren't even the last ones there!

Vegetarian Tasting Menu was on the docket!!  We found these cards on our table w/ 4 different "tastes" for you to choose your preference - our evening had Apple, Cranberry, Maple, or Fennel.  We both chose Maple as our preferred "flavor" & were off to the races!

Started w/ a glassie of champers - Cremmant for the Mr which he liked very well & a Pinot variety for me that was a bit sweet & delightful

Asked the sommelier to recommend a bottle to go w/ our tasting menu & he recommended a lovely 1994 white burgandy

Started w/ a B&W Cookie w apple chutney.  The cookie had cheddar in it & it provided a fantastic mix of sweet & savory

Pears w walnut powder & balsamic dollop - this was tart & refreshing

Apples & horseradish w/ apple snow - extremely inventive - the "snow" provided a sweetness that was countered by the spicy horseradish - lovely

Mushroom sabayon w/ chives oil & diced mushrooms served in egg shell - very rich & creamy

Toasted shittake mushroom w/ peanut potatoes & quail egg, everything bagel w/ pickles & cucumber cream cheese on toast - getting into more of the savory, spiced part of our meal, this was heaven.....plus, it was paired w/ this wonderful homemade maple soda!

Sunchoke salad w/ crispy sunchoke & a buttermilk vinaigrette foam

Waldorf salad - This was prepared at the table from scratch - apple, celery root, lemon, mayo, candied walnuts, cranberries.  Loved their interpretation!

Under the bowl was another hidden/surprise bowl of crispy grains & yogurt - 2nd version of salad that was more like an apple-granola cereal w/ a yogurt dollop in the hidden spoon

Parsnip crunch; parsnip pana cotta w black radish; parsnip w/ horseradish 

Parsnips w quinoa & mushrooms - I really liked the nuttiness of the quinoa w/ the earthiness of the mushrooms

Celery root ball w/ celery root purée & black truffle jus - you add truffle jus to anything & I'm going to be a fan!

Freekah broth w/ a rye crisp & gruyere, pickles, mustard seeds - can't say I've ever had freekha before but I liked it - a nice nutty grain that was also tender & like a barley

Freekah Risotto w/ a crispy something on top & black sesame purée

Picnic basket w/ runny cow cheese that we could have bathed in it was so good, plus a fruit & nut cake & a sweet onion jam - paired w/ their homemade wheat pale ale.  I'm usually a pale ale hater but I absolutely loved this one 

Then onto desserts, we started w/ a Sweet Potato w/ orange sorbet & espresso crisps - loved the combo of sweet potato & orange

Baked Alaska served w/ an entire bottle of St Georges Apple Brandy so we could enjoy as much as we wanted.....but 1 glass was more than enough for us

By this time, we absolutely had to cry uncle - we literally could not fit in even 1 more bite so we took home the following:

Chocolate Dipped Pretzels w/ white chocolate crumbles INSIDE the pretzel!

Another B&W Cookie but this time is was sweet w/ a filling I cannot remember except for the fact it tasted a bit caramelly

Homemade Granola for the next morning - it was crunchy & a bit caramelly & chocked full of fruit.  Divine!

Overall, even though we arrived at 10pm & had a constant stream of food coming in, we did not feel too rushed - might want to go for an earlier rezzie next time just to pace ourselves a bit better.  Regardless, we thoroughly enjoyed the experience to the fullest - would totally come again!

TOTAL for the evening:
2 People
18 Courses
2 Champers; 1 Bottle Wine
3.5 hrs
$950 (including tip)
Just amazing. Just too much food. Just the tables are a little too close. Just strange to be siting in parallel to your couple (instead of one in front of the other). Just so much GREAT food

This was probably the most astonishing dining experience that I've ever had. We came to NYC for my 30th birthday, and it was my choice to come here vs Per Se. It was the correct choice. Not only was the food amazing, but we were treated like VIPs, we shown to the kitchen and happened upon the brilliant Daniel Humm. Dinner? No, an eating experience. Highly recommend this place.

Lots of hype, I'd venture to say too much.  Regardless, its difficult to believe this is the #5 restaurant in the world. 

The service and sommelier: phenomenal. The space:  impersonal and without character.  The Food: varied drastically from dish to dish.  Some of the tasting menu items were great, while others were mediocre.  The meal took nearly 5 hours, and it was simpler dishes (like the basket of cheeses / soft pretzel / mustard / fois gras / exclusively commissioned Ithaca Beer Co.'s Picnic Basket brew) that my table preferred over the highly engineered attempts to be creative. Fois Gras, beef tartare with caviar and bone marrow, and the duck (main dish) were all notably delicious.  The lobster and razor clam, as well as the baked alaska dishes were notably unimpressive.  The plating and presentation was flawless across all courses.  

Overall: an undoubtedly solid meal and certainly a unique dining experience, I am glad I had the opportunity to eat there. Taking into consideration the critical acclaim, 3 Michelin star status, and sea of fervent Yelp reviewers, EMP gets 2.5 stars.  I'd expected more.

Incredible service and experience start to finish.  The entire staff was extremely friendly and attentive without being pretentious. 

From a technical, execution, and presentation pov, the food was equally as impressive as the service.  The four star review is only because the flavor profiles of the 14 courses felt a bit redundant midway through the menu.  Also, the "surprise" 2nd part to the Waldorf Salad dish was not very good at all. 

Definitely an experience you will not forget. Save up and go.

The only thing I could ever, possibly review negatively here is the cost is a bit much. Everything single other inch of this restaurant has been painstakingly thought out, considered and created to please .

I only went for lunch and I can hardly imagine what a fabulous fancy date spot or impressive celebratory destination this would make. The menu is constantly being updated but everything I had was delicious - so that's what counts.

Everything about this restaurant is exceptional. I respect the presentation and ambience they wish to express to customers. I was a little discouraged prior to arriving at the restaurant as most of the reviews I read stated the food was bland and boring for the price however I completely disagree. In my opinion you have to go to the restaurant with an open mind and understand the chef's goal for your meal here. The flow is wonderful and the meal is like a theatrical experience that crescendos with each dish. Our meal lasted exactly 3 or so hours as stated by other reviews. I liked that because you are paying for a service and experience not just the food here. I recommend the wine pairings as it helps keep the night going smoothly by finishing each drink and chatting between dishes. The service is phenomenal and timeless. Another bonus.. I was cold and they provided me with a scarf to keep warm. Simple gesture but appreciated. Would go back for sure!!

The place is a very tasty Organic restaurant They have a cute lay out where you can eat inside or their outside backyard area.  I enjoy their coffee and I believe they have Wifi connection as well.  

The price is just right and the taste exceeds the expectation.   Will come back to when in the neighborhood.

I'm very sad that I'm giving EMP 2 stars.

My husband and I came here last year. I woke up at 5AM on a Saturday and waited almost an hour on the phone just to make a reservation at EMP. I was so thrilled that I was able to get a table.

Finally, the day has come. I was so excited about coming to this restaurant as I've read many positive reviews on Yelp and people have been raving about it. This was supposed to be an extraordinary culinary experience, right? Both my husband and I didn't feel this way at all. We had 16 courses and out of all the courses, we only liked 3-4 of them. Some tasted the same; it wasn't very exciting. The saddest part was that we didn't even get the WOW feeling for any of the courses. I was extremely disappointed with the desserts. I was hoping they'd have something better than chocolate covered pretzels and some ordinary chocolates.

The only thing we enjoyed about this meal was the presentation of the food and the service we received.

It was unfortunate that we didn't get the same experience as others. Maybe we will give it another try the next time we're in NYC again.

I have been lucky enough to come here twice.  The first time was exceptional and the second time around was just as good.  Fine dining can get boring and routine, even being unique is not so different. But I have to say that eleven madison still had an edge, in addition to the quality of food and impeccable service.  They were able to stand out with the little things that made a meal of this caliber special. 

We we're celebrating my birthday.  We were given a choice between four leaves,  I picked the maple my boyfriend picked the fennel.  From here on, our tasting menus took on subtle nuances of the choice flavor. It was so much fun.  My favorite was the maple and fennel sodas, respectively. 

I gave them four stars because a server poured tap water over our sparkling water.  And I had to point that out.  And then the printout of our menus were reversed.   Since I have a no shell fish/vegetarian restriction, our menus were different.  But they missed that in the printout and reversed our maple and fennel pick. Really, it did not change the quality and artistry of our food.  But these kind of mistakes are obvious and fully noted.

It's probably cliche to rave about Eleven Madison Park, but I'm going to do it anyway.

Dinner at Eleven Madison Park has forever changed my perception of what a meal can be; a transcendent blend of theatrics, culinary perfection, and overwhelming royal service.

The second we entered, the ballet was set in motion.  The greeters knew exactly who we were and escorted us to our tables in a perfect concert of chair pulling and pleasantry.

From there came a few of the first courses, lighter seafood bites that one comes to expect from a fine dining Michelin-starred prix-fixe kind of establishment.  Yes, they were perfect bites of Oyster and shrimp that did their job to excite the palate and get you in the mindset for an experience.  But so what? Every restaurant does that.

At this point I was happy, but I hadn't been fully wowed as I expected to be.  Then, one of the waiters topped off the champagne I had been drinking for the wine pairing, which is something I had certainly never experienced before.  More relaxed and basking in the happy surprise at the free booze recharge, another course came and went.  A sturgeon and foam filled egg shell that hinted at the greatness to come.

By this point, I had emptied my refilled wine glass half way.  Then the waiter came back and pulled out a bottle of smoked porter, which delighted me because who would have expected the next round of the wine pairing to be a pitch black beer?  Right about here is the point where I realized that this dinner had jumped ship and elevated itself to some higher plane of existence.

The waiter took the smoked porter and proceeded to pour it into the half-full champagne glass, creating what he explained was a smoked porter champagne 
cocktail instantaneously at the table.  My mind was sufficiently blown.  All the rules were out the window.

Then came tins of caviar and cream, freshly baked rye crisps, house made dill pickles, and a poached quail egg nestled gently upon what was described as "everything bagel crumbs."  Then they brought out a bell jar filled with smoke and 
unmasked ten perfect slices of smoked sturgeon resting over charcoals.  The sturgeon was the most perfectly smoked object I had ever tasted, a complete embodiment of the flavor of fire.  This course was basically a smorgasbord of New York City in sight, smell, and taste.  This is why we came to New York.

At this point I was completely converted.  Chef Humm could have served a plate of pickled cough drops and I still would have been his culinary slave, doing whatever I could for just one more bite.

Foie Gras here, Foie Gras there, perfectly poached lobster over brussel sprout puree (which I was delighted to discover is a perfect pairing).  There's the carrot tartare they grind tableside and serve with another smorgasbord of condiments to mix in to your heart's delight.  There's the roasted squash stuffed with aromatic herbs that they could just serve to you, but instead they bring it by to cut it open and have you smell it two courses before you eat it, just to get you wet with anticipation (for a vegetable no less!).  Perfectly prepared venison served in a log, also teased several courses in advance.  Every course pounding with theatrical grace.  

For the cheese course, there wasn't just cheese.  There was a picnic basket placed on the table for everyone to discover the treats hidden inside.  Fresh homemade pretzel, local cheese, grapes, home made mustard, complimented by a delicious wheat beer made special in Ithaca.  It was a picnic at the table, after we had already had dinner but before dessert.  I was basically speechless.

Seguing into dessert they make an egg cream drink tableside (and with olive oil!), further compounding that New York experience.  Then several more dessert courses followed, all beautiful and surprising (nothing screams creme brulee like bay leaf).  And, as if it wasn't theatrical enough, the final dessert course was also literally a magic trick (what?!) and they left a bottle of apple brandy for the table to drink at their leisure.  

The whole experience was like a five hour play, with a rhythm and flair for the dramatic.  Except it was far more entertaining (probably because you get to eat).

In retrospect, dinner at Eleven Madison Park  was the highest form of entertainment.  It's hard to imagine many more entertaining ways to spend five hours on a Tuesday evening.  For weeks after this dinner, I would daydream about a different one of the myriad courses all day long, trying to come up with some way to revisit those flavors or surprises.  The best solution I have come up with is to keep eating out and to keep chasing that dragon in search of a better meal somewhere else.  It may be a while.

I think the part of my NYC trip I was looking forward to the most was EMP, and I was not disappointed! I loved that the atmosphere wasn't stuffy like some of it's other 3 michelin star counterparts. The food was simple and delicious and I still daydream about some of the dishes. For me, most notable courses were the seared foie gras and the beef tartare with caviar served in bone marrow. I won't go into too much detail about the overall experience because I want everyone to be pleasantly surprised when they dine there. I pretty much have the worst allergy known to man - shellfish. Yes, I can't eat lobster, shrimp, oysters etc. Usually I'm pretty displeased with the substitutions that I receive, but I loved everything. Instead of the lobster, they gave me sea bass which was buttery and perfectly cooked. I can't wait for my next NYC trip because I'm definitely going back!

If you want an experience, rather than just a meal, then you should consider this place! It's a dining experience that they try to make interactive, I enjoyed it! It felt very luxurious with all the servers there to attend to you, I don't think this sort of experience is for everyone but if you appreciate good food and beverage & you have the time (3-4 hours)/money then check it out! 
The icing: they gave us a take home gift at the end of the meal! 
Tip: ask for drink pairing as the wait staff pair not only wine, but ciders, beers and other types if alcohol you may not ever get to try otherwise.

First of all, if you do this right--cocktails, a couple bottles of wine for a table of 4, you will come away paying $400 per person.  Or more.  This is the price of entry--some people splurge by going to the Super Bowl, and some people go to fancy restaurants.  Your team doesn't always score on every drive, and they may even lose at the end.  But you can still have a fun time and come away happy.  Some people like to sit out in the cold for 5 hours.  I would rather spend that time tucked into a cozy table at 11 Madison Park.

Numerous people have complained (!?) about how long the meal lasted.  Really?  We sat down at 6:15 and got up at 11, and the evening flew by.  Every need was attended to--every one.  We got information when we wanted it, and were left alone when we didn't.  Our head waitress set the tone right from the get-go--easy, relaxed, yet prompt and efficient.  We were 10 minutes ahead of our guests, and we got drinks at the table, then they came, and more drinks were ordered, and then things slowly got rolling.  The four of us have celebrated our birthdays together for many years now, at Le Bernardin, Jean-Georges, Daniel, The Modern, Gramercy Tavern, etc.  The service was the best I've encountered.  Serving what amounted to 18 courses (as two of the 16 courses came in two iterations)--and three variations on the menu, one for someone who ate no meat, one for someone who ate some meat, and one for the two of us who eat anything, is a huge task.  That it all came off seamlessly is something of a miracle.  

Was every dish a home run? No.  Are you obligated to eat every one of the 18 courses?  No.  Can you pass on some that you don't love and still be enchanted by the ones you do?  I hope so.  I loved the baked Alaska in flames on the table, but not so much on my plate.  And then along came an excruciatingly delicious chocolate-covered pretzel.  I have never understood the appeal of black-and-white cookies--but 11 MP's transformation as a savory starter and a sweet meal-ender made me a believer.

And the space--the deco grandeur of the former bank lobby is one of those unique gilded-age relics that survived the wrecking ball.  The decor is appropriately minimalistic, so that the architecture can shine.  

The bottom line, I think, is that for creativity, service and experience, 11 Madison Park deserves its reputation as one of the top restaurants in NYC.

It was supposed to be my foodie dream come true. I waited and waited for a very special occasion to finally come to EMP. After 8 years in the city, it was actually happening. I matched to my dream residency and my fiancé surprised me on the same morning while I was still in tears with the reservation. When he asked me if I wanted to go, I teased him that we needed to make a reservation 28 days in advance and we can't just walk in - he then told me he actually made one while we were still in Canada. Yep I'm marrying this one. 

We were warned to save our belly by friends and were told actual dinner would last up to 4 hrs. We arrived promptly for our reservation and were seated immediately. They then presented us an envelop where we were to select an ingredient to be incorporated in our tasting menu. My fiancé went with maple and I went with cranberry. Then our food journey begin. 

Black/white savory cookie - tasted just like Ritz cheese crackers

Oysters - really bland, lemon and cocktail sauce might actually taste better

Scallop - the apple sorbet was so overpowering, could have put anything under and I wouldn't know what I was eating

Beef - actual bone with stuffed tartare. Tasty but not memorable

Pastrami - made my own open face sandwich, a waste of a course to be honest. Paired with maple and cranberry soda - both screamed diabetes 

Foie gras - our waiter actually forgot that one of us wanted it seared. When my fiancé and I grabbed his attention and asked since our dishes looked exactly the same and we actually didn't know what seared one was supposed to look like - our waiter thought that I was being difficult and changed my mind - he kinda just rambled on how he thought he established that we both wanted cold which wasn't true and just ended the misunderstanding with an extra order of seared foie gras for my fiancé and I to share. He never actually acknowledged his mistake and it seemed our convo was cut short. But I guess I can't complain about free foie gras. Cold foie gras - again really plain and couldn't tell for my life what I was eating. Seared much better - especially when I smother a thick cut of it on top of their house made bread. But it wasn't anything special - Asiate's had this beat hands down

Apple - a bit too sour but made Bleu cheese tasted ok (I hate Bleu cheese)

Lobster - the lobsters were so overcooked. It almost flew out of my plate when I was sawing it

Celery root - 1 of the better dishes of the night and it was the truffle mushroom cream not the celery root itself.

Duck - We chose the duck over the pork for our main course. started us off with duck broth and a cracker with foie gras and cheese. Both a treat! The duck broth had a layer of oil but the taste was light and flavorful. Main dish - Even though I loved the herb seasoning on top of the skin, my duck was cold and the meat was tough. This was supposed to be the star of my tasting? The side cup of foie gras pudding was really rich and flavorful - I enjoyed dipping more bread into it but straight up spooning and eating it would be impossible. 

Greensward - presented in a whimsical picnic basket - sparking cider + fruit cake + onion jam. Not enough pretzel to go with all the pairing. When I asked and waited for a second serving of pretzel, another waiter came by and was ready to clear the table. When he learned that we were waiting for more bread and he seemed really surprised "o really?". Yes I know we are more than half way in in our tasting and I stuffed my face with 6 rolls. But there are 4/5 of the cheese, jam, and fruitcake left and I will eat. 

Sweet potato - should have named this espresso because the taste of the espresso meringue overpower everything else

Baked Alaska - beautiful lighting presentation by the table. They incorporated the maple and cranberry that we chose in the beginning of the tasting by splashing a bit of the maple cream and cranberry sauce onto the dish. The rum cream again overpowered everything else. The maple tasted like a shot of caramel sauce 

Chocolate pretzel + black and white sweet cookies - can probably find these in Walgreen and have handful of them all to myself

Service was acceptable but felt a bit ignored (I had to struggle getting in and out of my seat) perhaps it was because the 3 tables around us all got wine pairing. They gifted us a jar of housemade granola and a box of peanut butter chocolate with a slip of Congratz to go. A nice touch but we saw every table got one. Taste wise - My fiancé and I expected so much more a Michelin 3 stars. Nothing was memorable. There wasn't a moment where I took a bite, my eyes lit up, grabbed my fiancé's hands and said "omg u have to try this". Sad to say but we had better food in the city during Restaurant Week. It was a reservation that I've always dreamed of but only to learned that the dream was much better than reality.

Review is just for drinks

Excellent execution and extraordinary service. Coming here is a fantastic experience and I highly recommend it if you're a group of less than 6. Will be back for dinner!

This is my first time eating here although I have passed it many times.   Eleven Madison Park looks like a beautiful Zen-like restaurant.
 
Our meal began with a white paper box tied up with ribbon. Inside were three black-and-white cookies.  They was absolutely amazing!  The only way I can describe them is by saying they were they were savory, very savory!.

Soon afterwards, we were brought a picnic basket. It was up to us to investigate and discover pretzels, mustard, and a fine cheese.

Then, there was the course above, with minced carrots via a metal grinder clamped to the table, and ten tiny plates meant to be all mixed together, and added to bread.

There was also a chowder served out of a tea kettle., yes a tea kettle...lol.  OMG... All I can say is it was beyond delicious.  

At the end of the meal, our waiter performed for us a card trick. It ended with three cards face-up on the table, reading chocolate, peanut butter, and mint. (Waiter: "These are the ingredients of your last course, and it's already here.") Our plates were then lifted up to reveal second, smaller plates, with these desserts. All I could say was WOW!!!  

At the end of the meal, The same white box as in the beginning. With the same black-and-white cookies inside. Was this in error? No: they tasted totally different. Sweet, as a dessert should.

I cannot wait to go again!!!  If you don't go here you are CRAZY!!!

Atmosphere 5
Decor 5
Food 5
Service 5

This place will always hold a very special place in my heart, because...I got engaged here :) 

So I have been to Alinea, Next, Ing, Moto, Bouley, LeBernadin, French Laundry, etc....so I have been to my fair share of taster menus...my top would be Alinea and Eleven Madison tied...we were later told that they are sister restaurants by the MaitreD...

I am really into molecular gastronomy, so this place was sort of perfect for me. I don't even know how many courses we had...and you don't get a menu when you step in, because they are like they want the courses to be an element of surprise, but they do ask you if you have any allergies...

So things I do remember that really stood out...Not going to go into too much detail, in case you get a similar course, I don't want to ruin your experience...but put your trust in them...they know what they are doing...
Duck main course - this was good, but the portion was a little large for later in the meal
Picnic Basket - this was good, but we were too full for more crabs
The bread - with goat cheese butter...my fiance had like 4 of these...and he was so full at the end
Scallop - cooked to perfection
This carbonated milky cinamony drink...I forgot what they said this was a play on...but it was goooood
Carrot Tar Tar - this was a fun course. It was delicious...interactive 
 The creme brulee Dessert w/ hibiscus sorbet - this is one of my favorite desserts...I was soooo full, but I still devoured this. The creme brulee was very light and creamy, paired with the sharp citrusy hibiscus sorbet, this really blended well, the contrast in texture and taste really brought the best out of both components

We also got these PBJ chocolates and granola to take away...if anybody knows where you can buy the granola...please let me know...I am in love with it..and I do not eat granola...

My fiance said that the restaurant was very accommodating with the proposal and everything. So for one, we got the best seat of the night, the corner seat, where we were able to hold hands all throughout dinner, and sort of had our privacy...at the end of dinner, my fiance had a very concerned look on his looking on his phone, he was like I have to take this call..so he walked out...and then the MaitreD comes over looking all concerned and was like "You have to come with us, your bf needs you"...so I come out with him...and there...to my surprise was not only my bf, but my dad (who I thought was at home in HK) and 2 of my really good friends...I was shocked...They gave us a bottle of apple brandy to celebrate with :)...This apple brandy was very strong :/...Then they brought us to the kitchen and made us a special drink...with frozen chocolate cream on top with I want to say it was pear or apple chunks on the base...I would order this again and again...even though I was soooo full...it was an edible cocktail (the last time I had edible cocktail was at Alinea)...delicious and unique...

In summary, it was a magical night!
Eleven Madison Park is one of my favorite restaurant. I enjoyed the service and the food. Everything was exquisite and coupling the course with wine was the cherry on top.

i met daniel humm and will guidara at the SF JCC last year while they were promoting their new book, and i knew i wanted to eat here.  everyone i know who has been has loved it.  

my dear friend made a reservation for us exactly 28 days before the day we planned to dine here.  she called at 9 am and had to wait a while before being helped, but that's just the way it goes.  

food here was great obviously (but not my fave of all the other fancy restaurants i've been to), but what stands out is the creativity and the experience.  i loved the picnic basket and the carrot tartare (made tableside) courses the best, since they were the most fun.  i also liked the card trick at the end which revealed the flavor of chocolate we got.  

all in all, a fun and special experience.

Returned to EMP, and it was even better than the first time. I didn't think it was possible.

One of the amazing moments of the evening: I mentioned offhand that I hope a local wine shop sells the wine we were drinking. Shortly after, the sommelier returned with a printed list of NYC liquor stores that sell it. Service.

Menu was similar to the first time around, but with a few modifications. Didn't bother me since everything was so, so good. It was deja vu, since we sat at the same table and had a 5:30pm seating both times... and of course, had a wonderful time.

And they served the duck butter again!

Eleven Madison Park was on top of list of restaurants to eat while I was in NYC, 3 michelin star, top 50 restaurants in the world, and we wanted somewhere fancy, so why not book. It took me 3 phone calls to finally get a reservation during the holiday period and on our last night in NYC too. 

The 15 course meal was beautifully presented with stories of where the produce came from and idea behind the dish (evidently it was encompassing all that was New York - whether it was Manhanttan or the greater state). It was an evening of fun and dinner theatre with amazing food.

Why did it lose 2 stars? 

1) we didn't get served the full course of our last dessert - the brandy was missing and all the other tables around us got it.. why were we missed? We didn't say we didn't drink or anything - so what happened there? Inconsistency in serving of meals on the menu that required no change is worrying and should not happen at a 3 michelin star restaurant!

2) The service - our waiter was uninterested in us. There was no pulling out our tables so we can go to the restrooms or pushing of tables back in when we did went - that is shocking - considering the other people around us got proper treatment - and it wasn't that they were busy, they were standing aorund and they saw us... - that again is somewhat unacceptable in an elite restaurant (i can understand it in other places, but when you are one of the TOP FIND DINING PLACES, HAS 3 MICHELIN STARS - service is paramount and flawless. 

I go to eat at fine dining places for the quality of produce, the flavours and the texture of food, along with getting impeccable service, but to pay $250 pp and to have one of our courses incomplete and the service very mediocare due to one bad waiter and unresponsive team of other waiters and staff it actually does ruin a rather lovely meal.

Eleven Madison Park is of course on the top of every New York diners list of must eat restaurants, and this Saturday I was lucky enough to dine there. On Friday I was browsing  Open Table and actually saw a 10 pm reservation available for the following day. So of course I snatched that up as soon as I saw it and prayed that I could convince a friend to spend crazy dough on this dinner. Luckily I was able to find a date with little trouble and we were off.

We were a few minutes early and were able to have a drink at the bar which was a very nice start to the meal. We were seated about 10 minutes after reservation time and the entire staff seemed to be apologizing for it. Once we did sit the 3 1/2 hour meal with wine and beer pairings commenced:. The beverage team was very accommodating and provided great pairings for the $100.00/pp I asked for.

You are asked to pick a flavor profile for the evening, I chose Maple and my partner in crime chose Apple. Cranberry and Fennel were also available. These flavors appeared in several of the dishes throughout.

- Cheddar: savory black and white cookie
- Oyster: Vichyssoise and Caviar
- Scallop: with Apple, Pear, and Water Chestnut
- Beef: Tartare with Caviar and Smoked Bone Marrow/Pastrami with Pickles, Rye, Mustard, and Apple
- Foie Gras: Terrine with Sunchokes and Fermented Mustard Greens
- Apple: Waldorf Salad
- Lobster: with Razor Clam, Sea Urchin, and Kale
- Celery Root: with Black Truffle
- Duck: broth with Sausage and Gruyere/ Roasted with Lavender, Honey, and Rutabaga
- Greensward/Picnic Basket: Pretzel, Onion, Dried Fruit
- Sweet Potato: Curd with Espresso Meringue and Orange Sorbet.
- Vanilla: Baked Alaska
- Pretzel: Chocolate covered with Sea Salt.
- Chocolate: Sweet Black and White Cookie

99% of the food was absolutely incredible. The only dish that neither of us liked was the Lobster, just didn't work. The favorite for both of us was the Celery Root, so flavorful and so simple. There were also a few other extra courses that were thrown in that were not on the menu that we received at the end of the meal.

The table side Waldorf Salad preparation and the flaming Baked Alaska were nice little breaks built into the meal.

The service was stellar but relaxed and comfortable and the environment is open airy and bright.

By the end of the meal I was stuffed (my male dining partner was not) and quite drunk (neither of us could keep up with the wine/beer pairings, at times we had 3 different drinks on the table) then they presented us with the rocket fuel apple brandy. That is clearly what they use to get people out of the restaurant, its impossibly strong and there is no way anyone could have more than a few sips.

Over all this was a wonderful fun exciting dinner. If you have the means (or just say screw it and put down your credit card like I did) it is an experience that you will never forget.

This is truly a wonderful place. The food is stellar, the waitstaff are lovely and the cocktails are clever. It's worth the wait to get a reservation here. If we lived in New York, we would be here as often as our wallets would allow. Each course was creative, explorative and hinted at a larger concept which left us wondering. If the foodie world is accurate in stating "you always want to leave them wanting one more bite" (or something of that nature), then Eleven Madison Park has nailed it.
Plainly amazing! The best meal I've had in NYC! Wrote a complete review with description of the 15 courses

We probably saw you --coming and going--
The 5 hour dinner--our reservation was at 7--the four of us practically closed the restaurant when we were finally freed at midnight--after one bottle of wine and long itermidable waits between courses when wait staff, various dishes, and other customers flowed past us in the theatre that's become EMP.  Something went terribly awry last night and we were the victims--As our friend pointed out, if you divided the minutes we were there by the check, it was probably one of the cheapest meals we've ever had.  We are fans of EMP.  Ate there in its first menu iteration and think it'spossibly  the best restaurant experience in NYC.   None of the food meccas in NY can duplicate the intricacy and creativity of the food, the thought of combining them into a menu, the detail and layout on the plates, the presentation and the ways of engaging the diner.  Even with this 15 course menu (that changes every three months or so) food and the dining experience is planned to engage and enchant--the Waldorf salad served at the table with the original 1895 cookbook, the picnic basket with the house-brewed beers--Here food is theatre and we're audience and actors.  Unlike the worshipful silence of the food meccas in NY like PerSe and Bernadin, where suited men and proper women make hushed murmers of appreciation when food is presented, here a younger, moneyed crowd, in various states of NY chic, almost applauds when a dish lands.  
But something is different, and its not the food, it's the staging and the haphazzard service, with captains that are officious, polite, and indifferent.  Everytime someone staggered off to the restroom and in five hours that happened frequently--wait staff appeared to pull out our chair, fold a napkin--but if we asked what happened between the interim dessert and the baked alaska, suddenly they all disappeared--the baked alaska was presented, flamed and taken away--since I had spent a good deal of time watching the others around us I knew there was an iterim dessert and chocolate pretezels and the black and whites to end the meal--ours didn't appear--45 minutes later--it was now 11:00 p.m.  and are jokes were beginning to have a sadistic twist about cruel parents who made children sit at the table until they ate all their food--and were we really in a hostage situation, and numerous waves to various captains, one who looked right at us and ran down the stairs--it was explained there was an interim dessert--ours would be arriving 
shortly--  We begged for the check, this was a week night after all--packed up the pretzels, goobled down the baked alaska and sprung from our table--left--  Oh, and did I mention the unhelpful waitress who grabbed my wine glass, 1/3 full, off the table after the main course and then said, I thought you were finished?  -We were reduced to watching tables around us who had arrived later and remarking, "They're catching up"   The captain and staff knew we were unhappy and they knew 5 hours was an aberation.  Three hours seems average and that's what we spent the last time we were there.  Nobody apologized.   Last night EMP had acquired a haphazzard, amature quality.  Hate to see the best restaurant and most talented chef in the city falter.  Hope it was just an bad night for them as it was for us.
EMP is a good  restaurant , but Betony 57th it's a different world, trust me its like being home in new and old  A merivan perspective all the way!!!you must try this place !!

i don't understand what all the hype is about. Sure, the place was nice, the service was amazing......but the food left something to be desired. 

The 15 course meal was well presented and each coarse seamed like a present with envelopes, boxes, and picnic baskets that you unpack to reveal well presented cuisine but the flavor of the food did not meet expectations. For the price, you'd expect to be blown away. There were maybe 1 or 2 things that we considered good, a couple of things that were fine..... but nothing that was memorable. 

I would have been much more satisfied going across the street to the shake shack and having a cheeseburger, fries and a shake.

Another stellar dinner tonight at EMP!  Tonight was the first dinner of EMP's new winter menu, and it's a winner--delicious and creative. Service continues to be the best. Dinner starts with a ticket in an envelope with 4 flavors on the ticket: maple, apple, fennel and cranberry; I was asked to "punch out" from the ticket my favorite flavor which was a "no brainier" for me since I love everything maple. I was asked whether I would prefer a cold or hot foie gras preparation; I chose the hot prep. The other choice I had was the main protein: either duck or pork. Since I've enjoyed EMP's duck many times, I decided to try the pork. 

Tonight's menu:

Cheddar: savory black and white cookie with apple
Oyster: vichyssoise and caviar
Scallop: marinated with apple, pine and water chestnut (pine was a crumble on branches that one shakes onto the dish)
Beef: tartare with caviar and smoked bone marrow
Pastrami: with pickles, rye mustard and maple -- served with maple soda (best soda flavor)
Foie gras: seared with sunchokes, hazelnuts and solera vinegar
Apple: Waldorf salad with cranberries and walnuts that is prepared table side 
Lobster: poached with razor clam, sea urchin and kale
Celery root: braised with black truffle
Pork: 3 courses--pork broth with morcilla sausage and gruyere; followed by the tenderest pork loin roasted with cabbage, coco beans and almonds; accompanied with a Pommes purée with pork and foie gras 
Picnic basket: Greensward cheese with warm pretzel, onion jam and dried fruit
Desserts: sweet potato curd with espresso meringue and orange sorbet; vanilla baked Alaska with raisin and maple that is first covered with rum and flambéd tableside and then plated in the kitchen
Chocolate covered pretzel
Sweet black and white cookie with cinnamon
Jar of granola as take home gift. 

Terrific croissant-like rolls served with 2 butters (plain and flavored with pork). 

I've been dining at EMP for many years, and after tonight's menu, plan to continue to dine at EMP for many more years!

Not sure it needs my pile-on review - but it is a fantastic restaurant.  From the drink at the bar before dinner ("of course we have Junipero gin") to the book-end black and white cookies.  Truly spectacular.   For me the best dishes were the carrot tartare and the venison.

Without a doubt, the best meal of my life to date (I've been to many Michelin star restaurants). They really understand how to make you feel comfortable and important without coming off as pretentious. The nice lady greeted us at the door (by name) and took our jackets.

We did the lunch tasting menu. It was absolutely wonderful. I won't give away any surprises, but just know you should expect amazing food with a whimsical twist. Yes, it is a little pricey, but it's an experience that you'll never forget.

5 stars for service and presentation but only 3 for taste so ultimately I have to give EMP 3 stars b/c taste trumps everything for me.  

We went to celebrate my birthday in November.  And although I love the idea of seasonal menu, we weren't blown away.  Yes, the presentation was very cute and with each course we were excited to see what they would do next.  It was kind of like a magic show.  But like a magic show, it's fun to watch but you don't leave thinking wow, that tasted amazing.  Maybe it's bc winter produce and meat isn't that exciting.  The lobster dish was good and we kind of said "wow" but overall we were more disappointed.  Given the price and the rave reviews, we just expected more.  

Maybe this place would have been better if we had gone in the spring or summer.  I think spring/summer produce is better.

This restaurant got it right in so many ways. The tasting menu was exceptional, and the wine selection was great. I thoroughly enjoyed my dinner here, but the service was a bit stuffy; nonetheless they were very professional.

The restaurant itself is very beautiful, it is simple but yet very elegant. I enjoyed my experience here, but I think this restaurant is one to be saved for special occasions.

Quite a nice restaurant. Big, lovely room, very attentive service (although a couple of the young waiters were a little snooty). Just a great setting for a three hour tasting menu.

The carrot tartare and the granola were the standouts, surprisingly. Oh, and the duck. You must have the duck.

Watching the waiters perform the final steps of presentation for some of the dishes was kind of fun, but mostly took away from the experience, I thought.  

Still, this is outstanding food in a beautiful setting. Plus it's where Carrie Bradshaw fell down the stairs, remember?
Great experience here, meal lasted a little longer than expected but was worth every minute. Excellent service, and the food was great. The granola parting gift was a nice touch too.

Such an amazing experience and now forever ruined for other fine dining establishments.  I was lucky enough to be a guest of the restaurant as my BFF's cousin is the pastry chef there.  

First of all, everything about this restaurant is majestic, from the entryway from the street to the bar and the dining area.  (For all you SATC fans, this is where Carrie fell down the stairs after meeting Big.).  The staff is so very professional and cordial and needless to say, service was impeccable.

My friend and I lost count of the number of courses on the tasting menu but each one was exquisite, both in taste and presentation.  Entrees ranged from a tiny clam bake to various meats and numerous tasty little desserts.

No wonder this restaurant is always touted as the Best in NY.

"No, sir, you are supposed to pick one ingredient for each dish. And you didn't need to connect them."

"No, unfortunately we don't have the duck this evening."

"No, sir, I'm afraid the chef can't make a cheese souffle or sea urchin cappuccino for you."

It turned out that I didn't like the then new format that much.

I was actually only lukewarm about the since defunct grid format, as nothing beats the gourmand tasting with the muscovy duck supplement.  There is something about leaving a restaurant at one in the morning, drunk on Cognac,  walking past Shake Shack and the thought of a downing a shackstack utterly repulsed you.  When usually I'd knock any sweet old lady down a flight of stairs to get my hands on one....

I had started this particular review 2 years ago, back then little did I know they'd revamp the concept yet again, and that I'd hate it even more.  

Of course, the food is still superb, when it is actually served to you, for example the lobster, scallop and duck are as incredible as before.  However, despite a supposedly longer tasting menu I felt I was getting less quality food overall.  None of the new courses were really substantial, and, while inventive and fun, they were more gimmicky than satisfying on the palate.   

So now I'm paying a surcharge for magic tricks and a smoke show, and due to difficulty in securing a reservation, eating here means having to start your dinner at 10:45PM and find 5 other friends willing to pluck down $400 for a meal.  Obviously I am glad that EMP has grown into a world-class restaurant right in front of our eyes, but part of me wishes that it had remained the upstart with unbridled enthusiasm and confidence in execution but not yet in concept.

I have been here and done the 14 or whatever it is prefix course a couple of times and have tried my hardest to like it. I found the food is okay - not mind boggling. The two standout dishes were the carrot tartare and the homemade granola. But worth the price... not really in my book.

Pros:
-The staff is really pleasant
-The staff ask your preferences so they can semi customize what you eat
-Presentation is nice - not really that creative compared to some places I have been
-They use high quality ingredients and source them from fresh places

Cons:
-The food felt mostly just heavy, not decadent heavy. Food combination was okay-ish for most dishes
-It is really a long experience. I do a decent amount of dining experiences that are long, but this felt almost torturous (and I was with friends!), The decoration isn't really there so you can't feel like you are being entertained (Tickets in Barcelona is similar, but has a better and fun atmosphere). Last time I went, we got to the 7th course and asked to get the bill because it was getting to 2.5 hours and we were getting late for an appointment (which we had mentioned in the beginning). They charged us the full amount but didn't package the last half of the courses... so we had to ask them to do that, which they did (which is good) - but I felt that they should have asked us if we wanted the courses given we paid for it and mentioned the time constraint early. 

Nice people, but I don't think it is worth the hype.

service is exceptional.

decor is a bit weird for a restaurant. I like small rooms like Cafe Boulud but this place is like emptying grand central station and having dinner in the middle of the Main Concourse entrance. 

went last year and its an experience all grown up should have. 
I heard from rich people that they haven't gone because 1) rich people don't spend for anything and 2) its harder to get into then ever before so get reservations or stay at The Langham Hotel and use a concierge to do it for you and still give them a month of time.

This place has food that is exceptional enough to be considered orgasmic but intriguing enough to confuse you. So... it's like this... to describe the dining experience here in non-michelin but yelp people terms... you are having multiple mental orgasms derives from tastebuds but don't know exactly why. 

This place has pinnacle service right along with Per Se. To me, SERVICE makes a Restaurant... if you have amazing food with bad service; be a take-out restaurant. The ninja Service here; anything goes without the diner's notice. Water & Wine is always automatically replenished when you are not noticing it for a moment. Here, the drink pairing (its not just wine but includes concoction of beer) never sees the bottom of its glass. Just a consistent top off till the next set of what feels like endless courses. Experience feels so endless that its a bargain at $500-$600 per head with drink pairing & tip when done. 
Besides the service and great uncomprehensible meal, the cocktails taste like nectars of Heaven even as simple as a "Belvedere Martini".

For the wine geeks; THIS restau has BOND by the glass... expensive at like $120 or something but that's no competition right there for wine nerds.

Burgundy List is like... now I know why Domaine Ponsot, DRC and Leroy are so rare... they are all at Eleven Madison!!
Rarely will you find wine geeks paying restaurant prices for rare Burgs but there is a monumental bible thick encyclopedia wine list here so you guys will find something. The winelist is so thick that you can teach a wine class with it since it should qualify as another version of many Wine Encyclopedias (which by the way there is never actually a wine encyclopedia sold as a wine encyclopedia that is completely 110% comprehensive but always "just about" if you actually read them). OR try the pairing although if I do it again... I'll pick a elegant and modern red burgundy with a smooth enough mouthfeel to make it seem like a light wine for the entire meal. 

If you can get a seat, go here... even if its hard to afford, its worth saving $50/month to go once a year.... like i said, The meal experience is orgasmic and The cocktails taste like nectars sent from Heaven.
Wonderful food and atmosphere. Service was to the nines.
best restaurant I've been to. Excellent service, comprehensive wine list, delicious food

This was an experience more than a meal.  From the waitress arriving to ask you about your preferences and foods you dislike all the way to the kitchen tour we were lucky to take, it was a dining experience I'll never forget.

I had wondered the whole time leading up to this how on earth I'd eat 15 courses, but I realized when I received the first sweet little box containing a savory cookie that they know just what they're doing.  The service was impeccable without being too stuffy - they certainly anticipate needs and take care of it before you've even gotten that far.  It was timed really well so as not to be bored in between courses or overwhelmed with too many.  We left full but not overly stuffed.

Some courses I liked more than others - the grape snow was incredible - and I wasn't as big on the sturgeon or octopus.  But that was kind of the beauty of it - there was so much variety and it would be hard to go anywhere else and have the chance to try oysters, lobster, octopus, sturgeon, venison, and more all in one sitting.

I would highly recommend EMP for a special night out - it's sure to please!

As if this place needed another 5 star review... Couldn't help myself though!! 

Incredible experience!!! I'm in the cab  writing this review. Rarely am I ever as equally impressed by a restaurant's service and food quality! Lisa made my meal experience PERFECT. 

Normally when I go to fancy schmancy restaurants they make me feel guilty for substituting or saying I don't eat this and that... But Lisa insisted I tell her everything I don't eat... And boy am I glad!!! I licked every single plate clean cuz everything was stuff I would eat!!!! She took the time to write down with pen and paper... And they came up with the most incredible substitutions for every dish I wouldn't eat. 

Food was prepared with seasonal, local, organic ingredients. A lot of which were prepped right in front of your eyes! 

They even had a magic trick incorporated into the last dessert course. 

Parting gifts included granola and cookies and a menu with everything we ate written down. (My menu was changed to reflect the changes I made!! The Bf's had all the items that he ate).

Hands down best experience ever. Go. You will not regret it!!!! 

Thank you Eleven Madison Park! Will be back for more! :D

I returned to Eleven Madison in the Fall with my Mom, for the fixed menu.  

After our three hour, 15+ course meal, my mom said, "That was the best meal I'd never want to eat again."

Agreed.

Yes, one of the great dining experiences in the world, but my expectations were set super high and so this wasn't quite the tour de force I'd been expecting.  Some really great and inventive dishes - one was a little picnic that came in its own hamper... but its also very expensive and for the money (or a bit less) I'd rather go back to Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare.   But if I'd not been expecting so much, or if someone else had been paying!, I might have gone the full five stars.

My husband and I ate here three years ago on our honeymoon.  IT WAS THE BEST EVER!!  I cannot even begin to explain the magnitude of the meal and the experience that went along with it.  First, the restaurant is gorgeous; very art deco styling but warm and intimate for being in such a large location.  The service was impeccable, no one was too invasive or annoying, but the entire staff was helpful, interested, and extremely knowledgeable.  The menu doesn't look like much, but it is so fun to pick what you like and let the chefs surprise you from there.  We had so many great things and they made sure that I didn't get an foie gras, but made sure my hubs did.  The whole experience was a few hours and one on the most memorable moments of our trip; we still talk about it to this day.  If you have the opportunity, don't pass it up.

We celebrated my birthday at EMP on a Sunday night. It is amazing as expected - from ambiance to service to ingredients to presentation. You can probably find more hearty and tasty food somewhere else, but if you are looking for an elaborate and impressive experience, this tops every restaurant I've been to so far in NYC. It takes about 3.5 hours and I highly recommend you start before 7pm to have enough energy to enjoy every course.

Oh yeah the famous EMP.. here goes a quick review and a few points that others DID NOT mention. Completely factual:

1) Prefixed 14 course meal for $225 (menu changes but you will get 11+ courses). Most of the appetizer courses are biscuit-bite sized-- the first course is literally a cookie; so don't deceive yourself going in and thinking that you'll get stuffed; you won't.

2) It's a Michelin 3-Stars restaurant, the quality is top notch and a thousand others have already wrote in-depth descriptions on how rich the Foie Gras tasted. However, not all dishes stood out to me. My own opinion is that half of which are slightly over-rated.

3) I was expecting the restaurant to be bigger. 

4) The meal lasted for 3 hours. It's a bit of an over-kill. (I started at 10 PM and it lasted till 1 AM and boy I was soooooo sleepy).

5) You need a credit card for reservation because EMP will charge you $50/head for booking and not showing up. Talk about opportunity costs heh..

6) At the end of your meal, you'll be give a full menu of what you ate nicely put into an envelope. Gotta say that it was a thoughtful souvenir. You'll also get a jar of homemade cereals/granola-- it tastes AWESOME.

7) This one is personal so take it with a grain of salt. I get that it's such a creative combination of ingredients and the chef must be such a culinary artisan to create "sophisticated" dishes out of "simple" vegetables and meat combos. However, I feel like these get over-emphasized, I value what I eat the MOST, not the lengthy descriptions my servers gave me before every meal. Maybe I'm too barbaric, but does adding 3 drops of Olive Oil into the dessert drink really makes it more aromatic? I had to intentionally pick out the oily taste to believe that it was there-- get what I'm saying? How much do we really have to pay for creativity though??

IN SHORT: A world class restaurant that appeals to the cozy sophisticate in us all. Chef Daniel Humm possesses an intuitive ability to transform the simplest of dishes into creations that will have us desperate to come back again.

THE STORY: Eleven Madison Park is only experienced via a multi-course tasting menu intended to take you throughout a local and seasonal New York with tastes and textures as diverse as its people and landscapes. My meal began with a smoked salmon appetizer with cucumber, salmon roe, cream cheese foam, and bagel chip crumbles. When it came stunningly plated and thoughtfully balanced, it took me a minute to realize that I was in fact enjoying a New York bagel with lox, merely deconstructed to the standards of one of the best chefs in the city. There is something delightfully unpretentious about being able to recognize and identify all the components of a dish, while marveling at the incredible freshness of the salmon (not a hint fishy!) and the classic texture combinations produced with the light bread crumbles.

The next dish also had foam (no surprises there, the food world we live in just can't get enough of this edible, texturized, dish soap lookalike), but was otherwise constructed entirely from local state squash. Bright, colorful, and hearty, it only confirmed Chef Humm's mastery of light, powerfully flavored vegetables. My last dish was made with celery, and featured the vegetable in every form you could imagine, from fried celery leaves to celery puree. Eleven Madison Park skillfully renders flavors and meals that are comfortable to us in unique and surprising ways, making the grandiose space with art deco details feel like home.

Because I was here for a special event, the chef's reportedly heavy-handed stories of each dish were not told to our group, leaving us to enjoy and experience each bite as if it were our own. I didn't need a narration to my dinner, as Chef Humm's food speaks so eloquently and passionately for itself. The atmosphere and decor is so reflective of the old, refined nature of the city, it convinces you that no other space could be more expressive of Manhattan. If I am ever taken here again, I know I won't be able to stop myself from falling in love.

After calling right at 9am (6am West Coast time, yawn!), exactly 28 days prior to the date of dining, I was able to secure a 9:45pm reservation for four this past Friday night.  Hubby, LO, and I arrived on a red-eye that same morning from Seattle, so needless to say, a disco nap was in order :)

All my tiredness melted away as soon as I saw the interior of the fabulous Met Life North Building.  The gorgeous setting only set the tone for the amazing food and service that myself, my cousin, her hubby, and a childhood family friend were to enjoy over the course of the next 3hrs and 45min.  Plus they all live in NYC (hence our meetings are way too infrequent) so the ability to leisurely catch up made the occasion even more special!

My friend, who is a fellow foodie (and shockingly had never been to EMP thus far), had just found out that she got a promotion so we were in a particularly celebratory mood.  My sister had called the restaurant and ordered a round of bubbles which will promptly served soon after we sat, with a congrats note to DF.

One of the many servers of our night came out to ask about allergies and discuss the concept of the chef's menu.  We all nodded, as I think we had all been so excited about this meal that we had all thoroughly read the website to prep.

By now, with the first buzz kicking in, I made the decision to go full-out and do the wine pairing with the meal.  Hey you only live once right? Right?

As you can imagine, this meal was definitely a once-in-a-lifetime experience (price and sheer luxury, as other Yelpers have mentioned), but it was worth every penny!  In our time at EMP, we got 15 courses, wine with 10 of the courses (there was a point in the night when I had to ask our head waiter to please not top me off anymore, I was definitely starting to feel the buzzz when he was so generous with the extra pours!)

Head waiter was a bit snooty as the evening started, but we quickly charmed him with our food and wine knowledge, wit, and west coast friendliness!  He was quickly our BFF.  Or perhaps we were just one of THOSE tables, the ones that think they are so witty and charming when honestly are (lets be honest) just plain drunkety drunk drunk! ;)

I don't want to give anything away, but at the end of the night when we received our souvenir menu (along w/ a mason jar full of housemade granola to take for breakfast), it broke the courses down by dominant ingredient: cheddar, oyster, shrimp, sturgeon, foie gras, carrot, lobster, squash, duck, greensward, malt, apple, sweet potato, pretzel, chocolate. Phew! I definitely enjoyed some courses more than others, but every one made me pause and think due to the complexity and depth.  A gastronomical success of the highest order!

This restaurant is definitely worthy of being #5 on the list of Top Restaurants in the World (S. Pellegrino 2013) and #7 on the 20 Most Important Restaurants in America (BA, 2013) and which I am on a quest to try as many as possible this year!!!

When we planned our trip to the US recently we made it a mission to visit Eleven Madison Park. We booked months in advance, as soon as we were able to! And this was all before I realized it was THE restaurant from THAT scene with Carrie and Big!!
