This place is not just a restaurant, it is also a theater. Eating here is an experience that features delicious food and magic throughout!

If I could give more stars I would!

Took my boyfriend here for his birthday, and it was a scintillating 4-hour experience.  Unfortunately, the first half hour was spent waiting for the Manhattan cart to arrive - we had to ask twice where our drinks were, and I felt bad that we had just arrived at this amazing 5-star restaurant and were actually searching for our waiter and drinks upon our first order.  I had been hoping for impeccable they-take-care-of-you-before-you-even-have-to-think-about-it service (the way I experienced at Le Bernardin), but unfortunately did not get that here.  Also, our waitress was perfectly nice, but kind of a damper on the mood, as she was a little awkward and robotic.  

Other than that, what a wonderful NY-themed menu.  The interactive and playful component makes for a great setting to a long dinner conversation, and the staff was extremely knowledgeable.  Of course, the presentation was exquisite and the flavors were always well-balanced and appreciable on a very nuanced level - made every bite worth it.  Also appreciated the sommelier's assistance in tailoring our own wine (and beer!) pairing with the dishes.

Also a delightful surprise at the end that we could walk away with our own dated menus as souvenirs of his birthday, along with a delicious (and beautifully wrapped) chocolate bar saying Happy Birthday, and a jar of granola to enjoy for breakfast the next morning.

I think trying this tasting menu once is enough for me, but can't wait until they change it up so that I have a reason to return!  (And hopefully won't have to wait so long for a drink this time)

Absolutely divine! Everything about it is pure luxury. 

Definitely one of those "once in a lifetime" restaurant experiences. Well, hopefully more like "once a year" kind of experiences!

Amazing experience. Go if you can.

I came here for an anniversary dinner and it was a great experience.  The food was great and staff were wonderful.  I appreciate the level of detail they put into preparing the dishes and I ate everything.  Even my wife, who is a picky eater, ate everything.
Expensive. Enjoyable. Take your best friend i.e. wife and enjoy the feast. It will take a while but it will fly by. We have been twice and we will go again...

Oddly disappointing.  Somewhat impersonal and not as enjoyable a meal as the "old" EMP.  The dishes lacked impact.  Having different staff bring different dishes didn't feel like having the chefs at NOMA bring out food they had created but instead like it ws "whoever is free now take this out please."  We won't be back.

Our company, took a trip to New York City at the beginning of October and we were lucky enough to be able to enjoy dinner together at Eleven Madison Park. 
Everything from making the reservation to paying the bill was seamless.  We decided on a private room (the South Room) with one table for the 11 of us, it ended up being a perfect setup.  Many of us had never done a tasting menu in such a highly rated restaurant - we were all really impressed. It was fun to dress up and have this experience as a group. The food and wine was really good and the service was amazing. For many of us this was our favorite part of the trip!

Wow! What can I say that has not been said already. The food is #*%# amazing. An interactive dinning experience at it's best. The service could not be better, you will be hard pressed to get these people to say No to anything you ask for. The 2-part sturgeon course and the duck were my favorite. Enjoy!

Definitely a nice restaurant.  We liked the food though the whole experience seems to be more about the show and presentation rather than the food itself.  It was amazing but haven't blown me away -- perhaps too much time in New York.

Best food experience I've ever had! Made a 10pm resy during a very busy week for me and I went in there a little annoyed at myself for picking the worst time for me to have a 3 hour, $250 Wednesday dinner. It was such a wonderful experience! Every course was a surprise in some way and each course tied seamlessly into the next. Every dish was perfect. I left thinking how happy I was to have mady the resy here and wanting to go again the next day!

one of my all time favorite restaurants. Unbelievable food and wine, the staff and service were the best of the best. I do not even like cooked carrots, but I would eat carrots every day if they were from here or even similar to the carrot tartare dish.  The food is simply so delicious you realize you are eating with a big smile. I cannot wait to return!

A truly different and wonderful experience.  I "felt" like a celebrity dining here.  The themed menu was incredible.  I finally tried foie gras, and to my surprise, it was delicious.  I'm big on atmosphere, and Eleven Madison Park is unlike any other restaurant in NYC.  This is not a "dinner on the run" type of place.  I would consider dining here the central focus of an evening.  The food was creative and delicious.  The menu offered a "tasting selection".  The service was exemplary!!!  This is not an inexpensive restaurant but as always, I'm the type of diner who doesn't mind paying for a dining experience if it's worth it.  I very much dislike paying even 20 dollars for a meal if it's obviously a frozen dinner dumped on a fancy plate, but have no problems spending around 100 per person for an exceptional experience!  Highly recommend for your next special occasion!

Holy shit.

No words.

So awesome, so different, perfect service. Such an experience.

Besides those.

this was such a magical dining experience. my friend and i were able to get a table for two on saturday for lunch. (lunch and dinner tasting menus are the same)
as soon as we came in, we were seated immediately and our waiter appeared promptly explaining the menu.
out of the 15 courses, my favorite dish was the sturgeon (see pictures). it was a take on new york city bagel breakfast kinda feel where you eat an everything bagel with cream cheese. instead they gave an everything bagel crumb and a good amount of cavier cream cheese topping it off with sturgeon and pickle. 
i love playing with my food and this 3.5hr meal made me one happy, playful eater. 
at the end of this delicious meal they give you a wonderful parting gift (granola in a mason jar or chocolate (depending on the occasion). 
this meal was worth the wait. EMP showed why it deserves to be #5 in the world and #1 in north america

Overrated. The food is good. Looks pretty, well made, and quality ingredients..... But the dishes don't always taste great. The chef thinks too much about being creative and original and not enough focus on how the dish tastes. FOOD SHOULD TASTE GOOD! 

The service is exceptional and I would recommend anyone who has the extra income to try it at least once just for the experience but do not expect amazing food. If you're into molecular gastronomy more than taste then this is the place to go otherwise go to NoMad, same chef amazing food and desserts and half the price.

I went here with my boyfriend and his parents (their treat, yay!) back in March 2013 to celebrate him getting into grad school. 

All I can say is, it was HANDS DOWN the best meal of my entire life.

(Seriously).

Hugely disappointed. For this kind of money you want to feel pampered, everything should be flawless - and, well, it is not. Most important, in my opinion - too many courses, none of them first rate. They desperately want to present 'cool' factor and it definitely present, but in 15 courses range - you have to have to at least 2 great quality (and sufficient amount of) main courses - meat & seafood. We have venison, it was only ok with barely warm very small piece of meat. Very questionable choices, such as beer and pretzel????? and 2 cans of granola as a parting gift?????; Also, I'd question how plates were chosen for some courses...No question in my mind, this is not comparable to Per Se, not even close...

I went to Eleven Madison Park for my 29th birthday.

Normally, themed restaurants are tourist traps, like the awful Mars 2112, or worse Ninja, where waiters appear in a cloud of smoke to hand off California rolls. Fancy restaurants are often merely that: fancy. Many don't even claim a cuisine, but hang out in the comfortable and noncommittal zone of American.

In that sense, Eleven Madison Park is an anomaly in being so, well, specific. It is one part beautiful zen art and another children's magic show. In his TED Talk, JJ Abrams talks about the "mystery box," a theme throughout his work as a writer and director. Eleven Madison Park is the JJ Abrams of restaurants, surprising and delighting with tension and reveals.

Our meal began with a white paper box tied up with ribbon. Inside were three black-and-white cookies. (Josh: "Wait, what? We're starting with dessert?") But then: they were savory, like pate on toast.

Soon, we were presented with a picnic basket. It was up to us to investigate and discover pretzels, mustard, and a fine cheese.

Then, there was the course above, with minced carrots via a metal grinder clamped to the table, and ten tiny plates meant to be all mixed together, and added to bread.

At some point, there was clam chowder served out of a tea kettle. (Vince: "I haven't had anything this good since my mother's breast milk.")

Perhaps the best example was last. After our first dessert, our waiter performed for us a card trick. It ended with three cards face-up on the table, reading chocolate, peanut butter, and mint. (Waiter: "These are the ingredients of your last course, and it's already here.") Our plates were then lifted up to reveal second, smaller plates, with these desserts. Alakazam.  

And finally? The same white box as in the beginning. With the same black-and-white cookies inside. Was this in error? No: they tasted totally different. Sweet, as a dessert should.

Long story short, while I'll wait to go again until the shtick has changed (after all, what's a twist if you know the ending), unwrapping so many food gifts made for the perfect birthday present.

This is an experience that you just need to enjoy for yourself.  We celebrated our 10th wedding anniversary with a weekend in NYC and our meal at EMP was the big splurge.  It was a meal I will never forget- really.  Go to celebrate an occasion- it is expensive, but totally worth it.  As my sister said, "It transcends you" and I agree.  Just go- you WILL NOT REGRET it.  The impeccable service and beautiful decor pair perfectly with the creative and adventurous menu that is prepared with so much care- it is obvious.  I almost can't even write this review because I hate to try to put it in words how much we loved it.  JUST GO.

We lucked out and got pulled from the waitlist the night before (weekday) for a 9:45 sitting. (We didn't get out until like 1am though, haha, but well worth it)

I don't ...I can't not like this place, it was one of the most entertaining fine dining places I've ever been to and everything was done perfectly - the servers were cordial without being too formal (and pretty amused at our antics...but then again, we were the youngest in the room by far,) which hasn't happened at some of the other Michelin-starred restaurants I've been to. 

I think no matter what though, my enjoyment of EMP is a little tamed by the fact that it's fancy pants dining and a lot of the textures seemed to blend together after a while, and not every single bit of the meal was mindblowing. I think a lot of it was due to the use of foam/concentrating intense bursts of flavor into small portions/just a lot of small bite overload.  
However, all of the dishes in the meal was at least good/delicious and cooked well - which is still points in their favor, since there actually weren't any major off notes, just..less interesting ones. That being said, the theatricality of everything that was presented elevated this meal beyond anything I've had by far.

Things I loved: picnic basket with pretzel bread, carrot tartare, ostrich egg (although maybe because we had been dilemmaing over buying ostrich egg at Whole Foods the night before), the duck, the "clam bake" (probably the most favorite presentation I've had of a course, ever),  the egg cream....yhe menu has probably changed, since this was the July menu, but - their bread (Parker House rolls? I think) is knock your socks off amazing. And the butter that goes with it. Legitimately some of the best bread I've ever had.

Also, the takeaway granola is awesome. Salty, almost a little overpowering, but extremely hard to put down for a couple of bites. 

Besides, if you're reading a review of EMP, and you're considering going, you already have the wherewithal to afford it (thank you,  celebratory dinner), and you should have already started calling for that reservation, because 28 days before is not a joke, unless you want to chance the waitlist, because it's definitely an experience to have. Maybe not twice, but at least once.

There were dishes that I thought were delicious (smoked sabayon, the foie gras, duck with lavender) and the plating and presentation of some dishes were interesting (smoked sturgeon in a glass cloche, a picnic basket with pretzel bread, carrot tartare ground fresh at the table), but I was looking for something....more. Especially when you're in the same category (three star Michelin rating) of restaurants like Per Se and Daniel. I guess I feel that way because there wasn't one dish that I was completely blown away by. 

But their wine list is amazing. And the sommelier was extremely knowledgeable and did help us pick wines from our favorite region in France.  We chose to get bottles of wine instead of the pairing - but the tasting menu did come with beer (part of the picnic basket course) and apple brandy as part of a dessert course.  

And the service here was nothing short of spectacular. We were truly given the royal treatment, but in the end we came here for the food and I was honestly underwhelmed.

I want to love you EMP, but I can't....But I do want to come back again to see if there's something I missed.

This was a birthday dinner from a few months ago, so I don't recall every course. It was a good experience, though I came away feeling a little too stuffed. A couple of courses less would probably been just-the-right amount of food for me!
The making of the reservation was a process in itself  - woke up early on a saturday, both the bf and I dialled from our phone at 8.59, still did not get through till 16 minutes later (yes, I remember it to the last minute) and finally got an early reservation for a saturday 28 days from then.
The service was excellent, and they were accomodating of my quirky diet. The courses innovative, and there was enough showman-ship to make it interesting. (Card tricks, picnic baskets etc) 
It wasn't the 5 star experience I expected it to be - I think for the price range and the number of courses, I expected more courses to have that "wow" factor. That wasn't the case. Of the 16 courses, the Carrot Tartare, the Clam chowder and the Lobster were exceptional. 
We also got granola and a chocolate bar (my birthday present - best chocolate I have ever had) when we were leaving. 
To sum it up - an experience worth having once, not sure I would go back.

This place is very good! The service and food bring you to a climatic experience ! Will def. be back to try something different, so many things looked and sounded great! I was with my wife and she is a picky eater and she loved everything we ordered . Oysters where great the wine list had everything you would want from reasonable priced to very expensive. My duck was killer, loved how crispy they served it and the lobsters was perfection. I wish I can remember our server he was great. Well done!

The food was amazing, no questions asked. Seriously great. But the real reason you MUST eat here is the journey and experience of the meal. It's unlike anywhere else, including the two other 3-star Michelin restaurants in NY I've been to.

Some of the best service I have had in a LONG time at any restaurant. They are doing it here and they know it.  Pricy but well worth it and since I don't eat at places like this often, it was a treat and thankfully worth every penny.  Caviar, lobster, venison, wow, amazing place and food.  And the atmosphere matches the food, just awesome.  I will remember this place for a long time.
Excellent cuisine.  Nice selection on the menu.  Impeccable service.  Bright and spacious.  Highly recommend for business lunches.

My 400th review goes to Eleven Madison Park. I really wish I could give EMP a 5-star review, but you will learn why in this review:  My friend and I celebrated our birthdays here. We called 28 days in advance and got at 10 pm reservation. This place can easily be missed, just remember the entrance is right at the corner of Madison and an alley.  We arrived right on time and were greeted by a line of employees. It was like they rolled out the red carpet for us. 

The first course was actually the black and white cookies since it was our birthdays. They tasted like Cheez-its, which was good because I was afraid that it was going to be sweet.  

Oyster - This was ok - didn't wow me, but you could tell it was very fresh. They did serve this really cold - I was shivering after this. 

Sea Urchin - (Marinated with shrimp , foie gras and Chervil) To be honest, I didn't remember this dish, come on there's 15 other dishes to remember! 

Sturgeon- (Sabayon with chive oil, smoked with everything bagel crumble, pickles and caviar).  This was served in a little egg shell, it was cute.  The texture was creamy and the chive oil was on the bottom so you do have to stir it.  

Foie Gras- (Terrine with plum and bitter almond)  I usually like my foie gras seared but this dish was unique.  It was a terrine foie gras, served in between a thin piece of cracker.  The cracker was really sweet and it might have over powered the foie just a little.  You couldn't really taste the foie because of how sweet the cracker was. I was a little bit disappointed with this dish.

Carrot tartare- The waiter Jesse came our table to pureed the carrot for us. There were condiments such as garlic, radish, sesame, and so much more.  They were literally asking you to play with your food, because you are deciding how you want your Carrot Tartare to taste with the rye bread, which by the way was perfect.  It was one fun dish to explore!

Lobster- (poached with Brussels sprouts). The lobster was sweet and cooked just right. The Brussels Sprouts was my favorite from this dish.  It was cooked well and had a sweet taste to it, because it was paired with light sauce. 

Squash- (Roasted with cranberries and sourdough)  When we got the kitchen tour they were showing us how they were making this dish. I love squash so this dish was delicious. It was firm and not too soft.  

Duck- (Grilled with onion, corn and Lardo. Roasted with Turnip and huckleberries.)  I was very disappointed with this dish because the crust of the duck was so hard.  The huckleberries actually made the dish a little too sour for me. But my friend thought it was too salty.  

Greensward- This was by far my most favorite dish. As simple as it may sound, the pretzel was perfect.  This was served in a picnic basket and they said "we will allow you to explore this basket".  We didn't know what to expect.   I believe that all their products in the basket was made upstate or in New Jersey and is catered to EMP. The cheese, pretzel and beer will blend perfectly in your mouth.  

Malt- Ok I lied, THIS was my favorite dish that I've ever had. This egg cream tops everything that I've ever had out of all the fancy restaurants I've been. The egg cream with vanilla and Seltzer so delicious. I wish I knew how they made it. Okay , I'm lying again, I saw them make it, but I really wish I'd saved drops of this dessert to analyze how they made it. It wasn't too sweet and it was so smooth, light and creamy. It was like a party in your mouth, not just any party like a crazy Great Gatsby party! 

Apple Sorbet with bay leaf crème brulee and hibisicus. This dish was really good as well. You can tell the sorbet was made fresh in house along with the crème brulee. 

Sweet Potato cheesecake with honey and chestnut.  Yes, you read that right: sweet potato cheesecake with honey and chestnut. The three things I love in life.  I love chestnuts and I love cheesecake. Blend those two together with my third favorite ingredient in life, and you get perfection. 

We got the kitchen tour and they showed us around. And Nina made us a drink called Aviation.  It was so good, it was pretty cool crushing up the dry ice for this drink and I think it went well with the dishes that were served after the tour.

They end the night with a magic show which I prefer not to spoil it for you. Just don't blink.  But overall the service was impeccable. It was like they were trained to perfection even the presentation of the food was perfect.   The only problem I had was with the wine: they didn't even ask us to taste the wine at first before serving it. We didn't really like our wine, because it was a little flat. They give you a jar of granola for your breakfast the next day to continue your tasting adventure! Overall, Thank You EMP for an unforgettable birthday experience and for the gift!

Had the 10th course been the last one, I would probably have rated it four or five stars. Unfortunately, it was the dessert that spoiled our dining experience. The five dessert courses (including the cheese) were as much food as the first 10, they were too heavy and just not balanced at all. We even felt a little nauseous and sensory overloaded after having finished our meal and that feeling did not stop until the middle of the next day.

On the positive side, I loved the main dining room with the high ceilings, the service was impeccable and the extraordinarily creative presentation of the different courses was among the best I've ever experienced.

I would give it 10 stars if I could. 

Hands down THE best meal and THE best dining experience I have had (August 2011).  Impeccable service matched the artful and delightful food, which was paired perfectly with our wine flight. Dietary restrictions were no issue, and the "takeaway" granola at the end was a brilliant and seamless way to continue the experience into the next morning.

By far this is the most thought out and well put together tasting menu I've had. I didn't enjoy all the courses that were served to us but the courses were all prepared creatively for the given in season ingredients. They change their menu once every season, but if you dine there frequently they will prepare something different.

They might have changed their menu as my friend mentioned there used to be choices for the tasting menu. Reservation was a lot easier than expected. I placed it online two weeks prior to the date I had wanted and easily reserved the earliest seating. The coordination here is right on point. If you were first ones in, like us, you're guaranteed to be the first ones out. The only dinner service is whatever is being served for the tasting menu. Our waiter only asked us if we were allergic to anything or what we didn't care to eat. We didn't get to see the menu, which creates a mystery of what will be served. 

We started and ended with a box of black and white cookies. The start of the meal, the cookies were savory, where as at the end of the meal the cookies were the more traditional sweet black and white cookies. 

We had a total of 16 courses or items based on the menu we received along with the parting gift, home made granola in a glass mason jar,  at the end of the meal. Instead of listing everything we had, I'll highlight the creative aspects of the courses. 

They created a sea urchin flavored shaved ice. They created their own version of Manhattan clam chowder by serving it with various types of clams. The soup base was fresh tomato juice, clam juice, and some other ingredients poured from a glass tea pot. They created a Foie gras brulee; consisting of foie gras in a round shape with burnt sugar on top to simulate a creme brulee. The foie gras had the same texture as a creme brulee. 

They made their own butter. One was plain with sea salt and the other was infused with the beef fat from the beef portion of the course. They had one course that was carrot tartare with rye bread and condiments. They brought out a meat grinder to the table and attached it to the table. We were intrigued on what it could be (thanks to them not showing us the menu prior) and later they brought out some garden fresh carrots and grinded them up at the table. We were instructed to mix in any condiments and seasoning that fancied our taste buds. 

Someone brought out the beef, raw form, to show us what we would eventually eat. It was like inspecting the fresh catch of the day for a seafood item but in beef form. We got a picnic basket containing our cheese and crackers course. Since we opted out of alcohol, they served us apple cider with our cheese course. 

They made us fresh egg cream with some olive oil drizzled in as their secret ingredient. Then we had a deconstructed root beer float which is listed as a Sassfaras on the menu, and a red pepper cheesecake. 

After all the creativity put into the courses, we even experienced a magic trick at our table performed to perfection. I won't spoil the trick as it's quiet fascinating. I'll only reveal that it involves a dessert course of your meal. 

The take home granola was scrumptious and there was plenty for four servings. This is one of the better take home gifts I've experienced. 

Overall I really enjoyed the meal. Even though my guest and I may not have liked every course served, we appreciated the creativity, service, pace, and the thought out menu. 

As a side note, it does not seem like dress code was enforced. We saw several people in sweaters and wearing jeans. It's listed as tie mandatory. Majority of the patrons wore a shirt and tie, a few wore a jacket but there were a handful that wasn't in appropriate attire.

There is a reason why EMP has emerged as the top restaurant in NYC, above Per Se and many other 3-michelin restaurants in the past year. The service is top notch but above all, EMP provides a unique and memorable dining experience for it's patrons. I won't go in to much detail because I don't want to ruin the magic (literally, magic) for anyone dining here. Just leave your expectations at the door and come prepared to enjoy flavors and food preparations that are unexpected. The granola that they give to take home is also amazing.

Update: try to get an earlier reservation if you can. The food at our 9:30 pm visit was still so yummy and delish but the service was lackluster and tired. I had a MUCH better experience last time when my reservation was at 6pm. We were one of the last tables to leave that night. Still highly recommended but for the AMAZING dining experience, go when the staff isn't exhausted. Enjoy!
Wonderful service and a fun meal. I like how they involve the diner in each course. Loved the clam bake.

Vibe: Unwelcoming, stale, pretentious, bank vault, quiet. Like they are doing you a favor by letting you eat here. WHAT IS ALL THE HYPE ABOUT HERE?

Price: Extreme. $195 pp/ food only.

Service: Professionally excellent yet over bearing.

Wine List: Extremely priced. Go to USA Syrah or Italy Nebbiolo for best deals.

Food: Oy Vey! A huge disappointment. How are you supposed to order wine when you do not know what the menu is? This is more of a magic show than fine  food that wows you. The only dish that made us go wow was the NY egg cream! The flavor concentration was delicious. Opening bakery boxes with black and white cookies that taste awful. Smoke in a glass sturgeon, picnic baskets and card tricks are the focus rather than the food. Grinding carrots table side is a great visual effect, but does not tantalize the taste buds. Showing a pumpkin filled with sage leafs and then serving an overly sweet squash dish does not work either. (We heard the dinners visiting from Italy next to us, complaining about the food). The best trick of the night was showing the table a plump 5 lb cooked duck and serving us one slice is food robbery. Telling us that is all the duck meat that can be used from the duck because the dry aging process renders any other meat on the carcass inedible is unbelievable. This poor duck died for three slices! It must have been granted a halo and harp!  Why are there no beef or chicken dishes in the mix. Menu lacks food diversification and clarity and direction. It's like starting a business without a plan. This place is definitely more theatrics than dinner.

Deserts: A total disappointment. Overly sweet, overly citrus, lacking innovation. A bottle of local apple brandy is provided with unlimited pours. You need a shot or two because you are dizzy from the showmanship and disappointing by the food. A mason jar of homemade granola is provided as a party favor when you leave. Another round of egg creams my party shouted! 

Bathroom: 2/2/2 Men. Feasible and clean.

WIGB? No

I loved the smoked sturgeon in a cut eggshell mixed with green chive coloring (cut by a laser from an outside company)! The two walnuts on the cheese plate were the best toasted walnuts I ever had in my life, the foie gras had the consistency of butter. I'm not a big fan of foie gras but everyone on my table enjoyed it. Personally I preferred the beef with plum and onions...

I still think about you my love. 
I will come back for you.

One of the best experiences of my life.

Had dinner there to celebrate our anniversary. Very special evening. I've had more personal service but none so attentive. The food was outstanding and creative. All 15 courses were inventive and very tasty. The wine pairing was spot on and you got generous pours. Service is a team effort which is nice but you don't make a connection with one server which lends to the impersonal nature of the meal. The meal will be a night I will never forget!!

After seeing Eleven Madison Park ranked #5 in the world and #1 for NYC, I knew I had to eat there during our recent trip to NYC.  My husband and I have eaten at some of the top restaurants all over the world, and I expected EMP to easily equal, if not surpass, some of our past experiences.

Unfortunately, it fell short for us in several areas.  First the good- we liked the ambience of the restaurant.  The super high ceilings and open atmosphere give it a more relaxed and comfortable vibe than many other high end restaurants.  It also provided for great people watching.  However, the ambience alone doesn't make up for issues we experienced with the food and service.

Service was the most surprising to me.  That's usually the easiest thing to get right- be attentive and aware of attention to detail.  After showing us to our table, we ordered a cocktail to start the night out.  Our glasses were completely empty and the first course served and we still hadn't been offered another drink, received a wine list, or been visited by the sommelier.  It was rather strange for such a high end establishment.  I had to ask for the wine list and the sommelier to visit our table two or three separate times before anyone stopped by.  We also felt that the spacing between courses was off and the kitchen let way too much time elapse before serving the next course.   

The food was good, but not great.  Again, for a place of this caliber, my expectations were much higher.  I would rate it a B+.  My biggest issue with the food was actually not with the courses themselves but with the treat of granola they give you at the end of the meal.  I had explained upfront that I have an allergy to tree nuts (like anaphylactic shock severe).  Now nut allergies aren't entirely uncommon, and they did a great job accommodating it during the meal.  But you would think when the granola was dropped off they would have a batch of nut free, or at the very least, mention to me that I might want to avoid it due to the large amounts of almonds in the mix.  Not a word was said, which I find incredibly careless.  Luckily I know that most granola contains nuts, but I was shocked no one thought to point it out to me.

Overall, just an average experience.  I wanted to love you EMP, really I did.  Unfortunately, there are way too many amazing restaurants in NYC to pay a repeat visit to this one.

Another five-star review for EMP...

I've been wanting to try this place out for a long time. Reservations are hard to get - you have to call in at 9am exactly 30 days prior to the date of your desired reservation. Even if you call at 9am, there's a wait to get on the line as I think they only have one person taking calls...!

My boyfriend and I came here on a Sunday night at 7pm. We got our first course at approximately 7:15 or 7:30...and we didn't leave until past 10:30pm! So prepare for a 3-hour long culinary adventure...

I wont't go over all the courses in detail since they change, and EMP has a tradition of changing the courses to accommodate different diets. They also change the foods with the seasons and source all of their ingredients locally - every time a new course came up, they would explain where the food came from, how it was made, etc. It was actually very interesting!

The whole meal is somewhat extravagant and definitely a tasting experience. The people watching is interesting. After eating at EMP, I noticed how everything else I ate was extremely bland and boring.

The meal was around $550 for 2 people including a half bottle of wine. Not cheap!

PS - it's much easier to get a lunch than dinner reservation here!
Astonishingly good.  Amazing food creatively served without being over the top.  Superb service

So the short of it is service is excellent, atmosphere great , food nicely prepared and theatrics are kind of fun, but the  theatrics only highlight the letdown when the food comes. Everything is prepared well and tastes good but not one dish was memorable or just gave that yum satisfying experience.  I have eaten many 16 course meals and this multi-course meal was by far the greatest let down. Management even gave us 2 extra courses and listened to ur comments but even these dishes could not save this meal.

We arrived in New York early morning checked into an awesome hotel there was so much excitement leading up to our lunch date at 11 Madison Park. The restaurant was spacious and airy not overly trendy. We dressed up even though it was just lunch, why not? To our surprise people dressed rather casually in the restaurant. We were seated at an awesome corner table over looking the entire restaurant. 

We started with manhattan the presentation was great the bartender pushed a liquor cart over and made the cocktail right in front of us. I looked over the wine list we went with a 2006 premier cru La Truffiere Puligny-Montrachet, it was a full bodied white that went with every course as recommended by our sommelier who turned out to be Belgian. The wine was fantastic! 

Most courses had a light, clean quality with a touch of complexity. I would highlight these and these courses ended up back to back: 

Sea urchin custard with baby squid and scallops - beautiful presentation and great mix of seafood flavors

Smoked Sturgeon in a cloche presented to us with a platter of caviar with garnishes and an creamy sabayon.

Salsify with bulgur wheat and mangalitsa ham - amazing earthy flavors.

Carrot tartare just the sound of the name was interesting but the presentation was even more appealing the carrot was grounded with a meat grinder with served with an array of mini condiments honoring vegetable in its raw form.

Lightly poached lobster served with a shellfish bisque that was a shiny glistening black sauce topped with a green onion with roots that were charred - that really made the dish

Parsnips in a few ways I particularly loved the roasted sheets of parsnips with sesame served with the softer whole parsnip - another well-prepared dish

The apex of the dinner was the 150 days aged beef served with braised oxtail and foie gras this was the single most luxurious dish I ever had the beef was by far the best morsel of meat. Such a remarkable dish!

Then we thought there could not be another course that could top the beef. We received a covered platter et voila! It was my engagement course with a ring in it. Then the sommelier presented a bottle of champagne sabering the bottle for this joyous occasion!

We took a tour in the impressive kitchen and had a cocktail made at the kitchen table, chatted with the chefs for a bit.

Another memorable and whimsical New York experience was presented in the next course a picnic basket with fresh pretzels on a "paper" plate and a bottle of wheat beer. 

So if you have a chance to dine at 11 Madison Park you would get the ultimate New York experience including the great showmanship! It was as New York as New York gets. 

Congrats on being #5 in the world and thank you for a memorable engagement.

O-- M -- G. 

this was one of the best meals in my life. Visually, the food was beautiful. Flavors/ingredients complemented each other in taste and texture perfectly. Service  was impeccable. Ambiance was elegant and yet warm/inviting. 

Went to friend's wedding reception on the second floor. There were 5 tables set up in a private area overlooking the 1st floor. Wine/water was constantly refilled and the waiter announced each dish with explanation of what it is and how it was prepared and answered questions patiently (i.e. how did you get the egg shell to be cut so evenly???). 

We had two 3 complementary items - black/white cookie to begin the meal (cheddar filling), an aerated souffle (foamy, salty, with bits of ham and sturgeon) as second amuse bouche, and a sweet version of black/white cookie.  

The multi course meal started with salad with wax beans (i don't even like beans but I devoured this salad!), followed by a nice big rectangular piece of foie gras with summer berries, cod (my least favorite dish of the day but still yummy), then beef tenderloin that melted in my mouth (cooked medium/medium rare but not bloody) and will remain in my dreams, then finally the mint chocolate dessert to end. Wedding cake was raspberry mousse (?) that's still semi frozen surrounded by some kind of custard on each side with cake on the ends. YUMMY! 

I loved the whole meal even though it was 3.5hrs long and I was amongst strangers. I enjoyed the food so much that it put me in a good mood to socialize. :)

Just a wee bit overrated. Ok, maybe more than a wee bit. Well, really just way overrated. 11MP pales in comparison to Next in Chicago.

There was 1 truly outstanding dish that was aged beef in a marrow sauce. The rest was simply average, lacked flavor (such as the sea urchin snow), or unfortunately I just did not like (sassafrass dessert, savory black & white cookie which tasted like a ritz cracker, the classic black & white cookie which tasted like an unfrosted animal cracker).

Not trying to be harsh or a hater. Just telling it like it is. 

Service is great. Food is sadly mediocre. I expected more of you 11MP and I'm so sad that you didn't bring it.

I did make a special request to visit the kitchen, and they did bring us back. Pretty impressive operation back there. Didn't see a lot, but they did make us a special drink that was alright.

Going in, I expected greatness -- after all, it's not everyday that you eat at a 3-Michelin Star restaurant that is also ranked 5th in the world by Restaurant Magazine (2013) -- and greatness is what I got. Thus far, the best meal and restaurant experience of my life. From the mysterious tasting menu (courses are not revealed until they are served) to the beautiful decor to the impeccable service, nothing at EMP was short of world class. Of course, all of this was married with food that transcended all fine dining standards  -- unrivalled culinary vision, artistically crafted presentation, genius flavour combinations, and above all, masterful finesse and execution. Classics are classics because they are great time and time again -- improving upon a classic is a challenge in itself. EMP did more than that. They revolutionized the restaurant experience. From the two-part Manhattan clam chowder to the play on a picnic to the do-it-yourself carrot tartare, my experience felt more like a culinary adventure than a meal, and it told a story unlike any other.

Hmm - everyone loves this place so maybe I just had a bad experience.

Wife and I dropped $600 for our anniversary.

What can I say? First of all it was cold. Like damn cold. Unpleasantly cold. It was 90 outside and coming in here was just so unpleasant.

The cocktails were phenomenal and the service is at the stratospheric level you would expect at a place like this but when the food came out? We both thought "meh"....was ok and nice and fresh.

Again, all my friends love this place and it's impossible to keep everyone happy but for that price tag, the AC and taste of the food made it less desirable.

Will keep this short and sweet, as 1000+ other reviews have covered every topic. Went there for birthday lunch for two, did the $195 tasting menu. Will try to focus on the key must-dos / hidden surprises:

1. Reservation policy is about a month in advance... if you are planning to eat during prime hours, make sure you plan accordingly while booking
2. Extensive wine & mixed drinks list but no beer menu (try the voodoo down if you are a whiskey/bourbon drinker, one of the best mixed drinks i've had)
3. Some of the utensils / cups / glasses are very thin and delicate... take care while handling otherwise likely to spill during one of the courses
4. Expect the tasting menu to last ~2.5-3 hours long
5. If possible, after the reservation, ask to be seated in the upper section of the restaurant in one of the corner areas. The restaurant itself is quite beautiful and the view can be best taken in from these seats

Overall, best meal I have had to date. I specifically chose not to include details of the each course b/c half the fun is in the surprise. I would recommend not reading the very detailed reviews, just know the meal is a bit seafood heavy & and has a few DIY (do-it-yourself) courses.

Great service.  But the food was good.  But for the money you spend, you expect sublime.  Enjoyable experience but would be hard pressed to go back again.  They charge for each bottle water even though you may not ask for another bottle.  Seems to be a practice many restaurants are now doing.

Best.Meal.Ever. The End. 

Okay, no just kidding. I dont know what exactly I can add that hasn't already been written here on yelp. The room was quiet and peaceful. The courses timed just right. flavors just right. service just right. portions just right. Everyone made us feel comfortable and not like we were some tourists just here for an occasion. I noticed a few others in the room having a meal for a special occasion as well. We got the kitchen tour and a great specialty cocktail based on the aviation made with liquid nitrogen. Pretty awesome. Perfect birthday meal.

Oh yeah and of course my boyfriend knocked my water glass over after sneaking extra apple brandy at the end of the meal. They were very gracious and acted like it happened all the time. 

When can we go back?

This is one of the memorable restaurants that i have been, particularly because I went there for valentine's day. 

They have the most interesting menu that I've seen so far as it shows only the primary ingredients, and that definitely let your imagination run wild as you never know what you can get. In terms of the meal, most memorable dish was the foie gras. I don't have much impression on the other dishes but one thing for sure, both desserts were disappointing. Aside from that, I like the amuse-bouche, organic bread + goat/milk butter, and the cookies and granola jar that we were given at the end. 

I have never seen a chef that is modest and humble, willing to go out, talk and hear people's inputs. I had the chance to talk and take picture with the chef and Christopher Kostow (who was a 'visiting' chef).

Overall, perhaps I went at a bad day as the main dishes were not the highlights of the meal but the amuse-bouche and other assortments were. To me this is a 3.5 star considering the amount spent, but I will definitely try it again.

There's barely a reason to review Eleven Madison Park. If you're even remotely interested in the place, it is most likely because of the following: A) You are seriously interested in Haute Cuisine (capital-H, capital-C), or B) You have prodigious amounts of cash burning a hole in your pocket and a more-than-moderate interest in status symbols (the two are not necessarily mutually exclusive). 

Either way, you know better. The place is sublime. 

If you're one of those people that is offended by "small" portions and the occasional challenging flavor combination, do not go here and then complain that you wasted your money on a pretentious meal. You, too, should know better. 

To the rest of you, go here. It's more than worth the money. The food is excellent. Beyond excellent. I need a new word for it. Excellent & spectacular. Ex-taculous.

Important to Note: If you choose the wine pairing (which I recommend, with reservations), please be aware that the amount of booze they serve you, even combined with 16 courses, is borderline irresponsible, if not an extraordinary amount of fun. My boyfriend and I left the place considerably sauced, even after 3+ hours of eating. 

So, find a card with a high credit limit. Scrimp, save, take on a second (or third, or fourth) job. But it's worth your time to go.

Eleven Madison Park is a place to add to your bucket list. 

Service you will experience at no other restaurant. 

Detail oriented - from greeting us with towels after being hit by a torrential down pour to the perfect amount of ice in every drink. 

There is a story to every course you receive and the food is divine. 

Hands down most memorable dining experience.

I'm not sure if I recommend reading a lot of detailed yelp reviews before going! The reason I say this is ... you are not provided with the menu until the very end of the meal, so each course is a "surprise" when it is served to you. (Yep, gone is the grid of 16 ingredients that used to be the menu.) If you want to keep this element of surprise in your dining experience, then these reviews are not going to help. You already know it's a really expensive restaurant with 3 michelin stars and creative, interactive courses.
Food was Very Good, Service Unbelievable. Our check came and for four tastings and three bottles of their most reasonable wine the bill after tip was $2k...

I have to agree with every positive review posted thus far.

The service and the food are impeccable and a lot of thought has been put into providing a first class experience. While the meal is pricey, there is no doubt in my mind that you are getting exactly what you pay for i.e. gastronomy at its finest!!!

Do not miss out on the opportunity to dine here!

Fantastic place. Beats its closest competitor (per se, probably) hands down and, amazingly, also manages to do it cheaper.

We've been there several times and it still delivers a unique and exciting experience each visit. The menu is set, which doesn't leave you with a lot of choice, but it also means there is no "supplemental" pricing for dishes that you really want. In addition, each course is beautifully and uniquely presented. Flavors are subtle and delicious. Chef Humm manages to elevate familiar flavors (e.g. tomato) to heights heretofore unseen!

We're going to use EMP to celebrate every milestone... if we can get the reservation! Getting engaged soon. Wish us luck!

Back when I was working full-time and going to college at night, losing sleep and second-guessing why I was putting myself through a life of student loan debt, I promised myself that I'd go to Eleven Madison Park as a omg-you-did-it graduation present. Four years later, I graduated in May, and proceeded to spend the next three months trying to snag a weekend reservation at EMP. They have a 28-day advance reservation policy and the phones open at 9am. After many phone calls and sadfaces later, I got through on a Friday at 9:40am and was able to snag a tasting menu reservation for 10pm four weeks ahead.

Was it worth all that hassle, and the mad amount of cash we dropped that night? Eff yeah. Absolutely eff yeah. EMP earns its 3 Michelin stars and reputation for a reason, and the experience we had that night was simply out of this world.

I was initially concerned that both me and my bf wouldn't be full at the 16 course tasting meal, knowing that the portions are notoriously small -- however, I was absurdly full three-quarters of the way through, almost unable to finish the dessert portion.

Honestly, I can't say what was the best highlight of my meal. Everything, from their version of the Manhattan clam chowder, the tomato soda, the sea urchin snow, the carrot tartare... it was all presented so uniquely that everything seemed amazing. Even the picnic basket, which was somewhat kitsch, was in itself a remarkable idea, and the magic trick is really sweet. At the end, we were gifted with a copy of the menu, plus some breakfast granola if we were hungry the next morning. (Nope.)

Amazing presentation, accompanied by unobtrusive yet attentive service, and imaginative food. If I am lucky enough to come back to EMP for a second time, I will die a happy woman.

The only thing I regret is that we didn't remember to ask for a tour of the kitchen. :(

Had an awesome meal with my wife here, it was quite the culinary experience, one not easily forgotten. We had the 16 course magnificently crafted dishes and this is haute cuisine at its finest. Not a place I'd visit regularly, but worth a visit once a year.

Took my husband (then boyfriend) to Eleven Madison Park for his birthday, as he had been wanting to go there for a while. It was an amazing experience since we entered the restaurant. We walked in, and all I said was that we had a 9:00pm reservation; the two people at the entrance greeted us by our names and wished my husband a happy birthday... it was amazing! When we were seated, we noticed there was a card with my husband's name on it on the table; he opened it and it was a beautiful birthday card with a nice message written in the most beautiful calligraphy... who does that?! Eleven Madison Park.  The bread came and we LOVED it; it was so buttery and sweet and salty and warm - just perfect!  Before we ordered our food, they asked if we had any food allergies, which was so thoughtful because I do have a lot of food allergies and every time I go to a restaurant I have to ask what is in the food before I order. The waitress wrote down every single thing I am allergic to, and waited for me to remember more allergies. The food was amazing! It is something you have to experience in person because no detailed description will give you a close idea of how delicious and interesting the food is at this restaurant. The cool part was that we had a six course meal, but we ended up having about 10 courses with all the little treats they bring you between each course. At the end of the night and after we paid, they gave us a little bag with a bar of butter and a jar of granola that they give to each customer; they are so thoughtful. To make it even more thoughtful and special, they surprised us with a container full of their bread because we told them how much we loved it. I only have great things to say about this restaurant and I will recommend it to anyone who is looking for a very unique and delicious dining experience. It is on the very pricey side, but it is totally worth it!!

The fall tasting menu was a full, interactive experience.

Highlights:

- We were the first ever to partake in the Martini Cart. I recommend taking a look at the cool hand drawn menu

- The tomato gilet with huckleberry and tomato appetizer made me a better person

- A full picnic with basket, beer, checkered napkins

- Each server, sous chef and chef who came to serve and speak to us created a new, cool experience including: card trick, grinding a carrot into minced amazingness, directing us outside to talk to the guy at the Sabrett hot dog stand who then handed us surprise gifts

This kind of restaurant makes having a sugar daddy or momma a real blessing, since it's a little on the $$$$$$ side. So get on that, and make Eleven Madison your next food-tastic destination.

When it comes Michelin 3 star restaurants, it's all about the unique experience.

16 course of artistically crafted dishes, yet the surprises kept coming. The whole tasting menu is prepared in such an order that your taste buds could fully appreciate everything. The early courses (sea urchin, surf clam, little neck clam/Manhattan chowder, tomato confit w lobster), more or less had a hint of sourness (lemongrass, lemon/mint and other herbs) in them, but are quite refreshing to the tongue. Once your tasting sensation is awake, you may fully enjoy foie gras, black bass, ostrich egg(truffle w. butter milk), guinea fowl and age ribeye steak(or duck). Just as your taste buds start to feel a little saturated, a refreshing eggnog helps you to reset them before moving onto desert section.     

I go to Mich 1 star for innovative dishes, Mich 2 stars adds services, ambiance and decor on top of creativity. But for Mich 3 stars, it's the experience that's hard to describe in words. You just need to try it yourself to fully grasp. 

Gave it a four star because of 2 tiny little details/ or preferences. I personally do not like to start the meal with cookies/sweets, especially if it was followed by sea urchin. The apple brandy at the end was just too strong, don't think many people would enjoy 80 proof liquor after completing a 16 course meal. 

I requested a silver needle tea (one of the top-ten Chinese tea varieties, i was actually surprised that they had this), but the brew was mediocre and the tea itself isn't the finest. The waiter also mis-classified it to me as white tea (it's actually a kind of yellow tea), but you shouldn't worry too much if you are not a picky tea drinker who pays $600-700/lb for tea :)

Nevertheless, it's top notch and close to perfection.

They should rename this "The Emperor's New Clothes" because that's what I'm witnessing here. $600 for a 16-course lunch where only a couple items were worth eating yet, unfortunately, in portions too small to satisfy. When they showed us the duck we'd be eating I thought "Finally, something good" but the single small slice was pitiful. They must go through a single duck for the entire day. Midway through the meal I realized how brilliantly positioned the hot dog vendor outside was; I had to eat a slice of pizza after leaving.

Running a carrot through a meat grinder and then presenting it with some other raw ingredients for me to mix is NOT what I pay for at a restaurant. What do I know about mixing flavors in proper proportions? I'M NOT A CHEF. It was so obnoxious and lazy.

They made a big production out of some beer made only for them but it tasted like a repackaged Budweiser.

You know what else I don't like? Eating foam like an infant that can't chew real food.

The service was fine but nothing can make up for the (alleged) meal we were served.

If you want to get on the uber-pretentious bandwagon and pretend the Emperor's new clothes are the finest you've ever seen, go to Eleven Madison Park.

EMP defines fine dining. I could go on for days about how heavenly and memorable this meal was, but I will try to keep it short and sweet as we all have lives.

 I took my gf here to celebrate my first year making 100k as a telemarketer. So glad I did. We were treated as King and Queen, respectively, by a very unpretentious and warm staff. When you're greeted at the door by men in suits (not cheap) that addressed you as Mr/Mrs...., that's when you know its serious.

Each of the 16 courses were breathtaking. Some were actually prepared tableside, one involving a vice that was attached to the table to puree a carrot... yes. that happened. Course after course it got better and better, leaving us to wonder how can the next one be better. it was, they all were. 

At age 26, im confident ive experienced the best life has to offer after eating here. There is no place that compares or even comes close.

With a few cocktails and a bottle of Spanish red I felt like I could walk on the moon. Instead, I settled for a cab to midtown and some backbreaking cardio that occurred at the Marriot Marquis. 

Superb food, wonderful atmosphere, and extremely attentive staff all sort of convalescences into happiness....is what I say!

Best service, Best food, Best ambiance, a little expensive but well worth it.  They made a small mistake of sending the wrong dish to us, and to make up for that, they gave us a tour of the kitchen and showed up how a dessert dish was made and had us eat it there.  LOVED IT!!!!  And because one of the server heard me saying I will do a review on 11 Madison, they sent me extra dishes to try.  AMAZING!!!!!  Very good service.  Anyone visiting NYC, they have to try this place.  It is a MUST!!!

Eleven Madison is the epitome of how a perfect, lavish, over the top, extraordinary dining experience should be in an ideal world. And for foodies, especially, this is your goal, what you've been waiting for all your life, and the absolute perfection in its divine state. 

This dinner was a wedding gift to us and maybe it was a momentous occasion that this experience was just that amazing but it was amazing. 

The tasting menu gets you from the very beginning until the end and for all five hours, your senses are all so fully alert to just take all of it in and then some. What's fascinating about their menu is that it is simplicity and its best without overly complicated nor flowery description but the dish itself created with expertise. It was simple enough for non foodies to understand and appreciate and for foodies to embrace and appreciate even more. 

The ambiance and the set up of the restaurant makes you feel like you and your party are the only people in the restaurant with full attention and care devoted to you and you only. It feels like a super private affair and when you look around, everyone is feeling the same as we are. 

We plan on making this an annual tradition on our anniversary to relive this experience over and over again. 

I highly, 100% recommend and even their price tag is justifiable because of the overall experience.

We made our second visit to Eleven Madison nine months after the first.  We were greeted as welcome guests, literally by our server who remembered us and was very attentive.  Everyone was very gracious, and the food was phenomenal, especially with the long list of allergens one in our party had to avoid.  It was a superb meal and four hours well spent.

This restaurant is simply put-  Michelin StarS Worthy. 
I love the presentation of the prix fixe. It almost tells a tale to the diner...I would compare the experiences here as something like watching an art performance.
Everything melts in your mouth~ Simply YUM!!

Truly a dining experience! Dinner starts with a box of savory black and white cookies and rounds out at the end with sweet black and white cookies. The concept is unique - the menu is a matrix where you can select a theme from each row/column. I liked the greek yogurt pops and lobster tail. Ladies each get a jar of homemade granola to take home. Yum!!
If you are ever going to spend $600 on dinner for two, this is the place to do it. One of the best four hour meals of my life

Been there several times and have never been disappointed. They offer a great tasting menu, and being from California I haven't seen that anywhere else. The service is great, they are "showy". All round great experience.

How does one review a world class restaurant in New York City that serves 16 amazing courses prepared with oversight from a world class chef, that are the most delicious and interestingly creative that one can imagine?  I will give it a try.

The start: It all begins with a fabulous seating in a superb setting next to Madison Park.  We overlook the seemingly endless windows (maybe  40 feet tall) and the park.  Upon sitting the  beautiful curtains were closed.  Then about one hour into the meal as the sun set, magically, and on cue, all of the curtains electrically opened in a symphonic way that reveals the top of the trees in the park outside. Gorgeous! The service throughout the night is impeccable as we must have had at least 6 to 8 different people attending to our every need.  As our excellent waiter mentioned several times, "there will be many surprises tonight"!  There were indeed.

The meal: 16 courses ranging from savory black and white cookies with apple to poached striped bass with zucchini and squash blossoms to a carrot tartare...all these and many many more unimaginable "surprises".  I don't want to give it any more away because it IS a magical and unforgettable meal for all possibly excepting the greatest snobs.

The Surprises:  Really fun..but I don't want to give it all away.  Be surprised and go!

The Wine:  Excellent Sommelier who will guide you to any price point you can muster.

The Price:  If you have to ask.......

Honestly...this is not a restaurant for everyone.  It is not traditional, the portions are many but small and appropriate to the depth and quality of the entirety of the meal.  I can imagine some do not like the concept that all is selected for you but the kitchen is very adept at making changes for you if you do not like certain items. If you are able to enjoy paying Per Se money for a similar but different experience.  Try it.  It was amazing.

This was a fun experience. I would definitely come back here again. We did a tasting menu plus the duck. The experience was like a show, the waiters were the performers preparing and serving the food for us. And also there's some gifts throughout the tasting menu. My favorites were the egg cream (gift), clam bake (gift), duck, the sea urchin cappuccino, poached lobster, and dark chocolate with lavender meringue. 

I really wish they gave us the the lollipops as part of their gifts though. Been eyeing those on yelp before I got to New York but that's ok since we've had so many gifts throughout our meal.

Dining at Eleven Madison Park is definitely an all-out experience. Sure, the food is inspired and great, but the fluidity in the service and progression of the tasting menu truly make dining here magical. 

I was fortunately to celebrate my birthday here with my bf and BL, to which the staff acknowledged and made sure I had a special time. It just so happened that the night we visited was our main waiter's birthday as well, so bonus points for our little Zodiac connection. But I digress.

EMP has an impressively extensive wine list, which our knowledgeable sommelier seemed to know like the back of his hand. We started off with a few different wines by the glass and cocktails, followed by a bottle of a light and fruity Gamay, which went pretty well with many of the courses.

All in all, I enjoyed pretty much all of the 16 courses served, over the 3.5 hours that we were there. Standouts for me included the surf clam (3rd course), tomato confit with lobster salad and bonito (5th course), foie gras (6th course), carrot tartare (7th course), striped bass (8th course), ostrich egg (9th course), duck (10th course), and mint sorbet (13th course). The tomato confit had such intense and pure compressed tomato flavor and really brought out the sweetness of the meaty lobster. The cold foie gras brulee with summer berries and beets was perfectly luscious and light, almost as if it were whipped in texture; it definitely trumps any foie gras torchon I've had anywhere. The carrot tartare, which is processed tableside through a manual meat grinder and served with about 14 garnishes that you mix in yourself, was absolutely whimsical and creative yet absolutely worked. I was surprised that all those different flavors actually melded together, and complemented the natural sweetness of the carrot. Chef Humm's renowned roasted duck with Sichuan peppercorns and lavender, with roasted apricots and fennel was great as advertised. I'm a huge lover of Sichuan peppercorns (typically known as causing a tingly, numbing sensation), yet Chef Humm's treatment really accentuated the floral notes of the peppercorns, combined with the aromatic lavender. Sichuan peppercorn is, after all, "flower pepper." I only wished that the sliver of duck that was actually plated were just a little bigger, because I was left wanting more (a lot more) after just three bites. The apricot puree was a bit too sweet as well, mostly because the ratio of apricot puree to duck was just too high. While we were served about 5 different sweet courses at the end, the only one that truly stood out to me was the mint sorbet with Fernet Branca and chocolate ganache. It was like the most sophisticated and composed mint chocolate chip ice cream dessert I've ever encountered, yet totally crave-able. As for the other sweet courses - while the egg cream malt was fun and interactive, I found the actual drink to be a little thin. We also received a red pepper cheesecake with strawberry and cashew, which I wasn't particularly fond of; I'm generally a fan of savory elements in desserts, but the red pepper flavor just threw me for some reason.

As you can see, not every course of the tasting menu we had was a home run, but altogether the experience was every bit as exquisite as I had expected. I can appreciate that chef and owner Daniel Humm isn't only in the business of cooking, but also creating unforgettable memories.
This was one of the best meals of our lives... The duck was amazing, the clam soup was worldly, the service perfection. I will not forget this night

I'm going to throw my voice into what is already a very crowded pool of Yelpers before me. 

I've been to Eleven Madison Park three times so far. Twice during the old grid menu and most recently for their NY-centric tasting menu.

I'll spare you the details of each dish as there are too many to remember, but I can say they are all divine, fun and playful. This is cuisine at its highest form, with carefully thought out ingredients, processes, plating and even service. No detail is left untouched. Since the menu changes frequently and surprises await each and every diner, but I will offer a few tips and insights. Because, if you have the opportunity and go, you must. 

-First, you must reserve 28 days out, but if you want to risk it, they do put tables on OpenTable occasionally if you're open to the idea of a spur of the moment experience. 

-If you want to dine at Eleven Madison Park, but don't want the "hassle" of enjoying a 3-6 hour dinner, you can dine at the bar, which usually has seats available and most of the dishes seen on the tasting menu can be found in some for at the bar.

-When you reserve a table, ask for a kitchen tour. Not only will you see how such perfect dishes are created, you'll see just how a true, world-class kitchen operates (sorry if this crushes your dreams that kitchens of this caliber feature the chef screaming at everyone and dishes crashing everywhere). Also, they sometimes will offer you a cocktail of sorts as you see the kitchen, but less I spoil anything more, I'll leave it there.

-During dinner a course of bread will come. You are free to ask for more (I suggest you do) but also to ask for the other butters that may be available, the butters are all in-house and each is unique and delicious. At the time of my last dinner, four separate butters were available, but they originally only bring out two.

-Before you dine, you will be asked if there is an ingredient that you don't like or don't consume. The kitchen is surprisingly adept at developing new dishes or modifying dishes based upon diner preferences and tolerances. Some of the substitute dishes are even better than the dishes they replace.

-I must suggest that you try the wine parings with the dinner. The wines, as expected are paired to each dish, but, as with diners preferences with the food, the wines can also be adjusted based upon your likes and dislikes in wine. The pour are also not too small to feel skimped for the price, nor are they so large like in some pairs that you walk out nearly drunk.

While I'm sure there are many more little tips that diners have experienced, I assure you that if you go, you will enjoy it immensely. It is the highbrow, snooty cuisine that you might expect from one of the best restaurants in the world, but with some of the most friendly and professional service I've ever seen.

So for the last time, if you have the opportunity to go to Eleven Madison Park, DO IT!

Less than a week after making our reservations, Eleven Madison Park won the #5 spot on San Pellegrino's list of the World's 50 Best Restaurants. No, you did not misread that. THE WORLD. So obviously, upon entering the Art Deco building in New York's historic Flatiron District, our expectations were through the roof.

The verdict? Both the meal and the experience were simply incredible, and our collective jaws are still on the proverbial floor.

...

Looking back at my menu, I can see that all the foodie buzzwords were there: "foie gras", "tartare", and "truffle". But, you'll also see "pretzel", "clam bake", and "cheesecake". It's a delightfully odd combination of ingredients, which they execute with seamless transitions from course to course. 

In addition, the showmanship and presentation made for a uniquely memorable experience. One course was brought to us in a picnic basket, another involved a meat grinder, and a third course was set into motion following a very clever card trick. I'd love to do it all over again the next time I'm on the Atlantic Seaboard! 

Tip: If you dine at EMP in the somewhat immediate future and are given the choice between duck or lamb for your entree courses, do your taste buds a solid and opt for the duck. It was dry-aged for two weeks and roasted with honey and lavender, and came out with pistachio, rhubarb, and fennel. I'm not usually a huge fan of duck, as it is oftentimes rather greasy, but this bird was the exception to the rule. Totally life-changing.

I was disappointingly underwhelmed by the food here.  I had high hopes for a special birthday dinner, and left feeling that excellent service, beautiful and creative plating and whimsical presentations in no way made up for the mediocre, and sometimes outright unpalatable food.  Out of 16 courses, there were three that I liked (the surf clam, foie gras and ostrich egg courses), two that I completely despised (the sea urchin "snow" and the red pepper cheesecake) - all the others were just "ok" - not spectacular, not delicious, not knock your socks off amazing - just "ok".  For the price, hype and reputation, I wanted to be wowed, I wanted ot be in love with the food, I wanted to want to return again and again.  I wasn't any of those things.  Save your money, go elsewhere, there are many other restaurants in New York with better food that is memorable for being fabulous, not for being mediocre.

Started from the bottom, now we're here,
Started from the bottom, now my whole team here....

To quote the late great philosopher Christopher Wallace: "Mo Money, Mo Problems" or in this case, more courses, less food.  Eating at Eleven Madison Park has always been on my food bucket list.  Going in, I knew what to expect: artfully crafted food, upper echelon ingredients, and small portions (16 course tasting menu). I just wasn't necessarily blown away by the dining experience and felt slightly cheated of my time (4 1/2 hours) and money (it was free via a Birthday BNO, but the price tag was $195pp).  Not to mention having to call 28 days before the desired reservation date and being on hold for 20 minutes.

Service was phenomenal, they really make it an experience (table side service, magic tricks, and the dinner menu was a complete surprise), and the food is artfully presented.  So why 3 stars?  I wasn't impressed by the food - I enjoyed 2 of the 16 courses: lobster stuffed confit tomato and corn pudding with truffle/buttermilk.  Everything else was just ok.  At one point, each course felt as if we were only getting a spoonful of food every 18 minutes.  I also wasn't taken in by the use of espumas/foams and the bait & switch on the 140 day aged steak.  We were shown a hunk of meat and thought we were going to get a bigger course since it was the "main" entree.  Nope!  The steak portion was smaller than my thumb (Where's the beef?).  It was also amusing to get a picnic basket with 1 beer to share amongst 3 guys.  Overall it was a memorable service and they send you home with a gift (amazing granola in a mason jar), the food didn't leave me with the need to return.  We actually joked about going to Shake Shack afterwards.

Simply the best meal of my life!  I would give it 7 stars if I could. It was expensive but worth every penny.  I never knew that food could be so delicious and creative.  The presentation of each of the 12 courses was so whimsical and unexpected. And although it was a lot of courses it was not too much where you feel so full you cannot handle it.  Each course was a couple of bites - but magical wonderful and interesting bites. And at the end we were invited into the kitchen for a cocktail and to see how it works. Bravo. I cannot wait to try it again for another special occasion !

I went here for my anniversary dinner and couldn't have been happier. This was probably the most incredible (and expensive) meals I have ever had. In summary:
- Unique interactive food experience
- Impeccable presentation of multiple courses
- Excellent service (my water was always topped up within minutes of drinking)
- We received complimentary anniversary chocolates at the end of our meal as a surprise! They were DELICIOUS!

We could only get the first reservation of the night (5:30pm), but it really worked out well. Since we were one of the first people to get there, this meant that every course was a surprise. And trust me, some of the dishes will really surprise you. The whole meal was about 3 hours and we really enjoyed ourselves.

If you're willing to pay the price, the food is absolutely like nothing you've tasted before. Eleven Madison Park lives up to its hype, and the creativity and care put into the food is clear with every bite. The food speaks for itself--simply amazing.

I called for a reservation for my wife's bday. She had been raving about this place and we were in town for her bday last minute. I was not expecting a miracle. I called at 11am and was wait listed. I called back at 630 and waited over one hour before hanging up. Food better be good because the customer service is not.
I really enjoyed my meal here. The cocktails are the bomb. Have I been dying to go back? No. Eating a lot of foam really doesn't make my mouth water. It was fun to try one time though.

Ok, I am SHOCKED to be giving this review. We went for my birthday, and while they seemed to be trying their hardest to provide decent service, everything fell a little short. The first courses were ok, and things were running smoothly. While eating things like a 'long island oyster' doesn't make me feel like I'm paying a ton of money for any great reason, the food was fine. But then, slowly, service started to wane, and we found ourselves waiting WAY too long between courses. We started wondering if they were short staffed, or whether they were short on groceries and needed to run out to pick up a few things. When you are paying the kind of prices this place costs, these 'amusing' thoughts aren't actually that funny. Then, to make it worse, one of the plates in my 'picnic' course came out to me dirty, with mashed carrot smeared on it! They did apologize and bring me a new plate....but are you kidding??? Can I mention again how much this place costs? Finally, they were really scant on meat courses, and my dining partner actually ended up eating two slices of pizza AFTER dinner...and no-he is not an obese glutton (in case you are wondering). Based on their overall reputation, I am guessing this was an off night and an unusual set of maladies for them. But still...I can't imagine returning. It was the most disappointing of all of my fancy birthday meals.

I ate here two years ago for my graduation dinner with my parents. WOW-- this is what I dream about on the regular. What makes Eleven Madison Park, beyond the artfully prepared food, fantastic selection of wines, and serene atmosphere is the service. Every moment of our meal was perfection. When we walked in, I was congratulated by the front of house staff and greeted by my first name. At my place setting was a hand written note thanking us for choosing to celebrate my special occasion with them. Umm Thank YOU for your wonderful hospitality and our extraordinary experience Eleven Mad!! I don't remember exactly what we ate. It included the five course tasting menu and a wonderful two bottles of wine chosen with the help of one of their sommeliers. Everything was presented in the most interesting, creative manner. We were treated exceptionally from start to finish and the food was the best I've ever had. This is definitely a special occasion spot... think engagements, anniversaries, graduations, and milestone birthdays. You will be in fine dinning heaven at Eleven Madison.

Best meal of my life. One of the best experiences as well. Every dish was a delicious work of art that amazed the senses. The service was impeccable and made you feel like royalty. We were there for close to 5 hours experiencing pure dinning perfection. Still to this day we reminisce about our evening at Eleven Madison Park.

Pros
- Really good service
- Interesting dishes

Cons
- None

Every dish really is a surprise. You don't get to see the menu until they bring it to you after the meal. My favorites were this eggy drink, the carrot tartare, the duck, and the foie gras. There's not much to say about this place except bring your wallet and an open mind.

I love the new format, but also loved the old one. Hands down this is my mom's favorite restaurant both before and after the change. Last time we went it was for my birthday and they let us go in the kitchen and watch the food prep and prepared this amazing drink for us. They continue to blow us away each time we visit. Can't wait to go back.

What can I say about this place?  Perfection would be a good start, followed up by a good amount of friendly staff and a fantastic vibe with the focus completely on the food, which starts off as amazing and gets better as the courses go on.

This is an imaginative and creative menu created by a chef who is a master of his game.  This place is ranked number 5 in the world for a clear reason.  I have been to other restaurants in the worlds top 50 list and this stands head and shoulder above those other experiences.

It's one captivating journey that begun with a black and white cookie, but substituted with cheese and finished up with the real deal.  Eleven Madison Park is a culinary journey that I won't forget.
