My wife and I went to celebrate our tenth anniversary at Eleven Madison Park, and had one of the most incredible dinning experiences of our lives!  The NY theme was a hit and the surprises (service and food) kept coming to the very end.  We ended up getting a tour of the kitchen at the conclusion of our meal!  It's no wonder that Eleven Madison Park is such a celebrated restaurant.

I'm always so fickle when it comes to my birthday. "Ugh let me just hide and forget it" usually turns to "maybe just a small dinner & drinks?" which then usually leads to "EFF that, big blowout is the way to go!" and then back to wanting to hide in bed. Evil cycle. This year was no different...except that the boyfriend was planning and plotting behind my back. 

Along with a family dinner, drinks with all of my friends and brunch with a small group (he really did cover all bases!), he also planned dinner for two on my actual birthday, which fell on a Sunday back in April (I know I'm a little late with this review). 

As we walked through the Flatiron area, he asked me if I knew where we were going. I racked my brain for restaurants in the area but couldn't come up with any that justified him wearing a suit. It wasn't until we walked up to the door and I read, "Eleven Madison Park" did it finally hit me. 

W-O-W. 

Upon entering, the smiling hostess looked at me and said, "Vanessa?" to which I nodded, amazed. "Happy Birthday! We've been expecting you." After being seated at a cozy table nestled in the corner of the main level, two glasses of birthday champagne were set down in front of us along with a birthday card. 

We ordered a bottle of wine, picked our main course for the 16 course tasting (we went with the duck) and let the servers and chefs do the rest. 

When the bottle of wine came, our server did the norm, presented the bottle, uncorked it, let the boyfriend have a taste, etc. Then she walked off with the corkscrew....and the cork. 

For those of you that don't know me, I collect corks. 

Seeing my shock, the boyfriend jumped into action and set off after our server to retrieve it. He came back a few moments later and told me the server apologized and said she would bring the cork back shortly. 

What? Wait. Why? I was so confused. It was in her hand, she could have just handed it to him! What was going on!? 

When our server returned moments later, she apologized again for taking the cork and then set it back down on the table...encased in a clear cube. 

Above and beyond. 

Double W-O-W. 

The rest of the night was phenomenal. 16 beautiful courses, a surprise birthday dessert, tour of the kitchen, "frozen" cocktail and jar of granola later we were back where the amazing night first started. Happier than happy but a little sad the experience was coming to an end, we bid the hostesses adieu and went on our way. 

Now I know you're probably wondering why I didn't go into detail about the 16 courses themselves but wouldn't  you rather experience it for yourself?
As a cheese lover, I have to go back five more times to try all their different kinds.

my first Three Michelin Starred restaurant & my boyfriend choose it for our anniversary because it was the only U.S. restaurant in the top 10 on the "World's 50 Best" restaurants 2013 list

they don't offer a menu (until you get a copy of it at the end of your meal), the ONLY dining option (whether it's lunch OR dinner) is a seasonal ~16 course tasting ALTHOUGH you get to choose your main dish (our options were duck or lamb) unless you have food allergies or are pescatarian/vegetarian

the tasting was a PLAYFUL surprise every step of the way! I'm not going to go into details so as not to spoil anyone's future experience BUT i will say that i loved the meal's NYC theme, the duck breast was some of the best i've ever had + COMPLIMENTS TO THE PASTRY CHEF, every roll we had was amazing

although eleven madison park is still not my favorite dining experience ever, i would definitely recommend it!! & yes 16 courses is doable w/o feeling too gluttonous

One of the best meals I've ever had. While other fine dining establishments are good they can also be quite boring. The food at Eleven Madison Park was not only amazing, the whole experience was inventive and playful. I can't wait to go back. I agree with other reviewers that it's in a league of its own.

Update: Came here for a second time a year later and it was still amazing and still one of my favorites of all time. I can't wait to go back again.

Well, well, simply the best. No need to rewrite what has already been written.  

The meal is like a journey through NYC, just don't get caught up on the price and understand it is not just a meal but an experience.  

Enjoy!
Remarkable experience! Outstanding quality of food, service and atmosphere without any pretense. Now that is rare.

We need a fourth Michelin star, a fifth NYT star, and a sixth yelp star. Eleven Madison Park doesn't have any peers. It is in a league of its own. 

Do not try to "prepare" for your evening by reading descriptions of the food. Do not try to predict your meal ahead of time and scan through photographs of previous diners' dishes. Go into the experience as naive as you can be. Allow yourself to be surprised. The staff go to great lengths to create an immersive dining experience and you should place your trust in them. You're paying for it. Don't shortchange yourself. 

The menu + wine pairings + tax + tip will set you back about $400/pp. It's a bargain.

Came here for the tasting menu.  Was seated at 12.40pm and we completed our meal 3 hours later.  It was worth it.  

Took the advise of another reviewer and asked if we could have a tour of the kitchen.  It was amazing watching the controlled chaos that occurs in serving up all these delicious meals.

Enough words have been said by thousands of reviewers in Yelp for this restaurant.  

All I can say to you is 'Do It' and be aware you will probably have to book weeks in advance.

Price wise, EMP is better than Per Se both on cost and the whole culinary experience.

This place seemed unusually classy given that we consumed a dinner that cost less than $10 for the fiancee and I at Prosperity Dumpling the night before.  I could have eaten dinner 60X at that place for just a single meal at Eleven Madison Park.  Think about that, 2 months of above average dumplings or 3 hours of getting served fancy pretentious New American food for 3 hours.  The meal was so long that the person sitting next to us fell asleep during his meal on more than one occasion.  I'm only used to seeing that at Dave Matthews concerts.

It was so worth it, I can't imagine a better dining experience than what we ate on Tuesday night.  There was one point during the meal (I think it was course 11 or 12) where I looked over to the woman and said, "I think this is quite a bargain considering all you get."

I know other yelpers have gone in depth about the menu and surprises and some may find that helpful, but knowing that certain items or interesting dishes were coming before-hand from reading on yelp actually detracted from my overall experience.  The less you know about the dishes, presentation and magic tricks the better.  The woman knew nothing about what to expect and came away floored. 

My palette is generally pretty limited but I tried every single course, if anybody could make me eat tomato water jelly it has to be the crack team at EMP and Daniel Humm.  

Put simply, enter with an open mind and a full wallet and leave with your mind blown and eating halal street carts until your next paycheck.

Ever since I went for my birthday two years ago, every restaurant I've been to after has failed to live up to my experience at EMP.  To this day, I still remember the amazing tomato soup disguised at a cup of clear tea. 

EMP isn't just 5 stars for amazing food, but for the ability to also entertain without going overboard.  For example, they served us a clam bake, and poured water over the stones that were covered in seaweed and smelled of the ocean while we enjoyed our amuse bouche of clams and seafood.  There was a teapot that sat on top of the stone, but we just thought it was decor, until they poured out the most heartwarming, decadent and smoothest clam chowder I have ever tasted that I almost licked my bowl. Some other notable dishes - the lobster is a MUST, foie gras terrine, sea urchin cappuccino, and I even had to hold myself back from a 3rd serving of bread.  

The service was amazing, as they knew my name without even asking, wishing me a happy birthday. My husband (boyfriend at the time) got the best seats in the house, and every single person who served us magically knew it was my birthday and wished me a happy birthday.  I was also greeted with a birthday card!  

My husband and I don't have a high tolerance for a wine pairing for 50 courses, but I have to mention the sommelier.  The sommelier introduced us to some wine pairings that we now buy on our own because it was so memorable.  

I hope per se or alinea will live up to my experience at EMP, because the number 1 restaurant in the world didn't: NOMA

Eating at Eleven Madison Park is more of an interactive dinner theater experience, choreographed and catered by the chef.  We went in December 2012 and had the full tasting menu complete with alcoholic pairings.

When I say Eleven Madison is more of an interactive theater trick rather than just some ordinary expensive dinner, this is because the executors of this experience have incorporated whimsy that appeals to the pathos of the diner.  There was thought, attention to detail. and just enough imagination apparent at the presentation of each well planned course that you were left feeling the four hour extravaganza was moving at a brisk pace .It was most delightful.  The alcohol certainly helped.

Here are some of the highlights of our many (we lost count) coursed meal: a mini clambake at our table accompanied by wee teacup full of light and frothy clam chowder, a cheese course emulating a teeny Central Park picnic compete with pint-sized sodas, a freshly grated carrot salad whence the grating being done we were given our portions on wooden compartmentalized boards and prompted to play with our food shamelessly (& the result a foolproof savory delight),... you get my drift here.  At each juncture diners were drawn in and encouraged to get involved and have fun during the whole affair and the impression was we were in good hands and the food was all excellent.

The seats were cozy and, despite the cavernous art-deco style hall that looks as if it would echo ominously at the drop of a pin, I found the configuration of the tables, lighting, and overall ambiance kept things intimate and fun. A good balance of privacy and company.  We weren't ashamed to take photos of every course to Instagram and we could speak loudly after a few drinks without feeling like people were staring and yet it wasn't silent and awkward either.  

The staff is incredibly nice and the place is unpretentious too despite its lofty status.  My friend invited me out of nowhere and I being ignorant of this place had joined her dressed very casually.  Fortunately I was wearing a proper seeming trench overcoat so I was not rejected on the spot but in the true spirit of hospitality the nice man who took my coat seemed only subtly perturbed upon seeing my sweatpants (albeit nice dark sweatpants), striped casual shirt, and Lacoste slip-ons and did not give me any further cause for humiliation and all the other wait staff ignored my improper attire most nobly and generously for which I was grateful.  I generally feel the Flatiron area, which is near my own hood of Gramercy Park is far more genteel and unpretentious than the characteristics that define the more snooty and yet trashy areas of Manhattan (i.e. Meatpacking) and Eleven Madison is just another great example of excellence without arrogance.  

Price is definitely high and Eleven Madison is hard to get a table at but I wholeheartedly love this place and I have only been once.  It seems great for a special occasion or if you are looking to impress or entertain.  5 stars and thanks Eleven Madison. Would be back as frequently as my wallet would allow if only I could manage to get a table!

As all the other hundreds of reviews say IT IS AMAZING. 

Coming from Australia $195 for 15 courses is a great, no make that amazing deal. Every dish was cooked and presented to perfection. The service faultless. 

Try it. Now!!

We had the most amazing 16 course dinner here.  Each course is unbelievably creative as well as delicious, and there's a great atmosphere.  If you love food, put Eleven Madison Park on your list of must-visit restaurants.  They send you home with a copy of your menu which is the perfect touch!
Awesome place! It was lots of fun and it was enjoyable. I loved coming here. It was great time.

Pretty amazing. The menu is $195 pp and there are 15+ dishes (I lost count).

Probably the best thing I had there was the duck and the carrot tar tar... Everything is great including the gifts towards the end. The menu is fun and refreshing and somethings worked while others didn't, but it was a bombardment of food.

Also, they cater to your likes and dislikes... my gf can't eat heavy cream, so they removed anything that had heavy cream or cheese for her.

I've had the honor/privilege to be invited to dinner at Eleven Madison.  I will never forget how intriguing, theatrical and original this dinner was.  
I need to warn you... this is truely for the curious food critic with a wide array of food pallete.  I can't exactly tell you all what this amazing meal entails but, it incorporates special touches of NYC.....

The BEST period!!! The food, the service and the creativity simply the best.

My pictures: http://shruti-k.blogspot.com/2013/06/a-16-course-scrumptious-lunch.html

Best meal ever?
They are fun and creative and mix a bit of 'show' with the food in a funny nice way. Service impeccable- everyone knows every ingredient cold- wine list world class- pairings were excellent if you prefer that route- we did as its hard otherwise as courses a surprise. We did the chefs tasting at Daniel- trust me this is far more fun- service and food both superior

This is hands-down one of the "funnest" meals I have ever had. Eleven Madison Park recently rejiggered its menu last summer to highlight various culinary aspects of NYC's history, and many of the plates we were served were creative, whimsical takes on some of the bastions of NYC eating.

There is just a tasting menu, priced at $195 pp, and the only choice we were asked to make was a preference between duck or lamb as the entree. Then it's kind of a "sit back, relax, and enjoy the show" type of experience. Standouts included:

1. "Long Island Clam Bake": EMP's take on the summery staple, we were given a creamy clam chowder served in an oriental tea pot on a bed of seaweed, along with various shell fish and buttery parker house rolls. They poured hot water all along the sides of the tea pot to make it steam, and it honestly smelled like hot, briny, summers along the beach. Very inventive. 

2. Carrot Tartare. Towards the beginning of the meal, we noticed our server affixing a meat grinder to the side of our table.. EMP's nod to NYC's steakhouse / beef tartare tradition, except they take these gorgeous carrots and feed them through the grinder right in front of you. Then you get a platter of all these condiments (and by "condiments" I mean items like dried mackerel powder) and mix them all in with your carrot tartare and spread it on toast. SUPER hands-on and fun to eat, I vowed that my future children would only be eating organic carrot puree grown in Hudson Valley soil mixed with mustard-seed oil, pine nuts, chives, and Long Island fleur de sel. No Gerber for my babies.

3. Duck. This was the entree we selected over the lamb, and it was a great choice. They dry age the duck so that the skin separates from the flesh, and what results is this awesome, super crispy duck skin (which they slather with Szechuan pepper). Having eaten a few Peking ducks in my lifetime, I know the old Beijing masters employ a similar method. 

4. Cheese course. This gets points for creativity. They serve the cheese course in a picnic basket, alongside pretzels, grainy mustard, pickled strawberries, and a bottle of Pale Ale (specially created just for EMP). The quintessential NYC picnic, I thought about suggesting we take the whole basket and go enjoy the course outdoors in Madison Square Park. 

5. Chocolate course. This course BLEW MY MIND. Not because of the chocolates (which were obviously delicious), but because they use a MAGIC TRICK to serve you. Because I don't want to spoil the fun and ruin the magic, I won't divulge much. Except that I'm a sucker for card tricks, and this course was a wonderful way to finish our meal.

Overall takeaways: Dining at EMP feels different from dining at other high-end restaurants like Daniel or Le Bernardin. In the latter, the food feels very fussy and you distinctly feel that you are eating something that has 1,000+ ingredients and has probably gone through 4 different stages of cooking to be plated pristinely, drizzled with frou-frou sauce, and placed like the Holy Grail before you.

At EMP, the same probably applies to the food. The difference is, you don't see the effort behind the food. What's on your plate is recognizable, accessible, and fun. It's familiar classics served in an innovative way. 

What's more, the service is phenomenal. At Le Bernardin, every course is served with a sneer. At EMP, I felt like I was eating at the dining room table of extremely hospitable friends. Our servers were easy-going, gregarious, funny, and they laughed at all my bad jokes. Win. 

I will say that it doesn't feel like a meal -- it feels like a production. Because the courses are small and served in rapid succession, the servers are at your table frequently, and it makes it difficult to carry on a real conversation. While each course is served with a degree of excitement and fanfare, as the night wears on (and your stomach begs for cessation), you begin to feel that you are here as an audience to the food: the courses are the stage, and you are meant to be the silent, respectful viewer. 

I enjoyed my experience at EMP, but it is definitely a special occasion dinner, and the type of eating marathon that only be tolerated occasionally. Hats off to our excellent servers, however, for being such fabulous hosts for the evening.

If only there were 10 stars available for Eleven Madison Park... Or even 11, although I don't want to inadvertently make a reference to Spinal Tap. This restaurant is not a parody of anything. It's the real deal, and deftly mixes drama and comedy (well whimsy anyway) to create the best four hour entertainment experience of your life. Maybe not yours, but mine certainly.

I dream of another egg cream intermezzo. Of a second "clambake" with the bivalve-scented steam rising through a nest of sea beans. Of the tiny Parker House Rolls, the warm fresh pretzels, and some kind of puff pastry meets dinner roll hybrid. The beer-washed cheese, served with beer. An entire course comprised of nettles. The card trick. The mint/chocolate/espresso dessert. And on and on and on.

If my bank account and constitution could stand it, I would dine at Eleven Madison Park every week. Perhaps it's best that they would buckle under the strain. That way, every year or two, I can recapture the magic.

I am not as good a reviewer as a lot of others here, but will try.  I dined at EMP last weekend for the lunch tasting.  It was wonderful.  I was a little unsure what to expect & of course had read reviews both good and not so good beforehand.  That always peaks my curiosity then to see what experience I myself have.  

My son and I were pleasantly surprised & delighted at our dining experience here.  We have dined at other fine dining restaurants so we knew what a tasting menu was.  EMP is different than what we've had before.  The service was pretty top notch.  The room is gorgeous and at lunch time on a sunny afternoon, was such a nice atmosphere.  

I have a fish allergy so they substituted a few things but everything they substituted was wonderful.  I don't remember each dish honestly, but there was only one that I didn't like too well, maybe nettles?  Everything else was amazing.  The lobster & duck stood out as "awesome".  The 3 deserts we had were all good & this I have not found before in a tasting menu.  

We asked if we could see the kitchen and we were able to go behind the scenes for a look & were even treated to a special cocktail by one of the guys there.  

All in all, a totally wonderful experience.  Would I go here again, most definitely.  These meals are expensive, but I consider them an experience such as a play or concert or other special occasion.  I hope I can dine here for dinner one day.

The food and drinks are great, they have really good mixologists and definitely almost every dish is a masterpiece...

Maybe it's just me but the design or actually it's simplicity always remind me of those restaurants by the hotels, they are just popular because of being convenient but not because of the quality or service. Sorry 11madison...

One of the greatest culinary experiences.  I took my boyfriend there for his 30th birthday, there was a special surprise which awaited us as we reached our table...I won't ruin it for anyone.

The food....the food....AMAZING. We loved every single bite of it, my favorite might have been the smoke or the mango cheesecake....Nevertheless, we walked out three hours later beyond happy, it was worth every penny.

I visited for lunch because my trip was decently last minute, but I was not disappointed. All the dishes were inventive, the ingredients fresh, the service attentive but not particularly warm. I definitely think the service at Jean Georges was better overall. It's hard to say which restaurant I like better; both were quite good. My only food feedback is while the bread was wonderful, their sweet pastries still need improvement. I did particularly enjoy visiting at lunchtime because EMP's large windows let in the natural sunlight, which beautifully illuminates the restaurant. I had a nice chat with the wine director, Dustin Wilson, about the documentary film he stars in, SOMM. The wine pairings were excellent; the staff was accommodating to my mild food restrictions. I left thinking this meal is one I will remember for awhile.

One of the most stunning dining rooms in all of the city with a kitchen to match.  A wonderful, soaring Art Deco space with a beautiful view of the park, impeccable service and some of the finest food you will eat.  I've dined here on several occasions and have never left without feeling completely swept off my feet.  Snagging a table can be difficult so plan well in advance and don't be surprised if you're seated next someone famous (last time I was there we were across from NBA commissioner David Stern).  The service is attentive, well versed and perfectly calibrated for what can be several hours of fine dining.  Don't be overwhelmed if this is your first time; the staff will navigate you through the menu and are very accommodating.  If you have a special occasion to celebrate (or a healthy bank account) Eleven Madison Park is the perfect destination.

Has to be one of our favorite restaurants in NYC. 

The Sturgeon caviar is a great way to start any meal and it only goes up from there. I also recommend people consider using the upstairs to host nice events in the City. They did a great job.

I planned a trip to New York with my wife for our 3rd anniversary in March and we decided that we had to try one of the top restaurants in the world. We tried making dinner reservations about a month in advance, but there were nothing was available so we had lunch.  

The preset 16 course meal was amazing in every way. Each course from the oyster, sea urchin, foie gras, lobster and duck, to the smaller courses like the cookies, pretzels and malt, was prepared perfectly. The staff was very knowledgeable about each dish and they were able to tell me exactly what I was eating, which I admit, I had to ask more than once. My favorite course was definitely the duck. 

The entire meal felt like a show that you could eat. It was a wonderful experience for me and my wife and we couldn't have asked for a better way to start our anniversary weekend. I wouldn't say it's somewhere I would go back, but it was definitely worth the experience at least once in  my life.

I am long overdue for writing my review of Eleven Madison Park. In fact, I thought I had written one but just realized I hadn't! The shame! The format of dining at EMP has changed recently into a theatrical 4-hour-long meal that costs the same for both lunch and dinner. 

Previously, they offered prix fixe options, which is what I experienced. Fortunately, I'm sure the quality of food and service has not changed, which is why I feel okay to share my thoughts now, even with an overhaul of the meal format.

I can honestly say that dining at Eleven Madison Park was one of the best experiences of my life. Even though at the time I only paid $74 for my meal as opposed to the current price tag of $195, I would return pending financial ability :) I do believe that a meal at EMP is more of an experience than a meal, so I'm not surprised by the change they've made to showcase that.

Everything from the savory and sweet black and white cookies which bookended the meal to the aesthetically PERFECT dishes of food are on par with what EMP represents. 

During my visit, I had the pleasure of being invited into the kitchen for a little Chef's Table dessert presentation from one of the pastry cooks. Having a sneak peak into the kitchen was a truly special experience and gave me additional respect for the food and service at this institution. I can't wait to return!

Amazing presentation for basically all 16 courses. The main dish (duck) was out of this world. It was a little more spectacle than flavor though. Quite good, but probably not worth the steep price ($195 per person).

Hands down the best dining experience both in terms of food and service. We dined here three years ago when it didn't have the fancy Michelin three stars label on the name, but every bit of the creativity of the dishes and service standard indicates they will be there very soon. I am very happy to see it finally landed on the highest spot in the best restaurant in the world list from North America.

So, this place was amazing. Service was some of the best I have ever experienced. Food was great! So why not perfect? Well here is the thing. By the end of the meal, I was full, however each course was so tiny that although the taste was amazing, you wish you had more. Some courses were literally one bite. I would probably prefer fewer courses, larger portions. FYI, there was 16 courses. And once in a while you would get something that was not your favorite.  Dinner took over 4 hours. VERY expensive. $195 per person and an additional $145 for wine pairings.  I think I liked Le bernardin more overall, but that's probably because I am huge seafood lover. Ambiance was definitely an older crowd. You could probably find a better food "Value" somewhere else, but they definitely excel in creating an experience in making you feel like the king of the world.

The best meal of my life.

The food, the whimsy, the black and white cookies, the wine, the apertifs, the rolls (oh, those rolls), the picnic basket, the brandy, the morels, the DIY tartare, the approachable waiters, the magic tricks, the chocolate salty pretzels, the clambake, the duck done right in so many ways, the plating, the atmosphere and the many other things I can't possibly list here made this experience worth every single penny.

Amazing meal through and through. There's really nothing to say that hasn't been said before. By far the best meal I've experienced in my young life. Was taken here for my birthday last year and seeing as I've been dying to come here for years, I was more than ecstatic. Suffice to say, this was the greatest gift I've ever received. 

We sat down for dinner right when they opened and didn't stumble out in a food induced stupor till a little less than 4 hours later. This was prior to the new tasting menu when they still had their whole New York theme going on: clam bake, black and white cookie, egg cream prepared table side, etc. We were even treated to a kitchen tour and were surprised with a jack rose sorbet? cocktail made from liquid nitrogen. I even received a card which I got Daniel Humm to sign as he made his rounds to each table. 

The service was impeccable matching the incredible food and I would return in a heartbeat. The homemade gifts of granola and Twix-like bars were a nice touch to end a fantastic meal. Definitely an experience I'll cherish. Hell, I might even frame that menu I got.

This is by far one of the best restaurants I've been to in the city. Impeccable service, outstanding food and overall just a really lovely restaurant. We had a 15 course meal paired with some fantastic wines. Make sure you build up a huge appetite before dinner so you can get through every course!

As much as I loved the experience of going to Eleven Madison; i'd have to give it 4 stars. 
Reservation needed to be exactly 28 days in advance. i called for the 27th day and, by then, it was fully booked. 

Service was impeccable. They were very attentive, and observant. The waiters/resses were very knowledgeable of what and where the ingredients came from. They truly made the experience special and made me feel like a princess for the night. I would've given them 5 stars just for the service.

Drinks: My friend and I decided to let the bartender decide. We had 2 different drinks. Mine was a gin mix with ginger, mint, and etc. I personally don't like ginger but i definitely loved the drink. it had a nice kick to it. My friend had something different but i can't recall what she had. the ingredients were almost the same but they both tasted different. we actually joked around saying how the drinks matched our personality. 

Food: 
Presentation: was beautiful and very creative. With each dish that came out, i felt like i was traveling the world from the beach, to japan, on a picnic, and etc. Great at making the meal come full circle. 

Decor: i loved the fact that it had a 1920s up-class feel to it; like i was living in the Great Gasby era. 

Taste: is what made me drop a star. Although i did love the food experience and it also confirms my dislike for Foie Gras, they were able to make a perfect balance between the foie gras, black truffle and asparagus. Unfortunately, by the 5th course, everything after that started to taste too salty for my liking.The Ribeye, that i was surprisingly looking forward to, was too overwhelming and salty, i had to stop eating. The textures and food started to feel/taste the same between the dishes. By the end of the night, i probably down 7 - 8 cups of water.

Our dinner lasted about 3 hours. 5:30 - 8:30pm. It was definitely an experience i'll always remember and definitely worth trying.

Why to waste words, I will make it short.

Great atmosphere, beautiful interior, extraordinary dining experience with tasting menus and wine for me and my wife. Especially love their seafood!

Well done.

Greetings from Greggy

I feel terrible writing a three star review but that's really how I felt about the meal. 
To begin, the service is everything you hope and expect a place of this caliber and reputation to be. It was that good. The tables are comfortable and we felt pampered in the service aspect. The table next to us was celebrating a special occasion (birthday) and they got a cute little card and a tour of the kitchen shortly after sitting ( it was a cute touch and I was jealous). Honestly, the food just didn't cut it for me, it was just okay. It started out strong with the oyster, sea urchin, surf clam, and little neck clam keeping me in seafood heaven. I was particularly fond of the clam bake and broth-I thought it was really cute. The carrot tartare was fun, but didn't "wow" me in flavor. It all went down after that- lobster, salsify, beef, greensward, malt, celery root, sheep's milk, pretzel, chocolate. Some were good, some were bad, none were amazing. I think my big issue is that both the savor and sweet items with foam tasted the same, and it wasn't good. Additionally, because of the fact that it was just "ok" I felt myself getting really antsy at the 3 hour mark. We were out of there in 4. Novelty wise, I loved the cheese, pretzel, beer, and dried fruit that came in a picnic basket. The cheese was good and I loved the presentation. In the end, my fiancé really enjoyed the experience and food. I enjoyed the experience and thought the food was okay. I can't say I regret dropping all of that money, but I can't say I would do it again either.

I ate at EMP over a year ago for my wife's bday and it was one of the most memorable meals we've ever had.  Not only was the food was prepared to perfection, the creativity in each course made the meal a truly unique experience.  Service was impeccable and the chef came out in the middle of our meal and greeted patrons at every table.  

I don't think there is anything I can add that hasn't already been said about the food, services, and the overall experience.  For a special occassion, EMP should definitely be on the top of your list.

My wife and I had a fabulous dining experience here last Saturday for lunch.  This was in the top three, maybe even the best dining experience we have ever had.  There were fifteen courses over three and a half hours.  Every one of them was absolutely fantastic with the freshest, most unique ingredients we have ever had, each bursting with wonderful flavor and each presented beautifully.  The staff could not have done a better job, timing everything perfectly but in a relaxed, unpretentious way.  As one might expect, the courses were small, but in total, much more than we should have eaten.  We were happy every step of the way.

From the savory cookie at the beginning, to the Duxbury Oyster with Wood Sorrel, buckwheat and mignonette; Surf Clam with fava bean, lemon and green garlic; Clam Bake with Little Neck clam, Whelk, Parker House rolls and chowder; White Asparagus marinated with Teff Crisp and lemon;  Carrots, ground at the table in a meat grinder, with (9) condiments all mixed together by us; Lobster with Snap peas and Morels;  Nettles (yes nettles) with creamed and fingerling potatoes and goat cheese; Grilled beef with Mushrooms, Amaranth (a kind of crunchy, delicious seed) and bone marrow with braised oxtail and potato; Greensward (cheese) with pretzel, mustard and dried fruit and a bottle of Ale, all served from a picnic basket; Egg cream with vanilla and seltzer; Crème cake with apple sorbet, walnut and white pepper; Cheesecake with mango and peanut; Chocolate covered pretzel with sea salt and finally; Apricot with chocolate and a final cookie.  Oh and I forgot, somewhere in the middle, a wonderful roll with the flakiness of a croissant and two types of butter.  Oh and also somewhere near the end a bit of Apple brandy.

At one point we were offered a visit to the kitchen where one of the chefs prepared a mixed drink for us that she called "Widows Kiss, a very potent drink" with apples infused with angostura bitters, chartreuse syrup, apple jack sorbet and frozen apple brandy.  Amazing.

We ordered a few wines by the glass, my wife staring with a Chardonnay and me with a Chenin Blanc.  The pours were very generous, so from there we ordered glasses to share with a wonderful Puligny-Montrachet, then a 2007 Premier Cru burgundy and finally a very nice Saint-Emilion. 
 
After applying a very nice gift certificate, the bill was still eye-popping but worth every penny.  In fact to me, for this kind of experience I would have paid more.  We both went home and took a nap.  An incredible experience.

Reposted from TripAdvisor: 
"So Much Fun"
Reviewed May 4, 2013

We dined at Eleven Madison Park last week on an employee incentive trip to NYC. There were 4 of us and we had the tasting menu with wine. Total bill was about $1600.

Eleven Madison Park nails the prix fixe gastronomique menu concept in a very fun and enjoyable way. Honestly one of the hardest reservations I've ever tried to get, I had very high hopes for the experience, and was completely satisfied.

By now the concept of a 15 course tasting menu has been done to death. To keep it fresh and interesting is a real challenge, and chefs around the country are doing culinary gymnastics to solve this problem. I had heard that Daniel Humm had been experimenting with some ingredient matrixing and other terrible ideas to get over this "writer's block," but thankfully he has chosen a different route, and it works.

In essence, the staff focuses on the fact that lighthearted, purposefully charming, and only slightly ironic at times. This is what they are selling and it comes across as effortless and polished. The menu starts out serious (oysters with caviar) and you think that has set the tone and the salads that follow are along the same vein, but a note of whimsy begins to creep in. By the 6th course, you are looking at a picnic basket with a bottle of beer, some faux-paper plates, pretzels and you're thinking "what just happened?"

Tasting menu's should be a chef's meditation on place. The places where the ingredients originate, what they say to and about each other when presented in a dish, and the sum total of which should give you a sense of the place you've just visited. This is exactly what Eleven Madison Park delivers in such a fun way.

The night we visited the chef's meditation was a trip to New York, hence the picnic basket. Its also why we had New York egg creams prepared tableside as the first of the dessert courses. Its why we totally expected a carpaccio or steak tartare dish and were blown away and intrigued when it came out as a Carrot tartare again prepared tableside in a small sausage grinder. Hilarious but subtle, too. The final dessert dish tied it all together but to tell you would be to ruin the surprise, so I'll let you see it for yourself.

The service was almost flawless with the only wrinkle being alcohol served to someone who wasn't drinking and had made it clear to the steward. Not a big deal for us, but could have been for someone else.

We had dined at Del Posto earlier in the week (see that review) and the contrast couldn't have been more obvious. Give Eleven Madison a try, you'll talk about the experience for years to come.

It's been a year now, but I'm just realizing I never wrote a review for this place. My girlfriend and I ate here as our "last meal" before leaving New York. I won't try to remember all of the details of the meal, but just recall the highlights that have stuck with me. 

The decor is fabulous, with an old world power and new world cool vibe. 

The food was incredible. I don't remember everything but I do remember for our main course we were offered to have an entire lavender smoked duck brought to our table and carved in front of us. Oh my God it was incredible. It was visually stunning. I even remember the banker sitting behind me gloating about how often he spends thousands of dollars at this place shut his trap and marvel at our bird. 

Everyone was so gracious. I'll never forget this part. After we had finished coffee our server came over with a bottle of good cognac and told us the city would miss us and plopped it down on the table and told us to drink as much as we wanted. I don't know if they do this often, and I don't care. It mean't something to us. We drank our fill and walked out just having one of the most memorable meals of our lives.

As good as it gets. 
My expectations were very high yet I was still blown away. Dining at EMP is truly an experience. It started with the call confirming my reservation, the man I spoke with was polite and took his time. He asked if I was dining at EMP for a special occasion and I mentioned it was my girlfriend's birthday, not thinking anything of it. It was pouring rain that night and we walked in dripping wet (expecting to sneak to the bathroom to dry off). Instead, the EMP staff were waiting for us with fresh towels. Our table was ready immediately, and there was a hand written card with my girlfriend's name on it, thanking us for sharing our special occasion with EMP. At the other 3 Michelin Star restaurants in NYC the wait staff, while excellent, comes off as snoody or stuffy, but not at EMP. We didn't order wine but rather stuck to cocktails and beer. They actually have a extensive beer list and we enjoyed speaking with the head of their Beer Program who mentioned they have their own Beer Cave. Then the 16 (more like 20) course dining experience began, and it was remarkable, service and food at another level. Each dish brought a unique twist to the overall theme. 

Can't wait to return for the new menu!

I first visited Eleven Madison Park probably 6 years ago with my wife for lunch after having been there also for lunch with a colleague about 6 months earlier. I was blown away by the attention to service and the quality and innovative food choices. Trust me we never miss a chance to return and experiece it each year for lunch or dinner whichever fits for us. It is so clear why it is now the top American restaurant on the San Pellegrino 50 Best Restaurants in the World listing. We have been to almost half of the top 10 and we did experience El Bulli in its full glory about 9 months before it closed but let me tell you we certainly have a gem right here in NYC!

My fiance and I ate here in the spring last year. I loved the menu! It was great you that just pick the "category".

My favorite dish here is the little egg thing. 

Also, if I remember correctly, the drinks here were fabulous.

I was fortunate enough to attend a wedding here and basically have a mind blowing experience. The  appetizers were fantastic and so were the drinks, I was too busy talking as compared to reading a menu so what I remember is sketchy as far as names.  I do remember being blown away by all the courses at dinner, dessert and then THE cake. It was the best cake I have ever had. Amazing. The highlight by far was the wine that paired with every course, there was alot of courses. The wines were each an experience and this meal comes close to rivaling the best meal I ever had, that goes by far to Zuberoa in Spain.

Eleven Madison Park was good, but did not meet our expectations. Based on the reviews, my husband and I were anticipating an extrodinary meal, but several of the courses did not work. Conceptually, the food was fun and interactive, but lacked in execution. The lobster course was an exception, as it was memorable and  spectacular. Try the coffee siphon; it was perfect and a great show. Overall, a fun food experience.

The highlight of the meal for us was the excellent work of the sommelier. We really wanted to take him home with us. The pairings - both beer and wine - were wonderful. I especially enjoyed the clam bake course clam chowder with the champagne/white sherry concoction. 

The NYC themed meal was a bit cutesy at times. The black and white cookies at the beginning and end, the clam bake, the carrot in the meat grinder, "the picnic" cheese course, the magic trick dessert... but the food made up for the more precious moments. While some things seemed to work better than other things, I appreciated the ideas. The DIY carrot course was an interesting idea but ultimately not very exciting. But then I'll never know how it was intended since we were supposed to put it together ourselves. 

It's actually rare that the best course of a meal for me is the main course at places like this - but here I have to say that the duck main course was absolutely perfection. Best duck I've ever had. I will probably never eat duck again because I can't imagine it could be anywhere near as good as that. 

The service of the sommelier alone made up for any minor flaws in service otherwise. Our main waiter took himself too seriously but then I guess I've come to expect that in New York at high end places. Several of the waiters who presented various courses stood out, some good some bad - oddly since it's not usually something I notice. The restaurant seated us earlier than our reservation, which was nice. 

I would say this is a good place to go for people from abroad who want a more American high end dining experience.

I went here for my birthday a couple of months ago. The experience left me in a loving mood and full of laughter. Daniel Humm in one word, is a savant. With a knife in his hand, he conducts an orchestra of flavors that blend endlessly. Eating his preparations was the equivalent of listening to Beethoven's 5th for the first time. Chef uses so many techniques, both classical and cutting edge. It isn't also just about taste.  The plating was really like edible art where each dish was meticulously planned and executed. 

One dish I remember was a pork belly with hoisin sauce and cherry. The salt and fat from the pork meshes with the acidity of the sauce and cherry. My eyes, confused at first, were baffled by what the palate had bestowed upon me.

I also had a lobster dish with cous cous and grilled avocado. No real surprises here until you bite into the most succulent and tender tail...ever...

The manager happened to be my host for the evening and effortlessly made their rendition of NY orange cream. Smooth, balanced and sophisticated in its simplicity. 

One amuse bouche was actually cognac...they leave it at the table and say take as much as you want. 

The service is excellent and not too uptight. They are laid back but know their stuff. Wine pairing was terrific...hell the soda pairing was great.

Overall, I see why EMP got #5 on the worlds 50 best this year. If you want magic in an art deco setting, this is your place. Eleven Madison Park, you stole my heart and took my breath away.

Truly the quintessential dining experience. Service and decor were impeccable, as I expected of a restaurant in this price range, but the focus of the night was clearly the food - as it should be. Fifteen courses, each more amazing than the last, were as appetizing to the eyes as they were to the tongue. Not only were the plates beautiful, but it was also evident that there was so much creativity that went into their planning. 

Some highlights: the "clam bake" with a teapot of chowder and sinfully soft bread rolls, carrot "tartare" with all the toppings, a beer-inspired picnic basket, earl grey panna cotta with a secret dish underneath, and of course the legendary chocolate covered pretzels that I ate despite being stuffed to the brim. There was even a card trick in there, somewhere. My friends and I were very amused. The muesli/granola as a parting gift was also a nice touch, and made a great breakfast the next morning.

Eleven Madison Park is part of the cream of the crop of the elite restaurants in NYC. I consider myself extremely lucky to have been able to eat here. If you have the means and the time, it is not an experience to be missed.

Why can't I win the lottery so that I can afford to eat here all the time? Life is not fair sometimes! I have only been here once and I can say that everything was perfect--the atmosphere, the service and especially the food. It doesn't get much better than this.

Best Burger I ever had! 

I also got the cheesy fries and wacky sauce! My kids got the chicken finger blast off platter and seemed to like it just fine!

Will come back again, wanna try the ribs!!!

This was the best dining experience I have had in NYC. The food itself was obviously amazing. We did the 4-course menu before the new menu format, and the duck is a MUST!

On top of that, the staff was very warm and welcoming--not snooty and pretentious like a lot of top-tier restaurants. It was my dates birthday dinner, and he as wished happy birthday as soon as we walked in, and there was a bday card waiting for him at the table. The sommelier spend a lot of time helping us pick out wines and was very sensitive to budget and didn't just offer one of the most-expensive wines. He also brought us out a list of the wines we had along with some suggestions of places to go to take wine classes. 

I could go on and on about how excellent the experience was. I would like to try the reinvented menu for comparison.

The very best tasting in NYC. The very best meal I've had, period.  And oddly an excellent value.  We had just done the chef's tasting and pairing at Le Bernadin the month before with half the courses for twice the price, and EMP blew them away by a long shot. 

My boyfriend and I came here on my birthday 3/31.  We were excited to eat because we're both chefs in NYC and have known tons of people who spent time in the kitchen here and always wanted to come.  From walking through the doors I was immediately greeted and wished a happy birthday.  

The tasting was personalized, and the service was spectacular, which I expected after everything I've read and heard. But the food- oh my god. There was humor and whimsy to the courses, it was such a great progression.  Tableside carrot tartare, clambake, picnic basket, and magic tricks while showcasing brilliant technique and with no dedication to fine dining lost. But it was the flavors- so great, so perfectly executed, so balanced, it was astonishing.  16 courses and not one felt like a throwaway. I even heard my boyfriend who doesn't like anything mumble, "that's so good" after the first bite. 

We were invited back to the kitchen, passed the world's biggest server station- to see their giant brigade and enjoy a boozy cocktail with liquid nitrogen meringue and even more personalized banter about our restaurants and the industry. I run a 5 man line, they run a 5 man garde manger. It was stunning. 

We had to hold fire for some courses for bathroom breaks and I needed a cigarette as this was better than secks and magical. The meal ended  TWO HOURS AND 45 MINUTES later with their signature granola and a sweet little candy bar in a happy birthday box. 

I intend on framing my copy of our menu as a reminder of what I do and what greatness looks like in this industry.

To caveat this review:  I went to EMP last summer before their reinvention and I went only a month after eating at Per Se, so that might have spoiled my opinions of all other food for a long time.
We got the tasting menu with the wine pairings and everything was amazingly good.  The reason I'm giving it four stars is because the staff was sort of distant... a little bit like they were rushing us along, which I wouldn't expect from a restaurant like this.
The food was incredible, not only the presentation, ingredients and actual taste, but the creativity that went into each dish.  As a born and bred NY girl, I really appreciated the use of Mid-Atlantic food 'memes': a EMP version of a clam bake, NY sweet corn, and NJ blueberries among other foods that I've grown up around and come to associate with home.  The food was close to being perfect in every way, I feel like a jerk for the four stars, but I guess I'm doing it for a reason to go back.
It seems that they've reimagined the menu with a more whimsical trend (I read in an article last September that they do magic tricks?  Hope they still do that, I am a huge fan of playfulness.)
Looking forward to my second review!

This was without question the best dining experience I have ever had! We went at 10:00 p.m. for the sixteen course tasting menu and did not leave the restaurant until almost two in the morning! It was surprising, unique, filling, delicious, but most of all, it was fun! My favorite part was the magic trick! I won't say anymore. 

We left completely stuffed, and we were given a jar of their homemade granola as our parting gift.

Eleven Madison Park is everything you would want from a fine dining experience, without the uncomfortable pretentiousness that is often unavoidable in these types of restaurants.

11 Madison Park deserves a pass mark at best. Over staffed with an under qualified team, dangerously undercooked lobster and overly jealous plate clearing were only a few of the many disappointments we encountered. Our strong sommelier saved the evening but he disappeared halfway through our experience to deal with the increasing patronage. A fellow reviewer questioned the dessert card trick as genuine and I agree that this was contrived and ruined what was the most delightful chocolate surprise in the dessert jewel box. We found it highly amusing when we were shown the aged beef for a third time, particularly given we had just finished that course and were enjoying the clever do-it-yourself 'picnic' so did not need convincing of the age of the beef we had just been served 10 minutes ago. Please pay attention! When challenged on the undercooked lobster, not a whisper from the kitchen, an apology from the floor and front of house could not have cared less whether or not we enjoyed our meal when we collected our coats. 

We have recently dined in 5 of the top 50 restaurants in the world and 11 Madison Park had better watch out - in our opinion it's ranking is undeserved.

AMAZING 15 course meal!!! It was an extraordinary experience of dining.  The best foie gras I've ever had. Lobster dish was to die for!!! the dining experience was for both the eyes and taste buds. Every course was fun, gorgeous and delicious!!! I definitely recommend the wine pairing for the complete experience.  Be prepared to paid a hefty amount. In the end, it's all worth it, especially if you are a foodie!!! Great staff and attn to details.

Hands down one of the most unique and special dining experiences I've ever had. We came to celebrate a special occasion, and this place should definitely be reserved for that, and ideally with someone who's willing to be a little adventurous. Even though we called at 9am on the dot, 28 days in advance, the only reservations available were very early or very late. Given dinner lasts 3.5 hours, we opted for the earlier time. What impressed me the most about Eleven Madison was the creativity and effort that went in to each dish. Every dish had a unique element, and throughout the meal, we continued to be surprised both by flavor and presentation. Our menu was definitely seafood focused, which was fine by me. If you haven't been since the menu change, do yourself a favor and don't read all the Yelp reviews which detail every single fun aspect on the menu, because the best part really was the anticipation and surprise of seeing the next dish come out. Service was perfect. Very impressed with the entire experience but I guess for a meal of that price you shouldn't expect anything less.

and there............my verdict: a meal here is terribly moreish!
excellently trained staff that worked together like well-oiled machinery.
the pacing of the 16 course degustation menu was perfect.
food was freshness personified with a creative and interactive slant.
an outstanding overall package bar none!

as we collected our coats and walked out through the revolving door, with a heavy heart, i can't help but promised:" i'll be back!"

just when you think it's all over.....they gift you a jar of their homemade muesli(as a morning after reminder), let you takeaway the chocolate pretzels(covered with sea salt) and sweet b&w cookies with apricot that you can no longer stuff down your throat, present you a nicely printed menu for keepsake and as per my request, their custom made decks of magic cards.

the bill was a pleasant surprise! 
$195++ for a 16 course degustation lunch.
judging by the food, service and ambience(plus no jackets required!), this was value for money indeed!

by the time we reached sheep's milk, food comatose had set in and i know not what i eat.
or maybe i was still mesmerized by the magic performance prior to this?
i think it was a light cheesecake with earl grey and honey.

so somewhere here, the professional as can be, staff of all trades, pulled an unexpected magic trick on us!
with a mere deck of cards, each card depicting a flavour of the chocolates that they serve.
you choose a card, put it back in the deck, hocus pocus, she shows you the flavours that you won't be eating today, then shows you the card you chose and thus your chosen flavour and wala, you lift the dish below your sheep's milk dessert to reveal the chocolate that you have chosen!
simple yet entertaining for the uninitiated.

maple, was like our ice kacang back in SG, and thus it was the least impressive of the lot.

malt, was like sparkling horlicks, surprisingly good!

greensward, came in a picnic basket, you explore and lay out as if you were on a picnic.
unfortunately, right about now i accidentally knocked over the flower vase that was hidden from view behind the picnic basket!
dagger stares, perhaps?!
not quite.
in fact, they were so nice about it.
they immediately cleaned up the mess i made.
and swiftly reassured me i was not the first and probably will not be the last.
what can i say?
every dish serves a purpose here!

beef(or you can choose duck), was nothing in size like the block of meat they showed us.
thank god for that!
the bite size portion was all we can eat.
you also get a side of rich consomme and a oxtail, foie gras mash with it.

whilst waiting for the beef course a quick toilet break was in order.
and low and behold, a new napkin awaits you upon your return to the table!

salsify, may not satisfy,  those who don't like black pudding but i was.

the presentation of the aged and well marbled block of meat will leave you drooling.

lobster, my soft spot for thee.
easily the best dish for me!

carrot, winner of creativity.
firstly, a manual meat grinder is attached to your table.
what's up???
then a custom made wooden block containing a mixing area and an assortment of condiments arrives.
next, sweet thin carrots get ground and served on your mixing block.
you then choose what condiments you want and mix them together.
bon appetit.

foie gras, you have a choice of having it seared or in pate form.
but the accompanying crispy wafer thin potato skin wins!

clam, serve in two parts.
firstly, in a huge clam shell sitting on sand.
then as a fancy chowder served in a teapot.

sea urchin, simply umami uni!

crab, clean taste, not much there but this is just the beginning.

oyster, perhaps too much greenery for some?
and also, i'm not a big oyster fan.

cheddar, a savoury b&w cookie with apple, served in a gift box, to start the ball rolling.

your table is ready, please follow me.
a thorough explanation of how our lunch will progress followed.

please have a drink at the bar while we get your table ready.
we opted for a refreshing cucumber drink and a strong ass ginger ale.

may i know the name that your reservation is under?

can we take your coats please?

we were hanging around outside the revolving door as we were early.
spying within, they were all gathered for a briefing.
a couple arrived shortly after us and went straight in, so we followed suit.

EMP was the first meal that i successfully booked via open table for my recent trip to NYC.

as you can see for yourself, my world has turned topsy turvy after dining here!

We had the 16 tasting menu, which is the only option at this place. So, it is basically a super deluxe standardized production series for the kitchen.
Service is impeccable, they change setting for each of the items in the tasting menu. 
The first items, in the seafood/appetizer section were delightful. The clams, the lobster, the uni had balanced flavors and were interesting. Te clam chowder broth was a bit too salty, maybe was combination with the clam brine
It started going downhill after the carrot purée. They give you a marketing gig about the soil that carrot was grown, which made it sweeter. They place a meat grinder on the table, and they grind the cooked carrot in front of you, then you are supposed to mix about 9 different spices, ingredients along with carrot vinagrete, and mustard oil. It did not taste good at all, and I love carrots, eat it all the time. The flavors were very off.
The picnic basket was also disappointment, it lacked a tasty component, and the squash mustard was horrible, not good match in flavor. It was basically pretzel, a very small piece of cheese and a small block of dried fruit that did not complement much the cheese.
Then one of the servers come out with a huge slab of ribs (probably about 20 lb piece), and comes with the marketing gig that it is a 140 days aged that tastes wonderful, etc... We looked forward to our main course, and then what we receive is a very tiny piece, probably no more than 1.5 inch big,  and had braised rib on the side etc to make the dish look more Volumous. This tasting menu is $195 before tax, you would think that they could spare a bit more of this precious ingredient that they made the effort to market to us as so good.
The Waldorf salad type dessert was also not that pleasant combination, celery for dessert? That is a far reach... The other dessert was a cream soda, and liquid cheesecake. We love dessert, but did not enjoy the ones offered, perhaps the chocolate pretzel was the best of all, but that is such a cheap item that requires very little cooking skill.
Overall, it was not worth the amount we paid, too many items in the dishes  were too starchy (which are generally the cheapest ingredients you can buy). Maybe we from California are used to have more fruit and vegetables in our diet, also if they did not come with that huge slab of meat, it probably would make it a bit better.
It was an interesting experience , but I would not go back again nor recommend to anyone.
Goat Cheese pop sickle with Beet Marshmallow...this ain't no disco

I would have to say that this is one of my favorite restaurants in NYC which is a huge statement. Further, I have eaten at this restaurant on several occasions-twice before the first menu change.  The third time I ate at this lovely establishment it was horrible. Not only was the service bad, but there were a few cardinal sins violated. One, with three dishes uneaten at the table all waitstaff should be trained to realize that that typically means the mean was not good. The best chef I ever worked for on opening day of the restaurant for the next month did not cook one meal. Instead, he sat by the trash can with a pad of paper and a pen writing down which dishes were going into the trash barely eaten. However, although this experience sounds awful and it was I am so loyal to this restaurant that essentially even an experience as bad as that one could not prevent me from rating this establishment the #1 restaurant to watch out for in NYC. Daniel Humm gets it. You get up to go to the bathroom and you feel like a queen/king, all the waitstaff stands against the edge of the wall.

Wow. What an extraordinary experience. Loved all of the seafood dishes (special nod to the parker roll/clam chowder). I thought the foie gras was out of this world. Loved the cheese picnic basket.

The service was out of this world. Our sommelier was awesome and knowledgeable and our waitstaff was attentive. Would go back!

Overall, an exquisite dining experience, on par with my meals at places like Per Se and Le Bernadin.  I came for lunch on a Friday.

Decor and Service:  A beautiful room in a classic art deco space.  Tables in the dining room are well spaced: at no point, did I feel like I was intruding on others' conversations, and the overall noise level was at a minimum (in fairness, it was lunch, so there wasn't much bar noise).  The service was friendly and appropriately attentive without being pushy.  

Food: Overall, the savory courses were wonderful.  Chef Humm puts out food that is beautiful to behold and to eat.  The dessert courses were good but did not stand out as superior.  The pace of the courses was nicely spaced, and the progression of dishes was a well-considered arc, with touches like beef consomme or the egg cream that not only cleansed the palate but announced a shift to then next section of the menu.

My biggest concern about their current tasting menu is that the overall experience is still trying to define itself.  Gone is any introduction that defines this as Chef Humm's take on the food of New York.  The course to course descriptions to define the New York relevance of various dishes were erratic, delivered at some tables but not others, for some courses but not others.  Is this still felt to be a unifying theme? If not, then some of the more gimmicky courses (the picnic basket, the carrot tartare, the card trick) seem out of place at best.  I'd urge the restaurant to disregard NYT critic Pete Wells - sage advice always - and put its vision forward with confidence and pride.

Just to keep it short because words can't describe it. Being a regular tasting menu patron everywhere, and having gone with a large party (who also frequent tastings), even consisting of a CIA trained chef, the food was absolutely amazing. The only part I didn't like was having to make a painful choice between the duck and the 158 day aged rib eye! We chose the duck...the only word I can think of to describe the duck (and all courses) is "exquisite". The whole meal was impeccable. Nothing over the top with unrecognizable molecular gastro deconstructed courses, just amazing modern cuisine. I have no problem understanding how they received three stars and are ranked the 10th best in the world. HIGHLY recommended and all three Michelin stars are definitely earned! Oh, and if they still have it, we will be going back for the ribeye(I can't -not- taste a 150 day aged ribeye).  Oh, and it's not stuffy either. Very laid back as far as atmosphere goes, which was a surprise (but a good one).

It truly is an experience.  Its an event.  Its amazing.  Your not eating LOTS of food, but its not about that.  Your pretending to be a grown up, the service is over the top, and while you may want a pizza after, the tastes are amazing.  The pomp and circumstance give the place a pass for tiny portions that are straight out of Oliver Twist.  Still, make sure your into the night - its going to be a 4-5 hour dinner and a constant barrage of waiters and waitresses who seem as if they were conceived only to serve you the two small pieces of protein you will wind up getting.  
You will hear the waiter banter - almost adnauseum - about what their take on fish is, what their take on a piece of bread is, what their take is on a sweet dish.  Its gets to be a bit much.  And be mannered - dont fart, don't chew with your mouth open, dont talk loudly or gawk at the couple next to you (yes those are REAL diamonds).  Just enjoy.

Cross it off the bucket list! The food was heavenly and the service was impeccable. A little stiff around the collar but I guess that comes with fine dining. Better idea to come for lunch because the lighting was too dark for my SLR to take pictures and there's a no-flash rule, understandably. Definitely would come back with the amor once the big paychecks start rolling in.

I give Eleven Madison Park five stars for creativity and presentation, three stars for taste.  It took about a month to get a lunch reservation for which they took my credit card number in case I didn't show up.  Of course I was going to show up to see what the big deal was about.  The menu was a grid of different ingredients.  I picked lobster as one of the ingredients and the pieces of lobster were tender, artistically presented with some kind of blackened vegetable.  The orange milk shake that was one of the amuse bouche was pretty interesting.  I picked chamomile as my dessert ingredient and the dessert was surprisingly good.  I am trying to recall what the chamomile dessert was-- I think it was a spicy sorbet.  If you get a reservation and have about three hours and $100 to spare, definitely go to Eleven Madison Park to experience the lunch.  A place that will impress a date, for sure.  Or just go with a friend.   It's not as much about the food as the New York experience, in my opinion.

What can I say about EMP that hasn't already been said? Wow. Without a doubt, the best dining experience my fiancée and I have ever had, separately or together. 

We went here for my birthday three months ago. Timing the reservation just correctly is not easy, but maybe I lucked out because it was a Monday. The flawless service started as soon as we walked in, from the coat check to the understated opulence of the ground floor location of the restaurant, to the personalized birthday card waiting at the table for me. 

We started out with drinks, an oyster-infused beer for me and a cocktail for her. As an aside, I don't know what that beer was called, but it was one of the best beers I've ever had. 

I'm vegetarian and informed the staff, and they were excellent in accommodating me. I don't remember half the dishes we ate, but each of the meat dishes was accompanied by an appropriate vegetarian substitute for me, and they all tasted incredible. The highlights were the beet puree, NY smoked vegetables, carrots with ten condiments, wild mushroom entree, a picnic basket, and desserts. I'm sure the menu changes constantly, but what was true about every item we were served was the tremendous attention to detail, the creative presentation, our server's knowledge about the sources, the perfect timing of each course, and Mr. Humm walking around chatting with the diners. I know nothing about the gourmet industry, but he seems like a very humble and down to earth guy. We were there over four hours, but we were never without food or drink, and the four hours flew by. The cherry on the cake was when they invited us back into the kitchen where we got to see Mr. Humm ordering his minions about, and the cocktail chef made us a fabulous drink with liquid nitrogen.

I've been anxiously waiting to try EMP for a long time now. After visiting recently, I have to say it was a delight to all the senses. I do have my reservations about the restaurant but it is still a place I would highly recommend going to experience.

First of all, let's talk some logistics. They only offer a $195 tasting menu with about 15 courses. They do accommodate any food allergies or aversions. They take reservations 28 days in advance over the phone. The reservation line opens at 9 AM EST so you will want to call right as they open the phone line. You will be put on hold for a bit, but don't stress too much. They also release some reservations on OpenTable at the same time so you may want to have that open as well.

I won't say too much about the menu as it is constantly changing and I wouldn't want to ruin any of the fun. The food was well paced and each dish came with its own unique story. There were dishes I loved and there were some that left me a little confused. However, on a tasting menu this long I expect to not be in love with every dish. In general, the food was delightful, but not mind blowing. However, the complete dining experience left me more than happy. The service was top notch as well.

For the steep price of admission I don't think I will be back soon, but I'm very happy I got to experience EMP. Be prepared for an unforgettable 4 hour dining experience. Sit back, relax, and enjoy.
One of the best in the city, did the duck dinner - incredible

I went on a weekday for lunch so it wasn't too packed. We were seated in a quiet area and were started off with some delicious black and white cookies. The waiter asked us for any dietary restrictions. Since I'm such a picky eater it was great to be able to pick and choose what I want but still allow the chef to be creative. I wouldn't say I was stuffed by the end of the meal but it was definitely satisfying. 

I can't wait to go back!!

Life doesn't get better than this.  Two months later and I'm still thinking about each selection, the room, the service and the highlights the evening.

Despite a nor'easter, EMP was fully on target with each course.  Despite reading reviews and studying the highlights of each course, it was a surprise to have them introduced, and then our group of six discussed and shared.  The service was impeccable, organized, subtle and sophisticated to move through the menu and create anticipation of what was to come.  My husband, who is a fast eater, took time to dissect the ingredients, and to enjoy even items he would normally not eat.

Highlights were the scallop soup inside a real eggshell, the carrot tartare presentation, the beef and potato courses, and the picnic basket of cheese, pretzels and beer.  Dessert was a delight of three courses -and egg cream, vanilla snow with maple syrup, the magic trick of a delicious chocolate.  Fifteen courses with each item perfect, and we left feeling the magic of the craftsmanship, the flow of presentation, and service.

Pricey, but an evening we will never forget and happy we were able to share with great friends.

The meal at Eleven Madison Park wasn't just an ordinary lunch... It was an Experience.  From the start to finish it was a well thought implementation of New England's classics telling a story of New York's food traditions with and unexpected twist. 

The service was impeccable and staff knowledgeable about each dish. As we expressed interest to see the kitchen we were taken on a special tour and were prepared a little tasty surprise right in front of us. 

Tip: Be open-minded and share this unforgettable experience with someone who appreciates delicate dining.

I've occasionally left a restaurant miffed with a chef. But this was the first time I'd ever left a restaurant miffed at a food critic.

Back in September, Pete Wells of the New York Times reviewed the reinvented menu at Eleven Madison Park.

The restaurant, which currently ranks #10 on the list of top 50 restaurants in the world, had recently assembled a tasting menu meant as a tribute to New York and its culinary history. Which meant that the servers kept up a running narrative in order to put each course in context.

Wells didn't care for this, and wrote, in part:

"While people come to Eleven Madison from all over the world, those who live in the city may have to fight back the impatience and urge to interrupt that come with the keys to every New Yorker's first apartment. The narrative tone isn't sharp, it isn't quick, it isn't wised up, and it assumes the listener knows nothing: in other words, it's not a New York voice. By the end of the four hours, I felt as if I'd gone to a Seder hosted by Presbyterians."

Ouch!

I'd read on various food sites that Eleven Madison Park had toned down the patter in response to this critique, though no one let slip any details, so I was intrigued by what I'd hear during my lunch. Unfortunately, by the time my meal was over, what I heard, or what I didn't hear, made me want to find Chef Daniel Humm and tell him he'd have been better off ignoring all of Pete Wells' advice. Because the historical patter wasn't just toned down ... it had been eliminated entirely. As an ex-New Yorker, I could fill in some of the blanks. But still.

While every dish was magnificently prepared, causing me and my lunch companion to smile, or fall into silence as the flavors caressed our tongues, or eat as slowly as possible so a dish would not end, whatever narrative arc the sixteen courses would have conveyed was missing.

The servers, always professional, always smiling, always willing to answer questions, would bring each dish, describe the ingredients and their method of preparation, and then back away, at no point making reference to what was being honored or reinterpreted. Not even an introductory few sentences at the start of the meal explaining that we were about to experience the chef's tribute to the cuisine of New York. So while the food itself could not have been better, I had no sense of a journey, and my lunch of nearly 4 1/2 hours consisted of individual dishes, rather than story.

When my companion and I departed, not being "handed a pocket-size book of historical background on the food you've just eaten" as Wells had been, I felt strangely disappointed, and a bit sad, as if in order to placate an influential New York Times critic, Chef Humm had decided to strip away a vital component that sewed the individual courses into something larger, leaving the dishes unmoored. And as to the part of the meal Wells describes like so--

"And the meal's final moment (I won't be the one to spoil it) brought to life a fantasy of New York the way I've often wished it could be."

--I have no idea what that could possibly have been, because we experienced no such fantasy.

Am I ungrateful to have come away with the sense that even though I'd experienced one of the peak dining experiences of my life, I still walked away feeling something was missing? Perhaps. That's truly a First World Problem if there ever was one. But I can't ignore that at the end of the meal, instead of thinking, "wow," I was left a desire to head for the kitchen, find Chef Humm, put am arm around him and say, "I beg you ... please ignore Pete Wells and do whatever your heart tells you to."

I repeat and cannot stress enough that the food was prepared with precision, honoring the ingredients with every course. I just wish the opinions of one critic hadn't been privileged over the vision of one of the world's greatest chefs.

My favorites of the dishes? So hard to choose!

The creamy sea urchin? The seared foie gras? The roasted duck? The maple with shaved ice milk?

Chef Humm has made picking the winning dish of the afternoon an impossibility.

And now I urge him to wipe away all opinions other than his own--including mine--and do whatever his soul bids him.

Critics be damned.

this is one of those nyc restaurants that u must try.

Dont only read the reviews and think well maybe its good.. this place is ny's best and its a must to do on your trip or if u live here.

I made a reservation pretty earlier and my gf was amazed with this restaurant..very classy and good service.

You know what makes a place exceptional? Passion. The staff at Eleven Madison Park have it in spades.

I took my thirteen year old here for his birthday. He loves food. And I am not talking about he likes to eat, I mean he cooks, studies, reviews, plans, and thinks about food and cooking all the time. When we asked him what he wanted for his special birthday he said dinner here. He lobbied for six months unrelentingly. He had the recipe book. He studied it. what thirteen year old studies a recipe book?

Getting reservations wasn't easy, but we were able to get on the wait list and get a table. Plan ahead, plan ahead, plan ahead. They start taking reservations one month in advance.

The meal was spectacular. From the first course to the last it was a series of dynamic, fresh, interesting tastes and textures. Tomato tea? I have never tasted anything so vibrantly alive with tomato flavor. Every course had us discussing the flavors we could find. Was that sorrel? And being amazed at the combinations. Lardo and broccoli? I am writing this review more than half a year later, but I still remember the food.

In terms of food, it was the best meal of my life.

In terms of service, it was the finest service I have ever received.

They treated my family so well. They signed my son's book. He was overjoyed with the whole thing and it further stoked his interest in food.
