Yes the cost is dear, but the value is of a life experience.

I've dined well, and I've dined well often, but my meal and the service at Eleven Madison Park were so special, so beyond exceptional and so deeply appreciated that I wish I could give twenty stars rather than just five. It was absolutely the best meal of my life, certainly the best meal you can find in the United States, and quite possibly the best dining experience in the world (I'm hoping to try Noma in Copenhagen soon to find out if it rivals EMP). C'est trés chère, but it is worth it.

I went in December for more winter-weather fare. I'm hoping to go again this spring and see what sort of dishes might come of fresher spring veggies and fruits. Cross your fingers that I can get a reservation!

I might add that I had the best wine of my life there, too. I tasted my first Nuit Saint Georges, which was quite honestly the best red I've ever--EVER--imbibed. I've been searching and searching for the Burgundian wine to buy for my own stock, but haven't had much luck, unfortunately. I guess I'll just have to go back to EMP sooner rather than later to get my fix!
Worth the hype and the price. Simply delicious.

Fine dining at its best in a great New York setting.  My party of four attended on a Friday to find Eleven Madison Park very busy but still with a level of service above and beyond.  We first started with their intricate, fresh, and delicious cocktail menu and were all very satisfied.  Following we all decided to give the tasting menu a try and were very happy with the outcome. All of the dishes were presented in an artistic and appetizing way that is a little over the top but super necessary. Everything was super delicious with surprising flavors.  I definitely recommend Eleven Madison Park to anyone for a special night or in the mood for fine food.

We will definitely return again on our next trip to New York.

TIP: Make reservations as SOON AS YOU CAN! One of my cousins tried to book this place a month in advance, and still couldn't make it.

It was the most amazing fine dining experience I have ever had. It was just good food after good food, after great food. I was so stuffed halfway through, but I couldn't stop because everything was just so exquisite. 

Walking in, the interior design just made the atmosphere of the restaurant. It was classy, and open. When I received the menu, they explained to me that their system, which was to choose the main ingredient I wanted for each main course, and that the chef would make any type of dish using that ingredient. I suppose this lets chef use his imagination and to keep every dish unique. 

To be quite honest, I had no idea what more than half of the menu was. I just picked random things that sounded fancy, ha.
Every course that came out was fantastic. In between every single course, you would get a mini little dessert or such. 
I suppose my favorite one would be what their take was on a New York Style Raspberry Cheesecake because that's all I can remember! It was delicious, and it was so cute. I wanted to snap a picture, but somehow, I let the classy ambiance of it all stop me from taking it, thinking they would judge me if I took photos.
However, next time i'll be sure to throw my pride out the window and just snap a picture of everything.

I also tried the tea samples, my favorite would be the tomato tea with thyme. I wanted to have it with me throughout my entire meal, but once I put it aside, they took it away from me, and I didn't want to chase after them for it. :'(

After the FEAST, they gave us complimentary mini black and white cookies. They were so cute, and so good. 

Overall, it's a really nice place to go if you want to experience fine dining in a lovely little area in the middle of the city.

This restaurant is truly phenomenal. I cannot say enough about the service. They treat you like royalty and you feel spoiled dining here.

I took my friend her for her birthday and was completely blown away. We both ordered the tasting menu and savored every bite. I loved that they gave us countless amuse bouches. 

After our fantastic meal, the waiter told us that they had a birthday surprise for us. They took us to the back and gave us a tour of the kitchen. Then they sat us in front of the pastry chef and she prepared a personal dessert for us from liquid nitrogen. It was such a great experience.

When we got over the amazement, the waiter sat us in a plush couch and served us even more complimentary desserts. They then presented us with a complimentary bottle of pear liquor and asked us to stay and lounge. When we were ready to go, they gave us the mason jar bottles of their housemade granola. 

I will always remember my experience here and the A+++ service.

Dishes were well executed and the service was attentive.  That said, that is the minimum one would expect given the reputation and the price.  We had the tasting menue which was on the whole uninspired with the exceptin of 3-4 dishes out of 19.  The experience was a bit gimicky with card tricks and cookies in boxes and cocktails in the kitchen made with dry ice.  There was a "bread course" that was a horrible disappointment with a bun that was basically a croisante with butter and sea salt.  On the whole while the dishes were well executed and presented, they were really nothing special, dessert was decidedly disappointing, and overall the experince was more theme park than an excellent dining experience.  In addition, the style is a bit confusedwith almost more of anasian influence than anything French.  This could only attain the status it has in a culture with no real gastronomic culture.  Overall not worth the cost and clearly does not live up to the hype.   They did give the ladies granola to go - in the context of a restaurant with delusions of such grandure this speaks for itself!

This is a late yelp review, back when the menu was still in a grid form.  EMP gets 4.5 stars.  Nice to know some things stay the same, still gifting granola as your departing gift.  I was here when they had the special guest chef of Meadow Woods and he for some reason loved goat cheese.  His collaboration with Daniel Humm allowed him to prepare 3 dishes of the menu, wish that weren't the case since I'm not a fan of goat cheese.  Overall I enjoyed my meal (minus those 3 dishes), service was excellent, plating was beautiful, taste was good (but in my opinion not great which explains the 4.5 stars, still prefer Per Se).

I won't post a long review as if you do any sort of web search you will know what you are getting into. 

Definitely the tasting menu on a first visit & avoid looking at recent details. It's like going to the theater & you don't want to know how it all ends do you??

My take: the most luxurious & awe inspiring meal to date. One that all food experiences will be measured against. The bar has been raised & it is very high. The search is on for a better meal & definitely a yearly pilgrimage here is in order.

Seriously.. none of my past dining experiences touches how amazing this place is.. from the pan seared foie gras to the lobster, to the 150 day aged beef.. everything was immaculate.. It was a perfect combination of style and tasteful selection of ingredients. I always go into these hyped restaurants a little nervous that I will be disappointed but it did not disappoint. They gave the ladies granola to go. 

Every season they change their menu to ensure that people will come back to try something new! worth each and every one of those michelin stars.

came here for lunch and was not impressed. the only option for that day was a 11-course prix fixe which consisted of tiny, bite-size concoctions that were either bland or extremely salty. yes the tiny pieces of steak were above average and the dessert (shaved ice) was actually really good but overall not worth the price tag

If you just realized that your anniversary is tomorrow and you're frantically browsing yelp to find a perfect place to take your significant other, then look no further. EMP is the epitome of class, taste and romance. This is the definition of haute cuisine and is about as good as it gets anywhere. 

The service is great, when I arrived the host greeted me by name without ever having met me. Maybe he was psychic or I was the only asian guy on the list. But, either way it caught me off guard and impressed me from the get-go. From that point on, service is absolutely impeccable as you would expect from a 3 michelin star restaurant.

As for the food, it's perfection. I'll leave out the details since any word I write won't do it justice. You have to visit yourself and taste elegance on a plate.

The one critique I have of EMP was that service didn't flow as quickly as I'd like. At Jean-Georges we never felt like we were waiting for our next course but at EMP there are definitely times where we felt the time between the courses was too long. Well that is not too big a deal and it doesn't negatively impact the overall score. EMP is a solid 5 star establishment!

This is the best food I have ever had in my life. If you want to get the real deal, do the tasting menu but be warned its like 16 courses. So, you will be there for a long time. Also, they were able to accommodate me with my gluten allergy with is awesome. I just called ahead of time. There is a reason that this restaurant is rated in the top 50 best restaurants in the world. It is unbelievable. They also show my family and I the kitchen which was cool to see the cooking in action. They also made us a crazy cocktail with liquid nitrogen and it was delicious. I had the roasted duck as the entree and it was out of this world. I would go back here soon but its definitely expensive but you got to pay for world class dining. I also like the fact that really wasn't a dress code which makes it less pretentious. I highly recommend.
Simply stunning from beginning to end..  I could go on for pages. FLAWLESS from A to Z.

For a $1,000 lunch for two, this place can do better. 

Quick summary: The food are well executed and delicately prepared. However, nothing is memorable here. 

Turn off:  The way each course is served is either plain boring or overly gimmicky!  The last course was served together with a magic card trick. Seriously? The trick was demonstrated without the showmanship or enthusiasm is not a good lasting impression for the guest. 

Suggestion:  11 Madison Park needs to be more creative and further pushes their culinary limit. Otherwise, its fast rise to fame cannot be sustained.

Amazing place, i was invited here for my birthday and we got a tasting menu of 16 different servings. It was so graciously served! All those who work there look like movie stars and walk like dancers. It was some kind of amazing food ritual and we tasted things we never ever even considered eating before! I could not even think of people eating fast food or even dining in other restaurants on my way home. It was an exquisit and one of a life time experience...

Hands down one of the best dining experiences of my life.  I had a lunch reservation here February 2012 immediately before my flight back to Los Angeles.  I felt a little sheepish walking into such a grandiose dining room, carry-on luggage in tow, but the hostess could not have been sweeter about it.  My friend who had arrived at the restaurant earlier than I inadvertently walked into the kitchen and was courteously walked to the front of the restaurant by the Chef du Cuisine, James Kent.  We were off to a very unpretentious start.

Soon after we were seated, we were served a veritable potpourri of amuse-bouches, the highlights of which were the sunnyside up quail egg with bacon on toasted brioche, smoked apple tea, smoked sturgeon sabayon with chive oil, and their signature twist on the New York clambake.

Prior to the start of our courses, we were whisked away to the kitchen for a tour and served a delectable, sorbet-like jack rose cocktail prepared with liquid nitrogen.  Upon returning to our seats, we were presented with freshly baked bread and a selection of both cow and goat milk butters along with fleur de sel.

After scarfing down the bread, the first course, a cauliflower couscous, was brought to the table.  The minced cauliflower mimicked the texture of couscous wonderfully.  A stunning terrine of foie gras terrine was brought out next.  Despite being almost too beautiful to eat, it was devoured with a quickness and thoroughly enjoyed.  I can't say I'm particularly fond of watercress but Eleven Madison Park's preparation of it with sunchoke and horseradish was tasty.  This was followed by a portion of Maine lobster served with charred leek and bay leaf charcoal; the smoky notes of the bay leaf charcoal complemented the clean flavor of the lobster superbly.  Rounding out the main courses was a squab au jus served with beet gel which was excellent.

A trio of tasty triple creme cheese served with pumpkin, apple, and mustard was brought out leading into the dessert service.  A cart was then brought to our table where deliciously sweet soda-water spritzed egg creams were prepared for each of us.  The goat's milk cheesecake and berry sorbet proved to be the perfect palette cleanser leading into the final dessert of milk and chocolate sorbet served with bergamot and olive oil.  We were then given a bottle of cognac which was hilariously massive for a table of three at 2 PM but packed a nice punch nonetheless.  This was enjoyed with their signature sweet black and white cookies.

Service here was nothing short of phenomenal.  Despite my relatively young age, there was not a single iota of stuffiness to be seen anywhere.  The servers were both on point and jovial throughout the meal.  Subjective though this may be, presentation was unequivocally the best I've seen.  There's a certain playful elegance to many of the courses they serve.

Reservations were somewhat of a bitch to secure and I imagine they're even more difficult now following Eleven Madison Park's meteoric rise to number 10 on San Pellegrino's list of the 50 Best Restaurants in the World.  You'll most definitely have to refresh your browser constantly leading into the release of your desired date and time and even then you're far from guaranteed.  I recommend going for lunch as the dining room is markedly more stunning when lit with natural light.  If you're lucky enough to get a reservation, expect deliciously inventive food and top-notch service.  This place more than deserves its three Michelin stars.

The best dinner I have ever had.  My gf and I went there for our anniversary.  The food and service were wonderful from start to finish.  We had the tasting menu they offered.  Think it was around 12 courses, it included oyster, sea urchin, lobster, caviar, sturgeon, foie gras, 140 days aged steak, carrot tartare, wonder bread, cheese, picnic basket, desserts and drinks.  Everything was very creative and tasty, we were stuffed.  I would recommend this to anyone who wants a once in a life time experience.

Can I give 10 stars?   I wish I could.   This is an amazing place for atmosphere and food but the service is incomparable.   I have already made my next reservation with friends and have a new favorite place to WOW out of town guests.  Thank you for keeping with the New York tradition of excellence.   The bar has been set very high.

Save. Your. Money.     and. time.

Figure out 2-3 most important people in your life and spend this money on taking them to dinner in one of hundreds of great restaurants in New York. I don't think the price is justified for the quality of food.

$195 for 16 courses. You also get to choose 120-day-aged rib-eye or duck. One choice for the table; the waiter recommended duck so we went with duck.

Surprisingly the restaurant had a very extensive beer selection; maybe 5 pages of different beers. There was no ABV% mentioned next to the beer name which is a miss of the restaurant. Most beers are bottles and most are expensive. I picked one of the cheapest varieties for $15 for a 12-oz bottle. Cocktails were $16. One course actually had a little bit of beer included (the picnic basket) and one of the very last courses also had 40% ABV liquor.

Time management was not good. We started at 8 and ended well past 1 am. Yes, make sure to allocate FIVE hours for the dinner. There were moments when I couldn't understand why we were not being served courses back-to-back. Dozen of waiters standing around with nothing to do and we had no food at our table. We were also one of the last tables left this late on Tuesday night and still the breaks between the courses at times were ridiculously long.

The lighting in the restaurant was not the greatest; it was too dim, putting me to sleep after all the eating. We all prepared to take pictures of our food and we had to use flash because it was so dark. Our waiter right away started scolding us saying we can't use the flash. What is this, museum? And even after every table around us left, our waiter continued to insist that the use of flash is not allowed. That was very ridiculous.

A lot of food was wasted. That bothered me. I already agreed to your 2000% margins so let's not throw away food now. For example, the carrots were ground and then distributed among our 6 plates and some was left so why not distribute the rest? No, it was taken away. Tiny barely-there amount of clam chowder was brought out, 2 tablespoons were poured into each of our plates and again, some was left - it was taken away as well. The duck that was cooked specifically for our table, was brought out and shown to us, and then taken away again and 10 minutes later we got slivers of it cut out (it was already cold by then) and brought back to us. It was probably 25% of the duck. So what happened to the rest? I surely hope it was eaten by someone and not thrown away. Little tiny containers of butter were brought out and after we took a very small amount of it, they were also taken away. When we asked to leave them on the table we were told "we'll bring you new ones". Again, no need to waste perfectly fine food. Silverware was continuously taken away and new one brought back. How much soap and water does that waste? I understand that the restaurant needs to justify the garnisons of wait staff it employs but still.

The portions started extremely small. Each one was maybe a tablespoon. During the course 6 or 7 I actually complained how hungry I still was. However during the course 16 I was stuffed beyond any capacity. I couldn't even finish the last course.

Food was fairly boring; presentation lacking. The first course was this tiny microscopic black-and-white cookie half an inch in diameter. I didn't even grasp that it was considered a course. It was served just like that, no garnish, no presentation, just a microscopic cookie. The last two courses were a basic, very basic, chocolate-covered small pretzel and this microscopic cookie again! 

Other than duck all courses were either seafood or vegetarian. Chef must also love shaved ice because two courses had it in plentiful amount.

I spent $300 total which was the tasting; 2 beers and tax and tip. I had great table company and overall had a good time but in hindsight this amount of money and time are not justified in my opinion.

seriously- i am negating my previous glowing raves for this place solely on the pathetic way we were treated upon entering.

i have touted this place forever to everyone as the cream of the ny crop.  you not only lost my business and that of a major us ceo- but i will be sure to share this awful experience as much as the good ones.  

my friend and i love to dine well- and that;s the only way we dine- we like to sit at the bar- less stuff- but we drop some serious coin.  

here's the set up- we walk in- 'can i help you?- yes we would like to have dinner at the bar and a couple bottles of wine.- well the bar is full right now. no problem, we can wait- we will just grab a drink. we have a no standing room policy so you can't, what do you mean? there are a lot of pubs in the area if you would like, i can recommend a couple places.'  we stare at each other like this troll is kidding- half the people at the bar were standing????

we looked at him and said no thanks- we don't need a pub recommendation..  walked out- whisked in a cab uptown to marea where we were treated like gold- amazing dinner- two bottles of a white burgundy (at 300 a pop) and not a worry.

he could have offered to take a look at the bar and see if anyone was closing a tab? getting ready to leave? something- but a pub???? are you f-n kidding me???  i know you guys don't need the business- but the person they turned away was a very frequent diner as i am.  probably 25-30 visits a year between us.  as julia roberts said- big mistake!!!!

we don't expect anything more than a proper courtesy- but the way he treated us.. i will no longer stop in for my over priced yet perfect weekly martini... idiots
The dining experience is so well thought out, even my bowel movement this morning was amazing.

The Eleven Madison Park experience is unbeatable in New York.  It is not so much the surfeit of food or even the consistency of quality that impresses as much as the ambiance, the attention and the accouterments that render an interesting twist to the mechanics of meal-making.  Not to forget my delightful company--no, that is not a reference to Mister Hanks who was holding court at the next table to ours as only an aged version of Josh Baskin can.

What pleased me also was that Eleven Madison Park has such staff in their employ as a 'wine director' and a 'bar manager'--when you pay for an expensive meal, you like to know that the restaurant is splurging as well.  Equally pleasing was their ability to cater to a vegetarian palate in a surprisingly seamless manner, matched only by their desire to pamper and please every patron.

The sixteen-course meal had its statistically inevitable ups and downs.  The black and white cookie, the squash, roasted salsify with wheat and walnuts, the baked potato and the parsnip roasted with sesame and parsley are fresh in the mind's eye, ably complemented by a printed menu that I hope to preserve at least until the next time I move apartments.  The most impressive item in the series of desserts was the Maple--bourbon barrel aged with milk and shaved ice.  I wish they gave us more of that to take home rather than the granola, but I am not complaining--they were quite generous about giving us two bottles of the granola for the road.

This was only my second time at the restaurant, and the new team seems to have done a magnificent job of preserving what was essentially right while tweaking or transforming other elements of the experience.  I hope to be back soon!

I Wish there were more stars to give this restaurant.

We had an office celebration here and were given a tasting menu that was unparellelled.  Service was incredible the first courses gave way to second courses and finally desserts that ended a meal that everyone agreed was the best they ever had.  And what an environment. 
I am sure i will have a difficult time making reservations but I'm sure going to try. What a great meal. Well worth the money.

It was absolutely one of the best dining experiences.  The clean and serene course menu reminded me of kaiseki.  The reservation process had put me off initially but it was well worth the pain.  It was our perfect 10th anniversary celebration.

This is an impressive place.  We went here for lunch, when visiting NYC.  I had done some research and it seemed to be the best fine dining lunch option (for the price).  it was $56 for a three course lunch.  

Now, this is probably the fanciest restaurant I have ever been to, as Vancouver does not have places like this.  This is basically a white glove type of service, but without being too stuffy.  

We got one of the best seats in the house, at higher level facing the rest of the restaurant.  The three course menu turned out to be more like 5 or 6 with all the cheese buns and amuse bouche they brought out.  The food looked like art and one of the highlights was being brought back to the kitchen for an egg cream.  

The wait staff were probably the best I have ever seen and extremely nice.  As we were tourists, they recommended a few other places to us and printed it out on a nice card.

The food was divine and my boyfriend was the smart one as he upgraded and had two meat dishes, which were both to die for.  

The entire experience was as much or more than I was expecting, which included the ambience of the restaurant (very high class), the service, and the food.  As it was lunch and we didn't go overboard with the alcohol, it wasn't even as expensive as we were anticipating.  I tell everyone I know, who is going to NYC, to go to this restaurant.   I even sent a card, showing my appreciation, when I got home.

You know exactly what it will cost - a lot.

But the total focus on quality in all forms is like few experiences you will ever have in your entire life.

wow!  the only problem here is that I can only give 5 stars to this place!  

We went with a group for a tasting lunch and it was probably up there with the 4 or 5 best lunches I have ever had.  the food was creative, unusual, beautiful and delicious.  

Favorite dish was a parsnip dish.  a few pieces of poached or roasted parsnip, then some parsnip puree, then a very large, square flat sheet of what looked and tasted like parsnip bark.  Extrmeley thin and extremely crispy - like a parsnip tuille.  Extraordinary! 

There was  great sea bass dish as well;  cooked to perfection.  and an amuse bouche of a sabayon sauce poured into a hollowed out egg shell, with some small dice of smoked sturgeon and a little chive oil in the bottom of the eggshell.  Wild!  

Not cheap, but worth every penny for a once a year, or once in a lifetime splurge.

A great culinary experience.
The menu was definitely something new and entertaining.  There was a smoked dish, a picnic, a science experiment..  We didn't know what to expect and that was part of the fun.

The ambiance was beautiful.  We were seated at a corner table where we could see the entire dining room.  We watched the sky and nightscape change outside the windows overlooking the park.

The staff were all friendly and helpful and answered any questions we had.
Great food and great service. I have eaten here several times and it never fails to impress me.

pros
- great service when you get to the restaurant.  Just communicate and they'll accommodate.
- the staff was friendly, youthful, and knowledgable
- they are trying to make fine dining fun and interesting with more visually interesting displays of presenting your courses and drinks.  There is a fun and mobile cocktail cart that they pull out to serve your New York City inspired cocktail.  There's a card trick to present one of the final dessert courses.  Very obvious they are pushing the boundaries and experimenting.
- the orderly manner in which the staff navigated the room was noticeable and efficient
- courses were diverse, delicious, and interesting


Cons
- we felt we waited  too long for our first courses. 
- too many course...16!  And, between when we made the reservation and dining date, the menu changed so that the lunch menu was the same menu as dinner.  If i had known that i'd have made the reservation for dinner.
- 4 hours for lunch is a marathon...and i was not informed of this when when EMP confirmed the reservation
- very expensive for lunch, $630+ for two including drinks and tip
- the staff was youthful and not too stuffy, but i did feel that the uniforms were a bit too casual and not well disciplined as a whole.  Some messy collars and such.
- with the compliment of experimentation, comes the criticism of not being polished and perfected.
- 4 sweet courses were all salty, and could have been more diverse
-at times the courses mixed culturally high and low ingredients...sometime i thought this was not in line with fine dining
-if you have a party of 6 or more they will not accommodate your party without a large party reservation.  (they ask for a minimum of $3500 for this)
- the plateware and settings were not paired perfectly with the environment.

Even with all the criticism, EMP, was an experience worthy of trying once or recommending to others with caveats so they know what to expect.

Recommendations-  We agree with another reviewer...ask for a kitchen tour beforehand or they cannot accommodate you.
Also, we were seated at a perimeter booth and requested to be seated side by side so we could both see the space and activity in it.  Very nice!

 Will still give it a 5 stars though...
My wife and i agreed that there was some hype that EMP did not live up to...We personally feel that LeBernardin is superior in service, continuity of a total fine dining experience, and rigorous pursuit of perfection.

Overall a great experience. I love food and enjoy having new food experiences - I don't love the whole get dressed up/ heels/ dress/ makeup  etc part of it - especially with a 15 course meal - which, in my view, is more well suited for stretchy pants. That being said, I'll go through the motions for a great new food experience - which Eleven Madison Park definitely was :) 

The positives vastly outweighed any negatives, but am pointing out salient points of both for a balanced review. Positives - food was interesting/ fantastic, wine pairings were nice (we got the smaller list of pairings - 5-6 wines, versus a mix of 15 with each course), and our table's main waiter was great (as were the other staff who brought out each course). Negatives - the sommelier seemed aloof and was off-putting (get a personality buddy!) and the stress some of the waiters felt was tangible and even made me uncomfortable at times (one server took my plate too early - my boyfriend hadn't finished eating just yet - and she realized her mistake immediately and so just lingered by the table with a sad/ exasperated face hoping he'd scarf down what was left on his plate before walking away visibly upset). 

Tip for future diners - the kitchen tour requires pre-planning. You need to mention to the reservationist in advance. Didn't realize and so was very disappointed that this was the case. Cest la vie I guess.

I  was  here for a going away party and  this was nice . 

This place was impressive on every single thing you can judge a restaurant on. The service was very  good, the food was beautiful, and delicious. The drink menu was thorough.

I would 100% come back here.

I've been to EMP* about 5 times now. Twice with my friends and three times for work related events. Every time the food and the service has been nothing short of stellar. Last time I was here with a group of friends, one of my melodramatic friends commented that their service made her feel like a princess. I didn't have the heart to tell her that it was probably because she acts like one.

To be honest, I can see where she was coming from. You will be hard pressed to find a more attentive and pleasant wait staff.  

You used to be able to do a cheaper, more compact tasting menu here but not anymore. I suppose that's the price of going from a one michellin starred restaurant to a 3 michellin starred restaurant. I had one of the tastiest suckling pigs in my life here (and also the most expensive).  The salmon was mind numbingly good as well. Not only was it cooked perfectly but it came with a frothy broth that was as beautiful as it was tasty. That's what I found the most impressive about EMP - not only did the food look good, it  also always tasted a notch or two above the rest of the high end places. The other thing is they kept surprising us with small knick knacks that we didn't expect.  It's their way of saying, "thank you for letting us blow a hole in your wallet".

If you are looking for a place to host a small private dinner - I don't think there is a better choice in the city especially if your firm is picking up the tab  ;-). Our firm is small and we had our annual holiday party here 3 years in a row. They set us up in a private room upstairs with a large square table and a small bar that we could stock up with pretty much anything we wanted.  The hors d'oeuvres  and the entrees were fantastic. My only complaint was that they were so dainty that they didn't really fill me up but that was also because I drank so much that I needed to keep eating the whole time. That's what happens when you get free food and liqor.

* That's Eleven Madison Park not to be confused with Electro Magnetic Pulse!
No. words. to. describe. this. meal. Simply, the best. meal. ever. I'll concentrate next time so I can write a more meaningful review. Just go.

WOW... that's what I kept saying as each course was wheeled out from the kitchen. If you haven't been here post menu renovation, you must! Eating here after their menu renovation was like coming to eat a completely different restaurant. The new concept has not only transformed the menu offerings but the serving style, presentations and plating. 

Every course offered here is definitely one for the books -- from the smoked herring course to the cheese picnic basket. I don't want to say too much to ruin the experience but will say it has been one of my most memorable experiences to date!

How do I love thee?
Let me count the ways.
I love thee for the friendly and attentive service,
The amazing innovative dishes which were presented so beautifully,
The creative and tasty amuse bouches throughout,
And for making our anniversary so incredibly special.

please bring the grid back...
please bring back the best meal that i had in 2011..
the new tasting menu does not warrant the increase in price nor does it compare to the experience prior to the change...

1. per se 
2. le bernadin 
3. jean george

EMP..you've been bumped...

3 stars in view of EMP's capability

we decided to have 1 really nice meal with our baby while visiting family and friends in nyc. since we had baby in tow, we opted to go for lunch which was not difficult to get reservations. the service was excellent, super accommodating. from the host to the server to bus boys, everyone was really wonderful about us bringing our little boy.  granted he was asleep during most of the meal but when he awoke and became a little fussy, they offered to move our table to the corner lounge area to finish our meal which worked out really nicely.

i can't even remember all the dishes we tried here. they present a bingo-like card of different ingredients and you pick some permutation of your choice. the dishes were playful and creative and the presentation was very pretty. the duck stood out - it came with lavender and was cut tableside.

EMP showcased the best preparation of the CHEAPEST ingredients I've ever had at a Michelin starred restaurant. 

We initially went to EMP in 2010 and strongly felt that was the hands down best restaurant we'd ever been to. This will essentially be 2 reviews, EMP in 2010 (before they won their 2nd and 3rd stars, before Daniel Humm opened Nomad and also bought the restaurant from Danny Meyer) vs EMP in 2013:

2010: Wine pairings were perfect, featuring wines from France, Switzerland, and Italy. Courses included Sterling Royal Caviar with Spheres of Smoked Sturgeon and Salmon Cream (insanely delicious!), Salad with Buffallo Mozzzarella, Mille Feuille of Foie Gras and Big Eye Tuna, Black Truffle, Cheve Frais and Potato soup (which was plated by Daniel Humm himself), Boulibaise of Sole with Mussels, Scallops, Hawaiian Prawns and Chorizo, Poached Nova Scotia Lobster, Sauteed Frog Legs with Parsley and Porcini Custard, Quail with Roasted Endive, Medjool Dates and Juniper, Veal with Braised Cheeks, Celery Root and Black Truffles, a selection of 3-4 artisanal cheeses, "Soda Pop" Dessert with Tangerine, Grapefruit, Pomelo and Lemon, Milk & Chocolate dessert, and Mignardises.

Like I said, 2010 was the best time to go to EMP. 2013ers, I'm sorry, but this is what you have in store:

2013: WIne pairings were just ok, featuring a couple of wines from France but also wines from the Fingerlakes and a Brooklyn winery, and an Ithaca beer. The waitstaff did tell us that the wines were predominantly white. I had no idea that was code word for cheap and disappointing. Yes, I paid $145 for that. It pains me. 

Let me HIGHLIGHT the cheapest courses for you. Courses included CHEDDAR (a savory black and white cookie with apple, yes, a tiny cookie counts as a course), Oyster (wood sorrel and minonette, which was quite good), CRANBERRY (Snow (frozen water... really) with beets, goat cheese, and caraway, ingredient price estimate: $3), Sea Urchin (custard with baby squid, bay scallop, and apple, yum), Sturgeon (sabayon with chivies, smoked with everything bagel crumble, pickles and caviar, probably my favorite), Scallop (seared with radish, caviar and apple), CARROT (they grind up a carrot table side to be cute and tell you to mix in some spices and nuts. That's just insulting!), Lobster (poached with leeks black onion and shellfish bisque), PARSNIP (roasted with sesame, parsley, and millet, worst dish of the night), Beef (grilled and aged 144 days, came with a braised oxtail with foie gras and potato, but the braised oxtail was way salty and foie was barely there), GREENSWARD (this is the CHEAPEST, a picnic basket with grapes, one tiny slice of cheese, and a hot pretzel. SERIOUSLY?), MALT (egg cream with vanilla and seltzer, I'm again, offended you call this a course), MAPLE (bourbon with milk and shaved ice, did you just serve me ICE AGAIN and call that a dish?) WALNUT (cheesecake with port, this wasn't good at all), PRETZEL (wait, did I just get served another course with a PRETZEL?) and CHOCOLATE (another tiny cookie that counts as a course).   

All together, the meal for 2 was $700. Of the 16 courses, 9 courses probably had ingredients that cost about $5, maybe even less. It seems like Mr. Humm has bills to pay now and can't afford the expensive ingredients. Sorry folks, EMP peaked in 2010, now I just feel betrayed. Let this be a lesson to all of us. Mr. Humm, please fix this. Say no to your restaurant consultants and make a swift return to the good old days.

Small menu, but with all you could want. Just make sure to order an app each person, entrée or two! Portions are so so small. Great if you are on a diet. Tile fish was cooked perfectly and beautiful presentation. Rib eye was two bites of deliciousness ;). Staff was so very professional,knowledgeable and great hair cuts! I love that someone came out with of the kitchen following the server and food to give a description of the food. More about the art, than sustenance.
This is place is well worth it! It's a wonderful dining experience, from the food to the service to the decor. You must try!

I've been working on this review for 6 months. My then boyfriend, now fiance, had made reservations here for our six month anniversary. Words can't do the experience justice. THE best dining experience I have had, and it was everything (and more) I had expected from a 3 Michelin Star/#24 (now #10) restaurant in the world. All 5 senses are engaged during the meal.

We did the 16 course tasting menu - every. single. dish. was. to. die. for. We asked for a tour of the kitchen as well which was a wonderful experience. I was really surprised how clean it was despite how busy they were.

Our initial server was okay, but he was shortly replaced by a much friendlier and personable server. I wish I could remember his name because he added that extra flair to the dining experience.

The end of the meal is of course always going to be the most memorable and best part of the night. My fiance had planned to do a table-side proposal, however, I foiled his plan. We were talking about proposals, and I told him I considered restaurants to be too public of a place for my liking. Last minute, he had the staff move patrons from the small, private lounge area. After our last course, we were guided to the private lounge where they had two champagne glasses placed on a table & my favorite song playing on a small speaker in the background (as requested by my fiance). The whole staff cheered as they popped a bottle of champagne bottle. 

They asked us to wait so they could get the glasses ready for us after we were done. They actually packed the (Vera Wang) glasses in a nice box AND boxed the cork in a small, cute box with an EMP ribbon - so sweet & sentimental.

It really is the best dining experience, and if I could give them extra stars for their thoughtfulness, I would. Thank you EMP!

Came here for the 16 course tasting menu for my birthday dinner last night and was definitely blown away. The food, of course, was amazing but the service was flawless. I now understand what people are talking about when they said EMP is not just about the food but the whole dining experience. Everything was very delicious and the presentation was just so creative and interesting. One of my favorite courses was the picnic basket which consisted of the cheese course and specially brewed beer. Another favorite was the do-it-yourself carrot dish with multiple condiments on a dish that resembled a palette. While the ribeye, lobster, scallop, sea urchin, and parsnip dishes were all amazingly delicious, I am a huge dessert lover so I thoroughly enjoyed the last 4 courses of dessert. My fave being the shaved ice with ice cream, maple, and what seemed like a type of peanut brittle. 

We had the opportunity to go to the kitchen which made our experience even more fun and amazing. Our guide was so patient in explaining the whole kitchen process and answered all of our questions. The complimentary cocktail was also very interesting as they used molecular gastronomy to make our Widow's kiss cocktail. I really enjoyed it!

I really appreciated the complimentary granola (eating it right now as I write my review) and the hand written birthday card. They even gave me a complimentary birthday gift: sea salt caramel millionaires shortcake. Love it!

Overall, it was a great and fun experience. I would definitely recommend EMP for any special occasion as it will definitely be worth it!

Good and mediocre at the same time. Nothing was bad, but nothing was amazing. When going to a 3 star Michelin, you always expect the very best.

The sommelier gave us a captivating wine list, but It is hard to choose a wine when you do not know what you are going to eat. They did not offer us a wine pairing.

The art deco space is gorgeous, but still I found it lack of charm. The service was good, but not great, for being a 3 stars Michelin. The food was interesting, but only 4 of the 15 courses where really superb.

Left feeling disappointed. Definitely not my favorite.

I came here and did the 16 course tasting menu. This is more than just a dinner but a dining experience. The food was very creative and delicious. Some dishes were a little more bizarre than others but all in all it was very good. Extremely proper and sophisticated environment, maybe a little too much for some. 

The service was impeccable. I informed someone I forgot my phone in my coat pocket (which was checked in the coat room). A minute later I see a waiter walking toward me with my phone on a silver platter. Insane. After the 16 lavish courses, I was given a mason jar of granola to enjoy the next morning compliments of Eleven Madison Park. 


I definitely recommend coming here for the experience just as much as for the highest quality of food you can taste.

Rank: A-. The first thing that stands out when stepping inside is the building. The restaurant feels cold and like a bank (originally MetLife building). Rather austere and filled with suits and pretentious people (I don't consider myself as one, but I guess eating here makes me one?) sitting at tables that are placed too close together. Make sure to ask for a corner table or a seating further away for a more intimate experience. As sad as it may sound, the only truly memorable dish was the Coke-Float at the end for dessert (grenadine, egg-yoke, licorice, white tea, and Coke). The lobster, the fish, etc. are good, but once again, nothing that is uniquely prepared/flavored. I heard that they've eliminated the $125 tasting menu and replaced it with the $195 tasting menu. I would argue that the food here, while superb, is not worth the incremental price hike. At this price, save your money and go to Per Se for a true, once-in-a-lifetime dining experience.When we were leaving, the hostess gave us toasted honey granola which was delicious and a great touch.

We really enjoyed our overall experience BUT the food didn't blow us away. It was good. The staff was amazing! We had a lot of fun with them and the overall creativity of the service really makes for a great experience. I'm glad we tried it and I would encourage others to have the experience but it was a one and done experience for us.

Everyone came around with a welcome smile... From beginning to end.  Had wine pairing with tasting menu... There's no such thing as too much wine I suppose... But 9 glasses of wine plus champagne plus apple brandy... How am I sober enough to write this review??? It was fabulous! Great times.

Simply amazing. My boyfriend took me here for our one year and it was a great surprise. Upon our arrival we started at the bar and our bartender looked very sophisticated and genuinely nice. I had the amaretto sour with an egg white and that was the best amaretto I've had in my life! My boyfriend had the sleepy hollow and that too was delicious. We then were seated and had a very nice waitress who explained everything well and into detail. I was so excited to start on the 15 course meal! We chose the rib eye over the duck and oh my god it was soooooooooooo amazing!!!! Every meal that was given to us was explained well and was all DELICIOUS! I was soooooo full after my ninth meal ah I want to go again! I LOVED all of it. Also, the chef came out and was very nice and asked us how our meals were and how. We were doing. Amazing amazing amazing. Definitely coming again soon.
Best.  Meal.  Ever.  I hate cooked fish and to this day the best item I've ever eaten is the oil-poached halibut.  Very costly meal, but more than worth it.  Again, Best Meal Ever!
5 STARS 11mad is for food lovers who have the wallet to pay for it! Perfect for any special occasion and the food service and room are one of the best in NY!
Truly an experience, the food and service are impeccable. A perfect visit would be with three friends so we could order and share everything on the tasting menu!

Big, bold, brash, in your face, NY done Danny Mayer style.  Did the tasting menu.  Very pricey.  Was it worth the $? probably not, but the experience was fun, the food was inventive, we were in NY for the weekend and all sense of propriety and value went out the window. Special Occasion or expense account kind of place.

My husband and I have been here twice, once several years ago, before the minimalist grid menu, and once after, for the new 15-course tasting menu. Both were the best meals we'd ever had, the second replacing the first for that title.  The entryway to the restaurant gives the feeling of entering a different world, and for four hours, that's what happened for us. Both visits I have been struck by how professional and how friendly the staff are.  I've never been to another restaurant where I felt the staff approach Eleven Madison Park's for knowing what they're doing and paying attention to what's going on around them.  On our first visit, Daniel Humm came out to say hello, and we almost fell out of our chairs.  At our more recent visit, the tasting menu reminded me of kaiseki meals served in Japan, so many beautifully prepared and presented dishes.  I ordered the drink pairings, which were outstanding.  A lot of memories to hold us over to our next visit. Another nice touch: you get to sit next to your sweetie rather than across, so you can actually talk with them without yelling.

I haven't read the other reviews, so I'll write a sentence about how to get a reservation in case it's useful: call them when the reservations line opens at 9am 28 days before your visit.  I've never seen an open slot on Open Table.

The meals I've had here have been some of the most forward leaning, avant garde cuisine ever. Who knew you could make "tomato tea" and who knew it would be that incredibly eye opening? I love that you simply make your selections via ingredients and that it then comes as a surprise. Often times I just say I'm feeling like something really rich or delicate or whatever and the ingredient is prepared. Some dishes come to your table with a side preparation which adds to the experience. Truly deserving of its upgrade from 1-star to 3-star. Also, the best kitchen tour I've had - if you've done it, you know why!

Simply perfect.  The splendid art deco decor is open to the adjacent Madison park greenery through tall glass windows.  We had a lunch sitting and after arriving at noon we got to experience the whole arc of a winter's day as the sun set by the time our meal finished some four hours later.  I recommend coming for lunch as there are so many courses to try I couldn't imagine eating significantly before arriving.  The lunch menu is the same as the dinner menu.  Speaking of dinner, we had no need for a dinner that evening!

The service was personal and impeccable.  Dietary restrictions are honored which I truly welcomed (I eat fish but not meat) but my dining partner ate the standard menu.  She received butter for her bread flavored with beef fat, whereas I received mushroom infused butter.  So many surprising options.  My favorite was the smoked whitefish... the presentation was a surprise so I won't say more.  All of the dishes were intriguing and framed like a small work of art.  Many were even surprising and revealed themselves fully in layers or by table presentation.

If you ask nicely, your server may even gift you a pack of signature playing cards to take home :)

We went to Eleven Madison Park to celebrate a special occasion. Daniel is usually our first choice in these cases, but the thought was to give Chef Humm and his several accolades a try. After all three Michelin stars are usually a reliable guarantee of quality...
The result was however the conclusion that Daniel Boulud's stars shine much brighter than Daniel Humm's.

The idea of presenting the menu in a grid that only mentions the principal ingredient of the dish, while apparently intriguing (the intention is supposedly to leave some room for surprise when the guest receives the order), is actually obviously unpractical. Our inquiries to the waiter actually uncovered the worst side of our experience at Eleven: the service. The waiter was visibly irritated by my questions about the menu, and throughout the meal he treated us with distant condescension.
Eleven Madison Park is somehow known for one of the courses consisting in a visit to the kitchen. We were actually looking forward to that as, one by one, the tables around us were invited to meet with the chef and his staff. Well, needless to say that we were basically the only ones who did not enjoy this courtesy.

The food was not overwhelming. The chef must have had a recent trip to Japan, because all my dishes tasted like yuzu or some other Asian citrus. I'm not saying it was bad. It was just witnessing someone going for the most obvious way to try to be innovative...
Well, the cheese course was actually downright disappointing. Particularly for a Swiss chef that prides himself for being meticulous in the choice of his products.

In conclusion: 
Fantastic venue, but even a Gristedes would look great in an art deco skyscraper.
Average food, especially considering the hype (and the price!).
Far below average service.

TIP: Try to look like a big shot at Credit Suisse around the corner (as opposed to somebody who reads and writes on yelp). That might make your waiter happy. And if he's happy, you're happy.
The best culinary experience in New York City. Just go. You won't regret it.

I have had the EMP cookbook on my coffee table for the last year.  Dreaming of the opportunity to dine at this great establishment.  Well, I got my chance two weeks ago!

It pains me to give a restaurant of this caliber 4 stars, but it is what it is.  The service was impeccable and the food was good.  Therein lies the problem, the food was just good when it should have been great.  My most memorable dish was one that I did not get to try.  The dry aged rib roast looked amazing as I watched it being served to the table next to us.   EMP seems to relies on showmanship to make an impact rather than letting the food do it.  I essentially never got that tingly feeling or the  "wow" moment .  Compared to its peers in NYC, the food is a notch below.

My parents took me here the night before they dropped me off at college and boy was it the best "Last Supper" I could've ever imagined!

Let me start by saying, the service here is incredible! Our waiter was very charming, attentive, and cordial.

The meal was definitely one of the most amazing meals I have ever had. I ordered the tasting menu including Foie Gras, Lobster, Lamb, and Chocolate. Besides these delicious dishes, there were many complimentary dishes and amuse-bouches that made the meal more like a show. It was an incredible experience and we were all completely stuffed by the time dinner was over.

Eleven Madison is an amazing establishment with an amazingly talented chef, who came around once the meal was done. The food was enough for the 5-star rating, but the impeccable service is what really made the meal so enjoyable.

We reserved the private room upstairs. The food was outstanding! The wine list was nice and we managed to go thru several selections, and enjoyed them all.  Great service, and the room is perfect for a nice evening!

Amazing service. Amazing service. Amazing service. I can't imagine a restaurant with better service than we had here. The service was perfection from start to finish including a small break inside the kitchen to have a desert prepared in front of us by one of the pastry chefs. The yuzu cream cheese with caviar was one of the most delicious things I've ever had. Many if not most of the dishes throughout the meal had a nice tart/acidic taste to them - something that is not done often enough at restaurants. The desserts were the best presented I've ever had and incredibly delicious.

My friend said it best - "I am bored of eating."

For dinner, Eleven Madison only offers a 16 course tasting menu, which took us 4 hours to slog through.  I just can't sit down for dinner that long!!  

To be fair, the hostess warned me when I made the reservation that dinner could take 3 hours, which sounded fine in theory.  Now I know I can't do it in practice.  What ended up happening is we ordered more wine throughout the night so the bill was pretty crazy.  

If you have the patience and the wallet, then EMP is worth checking out.  The food was delicious.  Each of the 16 tasting courses were well portioned, so you didn't feel stuffed near the end.  There's one dish that is smoked, so it comes out in this bell shaped jar that still had smoke inside!  Well done, EMP.  

Service was very considerate.  Most of the dishes were seafood, which one of my friends doesn't like.  They modified her dishes to be sans-fish, and they were all just as good (or better) than ours.

I just so happened to be riding my bike past this place once I realized I was in the Flatiron district. This place caught my eye since it had a particular awe to it. Once entering, I had been very pleasantly greeted by one of the lovely hostesses. There was plenty of room even for busy Friday night, and I was directed to a table immediately.  The Menu was absolutely stunning, so many intriguing options that I could have passed out. To say the least, an Original Restaurant with an Original Taste

Man, this is just on another level.

My first foray into the tasting menu world was in Chicago, and since then my palette has been forever scarred. Beautifully.

EMP signifies all that is right with dining.

First, the service knew exactly who we were and what occassion we were celebrating - obviously, we divulged this information beforehand, but they space out their guests' arrival times for the express purpose of being able to greet everyone without being rushed. Our coats were taken and presumably hung in a space that corresponds with our table - no coat check ticket was given. This makes a world of difference.

Next, service was always always friendly, informative, enthusiastic. Everyone seemed to enjoy working there, even if the novelty may have worn off by now.

Drinks were unique and priced reasonably for what they were, we ordered two drinks: King's Arms (Rye Whiskey, Aquavit, Averna, Cold Brew Coffee) and the Sleepy Hollow (London Dry Gin, Amaro Abano, Chambéry Blanc Vermouth, Apple Cider, Spiced-Pumpkin, Lemon, Egg White). Oh man, they were tasty. 

As for the food, well it's pointless to tell you exactly what we indulged in that night because chances are, you probably will not experience the same journey.

Dishes were served in such a unique way, ingredients were melded in ways that you would never fathom. The meal was masterfully executed. I do wish that it is were more difficult to sneak a peek to the next table to see what's coming next - sometimes you just can't help it. The gift bag at the end that was just for the ladies? My only real complaint. What's up with that?

I look forward to having an excuse (and surplus in budget) so that I may make a return trip to Eleven Madison Park.

Don't know where to start, to much to write about.
I'll just say that I had the best time of my life.
Around 20 courses (depend on how you count), delicious (maybe 1-3 courses weren't so good) the best service I know (even got me an iPhone adapter when my battery went off).
I got to get in to the kitchen on a small tour + cocktail that they made me in the kitchen using liquid nitrogen.
I got drunk during the meal only a from the alcohol that comes with the courses (beer, how much brandy you want).
The menu is totally individual, they can handle every dietary request, don't be shy.
I even got a photo with chef Daniel Humm.
Not an every day meal, not even every month.
It is a lot of money, but kind of worth it.
It's not just lunch, it's an over all experience, 4 hours of culinary heaven. Just like going to amusement park.

My wife took me here for my birthday.  Upon entering, the doorman greets us and asks us our party name.  We tell him, and he says Happy Birthday!  Whoa,  the doorman remembered the guest list and each special occasion.  That is the first time that's ever happened.  We ordered the tasting menu consisting of
1.  Foie Gras
2.  Lobster
3.  Lamb/Fish
4.  Chocolate
(and a bottle of wine)

This was the most amazing and best dinner I've ever had.  The experience made it even better.  We were given numerous palette cleansers and a huge bottle of port to end the evening.  Not only we were stuffed beyond our means, but their drinks were nice and strong!  If I had one meal to eat in the US,  this would be it!

It was everything I dreamed of and so much more.

I had the pleasure of dining at Eleven Madison on Saturday night with my hubby to celebrate my birthday. Despite ringing at precisely 9am 4 weeks prior and holding for 45 minutes, the only table we could get was at half 5. "I'll take it!"

This was actually a blessing in disguise. As they bring you food and you don't know what's coming, being in the first seating each of our courses was a surprise. Also, we were there for almost 4 hours anyways.

With each of the 16 courses I professed how amazing each was, and each was my favorite. I couldn't tell you what I liked best, it was all so good. I was especially excited as a gluten bigot that they had prepared gluten free bread for me as we had notified them of my celiac status prior. And the bread was incredible.

Service was impeccable, not only were we well tended to but our needs (even needing to locate the loo) were anticipated.

While it was expensive, I felt the meal was good value - it was a lot of food and an experience worth having. If you can swing the $195 (+drinks) I highly recommend!

Fantastic.  Excellent food, incredible service, gorgeous space.... 

Exceeded my expectations.

If you eat in only one restaurant in NYC, Eleven Madison Park should be it.  It is pricy but worth every penny.  We had dined here last March but I had heard the menu had changed but wasn't sure we should go back so soon.  Don't just go but run.  If you have one meal to eat, this should be it.

The food is fabulous, the service is outstanding, the experience is an experience and it is one of those meals that I am so glad that I was lucky enough to share.  The meal is whimsical but sophisticated.  It is long.  We were there about 3.5 hours but I was never bored for a moment but the person I was with was getting fidgety at the end.  Come with an empty stomach since the amount of food is challenging.  I personally, thought, two of the courses could be removed not that I didn't enjoy them but I think I would have enjoyed the meal more if I could have eaten the dessert.  I suggest arriving at 6 so that you leave at a somewhat reasonable hour.  Some of the other reviews confirm my concerns about eating well past midnight.

I don't want to spoil the meal by revealing the courses and if there are photos posted, don't look at them.  I agree with the former chef from Romera who refused to allow photos, part of the fun is the element of surprise, at least for me.  I think the meal was incredibly delicious and one of my favorites in the world.  I have been fortunate to have eaten at some pretty incredible restaurants so this is quite a compliment.  What I loved about the meal was the complete nod to NYC.  Every detail from pickles to everything bagels were incorporated into the meal but with a twist.  That is as much as I will discuss the food because I really don't want to ruin it.  I even tried not to look at anyone else's meal.  

Delicious food is important but service is also critical.  The service is outstanding.  Although, the person who answers the phone needs training.  We were stuck on the FDR and called to say the traffic wasn't moving and she told us that they give away the tables after 15 minutes despite receiving a nonrefundable deposit.  We walked in and the room was empty.  Seemed bizarre and inconsistent with the rest of the service.  

Everyone else just seemed to magically, appear without being intrusive which I despise or being too familiar which is my pet peeve.  The water was always full and the table constantly, cleaned without being annoying.  

But, my favorite part was when we were looking at the drink list.  The server and asked me what I wanted, without really thinking, I said a rum drink in a coconut.  It was truly, what I wanted but the reality is we were not in the Caribbean.  They made two delicious rum drinks.  Although, I wish the presentation of the drinks was as spectacular as the food even though, they tasted great.  (The mixologist should venture to Daniel who has nailed the art of the drink presentation with ice.)  

In the middle of one of our courses, the server appears with a pina colada with two umbrellas and two straws IN A COCONUT.  I couldn't believe it.  WOW.  The server, told me the restaurant has someone dedicated to making the client's wishes come true.  Seriously?  Had I known that, I would have considered my wishes a little more carefully...  I have never had any restaurant go so above and beyond.  It was perfect and reminded us of a wonderful trip where we had coconut drinks so thank you.

I cannot say enough wonderful things about the meal which was flawless and beyond anything that I have ever experienced.  The meal was truly "magical".  Thank you.

I wanted to save my 300th review for this place because it has quite a sentimental value.  It was my very first fine dining experience and it's where my wife and I had our most memorable meal when we first started dating.  

It's been three years since we dined here so I can't remember all the details on every dish but there's one main dish that still lingers in my mind - suckling pig confit with plum chutney.  This is nothing like the suckling pig I've had at Chinese restaurants.  It was so juicy and succulent with a nice crispy skin.  The plum chutney added just the right amount of sweetness to the dish.  To this date, this is the best thing I ever ate.

We also had a caterpillar looking dish which was comprised of Hawaiian prawns wrapped in avocado with some lime and yogurt.  Ingredients seemed simple but worked really well due to freshness of the ingredients.  

As far as desserts, Symphony No. 2 was spectacular.  It's chocolate tart with caramel and some type of salt.  This was my first introduction to salted caramel combination.  I think it's still on their menu due to popularity.  

Tahitian vanilla souffle wasn't as good as Symphony No. 2 but it had its own charm.  It was spongy soft and warm.  The server brought it out, made a hole in the center and poured some passion fruit syrup in the middle.  

At the end of our meal, they brought out several macarons for us to try.  These guys really know their macarons because they were all fantastic.  I really liked the hazelnut brown butter and toasted sesame but there were other interesting flavors like candied violet, rose chocolate, and black olive-white chocolate.

Service was top notch and very professional.  They really paced our meals well and truly made us feel special.  We had three servers who all worked in conjunction with one another.

They gave each of us a small box of fruit jellies to take home.

Like most fine dining places, Eleven Madison changes its menu so you will need to check their website for the latest fare.  I can't wait to go back and try their 16-course tasting menu.

I don't give out 5 stars very often, but EMP was amazing, we have dined at many Michelin 3 star restaurants and this one is the best one we have visited in the US. I usually try to visit a restaurant three times before reviewing, but this is out of town so one visit will have to do....for  now. My fellow reviewers have done a good job describing the menu so I'll not repeat their info. The food was not only great but the presentations were works of art. We almost didn't want to disturb them. Sometimes it's the funniest things that stick with me after an amazing meal like this one was....for me it was the twist on the Egg cream soda! Yum! If you cannot get a table but your are in the neighborhood, at least go to the bar and get an egg cream.

I have been fortunate, over the past 40 years, to have experienced dining at it's best: from the traditional (Père Bise, The Four Seasons, La Tour d'Argent, Lasserre, Taillevent), through the birth of nouvelle cuisine (The Quilted Giraffe, Girardet, L'Ambroisie), to modern cooking (Daniel, Jean-Georges, The Modern, Blue Hill, though sadly never El Bulli).

My taste now generally trends toward the simpler, less fussy cooking of the Mediterranean, and the fresh style embodied by the farm to table movement.

So it was with a bit of trepidation that I went to the "new" Eleven Madison last night, having scored a last minute table.  Many of the reviews and articles I had read about their latest re-invention led me to believe that I was in for a "show" that emphasized style over substance, and mysterious combinations and preparations of food.

Well, maybe Eleven Madison is responding and "improving" to those critiques on a daily basis, but I can safely say that my meal last night was certainly near the top of my dining experiences. The service, the presentation and, most importantly, the food were all stellar. I found the occasional New York "story" that accompanied some of the courses (16 in all) interesting and charming. Yes, there were some creative combinations of ingredients, and yes some presentations were theatrical, but NEVER at the expense of delicious taste and smell.  The staff seemed genuinely to share in our delight and experience. There was a minimalist beauty to everything.

And, yes, it was the most expensive meal of my life....be prepared! And enjoy every single minute.

One of my favorite NYC "staple" restos. Classic and yet not stuffy at all. I've been many times, but I have to say the last time was the best. The chef and menu have changed and the food has gone to a new level. Inventive dishes that mystify the tongue yet still light so that you don't leave feeling like you just ate a Thanksgiving meal. 

A place you can take a date for a romantic meal, grab a causal bite at the bar, bring a business associate you want to impress or your parents- it fits all bills and does them all perfectly.

Intense, honest and it comes surprisely not expensive at all.

The Amuse-bouches were truly delicious. My starter, the beet was good but i preferred the seared foie gras of a friend better, this was divine. Then we all had lobster, was not a big fan, but still good. The highlight for me were the morel mushrooms, amazing dish and beautiful too.

The staff was top notch, we were obviously more casual dressed as the other guests but they made us feel very comfortable and gave us at the end a tour through the kitchen.

I've only ever eaten at the a la carte bar area, but the dishes were always extremely well executed. No single dish completely wowed us, but overall it is worth visiting and is a more economical way to go than the extravagance of the full tasting menu (obviously, the full tasting menu would probably be preferable if it is available to you).

Getting in here on a weekend was like winning the lottery.  The art deco decor and a super serious attitude made me feel that the food would be serious.  I loved it when the server said, "the menu has been preselected for you."  Everything we had was just out of this world, next level eats for sure.  Every course was filled with flavor, my taste buds were overloaded.  I knew that every meal after this one would be like eating at a soup kitchen.

I feel compelled to write this review since I have had EMP on my "must go" radar for months and months.  My brother and his wife came to visit so I felt this was the perfect occasion to wow my guests with one of the best tasting menus in NYC.

For me. .. . it fell short.  Let me first say that the service is impeccable.  I couldn't have asked for better in that department.  The food left much to be desired.  Now I consider myself a foodie, I have been to many great restaurants in NYC including sampling tasting menus.  

I totally agree with other reviews that stated that it was more of a fancy presentation or experiment rather than amazing food.  With other tasting menus - for a fraction of the price I might add - I received outstanding, unique, artfully prepared courses.  At EMP I can only think of ONE course that impressed me.  To be specific I was not impressed at all with a "cranberry snow" course.  If i wanted cranberry flavored ice I would surely go somewhere else to get it.  Also, "beef broth" although tasty seemed like a ridiculous course.  A cup of broth? really?  Others found the carrot course to be interactive and fun, but I was not impressed with a pile of shredded carrots and 20 different ingredients that I received the job of mixing it all together - it was odd and i didn't find it tasty at all - mustard seed, horseradish, onion, just to name a few and shredded carrots?  NOT impressed in the least, it was odd and tasted bad, but maybe I'm just not a master carrot mixologist.  

In general there was a LOT to be desired food wise after leaving EMP.  Also, I will warn you not to participate in the cocktail pairing unless you can drink a LOT and eat very little.  I was so sick after all the combinations they brought i could barely keep the two bites of food i had down.  They started with champagne, more champagne, added Guinness to champagne, white wine, a concord grape cocktail, a whiskey cocktail, red wine - WHO would not be sick after all that???  Also, i felt a bit misguided since they made you feel like with the pairing they were bringing "custom" cocktails to go with the food - the drinks they brought were straight off the cocktail menu - and the two cocktails they brought were not my taste at all - i would have rather picked a bottle of wine or just picked my own cocktails.  I love mixology so I was expecting a custom tailored drink - not my waiter just picking drinks for me off the standard cocktail menu.  Had I known that I would have saved $145 per person.  

If you want to go to EMP to say you went and you don't have a big appetite I recommend it for the experience and top notch service. 

Overall I think there are MANY tasting menus in NYC - some for under $100 that were hands down way better than EMP.  

It pains me to write this review because I really thought this was going to be the best food I had ever tasted - unfortunately in that department it fell short, very short.

I came here for a going away party and whoa, this was amazing. I do not consider myself a "foodie" at all, I also do not consider myself very fancy. I am not a picky eater, I am easily impressed, and pretty open to trying new things.

That said, I really enjoyed this place. And I think a fancy foodie, who is not easily impressed would enjoy it too. 

This place was impressive on every single thing you can judge a restaurant on. The service was impeccable, the food was beautiful, artfully arranged and delicious. The drink menu was thorough.

I would 100% come back here.

Total: 3.5 
We visited a three-Michelin-star restaurant and ordered a 16-course tasting menu which was $170 per person. EMP offered rather experimental experience than the delights of the cuisine. The decor and the service were absolutely the top-notch but the food was not. I felt that EMP entertained through its experience and not focus much on the taste of the food itself. Scored 3.5 for total but refine with a next visit.

Food: 2.5 
Honestly I was not satisfied with a taste of the food but I enjoyed their participative experience such as Carrot. I scored 2.5 for the food but if I could score for the entertainment, I would score 4.0.

My favorite 
To be decided

Service:4.0 
Professional, attentive and entertaining but you might expect more at a Michelin 3 star restaurant. 
Note: The dinner took 4 hours to the end of the course

Decor: 4.5 
I loved their green-themed interior. I was very comfortable from beginning to end. Absolutely great for a date or with your important ones.

The experience couldn't have been any better.

Delicious cocktails, creative yet flavorful food and impeccable service. The chef Daniel Humm stopped by every table to have a conversation. He was extremely humble. We are fan for life Chef Humm!

Return ? Yes 
Frequency ? Occasionally

We went for the tasting menu. 

Compliments
Service was excellent. 
Food was prepared perfectly. 
Sea urchin was very fresh

Complaints
Not enough protein. There was a small amount of lamb, and some fish, but not enough. 
Dessert was creative but not very good. Petite fours were better than the dessert.

Personal preference..
I didn't like the orange infused egg cream. It tasted good, but I hate the creamsicle flavor.. Citrus and milk.. 

I went, I enjoyed myself. Would I go back again,maybe. I'll try per se next!

This place is truly and experience.  From service, to taste and presentation of the food, everything was absolutely perfect.

Of the michelin star restaurants that I have been fortunate enough to eat at, this one by far, stands out the most.  I'm almost glad that it took me a while to get to Eleven Madison Park, because it would have surely created a bias for me for the other restaurants of it's calibre.

They serve 16-course prix fixe at a hefty price, but by the end my wife and I were raving that every penny was worth it for the complete experience.  I must spare the details of our menu, because even I don't like to read long reviews, but if I get started, i'd have too much to say about every dish.  Take a look at there website for current menus and photos, they speak for themselves.

Dinner reservations fill up very quick for all nights of the week, so be sure to call at least 28 days in advance (which is the earliest you can make reservations).  And I recommend to call rather than use opentable.com.  I get the impression that phone calls get priority over online reservations.  (just a hunch, not a fact)
Amazing food, ambiance and service. Definitely recommend this place for a special occasion.

As is the case with a lot of fine dining restaurants, the starters at this place totally blew my socks off and then the mains sort of failed to wow me.

What we ate:

1. Black & white cookies (savoury)

2. TOMATO - tea with parmesan lavash and lemon thyme

3. HAMACHI AND SCALLOP - horseradish and mustard; chip with pickled daikon and sesame

4. YOGURT AND CHICKPEA - lollipops with curry; panisse with yogurt

5. TROUT ROE - marinated with dashi, cantaloupe, zucchini and watermelon snow

6. CLAM - clambake with chorizo, corn and zucchini

7. COUSCOUS - smoked with tomato, yogurt and olives

8. FOIE GRAS - marinated with nepitella and blackberry

9. CORN - smoked with blueberries, chanterelles and lapsong souchang

10. LOBSTER - poached with zucchini, avocado and amaranth

11. LAMB - roasted with artichokes, freekah and lovage

12. CHEVRE - meridian with strawberries, pistachio and garlic

13. EGG CREAM - orange, cocoa nib and seltzer

14. CHEESECAKE - goat cheese, chamomile and raspberry

15. CHOCOLATE - ganache with caramel, apricot and cocoa nibs

16. Petits fours

17. Black & white cookies (sweet)

I loved dishes 1-7. They were the most creative, amazingly flavoured appetisers I have ever eaten in my life. Dish 8 (the foie gras) tasted very metallic and was not to my liking. Dishes 9, 10 and 11 (the corn, lobster and lamb) were excellent but not exceptional. The remaining dishes (dessert and pre-dessert) were much in the same vein. I loved the black and white cookies at the start of the meal (they were somewhat savoury as they were made with parmesan) but the ones at the end were fairly ordinary.

Service was good but not as polished as you would expect at a three-Michelin-star restaurant. Ambience was classy yet laid-back. A young man quietly proposed to his girlfriend in the corner of the restaurant during the night, and after it happened a waiter walked from table to table informing everyone that a proposal had just taken place and a bottle of champagne was about to be opened. When the cork popped, everyone clapped and cheered and the couple in the corner looked thrilled. A touching moment.

What great seats we had to start; a corner banquette, with a great view of the entire room.  Almost all the other two seaters were small tables along a long wall, with one guest looking at the room, the other at the wall.  We sat next to each other at the corner and that was great. No menu when you are seated; the waiter comes to your table and asks you if you have any allergies, things you don't like, and then the tasting menu is somewhat customized for your tastes; they then give you this printed menu after your meal is completed.  As an example, my wife said she did not like oysters, so she had a different 2nd course than mine.
