Part performance art and part gourmet experience, as the service and delivery of the courses was as much fun as the food itself.  For example, with the Sturgeon course, they delivered a glass dome covered plate, with the area filled with smoke and left instructions to not remove the dome.  They came back a few minutes later when the smoke was gone, removed the dome, and that was the smoked sturgeon course.  

A favorite of mine was the Carrot course; they brought out a tray filled with small dishes of garnishes and spices and then came and fastened a hand cranked meat grinder.  Then someone came to the table with a tray containing a large carrot, which had been poached in thyme and wine, which was then ground up and placed onto the tray, for you to mix to your taste with the various seasonings and garnishes; Carrot tartare.

Another fun one was the Greensward course; they brought a small picnic basket to the table, which you could then unwrap. Two white china plates, formed to resemble slightly crumpled paper plates. A bottle of  house labeled beer, along with a delicious pretzel, grapes and an upstate new York soft cheese.

And on and on.....3+ hours of fun and enjoyment......

There's not really much point to reviewing a place like 11MP on Yelp, but here goes anyway: the lunches they offered this past summer were some of the greatest meals of my life.  All in all, with two amuse bouches between every course, it came out to a very long and very decadent lunch.  I haven't been since they revamped their menu, however.  I am a little hesitant -- I wasn't a big fan of all the "New-York-inspired" fare they were trying out during the lunch, but in 11MP one must trust.

Managed to snag a last minute reservation for the highly raved Eleven Madison Park.  Had a choice of 5:45pm or 9:30pm.  Opted for the 9:30 pm seating, while in hindsight perhaps we should have went for the earlier seating.  It was fine for the first two-three hours when the dining room was still full, but after a 4 hour tasting menu we were the 2nd last table there.  All the wait staff left at 12am or so, leaving us with the two or three waitresses/waiters still waiting on our table.

Also, after checking in our jackets the SO took off his isuit jacket and asked a member of the waitstaff to check it in with the rest of our stuff.  When we left, we didn't realize that the host didn't give us back the 2nd piece.  While things do happen.  I don't expect such things to happen at a 3 Michelin star restaurant especially if the second star is for service.  Now we have to make another trip back there to retrieve it.

-----------
Now for the food:

This restaurant has definitely offered the most interactive dining experience of all the fine dining places I've been to.  It's nice to have my carrot tar tar made table-side, to play with an indoor picnic basket, to open up gift boxes etc.  It was all cute and different, perhaps sometimes even a bit gimmicky.

While some of the dishes really were delicious and creative, I found a few dishes with their mash-up of flavors undesirable.  It seemed to me that they started off with a gift box with savory black and white cookies and end with sweet version.  You work towards your main dish of roasted duck for two or 140 day aged steak.  We opted for the duck since we saw the chef bring out our neighbor's duck.  After the main course all the flavors are used again in a slightly different way to bring it back full circle.  Credits to Daniel Humm for thinking of such ways to make food more interesting, but I honestly don't think the lobster, black onions and leak dish worked very well. What's up with the Apple Brandy?  Don't make things overly complicated when they don't need to be.

The local flavors were a highlight.  I enjoyed the explanations of what each dish was and the ingredients involved.  Tastewise I prefer Per Se or Nomad.

Also I felt that they were just pushing food out of the kitchen as if we were just a timeslot.  At least at Per Se, the waiter came to check on how were were doing before the next course was brought to our table.  They gave us some time to ponder on the dish instead of rushing the next one over.  It was an exhausting meal, perhaps due to the late hour or the massage we had right before.

Conclusion - this could be a very interesting experience worth trying if you want something different and interactive.  I would give it a yes recommendation because you have to try Eleven Madison Park at least once, but it is definitely not one of my favorites.  I feel like the chef tries so hard, yet something just doesn't work about the whole thing.  

I wonder what it would be like had I not given up my reservation earlier in the summer and several others, before they've gone full tasting menu only...

This was the most amazing meal of my life! In total, me and my dining partner ate/drank 15 things. Everything was great -- the buttery crescent rolls that come out in a warm towel... yes, definitely ask for more bread!! My favorite things included: the two bites of fish (one was scallop) in the beginning and the main meat entree. I had the duck and my dining partner had the lamb. GREAT. 

It's hard to get reservations so plan ahead (at least a month or so, I think you can make reservations starting 28 days before your desired meal date at 9am). It's a nice spot for anniversaries, birthdays, and celebrations.

This was hands down the best meal I've had so far in Manhattan. My boyfriend took me here for my birthday and the staff at EMP made sure it was a birthday to remember.

When we arrived, my boyfriend gave his name and the hosts seated us immediately (they did not even have to consult the reservation book/computer as it appeared they memorized all of the evenings reservations). At the table, there was an envelope with my name on it in calligraphy with a personal birthday note enclosed and signed by the staff. 

I'm writing this several months after the event (because I don't have work due to Hurricane Sandy and finally have the time to review my favorite restaurants), so I can't remember each dish, however these were the most memorable:

-Amuse Bouche: all were amazing...particularly the black truffle and parmesan "black and white cookies" and the quail egg
-Foie Gras: cooked with pork juice and scallion sauce - the best foie gras I've had so far
-Lavender Roast Duck: this was perhaps the best course of the evening and perhaps one of the best entrees I have ever had in my life

All of the desserts were great, and at the end of the meal they sent us home with a jar of homemade granola, chocolate truffles, and black and white cookies (actual cookies, not the black truffle and parmesan kind).

Overall, the service was outstanding. Though EMP is a very upscale, elegant place, the servers do not exude any kind of snobbery or stuffiness that one might expect at a restaurant like this.

I was so excited to eat here and I was not disappointed. First off, we started at the bar and I ordered a "bartender's choice". He asked what I liked : sweet, hint of lime, gin, and I got one of the best cocktails I've ever had: gin, lime, an herb, and chartreuse, I think. It's called the Last Word. Order it!
The service was amazing too- but be prepared to get to know your server well-- they talk to you a lot. 
When I eat at places like this, it's always a little bit of a different experience, because there are around 14 courses and some are amazing and there are always a few that I could have done without. There was a seafoamy cucumber tea dish bite that wouldn't order again, and an eel chip and foie gras bite that I had to wash down a little (too fishy for me), but everything else was awesome. (The bad dishes weren't even bad at all, just not as amazing as the others).
Carrot tartare-- beautiful, interactive, fun. Mushroom entree-- earthy goodness. Chocolate pretzel-- so decadent and yummy. The "bagel" was much better than it sounds. Oh, and the egg w/ chive on the bottom tasted like the best onion dip you'll ever eat, just salty, rich, and satisfying.
This place epitomizes dining as entertainment. It lasts for a long time, your tastebuds are, frankly, exhausted at the end, but I was on the edge of my seat the entire time and didn't really feel full until I tried to get up at the end. If you like classic, sophisticated, simple dining, go to Le Bernardin. If you want the fun, foodie experience (and a waitress who remembers you said your husband loves sunchokes and had the chef make a special entree), then go there. You won't be disappointed.

My husband and I had the enormous treat of celebrating our first wedding anniversary at Eleven Madison Park on Tuesday night.  We were delighted from start to finish by surprising and whimsical food that was as entertaining and engaging as it was delicious.  In addition, the theme running through our 16 course tasting menu was an homage to New York City (our home town), beginning and ending with two different treatments of the iconic black and white cookie: savory truffle and goat cheese cookie to start and the more traditional iced sweet cookie to finish.

The service was, as everyone attests to here, impeccable and yet personal. This duality is at the core of  what makes Eleven Madison Park such a delight: this is true fine dining, and yet it doesn't take itself too seriously.  There is incredible refinement to the flavor profiles (Lapsang Souchong tea infused grapes with Cucumber "Snow"), and yet the food never seemed fussy to us, instead it was playful: artfully planned yet seemed spontaneous at the same time.

Although the food was incredibly bountiful, we never fell into what I call a "tasting menu coma." Instead, we were perched at the edge of our banquette wondering, like little kids, what treats they were going to bring us next. The food never overwhelmed and seemed too much: it felt light and just right.  The dining experience was like being on a culinary adventure and the staff--including the affable and modest Chef Humm who came by our table to greet us--was taking us on a magical mystery tour of gastronomic delights.  It was a little like the amazement you might experience if Willy Wonka was the proprietor of an elegant 3 Star Michelin restaurant in Manhattan: "come with me and you'll be in a world of pure imagination..."

There was definitely magic in this meal that culminated in a trip to the kitchen that was a perfect way to cap off the evening.  There were scores of chefs and staff working away like clockwork in the blazing white kitchen, adorned with eleven inspirational words associated with Miles Davis that the staff stakes very much to heart, for example: Cool. Endless Reinvention. Inspired. Innovative.  We were led to a stand set in front of a photo of Davis where the charming pastry chef, Renata, made like a sorceress and turned Brooklyn gin into a final dessert/cocktail with the help of fruit, pop rocks and liquid nitrogen.  

Enjoying the adventure of dining at Eleven Madison Park was a wonderfully memorable experience and totally perfect for a celebration: I think Miles Davis would be proud and Willy Wonka would be impressed--we certainly were.

My friend and I made a "reservation" a month in advance, in early September. We were looking forward to  finally dining in a 3 Michelin restaurant. Two days before our "reservation" date, we called in to see if it was possible to add a seat. 

Then the host said we were not on the reservation list. But instead we were on the "waiting list" for the reservations. 

When my friend called EMP to ask for a reservation, the whole process of being on the waiting list first was never mentioned. Extremely unprofessional. Especially if the seats were in such high demand, every little detail should have been mentioned. 

I am highly disappointed at the level of service this 3 Michelin star restaurant has to offer even before we walked through the actual doors.

Despite feeling like a total zombie (we literally rushed off of our redeye, cleaned up/changed and hoofed it over to EMP), my experience at EMP was really eye-opening, and I enjoyed it thoroughly.

AMBIANCE: High vaulted ceilings and nicely spread out tables made the space feel enormous yet still intimate.  Decor is clean, modern and bright, with nice floral arrangements scattered throughout the dining room (although... it did remind me of an upscale hotel).

SERVICE: Impeccable.  Host was gracious and accommodating, staff were all incredibly attentive and detail oriented.  Our corner table held a handwritten card (snarky comment: whoever wrote the card, please work on your penmenship!) propped up by forks, congratulating us and thanking us for choosing to dine with EMP to celebrate.  Cute.  Our waiter was faboosh, and took a lot of time to explain each dish, answer questions, and occasionally have a friendly chat when one member of the table was away.  Every time we wanted to head to the restroom, someone would come and gently pull out the table to make leaving easier.  Empty dishes were whisked away promptly, but the staff was never intrusive.  A++

**One minor note:  I made reservations a month in advance, under the impression that we would be able to sample the 4 course lunch menu for $75.  $75 for lunch is not cheap, but hey, we're in NYC and we'd like to celebrate at a nice spot.  It was easy to justify.  Three days before our reservation date, I received a call from the host to confirm my reservation.  During this call, the host informed me that the lunch menu would consist exclusively of the $195 tasting menu.  Imagine my shock at this astronomical price for lunch!  J and I decided to suck it up and splurge, but we harbored uneasiness over the thought that we were bound to be disappointed.  Fingers were crossed that we wouldn't be, but hopes were not high. 

FOOD: Although I was provided with a menu to take home with me, I'll just give you my broad impression of the food-- everything was good, many things were delicious, some things were foodgasmic.  The one thing I appreciated the most, beyond the gorgeous plating, yummy, interesting flavors (which was to be expected when dining at a restaurant of this caliber), was the element of WHIMSY.  I LOVED how fun the dishes were.  Seriously, the amount of thought the chef put into designing the menu, executing and presenting each dish to the maximum potential of playfulness was incredible.  I've never had a meal like this before, and in that regard, EMP went above and beyond my expectations.  Hip hip hooray!

OVERALL:  I'm so happy EMP proved all my negativity wrong, and knocked it out of the park with the meal.  No regrets dining here... but probably won't be back any time soon (and not just because I live across the country!).  If you're the type to spend on experiences, definitely make a res to dine at EMP.  It's totally WORTH IT.

We had an incredible 4-course lunch from their "grid menu," which was a steal at less than $90 but is regrettably no longer offered. At twice the price, the food is still spectacular, but no longer such a good deal. 

That said, this is molecular gastronomy taken to a level few chefs can compete with. There is little else I can offer to all the amazing reviews here, but make sure you save 3-4 hours for lunch or dinner and come hungry. It's easily one of the 10 best restaurants worldwide, and perhaps the best I've been to so far.

I recently had the chefs tasting menu and it was one of the best meals of my life.  I really enjoyed their taste of New York themes. I particularly liked the take on the clam bake.  I hope they continue that.  

Be warned however, to do the chef's tasting menu be prepared to spend 4 to 5 hours.  One of our guests didn't realize that at first and had to run out early and miss the last two courses to catch a flight.  The servers were extremely knowledgeable and were able to answer all of the questions we had.

One thing that I wish we had thought of was to ask for a tour of the kitchen.  The table next to us asked for a tour and they were allowed into the back to see where all the magic happens.  By the time we asked they had already started transitioning over from lunch to dinner so we were unable to go back.

Enjoy your meal. I know I did

Just go - agree with other reviewers. This is one of the best meals we've had in North America. Perfect for special occasion.
Beautiful high ceiling, art deco room.
Friendly, attentive service without the formality and stiffness in many European equivalents. There was no problem with delaying dessert whilst we digested the mains. For my wife's birthday, they gave a small present (chocolate bar) to take home - needless to say it didn't last the trip home.

And the food was amazing. Wonderful flavours, textures and presentation. The amuse bouches perfect and nice to some small surprises during the meal. 

We had the 4 course lunch with wine pairings - a good option if you want to limit your spending, and also if you don't like sleeping completely stuffed!

Hands down the best meal of my entire life.  I love dinning and consider myself a fairly seasoned and knowledgeable foodie.  The innovation and perfection of execution along with the seamless exceptional service are what combine to make this such an overall experience.

My guests and I had the tasting menu, which in its natural state is 16 courses.  We decided to add the 2 additional duck courses that were being offered that night.  So, 18 courses with wine parings.....it was a culinary adventure into the splendid and rapturous.  From black truffle to cucumber snow, foie gras to carrot tare tare, caviar to duck heart salad, and lobster to sweetbreads, the amazing cuisine just kept on coming.  If you have the time, budget and, most importantly, the palate to appreciate, just do yourself a favor and go.  I wanted to go to this restaurant for over 2 years, and it exceeded my wildest expectations.

This will be a no spoilers review.  This is the kind of meal you should have without knowing what will be coming.  Including all bites, petitie fours, mignardises and such, the meal came to 18 courses (including adding a 2 part Duck course).

We were there for just under 5 hours.  Tempo was perfect, servers were elegant and professional without being snotty.  Dining room is stunning: there isn't a bad seat in the house and the tables have enough space in between them so you're not on top of your neighbor.  

Did I love every course?  Some were mind blowing, some were just alright.  Nothing was bad, everything was original and interesting at the very least and was plated and presented impeccably.    

If I were to nitpick I would say that our Somm was a bit to much of the cliche snobby NY somm.  Being a Somm myself, I loathe the typical snotty Sommelier.  He didn't hurt our experience, he was just not as kind and open as the rest of the team.  

The kitchen tour featured the single best cocktail I've ever had. 

Well worth the expense if you can get a reservation and like indulgent dining.

I have to say I wasn't as impressed as I thought I would be. I attempted to book a reservation for dinner with a colleague and was surprised when I was told the reservation time frame was 2-3 weeks in advance.  A month later, my company rented the 2nd level of a restaurant for dinner meetings.  I arrived and low and behold, it was EMP.  I had great expectations.  The food was good, the service was great, but I was expecting fireworks.  I didn't get that.  Maybe I'll try again and book the reservation for the 4 hour lunch tasting menu.  Hopefully I will get the full experience that so many have talked about.

I came here for my birthday with 3 other friends.  Since we weren't extremely hungry, we ordered the 4 course pre-fixe rather than the tasting menu.  

The food was great, but I wasn't particularly impressed by any of my dishes.  I had:

Cucumber couscous salad - bland and dissappointing. 
Poached lobster - uninspired by this dish.  "butter poached lobster" seems to be a common dish these days, and I expected EMP to execute this dish in a more unique way.
Roasted muscovy duck - This was pretty good.   Duck was cooked perfectly.   I didn't really like the seasoning on the skin, but everyone else at my table loved this dish.
Malt dessert - too salty and overall disgustingly inedible

My friend ordered the foie gras, which came covered in daikon.  This was one of the most delicious preparations of foie gras I've ever had.  

They didn't serve the complimentary free cognac they usually serve, which was strange since all the other tables received it.   We were one of the last tables in the restaurant though, so maybe they wanted us to leave.

During my dinner, Daniel Humm came by to introduce himself.  I thought that was a really nice thing for the maitre d' to arrange.

Service was good, but not great.   I didn't feel pampered like I did at Per Se.  The wait staff to customer ratio seemed lower.   

Summary - one great dish and 3 boring ones, which is why I only gave this place 4 stars.  I didn't order the tasting menu though, so I didn't think it was fair to take any more points off.

pricey for sure, but definitely worth the money

i had book a reservation for the wrong day so ended up not having a table claimed (imagine my surprise). the hostess quickly found a way to accommodate my party and the service remained top notch throughout the meal

the ambiance is great - the space has been redone and the way everything is laid out gives a private feeling, despite being close to the next table. 

the food is wonderful - ordering is simple as you just pick your main ingredients and the preparation leaves much to the imagination. i thought there may be a concern with portion size, but several "mini" courses are offered on the house in between the courses you've ordered, so you end up very satisfied. 

best course was the duck for two. best "mini" course was the egg cream - their spin on a classic NY treat
Great service. Dining is a process more than an endpoint. Extremely creative. Have 4 hours to kill?

I can't EVEN.  

Just go.  Have about 4 hours free and have it be a special occasion.  Bring money.  

EMP is the single greatest restaurant experience in my life.  Perfect and amazing from the huge amount of space they give your table to the cocktails to the incredibly attentive but calming and not snooty service to the meal to the kitchen tour that makes you feel like a important, cared-for, special person.  

Of all the Michelin-starred places in the world I have been, this is IT for me.

Also- they have gift cards on the website!  My parents bought my husband and I one with enough for dinner as a birthday present.  BEST IDEA EVER.

Oh. My. God.  This was fantastic.  I came here last night, and it was the fanciest, most delicious, and varied meal I have ever had in my life.  (Undoubtedly the most expensive, too.)  We did the extended tasting menu for dinner, which lasted FOUR HOURS.  It was amazing and inventive on so many levels.  I think the best way to sum it up is to say that the meal was just pure genius. 

First off, the service was stunning.  I lost count of how many waiters, sommeliers, mixologists, etc., we had attending to us.  To start off with, we had cocktails from their impressive cocktail list, which was really edgy, with fun names and odd combos.  (I'd recommend the Allen Street if you're a negroni person.)

The food was, as you can imagine from a three-star Michelin restaurant, breathtaking.  I cannot go through all of the 15 courses, but there were a number of things that impressed me off the bat.  First, of course they accommodated any allergies, etc.  But there were also four courses in which you got to pick for yourself.  However, they were cryptic about it!  They would just tell you the main ingredient, and that's the only hint you had.  As someone who likes living on the edge, I enjoyed this immensely.  I chose foie gras, sweetbreads, potato, and pistachio.  Let me tell you, "potato" sounds boring compared to lobster or the other options, but the waiter recommended it, and it was truly one of my top three favorite courses!

I don't want to ruin the experience for you if you go, but let me tell you just a little bit about the courses I loved:  one was a picnic basket course, in which they brought out a little picnic basket and it contained cheese, a craft beer to share, caviar, and bread.  It was so freaking adorable.  They also smoke sturgeon AT YOUR TABLE in another course and make carrot tartare tableside for another, giving you over ten little plates of ingredients to mix in yourself.    

We also did the wine pairings with the tasting menu, and if you can do so, you really should splurge and do this as well.  They accommodated our wine preferences, as well.

The ambiance was interesting, too!  It's in the Credit Suisse building, so the restaurant itself really still has that old bank feel... in an amazing way.  Picture marble floors, beautiful pillars, high ceilings, etc.  So cool.  

They really crossed all of their T's and dotted their I's in the most unexpected way here.  They apparently had asked when the reservation was made if there was a special occasion that we were celebrating, and when we were seated, there was a greeting card waiting on the table with my name on it from them, congratulating me!  (They also furnished a fancy letter opener, of course.)  They ended the meal with a card trick and sent us home with a fun little bag of souvenirs (which I also won't ruin for you).

This was just something I will remember for the rest of my life. If you have the means and want to really have something special, I promise that you will not be disappointed.

3 hr lunch, 12 courses. 
Very good. Creative. 
Young service staff (all looked like they were 20 something) will need time to develop to true Michelin level. Def recommend.
Hands down the best place I've eaten all year.  It's inventive, smart, delightful and so tasty.  You must try it out!!

3 star Michelin 2012

Ok, almost one year as passed since Ive returned, and let me tell you this place will blow your socks off.  They recently revamped the way they serve food as of Sept 2012 and as a result have gone tasting menu only at $195 per person without drinks for a 15 courses of amazement.  Im not going to go through each course, but they added a huge entertainment factor to their menu from the dome of smoke, to magic card tricks they are clearly trying to put that WOW factor seen at other world class restaurants ie. Alinea.  They still have the grid format for you where you do choose 4 ingredients.  These 4 courses will be different amongst your party while the other 10-12 courses will be the same.  And priced at around $200 pp its actually on the lower price end of most 3 starred restaurants in NYC.  Service has also improved since the last visit.  And I can say without a doubt, that the 4 hour lunch I had here will stick with me forever.  It is a must go, if you are in NYC.

I am almost at a loss of words to describe how utterly amazing and memorable my meal was at EMP. From start to finish we felt pampered by the incredible staff and were blown away by the creativity and whimsical nature of the menu - the food told a story about New York's history and the vast majority of the courses tasted at least as good as they looked (the only misses for me were likely due to personal likes/dislikes rather than to anything being wrong with the cuisine).

EMP now has a single tasting menu for $195, approximately fifteen courses and is exactly the same at lunch and dinner; expect the meal to last approximately three and a half hours.  I never thought I would say this about a meal in this price range, but it actually is a bargain for what you receive! EMP is located across the street from Madison Park in the Credit Suisse building. You walk in to a large open dining room with massive ceilings and there is instantaneously an elegant vibe. Tables for two are quite large and roomy and seating comfortable; there is very pleasant and tasty modern decor. The view out the windows of Madison Park reminded my wife and I bit of the pleasant ambiance and view in one of our favorite Chicago restaurants, North Pond, but the cuisine and experience was very similar to my favorite restaurant, Alinea (of which EMP is in the midst of doing a collaborative project). The main difference between the two venues is Alinea has more of a modernist focus where each dish has a theatrical presentation and EMP strikes a balance between playful and serious courses. 

From the moment you are seated at EMP you are treated royally, but the servers despite being so polished are incredibly friendly, chatty and down to Earth - by the end of the meal you feel like you have developed a friendship with them. One aspect of EMP that I love is that even though it is a tasting menu, they want you to be comfortable with your food and encourage you to state not just any allergies you have, but any dislikes or aversions you have. They listen to this in earnest and flawlessly accommodate all reasonable requests making great tasting substitutions without detracting from the presentation. This makes experiencing EMP approachable for a finicky eater who appreciates high end cuisine, but is nervous about tasting menus. Interesting side note, we asked what the oddest request our server has received and he indicated that one diner claimed to have a salt allergy!

The first several courses are a series of Amuse Bouches and all were excellent with my favorites being a play on the classic Black & White cookie (this one was served in a gift box and was savory with Parmesan and black truffle) and a Cucumber snow dish. There are also some shared courses (my favorite being carrot tartare that is prepared in a meat grinder tableside and accompanied by a fun tray with all sorts of fixings so you can doctor it up to your liking) .There are also four courses where you choose the main ingredient (you can either be surprised by the preparation or ask for a description before ordering). Prior to the desserts there is an extremely fun cheese course delivered in a picnic basket; along with the cheese is a pretzel and a really tasty beer made special for EMP. At the start of dessert your server rolls a cart tableside and whips up the best egg cream imaginable.  Then come the desserts followed by mignardises served with a magic trick as well as some apple brandy and finally some parting goodies to take home. 

Unlike some of New York's other top notch venues, EMP has really reasonably priced adult beverages. They have a wonderful cocktail list (with most costing $15), my favorite was the Manhattans - they have several varieties and the bartender rolls up a special cart tableside and creates it in front of you. There is a vast wine list with mostly expensive choices, but there are some under $100 and most of the wines by the glass run just under $20. 

We had the privilege of receiving a kitchen tour as a little intermission before the dessert courses. While inside the kitchen we were treated to the most amazing gin based cocktail made with pop rocks and frozen with liquid nitrogen; this rivaled any cocktail I have consumed at my favorite lounge (The Aviary in Chicago) and was such a treat to drink this inside the kitchen. My wife and I were truly touched by how well we were treated at a restaurant we were dining at for our first time. This was more than just a phenomenal meal but an amazing, unforgettable experience. This ranks as the second best meal I have ever had (with Alinea being number one) and came extremely close to supplanting Alinea for my number one spot. EMP is truly a destination restaurant and an absolute must for dining enthusiasts. A big thank you EMP for being the highlight of a great vacation; I will definitely be back next time I am in New York and will be returning to New York sooner than I had anticipated just to experience EMP again.

The entire meal was perfect from start to finish, but the best dish I have ever had in my life is the duck entree.  It comes with 3 slices of tender duck breast, then the leftover leg is used to make a creamy stew.  The best duck dish (or that of any meat) in the world, in my humble opinion.

In regard to the other food - nothing short of extraordinary as well.  While the dishes change by season, I had the lobster and green almond appetizers, both of which I thought was not nearly enough in quantity (in a good way).  Ashamed to admit that I forgot which dessert I chose, but since there were so many sweet dishes (from the amuse-bouches to the black and white cookies, seemed like sweets permeated through the whole meal) that all of them were delicious. Also had one of the best cocktails in my life - a liquid nitrogen-cooled ball of rum that literally exploded once it hit my tongue.

amazing restaurants! the best in NYC!
tasting menu is excellent with an great wine or the wine pairing menu.  constantly 
changing menu that has never disappointed over the years.  roast duck is out of this world

Pretty much everything everyone else has said here - best meal ever.  Friends asked if we wanted to dine at EMP when we came into town.  3 star Michelen?  Yes please.   Clear out your evening for a 5 hour dinner that you will never forget.  It's not just dinner....it's an experience.  It's tasting menu only and you get the most perfectly executed food and service that will leave you speechless.  Excellence is the stand here and it's worth every penny.

Just had dinner with the new format - 12 courses for $195 per person with wine paring.  Overall, it was a fun, whimsical, delightful meal with lighthearted but impeccable service.  The New York theme felt a little heavy handed and a few of the dishes were gimmicky and just ok taste wise, but we had a great time.  The pace was brisk - we were out in under 3 hours but without feeling rushed.  

Highlights - black and white cookies with truffle and parmesan, tomato gelee, parsnip, squab, egg cream, sturgeon.  All sublimely delicious, creative, whimsical, gorgeous.

Lowlights 
- cucumber snow with yogurt, smoked grapes.  This was unpleasantly, subarctic-ly cold, as in stick to your tongue and painfully freeze your saliva cold.  Only achievable with some liquid nitrogen.  So cold I could barely taste the difference between the grainy cucumber snow and the rock hard yogurt.
- gimmicky three card monte.  Contrived.  The food it accompanied was unimpressive and the trick utterly failed at the table next to us.  Watching the failed trick was way more entertaining than our successful trick.  And it's not three card monte!
- carrot tartare.  bland, bland bland. was just ok after mixing in the dozen cutesy ingredients on their itty bitty individual plates.  form over function.

Transcendental.  If you're going to have a four-figure dinner somewhere, it should be at EMP.  

Now that EMP has gone only tasting menu, those of you who have to stay closer to the ground can still get a taste of heaven at The NoMad.  The duck and foie gras are similar enough, as are some of the desserts.

But EMP is the full package.  It's worth it.  If he takes you here, you'll know that you're worth it.

I dined here solo for lunch, and had the lunch tasting menu.  The service was off the charts good.  I was invited to the kitchen where they made one of the courses for me, which was very cool.  I definitely tasted some flavors that I've never had before during this experience, and I would recommend it.  That said, I don't think it's for everybody.

Delicious
Again, of course in a place like this the staff  are in complete stealth mode
Profesionals at work
Food was presented in a delicate artful form
I love the intermediate surprises...
And additional cookie perks here and there....

start of by saying, best meal of my life. Not only that...best service. this truly deserves 5 stars.

1) impeccable service
2) endless complimentary tastings from the chef
3) DELICIOUS FOOD--everything i got was superb. 

there were so many tastings that came out that i wont even have time to write a review for each dish. However i will do a quick blurb on the most memorable ones:

-Lobster app--cooked just right, the ink from squid added a unique flavor.
-Duck entree--awesome presentation. they took a whole duck out and carved out the duck breast for two...a tad over cooked but still delicious
-Quail egg was jiggly and melted in my mouth...oh so perfect
-black and white cookies - the sesame seeds flavor really shined

i can go on and on....this is hands down one of the best restaurants in NY. Yes, it is a little pricey, but compared to some of the other places in NY--this place holds the top for me. its not as pretentious and with all the little tastings throughout the meal...makes it all worth it.

the chef also came around the end of the meal to say hi...very nice touch.

I had been wanting to check out Eleven Madison Park for a while, and my wife and I saved up and made it our first big night out after our son was born.  It was completely worth the wait and the money.  
They started us off with tomato water, which frankly neither of us was expecting much from.  We were both blown away right off the bat.  The various small bites they provided before getting to the main tasting menu were all amazing.  I went with cucumber, lobster, guinea hen and cheese as my four courses.  The wife chose foie gras, beef and chocolate (i can't remember one of her courses). The foie gras was stunning.  she requested it seared as opposed to the cold preparation they were also offering.  it was literally one of the best things i've ever tasted.  each of my courses was amazing as well, and the wine and beer pairings were excellent.
If I have any negatives to the experience, I would say that the service was not quite as great as I was hoping for, and the cheese course was somewhat subpar.  Everything else was spectacular.
Exquisite, the best meal I've ever had. Have returned a few times, and always consistently awed and inspired by the highest quality service, artful preparation, and astounding taste.

One of the best meals of my life.

Get the whole tasting menu.

Arrived at 5:30pm, left at 1:30am complete with kitchen tour and bottle of cognac to close out the night.

Do NOT miss this if you are a fan of your palate.  It costs as much as a vacation and it's worth every penny.

Treat yo'self.

Yes, it's all true. I agree with Karen K. EMP would also be the restaurant to eat for the rest of my life. I just love the whole experience. I think the space is beautiful. I appreciate the limited seating because it doesn't get loud and chaotic. The service is perfection as expected. Of course, it's all about the food and EMP has the perfect balance. As any top restaurant, it's like a symphony. Everything works so well together and each course is pitch perfect. 

I've done winter and summer. Can't wait for the fall and spring visits.

Food is very tastefull and deserves 4 stars, the ambiance 1 star and the service 3
Far below my expectations and doesnt deserve the credits it gets.
Would never get 3 stars in europe

If I could pick any restaurant to eat at for the rest of my life... it would be Eleven Madison Park.

EMP came highly recommended by a friend, so I had to slot it in during my 2 week visit to New York. I spent 4 painful months just oggling the website and waiting for the day I would finally get to try the famous EMP. When asked by anyone what I was most excited about for my 6 week holiday to the States, I promptly replied "Eleven Madison Park", and boy did it exceed my expectations. I am almost certain that EMP has destroyed me forever, any meal I have from here on out will just not be as good.

We had a party of 4, so we were able to try every single thing on the 4 course menu (and we wowed on every single thing), oh, speaking of the 4 course menu, what a steal at $75! Though I think they recently stopped offering their 4 course lunches, they now only offer the degustations for $195... not that that would stop me, a 10m high ring of fire around the restaurant wouldn't stop me from entering, no sir.

Just before and after our 4 course meal, we were given little treats to start and end the meal, for a person who doesn't like surprises, I welcomed these with open arms, I was constantly on my toes waiting for what gastronomical delight would come next. We sampled a black and white cookie (dipped half and half with truffled butter and parmesan... I'm salivating as I type this), an egg and chive soup in a perfectly cut egg shell, a new york cheesecake with goats cheese and sorbet, an apple tea, egg cream... and some other things I seem to have forgotten.

EMP hits the spot with both service, ambience and food... I will definitely be doing their degustation when I return to NYC!

Epic-Start to finish-all FIVE hours! Admittedly, we went on the first night of the new format and it seemed the flow of the courses hit some roadblocks once in awhile causing delays.  However, I would expect this to improve once the attentive staff and the kitchen get more comfortable with the new changes. The little surprises were fun, but it was the quality of the individual presentations that made it such a remarkable experience. Best dinner in America? It gets my vote.

Wow. Just wow. I can't even begin to explain the tasting experience (dinner doesn't seem like an appropriate word) and I don't think I should.

I didn't read anything prior to coming. I knew the hype, I knew it was good, I knew it was a Michelin 3 star but I always feel like with most things in life (like listening to the soundtrack of a musical before watching the actual play), that I just wanted to go in clear headed and experience it in its entirety with an unbiased opinion.

(Note: Dress code is 'jacket preferred' but I went in with just a nice dress shirt because it is just too hot to be wearing a jacket in summer. I would say 90% of the other diners did wear a jacket though. Bravo to them for sucking it up.)

I took my parents for dinner tonight without knowing that the restaurant had closed for a week and this was apparently the second day of its new format. Upon reading past reviews, it seems a lot of the old format has remained. I don't want to go into specifics because I feel that a lot of our enjoyment was derived from the surprise element, the amazing service, and the nostalgia and playfulness of the entire night. It was thematic, thoughtful, and beautiful. There was a nuanced and appropriate progression of the 19 course tasting (Yes 19-ish depending on if you want to count things like bread and this isn't including the goodies you get to take home).

I will admit to feeling a bit out of place in the beginning. I don't want to say there was a pretentious air but I think it was more an assumption to us knowing a lot about wines on the sommelier's part - which isn't a bad thing. I think it was my own unwillingness to ask questions at first given the daunting booklet that they call a wine list. After a while of looking through the wine list, we asked for an opinion, and were asked which kind of flavor notes and wines we liked and the sommelier was very helpful and not pushy in the least.

I was so impressed with the amount of detail that went into every part of our dinner service: handshakes and handwritten notes, remembering conversations (even as far back as my reservation reminder phone call), smiles as I walked to and from the bathroom, and napkins folded and crumbs removed as I returned. Just impeccable.

Over three years in Manhattan and I have never had such a memorable and pleasant dining experience. Over 26 years of life and I have never had such amazing food or service.

I want to come again soon. The soon being when I find a rich and generous boyfriend.

They really know how to treat their diners here.  For such an upscale restaurant, the service is incredibly down to earth while still being able to maintain its professionalism.  Love the atmosphere, the place is wonderful, love the decor.

The highlights of my meal.

1. Before we even saw a dinner menu, we were presented with gruyère cheese gougères and a sample of 4-5 different bite sized appetizers.  Yum, oh my yum.

2. They make the most amazing duck here.  They bring out a whole duck but only serve the breast and then take the rest of the carcass back to the kitchen for a second preparation with foie gras.  The duck is infused with lavendar, topped with szchewan peppercorns, and served with grilled strawberries and asparagus.  The sweet and savory flavors went together perfectly and the presentation was so colorful and pretty!  

3. For dessert, great selections to choose from, try them all!!!

I couldn't give it 5 stars though because the appetizers were sub-par and the desserts were just alright.  My friend had the ricotta stuffed gnocchi, which was too rich and salty.  I had the frogs legs with mushroom assortment, which was kind of mushy and had a strange presentation - all the component ingredients were separated and I didn't know what I was supposed to do with it all.

Had the chance to dine there last Saturday over Labor Day weekend, before they would be closed for a whole week to re-open as something new.  EMP is changing things up with their service and/or food, so I am glad I got to experience it before the change.  It was the best dining experience I had ever had, even after eating at Jean-Georges and Marea.  Service was full of surprises and the food was prepared to perfection.   Everyone was extremely friendly, from the host that greeted us to the lady that refilled our water.

 We did the 4 course prefixe which came with about 6 mini courses.. Took about 3 hours total... Everything that was sent out tasted great.  The tableside 'egg' cream was a nice show and tasted rich and delicious with a hint of orange and cocoa.  Both desserts were phenomenal all the mini cookies that were sent out were a bite of perfection.

Upon our exit, our server gave us some gifts to go. We received chef humm's famous granola in a mason jar as well as two twix-like candy bars that had wrote "happy anniversary" on the little box it came with.

One thing that did put me off was that as we left, I saw a lady getting a kitchen tour which I really wanted but did not get to do, maybe because she had the tasting courses which costs more.

The food was amazing but unfortunately the overall experience was not.  We had theatre tickets arrived at 5:30 and had allowed 2 hours to eat.  When we arrived we explaned that we needed to leave by 7:30 for the theatre.  Around 7:10 we reminded them that we had 20 minutes and would have to leave at 7:30.  At 7:30  we asked for the bill.  Dessert did not arrive until 7:40 and we asked for the bill again and hurried through dessert.  The bill was not given to us until after desert despite our multiple requests and then instead of waiting for the credit cards the bill was set down and the table captain  walked away.  Once the credit card was picked up it took another 5 minutes to return it.  I think what floored me wasn't that the kitchen got behind, it was crowded, but that no one hustled when we were getting clearly crazy.  There was no attempt at an apology and I thought they would at least comp a  drink as a good will gesture but they did not.  Then when we got to the theatre we had to be "that person" and of course we were sitting close to the stage.  A potentially great experience gone bad enough to get up and write a yelp review before breakfast.

Wonderful, creative food, amazing service!!!!!

Now why would i give this Highly star rated total foodie place 1 star

Trying to make a reso for my wife's Birthday (28 days away)  after having such an amazing meal there has totally turned us off

Open Table you cannot book 2 people
Calling you cannot book 2 people (only wait list)

But this is not for the availability. This is their rude petty way of economics
They did have many tables available for 3 or 4
Easily, we could have booked open table for 3, showed up, and said sorry one went ill or whatever. BUT THAT IS CLASSLESS AS THEIR NO 2 PERSON RESO Even after speaking to the booking manager and her boss

NOthing is that worth it

We have waited in line at 5am at Tskijji Market in Tokyo , eaten at many of Joel Robuchon's amazing M star , But never needed to hassle so much to get a table

IT IS EASIER TO MAKE A RESO AT BROOKLYN FAIR OR LA ESQUINA or MomoFuko Ko

Many many other talented chefs and foodie haunts in NYC and more opening
Michael White, Babbo, Blue hill, Rao's 
This list goes on

TOTALLY A LOW BROW MOVE....

For a $125 prix fixe only menu, I think one is entitled to high expectations.  With respect to the food, they were met.  I've had better food in michelin starred restuarants in Paris, but all dishes were creative and very well executed.  The extra amuses were also a nice touch.  With respect to ambiance, my expectations were also met.  The restuarant is beautiful and not too noisy.   Where Eleven Madison fell short, however, was the service.  It was so bad, it pretty much ruined what was otherwise a lovely meal and ensured that I will not go back.  The service started out as I expected.  The door was opened for me, we were seated immediately, water was brought and someone came by to discuss cocktails.  From there it was down hill.  They clearly forgot our drink order and started bringing food (which was ordered after the cocktails) before our drinks arrived - a major no-no.  When I asked about where our drinks were, I got an "I'm so sorry," but nothing more.  After waiting 20 minutes, they should have been comped.  Our first course came and went as did our second course (we both ordered the lobster, which may have been the highlight of the meal, although it was very rich).  And then we waited, and waited and waited.   At least 15 minutes went by before our 3rd course arrived.  The maximum wait on something like this should be about 5 minutes.  After we finished our main course at least 15 minutes passed before someone came by to prepare cream sodas for us tableside.   At this point, we were tired - we'd been there about 3 and a half hours and wanted to wrap things up.  We drank what we wanted of the cream sodas, they took our glasses, offered us coffee which we declined and then about 20 minutes passed before they finally brought our dessert.  At this point the place was less than half full and had at least once server per table, but yet we struggled for atleast 10 minutes to catch someone's attention to remind them  that we had been waiting a very long time for our dessert (no apology), which when we got it, we saw required no cooking just plating - yet we had waited over a half hour for it.  To wrap up - they were slow bringing the check and slow closing us out.  When the credit cards are on the table, they should know that the party wants to leave.

For a restuarant of this caliber, it is unacceptable that they blew the pacing of the meal.  I do not expect to have an 8:30 reservation for a 4 course meal and get home well after midnight.
I think part of the problem is that a different server brings each co 
urse so no one person is responsible for a table.  The servers are also all very young for the most part and maybe aren't quite experienced enough for the job or maybe the Front of the House Manager took the night off.  It's a shame though because the food really is something special.

My meal at Eleven Madison Park was sublime.  It's food, art, and a performance all rolled into one, and it's worth the price.  If you plan to go, don't read too many reviews because the surprises that are built into the meal account for much of the enjoyment.  It is exciting to see what the chefs will do with the ingredients. Unique combinations and creative presentations result in things like a frozen Greek yogurt lollipop with curry and lentils.  That's the only spoiler I will include.  This is not a place for fussy eaters or for people who are not there for the food.

Well... where do i begin.

Eleven Madison Park. Be ready to eat INSANE food, and drop a pretty penny if you are extra hungry, or like me, and love to go nuts when you try a place for the first time. 

Very Upscale. Snazzy furniture. Park view if you really do it right. 

Pretty sure these guys have a handful of awards from the who's who of restaurant award giver-outers. 

I'd probably recommend the chef tasting. I believe it was at least 10-courses. 

Some of the most delicious lamb (from Colorado, of course) with yogurt made from sheep's milk. From the taste, i'm guessing the lamb was given a EMP foie gras massage before they killed it and put it on my plate. 

If you want to impress your date, wife or girlfriend, take them here. 

Oh, make sure to try the prawns with chorizo!

FIVE STARS. Due to my wallet, i've been once. Plan to return.

Came here for my wife's birthday.  Not the easiest reservation to get but I was lucky enough to get a nice table on her birthday.  I don't want to go into all the details as there are already numerous reviews that go into that.  I do want to say that dining here is an experience.  It is not "hey, let's go and have a nice dinner out tonight," it is more an experience to be savored and remembered.  There was just so many nice touches that really shows their attention to detail, such as the nice little card wishing my wife a happy birthday, and all the little "gifts" they gave her at the end of our meal.  The food itself was delicious and once again it is a culinary experience.  The service is outstanding.  It is a bit pricey but trust me...it is worth every penny for the experience.

Excellent fine dining, my favorite in New York. Service is impeccable and Daniel Hummer is a culinary magician. The decor is clean art deco with crisp linen and beautiful windows overlooking the park. A culinary celebration.

My fiance (now husband) and I had the tasting menu to celebrate our birthdays - EMP is as excellent and beautiful as ever.  Loved the kitchen tour and parting gifts, the granola (!!) was especially unbelievable.  Leave it to EMP to make a special occasion even more memorable. This is still my favorite restaurant ever, the food and service cannot be beat.

[For the full set of photos, see the link to my blog on my profile.]

All one can do at a restaurant like EMP is sit back with unalloyed admiration and marvel at the scope of their accomplishments, and that's exactly what we did for 3.5 hours.

Food: world-class
Highlights: the smoked couscous, the mosaic of foie gras and the smoked corn (but honestly you cannot go wrong here; just about anything they put in front of you will be revelatory)
Service: world-class

I don't know that EMP needs another five-star review, but I'm happy to give them one anyway. I made the reservation for my birthday precisely 28 days in advance. The day finally arrives, I avoid the requisite birthday hangover, but naturally something else has to go wrong--some Mexican food (won't call out the place; have had many fine meals there before) from two nights before hasn't been sitting right. Nonetheless, I take some over the counter stomach soothers and power through.

And I'm quite glad that I did. I've eaten many lovely meals at restaurants of similar caliber, but EMP might have been the best.

We opted for the four course, which was the perfect amount of food (might as well save the tasting for the new menu if I'm ever lucky enough to make it back). The grid is different, though not markedly so, from the one on the website. Families tend to have similar eating habits--we all selected either the couscous or snapper to start, the lobster or corn for the second course, and veal or chicken for the third. Diversity finally came during the fourth course, in which cheese, milk & dark chocolate, and the plum selections were represented. 

Nonetheless, each course was superb. Even better were the extras--the tomato tea and raw scallop were particularly memorable. Not to mention the rolls and butter. And the savory black and white cookies. All of this has been said, but why not say it again. The sad thing was, I was starting to get full by the time my couscous came out, but I managed to make room--I'm glad I did. It was so flavorful, salty and citrusy, cut by a smoky melon and tomato and yogurt mix. My lobster, too--soft and sweet, paired nicely with avocado. My sister's corn might have been even better, with altered blueberries and the most delicious onions (that she wouldn't eat!). Chicken was cooked perfectly, with quinoa and braised lettuce and jus to tie it all together, and I didn't have a bite, but my father loved his veal. The end was a bit of a blur (due to wine, the sad return of older food poisoning, and fullness), but the egg cream was particularly memorable, and it was pretty sad that none of us could finish the cognac. The chevre with tristar strawberries was a hit of the table, as well. I was sent home with a dolled up Twix bar (twix are my favorite candy, and this was the best twix bar EVER) for my birthday & a meal not to forget. The room and service were impeccable, though this goes without saying at this point.

Came here for lunch today to take my family to celebrate my parents' anniversary. When we arrived here, the person waiting at the front was slightly awkward, but no big deal. We were immediately led to our table and a card that was propped elegantly awaited us along with a letter opener. It said something along the lines of thank you for choosing EMP to celebrate this very special occasion. SUPER presh. Overall, our 4 course meals were delicious. Some of the flavors and sauces used were very bold, but still complimented each other. We had about 4 to 5 dishes served outside of the 4-course menu and they were all presented very elegantly. Not the biggest fan of the black and white cookies at the beginning of the meal because it was too heavy on the parmesan side for me. And the other few side dishes were a little too heavy on ingredients/flavors that I didn't expect and personally weren't too pleasing to my taste. What was really great though was that at the beginning of the meal when they asked if we had any dislikes/allergies/etc, my mom mentioned she doesn't like cheese and from there on out, they made sure to follow that request. Even with the side dish of the goat cheese cheesecake, they replaced hers with a soy ingredient instead! Definitely very attentive. Between the four of us, we had the snapper, lobster, corn, broccoli, veal, pork, malt, and chocolate. The lobster and veal stood out the most for me personally. I left feeling full for about an hour and then my fullness subsided. The meal took about 2.5 hours and the waiters and staff were all very knowledgeable and sweet. My dad had the wine pairing and he approved of the choices for the most part. When we were about to leave, we were given a printed menus of what we each ordered ad as well as the cutest two chocolate bars wrapped in a box/ribbon and said "Happy Anniversary!" when you opened it. It wasn't too dressy since it was was lunch time, but my dad still brought a jacket just in case (wasn't needed at all). Our waiter was nice and the side staff didn't mind taking a few pictures for us either. All in all, I think it is definitely a must-try especially if you are around in the city!
Every accolade has already been properly said.  So simply saying it has the very best Manhattans in Manhattan.

I only came here for a drink, but I must say, that their Manhattans are the best I have ever had! The bar is pretty and the service is good. I wish they were a bit more attentive but other than that, it was definitely a nice place to grab a quick drink and chill at the bar. I will be back again to try the food (and another Manhattan!)

6/13/12: 
Dear EMP,
Thank you EMP for helping me give the best birthday one could possibly purchase and consume. Thank you for the exciting kitchen tour as per request. Thank you for the parting gifts at the end. And thank you for the best meal of my life (I especially enjoyed the lobster).

Love, Christy

Really wasn't worth all the buildup or $$. The portions are minuscule and the courses didn't blow me away but they were quite tasty except for the overly salty pretzel chip. Foie Gras was yummy and so was the lobster zucchini with perfectly cooked meat. However a meal is supposed to satisfy you and I was left still hungry and I had 3 courses plus 2 beers!

Long overdue - took the husband for birthday lunch.  Had the lunch tasting menu.  Everything was too beautiful to eat.  Loved all 3 hours of it! Highly recommend it for special events - pretty pricy but worth going at least once!

After waiting a month for my reservation to come, I've finally dined at the supposedly "best restaurant".  I was quite disappointed.  What did I eat really for $560 for two people?  We got the tasting menu, had no idea what to expect from the chef, but was very excited at first.  The first couple of appetizers were bite-size, and kinda interesting in presentation; then it goes down-hill from there.  We probably had a total of 14 course, almost everything was a little sour to my liking, and the portion was really small.  I only liked 2 out of those 14 course.  I feel the food was just mediocre, presentation is somewhat nice and delicate; maybe the food was too delicate, that's just not what I like. 

The whole time we saw a guy bringing random guests to take a tour of the kitchen, I thought he was gonna bring us too sometime during the course of our meal.  He never came to us, which is okay.  But when I asked to take a tour of the kitchen, a waitress told me that it's kinda of booked, she'll have to find out.  I KNOW that they don't book guests for the tour, they just take random people.  After requesting to take a tour of the kitchen 4 times over 20 minutes, someone finally came over and took us; by that time, we were both mad and disappointed, we didn't care about it anymore.  Maybe we don't fit the racial profiling for the people who SHOULD take the tour.

I wouldn't recommend this restaurant to those who live in new york city, there millions of restaurants out there that offer tasty n good food.  It's nothing special, unless you want to impress your date with the tab.

After weeks of failed attempts to score decent reservations on the weekend, I was FINALLY able to make it to Eleven Madison Park for a special night out. Everything I read about this prestigious, now three Michelin star restaurant made me believe it could rival per se in all categories. Naturally, I was intrigued and I had to check it out for myself.

The reservation process and the wait once we actually got inside was arduous and almost teasing. To EMP's* credit, the bar provided delicious table-side munches and impeccable service at the bar area while we waited for our table.

Upon arrival to the table we were greeted by an enthusiastic, charismatic waiter who endearingly reminds me of someone I work with. Unlike the waiters in restaurants on the same caliber, he didn't fall all over himself to constantly dote over us -- which is fine with me. He looked pretty busy with his tables, anyway. 

My first real taste of EMP's artisan work with gastronomy was the smokey apple tea. It was tantalizing and almost tasted like apple cider with a hint of broth. It was accompanied by a delicate quail egg with bacon and chive. 
 
The rest of our courses seemed to resemble some themes

Ode to New York:

-Not long after seating us, our waiter offered a quaint box of mini black and white cookies. Did I taste truffle oil? Who knows, they were soft and delicate, clearly reminiscent of old time bakeries in New York City.
 
-Clamming was a historic, money making pastime of Long Island and was represented tastefully in our meal. We were entertained with a "clam bake" complete with clay pots and a steamy presentation. Fresh clams teased our palates while the clam chowder was viscous and salty. 

- For one of our courses, our waiter whipped out a vintage seltzer bottle and frothed up two egg cremes (minus the raw egg of course) that sported a hint of orange. He enthusiastically  briefed us on the history of egg creams in New York while he served us a pair of glasses with a little "Eleven Madison Park twist", he chortled. I never liked a single egg cream in my life but this one won me over. 

Funky Sunny Springtime:

EMP served up a collection of appropriately spring themed dishes like epoisses - a sour soft cheese along side of little marble potatoes, pearl onions and mustard greens. Minimalistic and tart. Meh. The cauliflower with tabbouleh salad was diverse but left a little to desire in the flavor section. The yogurt pops with lentil curry and cocoa butter were a fun combination and super cute to look at.

From the sea:

Notable: Poached lobster with lemon, butter and burnt leeks. Yum. The Hamachi w/horseradish out shined the sea urchin dish by a long shot. Clams (previously mentioned in the new york section) were a huge part of the experience.

The end of our meal was graced with a mini cheesecake and blood orange sorbet with goat cheese. Delicious - it almost tasted like a high quality version of the amusement park favorite, dipping dots. Youthful giggles were heard while sampling this.

To top it all off the host/door guy was gracious enough to take some decent photos of us. The bonus was that unlike our waiter (who gave it an honest try), he actually knew how to use my DSLR camera proficiently. Now, if I could only master the art of not blinking....

While EMP was not able to trump Per Se in my standards, it was still a fantastic meal in a beautiful venue. Worth your paycheck and the wait? Yeah, probably... you only live once ;) 

----------------------------------------------
* Not to be confused with an electromagnetic pulse, my nerdy friends.

Omg. Omg. I am still recovering. This is the best meal I've had in New York. The quality of the food, the outstanding service, the presentation of the dishes, and the creativity are all phenomenal! Not sure how the other reviewers thought that the service was "stuffy". Compared to my experiences at Le Bernadin or Jean Georges, I found our server to be very friendly and chatty. I had a blast and didn't feel too constrained or formal (though they do have a dress code... men need to wear jackets.). 

My selections were:
- Foie Gras - Incredibly rich, almost a little too rich for me (though that didn't stop me from eating it all!). I wanted mine served warm, and it came with pork broth, some type of delicious oil, and crispy bits. Very fatty and delicious. 
- Broccoli - served 3-4 different ways? Poached, roasted, pureed, heck I have no idea. Delicious. 
- Duck - special of the day, off the menu. The duck is by far the best dish. They bring the carving board to you and the roasted duck is beautiful. Lavender honey flavoring and an incredibly crispy skin. I never eat the skin on duck or chicken, but I couldn't not eat the skin here! Served with braised duck legs topped with some creamy substance that is tasty but completely overwhelmingly rich. You. Must. Order. The. Duck. (They require two people to order.)
- Malt - my least favorite dish. It was pretty (aesthetically) but pretty average in flavor and I would've preferred a more substantial dessert. It had deconstructed pretzel thins, malty vanilla ice cream, a mustard-like sauce, peanut brittle, some other sauce, and some kind of crumbly sugar pile in the corner. Meh. 

Extras that come with the meal:
- black and white savory parmessan and truffle "cookie" - totally unexpected and delicious. I wish we had more of these!
- tomato "tea" with thyme and cheese crisp
- some type of foamy eggy soup with stuyvesant fish that was delicious and served in an egg shell
- bread rolls - ask for refills. Just do it. And don't be afraid to lather on the goat and cow's milk butter and sea salt. This is the best!
- deconstructed new york strawberry cheesecake - mmm
- black and white sweet cookie - meh. I prefer my black and white cookies huge and sugary and from a new york bakery. 
- egg cream seltzer drink thing - sounds disgusting but trust me on this one, it's strangely and confusingly delicious. 

I also ordered the coffee, which was amazing (duh). 

My only complaint is that things tend to be a ::tad:: oversalted, but no complaints with overall flavor and tastiness. The dishes are incredibly rich, so it's a bit of an overload. 

Just go to Eleven Madison. Just do it. You can thank me later when you're ready to pass out from the deliciousness you just consumed. 

!!! Be warned that you will be charged $75 per person if you don't cancel your reservation within 48 hours or don't show. Reservations can be made 28 days in advance-- I'd call as soon as you can!

Lunch four course tasting menus are $74 before tax/tip. Lunch will take you 2.5-3 hours.

There is no use writing about the food.  you need to go there to experience it yourself.  reading my babble will prob just annoy you :-)

but i would like to compliment the staff for the excellent service making it an all around wonderful experience.

Eleven Madison Park is like a gold-medal-winning Olympic team. It's all-around outstanding and leaves you in amazement, even with the occasional blip here and there.

We did the four course tasting menu and two bottles of wine for six people. Also tried the single-cup coffee. They book-ended the meal with matching black and white cookies (first set filled with a soft cheese and truffle, last set filled with apricot jam). This was emblematic of the whole experience - elegant, well-executed, thoughtful. Our waiters were fantastic. Sommellier didn't blink when we asked for options with a very limited budget.

I chose:

1. Beet (delicious, slightly tart, unusual)
2. Lobster (loved the roasted avocado; lobster itself was under-cooked)
3. Corn (only non-meat option; great as a side or starter, but didn't have the feel of a main dish)
4. Rhubarb (amazing, both sweet and tart, would get it again)

Everything of course was beautifully presented, and there were so many "extras" I won't try to list them here. Favorites were the chickpea stick with dill and the mackeral & scallop sashimi. Also the tomato "tea" (really a rich broth).

At the end, they left us with a whole bottle of cognac and individual jars of granola to take home. Our waiter even brought granola for the men (told you he was fantastic!) My feeling is this place is worth it for a special occasion. I still prefer Marea of the NY Michelin restaurants, but Eleven Madison is a close second.

With no offense to Eric W, I wish EMP was my boyfriend.  Stylish, fun, thoughtful, and always finding new ways to impress.  I was a little anxious our trip back wouldn't live up to our first visit/Best Meal Ever, but it did!  The artist in me loved the circular theme- starting with a savory black & white cookie, and ending with the sweet original.  They were so kind when I thought I ordered fish but it was actually chicken (who knew one letter could make such a difference) and it was even cool when they joked about it a little.  This time we got the kitchen tour with a special cocktail.  They even remembered the hub's favorite item of the meal and sent him home with a little tasting!  How amazing is that?!  I kind of want to come back for my b-day... hint hint.

Simply one word......WOW.  Hands down the best dining experience I've ever had in my life.

The food was creative, exceedingly delicious, and, though pricey, worth every single penny.

The service was exceptional. The entire staff was warm, gracious, attentive, and personable.  They could not have made us feel more welcome, and every detail was professionally executed.

I will be returning again.

Wow. This place is amazing.  After visiting Per Se last year (rated as the top restaurant in New York by S. Pellegrino), I convinced my family into going to Eleven Madison Park (the second best in New York).  It has been some time since Per Se, but I have to say I think I may like Eleven Madison Park more.  

While Per Se was about amazing innovative food, great presentation, and perfect service by the staff without seeming too rigid, Eleven Madison Park brought something a little different.  The two were definitely similar, but I think EMP brought a little bit of a "performance" to the food (more on that later).

We opted for the full tasting menu. Each course was delicious, and extremely innovative.  One of the first amuse-bouche was a tomato soup.  It was a clear light broth, but it tasted like the richest, thickest tomato soup I've ever had.  It looked so unassuming but was bursting with flavor.  One interesting course was a clam bake, where a tea pot sat atop some rocks with some type of seaweed lining it.  The server poured some water over the hot rocks that quickly steamed up and smelled of a delicious seaweed, and the tea pot contained a smooth and creamy clam chowder.

Another course that stood out for me was the pate course.  There was a trio of pates, foie grois, mint, and blackberry I believe.  Instead of being the usual thick and dense pates you normally find, these were extremely light and fluffy, the consistency of whipped cream but shaped into thin squares. Delicious.  My favorite dessert course was an egg cream made table-side.  Fairly simple, but this might have been the best tasting thing of the night for me.

All the other courses were amazing, although I can't remember a lot of them (well over 20 including the amuse bouche).  At the end of the meal, we were treated to a kitchen tour (I think this is reserved for those who order the tasting menu) where they made us a cocktail made with gin and other flavors that were frozen into an icee type of thing with liquid nitrogen, topped with a scoop of whipped egg whites also frozen in liquid nitrogen.  This was a great touch that helped set this above Per Se in my mind.

We were given a mason jar of granola at the end of the meal, which is a unique choice and nice change from the usual cookies or chocolates that most places give.  I highly recommend this restaurant and the full tasting menu, and I hope I can come back here soon.

This is my first Michelin 3-star restaurant on this trip.  I have only one word to say about the food. - WOW.  Chef Humm knows his ingredients and how to use them in a way a normal person could not imagine. From EMP version of New England Clam Bake and corn soup to gnocchi with "decomposed" buttermilk.  Very carefully controlled and calculated lavender ice cream.   

Service is professional but a bit ridged,  Everything runs like clock work.  Which make me feel like I need to be on my best behavior in the restaurant.  The restaurant has strict rule of no flash photography.  The wait staff will come lecture you sternly if you violate it.   I wish the website actually states that no flash allowed so I know to make the lunch reservation instead of dinner.

With all that said, you may ask why the three star rating.  The waiter provided the personalized menu after the dessert course.   After reviewing it, we realized that he forgot to serve us one of the courses on the tasting menu.  I am really disappointed that a Michelin 3-star restaurant who should run like clockwork could make such error.  I was so looking forward to dining at this restaurant for a month after waking up at 5:30 am to ensure I called the reservation when they are taking reservation for a week.  We did mention this mistake to the maître d' on our way out.  He promised to make it up to us next time we visited.

All in all, I am not sure what is a major sin,  violating their unpublished  "no flash rule" or them forgetting to serve us a course.

I think I would go back again for the food.  I hope the maître d' still works there then so he can make it up to us since it may be quite awhile before I visit NYC again.

I've been here a few times and it never disappoints. The tasting menu is truly exceptional and each course is a revelation.  The service is impeccable without being stuffy. They go the extra mile in so many ways, sending you home with a nice memento of your experience, providing information cards on any ingredients you inquire about, etc.  And, unlike a number of other restaurants of similar caliber, EMP will try to work with you if you have dietary restrictions.  

It's expensive but worth every penny - go on a special occassion for an experience you won't forget. I've celebrated important milestones at EMP and each time, the EMP experience has helped create a lasting memory.

Oh, Eleven Madison Park, how I love you!

I was lucky enough to visit EMP for the first time about two years ago, before the James Beard Award, before they went from 1 to 3 Michelin stars, before they were named one of the world's ten best restaurants, and I knew then I was enjoying something special.

I will come back as often as I can when I'm in New York City.

The magic of this place is their ability to take simple ingredients and make them taste amazing.  A whole course on sunchoke?  No problem and it will blow away food containing expensive proteins from other restaurants!  Want a goat cheese lollipop?  They've got those.  And when they do put the heavy proteins in the dishes?  Heaven!  And the dessert, oh the desserts!  No simple flourless chocolate cakes here...no, they are going to create complex dishes that are memorable and unique.

Service is impeccable, as you'd expect from a restaurant of this caliber.

My recommendations: go early (the service is faster), order the tasting menu (best $195 you can spend in New York) and skip the wine pairing (overpriced for what you get and not necessary with this quality of food.)

This was a fantastic dining experience on all levels. EMP is well deserving of its three Michelin stars and is one of the few restaurants in the world that could be described as offering real value at such high prices. Delicious food, a magnificent wine list, reasonable corkage fees (only $35/bottle!!) and outstanding service all come together perfectly. A real gem.

Everything was perfect- food, service and the facility. One of my top 5 restaurants in NYC. I had the hot foie gros, broccoli, Muscovy duck and chocolate dessert. The preparation was excellent, innovative and perfect. The surprise is part of the excellence that chef Humm brings to the table!

I had tasting menu here for my birthday. Service is excellent. Waiter is very professional and knowledgeable, courteous and give you enough attention but enough private time. But the food itself was not my liking. Everything was served in small portion stylish style which I really like but the taste..... Lol not so impressed for $200 meal... Presentation is it...

Last time I was there, I mentioned how much I liked the tomato tea, and my granola goodie bag on the way out had an extra in it -- a far of the tea!  

Also, another awesome kitchen tour with a liquid nitrogen demonstration.

Also, Humm did the rounds and actually spent a lot of time at each table.  #fanboy

This place was amazing! 

Service: 5 stars
Food presentation: 5 stars
Flavor: 4.5 stars (Some were a little too intense for me)
Variety: 5 stars
Overall experience: 5 stars

We dined here for lunch, and we ordered from the grid menu where you pick an item off each row and they will surprise you with its preparation. No worries if you are a picky eater; they ask you if there is anything specific that you do not wish to be in your dishes. 

The meal started with savory black and white cookies in a box with a neat bow.
