Then came the warm bread with goat and cow milk butter. Hmmm. The bread came in little fabric pouches. 

There was many amuse bouches throughout the meal. 

I had the foie gras, and selected the warm preparation. I never had foie gras warm so I was quite intrigued. It was amazing! It was seared and placed in a broth and with pickled daikon. I could do without so much daikon because the flavor was a bit too strong for me. 

I also had the lobster, which tasted refreshing and delicious as well. I don't remember what it came with though, sorry. 

For the third plate, I chose corn. This dish was a bit underwhelming because it includes pretty much cut corn and mushroom. The soy sauce was too salty for my bed of corn. But the mushroom sauce was savory and delicious. Those who chose pork and lamb really liked their dishes. I think out of the three, pork won that course. 

Most people at our table ordered chocolate for dessert. The preparations for dark chocolate and milk chocolate desserts were different. I'd not recommend getting the cheese dessert. While the cheese were nice, it's just a plate with two slices of cheese on it. 

I love the surprise at the end - the egg cream! The server serves you table side their take on the NY specialty. Delicious! 

And the meal ended with sweet black and white cookies. 

So you pay $75 before tax and tips for 4 courses and about 4 amuse-bouches, and lots of warm bread. It's not a bad deal for upscale NY dining.

Eleven Madison Park has earned every accolade that a restaurant could ever hope to win... 4 stars from the New York Times, 3 from the Michelin Guide, and of course almost universal acclaim from every single diner that has ever had the chance to go to Eleven Madison Park.  My humble review, will change none of that , for I am in love with Eleven Madison Park.  I am of course adding nothing new, but the restaurant absolutely deserves every award and accolade that has ever been bestowed upon it.

In short, the restaurant does no wrong.  It may not be perfect in every respect, but it's hard to leave the restaurant not thinking that you've just experienced greatness.  From the outstanding service that proves that luxury dining does not have to equate to stuffy and snooty, to the impeccably sourced ingredients and of course the techniques utilized to create the delicious food.  To me, there was no singular out of body experience revelatory bite, but every bite was extraordinary nonetheless.  I only sampled the four course tasting (which of course ends up being closer to ten or so with all the amuses and dessert courses that you're given), but even with that, you're whisked away to another dimension of service, luxury, and pleasure.  

While I personally prefer my experience at Per Se more, Eleven Madison Park is a much more accesible entrance to the elite fine dining scene.  While it is not the gastronomic temple that is Per Se, it is by any metric deserving at the very least, five measly yelp stars from this humble diner.

[1 visit, June 2012]
This was more than the best meal of our lives. This was a journey, a play in many small acts. Some of the dishes impressed, some hit a cozy spot, some were addictively munchable, some were humorous and intellectual, and some dishes I didn't much care for. Yet even the dishes that I didn't prefer were captivating in their alienness and complexity. I didn't like the uni with apple snow dish at first, but it might be the single mouthful that has most firmly taken hold of my memory. 

Transcendental cuisine. Casually telepathic service. So many small touches and surprises conspired to make me and my girlfriend feel like special guests that night. 

Come ready for an adventure, all senses open. Listen closely to the food, as not every stroke of brilliance is painted loudly. It will be the ride of a lifetime.

This review is long overdue but the experience was unforgettable.  Husband took me here for my birthday over 2 years ago.  Upon entering the restaurant, we immediately noticed the beautiful large floral arrangements in the dinning room.  Our waiter was very polished and well spoken and the sommelier recommended an amazing bottle of pinot noir.  Husband and I both had the tasting menu, which I highly recommend.  The quality and creativity behind each dish could not be replicated.  The anticipation was slowly building up as we went through each course, wondering what the next might bring.  At the end of our meal, the manager invited us on a brief tour of the kitchen and we ended the evening with a tower of french macaroons and cognac champagne.  It was absolutely one of the most memorable dining experiences for me.

Home sweet home back in Oregon but I'm missing this place already! Since I'm not there, you should probably go so I can live vicariously through you! Just don't post any more photos because I'm salivating after looking through all of them. Actually, on second thought - go right ahead! ;)

Yes yes we all know the food is amazing from start to finish. What sets the service at EMP apart from all the other fabulous restaurants in NYC is the fact that you mention they happen to have your favorite beer on draught which you only get to have when you head up to the NH/Maine New England area and they run out to get a growler at Whole Foods and send you home with some.

Eleven Madison Park provided us with such a wonderful dining experience.  My boyfriend took me here for my birthday and it was absolutely delightful. 

We went with the 4 course tasting menu and every course was superb! On top of that, they provided the most delectable amuse-bouche courses which included greek yogurt pops, a savory black & white cookie, and more.  At the end of the meal, they leave you with a bottle of cognac to drink as much of as you'd like and a jar of delicious granola as a parting gift. 

I look forward to my next visit.

Terrific place. Certainley one of the best restaurants in the city; ideal for a special occasion.  The service was stand-out and the food delicious!  Tip: order the duck.  Not on the menu but have it most likely available - delicious.

One of the best dining experiences that I've encountered.

The service was impeccable and second to none.

At the end of our dinner my dinner party and I were invited to a private tour of the kitchen where they fixed us up a special cocktail!  After that they took us to a lounge area toward the front of the house where there was a bottle of cognac waiting for us.

I can't say enough for the food. My friends and I decided to do the 4 course tasting menu and I must say that it didn't disappoint.  Diners are presented with a menu that consists of 16 words associated with food and you get to pick your four courses. There was enough food that I didn't leave hungry.

I would highly recommend Eleven Madison Park to anyone.  You don't have to be a "foodie" to enjoy this dining experience! Well worth the $$! You won't be disappointed.

From my initial contact with Marcus, a wonderful ambassador for EMP, who set the stage beautifully for our dinner to our final and reluctant good-bye, our experience at EMP was one we were both sad to end and eager to repeat. We chose EMP to celebrate our daughter's birthday and wish her bon voyage. EMP did not disappoint. The moment we walked in the door, it was as if we had arrived to have dinner with friends-albeit, incredibly creative and knowledgeable friends. We chose the 4 courses, and each dish was flawless. A surprise meeting with Chef Daniel Humm and a tour of the kitchen added to an already memorable evening. If exciting and innovative food, flawless presentation and professional and personable staff rank high on your list for dinner, Eleven Madison is the best choice.

It's going to be a great night...

I've sampled some of the top restaurants in the country and this hands down has to be the most inspiring dinner of my life.  It's almost an insult to just simply refer to this as a dinner however, as it was a totally inclusive and immersing experience transcendent of your standard dinner.

My partner and I chose EMP to celebrate my birthday and after being on the waiting list for only 3 days, got a reservation.  Upon arriving 40 minutes early for our 10:30 reso we were greeted by a sharply dressed man with no reservation book, no host stand, and no computer.  He welcomed us and asked for my last name, to which he quickly and accurately assumed my first name and wished me a happy birthday - it was going to be a great night.  We were escorted to the bar, asked what type of table we preferred, and were treated with masterfully executed and exceptionally potent cocktails.

Within minutes, a full 25 minutes before our reservation we were whisked to our table which was preset with a sealed envelope with my name on it wherein lay a handwritten EMP card wishing me a happy birthday - it was going to be a great night.

What would follow was the most amazing type of overwhelming you could wish for.  Although we lost count after 12, there were at a minimum, 15 different people who paraded to and from our table in perfect harmony. From the joyfully exuberant sommelier to the hard to read, yet playfully stoic manager, the entire service staff (including chefs) expertly walked the line between catering to your every whim and making themselves invisible.  The dining room is stunning and timeless, yet not overwhelming - they really allow their food and service to speak for itself. Oh the food....

We chose the 8 course tasting menu (try 18 courses) and let the sommelier suggest 2 half bottles to pair with the overall experience.  I'm more of a foodie than a oenophile, but in my summation, the pairing was perfectly passable.  But oh, the food: Our personalized, happy birthday menu read:

TOMATO: Tea with Parmesan Lavash and Lemon Thyme 
MACKEREL AND SCALLOP: Horseradish and Mustard Chip, Pickled Daikon, Sesame
YOGURT AND CHICKPEA: Lollipops with Curry, Panisse with Yogurt 
SEA URCHIN: Celery Root and Apple Snow
CLAM: Clambake with Chorizo, Corn, and Zucchini
COUSCOUS: Smoked with Tomato, Yogurt, and Olives
FOIE GRAS: Cured with Black Sesame, Gem Lettuce, and Duck Prosciutto
WHEY: Fresh Curds, Caraway Gnocchi, Spring Herbs
LOBSTER: Poached with Meyer Lemon, Burnt Leek, Black Shellfish Bisque
LAMB: Roasted with Artichokes, Freekeh, and Spring Onions
CHEVRE: Meridian with Strawberries, Pistachio, and Garlic
EGG CREAM: Orange, Cocoa Nib, Seltzer
CHEESECAKE: Goat Cheese, Chamomile, and Raspberry
CHOCOLATE: Sorbet with Lavender, Orange, and Maldon Sea Salt

That doesn't even include the mind bending "black and white cookie" with Parmesan and black truffle, authentic black and white cookie, and surprises like caramel popcorn bon bons, the take home granola for next day's breakfast, or the edible birthday present for the road. All was amazing but the Foie Gras, Sea Urchin, Clambake, and Lobster stood apart from the rest - simply inexplicably decadent.  

Clearly, I can not speak more highly of my experience at EMP.  With any luck and a financial recovery (dinner ran $725 after food, bar, wine, tax and tip) I will be back again.  Still need to check Alinea off the bucket list, but I cant imagine many other restaurants, especially in North America, overtaking this experience.  If you can get a reservation and acquire the necessary funds don't second guess yourself - it's SO worth it.

It was a GREAT night...

This place is awesome.  For sure one of the best restaurants in the city; perfect for a special occasion.  The service was stand-out and the food delicious!  Tip you'll thank me for later: order the duck.  It's not on the menu, but they almost always have it (unless they've run out).  It is the most ridiculous duck ever.  Soooo good.  And the chef even came around to say hi to everyone!  I love that.  Pics and more details of my recent momentous dinner: http://photo-hungry.com/post/24558134002

I would like to do a list of things to say about this restaurant however its quite unique.   So will try my best to be short...

The Food:
Many multiple mini courses prior to the four courses or tasting menu, whichever you decide to get. The menu is simple. Out of 16 food words, you choose 4. The menu is seasonal. The chefs will make your 4 courses according to the 4 words you chose. 

For example, I circled duck and the star of the dish is the duck with delicate vegetable/fruits/other kind of meats/or whatever kind of edible morsels  placed carefully on the plate like supporting actors on stage taking their place surrounding the main actor...the duck.  Delicious? Yeah!

Oh yeah, the free bread that you get when you go to restaurants? They served you two pieces of fresh baked croissants tugged under a warm cloth. If you wish to have more, please feel free to do so as you are paying over $100 per person for the meal.   

The Service:
Fuck me, did i checked into a 5 star hotel?! Yeah, its THAT good. 

Bonus:
Got chosen to go back to the kitchen to see the 30+ chefs making the food. A chef prepared a drink for me and my lady.
 There are imaginary lines for the workers to follow to assure no crashes will pursuit. At the end, the lady was given a glass jar of granola to take home and the guy gets nothing but the bill.

We had a lovely experience here.  This is definitely an "experience" restaurant.  Service is impeccable but you would expect that from a Danny Meyer restaurant (and the price level).  The food was interesting & tasty but not my favorite.  Gramercy Tavern is better I believe.  But well worth coming to at least once if you can afford it.  Get the tea service with your dessert.  It is quite the show & you learn a lot about tea.  A fun night to be sure.

I've waited a year to write a review for this place thinking that I'll finally be able to articulate why it's so damn good. But as it turns out, I'm having as much trouble as I did when I attempted to write about it a year ago.

But I'll still try.

 I couldn't help but feel somewhat queenly when I walked into the place. The first thing I wanted to do was steal the flower display by the entrance, but I figured I'd eat first and would have another chance to snatch it on my way out.

The experience lasted almost four hours, but had my sister not prompted me to get the f*ck up, I would've sat there until sunrise. 

In terms of the menu, I give it roughly 9 stars. I love not knowing every single ingredient that'll be on my plate. It's like going to another country and not researching every little detail of your destination. Kinda makes you appreciate it more, ya know? 

Anyway, if I plan to write about every little thing I put in my mouth (that's what she said), it'll be 2013 by the time I'm done. So, I'll just say that the goat cheese lollipop with beet powder was one of the best things I've ever eaten. Visually yummy, too. Umm...the egg creme? I had mine and my sister's. If I remember correctly, I think I chose Lettuce, Ricotta, Eggplant and Chocolate from the summer menu. Maybe it was ricotta? I can't remember. Whatever it was, it was delicious. 

I hope to return soon so that I can:
1) Finally take the flower display 
2) Spend all that I've saved up from my summer internships and babysitting money
3) Look really fancy
4) Try to get Daniel Humm to go out on a date with me
5) Eat really, really, really good food.

Best lunch of my life (did the tasting menu). One of the two best meals I have ever had. Amazing value to lunch here (ONLY $125/ person for this???? Seriously???). Hope to come back for dinner soon.

I made a five-day culinary trip from SF to NY which featured pizzerias and delis up to 3 michelin-star restaurants. More specifically here and Daniel. After the huge disappointment that was dinner at Daniel (it's a disgrace that it receives three stars -- it's clearly way way less exciting than any 2-star restaurant I've eaten at and would make a solid one star), Eleven Madison Park more than made up for it. What a great place, solidly deserves every bit its current high reputation.

The best tea you can imagine. The Greek yogurt lollipops. The foie gras. The macaron. The farm egg with asparagus veloute. Astonishing, wonderful dishes. 

The waiter was really good at explaining the dishes, which is really important to me (the guy with the Poli Sci degree, cheers!). The chef himself made rounds to say hi -- what an agreeable, humble looking man!!

Congratulations!!!

I've been here once before for dinner before the restaurant concept was reworked.  I don't recall it being particularly memorable.  But lunch at EMP in 2012 was completely marvelous. 

For lunch, they offered a tasting menu, which was pretty much whatever the chef came up with, or you can select from simple 4x4 grid with simple one word descriptions such as "beet," "Hamachi," "plaintain" or "rhubarb."  The server explained that the dishes would be made emphasizing the selected ingredient.  Very Iron Chef.

We opted to selected four items each from the grid.  Every dish was delicious.  They even came up with excellent wine pairings for each dish.  Pretty impressive for sixteen possible dishes that change frequently.  

The service was impeccable.  Our server was knowledgable yet very friendly and fun.  He made it a relaxing, pleasant experience all around.

If you like tea, they had some unique, very involved tea service options.  We got the matcha green tea service, which was beautiful, educational and delicious.  Definitely check it out.  

Afterward, the server gave us printed menus with our dishes and wine pairings printed on them (see photo).  Super neat!

This trip has made EMP one of my favorite restaurants in NYC.

As good as it gets, although we didn't love everything. 

I went with my wife and some of her friends for lunch. We all had the 8 course tasting and a bottle of wine - a sancerre, which was the recommendation of the sommelier. We added the duck to the tasting, and that was the right decision. The sommelier also recommended a perfect Cotes-du-Rhone to complement the duck for me. 

The Good: Almost everything. The service is attentive and welcoming. This is a top tier restaurant and they know it, but never flaunt it. I liked the triubutes to NYC traditions, although the dishes stood on their own. For instance the meal started with a black and white cookie - but savory with truffle oil, rather than sweet. (Spoiler alert - the meal ended with a sweet version.)

The presentation of each dish made EMP stand out of other restaurants of this caliber. Many dishes were nearly prepared at the table or had to be eaten in stages. It added a whole new dimension to the experience. A standout was the deconstructed steamed clam bake. This started with a bowl of clams and finely cut chorizo, then corn bread wrapped in the husk and finally a savory broth. 

Other details to note included: edible flowers to add color and uncommon flavors to mixed greens, a literal bouquet of thyme to flavor a sweet apple wood tea, and a totally deconstructed cheesecake which blended on your palatte, home-made chocolate rice crsipies in the dessert that had every texture of chocolate (from powder to rich cholated shell) and creamy vanilla accents. 

The duck marinated with lavender and honey was well worth the extra charge. It is sliced at the table and I can't do it justice. 

They made allowances for all of our friends' dietary restrictions, which primarily meant excluding meats. 

The Bad: I am shocked to include this, but there were a few early dishes in the tasting that were to my taste - the salt or sour were a little overpowering. The lollipops with chickpeas tasted like a glob of butter. It tasted like a mistake. One of my friends didn't want to finish it but did out of embarassment. I had taken it all in one bite so didn't have the opportunity. I would have been interested to see what happens though if we actually sent a dish back. Oh well, the rest of the meal was so good, I was hapy to overlook this. 

We would definitely go back for the full experience.

I arrived at noon with a bag and suitcase. The maitre d' greeted me at the door and took my bags. We chatted for quite a few minutes and asked me what my itinerary was for the day. I told him I had a flight at 7 PM. His response: "You'd probably want to arrive there by 5 PM. We may have to hasten the pace of your meal; would you be okay if we wrapped up by 4 PM?" A hastened 4 hour lunch? Yeah, I think I'll be just fine. 

No two ways about it: my experience at Eleven Madison Park was absolutely astounding. 
 
When you arrive and sit and look around the place, you can sense the history. Eleven Madison Park is just outside the big imposing windows. A nearby couple asked their waiter a question and the answer makes sense. The four leaves (the restaurant's symbols) are the leaves indigenous to Eleven Madison Park. 

I told them I wished to do the Chef's Tasting. I never even saw a menu. I tried to surprise the giggling child inside of me. I failed in this endeavor.  

It was a ballet, watching the servers circle about, effortlessly presenting beautiful dishes and whisking away the finished plates. No wasted movements. There but not there. Each dish was an absolute adventure and thrill. 

My Tasting for May 1, 2012: 

- APPLE (Tea with Quail Egg and Bacon)
- YOGURT AND CHICKPEAS (Lollipops with Curry, Panisse with Yogurt)
- SMOKED STURGEON (Sabayon with Chive Oil)
- CLAM (Clambake with Chorizo, Apple, and Potato)
- HAMACHI (Marinated with Horseradish and Peppercress)
- FOIE GRAS (Cured with Buckwheat, Buttermilk, and Lemon)
- WHEY (Fresh Curds, Caraway Gnocchi, and Spring Herbs)
- LOBSTER (Poached with Meyer Lemon, Burnt Leek & Shellfish Bisque)
- BEEF (Roasted with Wood Sorrel and Marble Potatoes)
- CHUEFLADA (Pickled Mustard Seeds and Pearl Onions)
- EGG CREAM (Orange, Cocoa Nib, and Seltzer)
- CHEESECAKE (Goat Cheese, Cara Cara Orange, and Vanilla)
- CHOCOLATE (Sorbet with Caramelized Cocoa Pastry, Lemon & Olive Oil)

Each and everyone of these dishes were superb.  

The quality of the food goes without mention. But let me mention a few of my other favorite parts: 

I was reading a magazine. Immediately after I finished, one of the servers brought over "some additional reading material in case you needed more."

I was asked if I wanted to visit the kitchen. "Does anyone say 'No'?" I asked. I got a tour of the kitchen. It was a sight to see. A well-oiled machine. The preparation of the dishes. Watching the dishes go through a final inspection. One of the pastry chefs even prepared a special dessert for me, with the help of some liquid nitrogen. Fifteen minutes later, I was back at my table. As if I wasn't already in awe. 

Numerous times I was asked if there was any more any one could do. Dining here is the most wondrous kind of exhaustion.  
 
I was escorted from my table to the front. My luggage was retrieved and was wished a safe journey home. I looked at my watch. 4 PM on the dot. As agreed upon.

My girlfriend surprised me by taking me here for my birthday. It was one the best dinners I have had. The service was top notch, and they really went out of their way to make it a special birthday. The food was creative and very delicious. Would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a special dinner.

Simply one of the best meals of my life.   The service is outstanding.  They make you feel like you're the only table in the restaurant, without being overbearing or stuffy. 

Dining here is not about that one dish that's so yummy that you have to come back, it's really about the whole experience.  

Eleven Madison is an edible opera.

wow, this place is absolutely amazing. very rare to find a place this good - quality of food, concept of organizing the food, choices you have to make on the menu designed to get you out of your comfort zone. amazing staff and services, this is a true rare gem. some of the very very best food i have ever eaten anywhere. without question.

The memorable: truffle ice cream, New York egg creme, and the granola -- what a nice touch and they are YUMMY too for breakfast.

Overall a very nice experience from beginning to end. Everything and everybody is very tasteful and elegant. The menu is quirky and simple and I love it! Would I go back? Maybe; after I try the other 100 fancy restaurants New York has to offer :) But if you haven't been, you will surely enjoy it and it's worth it.

One of the best places I have tried in NYC. At first I thought it was formal attire, but every time I went inside dressed casually the staff greeted me with the same bright smiles. 

Enough people have talked about the food, so I am going to focus on the drinks. Their bar is one of the best in NYC. I have tried out almost all their cocktails, and my favourite is the English Milk Punch. All of their drinks are completely worth it, and it is a great place to catch up with old friends. High ceilings, professional staff, good finger food, and some of the best cocktails in NYC.

Now the challenge is getting my Dad to eat here for dinner.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Eleven Madison!

We had a party of 4 and we shared so we literally got to try everything on the menu.  We also added the duck which I highly recommend.  It was dry prepared and stuffed with lavender.  My friend said it was the best duck she has ever had in her life and I might agree with that.  This is a bold statement considering the both of us have eaten out a great deal.

I also loved their black and white truffle cookies.

At their bar; if you don't know what you want; you can describe your taste to the bartender and they will prep something special for you.  I had "the Heart of Stone" which was light and tequilla based with a hint of ginger and not too strong.  

The ambiance is beautiful. I love their super high ceilings and very attentive staff.

There is no confusion that this is one of the 3 ultra-elite restaurants in NYC. Here is why:  The beverage program is world class. The dishes are meticulously composed and executed. The service is professional at a higher level than is obvious without careful observation. In short, this restaurant is essentially flawless. The small touches take it to another level. The freshly baked bread, made with NY flour is the best bread I have ever tasted.  Go and experience what excellence in dining is.

Dear Eleven Madison,

I've ignored you for far too long. Since you are the restaurant that I dined in right before my engagement, I've been a busy, busy girl and, as such, didn't give you the just review that you so deserved.

Here we go...

Everything at this restaurant was TOP NOTCH!! From the stellar & impeccable service, to the decor & ambiance to the out-of-this-world food, I wholeheartedly fell in love. It's so hard to know where to start because everything really jumps out screaming for attention first.

The SERVICE... I have seriously NEVER had service this good. They were on point from the second I stepped foot into their abode to the moment that I left. How does the host stand know to stand with OUR coats in hand waiting for us to arrive, for example, and that it was exactly us that just paid their check and left the table when we hadn't even reached the front of the restaurant yet? I'll tell you how. They're stealth and sleuth, making it their job to know exactly what you need whenever you need it without you even noticing that they're paying that close attention. Another example, they had so many servers serving you but NEVER did you feel like they weren't communicating. What I hate about restaurants that have to many servers per table is that I get asked the same stupid question several times over. No, I am NOT done eating yet. Please stop coming by my table to ask! But at Eleven Madison, this never happened! They managed to have a sommelier, the waiter, the water pourer, the dish server, the dish explainer (and by that I mean the guy that explained to you what you were going to be served) all at your disposal, but never, ever were they overwhelming, slightly annoying or lacking. Eleven Madison somehow managed to get the art of service down to the "T". What's more, I absolutely loved that every time our dishes were taken, we were asked whether we liked them or not, and what we thought of them. To me, that meant that we were at a restaurant where the chef takes great care and note and really cares about the opinions of his patrons.

The FOOD... OMG was the food amazing!!! And so much!!! We went for dinner which was something like 5 courses. What we had, however, was something like 3 amuse-bouche's that preceded our first course, followed by our first 3 courses, then a pre-dessert, then some sort of drink, then our dessert, followed by 2 more unplanned dessert and then a complimentary bottle of cognac that was left at the table "just because the chef likes to finish his dinners that way". What?! How is this much good food by one chef all on the same night even possible? By the time we were finished, we honestly could not eat one more thing. 

The DECOR... I loved Eleven Madison because it had that elegant feeling without being stuffy. I believe that they're impeccable and unpretentious service helped with this. From the high ceilings to the beautiful flowers to the large windows, everything about it screamed elegance and class.

Overall, I can say that, for once, all the hype is totally worth it. And those 2 Michelen stars... those were very well deserved here. It was so refreshing to finally see a chef at a high-class restaurant that really did care about his patrons. And it was so nice to be reminded that service really is an art, and that great service definitely is possible.

Eleven Madison... I bow down to you. You have my heart.

Lunch at EMP was the highlight of my trip to New York. From beginning to end the service was simply exquisite. The room is beautiful with high ceilings, a cream palate and tons of beautiful fresh flowers. 

From beginning to end the meal was delicious and it seemed like the food never stopped coming. I had opted for the asparagus, lobster, poussin and malt and each course was delightful, the lobster with crispy leek was my favorite. 

That doesn't even include all of the extras: savory black and while cookies, quail eggs with smoked tea, sturgon with chive oil, bread with both goat and cows milk butters, egg creams, goat cheese cake, sweet black and white cookies, peanut butter cookies, a bottle of cognac and take away chocolates that tasted like gourmet Twix bars.  

I also had two drinks including a Hemingway's Daiquiri and both drinks were delicious and strong. 

While I wouldn't say this was a cheap lunch by any means, I felt like the price I paid was a steal for the experience. The tasting menu is next on my agenda the next time I'm in New York!

Went for our anniversary it took 15 minutes for a waiter to take our drink order.should have left then. Had to ask multiple times to have our wine poured. It took an hour between the 2nd and 3rd courses. We asked 3 different people to check on it..we were told that they didn't want to send out any food that wasn't 100 percent. No acknowledgement of our anniversary. They did buy us an espresso for our inconvenience.food was good, but the chef spent more time in the dining room than in the kitchen should have gone to le Bernadine. Called the next day. Mgr was in a meeting.secretary was aware of problem. NO CALL BACK.. You can tell that Danny Meyer isn't here anymore.

3 Michelin stars, currently ranked the 10th best restaurant in the world, #1 on Adam Platt's 101 Best Restaurants in NYC, and Daniel Humm's recent James Beard 2012 title of Outstanding Chef, Eleven Madison Park is not short of reputable praises.  I've been dickriding this restaurant (and any Daniel Humm related news) for the past 2 years so I was really expecting EMP to be one of the best dining experiences of my life.

Ambiance: 5 (classy and upscale without being overly romantic  or stuffy)
Service: 5
Food: 4

To sum up the food in a nutshell: everything was delicious, but no dish stood out as a dish that I crave to return to again and again.  My favorites of the night were the seared foie gras starter and also the ribeye steak.  However, this still remains one of my favorite meals given the unique menu format, ingredient-driven farm-to-table dining, friendly and flawless service, spectacular interior space, beautiful plating, and attention to detail (ok there was someone IRONING the tableclothes here) throughout the night that really pulled together the entire meal.  I really appreciated the toast to NYC that was a central theme to our meal.  For example, the meal started with the EMP take on a NYC classic, the black and white cookie (but in this case, it was savory), presented in a wrapped box, and our meal ended with black and white cookies again, this time sweet as they originally should be.  Details like these are what makes a restaurant like this so memorable.  Also, the hors d'oeuvres here (and they bring out a lot!) are actually the best I've had at any of the top-rated restaurants in Manhattan.  

You should definitely dine at Eleven Madison Park at least once for an incredible and unforgettable dining experience with a well-scripted homage to the city.

So I went back in here for my birthday because my previous experience was THAT GOOD that i actually didnt entertain any other restaurant in mind for my birthday. EMP, you get another 5 stars from me.

I have a blog, and In that blog (go to my profile, the link is there), you will see the entire progression of my mealS in this restaurant.

If there is anything that I can suggest, come here for lunch. It is definitely a good deal and it feels like a mini vacation.

The food here is definitely show stopping, both in taste and in presentation. The dishes are not something you would necessarily eat daily, but to taste them at least once in your life is a gift. Everything is exquisite, cooked perfectly and of course, presented so uniquely. The service is also very friendly and you would never feel out of place if you weren't used to dining at such high-end restaurants. 

My husband took me here for my birthday and it is definitely a birthday I will never forget. I don't think you can experience the same cuisine anywhere else, perhaps in t he entire world. I also loved how the bill was handwritten (in very nice fancy handwriting too) at the end of our meal. It was such a nice personal touch and I kept the bill as a momento of my bday dinner because it was such beautiful and lovely handwritten receipt. They also gave us a jar of their house-made granola to take home, which by far is THE BEST granola I have ever had in my entire life. It is AMAZING. Very crunchy and fresh with a hint of honey. I wish they sold it in store. I will forever dream of eating another jar of that granola. 

Would I come back? I'd love to, but the price is a bit hefty.Maybe if someone offered me a free lunch or dinner.

One of the best meals I will ever have in my entire life. Food was outstanding as expected with some unique twists, but service was beyond belief (including other notable michelin star restaurants in nyc). Went with 5 other close friends and dined for over 5 hours. Chef treated us to nitrogen blasted sorbet and a kitchen tour afterwards along with signed cook books. 

Definately a must return.
Friendly service, excellent, artistic and inventive went with the tasting menu and nothing but pure gourmet bliss.

Dinner at Eleven Madison Park does not disappoint and I'm now clear why they're the 10th best restaurant in the world. The menu is a grid of 16 ingredients, for the normal people who do the four course tasting menu, you simply choose one main ingredient from each of the four main sections and then they'll create your course. Aside from the main ingredient list, they don't give you any details. If you're not adventurous, this can be a bit anxiety producing but this is the place to let it all hang out, trust me. If you're a "foodie" I would highly recommend doing the entire tasting menu (which turns out to be 14 courses and just over 4 hours, yes, four.hours.). With the tasting menu, you don't even get to select your ingredients (similar to the 16 course menu at Joël Robuchon*), you simply tell them your dietary restrictions and then let the chefs play.

I was informed by the staff that the chefs love it when a vegetarian comes it because they like the challenge (my theory is that they also like the enormous profit margins they make off a vegetarian tasting menu vs. a carnivorous one which includes foie gras, lobster, scallops, filet mignon, etc. etc.).

As with any tasting menu, they print and give you a copy upon departure so that you know what you consumed. Off my menu, I really enjoyed the apple tea, the yogurt lollipops (even though I'm not a fan of chicpeaks or curry, which says a lot), I really enjoyed the mushroom sabayon with chive oil (*so* good), the asparagus poached in white wine, and the gnocchi. I was really surprised they didn't rely more on risottos and pastas as those seem like the safe "go to" dishes for vegetarian selections at Michelin's these days. I must also say that I was not floored by the dessert but I was already full at that point and just wanted the gavage to be over with. They also neglect to mention on this menu the entire bottle of cognac that they conveniently  leave at your table at the end of dinner. Don't do it. At least, don't do it all.

I'm giving it four stars rather than five because I found a hair in my 6th course - they quickly replaced the dish and because the dessert was simply an unacceptable afterthought for a Michelin rated restaurant. 

Upon reflection, if you were to ask me if EMP is worth all the hype, I would say so. The service was impeccable as you would expect and the restaurant is not as stuffy and pretentious as other Michelin restaurants in New York City and the decor is severely understated. With that being said, it's a world class restaurant so get those reservations in early, dress up! (please, people, leave your jean jackets at home), and enjoy!

-------------------------------------- 
* = Joël Robuchon: http://www.yelp.com/biz/jo%C3%ABl-robuchon-las-vegas-5

Went for celebratory graduation meal on Mother's day- they served dinner throughout the entire day. The moment we walked in, the service was impeccable and friendly. The decor of the restaurant was beautiful. We received a warm welcome letter on our table- although I guess sitting next to the date was a bit...odd? but understandable to view the different creations from the kitchen. 

Food: We both got the four course tasting menu which lasted for about three hours. I got the hamachi, cobia, duck, and chocolate. The Hamachi was extremely fresh and I really enjoyed the, i think its the wasabi tasting "kick" to it. The cobia was really delicious as well-  all the main dishes were portioned about right or if anything a bit much. There were many different flavors on a dish, so for me, so it was a bit overwhelming. However, all the different flavors did somehow magically "worked together" to make an amazing dish. Throughout the dining experience, there were many unique amuse bouches. I was not a big fan of the lollipop looking one, However, I did love their cheesecake inspired dessert and of course the lavender and honey duck. I would go back to EMP just to eat that duck again. The presentation, texture, and everything about that duck was AMAZING. They also made a roasted duck breast and duck leg a la crème fraiche. A bit salty but nonetheless really tasty. I was stuffed after the meal and could barely get out of my seat. 

The plating of the food was also very unique and beautiful. I would go back to EMP to try some of the different main ingredients and of course the duck.

Recently came here for a wedding reception lunch and it was absolutely fantastic!  You can see why this place has the reputation that they do, they care about customer service and creating amazing food!  Everything from the bread to the dessert was amazing, even when served in quantity (for a wedding).  If i get the chance, I would love to try this place again.

I suspect this would've been a different story if we had gone for the 4 course lunch, but my friend and I opted for the tasting menu. Over the course of three hours, my friend and I tried a variety of courses, and our big take away was EMP makes some really interesting, beautiful food. That doesn't necessarily mean the food was the most delicious, though. 

The two stand-outs included a course where we had two types of clams, chowder served in a tea pot, a lobster croquette and some sort of cornbread. The other was the lobster with burnt leeks and a lobster bisque. The sauce was so good, I was lapping it up with my spoon. The black sesame vinaigrette on our foie gras dish was also to die for. All the other dishes were interesting, but really only had one or two elements that were delicious on the plate. 

The service was impeccable, although the way the staff came out was precise to the point of being almost too militaristic. The restaurant itself was gorgeous on a sunny afternoon, and there was a nice, casual hum to the dining room. 

Overall, I had a wonderful dining experience. The food was so inventive and worthy of EMP's 3-Michelin stars. However, compared to Per Se, I can't say that it's the best I've ever had.

went here twice, I want to give it more, presentation was superb but the dishes itself didn't impress. For appetizers we've had fois gras, crab, octopus, fluke, which were all nice, but I can get the same at mid-tier restaurants. Not much skill required to prepare these dishes. Same said for their mains - veal, pork, venison, lamb. Where's the sauce? And most dissapointing is their desserts - ice-cream and raisins? crumbled oreo? save yourself the $ and go to Dominque Ansel for dessert. 
On the plus side, service was excellent, we also got to meet the chef and they gave us nitrogen sorbet and bottle of cognac on the house.

I think my friend summed it up perfectly when he said in another review of EMP that "You know it's a good sign when you haven't even gotten through the hors d'oeuvres and you feel like you've already had the best meal of your life."

The four course tasting was perfectly sized, timed and paired. Each of the dishes which were amazing in themselves were interspersed with well thought out amuse bouches. Each dish did an excellent job of highlighting and showcasing the main ingredient while providing an healthy amount of flavour.  Although my wife didn't appreciate the savoury (cheese) dessert that I selected, it was one of the most delightful desserts I have ever had.

Without a doubt the best meal I've ever had.  Now I just have to figure out when to come back...

Let me start by saying "Oh My Goodness"! One of the few three star Michelin restaurants in the City and I can see why. Dip deep into your pocket for this one but enjoy every minute that you are there. The service was impeccable. The menu is crazy good fun with you choosing an ingredient and then they cook the dish with it. Everything was as it should be including a bottle, yes a bottle of Cognac for you to enjoy at the end of the meal.

One of the best resteraunts in NYC if not the best in terms of service, atmosphere, and food. Dishes are both aesthetically and viscerally inspiring. Rarely do I encounter a resteraunt where nearly each dish broadens my understanding of what food can be. The price is steep for the tasting menu as can be expected at this level of resteraunt but well worth the experience if you have the money. I compare this to other similar echelon resteraunts such as Daniel and Jean Georges and found this to be my favorite experience. Daniel is of course nearly flawless but I found the environment at 11 Madison more comfortable.

Where to begin....

I enjoy the lavender and honey duck the most, presentation and texture of the dish was just top notch. They made a duck duo, roasted duck breast and duck leg a la crème fraiche (latter was quite heavy but I never had duck leg prepared this way). The server only carved out the best part of the duck breast for plating but I secretly wanted to ask the waiter if I can bring home the duck bones to make congee, yet that would have been embarrassing at EMP.

Other than that, the foie gras wrapped in cured duck prosciutto as first course deserves a standing ovation on its own. It was melting-in-your-mouth kind of perfect. Another first course I tried is the hamachi ceviche dish in which one can taste the freshness of the sea but the level of craftsmanship is similar to those at Marea.

Love the amuse bouches especially the scallop ceviche. Wine pairing was just standard in this case. The paring did not bring any wow factor but it is probably primarily due to individual customization of the four-course tasting menu. I would imagine that the wine paring would be great if a chef's menu is chosen. The cocktails at the bar were well executed. Desserts were a bit different from my last a la carte experience since they prepared a New York black and white chocolate cookies, one savory before the meal and one sweet after the meal. The only thing I did not enjoy was the New York egg cream shot but others may find it enjoyable. I chose "MALT" for my dessert dish, which comes in with a malt gelato with splash of salted caramel, peanut butter, and malt chocolate saucing. Again, another great combination of flavors.

The kitchen tour was really fun! Its amazing how big the kitchen operation is. They made a special pomegranate-infused brandy cocktail for guests to enjoy at the "observation deck". A mid-level manager would walk the guests through the kitchen operation through a friendly chat.

EMP embodies a style of epicurean elegance with every detail intertwining together with perfection: from an organized kitchen and front staff team to even a well charred shallot on the plate that makes a dining experience so fine.

I ate here last night. 

The dishes were incredible.  I'm not going to pour into a detailed review because there are countless other ones here.

This is what I will say.


If you are viewing this site, you are mostly likely either curious about visiting 11 Madison Park or you are browsing the reviews being unproductive at your office :). 

If you are actually interested in going, just do yourself a favor.  Go.  Make a reservation.  

IMO, the best restaurant in NYC on this day, May 12, 2012.  Now this is NYC, that will change soon, but on this particular day, for me, these guys gave my girl and I a meal that she said she would never forget.  


Bon Apetit'

Really excellent service and food. Each course/extra little appetizer thing was delicious. There was nothing I didn;t want to eat throughout the meal. The servers were great as well, I was dining alone and the waitress brought me some of the magazines they had published which i thought was nice to do. Only critiques:

The lobster and the ribeye were cooked a bit too long. Both were toughish, but not bad by any stretch of imagination. 

The first appetizer things came a bit too fast, one right after the other. 

I wasn't crazy about the chocolate dessert. In theory it is very imaginative and beautiful, but I didn't think it tasted great. The combination of lavender and chocolate wasn't executed well.

Very nice atmosphere overall even at the check in area and waiting area. Few things I would like to make comments are:
1. Food - wonderful and decent portion. It take pretty long time to wait for one dish and other. 
2. Services - You actual won't figure who will be your server because there are so many of them are serving you at the same time which I don't really like it that much about it.
3. Price - it is a fancy but pricy place. 
4. Special event - I spent my birthday there and guess what? I got my own birthday menu! I felt special with this kind of special arrangement. :)

Food: marvelous
Service :  marvelous
Atmosphere: 4

They did a little kitchen tour and offered a lovely drink

Probably my favorite restaurant after Per Se. The service was excellent (as expected from a 3 star restaurant) and the food was also very creative. 

I'm from Toronto, and was only visiting NYC for the weekend. I had to wake up extra early on a Saturday morning to make this reservation. Now that I think back, it was all worth it! 

We opted for the four course dinner because we wanted to leave space for the burger outside in Madison square park. I think next time I'll definitely go for the tasting menu because I saw some pretty interesting plates being brought out to the other tables. 

At the end of our meal, they took us back to the kitchen as well. It was definitely a fun experience!

there isn't much left to say about how awesome this place is. the bottle of cognac left for us at the end was a very nice finishing touch. 

compared to daniel and le bernardin, this was more cutting edge and much more creative. the service was also on a level high above the other two. 

you'd be an effing buffoon to live here and not try this place.

Visit #3.  See the blog for the lengthy review.  Highlight dishes below:

"Cauliflower" with Tabbouli Salad, Olives and Orange would arrive and almost immediately the tone was set for the rest of the meal...in short, what Daniel Humm is doing with vegetables right now must be experienced.  Served as a sort of cous-cous at the center of the plate with the cauliflower literally broken down to individual grains and subsequently topped with grated orange, dehydrated and crushed olives, plus a veritable cooked wheat 'snow' each bite of the dish presented us with something new - at times brine, at times citrus, and finally an herbal note added by parsley cream at the center of the pile; truly an inspired dish.

Finding it hard to believe that I'd been so enthralled by cauliflower my expectations raised by about five notches when I saw the next course was my favorite food - "Foie Gras."  Admittedly expected given the fact that we were each asked if we would prefer a hot or cold preparation when we ordered the tasting the first version served to the lady of the table was hot, a seared lobe from Hudson Valley Farms measuring approximately 2-3oz in size and paired with Granny Smith apples, oat streusel, sorrel, melted leek puree, and sweet foie gras jus.  A beautiful preparation, caramelized on the exterior and creamy within, this dish again shined in its vegetal aspects as the mild sour of the apples proved a perfect foil to the savory leeks and sorrel while the oats added texture.

Moving next to the terrine, I must say that my first thought was one of envy; to put it lightly, the terrine was tiny, particularly when compared to the seared liver to my left.  Moving on, however, with my gluttony acknowledged the terrine was also excellent, not only in its own ethereal texture but more so in what it did for its plate mates.  Beginning first with the most abundant flavor, winter black truffles, the plate featured these in a shredded form first and then in both a foie gras vinaigrette and a purple Peruvian potato puree - the essence perfuming the palate with each bit and carried admirably by the unctuous liver.  Again showing a deft hand with vegetables and textures, additional rounds of the sweet potatoes were added along with locally foraged greens and finally a rye crisp adding a slight bitterness well matched by the vinaigrette.

Next, "Sunchoke" was specifically requested by my dining partners.  Already a fan of the vegetable but rarely seeing it 'featured' outside of soups I was curious to see what the praise was about and when it was not until I took a bite that I truly understood - this was not just a dish made with a sunchoke, but rather an homage to it and featuring it in no less than six forms including sous vided, dehydrated, pureed, roasted, and fried accented by notes of lemon, watercress, horseradish, and pickled mustard seeds.  Likely a dish that I would have never ordered, particularly given my general distaste for the later two ingredients, this is simply a plate that needs to be experienced to be appreciated and much like the cauliflower a dish that showed me the kitchen thinking on a different wavelength than prior.

With course four a protein would finally be presented in the form of "Lobster," and much like the foie terrine the portion was petit while the impact was profound.  Described at length this bold and decidedly dark dish featured the aforementioned snappy, sweet, and butter poached but mostly obscured from vision on arrival instead choosing to focus the diner's gaze on a background of army green and ink black - the results of charred leeks, burnt bay leaves, scallions cooked in squid ink, and black garlic shellfish bisque.  Beautiful, intense, and equal parts cream and crunch with just a hint of Meyer Lemon acting as acid meld the flavors this was my favorite course of the meal, and one of the best of the trip as well.

Finally, "Beef" would arrive.  Described as rare roasted 55-day dry-aged ribeye prepared simply with cracked black pepper and sea salt the beef itself was supple and tender with just a touch of funk - good, but honestly a bit more fatty and tough than I'd have expected based on prior experience.  Moving next to the accoutrements, an composition of wood sorrel puree, pickled white beach mushrooms, baby marbled potatoes, and 'Bordelaise' beef jus infused with marrow - it probably goes without saying at this point that they were exemplary.

Rarely one to revisit restaurants it says a lot about my feelings for a place when I do so, let alone more than once, and in the case of Eleven Madison Park it speaks of trust - a restaurant I trusted on my first visit, a restaurant I sent one of my best friends to on her honeymoon, and a restaurant I recommend unequivocally to anyone who asks.  In a world where some restaurants come and go before you ever knew they existed and other restaurants never seem to change Eleven Madison Park does nothing but evolve.
Amazing. Best dining experience I have ever had. Simply incredible. Impeccable.

My recent lunch at Eleven Madison Park was probably the best fine dining meal that I've experienced thus far.  The presentation, execution and concept behind all the dishes I tried were all well thought out and showcased what a restaurant of its caliber should produce.

Lunch options included the the four course for $74 or a full tasting for $125.  We opted for the four course, while pricey for lunch there are enough extras given to actually make it worthwhile.  The menu is laid out in a 4x4 matrix with each row representing a course.  There are four choices in each row that denote the main ingredient for the dish.  Your server then inquires about your likes, dislikes, allergies and any preferred preparation methods which they will convey to the kitchen.  The seemingly unconventional ordering style is a welcome departure from the norm that will appeal to both veterans and newbies to the fine dining scene.  It's a novel concept that brings about a little suspense and forces you to strip away any preconceived notions of how a dish may look, taste or feel.  It requires you to place your unwavering trust in the chef's talents with only a smidgen of knowledge about your meal before you commit.  Think if it as fine dining meets Japanese Omakase.   

Extra's such as an amuse bouche or bite sized samples from the chef throughout the course of the meal are often the norm in a fine dining restaurant.  At some restaurants the gifts you receive often feel forced, as if they threw something out there because the customer expects it.  But at Eleven Madison Park, the complementary dishes from the chef are an integral part of the meal and serve to enhance the dining experience and quite frankly brings it to a whole new level.  The meal started off with a series of amuse bouches: a savory black and white cookie, apple thyme tea, sunny side up quail egg on a cracker and egg custard with raw sturgeon.  Each served to whet your appetite for the main dishes to come.  

The heart of the meal was just as amazing.  The warm Foie Gras wasn't seared and served piping hot as I normally like it, but it was still a great perpetration.  My second course was snapper that was perfectly cooked and paired well with the accompanying blood orange sauce.  If this particular dish was described on the menu, I would probably not have ordered it thinking the pairing of the two would not have worked, but it came out to be an outstanding dish.  Their unique menu style worked out for me in this case as it showcased ingredients that I would have normally shied away from.  The roasted rib eye was a perfect medium rare, seasoned well and tender.  The dessert I chose that was a melody of different types of chocolate based sweets and ice cream in a dazzling presentation on the plate.  

At the end of the meal there were again treats brought out from the kitchen, an egg cream soda, cheese cake inspired dessert and another box of black and white cookies as we departed.  This time the black and white cookie was sweet instead of savory bringing the meal to full circle.  All in all, a fabulous meal.  

Eleven Madison Park is absolutely deserving of their 3 Michelin stars and 4 stars from the NY Times.  I have a whole bucket list of restaurants to try in NYC and generally refrain from revisiting a restaurant that is so expensive when there are still similar establishments left on my list: but I EMP will be the exception.  I need to come back and try the full dinner experience the next time I'm in town.  Yes, I was that impressed.

As most everyone says, WOW. I echo the rest of the reviewers when I say that this place is incredible. I think what makes it truly unique is the balance it strikes in demonstrating grandeur and class while remaining remarkably down to earth. That goes for the decor, food, and service. 

Decor - It's set in a former bank. Ceilings are enormously high. Yet, the zigzags on the lights and the unassuming images on the wooden paneling create a less formal air. 
Food - Expertly composed dishes, with heavy use of crunch texture, are presented with an earthy spirit (especially the lobster with charcoaled bay leaves meant to resemble dirt)
Service - They are at once nice, friendly, and professional. They let my fiance and I have our conversations, not approaching the table too often. Yet, when we appeared to have a question (yogurt lollipops came in a jar of raw lentil seeds, and we were unsure whether to dip them into the seeds or not) or another issue (it took us a moment to figure out how to best swap dishes to taste each others food) they were very quick to come over and offer assistance. 

The maitre d' was very friendly and we instantly felt like he was our friend. 
My only criticism was that when we were asked if we needed a car at the end of the night and said yes, we were escorted to a MB S550 and driven to Penn Station. We were led to believe that this was a complimentary service that the restaurant offered, but learned later that it was actually a $25 experience. Just left a little bit of a sour taste in our mouths, after we dropped almost $500 on dinner. They could have comp'd the 5 min. car ride.

OMG where do I even begin! 

EMP is definitely a restaurant that you need to experience for yourself. I had heard about it from a friend, and did some research. And what I discovered amazed me. And so I picked this place to celebrate my birthday. When we arrived, the maitre d greeted us with a big smile and wished me a happy birthday. There was also a birthday card waiting for me on the table written in beautiful calligraphy. I was impressed. 

I had read the reviews beforehand, and knew that the 4 course tasting menu would be enough, seeing as they give you many amuse bouches in between. And they were right. We probably had 6 different ones (4 savory, 2 sweet) on top of the four courses, making it a total of 10! I was extremely full by the time we were done. I chose the hamachi, lobster, beef and chocolate. Our server asked us for our preferences and dislikes/allergies, and also asked if I preferred a dark chocolate or milk chocolate for my chocolate course. I picked the latter.

Everything that came out was so beautifully presented and creative, and I really had my mind blown. The only other 3 michelin rated restaurant I had been to previously in NYC was Le Bernardin, and I was not as impressed with that. 

The whole experience was almost 3 hours long - but it definitely didn't FEEL long. Everyone made sure we felt welcome, and was very helpful in explaining the ingredients on the plate. 

I would definitely love to go to EMP again when I'm back in the city :)

Seriously one of the best meals of my life. I can't decide if I like this or Momofuku more. I liked this better than the French Laundry (but then, I prefer innovative / surprising food over traditional french). This blows Daniel away (and I liked Daniel a lot and would go back). Since it's spring now the presentation was absolutely gorgeous with little flowers and bright colors.

The hamachi was nice. If I go back (and I hope I'm so lucky) I would try something else, it was really good but didn't wow me.

The lobster paired with beer was amazing. I'm not a huge lobster or beer lover, but they were perfect together.

The beef was amazing. Yes, a small portion, but absolutely amazing. I am a huge beef lover and this beef could have made me cry. I tasted my friend's pork cheeks (I love pork, and cheeks) and was so happy I had gotten beef.

The dark chocolate dessert was "the best dessert I've ever had" (that could have been the wine talking). As others have said its very dark, more like 80%+ than 70% but so perfect with the ice cream and the chocolate crumbles.

As everyone else has said, the amuse bouche put the meal over the top. The amuse even came with a pairing of hard cider, one of the best I've had. The service was amazing. Perfect fine dining service, but with an enthusiasm that made it impossible to be stuffy.

Yes, as good as it gets.

First, the place is just wonderful. Really Manhattan looking restaurant, dramatic decor, I loved it.
The service is beyond what you can imagine, they almost know who you are before you tell them the name on the reservation. Daniel, the chef walked by all the tables and chatted with us. Only grey spot is our waiter was just 'normal' nice in contrast with everybody else being ridiculously nice.
I though the foie gras was excellent, but really star for me was the lobster (barely cooked, sous vide, with amazing crunches to go with it), then the morels. I actually did not like the chocolate desert.... my gf had the milk desert, equally disappointing.

One thing you need to know is that Daniel, the chef is really into the crunches... so every single plate has a crunch to it, it could be a chips, some fried little things... it's always there. Pretty cool too.

I went here for my anniversary a couple weeks ago and we had the most lovely and delicious experience.  They really take the time to figure out what kind of experience you are looking for and even catered to my tedious gluten allergy.  The whole thing was very personalized, down to the welcome cards hand calligraphed at our table waiting for us upon being seated.  We had the four course meal, excellent, which included canapes between courses and extra sweets and goodies to take home at the end of our meal.  The service was attentive, but not stiff...I got such a warm feeling the entire time.  I can't think of another restaurant of this caliber that manages to make one feel so attended to and relaxed at the same time.  Quite a feat, in my opinion.  And at $140(?) per person for the four course meal It's an incredible value. Just make sure to call at 9am on the dot 28 days before you plan to go.  It fills up instantly.  I think you can also eat at the bar off the a la carte menu, maybe without reserving?

You need to go to Eleven Madison Park for the experience. We went here in the middle of April for a lesbian bachelorette party for my friend Kim, who is getting married in August. I thought it would be fun to go to NYC for a long weekend and since I am not an actual lesbian, I asked her what she would like to do on this trip.She said she wanted to go to a fancy dinner and so Eleven Madison Park seemed like it would fit the bill. 
 First of all, you need to reserve 28 days , TO THE DAY, in advance,which I did and all i managed to score was a 10:15pm reservation. I was a little aggravated about it but my best friend Rich, who lived in Manhattan, was elated as I like to be hanging out with the senior citizens at 530 and 6pm normally. So everyone seemed fine with the idea of a late night dinner,which turned out to be a blessing in disguise. Kim, who is a lightweight at drinking, and thats an overstatement, did shots at the Cubbyhole and at the Ritz the night before, and promptly blacked out. I barely remember the evening, but apparently a hot dog vendor had to pull me back out of the street to stop me from getting ran over. Who says NYC isn't welcoming to the masses? Thank you hot dog guy! The next day, I was a little shaky like Katherine Hepburn (the later years) but I was functioning.Kim ,however, remained retired in place on the sofa. She was throwing up from 6am until after we got to 11MP. (i know,who wants to read about that while looking for a place to eat. Sorry. But its relevant.) 
 We thought she wasn't going to make it but she rallied and we got in a cab and made it there around 10 after 10, where Rich was already waiting for us. We entered and were greeted by a host who was effusive in his pleasure of our company. The dining room is huge, formerly being a bank, but it was tasteful and low lit. I will also note that almost everyone here is dressed tot the hilt.I bought a suit that day and I felt like the most underdressed person there . We were seated and almost immediately the food started coming out.Our first amuse bouche was a quail egg on brioche,which i never had and normally wouldn't eat but ....why not? it was 125 a person, before gratuity and alcohol. It was pretty good for an egg. They also sent out some kind of tortilla chips  with little vegetables and garnishes on them. The waiter who told us what they were did so in a low but rushed delivery. We all just shrugged and just ate them anyway. We also had a chickpea fritter that the whole table liked. I should stop and say that you get a menu with 16 hand drawn illustrations of food items and you get to pick 4 of them , one from each row. I chose cauliflower, whey, beef, and milk. Most of the table picked the cauliflower as well, which came with couscous. I have to say, I've never liked couscous or cauliflower but it was delicious.One of the best things i ate there. Next came some whey in a tortelloni with micro-greens and violets.The most beautiful and delicious dish I've ever had. I wouldn't say it is a dish I yearn for but it was surprising and beautifully composed and actually delicious.I made everyone at the table try it and they all really enjoyed it. I got some filet mignon with some type of gastrique.The steak was pretty good and I ate it. The milk dessert , which was a rice milk ice cream with some kind of crumble,was the biggest disappointment but with that said,it was good, it just wasn't as mind blowing as the cauliflower or the whey. Smitty picked out some wine, which was good.I wasn't going to drink since i was so hung over, but i relented since Kim couldn't drink and Rich was drinking white wine (no thanks). 
 The service had a weird lull that I've experienced in NYC before.Its overly attentive and then its not attentive at all and then its a struggle to get us out of there. Our waiter and the rest of the wait staff was very nice but we had about 12 different people coming to our table throughout our 4 hour "food journey". Id prefer to have one waiter to establish a rapport with, but that doesn't really seem to be the style of fine dining these days. I will say that the whole staff took note of Kim's being under the weather, and constantly brought out things to soothe her stomach and encourage her appetite. They even brought us coconut water,which i think someone had to run out and buy, and brought it to the table in a glass for her. Now that was what made up for the lull half way through service. After she drank it, she immediately got her 17th wind and began to enjoy the rest of our dinner instead of looking like she was white knuckling just sitting in her seat. Before dessert, they come out with this cart and make egg creams table side while they regale you with a history of the building and the area of NYC where they are located. While i can't say it is my favorite meal ever, I will say that Im going back in June with Jovanie so he can also have the 11 Madison Park experience.

I have to say this may have been the best 2.5 hour 15 course lunch I have had....have I had many? Has anyone?

It was my first visit to NYC and this seemed like a good place to start. All but 1 dish was fantastic. The duck was outstanding and a taste I will remember for a loooong time - if it's on the menu order it, if it's not, ask about it!! The rolls & goat butter were sublime!

I went into a serious food coma (I'm blaming the duck course) and seriously felt like I might explode like Fatman in Monty Python. I think my server noticed the glazed look on my face and took some time to bring out the final courses...thank jesus....

I absolutely loved EMP and would come back in a heartbeat.  

Side note - I was dining solo and never felt awkward. There were about 3 to 4 other solo diners so any of you folks out there weary about dining alone here, fret not.

A quintessential New York experience that is not be to missed and never to be forgotten.

My friends and I were able to procure a 5:30 pm reservation on a weeknight.  At first I thought it would be too early to eat dinner, but now knowing that the meal lasts for 3+ hours, the early seating was perfect.

We each decided to try the four course option.  After discussing the preparation of certain dishes, I decided on the hamachi, lobster, beef and chocolate options.  I don't have many food aversions or allergies so with my E-ticket in hand, I was ready for an adventure.

The meal started off with their savory, truffled black and white cookies.  It came in a box with a description of its place in New York history.  That was followed by several amuse bouche - soft cooked egg on a cracker, smoked apple tea with rosemary (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg), scallop, mackerel, Greek yogurt lollipops with lentils (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#6bzcrQmaQpY2reXC9OVxTg) and chick pea "fries".   The dinner rolls had croissant-like flakiness on the outside and were so very light and tender on the inside (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#qTlY1ozJhK1OR6JaI94ieQ).  They came with one butter made from goat's milk (this was so good) and another made from cow's milk.   If the meal ended right there with additional servings of those rolls, I would have been very happy indeed.

The hamachi was served sashimi-style, accompanied by ingredients that allowed the freshness and sweetness of the fish to shine through (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#hDuT_u7aK61nNIwQgid1nA).  The lobster dish was good, but I enjoyed my friend's cobia just a bit more (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#yqTQzSSZ1-XN-G28T7BYKg).  The fish was similar to texture and taste to a white salmon.  The beef dish consisted of rib eye steak with the tiniest mushrooms and potatoes I've ever been served (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#1LZLIcIqvFd2SvaMKDTZ9g).  The sauces were divine and elevated the primary ingredients of this dish.  

For a bit of an intermission, we were served the classic New York egg cream, but with hints of orange in this version.  Next came a their version of a New York cheesecake, with the "cheesecake" in the form of frozen bits courtesy of molecular gastronomy techniques.  The chocolate dessert arrived next - dark chocolate tarts with salted caramel and chocolate ice creams (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#qJ6s4vml-0_1eX72wMyXZA).  I typically prefer lighter, fruity desserts but this dish has made me a fan!  

Just as we were lamenting that our wonderful meal was coming to an end, our server offered to provide us with a tour of their kitchen.  I.WAS.STUNNED.  I'm still stunned!  For someone with a great appreciation of all things culinary, an opportunity to take a peek behind the scenes of one of the top restaurants in the world was an experience I just never imagined I would have.  They prepared a sorbet and apple brandy-based cocktail for us (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#MfdcjoJ-iz_F4Ug6sPKqIA) (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#bJ6XHxGsO8-UyJwao-nbfQ), while providing us with some history/background of the restaurant, philosophy, approach, etc. and patiently answered all of our questions (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#CcJI_DGihLN2y883OlCr0w).  We were then led to the lounge where we were invited to sit and enjoy some of their Cognac  (aged 15 years) for as long as we wished.  Yes, it was very smooth and we certainly enjoyed every sip (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=3Qe1nthp1CjiFpBCK4DWpg#hXFYw1EGQ-KL7TvwfUTEFA).  They also brought us another box of their black and white cookies, this time of the sweet variety.  These are one of my favorite cookies, so for me it was the perfect touch.

I would advise for first time visitors to not be shy and get to know their servers.  They encourage conversation and mentioned that we were selected for the kitchen tour upon learning of our interest in food and wine.  Service was excellent and completely exceeded my expectations. The staff is friendly, but professional, and not the least bit stuffy or snooty.   On my visit men wore jackets and the women wore suits or dresses. 

Upon my return (and there WILL be a return visit!), their duck will be something I will definitely order.  

To the team at Eleven Madison Park, thank you.

This was definitely a dining experience. The hubby and I have been trying to get reservations for about 3 months and finally succeed with a 5: 30 pm reservation this past Saturday night. In most circles a 5:30 pm reservation would be considered the 'early bird special.' Alas there were no discounts given for our early dinner.

The service was over the top friendly. The maitre d greeted us like we were old friends (the hubby said the person who called to confirm the reservation was the same way). We were escorted to our table and were doted on by the staff.

The wine steward was especially helpful when we were selecting our wine. The wine he suggested was amazing. The waiter took the time and explained how and what to order. We had:

Chilled Foie Gras 
Chilled Hamachi
Lobster
Cobia
Pork
Beef
Chocolate dessert
Epoisses dessert (disappointment - melted epoisses with potatoes and onions )

We also had several hors' devours: Curried yogurt lolly pops, assorted raw fish, an apple wood smoked tea (unbelievably good), savory truffle black and white cookie, dessert black and white cookie. All were yummy.

The epoisses was the lowlight of the evening, it had a slight ammoniated flavor and I thought they would have been a bit more creative with it - melting it over onions and potatoes isn't overly creative. The desserts in generally weren't 'out of the park' great but the other food was amazing. They also give you a complementary bottle of cognac to drink (at the table) after dessert. Unfortunately we are not cognac drinkers.

They also had sugar cubes instead of packets - to us - always a sign of a fine restaurant.

What we also found a bit disappointing was that it took us a long time to get a reservation because they are always booked solid, but there were several empty tables from when we arrived at 5:30 pm (when they first opened) until we left at 7:30 pm. That just doesn't make any sense to me.

Overall it was a great night out.

This review is just for the bar: 

I can't wait to eat at Eleven Madison Park, so much so that I decided to just get drinks and dessert there one night while waiting for my own reservation the next week. 

The drinks are truly spectacular and despite the name of mine ("sippy cup"--truly a bit patronizing, but delicious as it sits you down and tells you who is boss), I loved every sip. My friend had a ginger-bourbon mix that they made especially for him. I must say, amazing. 

The only disappointment here was the decor. I felt rather uncomfortable in this hotel lobby looking space. For a place with such amazing food and drinks, it was neither formal nor cozy, edgy nor classic. The artwork was thoroughly distasteful. Maybe because they don't want the walls to overpower the plates.... I will discover soon.

12:25pm in Hoboken, Thursday. I have only twenty minutes to get to my 12:45 lunch reservation. I can't believe I can't find ONE parking space. Getting stressed..honking horn..move! Ok..relax..focus..be nice to yourself..you deserve this. I turn my car towards the PATH train entrance and miraculously find a space available just footsteps away. The rub? Only a two hour limit..otherwise a $45 ticket and possibly a booting fine as well. Ugh! I don't care! I drop the quarters in the meter at 12:33 and I run down to the departing train and barely make it..or so I thought. The train ultimately sat there for another annoying ten minutes before exiting the station at 12:43. On the ride into Manhattan, I'm pondering the idea of how to enjoy Chef Daniel Humm's 3-Michelin Star lunch in just about one hour. I leave the 23rd Street PATH station and sprint across town, thru Madison Square Park finally arriving at Eleven Madison Park (EMP). I walk inside, out of breath. The maître d'restaurant welcomes me with a calming effect. I check in. "Of course..Your table is ready. We knew you would come.", the hostess ads with a smile. The dining room at EMP during the daytime is an imposing and cavernous, palatial space akin to the Hoboken Terminal Waiting Room. If you dared to raise your voice level high enough as EMP's ceilings, you would hear your echo distinctly. I was seated in a large and comfortable banquet and welcomed by Floor Captain, Kevin Browne, a veteran at EMP for the last six years. With his keen senses, he could see that I had experienced a bit of an ordeal en route to the restaurant. His instincts led him to ask me if I was on a time frame for lunch. I told him the whole story as quickly and concisely as possible and finished with, "Well, the meter expires at 2:33. It was 1:10. His eyes propped wide open and he replied, "That's a VERY aggressive time frame for a four course tasting menu." I told him that it was MY concern, not his, and not to stress the kitchen out by rushing. And I really didn't WANT to rush. I wanted to enjoy my lunch. Kevin responded confidently with, "We'll make it happen." I was impressed and skeptical at the same time. "We'll see.", I thought. Ok. I needed a drink at this point.
