I was happily surprised that the cocktails were reasonably priced at $15. This lunch was a tribute to closure and renewal, closure of a lost love and the embracing of a new one. When emotional closure is not given to you by the one who left you, one needs to find one's own closure. That is what this meal was about. One drink on the list reminded me of her..The Prairie Smash. When I saw the world "Prairie" I remember the fun trips to Iowa to visit her parents and how she wanted me so much to move there with her. After tossing down my decent Quail Egg canapé, a heavenly Sea Urchin Cappuccino amuse, and sipping my refreshing cocktail of Bourbon, Drambuie, Root Liqueur, Lemon and Mint, I reminisced about how I could have done things better or how she could have been less rigid and impetuous. Perusing the matrix-style menu, I chose the Foie Gras for my first course. It was a rebellious and spiteful move knowing that she would have reacted with that resentful look over my order and how cruel she believed the foie process was. At EMP, the foie comes innovatively cured and rolled on a bed of Buckwheat with a Jus of Buttermilk and Lemon. For my second course, I selected the Lobster. This dish was an eye opening disappointment. The lobster was poached in a Meyer Lemon and Seafood Bisque but with the egregious mistake of a Burnt Leek and Charred Brioche Crouton that left such a horrid black-ember aftertaste so overpowering, it reminded me of the bitterness I felt about my unrequited lover. Kevin could see I was not enamored with my dish and, to his credit, offered to replace it with the Cobia, but, for whatever reason, I declined. While waiting for my next course, I noticed a young woman dining along the adjacent wall..alone like myself. I wondered what she was thinking about. She had an air of disappointment and jadedness about her. Then I bit into the incredible house made biscuits with accompanying butter selections and snapped out of my pensive state. Then, the Rabbit arrived. Served in roulade style with Endive, Saffron and Pear Marbles, I found the rabbit slightly salty. And why do chefs today feel the need to arrange their dishes on one side of the plate? Alas, Kevin brought a much needed smile to my face with EMPs signature Egg Cream made tableside with Malted Milk Syrup and Vanilla Beans, Battenkill Cream, Milk and Seltzer. This may have been one of the best palate cleansers I've ever had. A dessert amuse of a decomposed NY style cheesecake with Goat Cheese, Blood Orange and Vanilla was an unexpected treat. I found the Chamomile Sorbet with Coconut, Jalapeno and Lime an exceptional finish to an up-and-down series of courses. I got back to my car at 2:43..ten minutes late, but no ticket. Thank you Kevin. Goodbye JoAnn.

I went hear a little while ago and it was incredible. Expensive but worth every penny. The food was perfect. The staff was incredible, attentive, and knowledgeable. We went for my girlfriends birthday and they had a hand written note from the manager waiting at the table wishing her a happy birthday when we sat down. The sommelier is world class, he picked the perfect bottle in our price range, based on only a few questions.
Dining here is something you wont forget anytime soon. Cant wait to go back.

My wife and I went for lunch for our anniversery.  We are not from NYC and were visiting for a "getaway" weekend.  We have never been to a 3 michelen star restaurant and we were really blown away.  The service was amazing.  The staff was pleasant, helpful, and not intrusive.  We really enjoyed the unique menu.  My wife and I ordered all different items and each one (all four courses each) was done really well. I ordered the hamachi, lobster, rabbit, and cheese (the only mediocre dish).  My wife ordered the cauliflower, chicken and pear. The presentations were beautiful, the falvoring was unique and delicious for each course (exception -- my cheese dish was quite mediocre -- melted cheese over potatoes).  the chef also sent out 4-5 amuse bouche (tiny appetizers) including sunny side up quail egg, sturgeon soup served in a top opened egg shell, and home-made goat cheese cake.  Every single thing we ate was delicious and had unique flavors.  We had a wonderful time (and the lunch pricing was very reasonable for this caliber restaurant) and would definately come back.  It is by far the best restaurant experience we have ever had!

I went there for an anniversary and I was happily pleased with amazing service, food and other pleasantries. It was an evening to remember - since i called in advance and request a quiet corner they were great enough to comply - not only did i find a corner table but a card from the staff on the table wishing us a happy anniversary. The staff was so pleasant the food was perfect the flavours were perfectly combined and everything was done just right / that did a lot of play on food - which was fun - we were so lucky and got a kitchen tour.. it was amazing and I couldn't be happier!  Will surely visit again!

Extraordinary start, strong middle... disappointing finish, but still, Eleven Madison Park remains one of the most memorable meals I've had in a long time. The service here is quite simply second to none. The ambiance is extremely pleasant, warm, and intimate. And of course, the food is divine. We ordered the four-course menu.. and were given at least three rounds of amazing amuse-bouches before the first dish even appeared. Less than inspiring at ordinary restaurants, the amuse-bouches at EMP were on the contrary almost the highlight of the meal for me. So many incredible flavors and interesting textures! The restaurant seems to be making a push for classic New York foods, so the evening started off with savory black-and-white cookies, infused with truffle oil. From there, we had flavors ranging from apple miso to scallop with jalapeno, each small portion tastier than the last. And then, of course, the most insane bread and butter (both goat and cow milk) were served. Naturally, we had seconds of that... of the main courses, there was not one that truly blew me away like the salmon course at Le Bernardin, but taken together, they were all well-prepared and impressive. Interestingly, Daniel Humm (head chef, duh.. well, I had to Google him to confirm that it was in fact him) visited our table not once but TWICE over the course of the meal to chat. He did not seem rushed and genuinely wanted to enhance our experience, which he did! Finally.. the big disappointment of the night was the sweet black-and-white cookie served to end the meal. I don't even like black-and-white cookies to begin with... so I wasn't too crazy about this little gimmick. But EMP's black-and-white cookie was even worse than one you'd get at the corner bodega. Why did they serve it? I don't know. Also, the caramel popcorn bite preceding the cookie was similarly unimpressive... but the free glass of cognac (and the fact that they left the whole bottle on the table to pour more!) certainly was! All in all, a very memorable evening given the quality of the food (despite a few misses), the ambience, the service, and my lovely date (my mom).

L and I had lunch at EMP earlier this year. We were considering ordering the tasting menu but opted for the four course at the last minute. 
The atmosphere is very laid back for a fine dining restaurant. It took almost 3 hours for lunch and we were so full before our desserts arrived. The dishes were too rich for us and L usually eats heavy foods. 
The four course + amuse bouches = generous amount of food for lunch. There's no way I could have survived the tasting menu. The four course priced at $74 for lunch is a great value. 
I can't say it's the best dining experience nor the best meal I've had, but it was certainly one of my most interesting ones. I wouldn't mind returning to taste the duck which looks fantastic!
love it!definitely one of my favorite restaurants in town: 5 stars on everything from service to food, to ambiance. thank you!

Went on a lunch this past Monday.  Alarmingly easy to score a reservation on OpenTable for lunch; very difficult for dinner.  Last hurrah before leaving town.  Inside is elegant with high ceilings.  Staff looks happy to see you and don't appear stiff.  Lunchtime options are 4 course for $74 or tasting menu for $125.  Would have tried tasting menu but waiter said that this is a 3-4 hour commitment.  Didn't have that time so stuck with the 4 course option.  

Menu is laid out in a 4 x 4 grid.  Each of the 4 horizontal rows has 4 primary ingredient options.  Each row is a course.  I chose foie gras, lobster, rabbit, and milk.  Other ingredients include hamachi, beef, chicken, vacherin, chamomile, cabbage, etc.  Had to wikipedia some of the ingredients.  In other words, the choices are varied enough.  Maybe the chef likes to play his own game of "Chopped" where you choose the ingredient and he whips up his own fancy dish.  It's a leap of faith that you only get to choose the ingredient and not the entree but it works for me.  Don't be fooled; despite only one ingredient selection per course, there are plenty of other things going on with each presentation.  Each entree is far from uniform with a multitude of flavors and textures.

Several little treats/amuse bouches intermixed with the entrees.  The bread is croissant-ish and flaky and addictive.  They'll give you more if you ask; we didn't ask but were offered and we accepted with drool.  

All total, we were there about 1.5 hrs and we are fast, down-to-business eaters.  Sure, we chit chatted some too but we can do that the other 22.5 hrs of the day.  Hungry enough soon after that I had to eat some pizza in a couple hours so if you have time and $$$, go for the tasting menu.  But then again, this was supposed to be lunch so maybe the amount was right for the time of day.

A very fine dining experience, would definitely go back.  Place is dressy but if you dress down a little, I don't think they would wag their finger at you as long as you still look tasteful in your appearance.  But then again, don't be an idiot about it and wear cargo shorts and a wife-beater just to be rebellious.  Just my opinion, not necessarily EMP's.  Sorry, didn't mean to veer off on a tangent.  Have a good time and treat it as a special experience; it's a really nice place.  And don't be afraid to take photos because everyone else was.

I really enjoyed it! I would say 4.5 but deservedly rounded to 5 experience.
Staff 5 stars
All the extras were amazing except the cookie before the meal( I even liked the yogurt lollipop even though most my party did not) it was different and amazing. 4.75

Octopus was so good ok maybe not as good as marea's but still really good. 4.75

Lobster was great too, I liked the souse even though again a guy in my group did not. 4.75

I didn't care much for rabbit, I found it a bit salty however I am starting to think I just don't care for rabbit period since I keep trying it but don't like it much:  3

I tried my friend chicken and I LOVED it ...5

Chocolate thing, 4.75

Wine paring 4.75

This place is awesome. The duck was easily the best duck I have ever had. The service was impeccable. 

The seating is a little awkward but that isn't too big of a deal.

I especially loved how they started and ended the dinner with a representative cookie.

On my trip to New York last November, I visited Eleven Madison Park for dinner in the bar area.  Several courses there were very good, and with high praise from Michelin and diners I trust, getting to experience the full menu was a top priority for this trip.   We arrived to a dining room with only a few other seated guests, but were in no way let down by the room's grandeur; large windows, a spacious table, and deep red roses as decor created great presence.

Our head waiter stopped by with a few questions: "any allergies?" (1 gluten in our table of 4).  "Any foods you don't like?" (no).  "Any time constraints?" (no).  "Great.  You're in for a treat tonight; I'll fill you in when I come back."  He hopped away, giving the sommelier a chance to pour us each a glass of Champagne.  The waiter returned a few minutes later to describe the situation: 

"Tonight is a special night.  Chef Christopher Kostow, of Meadowood in Napa, is working with us tonight.  He was formerly Daniel Humm's sous chef, and tonight they're collaborating on a special tasting menu.  As Chef Kostow has also earned 3 Michelin stars at Meadowood, we are cheekily calling this a 'six star Saturday'.  Would everyone like to participate in the full collaboration tasting menu tonight?"  
The four of us nodded in unison.  We were elated--if it weren't for the formality of the space, we might have been high-fiving and cheering our good fortune.  Given the murder's row week of meals this night fell into, my friend gave me a "is this real?" look.  Six star Saturday.  Fantastic.

Sadly, the high promise didn't deliver.  Overall, the food was mediocre.  Very middling--attempting to delivery something great, but repeatedly falling short.

The 15 course meal took 5 hours and just a few dishes could be acknowledged as great or exceptional.  Our group re-hashed and discussed, attempting to make sense of the situation.  The collaboration must have caused kitchen issues, forcing slow service.  Also, many of the folks I have heard praise Eleven Madison Park opted for the 4 course menu or went for lunch; if those meals only incorporated the best dishes we were served, the food could come off as outstanding.  But as it were, we experienced many poor plates & frustrating service.  Not the room's presence, the free drinks, nor the inventiveness of a few good dishes could uplift us from severe disappointment.

Not enough space to put my full writeup, but blog is here: fillc.blogspot.com

Sadly as I hate to say, this restaurant failed on many levels.  From the greeter at the front door - to the servers not knowing anything about the liquor selection and shoving a wine list on us, to the PRESENTATION of the food and even more saddening, the flavor of or lack of flavor in the dishes.  As many, after dining at Daniel, Le Bernardine and Per Se, we had high expectations and EMP fail short on everything that they had been praised about....  I was truly expecting this 3 star Michelin restaurant to really "wow" me.

So we arrived there a few minutes early (for a change!) and were greeted by a great smile and our coats were ushered away by the hostess! So far so good! We were kindly escorted to our nicely primmed table and courteously handed the wine and cocktail lists. We ordered a few drinks (which were extremely delicious!) and proceeded to choose from our menus. We opted for the 4 course menu. The staff was exceptionally attentive and responsive, without being intrusive. They were all professionals in their fields. After a few rounds of hors d'oeuvres, our food started to come out. We had a vegan dine with us and the chef showed remakable talent in accomodating for him. The master sommelier was very helpful in making the correct pairings with our food. After an intermission (which we needed to wake our legs up! ), we resumed feasting! Our table ordered everything and I can surely say that most of my food was quite amazing. The only hiccups I encountered were the mini lobster croquettes did not have enough lobster AND felt that the scallops were being over-powered by the subtle flavor of the apples that they were paired with. But the chowder's presentation and taste was impeccable! (I wish was having some right now) We ordered the duck, which was carved table. The skin was crispy with herbs and full of crunch and the meat was juicy with tons of flavor! The desert was sort of a miss to me because I guess I was expecting something a bit more, but was quite enjoyable nonetheless. I would definitely go back and hopefully soon! Tips: Be ready to spend HOURS of eating enjoyment!

I haven't yet felt the need to leave separate ratings for each part of the meal, but this one was so hit and miss and extraordinarily expensive. 

It is a beautiful and relaxing dining room. The staff is beyond professional. Both perfect and deserve 5 stars. 

The sturgeon sabayon is one of the most delicious things I have ever had in my life, as is the orange egg cream and goat cheese cheesecake. I loved the strong apple tea! 5 stars.

As for what I ordered. I had the cauliflower appetizer. It was okay... The lobster was amazing but I didn't care for the black croutons. The beef dish contained just one strip of beef, was not palatable, and I didn't have any desire to finish it. I do not consider it a main course serving. 2 stars.

I had the chocolate dessert and it was lovely. 4 stars.

Enjoyed the beer. The water glass was always full but it becomes a bit of an interruption.

Someone is going to have to put a stop to the cell phones and picture taking!!! This is getting ridiculous and has to stop. Can't anyone just enjoy the experience? The 3 tables surrounding ours had fiendish picture-takers and cell phone conversations. The staff has a responsibility to make sure everyone can enjoy their meal.  0 stars.
Hands down the best restaurant in New York.  The food is out of this world, the service is an amazing dance that is beautiful to behold, and the wine pairings are the best I've ever had.

Solid 5 stars to Eleven Madison! I've been in NYC for 2 years and this is what I have been imagining in terms of NYC fine dining. It was amazing from start to finish. 

Heads up, when you enter the maître will be literally right in front of you. Our table was great and very spacious; the service was amazing and never missed a beat. The bread was something between a parker house roll and a croissant...both the goat butter and regular cow's butter were very yummy.

As many yelpers have commented, you are indeed served a lot of amuses. First we had the savory black and white cookies (a sophisticated version of a cheese and truffle cracker sandwich) followed by two quail egg crostini, then apple-thyme tea, then surgeon-green garlic foam/soup served in an egg shell. All amazing but the surgeon was my favorite. 

For appetizers, I had the hamachi and the lobster. The hamachi was very fresh and the pepper greens were a wonderful fresh accompaniment. My boyfriend had the cold preparation of foie and also the lobster. The lobster was cooked well but the black croutons were somewhat strange,  


For entrees i had the rabbit---the texture was amazing and the rabbit rillette was very well seasoned. It was served with endive which added a good bitter element. My boyfriend had the beef which was aged---very tender with nice flavor. 

Finally it was time for dessert. First we had the egg cream. it was so much fun and tasted just like a Grand Marnier candy. Then we had a reinterpretation of a NYC cheesecake made with goat's milk. The topping tasted just like dipping dots! Then we had our main dessert. I had the chamomile and my boyfriend had the chocolate. He made the mistake of telling them he liked dark and very rich chocolate desserts when he really wanted a mousse. He couldn't finish his dessert but mine was well balanced. Finally they served us sweet black and white cookies with jam in the middle and a peanut butter-chocolate cookie. 

It was the most expensive lunch of my life! BUT it was totally worth it and I would go again in a heartbeat. Amazing! Next time I will request to see the kitchen. Service was amazing! Food was awesome, I haven't been to Per Se but Eleven Madison Park is easily the best of the best.

This is by far my favorite restaurant in all of NYC.  I only went here for a summer lunch, so I can't speak to the atmosphere during dinner, but lunch was enough to impress me.   First off, the decor in the restaurant is beautiful - so white and clean, and the wait staff is so great - they answered every question we had about the meal and were thorough in explaining what each dish was.  We started off with these cheese puffs, which were to die for...For the main course, we each chose our ingredients - I chose foie gras, lobster, and two others, and the dish was so unique, I can't even begin to describe it.  The other part of the meal I remember well was the homemade milkshakes (made right in front of you in cute little shot glasses) and the earl gray macaroons, which were some the BEST macaroons I've ever had -- aside from Laduree..)

Overall -- loved it!  Definitely worth the price and will be coming back here again for special occasions (since it is a hefty price to pay, even for awesome food and service).

This review is mostly going to reflect on things other than the food, which was exquisite, brilliantly creative and delicious.  Oh, and as some future diners will no doubt be aware, there is an atypical menu at Eleven Madison Park where you are asked to select one food item from four choices for each of your four courses.  This allows the chef to inject a great degree of surprise, which my dining companions and I relished.  It was very different from our typical dining experiences.

Apart from the food, the most notable thing was the service.  Upon entering the restaurant you are immediately greeted and asked for the name under which you made the reservation.  There are no computers or a bevy of hostesses milling about looking slightly perplexed as they try to find your reservation.  There is also a plethora of waitstaff about the restaurant, and as my gf noted, someone was always around to help you back into your chair.  I was surprised that our waitress was not always present when serving the courses but the staff was quite knowledgeable about each dish being served, and did an excellent job explaining to us the ingredients.  Water glasses never went empty, utensils were cleared after each course, and everything was done with a smile, a good attitude and in some cases a sense of humor. As my gf also remarked, she liked that the staff was lively and not stoic or stuffy...the atmosphere was relaxed.

Other thoughts...I want to make a quick comment about the dress code here, as I did not get a great sense of what would be acceptable.  I wore dress pants and a button down shirt.  I would say that there was a handful of other patrons wearing like attire but the majority were wearing jackets, if not suits and ties.  I did spy one individual wearing a sport coat and nice jeans, but he was sitting at a table in the bar area.  I do not know if that was a reflection on his decision to wear jeans, but I am guessing not.  I certainly was not treated any different from my jacket wearing compatriots. As a side note, I hate wearing a sports coat/jacket when I eat, if you share that same affliction then don't worry about showing up in just a dress shirt and slacks.  Oh, no sneakers.

Be prepared for a three hour meal. 

Also, the ladies in my dinner party were quite taken with the jar of granola parting gift. It was a nice little touch at the end.  Hey! How about something for the gents too?

I just went back this past week for a business dinner and was soo soo pleased. I had been wanting to go back since I haven't been for years and what a great opportunity. We had a private room and a fixed menu, but the food was delicious.

Started with a lobster amuse, squash app, amberjack fish (was amaazing, and ended with chocolate torte.

The service and wine were spot on, and the business dinner wasn't half bad either ;).

I will be back for another evening with friends to enjoy the delicious menu.

One of the best restaurant in New York!
The food is delicious and the atmosphere is wonderfull,the service is excelente and very attentive, we enjoyed it!!! Highly recommend this place to anyone!

It was a special night, last October when we visited Eleven Madison Park. Little did we know that on THAT DAY they had been awarded three stars and the places had an atmosphere that made me think 'there is nowhere else in the world I'd rather be right now' - you know those moments. The four course meal began with 7 flights of appertisers. My two favourite were the goat's cheese lollypop and the tomato tea. The lollypop made me giggle and confused me, in all the right ways. I know a restaurant is good when I'm giddy with novelty and of course not forgetting the exceptional taste.

Each of the four courses was exceptional, the dessert was a little heavy on dark chocolate for my taste but this would be very picky.

I loved the bread, the oatmeal gift on the way home, the dancing chef, the top quality service, I loved it all...

EMP tonight for dinner. Gracious thanks to Chris Camarda for the invite! But is that the best that we can do? 3-star Michelin? Food nothing memorable, water and wines not poured when needed, very long gaps between courses. The highlight of the evening was the clam chowder served with the clambake hors d'oeuvres; a vibrant, flavorful, briny essence of the sea, but the lone highlight of a four-course, 4.5 hour meal! Very, very disappointing. I remember 3-star Michelin meals in Reims and the Mosel and even a 1-star meal in Madrid that would totally embarrass tonight's experience.  Have standards been dumbed down to where this is the ultimate in dining?

I came back to Eleven Madison Park for lunch with Michael K.  This is one high end restaurant worth a repeat visit - the experience was splendid, and there wasn't a bite of overlap.  Two negative changes from my first lunch that didn't detract from the overall experience - the price went up to an astounding $74 for the four course lunch, and there was no lucky invite to the kitchen.  Oh well.  The service and setting were again immaculate.  The food - well, observe.

The meal started with a savory black and white cookie in a white ribboned cardboard box, establishing an occasional theme of New York classics.  The cookie was made with black truffle, goat milk butter, couched in a crumbly shortbread built with parmesan.  It yielded a nice dose of salt and funk, and a lot of rich tongue-coating flavor.  This was followed by a smoked apple tea served with a round of toasted brioche topped with applewood smoked bacon and a sunny side up quail egg.  The lovely bite of brioche was a cute version of a tea sandwich, and I loved that tea.  It was intensely flavorful, warming and savory, with apple and cinnamon and a bouquet of herbs.  Our last amuse bouche was an egg shell filled with sturgeon egg, chive oil, and smoked diced sturgeon in a sturgeon sabayon.  This was gorgeous, the smooth sabayon shimmering against the small chew of smoked fish and burst of caviar.  Bread service was also noteworthy - buttery rolls made with Cayuga flour from upstate New York, cow's milk butter with oat, and goat's milk butter with dill, and fleur de sel.

Then came our first course.  A lush salt-sprinkled foie gras terrine came surrounded by a gardenscape of purple potato, papery rye, and black trufle sauce.  It was luxurious stuff, creamy and cold, the unctuous flavor enhanced and grounded by the earthy accompaniments.  One of my favorite dishes of the meal was the charred octopus, served with a crumble of salty, dehydrated chorizo, a medley of pickled and charred onions, and a bright, piercing lemon sauce.  The octopus was perfectly firm, and it got along well with the salty, smokey chorizo.

Course two brought another favorite - the lobster, knuckle and claw poached with meyer lemon beurre blanc, served with charred leek, leek purée, charred bay leaf with dehydrated squid ink, and a black seafood bisque made with squid ink, black garlic, and seafood broth.  The lobster was meaty and full of flavor, and the black bisque spilled with velvet brine.  The sunchoke was also impressive, without a lick of meat.  The root was cooked a couple ways, braised and roasted, with horseradish, watercress, and mustard seed.  The centerpiece was the roasted cake of sunchoke, which resembled a latke with its softened texture and toothy crust.

For our entrée course, we ordered the Muscovy duck for two.  We had to order this in advance, and it was delicious.  The disadvantage is that everything at EMP is delicious, and you do forgo all four options for course three on the daily menu.  Nonetheless, if you like duck, go for it.  This was a whole little duck, dry aged, roasted, and glazed, flavored with lavender honey, cumin, coriander, lavender, and Sichuan peppercorn.  A server showed us the whole duck before it was carved, and then brought it back in pieces.  The bulk of the meat was in beautiful pink slices with the thick crispy skin clinging on, served with persimmon, fennel purée, fennel wings, and citrus duck jus.  The legs came confit with a potato mousseline and a flavorful gravy - the most decadent mashed potatoes I've ever had.

A couple intermezzos brought us more New York classics.  I loved the airy egg cream, prepared tableside with orange syrup, whole milk infused with cacao nibs, and a touch of orange oil, all frothed with a Brooklyn seltzer.  New York style cheesecake came crustless in a glass with vanilla and blood orange sorbet and gelée.

For our last course, we had cheese and dessert.  First, the triple creme three ways - straight, and encased in pumpkin seed, then apple leaves with apple cider, all served with apple dijon, pickled mustard seed, pumpkin seeds, and cubed pumpkin.  The cheese was fantastic, creamy with a light funk, and the different preparations were a delight to explore.  The poached pear was another excellent treat, plated with pear sorbet, burnt maple cream, and a gingerbread crumble.  The pear came in a few different forms, poached soft, and sliced, and balled into crunchy garnishes.  The maple was lovely, and the dish had an overarching taste of ginger that went well with the pear.  As a final gift, we had another black and white cookie, this time sweet, with chocolate, vanilla, and a lemon glaze.  Simple and comforting.

I planned poorly for this lunch, wearing a nice dress that was tight when I put it on in the morning.  Our Eleven Madison Park feast left me in great danger of ripping a seam.  It was worth the discomfort and the cool $97.  I'll do it again if I get the chance.

Had an 8:30 PM reservation for dinner today. After some disappointing cocktails, we chose the 4 course menu along with what turned out to be some very good wines. The first two courses met expectations, and the second two fell very short. Same was true with the hors d'oeuvres, it was hit and miss all night. For $800 we expected a grand slam and got a double instead. Service, ambiance and presentation were excellent, but we were there for the food foremost. Overall, the food was not what we are typically accustomed to at a Michelin star rated establishment.

The best lunch I have ever had.

I've eaten at a number of Michelin-starred restaurants (and a few 3-starred places), and 11MP delivers with the best of them. I won't go through each dish in detail because the dishes will likely have changed between the time you read this and the time you eat there. But here are the basics:

We brought a bottle of wine with us (very reasonable corkage fee of $35 per 750mL bottle) and enjoyed a couple of glasses of champagne to begin. Next up was a parade of amuse bouches. Perhaps the best of the excellent dishes was an egg shell filled with a sturgeon bisque over chive oil.

We chose the 4-course lunch prix-fixe menu. The menu itself is something I don't recall seeing elsewhere. Unlike the typical prix-fixe experience, 11MP has you choose the main ingredient of each course, and the preparation is up to the kitchen. It gives you some control (unlike the typical prix-fixe menu) and some surprise. I began with octopus, and my girlfriend had the hamachi. The octopus was poached, and the hamachi was served crudo style. Next up was lobster for me and sunchoke for her. The lobster was probably the best dish of the day. It was just perfect. The sunchoke was also quite good, but it could not keep up with the lobster. For our entrees, I had rabbit, and she had beef. The rabbit was prepared three ways (bacon-wrapped, braised, and what I would call the rabbit equivalent of tuna salad), and each was outstanding. Her beef was very good. It was essentially a slice of what I think was NY strip. Very very well done (in execution, not temperature!), and the sauce with tiny (but tasty) mushrooms capped it off nicely. There were a couple of transition dishes to the dessert. The most interesting was a modern take on a classic NY soda concoction from the 20's, which was prepared tableside. The desserts fell flat a bit. I ordered chocolate, and she ordered milk. The chocolate dish was a mound of crunchy, semi-sweet chocolate towering over a layer of creme. It was good but not great. Anywhere else, it would have been more than adequate, but when the rest of the meal is executed so perfectly, I was expecting more.

The waitstaff was as good as it gets. Very friendly, very attentive (when attention is needed), and they seemed to float around the dining room as if choreographed. And speaking of the dining room, it is a gem, stunning in every respect. The towering windows draw in the scenic Madison Park across the street (which is thematically recreated in the art on the walls), the soaring ceiling is finished in meticulous detail, and the plants and flowers nicely finish off the room. 

The bottom line is that 11MP served perhaps the best lunch of my life. While dessert was only good, everything else was remarkable. 5 stars for Eleven Madison Park.

sometimes it can be difficult to keep michelin style dining fresh and interesting.  or maybe it means you're spending too much on food.  anyway, having a four course three star lunch here was delicious.  the concept here is to show you a menu with the main ingredient or protein only, and then tweak the dish if you have any likes/dislikes, (though the dishes are in fact already ready).  great way to make you feel like you are getting what you want.  service excellent and decor very nice.
meal started with black and white -- made with parmesan and black truffle as a savory cookie (play on black and white cookie) -- smart and good
then had a quail egg brioche with a wafer thin apple wood smoked bacon -- so tasty
next had a smoked sturgeon sabayon inside of a cut off egg -- classic touch
*cauliflower: tabbouleh salad with olives and orange -- looks like a mound of ground up food with tiny flecks of olive but tasted strongly of cauliflower and had a parsley espuma inside the mound
*lobster: poached with burnt leeks, bay leaf, and meyer lemon -- so yummy given the meyer lemon butter used to poach the lobster, black garlic and charred leak really gave an interesting look to the plate
*rabbit: roasted roulade with endive, saffron, and pear -- loin with bacon wrap and tapioca saffron mustard seed jus and candied pears was a different take
*pear: poached with gingerbread crumble and maple cream -- 
best part before dessert was the egg cream using orange sprizter and chocolate infused milk with a dollop of orange syrup
*hamachi: marinated with peppercress and horseradish -- crudo served with pumpernickel bits, and solid way to start
*snapper: poached with bonito, seaweed and winter citrus -- also some octopus and blood orange with grapefruit marmalade, multitude of flavors, light
*beef: roasted with wood sorrel and pickled mushroom -- super juicy, marbled so well, tasty with potato and didn't even need the bacon bits
*mont d'or: vacherin with marinated potatoes, mustard seed, and pearl onion -- very smelly cheese, so not for everyone
also another dessert was the take on nyc cheesecake, so delicious
finally ended with the real black and white mini cookie to go.
beef and lobster dishes were great.  see photos.

fancy meets comfortable. delicious meets crazy. when the meal runs you $400 it can be challenging to leave feeling entirely satisfied, like you've really gotten your money's worth. EMP did all that and more.

Love the space. High ceilings, well spaced out tables (my table for 2 could easily seat 4) transports you away from the buzz of the city around you. A luxurious multi-course "complimentary" hors d'oeuvres makes you feel like this is something special. The evening starts off right.

The menu is avant garde. Pick a main ingredient and let the chef do the rest. Can't go wrong with foie gras, octopus, rabbit, steak. Dessert is innovative and delicious. Think you've tasted a new york egg cream? not the way they do it here.

if you are looking for a special restaurant for a special occasion then look no further.

The best meal (service and food) that I have ever experienced (and we've had some great ones, crossing things off our NYC bucket list before packing up and heading west). 

Decor/ambiance were wonderful. Tall ceilings, a good amount of space and big windows that filled the room with sun and light that reminded me of California.

Food was perfectly prepared and beautifully displayed, artistic and impressive without being snobby. Collectively, my husband and I ordered the cauliflower, octopus, plantain, sunchoke, chicken, rabbit, pear and chocolate. Everything was well seasoned and creative, the least impressive (though by no means terrible) was the rabbit. The variety of amuse bouches was wonderful, definitely kept us excited for whatever was coming next. Fantastic bread, too. For wine, my husband and I split a bottle of their (house) Onze 2007 Cabernet Sauvignon. It was the least expensive bottle on the menu by almost half, but knowing the caliber of the restaurant in certainly did not disappoint.

If possible, the service was even more remarkable than the food. Courteous, professional and conversational without being nosey. We had the pleasure of having Kevin as our server. After we mentioned that we were at lunch at Eleven Madison Park as we were working our way through our New York bucket list, he surprised us with some great samples of New York specialties as well as a list of other great New York restaurants to try before moving. Then to top it off, we were ushered from our table into the kitchen where one of the chefs whipped up a delicious cocktail, creating pomegranate sorbet by hand with liquid nitrogen right in front of us. We would have loved our meal and experience without this special touch, but that put it over the top. This was by far the most memorable meal I have ever had, and possibly ever will have.

Ambience and decor that made this one of my favorite places to lose a paycheck.
4 course dinner and 4 star service.
The table next to us taking pictures were frowned upon by the staff but handled so professionally (they offered to take pictures of them outside).
Pork was great!  Wine menu was adequate and not many recommedations to go with the particular meal but all was forgiven for taking away the parazzi wannabe's at the next table.

best lunch of my life without question. eight courses plus numerous extras, kitchen tour with a nitro cocktail, complimentary cognac at meals end, and some of the best service i have ever encountered. if you are really there for the food and not to just throw money around, let them know you are excited to be there and they will go above and beyond to make your meal as special as possible. also, go at lunch as the tasting menu is the same as dinner but priced much lower. pics in my blog.

In place of my dinner here, I could've bought the new iPad, or 2 round-trip tickets across the country. But to make some memories out of a special occasion, I wouldn't have traded the 3.5 hours for anything else worth $400. Fancy food may not be a birthday present you can put on the mantel of a fireplace, but company (and a camera) sure helps you remember the good times had with it.

We each got the $125 four-course menu, and he got a beer pairing with each course for $99 (which is overpriced but it's the principle of surprise that you're in for). 

I know they can give you a record of the dishes they serve, but I forgot to ask about it. Our petit fours included Parmesan and black truffle black and white cookies, apple tea with thyme [hot, strong, sweet] , sunny-side-up quail eggs, hamachi and scallop on savory crackers, Greek yogurt lollipops with lentils [ice-cold; I think they made this using liquid nitrogen], and chick pea fritters. For bread, we got the acclaimed soft and buttery croissant rolls, with cow and [awesome] goat butter. Near the end, we got egg cream (with orange chocolate syrup) prepared tableside, pomegranate sorbet with cheesecake, and traditional black and white cookies. To take home: a box of chocolates and a jar of granola (which is so good it converted me into a yogurt and granola fan; word is that because of the demand, Daniel Humm is going to sell this stuff on the market).

For the mains, the foie gras with black truffle and purple potatoes (they offer it served hot, but that idea seemed foreign to me) was perfectly prepared. The snapper was complemented well by the blood oranges on the side. The lobster tail with fennel puree and burnt leeks was decent. The honey lavender glazed duck served with fennel puree and persimmons was originally not on the menu, which is why I lit up when our waitress offered it; it's carved at your table and garnished with the use of tweezers: this is as crazy good as everyone says it is. The carcass is wheeled back to the kitchen, where they make duck confit out of its remains. The confit is delicious, served in buttery potato puree. The milk dessert was not impressive. The pear dessert killed.

We were at a table in the back and center, sitting side-by-side. It might sound gag-worthy, but it allowed us to watch the staff performing their art (it really is; everyone is happy to work there), and made it easier for them to serve us our food. We could also talk to each other without raising our voices. I appreciated that Humm himself came by to check in on us (but he didn't introduce himself as the man, so I didn't know it was him until the next table he visited kept him interestingly hostage). I enjoyed the amount of attention EMP pays to accommodate our interests; it's almost like an American-style omakase, in which they take your preferences to heart (just don't be an ungrateful douche about it). 

Making the reservation 28 days in advance was a dicey process; some people use two phone lines and Opentable, but I just used the phone because Opentable crashed at 9am, haha. Luckily I got a 7:30pm on a Friday night. Waiting a month to dine there definitely builds anticipation and hype, but EMP has become a favorite restaurant. I want another reason to come again.

Right across the street from the Madison Square Park, the restaurant is located on the ground floor of MetLife Tower, a grand old lady that is a historic NY landmark. Stepping through the revolving doors, we could see that the restaurant itself is housed in a truly grand room. Soaring ceilings, marbled walls, high windows, gold-hued lighting soaking the whole restaurant like a delicate mist, all work together to evoke the turn of the century feel that the building itself speaks of. 

We were seated quickly, all five of us eager for a good dinner. 

The drinks were just superb. Between the five of us, we ordered quite a slew of drinks off a very impressive and unique cocktail menu that definitely befits a Michelin three star establishment. My favorites were the Sippy-Cup and the Heart of Stone. I'd go back just for the drinks and apps at the bar every time I am back in NYC. Their cocktails are definitely among the tops I have had in NYC or anywhere for that matter, so far.

EMP I felt had too many people on the wait staff, moving around way too much, busying themselves right among the diners. They were very good definitely -- better be, considering that this is a Michelin three star deal -- but they could have made themselves less visible and distracting to their patrons. The kitchen staff, the apprentice chefs presumably, would come out with prepared dishes to serve to each and every table. Our own young chef brought out to show us the 55 days aged rib eye he was going to cook for us, as well as the different cheeses for the cheese course. Too bad I could hardly sometimes hear what he was saying or what the head waiter was describing for each course since the restaurant was a little on the loud side. On a surprising plus side, Chef Daniel Humm himself came out to our table and greeted us. Tall, affable, he was charming in that introverted Swiss way. He made us felt welcome.

We all had the tasting menu, which in retrospect might have been a pretty wasteful decision. The whole array of amuse-bouches was very good, especially their version of New England clam bake. It was very clever -- the clam chowder deconstructed was very much a delicious comfort food for a cold NY night. 

But the rest was just ho-hum for a Michelin three stars place in that nothing really stood out and jolted my senses. Maybe my expectations were too high, like they were with Per Se. Now that EMP is becoming more mainstream famous, I guess the chef is playing it safe with the tasting menu to accommodate the food tourists a la general public. There were the obligatory foie gras, caviar, and hamachi dishes, all average for a multi-starred restro. The only real proteins we were served were lobster and that 55 days aged rib eye. The cheese course was okay, if rather uninspired. The poached lobster was good, but I didn't get why the black miso was there in a carbonous state. The 55 days aged rib eye was indeed very good, the beef flavor I got from it was unlike any other. Even the beef fat had a foie gras like quality to it. 

The desserts were good, definitely above average, but again nothing spectacular. The Modern (even though owned by the same Danny Meyer empire) has its own pastry chef, and the desserts definitely evinced that fact, being wayyyy better. 

All in all, nothing really wowed me. They say the duck is THE must have item here, but I think our waiter said it has to be shared between at least four people. But since we opted for the tasting menu (unfortunately), we didn't get to try the duck. I did see the duck come out in a silver tray from the kitchen several times and it did look very mouth-watering. I also did read about the suckling pig, and the black sea bass etc., but they were not on the menu on our night. Bummer. We will go back one more time to try the four course menu, this time with the duck, and if lucky, the suckling pig. I don't know if the four-course prix-fixe comes with the little extra amenities like the delectable charming egg cream drinks that our head waiter prepared right in front of us, or the deconstructed NY cheesecake, or the bottle of (just OK) cognac at the end, but maybe you can ask for at least the egg cream drinks and let them charge whatever extra. 

I'd rate EMP as a 4 star out of 5. I think if Chef Humm didn't come out to woo us, it'd have been 3.5. Per Se was to me also a 3.5 to 4 star, the review for which I will try to write again after a second visit if there is to be one. The Modern out-rated both EMP and Per Se in my humble opinion. 

Biggest complaints? The wait staff being too visible and busy among diners. Above par, but just okay food for a Michelin three star, at least with respect to the tasting menu. 

Biggest wins? Drinks, the aged rib eye, seeing the chef mingling with bar patrons and customers.

Don't forget. Try the cocktails. Get the four-course prix-fixe if it is your first visit. And ask for the egg cream drinks if not given.

The service was impeccable and the room was comfortable and elegant but despite all the great reviews (everywhere) it fell a bit short.  

The amouse bouches were all very good.  I liked the cheesy poofs the best.

I wasn't crazy about the menu presentation.  It sets people up to be disappointed.  They give you what looks like a piece of paper with pictures (Scallop, Lobster, Chicken, Cabbage, Rabbit etc).  I was half expecting crayons to go with it.  The problem is you have to order by the MAIN ingredient only and leave the rest to them.  I'm fine with that but the dish has to be otherworldly in that case.  Well, in the end, it wasn't.

*Octopus with braised onions, chorizo and Lemon - Very good, excellent start.
* Scallop with marinated apple and celery.  The one real disappointment.  It was rather tasteless.
*Snapper - poached with Bonito, Seaweed and Winter Citrus - also very good, no complaints but no "Wow" either.
*Squab roasted with beets, onion and chocolate Jus - also very good but I'm still not getting overly impressed.
*Sorbet with cocoa pasty - good but by no means earth shattering.

Again, everything was very nice and the wine pairing was very worthwhile.  It was a terrific evening.  The bar for a drink is underrated before hand too.  In the end, there was just nothing there that I will say "remember when we ordered that_____at EMP".

(This is the experience from July 2011.  Don't worry.  This place is even hotter than it was around that time).  

This is another place, along with Del Posto, I would put 5 stars in no time.  Their food , service and ambience were exceptional, totally meeting the level of 4 star restaurant from NY Times.  We had 4 course dinner.  That time I had black bass appetizer, scallop, pork and pistacchio.  They were all exceptional but the black bass appetizer was so great (In fact, I really couldn't enjoy my entree and dessert because they had four pre-appetizers... yes! four!... and their bread was so tasty I kept devouring! Don't fall in that trap!)  This place surely is the hottest restaurant in the city right now, and you won't regret it.  It's worth every penny even if you end up paying more than 300 bucks (for two).

As I type this review, I can't help but feel a little pain in my heart. I don't know if my expectations for EMP were just too high...but I mean, it IS in the same category as Daniel, Le Bern, and my love Per Se. 

I know I shouldn't compare all these fancy-shmancy restaurants to each other, but when you are given such accolades, I feel the customer has a right to expect better...especially when you are paying so much money for the experience.

To say we were excited about finally dining at EMP is an understatement...after reading as many reviews as possible, looking at endless pictures on google, we were finally going to dine at EMP. 

The night started off strange enough, with the greeter immediately asking to take our coats...as in the second we got out of the revolving door, all I saw was his face. So we get to our table, and I must admit, it is a very beautiful restaurant. High ceiling, towering vases, and very open atmosphere. 

Our waitress was friendly, not very personable, not really attempting to start conversation. A few servers shined with smiles, but too few. We opted for the Chef's Tasting Menu...$195 per person versus the $125 for the four-course pri-fixe. So expectantly, by choosing the Tasting Menu, I felt that we were in for a real treat. The first few amuse bouche's came out, little bites here and there...some fish, some deep fried finger food...all good, not great, def not mind-blowing at all. We patiently waited for our real food...the actual tasting to begin..but more appetizers (and mind you, people around us who did NOT get the tasting were getting the EXACT same things...couldn't help but feel a little duped about paying for the tasting). 

The only different plates we did receive were a clam chowder pot, and some other strange bowl with cheese and caviar. NOTHING was memorable. The only real protein we received were lobster and a slice of beef.

I never thought I would leave not only disappointed, but actually hungry. I will admit that the dessert was great, yummy, tasty..but again nothing that would ever want me to come back. 

I guess the value here is the lunch pre-fixe... 20 something bucks for this food -- sure why not...that's a fantastic deal

I guess we would have found ourselves at the tables of EMP eventually, but I'm sad to say I would never go back to this restaurant again. I'll just check it off the list.

A must try in a city of Michelin Star restaurants.  Chef Daniel Humm wows with food that is fresh and creative.  The friendly service and unpretentious atmosphere only adds to the greatness of the experience.

"Where's the beef?" or better yet where's the meat? We both tried the chefs tasting, which could be classified as a tasting of hor d'oeuvres really.  Is it wrong to not love this food and not call it innovative and all that hoopla? Because I was very disappointed.  

Maybe when the server who seemed extremely robotic and forced asked me if we had any preferences in the beginning of the meal, I should have told her I had a preference for meat, and large portions of it, and not an array of food on a ritz crackers.  But since I did not mention my aversion to finger foods, I left extremely hungry 3 and a half hours after originally being seated.  

Of the 8 course menu, we received 2 dishes of meat.  One lobster dish "Pouched with Meyer Lemon, Burnt Leek and Shellfish Bisque" and a Beef dish "Roasted with Wood Sorrel and Marble Potatos" portions were a joke as mentioned earlier.  Okay it's a tasting, not meant to stuff you so full as to not enjoy the other courses, but this was ridiculous, my heart died a little when starving I saw them bring out the final course, my 55 day aged beef probably smaller than a pack of double mint gum.  

3 stars for the delicious desserts of cheesecake, chocolate, egg cream, and beautiful restaurant.  Service is not to par with other restaurants in eleven madisons category.  So inconsistent, too many servers running around like an assembly line with the diners serving as the product.  The saddest part was the friendly older couple next to us who were left unspoken to for 20 minutes when they arrived.  No one came by to explain the menu, offer cocktails, nothing, just unacceptable.  Most of the staff was impersonal, stiff, some even snooty, gaps between drink orders were ridiculous too.  Stick to the 4 course meal.  Do not order the chefs tasting, it will leave you hungry and very sad.

I had been before Daniel Humm was the chef.  I think i liked it better then--not because the food is bad not because anything was bad.  The concept now is a little different.  Dont get me wrong the food is well done, but i just wanted a perfect simply done piece of food and i got an over thought dinner.  It was so de-constructed that i really didn't know what i was eating sometimes.  Molecular gastronomy?  Not so much.  Killer filet of black sea bass, yes please!  I got the former and wanted the latter.

But from a techinical perspective its well thought out, well executed and everything you want when you are going to spend a ton of money to eat.  i notice some people compare EMP to LeBernardin, you cant...not sure why you do?

torn. i could have easily bumped my review down to 4 stars for my second visit. BUT, because this second visit was for my boyfriend's birthday AND because he absolutely LOVED it (said it was the best meal he's ever had in his life), then i have to give eleven madison park another 5 stars.

things always come full circle. including visits to awesome restaurants. a little less than a year ago, i was visiting nyc on spring break and i dined here with girlfriends for our splurge. now, i live and work in the city! and, for my boyfriend's birthday, i wanted to spoil him with an eleven madison park meal.

he was incredibly surprised and was impressed from the moment we arrived. 

the only reason i want to bump this review down to 4 stars is because the service wasn't as attentive as i remembered it to be my first time around. however, i think it mainly had to do with the fact that the first visit was lunch at noon - this time, we dined at 1:30 and the dining room was much more packed. clearly, it must be a bit more difficult for the staff to be as attentive as they may like. this was my only real complaint. not to mention that since i knew how everything worked, i could definitely be more critical of everyone and everything. again, however, i'm overlooking my critiques.

as expected, tons of amuse bouche - and this time around, i could hardly eat as much as i wanted! my boyfriend and i went for the duck as the third course and it was AMAZING. i wouldn't have known about its amazing-ness had it not been for other yelpers. so, thanks yelpers! the duck was my favorite of all the dishes. though, my first-course scallop was amazing. oh, and the bread rolls! we ordered seconds.i also loved the de-constructed strawberry cheesecake.

i requested we get a tour of the kitchen to celebrate the special occasion, and they politely followed through. we were served a complimentary cocktail and received little goodies! my boyfriend got some chocolates for his birthday, and i was given some scrumptious granola as a congratulations for moving to the city. 

we had a blast . . . even though we were bursting at the seams! it was definitely an incredible experience, and i am so glad i was able to treat my boyfriend to it.

if you live in the city or visit the city, EMP is a must.

**************************** UPDATE REVIEW ********************

       I came back here again after chef Daniel Humm earned the 3 Michelin stars, right on OCT 2011, Eleven Madison Park was impossible to make RSVP. I got luck out with someone canceled their reservation. I always love the entrance to this historical building, it's so grand, so elegant. Also the lobby, always stunning flowers, this time was beautiful orange roses, and yellow orchids, Fall colors for my BDAY, so welcoming!

      Everyone was polished in suite, made me feel as I was under dress, even  I was dolled up. The service was on point, the food was as good as chef Humm was here at Campton Place and the last time I visited when chef Humm earned EMP the first Michelin Star. 

- Poached lobster was delish as ever, big portion here.

- Skate sashimi, beautifully decorated plate, too beautiful for me to eat. It was so refreshing till the last bite. 

- Big Eye Tuna Tartare with Sorrel, Lemon & Taggiasca Olives - excellent dish.

- Seared Diver Scallop with Succotash, Watercress & Red Pepper Nage - 1 giant piece but the broth is tasty.

- Tagliolini with Alaskan King Crab, Black Pepper & Lemon - super creammy & plenty of crab meat to go around.

- Bouillabaisse of Striped Bass, Bouchot Mussels, Manila Clams & Chorizo - I love this dish, or anything stew this way. It was just perfect, the fish was nice, moiste & perfect cook, the Provençal herbs and spices in the broth are AMAZING!

        Highly suggest wine pairing, it's totally worth it. After all this is the ONLY additional 3 Michelin Stars in NYC! Rumor has it that he's taking over the resto from the famed restaurateur Danny Meyer, I'm sure the food will always be amazing as long as chef Daniel Humm is in the kitchen! Looking forward to coming back this Summer.

Overall: 5 stars
For value: 5 stars
For Food: 5 stars
For Service: 5 stars
For ambiance: 5 stars
Location: Beautiful historical Madison Square park

The Chef's Tasting Menu is the supreme dining experience.  The detail and preparation of each gem of a dish is exquisite, and considering the effort to make it, a "bargain" at the price.  The 17 courses are perfectly sized.  You are sated, not stuffed.  You will remember them in detail for a lifetime.  The pace is leisurely, which gives you time to have wonderful conversations with the wait staff and sommelier.  There are 80 staff for 80 diners.  For special occasions, this is the place!

I went here on a date on a Saturday night and looked around to find myself in company of rich old men with what appeared to be escorts as dates, which i am not and my dinner partner was around my same age, somewhere in our 30s.  We were by far the youngest diners.  The decor is ok.  We had the full tasting menu with wine pairings and, granted, we're not sommeliers, but while the wines and courses in themselves were quality, our palates never understood the pairings.  Time and again...and again we were tasting and sipping and like, i don't get it.  no dish was a stand-out to write home about.  the dessert was disappointing and left much to be desired.  The service was good, if slightly pretentious.  the tasting menu at Jack's Luxury Oyster Bar is a better option if you're looking to be blown away by art in your mouth.

Eleven Madison Park is a lovely restaurant, and I had a nice time there, but it is not the best option in New York at this price point. I expected this to be one of the best meals of my life, and it was good, but it was not THAT good. I mean, it's a great restaurant and deserves at least 4 stars, but this competition is fierce at this level.

Choosing only the main component of each dish is a fun little quirk, and it's nice to put everything into the chef's hands. It can lead you awry, though. I ordered cauliflower for one of my courses. I've never eaten much of it, and I figured I would go with something very out of my normal foody happy place. Where better to experiment? Sadly, it was just a very boring dish. Ok, fine, my fault for ordering cauliflower, but why was it on the menu in the first place?

The seared foie gras was truly delicious. Many of you won't order because of the poor, sad, ducks - yeah, yeah - but honestly, it's just that good. I chose the pear for dessert, and while I'm typically a chocolate girl it was a very good option.

Obviously the service is impeccable. I loved everyone we interacted with from the greeter at the door, to our waitress, to the chef from the kitchen who dropped off the amuse (which was mind blowingly good) to the downright hilarious somalier. 

Super fancy, BORDERline pretentious, a bit stiff, but a great restaurant

Didn't get to sit in the fancy restaurant because we had no reservations (although there were plenty of open spots.....) but my friend and I got to eat at the bar (fair amount of actually seating there).

They gave complimentary freshly baked bread with goat cheese and carrot cheese (oh my yummy).

Portions are pretentious but that's okay because I don't like to overindulge in food.
I got roasted guinea fowl with seckel pear, salsify, and shallots. It was a bit salty but overall, everything on the plate tasted yummy.
I believe my friend got the lamb. That was even smaller than my two pieces of meat.

For dessert, we got hazelnut meringue with chestnuts and pistachio ice cream. I'm not a meringue fan so I can't judge fairly. 

Presentation and atmosphere were both lovely.
I'd definitely love to come back with a date and reservations :)

During the last few days of my sister's visit to New York, we decided last minute to call and see if they had an opening available for 4 during lunch. To our surprise they did! Our lunch began at 12:30pm and ended around 4pm. It wasn't too busy the entire time we were there, so my guess is, if you are hoping to eat here last minute, lunch is the way to go. 

Overall really, really, really great. They even had a ''dish'' where they brought us to the kitchen and prepared it in front of us while we were able to watch the kitchen work. The incredibly strong edible cocktail that they made for us left me glowing red for the remainder of our meal...

My favorites were:
Chicken - Veloute with Parsley Oil, Liver Mousse and Brioche
Yogurt and Chickpeas - Lollipops with Curry; Panisse with Yogurt
Smoked Sturgeon - Sabayon with Chive Oil
Clam - Clambake with Chorizo, Apple, and Potato
Cheesecake - Cranberry and Lime Crumble
Bread and butter served on the side (BEST BUTTER EVERR)

Unfortunately, the worst dish was the one they specifically swapped out for me because of my request for chocolate in the dessert. The chocolate was incredibly hard and a little too bitter to be enjoyable. I ended up not finishing. 
Chocolate - Tart with Salted Caramel, Cocoa Nibs, and Chocolate Sorbet

Perhaps the best bang for your buck if you are wanting to try a 3 star rated Michelin, but do not want to dish out more than $200 in New York. Although their lunch states that their tasting menu is 8 courses, by the time we had finished. We had eaten over 14 different dishes not including the white and black truffle truffles they served with our check. 

According to our waitress, their menu changes seasonally which means I will definitely be back. My wallet hates me so much.

My girlfriend and I came here for a late birthday / early Valentine's Day dinner last night. If you're looking to come on a specific date, make sure to call the first moment you can a month ahead of time - just like every other hot spot in NYC, reservations fill up fast and furiously until you're either left with a late-night reservation or are just plain out of luck. We got a somewhat early reservation (6:15), but that was no issue, since the tasting menu is going to take at least a few hours to get through anyways...

You have two choices here: the four-course tasting menu (where you pick the main focus of each dish, and the chef constructs the plate around your preferences), or the eight-course tasting menu (where they pick the dishes, of which the main courses are centered around options on the main menu). We went with the latter, and it's safe to say that it's an eight-course menu if a) you count what has to be the longest amuse bouche I've ever as one course, and b) if you count the five(!) desserts as one course. It's not so much that the portions are huge, but that you end up sampling a lot more food that one would guess right off. The amuse bouche is probably 4 stars on its own - I wasn't particularly blown away by any of the dishes, although the borscht with caviar and the quail egg with bacon on toasted brioche were the highlights for me. Clam chowder was served in a kettle, but to me it was clear that clam juice or broth was used instead of full clams, which took away from it (despite the cool presentation). All in all, you probably end up sampling 8-10 items in the amuse bouche before hitting the main courses. Of those, all were delicious except for the puntarella, which was unfortunately not very memorable. The butter-poached lobster was delicious, particularly paired with squid ink sauce that just lit up the dish with flavor. The squab was very smoky and well-flavored, and the foie gras terrine was delicious as always (although the version at Ai Fiori is still a tough one to top). I also really liked the dinner rolls - milled with NY flour (they are big on NY-themed dishes here), they resemble croissants in how they fall apart quickly. They're served with fresh cow's milk and goat's milk butter that is utterly (pun almost intended) divine.

The dessert section was a bit extended, but it was great as well. The highlight had to be their interpretation of NY cheesecake - goat's cheese with vanilla snow and blood orange...so good, particularly with the lightness of the cheese and the bold flavor that the orange evoked. The triple creme was also delicious - probably the three most intense pieces of cheese I've eaten, given the high butterfat content, but it was great as well. The egg cream was good...it was my first experience of having this NY classic. The chocolate sorbet was delicious, while the last treat, a dark and white chocolate truffle - except these truffles literally had truffles in them. It was a unique way to finish the meal, pretty much in line with the rest of the meal.

This one will burn a hole in your wallet for sure, but it's definitely worth it for the experience of trying new dishes. The menu changes constantly, so you'll always be in for a surprise when you come here. Definitely one of the best restaurants I've been to, and the service was top-notch as well. I'll be back in the future...once my bank account recovers!

What can I say that 3 Michelin stars has not already said?  THIS PLACE IS GOLD, JERRY, GOLD I TELL YA!!!  I had the best lunch of my life there yesterday.   We had the four course tasting menu (which is really like 9 courses when you add in the innumerable amuse bouche courses).  Let me tell you folks, my bouche was HIGHLY AMUSED, HIGHLY AMUSED!!!  Somehow that sounds dirty.....anywho, you must get the duck as the main course.  Best duck I have ever had ANYWHERE.  I usually discard the skin with duck as it is to fatty. The seasoning on this skin was like some thing out of a dream.  I would have freebased this skin if I had a lighter.  If I were Buffalo Bill, I would be making a duck skin suit in my basement right now!  She's been rubbing a lot of lotion on this skin...NOW PUT THE LOTION IN THE BASKET!!!  Seriously though, It was ridiculously good.  I would gladly be morbidly obese to eat this skin every day if someone would agree to wheel me around and rub me down with WD-40 when I have to get through a doorway. As for the duck meat, it was cooked to perfection and carved table-side. It was incredibly succulent and juicy.  

The lobster was a great first course and be sure to go for the chocolate mouse dessert.  And please, did you really place an entire bottle of Champagne Cognac on my table and tell me to have as much as I like as part of the prix-fixe?  Talk about an epic end to an epic experience.  Thanks Chef Humm, you had me humming all day.

Did I say I liked the duck yet?

This was truly a dining experience that I will NEVER forget! From the moment we entered the dining room and throughout the 5 hours we enjoyed eating...everyone there made you feel like royalty! Eleven Madison is like a theatrical production! The presentation, the table side slicing of the duck, the table side making of the old fashion egg cream, the "special" lollipops that were palate cleansers, the sturgeon, the quail eggs...I can go on and on...this place delivers over the top service and food!
There is no menu....each dish is meticulously created for you. With the prix fix 4 course menu you will receive many little tastings in-between courses. The nice thing about all the food that is presented to you is that a cook from the kitchen runs the food out to you and explains exactly what you are about to eat and how it is prepared! Awesome!
Even though Eleven Madison has won so many awards this year it is unpretentious. 
Thank you to everyone at Eleven Madison Park for being a part of a very special birthday celebration!

Would honestly never return. I've been to many 3-star Michelin restaurants all over the world and never have I experienced such a pretentious restaurant! The food was good (worth 3 Michelin stars? Don't know about that.) and the kitchen staff was very nice as was the manager. But from the snooty, pretentious hostess to our outright rude waitress, our experience was totally ruined. Unfortunately, that's $500 I'll never get back. I'd rather spend double the money at Per Se and at least know I'm in for a great overall experience. So disappointing.

INCREDIBLE!

incredible food, incredible service, incredible space!

Simply one of the best restaurant experience I have had! The creativity and  taste is out of this world.  For what you get, the tasting menu is a bargain.

The courses kept coming!  Each was more impressive than the next.  What's really cool is that you get to mix and match your courses from their categories (veggies, seafood, meats, etc).  It's definitely worth trying.  

Oh yes, we also got a jar of granola to take home.  How cute!

This place is insanely ridiculous. 

3 Michelin stars, a bunch of James Beard awards, one of the best restaurants in the world. No joke. 

I was here a couple months ago celebrating with my fam. We came for lunch on a Tuesday.  I think we opened the place up arriving on the early side of noon.  

We all had the 4-course tasting menu, but it is much more than a four-course meal. 
This is one of those dining experiences you will always remember, or never forget, take your pick.  Each dish is a work of art, with the attention to detail and explosions of flavor you expect from one of the best restaurants in the world. 

The meal also was filled with many tasty surprises. In between each ordered dish, our servers (we had many) brought us small plates of delicious treats. Chef's choice, and they were all amazing. My favorite course was probably the lobster with wild mushrooms, paired it with the Gunderloch Riesling 07' a great bottle that we all enjoyed. Highly recommended. Other highlights included the goat's milk butter and my desert of all kinds of crazy chocolates.  

The service was also top notch, as to be expected. When my mom's guy-friend looked at the menu and declared to our server, "I can't eat anything on this menu, nothing sounds good." (And he was dead serious; I kid you not, as all of our jaws dropped to the floor.) Our server laughed it off and promptly asked what would satisfy him. Pasta and chicken was the answer and pasta and chicken was what he got.  Mind you, a normal meal for this guy usually includes tasty-cakes and hotdogs. 

Get here if you can, and plan ahead, getting a ressy can be tough.

Ate here last night as part of a retirement dinner.  Service was outstanding and the food was very good... but nothing really stood out in terms of flavor.  The presentation of the food was beautiful.  The dishes were interesting, and clearly used complex high end ingredients - but not sure that translated to superior flavor. Guessing ordering ala carte would be better.

Well... the food is excellent here. And you pay for it. You pay a lot for it. There are better places in NYC to get an excellent set menu that are far less stuffy. The service is questionable... they lost points with me when it took more than 45 minutes to get my second drinks, but they saved themselves by not charging for it. I'd say to go here if someone else is paying, but it is really not worth the money (unless money is no object).

The best cauliflower I have ever eaten. The kitchen folk sure work their craft with great ambition and perfection to highlight such a humble ingredient.
 This was possibly the best meal I have ever eaten, if you take away the way-too-many bites to begin with.
 These seem to go on for ever and ever. my father in law and I were starting to get worried that the entire meal will be like this. A chowder deconstructed is not a chowder. Daniel Humm, I am sorry but this course was a hodge podge of shit left over from family meal.
 But sure enough we received some amazing courses to follow. Foie, lobster, guinea hen and of course the cauliflower.
 Florets, purees and madras with raisins were transformed into a perfect harmony that I would request for my last meal on this planet.
It is worth noting that, Sophia commands the dining room floor like a conquistador and that our sommelier: Chase, suggested beer on two courses. Since I was the wine delegate for the table I found it some what alarming that Chase reccommended beer twice even though we made it very obvious we wanted to drink grape juice.
 Its hard to read people some times. I find it humorous that your beer list is a closer match to a new world sauvignon blanc than a french sauvignon blanc. Beer is bitter, has very little acidity and upon opening, a bunch of bubbles.
 With such a grand occasion as my parents 40th wedding anniversary, we would rather sip wine. Thanks for asking.

As of the time of this writing, Eleven Madison Park is ranked 24th in the world, holds two James Beard Awards, and recently received 3 Michelin stars.  It might be easy to think, with all the buzz, that this place must be trendy or overrated.  It is not.  If anything, it's still underrated.  I've only been to one of the top-20 global restaurants, and Eleven Madison Park was clearly superior.

The food is creative, artistic, original, incomparably and indescribably delicious, and prepared and served by the best team of people I've ever seen working in a restaurant.  It's hard for me to even imagine a better dining experience on any front.

Second time and I just got the best meal on my life. The food was delicious and adventurous. It was the complete opposite of my first meal in the restaurant. All the entrees and amuse bouche was amazing, except the dessert. The dessert wasn't on par with the other dishes. However, we were willing to overlook it as the meal itself was superb.

I'm definitely going back again. soon. But getting reservation is a hassle.

This is quite simply as good as it gets.

If there were a 5+ rating, this one of a very, very few restaurants that would earn it.

We went for lunch for our daughter's birthday and ordered the 12 course tasting menu ($125).  This is one of those exceedingly rare moments in dining when a $125 lunch will appear as a bargain.  A number of restaurants have high priced tasting menus, but none that we have ever visited came across with such an extraordinary selection of perfectly prepared courses served with a level of professionalism that every restaurant could learn from.  It is located in a great building as well (the old Met Life building), and the restaurant has a great feel to it.

Some of the courses had 2 - 4 distinct items to try, so you are able to sample about 25 different "dishes".  We dined for about four hours.

The wine pairing is $145 for the tasting menu.  We enjoy wine but are not connoisseurs, so we asked the sommelier to choose a couple of moderately priced glasses for us during the meal.  For a couple of courses he was nice enough to split a glass or serve a half glass so we can get a broader selection and better match the meal.  This was a perfect solution for us and very fairly priced.

It would be far too lengthy to go into each dish, but suffice to say that the variety included chicken liver mousse on brioche; frozen yogurt lollipops with curry; a miniature clam bake with fresh clams, chorizo, and lobster croquet ; cauliflower with roasted raisins, dehydrated grapes, and brown butter; and lobster served with burnt leeks (the ends burned to a charcoal powder). 

The desserts were equally interesting with an egg cream made with orange reduction; a sublime take on cheesecake with lime crumble, and of course your chocolate fix at the end only this time served with malt sorbet, olive oil and lemon.

As if things could not get better, they poor everyone a glass of cognac and leave the bottle when you are through.

As wonderful as the selections were, the diversity was secondary to the quality and pairing of ingredients, the interesting and highly skilled preparation, and the highest level of service.  

We were lucky enough to be given a tour of the kitchen after our meal, and it was as efficient and well organized as you could imagine.  A great finish.  We will certainly return.

If you are looking for a place to celebrate a special occasion, or just want a dining experience a cut above most anything else, I think you will thoroughly enjoy Eleven Madison.

amazing amazing service.
food and service was sooo perfect.

there is a serious reason why this place is so well known and has so many rave reviews. our hostess, sommelier, and the whole staff were the friendliest, funnest, and knowledgeable staff. 

food presentation was so whimsical and smart. i love that the menu only has the main ingredient and that is how you pick and the finished product is a surprise.

the ingredients i chose were the foie gras, the lobster, squab, and the quince.
all of these ingredients were prepared so well. each dish was phenomenal.

we also received many fabulous amuse bouches and extra sweet treats.
