my favorite extras were the white truffle white truffle. this is a small pretty white chocolate truffle filled with white truffle oil....delish! and the egg cream drink was superb and my first! and the cheesecake dessert was sooo perfectly delightful.

we did the wine pairing and everything chosen just enhanced each dish so well. 
ahhhh!!!! don't forget the sippy cup!!! it is a yummy cocktail that my bf felt funny taking sips out of because it is quite frilly but he couldn't help it...it was that good. lol

Yes, the food/service/ambiance is great.  You already know that.  Instead, I'd like to point out some memorable moments:

1) The couple dining in silence to our right who shot us DIE NOW glares when my date and I were asked if we'd like to go back and see the kitchen (and have the pop rocks/champagne dry ice nitrogen thing they make for you).

2) The goat's milk butter that I wanted to eat with my spoon.  My date conveniently preferred the cow's milk butter.  I have good choice in men.

3) Talking about The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills with our waitress.  She kept a straight face the entire time.  Skill.  She studied pre-med at Columbia too.  

4) Me deciding to take a literal shot of the cognac.  My date watching in amusement and not suggesting I sip it instead.  Me sputtering after said shot.  Date deciding that we should do a shot together for the hell of it.  Me sputtering again.  Date taking it like a man.

5)  THE FOOD NEVER STOPS COMING.  Food was brought to our a table a minimum of 12 times, and we only did the 4 course dinner too.  Every time I turned my head, another bite of something amazing and orgasmic arrived.  The worst part is since everything looks small, you don't realize how much you're eating until the sudden feeling of fullness hits you like a cab.  

6) The wine (Sancerre) my date ordered was amazing and according to him (who apparently enjoys the wine list here on the reg) the wine list is one of the best in the city.  

We were here from around 9:30 PM to 1:30 AM.  It was a fun experience.  The granola they give you is ridiculously good.  There are these little sweet, savory crunch bits in there that I couldn't place and still dream about to this day.

This was by far the best dining experience I've ever had, and I went for the $75 lunch.

While visiting NYC, I decided to try and compare Jean Georges and EMP. 
Conclusion: EMP wins. 
Why: Because they made me feel important and I like pretending I'm a celebrity sometimes.

But really, the experience and food was phenomenal. 

Ps. I appreciated the host and waiters treating me like I belonged there even though I pronounced foie gras "foys groys."

I can't wait until my next NYC trip, I will definitely be going for dinner this time. Even though I was stuffed after lunch, I didn't want the dishes to stop coming.

Let me start by saying interesting experience, but I wouldn't go back. I would rather go to other good but less expensive restaurants once a month than come here again once a year. It's that expensive. I was a bit disappointed since everyone seems to think this is the best place in NYC. Excellent, but the price and some aspects of my experience make this more like a 3.5, elevated by the granola to a 4.

Ambiance: Cavernous. Really odd choice for the room. Bar is the size of a subway car and just as crowded. Kind of strangely cheap and ugly in the bar, kind of stark in the dining room, like an abandoned art museum or something? A bank that Jay Gatsby would use? Everyone there is kind of like pretending they are the only ones there and are super awesome -- including us (table of 6); it was kind of infectious.

Food: about a third of what I ate absolutely blew me away. A third was excellent and a third was good but confusing. The sommelier did a beer tasting that was interesting and unusual but absurdly expensive  and didn't really go to my tastes. Worked with the food. No complaints on the wine and his service was excellent.

Service: There are dozens of captains, waiters, servers, runners, walking chefs, water waiters-- unending. Thing is, so much of what they brought us was unusual and the servers/chefs seemed miffed when I asked them the best way to eat it. Sorry, i don't eat foie gras daily. Very tight -- I'd like a looser, more fun experience.

Experience overall was stuffy, kind of boring and a bit too formal and perfect. Not for me but I can't argue with those who find it a 5 star either. If you have $1000 to spend on dinner, I would suggest spreading it around and having smaller, more fun experiences elsewhere then blowing it here.

Don't leave without the granola, it is absurdly good.

Look, I'm not going to write a book about this place, but it certainly deserves a review and I'll make it simple and brief.  
The reservations for a weekend dinner were hard to get, so get on the phone at 9am exactly 28 days before the weekend night you want to go.  Once at this beautiful restaurant, you'll find the most attentive staff ever and will indulge in one of the best meals of your life.  Choose one item from four different courses and let the chef surprise you.  It took us 3 1/2 hours to finish the meal and it was extraordinary!  Simply spectacular.  Enough said.

We took my parents here for their 40th anniversary last night.  I mentioned this when I made the reservation and was astonished at the level of acknowledgment they received while we were dining.  Not only did our servers wish them well, but a handwritten card was waiting for them at the table. Classy.

On to the food...we did the tasting menu and were blown away.  We have no dietary restrictions nor particular dislikes, so were happy to have them bring whatever the chef wanted.  Their take on a Long Island Clambake was particularly memorable, but everything was simply delicious.

The only downside was when my husband was searching for a bottle of white and explained to the sommelier that we enjoy a New Zealand Sav Blanc (which they don't carry), the sommelier informed us that the closest thing they had was a type of beer.  With a wine list that long, I would have hoped they would have something of a similar flavor profile that isn't a beer.  The other bottles of wine he suggested were spot on, however, and this was merely a minor blip in an otherwise perfect evening.

Truly a fantastic venue for a celebration.

Frankly, the best dining experience in NYC. If you have the tasting menu, please get ready for hours of wonderful service and delicious and tastefully presented food.  Their reputations is well-deserved. We also received several "service" offerings which were a pleasant surprise and much appreciated.

This place obviously doesn't need any more positive reviews, but I'm going to add my short one anyway.

I had an amazing birthday dinner here with my boyfriend.  I got addicted to those Orange Julius drinks and ordered 3 of them...maybe a little excessive, but it was my birthday, and I can't exactly afford to come here regularly.  My lobster dish with the orange foam and the duck for two were my favorites, but everything I ate was exceptional.  I'm pretty sure I spent the whole time smiling in between bites like a nerd in love.  We didn't tell our server we were there for any special occasion, but I guess our enthusiasm for the food was obvious enough to merit a tour of the kitchen.  I know they do this every night, but it still makes you feel special to get an extra little treat like this.

And the take-home granola  was insane.

I came here late last summer but delayed my review until now so that I could let my opinion settle some and see where EMP truly stacked up. After traveling a fair bit this last year both for work and fun, I did get a few chances to sit down for some incredibly memorable michelin meals around the globe. In retrospect, EMP was one of them. 

EMP is one of those places in NY you should try your best to reserve as a 'special occasion' spot - either for a birthday, meet the parents, anniversary, engagement, etc. Reason being is that first, it's pricey. Not gonna lie. (It's one of those min $250 per head kinda dinners) But if you can swallow the price tag, the two real major reasons to love this place is for the service, which is stellar, and the food, completely memorable. Both accolades I feel EMP genuinely deserved because the service was actually quite comparable to what I experience in Tokyo, which often never fails to be anything less than impeccable. And the food, thoughtful and well executed - just as you could expect from any michelin-star establishment in France, Tokyo, London or whichever food capital you're in.  

My favorite part of the whole experience was of course, the food we so enjoyed. At EMP, they offer their menu in the carte blanche style where you essentially select the main ingredient per each course but not told how it is prepared or what accompaniments would be included. For me, I love this method because the uncertainty gives diners & patrons the chance to be a little more curious and inquisitive about what they are going to experience. You could say, a heightened palette is where you'll start off whether you wanted to do that or not.

One dish I do recall absolutely loving was their pan-roasted duck. It was one of the few dishes that required the whole table to order it as one of the main courses, and no doubt, it was phenomenal. Highly recommend it if it's on your menu...
For other courses, they were all wonderfully presented and on par with what you could expect at a world-class establishment. 

The only thing that I can say I was not crazy about with EMP is their decor. While I love the architecture of the physical building, the exterior art deco detailing and all, I had hoped to come into a space that was slightly more warm. The high ceilings and open floor plan within EMP were a bit too bold/dramatic for me. But that is just my personal opinion. For others, the dramatic formality could be a perfect backdrop for some serious knee-dropping proposal action? Or a corporate NY black tie affair? I don't know, but that is just a style preference. 

Anyway, I nevertheless enjoyed the opulent experience here and would recommend it to whoever wants to experience the finest NY has to offer in an updated upscale Manhattan setting.

Best dining experience of my life in all aspects.

Food was indeed as good as it looked, the service was impeccable - nice and not stuffy at all, and the space was welcoming, classy and beautiful all at once.

If you had to make a choice between any of the top restaurants in New York, this is the winner by far.
One of those restaurants that I go when I want to reward myself and my companion (if a personal friend) or impress someone (if it is a business occasion).

"Firsts" are something that just about everyone holds dearly in their heart. Going to your first day of school. Hitting your first homerun. Getting your first kiss. Driving for the first time. All of these things can and often do leave a lasting impression on ourselves. In a similar vein, my first time dining at Eleven Madison Park (which also happened to be the first time I was dining at a three-star restaurant and my first time dining off the regular menu of a fine dining establishment) will be something I won't forget anytime soon. 

First, the food. Because what's a restaurant without good food? And boy, is the food here incredible. Every plate that passed its way through my table was devoured in its entirety, every crumb was consumed, and every drop of liquid was lapped up. Seriously, folks, the food here is ridiculously delicious. To start, the famous gougères and a parade of amuse bouches, which included a cup of intensely flavored chicken soup with parsley oil, brioche with shaved black truffles and chicken liver, and smoked sturgeon sabayon with chive oil. All were tasty, with the liver-topped brioche and smoked sturgeon sabayon leaving the most lasting impressions. Then, of course, came the bread. And oh, the bread. Served toasty warm, these soft rolls had a multiple layer-like structure akin to a cinnamon roll but with the buttery, flaky taste of a well-made croissant. Accompanied by goat's milk and cow's milk butters (use the goat's milk butter -- it was incredible) and a dish of sea salt, this was the bread that dreams are made of.

So all of that food had come and we still haven't even gotten to the first course yet, Both my brother and I (yes, I went on a man date with my brother; jealous?) elected to go with the foie gras because, well, would we really expect us to choose carrots over foie gras? Major props to the kitchen for accommodating our request to be served foie gras in two ways; while we both wanted foie gras, we didn't want to get the very same dish, either, since we wanted to try as many different dishes as possible. For the second course, my brother's lobster dish was the standout, though my black bass with black truffles and tapioca pearls was no slouch, either. But the star of the meal was, of course, the famous "Duck for Two" - a Muscovy duck roasted with lavender and a medley of spices and carved tableside. I'm Chinese, so naturally, I appreciate a well-cooked duck, and this duck was otherworldly. It was perfect: crisp, rendered skin layered up against moist, tender, and perfectly-cooked meat. This was, I daresay, the best duck I've ever eaten, and I don't take that statement lightly. Paired with a side dish of buttery whipped potatoes topped with a confit of duck leg, the duck course is a must-get. I repeat: GET THE DUCK FOR TWO. In theory, you need two people to order it, but really, if you're there by yourself or in an odd-numbered group, I wouldn't be against ordering a duck for yourself because it's so good that  you'll find a way to make room for two servings of duck anyway. An egg cream, dessert (chocolate and hazelnut were the selections), and truffles rounded out the meal.

Okay, so the food was incredible. How about the service? I'm glad you asked, because this was also the best service that I've ever had. As a table of two young guys in our early 20s, my brother and I tend to stand out quite visibly from the other diners at most high-end restaurants. This often leads to feelings of awkwardness, and service seems strained at such places as well, as if the servers aren't quite sure what to make of people like us dining at their restaurant when we obviously are nowhere near the wealth/sophistication of most of the other diners. Or maybe the waiters think that because we're Asian or that we're young guys, that we'll be really cheap with our tip. Who knows. But our main waiter here (I actually forgot his name, but if anyone from EMP is reading this, I think he said that we was Sicilian and that his wife was Indian) was extremely warm, accommodating, and helpful, and he was a pleasant guy to talk with. The service here was perfect: they were on top of everything, whether it was refilling our water glasses or removing empty dishes, but they weren't awkward and hovering near our table, either. And when our waiter saw how much we liked the bread, he happily offered (without our asking for it) to bring out another round of bread. 

It might have been a rainy day, but lunch at Eleven Madison Park was an incredible enough experience that I couldn't have cared less if there was a hurricane outside. Obviously, as a poor med student, EMP is way outside of my price range, but I will certainly remember this meal and look forward to returning sometime in the future when I'm actually making money.

Prix fix menu was a novel dining experience of many firsts.

-first macaron
-first sweet breads
-first time I've had breadcrumbs swept unto my seat
-first time we have had egg cream foamed at table side
-first time I've wanted to eat goat butter by the puck full

The food was presented with a flourish; with precision and beauty. The maître d' was wary of our every whim, sigh and smile. Pristine silverware for each course.
What would you expect with restaurant with Five James Beard Awards? After all the rave reviews, and the fact checks, the testimonials upon testimonials about the best meal of their life, I had sky high expectations. And EMP met most of them.

Dress to impress and make sure you get a reservation. Sometimes they get overbooked for lunch.

One of my go-to places for generally excellent French cuisine when I'm not craving anything specific for the meal. Pricey but so far with the food, service, and ambiance- haven't been disappointed- so willing to pay for it.
What can you say it's one of the best restaurants in NYC. When you are shooting for a fine dining experience they seldom miss. Do the tasting menu and get the full experience.

The Good - food, service, setting and ambience, attention to detail and overall experience is exceptional.
The Bad - Price could be an issue for some but you get what you pay for, and you're paying for a 3 michelin star dining journey you won't forget!

A good friend of mine recommended Eleven Madison Park for lunch as they offer a set meal for a reasonable price (75 USD for 4 courses, or 125 for the tasting menu). I have been to a number of Michelin star restaurants, and one 3 star before in Tokyo at Joel Robuchon's Le Chateau, where I had an incredible dining experience before so was keen to try. As my parents were visiting from England this provided the perfect opportunity for my Mums birthday! 

From the moment we arrived we knew we were in for something special! While some high end restaurants can be a little pretentious, the staff were very friendly and efficient in taking our coats and seating us, and the main dining area is set with a 30 foot ceiling and massive windowns looking onto Madison Park. After being seated, a rather unique menu arrived with 16 words written in a 4 by 4 grid. It was suggested we pick one from each row (appetizer, starter, entree, desert) however if we had any special dietary requirements they could cater for any changes which was good for my wife who's pescatarian. From there on started an incredible journey of food - as well as the dishes we ordered which were cooked and presented to perfection, the meal was spliced with various little tasters and teasers to set off the taste buds and cleanse the pallet from the previous course, or set it for the next. One thing that made it particularly special was the Chef's bring out the different courses and explaining what we were eating and how it was cooked! By the time we reached desert we were all pleasantly full and could not stop talking about the fantastic food.

While Eleven Madison is not for everyones tastes, or purse, for a treat it truly is an exceptional dining experience. Highly recommended!

What more can be said about this place?  I've had the pleasure of dining twice here and each experience was amazing.  Every staff member is excellent and very attentive to their guests from the host and coat check person to the dining floor captain and servers.  Each course is well paced and timely punctuated by in between courses of amuse bouche.  Every dish is a work of art, exquisite in composition and flavor.

The Spring menu is very light and well balanced.  If you're ever in the city during the fall, do try their white truffle course.  It is a pretty pricey supplement to the the prix fixe menu but it is well worth the price to experience the pungent scent of freshly shaved white truffle. 

Eleven Madison Park is quite easily my favorite dining experience.  I can't wait to go back to try their Summer and Winter menus.

We had a fantastic fine dinning experience here and would totally recommend people to come here for lunch as you can taste great food without spending too much money. 

My hubby decided to come here for my mother-in-law's birthday, there were 4 of us and we had 4 courses lunch. Every single dish was exquisite, the service was excellent. The waitress explained the dish well and gave very attentive services. From starter to dessert, everything was fantastic.

One of the most amazing places in all of NYC.  The seasonal tasting menus with the wine parings will leave you wishing for more. Beautiful place, excellent service. Great place for that once in the lifetime special romantic meal. Very pricey but worth every penny.

**********500th Review**********

My 500th review deserves something as amazing as discussing the wonderful, recently-crowned 3 star Michelin dinner Jim G. and I had for our 11th anniversary at Eleven Madison Park. Divine from beginning to end; my favorite dining experience in all of NYC!

The restaurant itself is in the stunning former Met Life building in the Flatiron, complete with original lighting and art deco inspired touches.  We had a wonderful table overlooking the entire restaurant and near one of the 9 foot exterior windows.  Excellent ambience and energy in the restaurant.  Of course, from the beginning of our arrival, until the end, everyone knew our names and where we were from, making our experience so very personal and cordial.  

We went with the four course tasting and had the wine pairing.  For the uninitiated, the menu is separated into ingredients, around which your dishes are created.  You choose the four ingredients that sound the best and then tell your server what types of dishes you enjoy, you don't enjoy, etc. The chef, the very talented Daniel Humm, then creates dishes based on your preferences.  Then the talented sommelier pairs wines (and other beverages) to match your meals.  None of this one-drink-fits-all pairing,  Our server asked if we had any drink preferences as well and I explained that I'm not a huge fan of the sweet, cloying (to me, anyway) dessert wines. We were presented with a coffee cocktail and an apple jack flip. 

There's no reason to detail every dish we had, since there's no guarantee they'll serve the same dishes when you go, but just know that, even with the so-called four course tasting, you'll end up getting a few amuse bouches, plus petit fours and other yummy sweets.  You'll walk out tons full! There was not one dish that was not amazing.  Perfectly cooked, expertly planned; excellent ingredients with intricate and creative preparations.  We enjoyed langoustine, foie gras, white truffle tortelli, poached lobster, roasted lamb, roasted pork, a delicious pistachio cake and a cheese plate.  I strongly recommend that you get coffee, as the restaurant does an amazing table-side coffee preparation.  It's both art and science simultaneously.  

After dinner (many hours later), our server placed a bottle of cognac on our table with some glasses and encouraged us to enjoy. Sadly we were far too full to really enjoy, but the gesture is great!  Sadly, Chef Humm was at a charity event that evening and so we couldn't meet him; that was the only thing that would have made the evening better.  Other than that minor glitch, it was perfect.  The server presented us with two in-house made chocolate bars, covered with freshly dried fruits and nuts, as an anniversary gift.  We were also sent home with a mason jar full of in-house made granola.  Of course we were also presented with personalized menus, helping us to recall what we ate and what we drank (minus the amuses; that would've been helpful too!).  

I would eat here a million times again, as long as I had the money to do so! Eleven Madison Park somehow manages to convey all the class of a 3-star Michelin restaurant but without the stuffiness that can sometimes invade. The service was stellar but comfortable and the food was amazing. This made our trip!

Took my family to celebrate my daughters 20th birthday. The experience was great, service was excellent and the food beautiful. Just be careful, had the $125.0 four course and was shocked when the bill came back with and extra $190.00 on it. It wasn't explained properly by the staff that if you choose the white truffle option it costs $95.00 on top of the $125.00!!! Would have given 4 stars if not for this.

98%
Excellent 16-course tasting menu with great beer pairings.

***Short Review

Came here for lunch by myself Nov'11

Although not listed on the menu, I was informed by a friend it would be possible to do a prolonged tasting.
Although this is one the best tasting experiences I've had, it's also one of the most exhausting.
The tasting took almost seven hours (arrived at noon, left close to 7pm).
The 16-course meal was a challenge to almost any appetite, which included a whole Muscovy duck.
I recommend dining alone if you want the whole duck to yourself.

Cooking is impressive and consistent.
I felt the emphasis the placement of aggressive yet compatible flavor combinations worked great.
It was thoroughly delicious, interesting, and hearty all at the same time.  
Two dishes, the Muscovy duck and the smoked sturgeon were close to perfect.
The desserts, although still very good were perhaps my least favorite of the dinner.

Drink pairings were very strong, and the Sommalier is one of the best.
It is commendable Eleven Madison Park is one of the few fine dining restaurants anywhere in the world that is so dedicated to beer and beer parings.

Prices aren't cheap but the value is strong given the quality of cooking and number of courses offered for their tasting.
Lunch prices are much more attractive and their 8-course for $125 is possibly one of the best values in town.

Service was exceptional.
All the staff were very professional, friendly, and enthusiastic with their work.
I spent a good deal of time chatting away with sommelier and servers.

Ambiance is very stylish and comfortable.
I enjoyed the lunch atmosphere even more than dinner.
