Bill was approx $511, here is the photo to the breakdown (posting b/c some were inquiring) http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=OWtjsyPKWUu7La7uOyC6Rw

Detailed Review will go further into each dish with more detail and pictures.
This will be a long review with multiple updates with my best attempt to document the experience.

***Detailed Review

No amuse bouche was served.  No bread was served either at the start, but there were some delicious cheese puffs offered at the table.  I felt it resembled the variety you might get in a Brazilian BBQ.  The flavor of the cheese resembled a gruyere to me.  They were a lot lighter, not so starchy and quite good.  They were served at a nice warmer temperature.

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=Mqu7tF0b5DRgo2dxKM1TeQ

Shortly after, the sommelier offered me a glass of champagne.  I'm not much of a wine drinker and don't recall what was used.  It was fairly dry and had a good deal of carbonation.  I enjoyed it and found it to be refreshing.  Not unlike most champagnes, was also very versatile with many of the beginner courses, and in some cases more that the beer pairings.

MUSHROOM
Tea with Brioche and Truffle
(Dish Rating 92%)

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/nRO136GRieGtxz18uD61DA?select=fNj_oOchcqH9fOy3JTTmNA

This was the first course of the tasting menu.  There are two items served.  First, is a light mushroom broth soup, with some lemon verbena herbs dipped in.  The soup is served in a teacup, with the herbs meant to resemble a teabag.  The soup was relative simple mushroom flavored savory broth with just subtle hint of the herb.  It was enjoyable but not the most memorable thing by itself (bar the more clever presentation).  Serving temperature was hot, but not too much so.

Second part of the dish is smaller brioche toast served with a good portion of white truffles on top.  Truffles had a pungent aroma and very robust flavor.  These are certainly some of the strongest tasting white truffles I've tried as of recent.  It's difficult to for me to give a poor rating based on the superior quality of truffles alone.  Taking a bite of the truffle toast and sip of the broth afterwards worked good, but I'm not convinced the broth actually added much.  In the end, I probably would have preferred enjoying the two things separately.  Great starter course nonetheless.

To be continued, please refer to 'earlier review'

Yes, it lives up to all the hype and the expensive price. Eleven Madison Park got elevated to three Michelin stars this year, and they have earned it. The menu is innovative especially on how you actually order. Dishes can be customized based on your taste. The service is fantastic, and the whole staff makes you feel important.

I took clients here, and they were dazzled! I had a great assortment of seafood, vegetables and meat. Don't even get me started on all the complimentary small dishes that come between your main courses. The cocktail list and wine menu are extensive as well.

If you are looking for main dining, Eleven Madison Park is a must!

~A
Exceptional resturant; excellent food, great drink menu an unbelievable beer selection and wonderful service. It's not cheap but worth the money.

Add my review to the many ones praising EMP for a job well done!  This experience was the highlight of our (husband and I) trip.  Our "captain" Cheryl lead the army of servers with humor, insight and great recommendations. I had foie gras, carrot, split 3rd course with husband-duck, hazelnut for dessert. Surprisingly, the carrot was amazing, cooked in duck fat, how could it not be? Carrot is not something I usually get excited about, but Cheryl recommended, so I went with it.  It was excellent.  The duck was a show in itself, carved table-side. Husband had crab, lobster and chocolate for dessert.  All courses and extras were beyond amazing, even the BREAD & BUTTER will make you swoon!! These people have it figured out to the smallest, thoughtful detail.  Get on the wait-list if they are booked for your stay, we were called the Saturday before our trip with an opening and we switched everything else around to eat here.  Do it!! It is wonderful.

While in New York I went to Eleven Madison Park to have lunch with my Houstonian, turned New Yorker, turned Houstonian, turned New Yorker friend who just so happened to be running a little late because of taking the wrong subway (name omitted as to not embarrass). I thought I would be the late one considering I don't live in New York. Anyway, it provided me with a laugh before going inside.

As is the case with most restaurants, when you walk in there are most often people in front of you waiting to be seated. After they were seated, the maître d' apologized for the wait (I wouldn't even consider it a wait), and welcomed me to the restaurant. I gave her my name and was again welcomed. Since I was waiting for my friend to arrive, I was asked if I would prefer waiting at our table or at the bar. I decided to wait at the bar. Even after being there for a few minutes it was hard to not notice how incredibly friendly everyone was.

During the short walk to the bar area, I was able to get a better look at the restaurant. A very high ceiling, a huge picture of Madison Square Park, large floral arrangements, and huge windows. And the best part was the abundant natural light that filled the restaurant. Thank you huge windows. At the bar, I decided to have a drink while I wait. I tried the Fig and Thistle. Very good and the first time I'd had a fig based drink. One drink from the menu has what I'd consider the best drink name possible... "Sippy Cup."

So, my friend arrived and they showed us to our seats. I believe the level of friendliness was even higher at this point. After being seated, our waiter pointed out the menu and showed us how ordering worked. We decided on the 4 course lunch. The menu consists of a 4x4 grid of items. For the non math majors, that's 16 items. No actual description, but just the main ingredient of each course. For the 4 course lunch, you choose any 4 items, and your dishes are prepared based off of them. I wonder how many people choose 4 desserts?

While deciding on our courses, we were brought out gougères (small, light, cheese/dough pastries). They were great and a good way to start off lunch. For my first two courses I choose "beets" and "carrots." I was very curious to see how the carrot dish would be prepared. Our waiter suggested the "duck for two" as one of the courses, so that was chosen as number three. My final course was "apple."

The long list of food:
toasted brioche topped with shaved truffles
truffle tea
smoked sturgeon sabayon in an egg shell (very interesting presentation)
warm, flaky, delicious bread with goat's milk and cow's milk butter
roasted beets
roasted carrots with a delicious sauce (very good)
duck for two
duck leg and foie gras in some kind of potato cream (surprisingly good)
egg cream (a drink that interestingly contains no egg)
ice cream and caramelized apple dessert
mini macarons, jelly/plum candy, and mini shortbreads with lemon topping

I won't describe all the food, but for me, the highlight of the lunch was the duck. This course was basically an extravagant presentation. The duck is brought out on a cart and carved at table side (which looked like a very difficult task). The duck was served along with turnips and figs. I can't say that duck is normally one of my favorite things, but this was very good. In the middle of the duck course, two small bowls were brought out that seemed to just be filled with some kind of cream. This was the duck leg and foie gras in some kind of potato cream. Surprisingly delicious considering I don't really like foie gras.

The first three courses were excellent. My final course, apple ice cream with caramelized apples, was not as good. That's not to say it was bad, but it just wasn't as interesting as the previous courses. It just wasn't memorable, whether describing flavor or presentation. 

Even if you don't like the food at Eleven Madison Park, there is no way you won't like and appreciate the service. The service was excellent. Extraordinary friendly, yet not obnoxious nor annoying. From the moment I walked in, to when we left, excellent service all around. The lunch was seventy five dollars and although that is not cheap, I'd say it was definitely worth it. Even at just four courses, with all the additions, there is definitely enough food. Maybe even too much. But really, can there ever be too much (good) food?

I can say confidently that I had the best dining experience of my life. Eleven Madison is a restaurant only to be found in  NYC, it is exceptional. Came here for a nice dinner, left with an experience of a lifetime. 
From the crab appetizer to the truffle risotto. Everything tried on the "four-course" grid menu was excellent. Besides from what is ordered, the servers will constantly bring small treats. 

Bottom Line: dinner will be 3hrs, your bank account will hurt, but I wouldn't think twice about going again. Really opened my eyes to excellent food.

This was the best dining experience of my life. From the warm greeting as I revolved through the entryway revolving door to the basket of bread handed to me as I revolved out, every minute of this meal was simply wonderful. The four-course "grid" menu with wine pairings morphed into an endless parade of amuses bouche, warm toasty bread, and egg creams. I was expecting four small pours when I ordered the pairings and got at least seven (I can't remember exactly...things got a little fuzzy after the foie gras) generous pours, complete with helpful descriptions from the sommelier. 

Everything was beyond delicious, of course, but the highlight for me was the impeccable and shockingly friendly service. Three Michelin stars is a little intimidating and I was emotionally prepared for some snootiness. But, no - everyone was so warm, fun, and almost casual (though, not actually casual. Let's get real, this is EMP). My boyfriend and I were pretty into the bread and mentioned it briefly to one of the busboys as crumbs were being cleared. On the way out, a lovely woman stopped us, handed me a bag, and said "We heard you loved the bread! Please take some home!" I mean, COME ON!

The EMP granola was delightful for breakfast the next morning, and I still have the jar in my kitchen to remind me of the best birthday ever.

If you don't know well now you do! I rate this as my top restaurant in the city bar none! I went for an anniversary and had the chefs menu with wine pairings. Creative, delicious, educational simply a perfect service with food to match. Walked 20 city blocks with my lady just waxing lyrical about the experience we had just shared. Front of the house is imposing and but oddly appropriate.  

You're going to drop serious coin but don't think of the money because it's really the kind of event dinning that will have your friend rolling their eyes when you bring up how magical a night you had there.

Had the tasting menu with my best friends and it was one of the best dinners of my life. More courses than expected and they truly went over the top for an incredible dining experience. Atmosphere is very formal.

Delicious. Every time I come here, I feel like I've been massaged from the inside out. I leave happy, relaxed, and a little too full, but in a totally Zen way.

My only warning is to not go on an umami binge like I did during my last visit. I had the foie gras (both in creme brulee and torchon form), followed by white truffle  tortellini (watching them shave the truffle was a sexual experience), and a whole bunch of other fatty wonderful things.

I learned that I am a weak, weak person. I became nauseous towards the end of the meal, and my vision started to blur. I insisted on finishing every delicious thing, even though my body was telling me to stop. If previous experiences were like a relaxing massage, this felt like a really fat, hairy Russian bath guy pounding my tummy.

So you see, in this case, the customizable menu was bad for me, because I have no boundaries, discipline, or self-preservation skills. So order smart, peoples!

Very good

The menu looks more customizable than it really is. But that said, lunch was very good. Went on a weekday and ate at a enjoyable leisurely place. Love the high ceiling and open decor. Service was great. Every dish had lots of variety of items on it.  Absolutely loved the malted milk soda - lots of malt flavor with a hit of salt and lots of vanilla bean specks - a unique retro fountain drink.

One of the very few places that is worth going to among the class of restaurants that sits just below the elite Manhattan restaurants like Daniel and Per Se.

i went here for my bday and let me say it was phenomenal. hands down the best restaurant experience i've had to date. service was spectacular and food was amazing. we had the 4 course pre-fixe. i'd go back here for any special occasion. simply amazing.
Their scallop made me want to cry because it was so good, and I don't even like scallops.

beautiful place. and that's it!! went for dinner and had about an army of 10 taking orders and not communicating with each other. extremely annoying. we got asked 4 times if we wanted another drink, while we had already placed an order with one of the soldiers. the cocktail were good, and i would probably go back (to the bar) for that.  As far as the food? Blah! The emperor has no clothes!

Currently on a flight back to California, compelled to write my first ever Yelp review because of our terrific experience at Eleven Madison Park on Friday afternoon.  This story won't go too much into the already well-documented food - suffice it to say we loved every course we were served and were particularly impressed with the quality and imagination exhibited in their vegetable dishes, a true rarity.  Instead, I'd like to focus on the restaurant's service and attention to detail...

In anticipation of a trip to NYC, my girlfriend researched restaurants and became intrigued with EMP's menu concept.  Unbeknownst to her I was planning to propose marriage sometime during our weekend in the city, and an idea came to me that EMP could be the place to do it.  I called the restaurant to tell them my plan and ask for a late reservation, and they were gracious enough to squeeze us in for Friday lunch even though they were booked up.  Then, in the days leading up to our meal, the restaurant called two separate times to ask if there was anything they could do to help me prepare for the event.  I told them I was planning to pop the question in a low-key manner and only requested a booth or semi-secluded table, but I really appreciated the attentive offer.

Once we arrived, they did indeed seat us in a nice corner booth and the meal began.  We truly loved it, right down to the fantastic goat's milk butter served with their fresh baked bread.  The EMP waitstaff are also remarkably great at their jobs: anticipating anything one might need or want more of, almost before you even realize it yourself, without ever hovering or intruding.  We had dishes of halibut, carrot, veal, and fluke, among others, and enjoyed every bite.

The ring was burning a hole in my pocket and I finally asked her the question over dessert.  It involved a doctored version of EMP's recognizable menu that I'd prepared in advance.  She said yes (whew), and the restaurant proceeded to pour us complimentary champagne to celebrate.  I am kicking myself because in my proposal-fog I failed to get the young woman's name who was our main server - or perhaps "facilitator" is a better title, her skill set and knowledge seemed to go way beyond simply serving - but I hope this review does somehow get back to her and I'll also write a note directly to the restaurant.  Her generosity the entire meal was so incredibly appreciated by my fiancé (ok, have to get used to saying that!) and me, even past when I'd paid the bill and right up to the moment we got our jackets from the coat check...to the point where I am so regretting not tipping more than the 25% I left.  I'll just say they gave us a really nice token on our way out the door as a reminder of the occasion.

Just to reiterate, I didn't go into too much detail here about the food because the intent was to focus on the service/experience.  I could honestly write poetry about the sublime flavors we enjoyed, but this is already quite a long-winded review.  Thanks so much to everyone at EMP for making our special day truly spectacular.  We hope to see you again very soon.

Daniel Green has made this place an amazing venue for my wife and myself.  I really can't thank him and the team enough for all of their great efforts.  Of course, the food is just as impeccable as the service itself.  

The portions are a smaller than Jean-Georges, but they are just perfect.  You can get out of there without feeling like you are about to enter a food coma!

I've been here several times, and I will be here many more!

One of the best meals I've had in the City. While the decor may be a touch classical for some (jacket), the preparation of the food was superb, the service excellent and the sommelier very helpful in pairing wines with our food. A truly well put together group of individuals who help to deliver what is produced in the kitchens and present it in the best possible light.

Spring for the long tasting menu... it will run you about four hours time but it is AMAZING!!  Not only did it taste absolutely delicious but it was quite clever and whimsical!  I love the creativity that went into each dish which added to the enjoyment.  Although I'm not a fan of manhattans, I loved the course where you get a tour of the kitchen and while there, frozen manhattan are made for your enjoyment right in front of you using liquid nitrogen!

Note:  If you do the wine pairing, don't mention you are going to split it.  They were very snotty about this, which having done this recently at both Ko and WD-50, I was surprised.  I've learned that if I do a full paring, I will typically indulge which doesn't help the hangover the next day, so if I have to be up early the next morning, I will share a pairing with my guest.  

I didn't expect or ask them to pour the one pairing into two glasses or anything and yes, it's clearly only intended to pair for one of the tastings and not the other when you deviate on courses but they were quite insistent that we each get our own separate pairings.  Eleven Madison Park has 2 separate pairings, btw.  One is strictly wine and one is a mix of alcohols, wine and beer.  Since we felt obliged to get 2, my date got the wine and I got the mixed, which except for one or two misses paired nicely with our meals.  This little encounter started before our meal so the standard of pretension was set but the first impression was not at all reflective of the service the rest of the meal and we had a fantastic time.  I knock off points for this, but the food was so good it more than made up for it.

If you don't want to be completely trashed at the end of the meal, then just order a pairing for one and share... but don't tell your server!

Eleven Madison Park is like the Disney Jungle Cruise and I don't mean that in a disparaging way. It is a well oiled machine. You are never in any danger because it runs on rails and just like clockwork, everything is scripted to measured beats. And if you have had friends that gone Eleven Madison Park you know that your experience will be exactly the same as their experience. Like an animatronic hippo that pops up to face the tour guide's cap gun at a precise time, you know that you will get scripted treats between courses. But that is also Eleven Madison Park's one achilles heel, anything you do to throw off that script really cheeses them off, and it shows. One person in our party was a little late arriving and another in our party who was incredibly indecisive really seemed to agitate our waiter on a not-so-busy Monday evening. No matter how hard our waiter tried to hide it, that "you're messing with my script" look and tone came through his proper zen veneer.

That aside, the meal was quite good. Our table had opted for the four -course meal plus an extra duck course. Personally, I thought the highlights weren't the four-course meal itself, but the little between meal plates. The plates really showcased the chef's creativity and were far more surprising than the mains. The mushroom tea was a great way to start things off along with the truffle bruschetta. And the yogurt lollipop and egg cream made at our table were a fun little accents.

This place was really good and not too stuffy, but I went during lunch.  If you go ask to see the kitchen that was my favorite part.  It was huge and immaculate they also made us an edible cocktail and it was delicious.

Moving blows.  Especially when you're downsizing from a nice place to a shoebox-sized apartment.

When that apartment is so much smaller than your previous abode that you're saving hundreds of dollars a month in rent, however, there is one saving grace - for that first month, you feel like you just won a bunch of free money!  And since moving into a smaller apartment is a financially responsible move, I think it entails a financially irresponsible celebration, to celebrate my responsibility (it makes sense if you don't think about it).

And so it was that Jason H and I planned a dinner for the ages here at EMP.  And let me tell you - it didn't come easily, oh no.  After nabbing a fantastic reservation for 4 at prime dinner time on a Saturday evening in August, we waited and waited and waited in anticipation of what we were sure would be the best meal of our lives.  And then, the weekend came......and so did Hurricane Irene.  And we got the dreaded call on Friday afternoon that they'd be closing the next day, forcing us to reschedule our reservation about a month down the road.

All I can say is.....SUCK IT, Hurricane Irene.  (Or should I say, Tropical Storm Irene?  OH SNAP!!!)

I got a call from Sandra, one of the managers here, just a few hours after I had learned about EMP closing for Saturday telling me that a 9:30 reservation had just opened up on Friday night.  Our other 2 friends wouldn't be able to join us that night, so being the nice people we are, we said, "Screw them," and took the reservation immediately.  We were in! (This was the only weekend we could reasonably expect to go at all!  We're not bad people!  I swear!)

From that phone call on out, this was an utterly divine dining experience, combining food and service in a manner that went far beyond anything I've experienced before.

When we arrived, we were greeted by a hostess who not only knew who we were before we even said anything, but who knew that we had switched our reservation because of the hurricane.  She thanked us for being flexible, as if we needed to be thanked for coming to experience what might be the best food in the city.  We were led to the bar where we grabbed a couple of (fantastic) cocktails and munched on delicious homemade potato chips and other bar snacks as we waited for our table to get set.  We chatted with the bartender (who also apparently knew that we had switched our reservation at the last second, too) for awhile about her favorite drinks/bars in the city/etc, and had a great time just sitting and waiting for the meal to get started.  The sort of personal attention that we got from the hostess and the bartender right off the bat was there all night, with every single member of EMP's staff offering constant helpfulness, great conversation, and endless knowledge of the food and drink on hand (and doing so without the kind of pretension that I had assumed would be running rampant at a place this nice).

I'm not going to go into detail about all of the food we got (we went with the grid menu and wine pairing), suffice it to say that everything here is just about perfect.  From the dishes in the spotlight...

(***IF IT'S AVAILABLE WHEN YOU'RE HERE GET THE DUCK FOR TWO***, because it was absolutely hands down without a doubt the !!!BEST!!! duck I've ever had in my life.  Carved in front of you at the table, just an incredibly, ludicrously tender and flavorful duck breast, and then they take the rest back to the kitchen to make duck leg confit with foie gras under cheesy potatoes) 

...to the amuse-bouche and other things on the sidelines...

(ie. the greatest bread ever baked by man, the tomato tea with thyme, the goat cheese lollipops, the mini egg cream, etc etc)

...everything that we ate was creative, beautiful, and most importantly, astoundingly delicious.  The kind of delicious where you can't help but close your eyes, dissociate yourself from whatever unimportant corporeal jibber-jabber was floating through your mind, and focus all of your energy on that one glorious bite of beautifully crafted food as it fills your palate.

We arrived excited, and we left comfortably full, more than a little tipsy (thanks to the wine pairing, which was great, but which I won't do if I'm back here again) (and also thanks to that bottle of cognac that they leave at the table....), and feeling fucking happy about life.

I haven't had many true "fine dining" experiences, and it's definitely not something that I'm going to be able to make a regular part of my routine for quite some time, if ever.  But man oh man, did I make the right choice in coming here.  If you can find an excuse to do so - even a bad one - do yourself a favor and make it happen.

Perfection. This is the only way to describe the meal and experience that was had here. It's really the ultimate experience in dining. EMP has created new dining expectations that will be tough to match.

My girlfriend and I came here for lunch in September to celebrate a special occasion. From the moment we walked through the doors on Madison Avenue, there could not have been more attention to detail. As we entered the restaurant, the maitre'd asked if we'd be joining them for lunch. I said yes and that we had a reservation. He inquired as to the last name and after I spoke it, he said "Happy Anniversary!" - without looking at a reservation book or computer notes.

As we arrived at our table, something was already waiting for us - it was a card, with our names on the envelope. Both the envelope with our names and the card itself was written in very fancy calligraphy and wished us well and thanked us for choosing EMP to celebrate such a special occasion.

Anyways, after we were seated, we discovered our menus underneath our napkins. As we were looking at our menus, someone came over to us with warm greetings and asked if we'd like to see the list of champagne. We agreed but i n the end tho, didn't feel like drinking that early in the day and politely declined. Back to looking at our menus, when the same server who had offered us champagne returned with two glasses of bubbly. She said that they wanted us to have something bubbly to celebrate with and gave us two glasses of sparkling French cider, The cider was amazing, like no sparking cider I've ever tasted before. After we finished, I asked if they could please find out where the cider was sold so that I could buy a bottle. They said they would find out for us.

At this point, we ordered, after our server explained how the menu works and what not. We opted for the four course menu and the ingredients my gf chose were tuna, lobster, pork and plum. I chose prawn, loup de mer, lamb and chocolate. Once we had finished ordering, the amuses began. They were: 

1. Gougéres - warm, cheesy and soft, with just a tad of salt on the outside. So yummy. 
2. Heirloom tomato "tea" spiked with lemon thyme that comes skewered on raffia and accompanied by a Parmesan crisp. Flavorful and savory.
3. Smoked sturgeon sabayon with chive oil. Yummy!

Next came the bread and butter. I forget the details on the bread, but there was goat's milk butter, cow's milk butter and sea salt. The goat's milk butter was outstanding and beat out the cow's milk butter. The sea salt was very good as well.

After this, our first course came. I had chosen prawns and received Prawns, Crudo with Grapes, Fennel and Marcona Almonds. My gf chose tuna and received Tuna, Marinated with Heirloom Tomatoes, Garlic and Basil. Delicious...

For our second course, she chose lobster and received Butter Poached Lobster with Lasagna and Lemon Verbena. I had chosen loup de mer and received Loup de Mer, Seared with Shrimp, Clams, Chorizo and Bouillabaisse. Again, quite delicious.

For our third course, she chose pork and received Pork, Roasted with Bacon Apricots and Spinach. I had chosen lamb and received Lamb, Roasted with Eggplant, Sheep's Milk Yogurt and Sweetbreads. I'm running out of words to describe how good the food was, but it was really good. The pork belly was definitely sent from the heavens.

In case I didn't mention it recently, all throughout our meal, people were coming up to us and wishing us well. Anyways, after our third course, we were asked if we'd like a kitchen tour - of course! As we entered the kitchen and as we stood in the viewing station, with the workings of the kitchen being explained to us, a chef started preparing something in front of us. I don't remember exactly what it was, but I remember hearing that liquid nitrogen was being used to freeze gin to make some sort of frozen cocktail. It had apples in it and whatever else and was like no cocktail I'd ever had.

After the tour was over, we went back to our table and waited for dessert, before which, an egg cream was served. For dessert, she had asked for plum and received Plum - Roasted with Crème Caramel, Orange and Sage. I had ordered chocolate and received Gianduja with Hazlenut, Espresso and Caramel. Both really, really good.

After dessert, I asked if they had been able to find where I could buy the cider, but they did one better and gave us a bottle! Along with that came petit fours, macaroons, madeleines and other goodies, including their fruit & nut bar. We also asked if they knew a place to buy macaroons and they suggested La Maison du Macaroon. We were also given printed menus of what we'd eaten. And the bill was stylish too.

If you have a special occasion to celebrate, go to EMP! Shortly after our meal, they were also awarded three Michelin stars. At $74 for four courses plus all the bonuses, it's totally worth it and they make you feel very special. The food and service kick this place up above 5 stars!

I'll def be back

The boyfriend and I came here for lunch on a trip to New York back in September and while the simple but tasty food was good enough to justify the cost (though not altogether memorable), the service was outstanding.  I never felt as if I was in the wrong place for my economic status and I never felt too rushed to enjoy my meal. The tomato tea and egg amuse bouches were definitely the highlight of our meals.  The duck was prepared at the table in an insanely elaborate fashion by the waiter.  Also, some time after our dessert, we were ushered into the kitchen and saw an amazing beehive of people getting ready to prepare dinner. The experience alone definitely made my trip worthwhile.  
 
If I had to, I would take a 1/2 star away, since the dishes were not necessarily a knock out of the park.  Still, comparing this experience to previous ones at the same price point, I do think I will definitely return for the dinner tasting menu some day.

We had our wedding lunch for 15 people here, in a private room in the second floor. We coordinated everything by email, and it worked just as we wanted.
The food was very good! We wanted a meal to remember, and we had it,all our guests still comment about it. 
In our room we had staff just for us, and they were really nice and patient with our group. 
In addition, I appreciated that they minimum consumption was very reasonable, which I didnt find in cheaper restaurants.

- Please read my initial reviews in order to get the full picture of the review. Photos: http://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=10150321898866676&set=a.10150234017951676.312867.727646675&type=3&theater

I was in EMP again on Oct 7th with a group for foodie friends for their tasting dinner. It was all their first time there and since I've been shamelessly plugging EMP for many months, I was afraid it would not live up to expectations; but it did. And to top it off, EMP just received their 3rd Michelin star, making it the 1st restaurant to jump from 1 star to 3 stars in NYC! Well done Team EMP!

The one thing that received the most commendation alongside the food was the service. Kevin did a great job and Maya was still her awesome self. There is nothing here worth saying that hasn't been said before about the service standard in EMP.

Tasting menus have all along been about the kitchen showing its talent in the form of experiential progression. EMP struck the right notes of being perfect - I left feeling light headed and not overly full and it became an obsession. I just wanted more and more. We decided to get 2 bottles of champagne for the night - a Vouette & Sorbée, Cuvée Rosé Saignée de Sorbée, and a Billecart-Salmon, Cuvée Nicolas François Billecart, 2000 which I cannot stop ranting about.

Amuse Bouche:
1. Gourgeres - Light fluffy goodness, beautiful fleur de sel textural contrast
2. Mushroom Tea, Brioche with Black Truffle - after the tomato tea, I thought the limits of tea was set. Now it is smashed. The brioche was a surprising strong but not overpowering complement
3. Tuna & Scallop - acid and sweetness by the meyer lemon is wonderful on the tuna and the tangerine & fennel elevated the scallop beyond distinction. Awesome way to kick-start the palate.
4. Goat Cheese Lollipop, Goat Cheese Croquette - Never ceases to amaze me, especially when I am not a fan of goat cheese.
5. Clambake: Clam Chowder, Lobster Croquette, Clam Gelee, Clam Vinaigrette - This seasonal amuse is a wonderful play on the clambake and the table display of steaming hot rocks makes this dish an experience for all 5 senses. Clam chowder is light and you actually get to taste the freshness of the clams. The other two clam dishes were the perfect contrasting dishes and great end to the amuse course. 

Next came the House-made Bread with Cow and Goat Milk Butter and Fleur de Sel. Awesome. Period.

Course 1: Cucumber - Cucumber Salad with Pickles, Mustard Seeds and Buttermilk Foam. Let me put things in perspective. I hate cucumbers. But I'm craving for this dish as I am typing this now.

Course 2: Foie Gras - Foie Gras Terrine with Plum, Bitter Almond and Umeboshi. Still one of the best foie terrines I've ever had. Yet another dish that exemplifies the EMP standard of making each bite a different experience. This dish is a marvel to behold.

Course 3: Endive - Truffle Roasted Endives, Egg Yolk, Gruyère, Brioche, Pear. This progression was clearly well thought out. The endives were almost meaty and a strong flavourful burst. I have no idea that it is possible to make roasted endive this juicy, and how they could make the transition from something light to something heavy like this.

Course 4: Lobster - Poached Lobster with Lobster Sabayon, Mushroom Puree, Autumn Mushrooms. Lobsters and mushrooms don't seem too fancy, but not in the hands of the chefs in EMP. They totally hit the spot with the mix or sweetness of the sea and the earthiness of the mushrooms. 

Course 5: Pork - Duo of Pork (Loin, Belly), Plums, Butternut Squash Puree, Amoretti. I had the full sized version of this dish the last time I was here and I would say that this portion would have been more perfect despite lacking the rack of pork. The flavours were just exquisite. I especially adore the crust on the loin and the rest of my companions think the belly is heavenly.

Course 6: Ricotta - Ricotta with Yellow Beets, Apricot, Gooseberries, Fleur de Sel. I have never had ricotta like this before. Once again, it is about progression and ricotta bridged the gap between the savoury and sweet. Wonderful dish this one. 

Pre-Dessert: NY Egg Cream - I could rant on and on about this but all should be said has been said in my earlier reviews.

Course 7: Chocolate - Hazelnut Sorbet on Pine Nut Crunch, Gianduja with Hazelnut, Espresso and Caramel. This is my first low point. I did not like this dessert the last time I had it and I did not like it now. 

Mignardise & Cognac - The sweet ending to the meal was great, minus the gelee that was my second low point of the meal. Maybe its just me. But, EMP ended the meal with something special - a bottle of Guillon-Painturaud as a digestif. It sent me halfway to heaven.

The 4 hour meal ended and we were given the EMP Granola to take home. I hate myself for giving away the two bottles to the ladies I've been there with. It shattered what I thought granolas can be. Now I'll never be able to eat any others. 

So close to perfection. So close.

Absolutely divine dining experience. You choose an ingridient and the chef creates a theme. For starters tomato tea was offerded to freshen the palate. It looks like tea, but when you take a sip, tomato undertone comes blooming with full flavor. Then there was ricotta, rabbit terrine, and other great dishes. 
Reservations are a must here, the place was packed. It took 2 weeks for an open spot, but it was totally worth it.

What has not been said about this place? Food and service was very good. I was not impressed with a few things that came to the table. But the ahi tuna bite on rice cracker with citrus was mind blowing. Fois Gras wha is not to love. Lobster with various mushrooms was exceptional. There was sand in spinach. I had the pork entree and was not thrilled. Dessert was ok o n the chocolate side. I found the cheese plate exceptional. The Cognac after the meal was a nice touch.

2012 Michelin New York Upgrades Eleven Madison Park to Chefs Club Of Who's Who Get The Overview TravelWithCarnet.Com

Winning 1 Michelin Star in 2002 wasn't enough for Swiss chef Daniel Humm so he ventured out west. He reigned at the helm of Campton Place where he won the Food and Wine Chef of the Year. With his mind set on higher aspirations, he struck a deal of a lifetime with Danny Meyer and moved to Eleven Madison Park with his full staff in tow.

Chef Humms' culinary influences are definitely European and reflect the sensibilities of market driven cuisine with preparations cooked gently under low temperature. His classic flavor combinations truly put him in a league with the best chefs on the international scene. 

The beautiful dining space, excellent wine list and connections to one of the best cheese mongers from the west coast makes this restaurant is a destination unto itself.

The editorsblog at: 
http://bit.ly/TWC_NY_DINING 
gives a quick but savvy overview

Eleven Madison Park is my one and only 5 stars. I can't imagine that any other place will come close. My mom was visiting me in the city in May and I wanted to treat her to an unforgettable experience. It truly was. Service, food and ambiance were all impeccable. We ordered the full tasting menu and each course was divine. The one course we did not enjoy was quickly removed and replaced with a better one. Because of a lovely co-worker's connections, we were treated to a few extras: a special after-dinner kitchen tour with a tasty liquid nitrogen concoction and a behind the scenes glimpse. And they even presented us with an old fashioned Mason jar of house-made granola. The dinner was more than $600 but well worth it. And the dinner was more an event than a meal: it was 4 hours long! I kept a running tally as each course was served. Here it is, though not with much detail:
1. Pea soup
2. Sea scallops
3. Beet and goat cheese lollipops with dipping sauce
4. Cheese balls
5. Apple, crab and sea urchin soup
6. Caviar on vegetables
7. Smoked sturgeon in egg shell
8. Bread with cow's milk and goat's milk cheese
9. Salad
10. Crab with violet flowers
11. Scallops with fava beans
12. Broccoli
13. Eggplant with lemon verbena
14. Pork
15. Egg cream
16. Chocolate mousse

AMAAAAAAZING!

I must say, this was the BEST meal I've had since I've been in NY.  My wonderful friend took me here for lunch on a Tuesday and we each had the 4 course meal for $75, which took about 2.5 hours (definitely something to keep in mind).

The 4 ingredients I picked were:
1. Foie Gras
2. Lobster
3. Lamb
4. Chocolate

I waited too long to write this review and now I don't remember the deets (bummer).  However, I know for a fact that my stomach was pleasantly content.

Service exceeded beyond excellence.
Food was impeccable.
Presentation was perfect.

Wonderful experience, amazing dishes, and the perfect company.  What more can a girl ask for?

Oh, and for you SATC fans, EMP is where Big told Carrie that he is engaged to Natasha.  Remember that???

Anyways, definitely worth all the hype and more.

What an experience.  It was fun, really fun.  Eleven Madison has service and then some.  Food was very creative and overall delicious.  Maybe every dish wasn't a knockout, but that service....

Beautiful restaurant right by Madison Park.  Little card on the table congratulating us on our anniversary.  Nice touch.  We opted for the full tasting menu over the four course grid system.  There are so many amuse-bouche courses, around four, that the full tasting is kind of overkill.  I think in retrospect I would have been more apt to go four course with wine pairing instead.   Wine and beer lists are both large and well varied.  Sommelier was very helpful in providing recommendations on both fronts, and seemed genuinely excited about helping us pick something we'd enjoy.

The most intense tomato broth I've ever had, goat cheese & beet lollipops, roe concoctions, hollowed out eggshells, and creative presentation all the way around.  It's been a bit, so I don't remember the exacts of everything, and I do remember a couple unspectacular courses, but I'll hand it to them for thinking outside the box and coming up with some delicious flavors.

3 hours and many courses later the meal was over, and then things got interesting.

Manager came by, informed us we were going back into the kitchen.  And into the kitchen we went, where the chef met us and a staff member provided a little liquid nitrogen dessert show.  Lots of fun.  In further acknowledgement of our nascent specialness, we were led to the lounge and told to enjoy as much of the waiting bottle of Amaro as we wanted.  Great night.

Nice to see them get bumped up to 3 Michelin stars this year, I think they deserve it.  This would be among the few restaurants I've been to world wide that I would give a special extra 6th Yelp star to.

I know they don't need another positive review but I have to say Eleven Madison Park is quite amazing. I've enjoyed fine dining all over the world and this is clearly up there. Go, enjoy an evening of food - it will be a special experience for all...

4.5 rounds up to 5. The vaulted dining area is amazing. One major factor was the timing - this was a ridiculously long meal. The 4 course meal took about 4.5 hours.

The bread was delicious and came nice and warm, nestled in a napkin with 3 choices of butter.

I started with the langoustine, which was really nice with a sweet tinge. Dining partner had the foie gras, which was also good. Next course was comprised of ever-delicious truffles. For the main, we shared the off-the-menu duck entrée, which was amazingly tender and juicy. Great food, but the desserts were not up to the par of the rest of the dinner. My partner's pistachio based dessert was better than my apple based one.

After the courses, a server wheeled over a cart and mixed a Manhattan egg cream in front of us, which was fantastic. I had the baicha, a very light green tea - decent but a bit too light for my liking. Afterwards, the waiter brought over a bottle of cognac and told us to drink as much as we want, but he neglected to serve us the petit fours. Shame!

We each received a mason jar of fresh granola at the end. A mason jar! So quaint and country. Love it.

The food was exemplary, but the service fell short of the orchestrated perfection that is Daniel.

Definitely looking forward to returning.

Stopped in at EMP's bar in serious need of a Negroni.  I ordered one, only giving the barkeep my preference that it be served in an old-fashioned glass with one large piece of ice.  He stirred (correct!), poured and placed it in front of me; I sipped.  Perfection.  He made it with Beefeater (correct!), and instead of following the classic 1:1:1 ratio of gin-campari-vermouth, he upped the gin (correct!).  He also ignited the oils in the orange peel garnish over the drink with a match.  Haven't seen that done for a 'groni before.  Classy touch, EMP.

For those of you who were wondering, it was $15.  (Eep!)

We went for the tasting menu. 


Compliments
Service was excellent. 
Food was prepared perfectly. 
Sea urchin was very fresh

Complaints
Not enough protein. There was a small amount of lamb, and some fish, but not enough. 
Dessert was creative but not very good. Petite fours were better than the dessert.

Personal preference..
I didn't like the orange infused egg cream. It tasted good, but I hate the creamsicle flavor.. Citrus and milk.. 

I went, I enjoyed myself. Would I go back again,maybe. I'll try per se next!

Believe the hype.If there is only one 3 star restaurant you can go to in NYC, it should be this one. It was better than the meal I had the night before at Le Bernardin.

Every single dish I had was not only delicious and prepared perfectly but it was creative and inventive. Even better no matter how creative it was, the taste was always on point.

The four course I picked from the 16 words on the menu were 1. fluke 2. lobster 3.lamb 4.chocolate

Before I even got to the first course there was a small bread course, an amuse bouche and a small dish. 1. a small dish of fluffy tiny cheesy bread, 2. a tea cup of mushroom broth and a tiny brioche 3. a beet creme lolipop. Beets are my favorite veg after brussel spouts and the way they used the beets was so perfect.

Then came the courses!
1. fluke, it was fluke carpaccio with grapefruit gelee, cucumbers, fish roe. so many components but they all worked so well together

2. Lobster, this was an amazing dish and the most amazing part wasn't the lobster but how it worked with all the other ingredients. There was both a maistuake sabayon and a creme sauce and neither overpowered the lobster, there were some lightly pickled vegetables.

3. Lamb this was probably my least favorite dish and I still liked it. It was lamb two ways, one of which was confit. It was good not great. I am a lamb snob having probably eaten more lamb than beef in my life so I've eaten it almost every way possible.

4. Chocolate, it was chocolate three ways, sponge cake, ice cream and ganache cake. Le Bernardin had better desserts but this was still very very good.

Between course 2 & 3, they brought me their version of a tret egg. It was far more interesting than Le Bernardin's egg. It was a lovely savory custard.

Also before the dessert I got the EMP egg creme which was made even more charming by the cart table side service.

The meal ended with a trio of tiny pasties.

I also liked that they have a selection of non alcoholic cocktails.

I really liked the art deco style and the big open windows that have great views of the lovely park and historical buildings.

The only negative thing was that there was very long wait times between dishes. It was almost a full hour before I had my first course but I did have three mini course before that. If you are getting the 4 course prix fixe plan for a 2 hour meal and for the tasting menu even longer.

We chose this restaurant as both our anniversary dinner and final dinner as New Yorkers, and it was absolute perfection. Since the meal just got better and better as time went by, I'll just start from the end:

Our meal ended with a complimentary bottle of Cognac and petit fours in an intimate little cove at the corner of the dining room. Maybe a nice trick to increase table turnover, but it was nice to be able to just linger and ruminate on our wonderful dinner.

Before being escorted there, the general manager took us into what must be the coolest place in all of the city: the EMP kitchen. They say they invite about 20% of their guests to see the kitchen and have a special dessert made (with liquid nitro!) in front of them, and it made us feel like royalty.

Our server asked us if we would like to see the kitchen as she was serving us a Chinese tea - a $20-something splurge that we decided on since, hey, we were there and we love tea. And it was so unique and special. Our server brought over an entire cart with tea supplies, and gave us first, second and third tastings using the same tea leaves and helped us understand why they all tasted slightly different. It was enlightening and amazingly delicious!

These last three parts of our dinner - tea, a tour of the kitchen and Cognac - were so memorable, that they actually overshadowed the meal. Not that the meal was bad or unmemorable, but that the other parts were just that special. 

But I do want to say that the meal was stunning - both in flavor and presentation - and I love the new menu format. Another factor that made our meal so special was the service. The care and attention that they put into every aspect of the meal - from when you walk in until you leave - you'll really feel like the only person in the restaurant who ever mattered.

Now I see why this is THE place to go for a special occasion. This is a truly, truly great restaurant. This was one of the top two meals of my entire life.

Housed within the 1920's era Metropolitan Life North building Eleven Madison Park is at once sophisticated and classy. The high ceilings, art deco interior, and crisp white table linens convey an air that is grand and every bit contrived yet at the same time welcoming and comfortable. The latter due to the irreproachable customer service that is a signature of Danny Meyer's establishments. Often at fine dining establishments the service tend to be stiff, formal and aloof at best. Here at Eleven Madison Park though, each staff was friendly and approachable and it gave the restaurant a personality, so to speak, the kind that would encourage a guest to return. Daniel Humm, a native of Switzerland and a James Beard Award recipient has been the executive chef since 2006 and under his talented hand Eleven Madison Park earned four stars from the New York Times in 2009 and is currently ranked 24 on the S. Pellegrino World's 50 Best restaurants List.

The meal starts with several amuse-bouches, the tomato 'tea' with verbena bouquet being the most striking to the palate. Simply put there is nothing quite like it. Definitively savory in flavor yet decidedly tea in quality it set the stage for a most memorable meal. For the meal proper guests can choose the 4 course meal or the full tasting menu. Only the principal ingredient is listed on the menu card and guests select their own meal combinations without knowing how each course will be prepared. On a recent lunch, octopus was paired with potatoes and grapefruit for a light starter that was reminiscent of the Galician tapas pulpo al feira, complete with the beautifully executed plating. The lobster 'lasagna' for the second course was the best dish of the entire meal. Generous portions of lobster is layered with fresh sheets of pasta, served on rich lobster bisque with thin slices of summer squash, and finished off with squash blossoms and lobster oil. Every bite was bursting with flavor and indulgence. For the third course diners can opt to try the duck for two which is carved and plated table side and looks divine but the pork dish was also memorable. The pork loin contrasts well with the pork belly in both flavor and texture and the grilled apricot rounds up the dish nicely. Finally the dessert course. But wait, like most fine dining establishments you can expect a palate cleanser to precede dessert. But since Eleven Madison Park seeks to elevate your dining experience instead of the usual citrus sorbet diners are treated to a malted egg cream prepared table side. Watching the staff prepare this classic treat was admittedly the most delightful part of the meal. For dessert the chocolate plate was as decadent as expected. Rich chocolate, salted caramel ice cream, cocoa nib, perfect for chocoholics. Along with the petit fours comes an after dinner drink, in this instance a cognac that was wonderfully fragrant and pleasantly smooth. A perfect finish to a sumptuous meal.
I definitely questioned the Michelin guide for it's rating on Eleven Madison Park, but the newly released NYC 2012 guide upgraded the restaurant to 3 stars, and rightly so.  Congrats EMP!

You know it's a good sign when you haven't even gotten through the hors d'oeuvres and you feel like you've already had the best meal of your life.

Seriously, they need to serve a straw with every dish so that you can suck up every morsel and drop of sauce from every possible nook and cranny.  The flavour combinations were so nuanced and poignant that I cannot stop thinking about them.  Sea urchin cappuccino with green apple and crab? Outstanding.  

The show-stopping flavours were also littered with a prevailing sense of well coordinated playfulness.  Their take on the "clam bake" was part performance as hot water was poured over hot stones and seaweed, releasing the aroma of the sea as you enjoy a delightful series of preparations of clams and lobster.  However, it was really the deceptively smooth clam chowder that warmed inconspicuously on the hot stones that reminded us that the most simple thing can often be the most delicious.

Another highlight was the guinea fowl, which was hands-down one of the most tender preparations I have ever experienced.  Sous-vide'd and then roasted, each bite of butter-soft fowl made me almost forget that there was a superbly piece of seared foie waiting on the side.

But speaking of foie - the foie terrine was breathtaking.  The intense creaminess of the terrine was balanced beautifully by the sweet and crunch of the surrounding crisp:  I swear, I thought I almost shed a tear with each bite I took, realizing that it was only bringing me closer to the end of that dish.

But these are just a few of the highlights of the tasting menu, which was still full of other amazing dishes such as lobster lasagna, potato gnocchi, and goat cheese and beet lollipops, just to name a few.  The entire tasting menu was so beautifully crafted, I don't see how I could come back and not want to do it all over again.

What I would also be remiss if I failed to mention was also the amazing wine pairings.  Not only were we served the most amazing wines, but I loved how they also brought into play a great Belgian beer, the smoothest sake I have ever experienced, and an uber-lush glass of madeira wine.  And every single pairing?  Fantastic.

What more can I say?  The one thought that did come to mind was "how does this compare to Per Se?"  One one hand, the presentations and portions did not feel as "grand" as Per Se, and you do not get completely flooded with as many sweets and chocolates at the end of the meal.  But I felt that the flavours and execution were absolutely on par, the service was just as spectacular, and there were certainly moments of brilliance in their food when I thought they convincingly out shone their more expensive counter part.

But I do not want to take away from EMP with comparisons.  It is an absolutely outstanding restaurant, a dining experience that you will not easily forget and will want to re-live soon, and soon again.  And yes, I'm pretty stoked that EMP got to be my 200th review!

Amazing restaurants in one of the best spaces in NYC!

Tasting menu is excellent with an great wine or the wine pairing menu.  Constantly changing menu that has never disappointed over the years.  Roast duck is out of this world!
The most inspired meal i've ever had in my life. Impeccable service. Words don't do this place justice.
Not a big fan of the new menu -- the old way was great especially the chocolate soufflé

Surprise!

They are prepared to surprise you!

Few of friends wanted to have my late birthday dinner here several weeks back. I had a wonderful time.

They prepared hand-written birthday card on the table with my name on it.
They gave me dried-fruit box for me to take home.

Menu: They have one page white paper that has main ingredient list without any explanation as purpose. For example, it is indicated as lamb, lobster, beets..etc. You are supposed to choose the ingredient that you like and everything is up to your imagination and chef.

Service: Top notch!

Food: Since the ambience and service are great, I feel the food tastes better as well! 

In between appetizer and entrée, there were so many complimentary dishes.

Tomato soup came out like tea - on mini cup with herbs. Very smart presentation!

I loved "frozen goat cheese that was covered by beets power" that looks like lollipop on the grass. Another smart presentation.

We shared whole duck for the table. Presentation was unique as they brought the whole duck in a separate mini-table and cut for us in front of us. The duck was from west coast as the chef think west coast duck are leaner than east coast...haha...I thought that comment was funny.

After dessert, they also brought mini cookie dish.

They gave complimentary granola glass jar to take home. I had it for next two weeks in the morning...I never had that fresh/crunch granola in my life.

Three course meal was around $125.  Definitely worth it to celebrate your special occasion.

I can't wait to go there again!

This review is from a meal from 2009 so obviously things have changed since then.  However, I wasn't posting reviews at that point so I thought I'd share my comments now.  It's a break out of all dishes I had during my tasting menu experience.

-Sweetbread and chive mixture fried in an adorable little baby triangle pouch and tied with a chive ribbon (LOVED THIS.......SO.........MUCH...........wanted more, so cute too - flavor explosion)
-5 different amuse bouches (lovely presentation) - marshmallow with beet powder (alright), parmesan crisp around some sort of mousse (quite tasty altho slightly over salted), tuna tartare nested between 2 radishes I think (good quality tuna, overall just okay to me), seafood egg tart (pretty good not earth shattering), and foie gras with cranberry (too tart, too much pucker)
-Potato ro-something or other, I can say it but I cannot spell it, it's a round potato puff thing surrounded by corn soup, they served the soup tableside which I love and also they had lovely corn nestled in the soup and it looked like it had been freeze dried or something similar to that process (this was delicious and fresh and bursting with corn flavor, I started to become excited)
-Bread: Italian mini and then an olive bread served with unsalted cow's milk butter, salted goat's milk butter and fleur de sel (olive bread was fine but the goat's milk butter and fleur de sel I quite enjoyed)
 
Appetizer
-Farm egg with farrow, frogs' legs, truffles (OMfG-note the little f.  So tasty and pretty substantial in size.  Great truffle flavor, egg was perfectly cooked, great build on the corn soup).  My sister had the Hawaiian shrimp which they served almost like sushi with the avocado wrapped around it.  It was tasty but mine was better.
 
Main
-Suckling pig with little baby sweet potatoes (This was amazing quality pork, I took one bite and could taste that it was just amazingly fresh and high quality.  They served it as 2 pieces of pork.  One was a perfect round little fillet which was juicy and succulent and the middle tasted vaguely of bacon - swoon.  The other was a square of roasted pork with the crispy skin on top - reminded me of the suckling pig I had as a child for Chinese engagement parties.  The skin was crispy and amazing.  I loved that piece a bit more than the other although quality was very evident in the other.)  My sister had the lamb and she said it was the best lamb she ever had in her entire life.  It was very tasty altho somewhat fatty but incredibly moist.  The presentation was beyond darling for her dish.  They placed the lamb beside a pearl onion, tiny zucchini, tiny tomato and then stuffed each vegetable with a tiny piece of sausage and then put the vegetable "lid" back on the top.  It was one of the most adorable things I had ever seen in my life.
 
Dessert
-I had the chocolate and peanut butter palate with popcorn ice cream (I was disappointed by this.  It was basically a very fancy chocolate bar with the tiniest little prob 24k gold leaf imprinted on it with one piece of caramel popcorn and a very small mound of popcorn ice cream.  There was a dark chocolate ribbon over the top of the whole thing.  I liked the popcorn ice cream but there was hardly any of it and it started to melt quite quickly and I didn't care for the chocolate bar.  And I never have fancied myself a gold eater.)  My sister had the blueberry corn cake thing which was very good because those flavors mesh together so well and her accompanying sorbet was very clean and tart and refreshing.
 
-Tiny little sandwich cookies - we were allowed 2 each.  I had the rose and violet ones.  They were interesting - the violet one reminded me of earl gray tea, the rose one was boring to me.
-Jelly candies to take home the next day.  Stylish sliding box presentation.  4 different flavors - tasted like intense, high quality Sunkist fruit gems.

This restaurant goes way beyond 5 stars. 

My husband and I came here for dinner and food was fantastic!

Service was just as amazing! Our server was very friendly and helped us pick a delightful meal and the perfect wine to go with it. I was also extremely amazed to witness how the servers seem to be trained to move in a certain manner and in a certain direction (like a carousel so they don't bump into each other when carrying food/beverages).

The place is very classy and beautifully designed. I especially love the high ceiling.

Definitely worth the money.

I'm not going to add anything new to this party.  This was hands down the best meal I've ever had.  Went there for lunch and got a three course tasting.  The total bill with drinks and tip included was about $260.  Here is a run down of what I got and would highly recommend it all, but the standout for me was the pork belly from my pork dish.  It was uncomfortably good meaning that it brought me to a new level of taste and I never wanted it to end...THAT good.  some might describe the skin as crack.

If I could, I would give this restaurant 10 stars out of 5. It has taken me over half a year to finally write this review --because each and every time I have sat down to gather my thoughts, no series of words could ever seem to capture the amazing meal I experienced at Eleven Madison Park!

The boyfriend and I were visiting NYC for New Years and were looking for the ultimate NYE in NYC dinner. We Yelp searched New American, Highest Rated, and as a result, booked a reservation for Eleven Madison's prefixed dinner, first seating at 5:30pm.

I must note, having gone for New Years Eve, I don't think we had the normal Eleven Madison dinner, but I can still speak regarding this amazing restaurant which I qualify as my most favorite dining experience to date!

Our meal consisted of the following:
-Gourgeres
-Goat cheese lollipops & beet infused marshmellows 
-Toast pieces with caviar & fish mousse
-Bread with goats milk butter & cows milk butter
-Chestnut veloute with sweetbreads and white truffles
-Foie Gras Terrine with golden pineapple and pickled pearl onions
-Nova Scotia lobster, poached with leeks and black truffles
-Duck, glazed with turnip and kumquat (MY FAVORITE DISH --rich and flavorful, but not over done at all!)
-Milk & Chocolate, dehydrated chocolate mousse and dulce de leche

Simply put, this restaurant is AMAZING, in every sense of the word. What I can say from my experience is that the chef of this restaurant seems to truly understand FOOD, not just as a science --but as an art! Not only was each dish cooked to perfection, flavors and textures of the ingredients complementing each other with every bite --but the menu itself is creative to the max and beautifully plated to create an experience for all the senses, most especially and importantly, the palette! 

If it could get any better, the service was superb from the moment we walked in the door. The restaurant, beautiful and serene to complete the package. No doubt, I at the most expensive meal I've ever had in my life at Eleven Madison Park, but my boyfriend and I both agree.. it was worth every penny.

I decided to go with the full tasting menu, which doesn't list any of the dishes to be served that night but instead lists ingredients that may be used. There were quite a few canapes served in addition to each course. Each item served was beautifully created and the creativity of each design stands out amongst all the different restaurants I've been to, but unfortunately none of the dishes actually tasted very unique or really had that wow factor on my taste buds. The service was excellent. Expect 3hrs+ for the full tasting menu. 

Ingredients/dishes served (might be missing a few): 

Tomato soup - blah 
Clam shell with small chopped scallop - blah 
Sea urchin soup with sea urchin, sea urchin foam - decent but only had one sea urchin 
Gnocchi - blah
Prawns - blah 
Lobster - good
Veal - decent
Drink - seltzer, vanilla (this might have been the highlight of my night) 
Gianduja ice cream with chocolate desserts
Petit fours

I have heard so many glowing reviews of Eleven Madision Park from foodie friends that I had to make a reservation which was no easy since it took me 6 weeks to find a Friday night table for 2. The staff at Eleven Madision Park are very hospitable and friendly upon entering the restaurant but to the point of appearing sickeningly fake with their strained smiles. 

I had the Foie Gras(really good), Lobster(tiny piece), Beet(yes, I got this for my meat course because I thought it read Beef) and Plum(horrible, it was too tart and tasted like flowers). I was extremely disappointed with my dinner especially since it cost me $200. Why would Eleven Madison Park offer BEET as one of their meat options??? I mean even if there was a bone marrow component I only saw 2 tiny pieces of bone marrow about the size of a peanut M&M on my plate. The so called "freebies" were not impressive either. Everything tasted too tart and flowery. There also seem to be plum on many of the dishes that night which was not a good think since it was so sour. 

I also felt like a second class citizen since I didn't get the Chef's Tasting or wine pairings. When I told the sommelier that I just wanted to get a glass of wine and a cocktail that was the last I saw of him that evening. Seriously??? NEVER AGAIN. Off to Per Se!

Note to restaurant:
Please don't treat diners differently if they order the 4-course dinner vs. the Chef's Tasting and wine pairings. Not everyone drinks and can stomach 8-courses of food. It felt awful to see the obvious difference in treatment among tables.
By far one of the best restaurants I have dined with.. The service is amazing, the food a ten and the wine selection perfect!! I will be back this weekend.. Very unique dining experience.

Next to Le Bernardin, the best restaurant in NYC. 
We went with the four course dinner rather than the 7 course tasting menu.  

First off, the restaurant made a point to ask of any dietary issues.  When told one of the diners had allergies and/or aversions to all fish and the other diner was allergic to peppers and hated coconut and anise flavor, they were more than happy to accommodate. This is where they excel.  Their focus on the customer's preferences as priority over a chef's potential need to stubbornly present a preconceived dish with these "forbidden" ingredients was obvious and appreciated.  

The four course dinner menu is widely creative in the way it is presented and created.  As a result, customers who order the same things may wind up with different meals. To understand this, you need to understand their menu. I'll try to explain as best i can:  The menu contains nothing but 16 squares.  The squares are presented in a 4x4 grid.  Each square represents a main ingredient.  The customer is directed to pick one ingredient square from each row of 4 squares.  The first row of squares represents the first course, the second row the 2nd course and so on.  So I ordered fois gras from the first row  as did my guest.  I ordered lobster from the second row and my guest ordered artichoke from that  row.  I ordered pork from the 3rd row and my guest ordered lamb. We both opted to pick chocolate from the last row.  As we each ordered, we were asked more and more questions so the kitchen could get a sense of what we would like.  This was illustrated in our first course.  I prefer warm fois gras while my friend was into a cold version.  When they were brought to our table, each were completely different preparations.  Her cold one was a terrine and mine was seared with a sauce.  To be blunt....Holy crap they were both amazing.  As were all the subsequent courses.  The key is the grid menu does not describe anything about the course.  It allows the chefs to "do their thing" and let their creative juices flow.  Again, amazing and unique experience.  I highly recommend this for anyone who is remotely serious about food and a willingness to try new things. Don't get me wrong... I'd bet the kitchen would accommodated the most boring eater, but then why shell out the big bucks (but worth it) for the meal? I guess I am saying that at a minimum cost of 125.00 a head without drinks, tip or taxes, this isn't a place to bring someone who only eats steak or salmon with no sauce.  However, I will say this would be amazing for a vegetarian since they are so willing to customize their dishes AND offer a vegetarian option on each row of the menu.    

Service:   The lead server and our sommelier were just phenomenal.   The other wait staff were just as topnotch.  They worked together like a well-oiled machine.  The service was perfection.  Wine parings were second to none.  I cannot say enough how important it is that anyone who loves rich and exciting food needs to hit Eleven Madison Park.  Even if you just venture into the bar to observe the awe-inspiring setting, it would probably be a memorable experience.

We opted for the 4 course menu on this night and we were very pleased.
 There is4X4 grid with 1 ingredient listed. You chose 1 item from each of the 4 lines.
 I chose Octopus, Loup de Mer (Sea bass), Pork & chocolate. Everything was not only beautifully presented but also was a fantastic representation of the singular ingredient chosen. 
 What really sets this restaurant apart was the onslaught of amuse bouche's, the super friendly & professional  service and the jar of granola our server gave us. 
 Not necessary to order the 7 course tasting menu here, we felt the 4 course was plentiful and a great value at $125 pp.

Our experience a year ago was fantastic (pork tasting menu and no wine paring). 

This year - not so much. 

Well, probably 5.30PM reservation was a mistake on my part - this gave11 Madison an opportunity to rush us through the courses and dump us (after a visit to the kitchen - cute) into a exit/waiting area where we were presented with some pastries and some water I think. Rushing through $500 dinner is not acceptable. 

Our waiter made some 'special' cream soda for us - not tasty at all, we could not finish it. Why do it?

During our visit to the kitchen, one of the girls in there made us another drink that was disgusting. Why do it?

The food was not memorable this time. 

Have to give 11 Madison one star this time.

They had us at the scallop amuse bouche!

My favorite was the most lovely tomato soup and the four course dinner for $125 was worth every penny.

Especially loved the little extra "bonuses" between meals. The service was professional, as you would expect in any restaurant of this calibur, with nice personal touches.

This was my third time here and not the last.

"The Best Restaurant In New York City"

My wife and I just returned from New York City where we went to celebrate our anniversary. This was our 5th visit since 2005 and we spare no expense from staying in a Central Park view suite at the Ritz to eating at the absolutely the best restaurants we can find. To add to our enjoyment this year, our friends from Toronto, who operate a gourmet food club there, flew down to join us.

On this trip we had just three nights to eat out, so we chose Daniel and Eleven Madison Park (EMP) as our two "top-flight" restaurants. We all agreed that EMP was head and shoulders above Daniel. 

At Daniel we all selected the six-course tasting menu, which gave the option of picking one of two items at each of the six courses. We also chose to have wines paired with these selections. So at any given course during the night, two of us had one of the choices, while the remaining two had a different choice. Yet in each case, the wine for the table was the same. We felt that the two different items at each course did not pair equally well with the wine selected.

Meanwhile, at EMP, you are given a menu with 16 items on it, but with just a one word description like "potato." A diner can choose any four and then either let the chef go wild, or suggest some things you would like to see (or not like to see). At each course, we all received a different wine with the wine pairing. To us, it seemed like Daniel was going through the motions and had us on an assembly line, while at EMP we felt we were the only diners there (which was totally untrue - the place was packed, including a wedding party of dozens upstairs).

At Daniel, our friend purchased a cookbook by Mr. Boulud and asked to have it signed. After receiving a few excuses, we were told he was out of town until September 11. Meanwhile, at EMP, chef Daniel Humm, who was named best chef in NYC in 2010 by the James Beard Foundation, came to our table and asked us if we were enjoying ourselves. 

At the end of our meal, manager Daniel Green asked us if we would like to see the kitchen. We have had this happen before, and we always enjoy it. What has never happened before was to have dessert prepared for us while we watched. While this was going on, we got to see how well-ordered and precise the kitchen's operation was. Considering that they are making almost every order to an individual specification, it has to be.

The attention to detail is amazing. They even press the tablecloths after one seating.

All things considered, this was one of the best meals of my life, and like I've said, my wife and I have eaten at some of the very best restaurants on the planet. And eating here the night after Daniel was eye-opening. Both meals ended up with eight items and both had wine pairings, but not only was EMP considerably better in our opinion, it was about 33% less expensive.

EMP is unique, and well worth a visit if you are looking for an incredible dining experience!

Visited September 2011

The only thing I could ever, possibly review negatively here is the hole in my pocket I see while walking out. Everything single other inch of this restaurant has been painstakingly thought out, considered and created to please their guests.

I only went for lunch and I can hardly imagine what a fabulous fancy date spot or impressive celebratory destination this would make. The menu is constantly changing and being updated but everything I had was delicious - so that's what counts. Dress to impress and bring your appetite.

11 Madison came very highly recommended by a friend that also brought us to Robuchon in Vegas.  Similar restaurants in a sense that their service is top notch and they offer an extensive tasting menu.
We LOVED Robuchon; maybe it was the limo that picked us up, the awesome breadcart that offered limitless carbs, the fantastic imaginative dishes or our very friendly host...
We were expecting much the same from 11 Madison minus the limo.  But honestly the food was forgettable except the fact that I'm allergic to apples and every course had apples!!  They did ask me what I was allergic to in the beginning of the meal but didn't think that my husband would have to run out to get me allergy medicine in the middle of the meal.  But I do have to say that the service is very good and it should be for what you're paying.
Don't think I'll ever go again...

If I knew I was going to die tomorrow - I would want Eleven Madison Park to be my last meal.

I've eaten two of the best meals of my life here and I make it a point to plan my New York trip around my EMP reservation.  To me, walking into EMP during the day is like walking into Heaven itself - high ceilings and soft-white light  beaming through the curtains.

The menu changes and I've never had a bad dish here.  I will say that their execution when it comes to seafood is flawless and beyond what I've eaten at top restaurants elsewhere.

My two cents:  The whole duck is amazing and a must try.  Order a Pimm's cup (or two) and enjoy one of the best meals you will ever have.

After having eaten both dinner and lunch there over the past year or so, I can't say that I am in love with the restaurant, but I can't deny that I have had some incredible dishes either. At times, I felt the service, though well-intentioned, to be a tad overbearing. But the one thing I am still searching for is the identity of the cuisine. There are flashes of brilliance, but as Samuel Jackson's character Jules famously asserted in Pulp Fiction, personality goes a long way.The second comingI first visited Eleven Madison Park last summer for dinner. I was very excited about the restaurant as many critics and bloggers seemed to agree that its Swiss chef Daniel Humm and his team had really begun to hit their stride. We had a very pleasant dinner, but only a few things remain engrained in my mind over a year later: the unbelievable roast duck with lavender glazing that was presented whole and then carved up by the side of our table, and the uncanny knack of the front of house staff to anticipate our every need and desire in a casual and subtle fashion. Everything else is a little bit blurry, no doubt in part due to some of the excellent wine that we consumed that night.Earlier this summer, I had the opportunity to return for a rare leisurely weekday lunch with a friend of mine who was visiting from overseas. We were both curious to see how this New York Times 4-star and Michelin 1-star restaurant (not to mention #24 on the most recent World's 50 Best list) would live up to our expectations, and I was personally curious to hear my friend's own views given his considerable culinary background and talent.At my first meal, there had been a traditional structure to the menu, but this changed in September of 2010. Now, for every course, the diner chooses the main ingredient for each dish, and the kitchen then constructs a dish around the selected core element, taking into account the diner's personal preferences and/or any allergies.
