I never asked, but would be curious to know how this works logistically in the kitchen as they presumably only have so many iterations or frameworks for each ingredient thought out, tried and tested ahead of time for each star ingredient.Although four courses (plus all of the extras) would probably have been more than sufficient, we opted to go for an unadvertised tasting menu (well, it is mentioned on their website, but it wasn't visible on our lunch menu). In the end, this turned out to be a mistake as it didn't equate to good value for money given that we spent nearly 70% more for what amounted to be only two extra courses.Things were Humming alongIt is suffice to say that the opening progression of small bites and dishes was fun, well-balanced and impressive.I remembered that I had been quite taken with the Champagne I sampled on my prior visit, and luckily they still had it on menu by the glass. The delicate grower-produced blanc de blancs (meaning from Chardonnay grapes only) Champagne was perfect with the meal's preamble.The golden, plump gougères were made from an excellent choux pastry and had just the right amount of cheese so as to be present and pleasant, without overshadowing the light dough. 8/10.A chilled, sweet pea soup was accented by some even cooler milky 'snow', with a crispy ham cracker lending crunch and saltiness. The combination worked well and was also artfully presented. 7/10.Besides being colorful and playful, the goat cheese lollipops were also downright delectable. The beet coating not only added vivacity to the presentation but also lent a subtle flavor which melded well with the cheese. 8/10.The little blonde spheres of (fried) bread and (goat) cheese were also delicious, with the rich flavor and saltiness of the cheese being offset by the watercress in the light emerald dipping sauce. 7/10.Two types of butter were served for the meal, one from a cow (left) and one from a goat (right)  both elegantly presented and quite delicious.The bread was freshly baked and of very high quality, with a lovely crispy crust. The presentation  they arrived in a little taupe-tinged blanket  reminded me of the way the 'snacks' are served at noma. 7/10 (I wish there had been a variety of breads offered).Smoked Sturgeon Sabayon with Chives:The saboyon was heaven in a hollowed out eggshell: luxuriously smooth, smoky, creamy, with a touch of acidity and perfectly seasoned. I wanted three more three-quarter filled eggshells full of it. 10/10.LETTUCE: Salad with Almonds, Mangalista Ham & Cucumber:The first of the 'real' courses was a wide assortment of lettuce seemingly randomly arranged and interspersed with two slices of excellent ham, moist almonds and edible flowers. I wasn't expecting too much; however, once I began

I had lunch here the day after the hurricane.  The service is attentive and friendly.  The food is wonderful.  There are some fun surprises here like the tableside egg cream.  I loved the tomato tea and the sturgeon amuse bouche.  I liked having female waiters and female sommelier.

This restaurant dinner was like nothing I've ever experienced. For 3 hours we received superb attention and delicious food - if you're looking to celebrate a special occasion in NYC - this place is it! The menu is a bit unusual, you're given a piece of paper with 16 ingredients listed. From those 16 ingredients, you choose 4 (appetizer, main, side, dessert) and then the chef creates special dishes just for you. You can also say what you like (i.e. spicy) and don't like (i.e. eggplant). Everything was super seasonal and delicious. We also had the wine pairing - pours were generous and they left a bottle of cognac on the table for us to enjoy post-dinner. Quite possibly the best (and fanciest!) dinner of my life. 

Bonus - they sent us home with a homemade chocolate bar and a jar of their granola!

All I can say is "WOW"!  The best meal I have had in NYC and in my top ten in my life! It is beyond words!  If you want a very special evening, with that special someone, this is the place. You will need to plan ahead, as they book out weeks to a month in advance. I'm still savoring the experience.

Hands down the best meal I've had in NYC to date! 

My girlfriend and I share a birthday so we like to go somewhere extra special each year to celebrate. This year she chose EMP and it was definitely a memorable one! 

I made the reservation approx. one month in advance, and called about a week out to inform the staff that it was a special occasion. 

We were seated at a nice table with the chairs set up right next to each other on one side of the table, facing out towards the dining room. It's amazing how small and intimate they are able to make such a big room feel. We both had the tasting menu (how could you not?) and left the choices up to the chef. We opted to split the wine pairing (read: she had about five sips total). The menu went as follows: 

PEA - chilled soup with buttermilk snow and mint crisp 

FLUKE AND SCALLOP - basil and meyer lemon; ceviche with tangerine 

GOAT CHEESE - lollipop with beets and croquettes with watercress vinaigrette 

SEA URCHIN - cappuccino with crab and apple 

SMOKED STURGEON AND CAVIAR - sabayon with chive; fingerling potato and creme fraiche 

FOIE GRAS - terrine with strawberry jam 

SCALLOP - seared with crayfish, smoked potato and garlic 

BROCCOLI - variations with parmesan, lemon and lardo 

EGG PLANT - roasted with bulgur wheat, wild herbs and licorice 

LAMB - roasted with summer beans, savory and violet mustard 

EGG CREAM - malt, vanilla and olive oil 

CHOCOLATE - cannelloni with espresso, caramel and yogurt 

MIGNARDISES 

Everything was totally on point! My favorites were the PEA, SMOKED STURGEON, BROCCOLI and the EGGPLANT. 

After dessert we put in our coffee order and the manager (I believe his name was Daniel) came over and offered to give us a tour of the kitchen...OF COURSE! He then escorted us to the kitchen where we were introduced to several members of the staff, I don't remember any of their names because I was pretty shitfaced from the wine pairing, which consisted of a glass of champagne, a glass of sake and seven glasses of wine! In the kitchen one of the chefs prepared an "edible cocktail" for us with brandy, liquid nitrogen and some other redish, purpleish stuff (again, things were pretty fuzzy). 

After our cocktail we were escorted to a lounge area in the front and seated at a table with a bottle of cognac and instructed to drink as much as we pleased...I'd like to say I drank the whole bottle like a man, but I was already pretty full and pretty drunk, I think I had two fingers worth. A waiter came by with a cart and prepared our chemex coffee table side, which I had almost forgotten I ordered, and was cool enough to let me pick his brain about the process since I would like to tackle it myself.

Upon leaving we were given a mason jar of the best granola I've ever had.  For real, it was awesome! I was so bummed when we ran out. We keep joking about how we're going to go back one of these days for another $750 jar of granola...it's not really a joke, we're totally going back!
Everything about this place is fantastic, starting with the room itself.  It is huge, and done in a very classic New York style.  The food was delicious, and the staff was courteous and attentive.

My favorite restaurant in NYC.

Shed a tear then they nixed their $28 lunch prix-fixe.

This is the best restaurant I have ever eaten at.

Everything about 11 Madison is impeccable. Their menu allows for the diner to chose between 16 main ingredients for a four course prix fixe, with each course highlighting a selection.

Their wine list is a thick as a dictionary and is presented to you by a world class sommelier. 

The meal begins with an amuse-bouche, followed by warm breads accompanied with a selection of butters. Each course is presented by a different staff member from the kitchen and is as beautiful plated as is on the tongue. Each course is punctuated by a palate cleansing morsel. I had rabbit terrine with rainier cherries , followed by sea scallop ceviche, ricotta gnocchi, the most delicate and delicious steak with legumes, beet and goat cheese lollipops, and a plate of truffles and caramel custard. Our meal was finished with a malt and vanilla bean egg cream. Then the general manager invited us into the kitchen. 

They run a french kitchen with pastry, broilers, and salad stations in well defined areas around a huge central refrigeration room. The table tops are topped with pristine white linens and there are dozens of cooks managed by their head sous chef. Here they served us nitrogen frozen Manhattans with house made brandied cherries and allowed us to watch them work for a bit. We were then ushered to a table in the bar to drink from a bottle of small batch armagnac and eat petit fours to our content.

This is a four hour dinner and is about $200 per person with modest wine.

5-star cuisine, ruined by truly disappointing service.

We walked into Eleven Madison Park right on time for our dinner reservation and were greeted by name at the door--"Welcome to Eleven Madison Park!" And then the hostess walked away without saying another word. We were left standing awkwardly in the doorway, unsure of what to do or where to go. Unfortunately, the awkward feeling that we didn't quite belong continued throughout our meal--and only got worse as the night went on.

I don't want to assume that it's an age thing, but it was obvious that at 30 you will be the youngest person here by at least a decade. We were dressed very nicely, ordered champagne upon being seated, and tried to engage the staff with friendly questions and comments. But in the end we were treated dismissively by nearly all staff. We were presented with the standard menu and never even informed that a tasting menu was an option. Questions about the menu got blunt, semi-rude answers. Could you tell me a little more about the hot and cold foie gras preparations? "One is seared and served warm; the other is a cold terrine. So are you ready to order?" Thanks for the insight. We didn't know what to think, as EMP has such a reputation for outstanding service. Did we do something wrong?

The experience went from bad to worse when the wine service started. We opted to do wine pairings instead of ordering a bottle. The server informed us that the sommelier would be by shortly to discuss our wine likes/dislikes and what would be paired with the food. This never happened. Someone came by a minute later with glasses of sake, apparently to accompany the various amuse bouches. Unexpected but okay. Then someone brought out a particular Sauvignon Blanc that we were sure we did not like. We politely asked them to bring something else, and if we could please speak to the sommelier to discuss our pairings as they had indicated. Apparently we HAD done something wrong, by voicing any concerns regardless of how we expressed them. They insisted that we try the wine they had brought, and were shocked when we confirmed that we did not particularly enjoy it. We finally spoke with the sommelier, who treated us like morons and suggested that we just didn't understand the subtlety of European wine. For the rest of the meal, two people came by with each glass of wine to try to sell us on it, like we were difficult children being coaxed into eating their vegetables. They were surprised whenever we liked something, literally exclaiming "wow!" when we accepted it. Apparently we had been labeled the "difficult" table. The condescension was so strong that we considered walking out at one point during the meal. All of this for disliking one glass of wine!

The funny thing was that we really enjoyed nearly all of the wine and food. Clearly the kitchen staff is talented and deserves plenty of credit. The only person who was happy to talk to us all night was the guy who came from the kitchen to bring each amuse bouche. He was entertaining and knowledgeable- the waiters could learn a thing or two from the kitchen. The amuse bouches were all unique and delicious. The chevre and apple desserts were both disappointing, but each savory course was original, artful and full of flavor.

In the end, regardless of how good the food might have been, the attitudes of the front of house staff were so poor that the entire experience was tainted. We watched other tables having lively conversations with their servers, asking questions and getting detailed responses about the food. Our servers dropped off plates of food and walked away without any explanation. When our egg cream was being made we asked what he was pouring-- he said "uh, it's milk" and set the glasses down. Nice dialogue! When we finished our desserts they dropped off the bill and one jar of granola for the two of us (the four-top next to us received four jars). No petit fours, no offers for after-dinner drinks. No "goodbye" or "thanks for coming" on the way out the door. I've never been so disappointed by a restaurant.

Maybe we set our sights too high by eating at Jean Georges shortly before visiting Eleven Madison Park. My understanding was that the two restaurants were in the same ballpark. I would say Eleven Madison Park has a long way to go.
tomato tea, black bass, lobster, and berry as desert. everything was just perfect. besides, it was in sex and the city, which added extra points. cant wait to go back again!:)

We were able to try this restaurant courtesy of my favorite art dealer.  We had the full tasting menu.  The restaurant is located in a fabulous renovated room that looks like an old bank branch (not sure).  There is balcony seating as well.  We had the full tasting menu.  Each dish was superbly executed.  Of the courses, fully 2/3 were outstanding and 1/3 simply very good.  Service was impeccable and approachable.  After the meal, we were taken back for a kitchen tour and the staff proceeded to create a frozen dessert for us.  We left even with a souvenior of housemade granola flakes in a nice jar.  My only negative comment and of course it shouldn't stop any of you is that the full tasting menu is alot of food.  If you are not starving or a big eater go with ala carte.  As we rarely get to New York these days, we had to go big.  I'm a big fan of Eleven Madison and this restaurant definitely competes with the other top Manhattan restaurants.

This is now the best place in New York
To find pleasure attached to a fork. 
My well-priced prix fixe
Left me raving for weeks:
Perfect service, pace, food--oh, the pork!

I had a lovely duck here, and the wine wasn't bad.  But this place could benefit from some transparency.  Just tell people how their main ingredient is going to be prepared.  I ordered the pistachio dessert, but SURPRISE! there were pistachios in at least two of the other courses as well.  I had some strange rabbit pate, which didn't delight and could have been avoided had I known that the "rabbit" would be unrecognizable and gross.  Also, they offered us a tour of the kitchen in the middle of dinner.  We declined, and they soon followed with a little snack because our next course was taking so long.  I appreciated the courtesy but thought the tour attempt was ill timed.  Also, the "friendliness" is a little strange.  It seems forced and conjures Mormonism.
Came here for lunch. Wonderful creative food, great plating/presentation that doesn't sacrifice portion size, and impeccable service.

A fitting place for my 550th review.  This place is among the best in the city.  Even though my braised squid dish wasn't one of my favorites, the chicken dish here is simply fantastic.  

The chicken main course here is a slice of roasted chicken breast with chicken jus (perfectly roasted, juicy, flavorful).  It is paired with a side of chicken fricassee made from the dark meat of the chicken.  The chicken here will likely change the way you eat chicken, as it is the best tasting chicken I have ever had.

Other dishes were also fantastic.  Service is top-notch.  They will also accommodate any food allergies or foods that you don't like.

Eleven Madison Park is one of the best NY fine dining experiences I've had.  I liked it better than Jean-Georges (flagship) and enjoyed similarly to my experience at Daniel.

The food was fresh and fantastic.  Excellent preparations, creative without being obnoxious.  Good portion size.  My vegetable course (broccoli) was possibly (or impossibly) the highlight of the meal - just surprisingly delicious.  Service was spot on.  Loved the beer selection that accompanied a good wine selection.

Ambience was good (if not the most New York-ish).  Actually, it's refreshing to eat in a place where you have comfortable seats and space around you as a nice change of pace from the squeezed-in seats prevalent in the city.

I don't normally care much about returning to the high-end NYC institutions, mostly because I like variety and there are so many to experience.  But in this case I'm sure I'll be back.

Cant wait to go back to eat it again! 

Fantastic - Foie gras, Lobster, chilled pea soup, poached salmon
Excellent - Sea Bass, Octopus
Good - Pork, Chocolate
Like everyone else we had the tasting menu. It was delicious. And the service was great. The atmophere was so cozy and romantic, just have to give five stars for this place.

The food and service was truly impeccable.  A little piece of heaven!  We got the 4 course tasting menu and legit had 10 different dishes.  I was just blown away with all the surprises dishes and each one tasted incredible.

I would highly go back here again!  And for a fixed menu, it didn't really break the bank.

Yesterday we had a reservation for Aldea(1 michelin star) for lunch but we were walking there and all the sudden Eleven Madison Park call and told me they have a opening right now so I cancel on Aldea and came to Eleven Madison Park instead. This is the TOP restaurant in NYC that I been wanted to try but never had enough time because of work. Anyway we walked there and got seated right away. We look over the menu and decided on the 3 course prix menu ($56) w/wine pairing for additional $48 which wasn't bad plus how many chance to I get to eat here. We were talking about getting champagne to start off w/ but decided not to go to far but all the sudden a Jeff(wine) came up to us and pour us a complimenty glass of champange because they knew we wanted it. What service is that!!!!! Anyway we got on talking w/Jeff and I asked if Abram(executive sous chef) is working because he graduate from my culinary school 10 yrs ago. Anyway after talking w/Jeff, he found out I work at Park Ave and etc and all the sudden we got VIP treatment, got to tour of the kitchen and they made us a liquid nitrogen manhattan, more alcohal, etc Also got to meet Daniel Humm(executive chef) and the executive Sous Chef Abram which was a GREAT guy. Far from everything that we got, the food was delicious. We started out w/2 amuse(pea soup & sabayon eggs) which was refreshing and then we started our 3 course meals. I let my friend had the 1 choice of everything and she got the Foie Gras, Lobster and the chocolate for dessert. I choose the octopus, halibut and the cherry for dessert. The first course was the best for me because the Foie Gras was to die for and the braisied octopus is soo tender but has a spring to it. The look wise of of the plate was gorgerous and I think I will copy the octopus plate when I get a chance. Next came the lobster and the halibut. The lobster was barely cook which i LOVE, i hate eating over cook lobster. The halibut was nice but nothing compare to the lobster. The dessert was good but it couldn't over shine the other 2 courses. Overall one of the BEST experience that I had in NYC so far and I think I will be coming back here soon when I can afford it. The eleven Madison staff were highly professional and now I know what to aim for because they made such a great impression on me and how food should be created. Thank you for everything!! You have just set the bar for me in NYC to a higher standard! :)

Wow! I felt like a child at a playground! Loved the creativity of both the menu and the food. Choosing the ingredients only was fun and reminds you that sometimes you should just leave the decisions to the professionals, and it was definitely worth it! Dish after dish impressed both sight and taste, a true play on all of your senses. Such a great "experience" meal and I will most definitely return, I also hear the menu in the bar is excellent and I look foward to trying that.

One negative comment, although not enough to overshadow the food by any means! Requesting a good seat is key as we were seated at a table facing the entry doors with huge fire exit signs all the way across the wall haha! I know this seems like a strange comment and not normally one I would note but each time I looked up from my amazing meal I couldnt help but notice these huge exit signs which seemed so unwelcoming and odd...and when I am enjoying such a wonderful meal it I want the ambiance to match it! Service was friendly and informative. The gift of jar of granola was such a nice touch and a wonderful reminder to a truly amazing meal! It would be fun to have a print out of the dishes featured because now months later I couldnt repeat them if I tried!
I tried this restaurant during my first trip to NY.  It was amazing! I was nervous at first but the staff made us feel very welcome.  I enjoyed everything I sampled including the Cognac and granola.

Came here for a late lunch and ordered the 4 course prix fixe.  

Positives:
-attentive staff
-fairly good food

Negatives:
-I get the minimalist menu thing, but it would have been helpful if the server had explained the items better.  He did ask if I had any restrictions, but who would have known that my eggplant dish had licorice in it?  Who thinks to say "No dietary restrictions but please, if there's any licorice, leave it off."?  Really?  Also, I managed to pick the 3:4 menu items that were dressed with some sort of crunch.  No better way to describe it besides kibble.  Crispy bits, what have you.  I love a crispy bit, I really do.  Best part, sometimes.  But when it coats every meal, it becomes a bit tedious--even dog foody.  Yes, I said it.  I was kibbled out.  The server should have acknowledged the unfortunate trend in my selection and steered me in a different, less crunchy, direction.

-the courses were poorly timed.  Although our plates were cleared promptly, the next course took far too long.

-housekeeping: at around 3:45, the staff began replacing the linens and ironing them in the dining room.  Right next to us.  It was so distracting and, in my opinion, completely tacky.  I have never seen this before, but perhaps I'm rarely in dining rooms when the cobbler's elves come out?

Too many good places to visit to return, unfortunately.

Truly worth of 5.0 stars!!  An amazing New York establishment.

Came here for lunch on a Thurs afternoon which was no less than a 2.5 hour meal :)

The restaurant is situated across from Madison Park (duh) inside a beautiful metropolitan building.  From the minute I walked in, I knew I was in for great service!  The hostess was graceful enough to grab my shopping bags and umbrella to store away.  

Each dish has many components that when eaten together are just a great marriage of texture and flavor.  Very "food-forward" yet still very tasty.

My lunchmate was running late, so I spent time perusing the wine list when plop comes a small plate of warm grugeres!  Whats more amazing was when my friend arrives, they replaced the unfinished plate for a warm plate just for her!  So awesome.

For lunch, you can pick a 3 or 4 course meal and of course you can pick out of any of the 12 choices, 4 of which were desserts.  Meaning you can each a 4 course meal of desserts if you wished.  Such a smart and creative way to do a menu.  You pick according to the main component of the dish but you really don't know how the dish will be prepared, so a degree of spontaneity is required :)

Next came the amuse bouches - yes multiple.  A cold pea shoot soup which was very light, then a sabayon with chive oil presented in an eggshell OH DELICIOUS.  i could have had 10!  

The bread service was simple but perfect.  Warm multigrain with a choice of cows or goats milk butter.

For lunch, I went with:
- Foie gras:  essentially a torchon de foie which had a thin layer of strawberry gelee on top.  What a great flavor profile!  The sweet with the rich..  
- Lobster:  beautiful pieces of lobster in a shellfish tasting foam/sabayon with microgreens and baby carrots flanking.  very amazing.
- Veal:  my least favorite but still very satisfying and well executed.  perhaps it was a bit too gamey for my personal taste.

palate cleanser was an egg white whipped drink with poppy seeds and seltzer.  tasted like a liquid form of lemon poppy seed muffin

dessert was good, but not amazing.  very beautiful presentation of "chocolate" but just paled in comparison to the main courses.

service was OFF THE CHARTS.  2nd to only Per Se in my book in terms of PERFECTION.  they anticipate your next request, they are involved, but not intrusive.  Professional, yet warm.  

Bravo to such an amazing dining experience -- and it was just merely a lunch!  Deserve every accolade.

We wanted a memorable meal for our 35th anniversary and we were not disappointed. (Home for us is Saint Louis and we were in town for a conference) We trusted our luck to the chef's menu, which saved us the tough choice of guessing which ingredients to pick. Not only was the food amazing and beautifully presented, but the wait staff was remarkably efficient. We spent nearly 4 hours enjoying our meal, and the time just flew by. Even more remarkable, one of our party is a vegetarian and they didn't even blink. In fact, some of the dishes she was served may have been better than the meat courses--a crispy dried eggplant still has me guessing as to how they did it. I hope they are still around for our 40th anniversary, but we may not be able to wait that long....

staff is very friendly. greeted at the door very enthusiastically.  we didn't choose anything from the menu and let them bring out whatever they wanted.  amuse bouche comes out quickly but then there were very long lulls b/w courses. food is good but i wouldn't say terribly memorable.  flavoring tends on the acidic side.  is the bread bowl not bottomless?  the rolls come straight out of the oven and taste like pillsbury crescents.  we asked for another but they never came.  i think blue hill stone barns is the best meal and dining experience in NY area. we've been 5 times and all but one beats 11 mad.  (the bad one was a terrible tomato-heavy meal in september, with tomatoes in every bite for 2hrs--and we like tomatoes).

This was likely the best meal I've had outside of France!  The restaurant is not for the unadventurous - you choose only the central aspect of each dish (eg. Beef, chicken, fish, lobster, etc) and the rest of the dish is a surprise.  The foie gras with strawberry jelly was surprisingly amazing (wouldn't have chose if I'd known it was strawberry) as were all of my choices.  The lobster was fantastic, and the beef was some of the best I've ever tasted - a filet with a side of greens mixed with tongue.  Soft and succulent!

What topped it off was the service and extras offered.  Service was American style - they are highly staffed and very friendly.  There were constant amuse bouches offered, including a very nice Cognac at dessert (they leave the bottle!).

My only regret is that I didn't have time to try the tasting menu - I will next time!

This place is perfect. We got the tasting menu with the wine pairing. It's expensive but worth it. Food is beautifully presented, delicious and memorable.The service should serve as a blueprint for all top restaurants. Egg creams prepared at the table was a classy touch as was the kitchen tour. The chef even took the time from his very busy night to say hello. Great night.

I went for lunch.  I was incredibly impressed by the service.  The food was very good as well, of course, but to me, you go here for the experience.  Being so watched over and taken care of is worth the money.

I've been in many stars restaurants in NYC and also around the world, and i never ever saw a Michelin guide mistake, for me Eleven should be classified as michelin do, just 1 star, Zagat is doing a terrible mistake, they're classifying the food as 28, common guys if Daniel is 28, Eleven should be no more than 24, it's a huge gap between both restaurants, Eleven is really an Average restaurant, maybe Zagat is comparing prices, than Eleven are higher than Daniel, but food never. i would not recommend for a friend.

I found the food to be divine if a little on the small side, however the service was awkward. We also did not receive granola or any sort of parting gift for that matter. No tours of the kitchen either :(

My dinner at Eleven Madison Park was perhaps the best meal I ever had, in my forty-three years. My three highly discerning foodie dining companions were pretty quick to proclaim it their best. I feel like I need to compare a couple other meals side by side before making that kind of statement. The other possible contenders are mostly Michelin-starred restaurants in France. I don't know if I could ever really decide, though I am ready to say that Eleven Madison Park was the best "dining experience" I ever had.

For this kind of money, a meal really should be a memory you'll cherish all your life--even change your conception of how you look at food, and there's no question that Eleven Madison Park didn't disappoint. The broccoli was like a lecture in the various ways a vegetable can be miraculously delicious. I actually wept throughout the fois gras course. Despite its ethically dodgy provenance, fois gras simply gets more delicious than any other ingredient, perhaps only to be tied with chocolate. Their fois gras with strawberries was likely the best thing I ever tasted. 

At this level, it becomes a ludicrous game to try to think of things that could possibly have been better, and what we four came up with were just silly details not worth mentioning. ("My goat cheese lollipop stick could perhaps have been cleared a little faster.") We all had the tasting menu, and agreed that the very worst course (eggplant) was absolutely delicious, creative, and beautiful. Its failing? It was slightly redundant with its preceding course, as both were more or less green. I'm so glad I had the opportunity to try it, though, as I really loved it, particularly the long, paper-thin translucent eggplant chip.

Every dimension of this dining experience was world-class fantastic. The food was delicious, beautifully presented, creative, varied, balanced, educational, stimulating--beyond perfect in all dimensions. We left stuffed but not to the point of feeling sick. The sommelier's wine suggestion was brilliant, and the markup was unusually reasonable. The service was impeccable: technically flawless, pleasant, knowledgeable, and cheery, without being obtrusive. The atmosphere was elegant but not ostentatious, and the chairs were comfortable, even after four hours.

Yes, it was among the most expensive meals I've ever had, but absolutely worth it. I hope you enjoy it too.

Fantastic - food was brilliant, service was excellent. 

We went for Thursday lunch which was fairly quiet, however we arrived late, and one person had to leave early to catch a flight - they bent over backwards to get through the four courses before she had to go, and then were happy for us to relax, have a few delicious cocktails once we were done. 

The food was absolutely amazing, and the sommelier did a great job matching the wines. All round, a great experience.

Lights out, absolutely black-out amazing.

Hands down, best restaurant food experience I have ever had in my lifetime, and I don't imagine there is much better out there in existence when it comes to food, wine, and service. One of the best restaurants in the world.  

Get the dinner tasting menu with wine pairings - that's all that needs to be said. Or lunch. Save up, and do it. Expensive, but there are less than a handful of places in the world that execute at this level and it is worth every penny.

Eleven Madison wiill change the way you think about food - seriously. More thought goes into one plate here than the thought that goes into entire restaurant menus.

I can't really review every course because the next course instantly made me forget everything and completely drew me into the present moment.

5 stars... 10 stars... 100 stars... EPIC.

Fresh and clean feel at Eleven Madison Park.  One of my favorite places in the city for a great meal.  I love their approach to food by highlighting key ingredients, and I was pleasantly surprised how much I really liked all of it.  Great imagination by the chef.  Definitely not stuff that I could have thought up or whipped up at home.

I'm a huge fan of Danny Meyer establishments, from Shack Shack, to Blue Smoke, the Modern, and the higher end, classy Eleven Madison Park.  He hasn't disappointment me yet.  He's a genius...

One of the most memorable menus that I've ever had. Food was very inventive and delicious. If I could say something bad it would be that some dishes were a little too salty. Salt is good though and overall the food was great!

We've been to Eleven Madison Park several times and have never ever been the slightest bit disappointed. They just get better and better every single time. Well worth the money and, honestly, better than Per Se, in my book.

Read our full review and see our photos from our most recent visit: http://smithratliff.com/2011/06/16/dinner-at-eleven-madison-park/
Came here once for Restaurant week meal and once just for lunch.  Food is great.  Also really love the decor.  Service is also great.  Classy place.

This really is a great restaurant. It starts with an innovative menu, features lots of neat little touches before and after the dinner, but the main event was the food, which was perfectly done. Wine list is good, very complete and not too crazily priced. Service was good too...everything was great.

The dining experience started off well with the greeters and host.  Then it went down hill.

We ordered the 4-course prix fixe.  And like everyone before has posted, you get a lot more than four courses.  The food was good and looked beautiful, but the service left much to be desired.  Definitely order the lobster if it's on your ingredient list, and I really enjoyed the goat cheese lollipops.  

We ordered cocktails, which they completely forgot about it.  We ordered cocktails from a server.  Then a different server came to take our main ingredients order.  Then they brought the first amuse bouche, no cocktail.  Then the second, no cocktail.  We had to ask them again.

I had read the previous reviews and understood we were going to be there for awhile, but they really need to work on the timing.  I'm all for fancy dining, but do you really need to have that many servers?  And if you do, the timing needs to be on point.  Timing of the dishes started well but, as the meal dragged on, there would be 20-25 mins between each dish.  The dessert took a REALLY long time.  

And the glass of wine they poured me was ridiculously small.  See photo.  I really thought he was pouring me a large taste at the time.  But alas, no, that was actually my entire $19 glass of wine.

Also, where was our granola?  I saw other patrons with mason jars of it; we didn't get any.  Maybe it was because we looked under 50 years old, or maybe it was because we actually had to ask for a second time for our cocktails and desserts.
upon entering, i was bombarded with about 5 greeters, all good looking. i felt like a rock star! food is great, as is the atmosphere.  above all, they served me the best gimlet i've ever had!
From start to end, probably my best ever all-around dining experience. The safe choice for a perfect meal. Refined plates and professional service.

I knew I owned a double-breasted white linen blazer for a reason. 

HA! 

But seriously, this was such a wonderful cap to a lovely Saturday with the family in town (two weeks ago). The night beforehand I picked the restaurant, and we had a great time at Freeman's in the LES, although I have to hand it to my father for this choice, it was excellent.

Last time I let him choose a venue, we ended up at Osteria de Circo, which I found decidedly droll and unimpressive. This time I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised. This is not to say that the crowd wasn't similar between the two, it was quite so, to be frank. Stiff, crisp, and Republican, of course.

We all went for the four-course menu, and while I cannot speak for anyone else, mine revolved around some lovely appetizers, a truly sizable black truffle, some perfectly cooked white meat, and indulgent desserts. 

While it's nowhere I would just wander into on a Friday night, for the occasion, Eleven Madison Park hit the sweet spot when it comes to striking a balance between my somewhat more adventurous taste and my fathers...shall we say..."pleated"...equivalent.

Two words: cheese sommelier! Food was great, staff was great and seriously, cheese nerd. Amazing. This place embodies why I moved to New York. People who know a lot about their craft and execute it well.

The server was knowledgable & friendly. The atmosphere was serene & relaxing. Most importantly, the food was absolutely amazing. Pricey, but worth every penny. The chicken with truffles left me speechless.

We went 5/28 for a 945pm dinner - got there early and sat at the bar.  Wife was going with non-alco cocktails this evening and they are quite nice here - interesting and flavorful.  I had english milk punch - I thought it was great.  We had asked in advance for a kitchen tour after dinner.  We decided to go with the 8-course menu and basically the chef prepares the dishes without you knowing anything in advance.  So if you think the "grid" format of the 4-course is too open-ended this is even more-so, but we liked the idea.  Everything was excellent - flavorful and cooked perfectly.  I really appreciated that they took into consideration that my wife may be expecting and cooked her food with that in mind.  I wish I had mentioned at the start that I would like a dish with foie gras because I had read nice things about the FG dishes people had but we did not receive one during out dinner.  We did receive crab, sea urchin, scallops, lamb, pork,  ham salad, several small starters, a few post-dessert desserts and a chocolate dessert.  The chocolate dessert was very nice, especially the accompanying ice cream but again, I wish I would have mentioned at the start that we would prefer a dessert not based on chocolate as it isnt a big favorite.  I had two glasses of wine that they chose and I thought they did a good job.  Service was fantastic.  The noise level was energetic all night.  We didnt get the kitchen tour at the end which was a bit of a downer.  Total with tax, tip, 2 glasses wine, 1 alco cocktail and 3 non-alco cocktails was $612.  Not sure I would do the 8-course again because I dont feel like the value is there but I would try the 4-course and I would recommend eating at the bar and trying cocktails.  Overall, Im really glad we went but Jean Georges is still the standard to beat for us.

This place is WONDERFUL!

We had eaten at Daniel two weeks earlier and Eleven Madison park blows Daniel waay out of the water.

Though it's a 4 course meal, as everyone has already mentioned they bring out tons of tiny little plates that are super yummy.
The menu changes seasonally so I'm not going to get into it. I was a little nervous about the "pick the main ingredient" approach but all the dishes we had were amazing and it was nice to be surprised in seeing how everything came out (I didn't bother asking too much as to how it was prepared). 

Waitstaff is excellent. They are super nice and attentive. 

Best part of our experience: OUR WAITER TOOK US ON A TOUR OF THE KITCHEN. COOLEST EVER. IT TOTALLY MADE OUR NIGHT.

AND one of the chef's came and said hi to us on our tour and she made us a dessert/cocktail thing with liquid nitrogen while we were standing there! SO COOL.

AND THEN, when we thought we were going to go back to our table, they took us to this mini lounge that only had 2 other tables (both were empty). And there was a bottle of liquor and more sweets. They had also brought all of our personal things over. We felt like total rockstars.
 
AND THEN they gave us granola to take home. Amazing. Only wish we got more than 1 jar.

Best restaurant experience ever. We had a 5:30 reservation and didn't leave till past 8:30, but enjoyed every minute of it.

By far the finest fine dining experience I have had the pleasure to sit through. The food was tasty, thoughtfully stimulating and creative, and the service was nothing short of IMPECCABLE. It was a few months ago that I went so I can't recount every single detail, but a few things that stand out:

1) the decor/ambiance was beautiful.
2) the server to guest ratio
3) the drinks were as delicious as the food
4) the food was incredible
5) the unique format of the menu
6) the customization of the menu items
7) the hand written check (beautiful! i'm a letterist so i appreciate great penmanship, haha)
8) the granola they sent us home with as a parting gift - SO CUTE! and delicious.

Everything about this experience was positive, and I highly recommend this restaurant. :) Thank you Eleven Madison Park for a memorable night!

Upon seating, they give you a menu where one chooses a key ingredient from each row, as the chef tailors your dishes to your choices (my key ingredients are capitalized below). 

Then, comes the barrage of amuse bouche:
gourges, smoked sturgeon sabayon with diced sturgeon and chive oil in a perfectly cut eggshell, chilled pea soup w/ buttermilk snow (yes, it actually tastes like you're eating snow), soft wheat bun w/ goat's or cow's butter and fleur de sel.

My key ingredients came to me as such:
FOIE GRAS w/ a pickled puree and roasted ramps on toasted barley.
SNAPPER w/ potatoes and squid.
PORK loin, confit, w/ a mint infused pea puree.

All were perfectly cooked, balanced, and seasoned well. 

Then came a gentleman with a cart with all the ingredients for an egg cream. Except in this case, the cream was malted. Once the seltzer water, cream, and milk were mixed, he placed a few drops of olive oil into the concoction from a Tiffany's sterling oil can. That's damn classy.
I've often had chocolate milk before bed, but the seltzer water was an interesting touch. To finish it off, they served large toffee brittle, coffee macaroons, and mango pate de fruits. 

While I was praising Nick, my waiter, on the my meal and asking about the complexity of constantly tailoring a meal to each guest, he asks if i would like to view the kitchen for myself and see how it's done. Would I...?? He runs back to organize a tour.

I receive my check and sign away a hefty sum, but it's not the bill I notice. It's the Cross pen that they gave me to sign the check. It had great weight distribution, clean lines, and wrote effortlessly. The company is based in Rhode Island and has been around for 165 years. 
Pretty impressive.

Once they are ready for me, I am escorted to a recessed area in the rear of the kitchen with a small standing table. One of their desert chefs arrives and pours Aperol and liquid nitrogen into a large stainless steel bowl to whisk an Aprerol sorbet. She tops it off with an orange syrup and marmalade, champagne foam, and pop rocks. 

While the edible cocktail was being made, I was given a brief history on the restaurant and the elements that they look to for inspiration. One such element was a person, Miles Davis, whose picture was hung behind me. 

After a couple elegant spoonfuls, the sorbet starts to melt and I decide to just take it to the face. I am then guided to the rear of the kitchen where they briefly explain the flow of the cold/hot dishes, the appetizers, and the deserts. As I exit and my coat is returned, I am greeted again by Nick as I finally leave the restaurant. What an experience. Every detail, from the dove shaped wine decanters to the pen, will give me a reason to come back.

Ambiance - 5 stars
Food- 4.5 stars
Service- 5 Stars

The food is inventive and clean.  The food doesnt feel like the chef is trying hard to be inventive, it just works.  The space is beautiful and airy, and the service is just right.  In terms of how it ranks w/in 5 star peers, think this place is better than jean-george but not as strong as brooklyn fare.
Overall, excellent experience.  Not every dish was perfect, but the atmosphere, service where really great.  Will definitely go back when I want to splurge.

wow, what a meal. my wife and i came here for our anniversary and we were not disappointed. the room is beautiful, the service elegant, and the food creative. they know how to treat you well here, with amouse bouches, cognac, goodies to take home at the end.
quite possibly the finest (and in any event the most expensive) meal i have had in nyc.  would definitely go back.  truly superb.

My wonderful friend Dan, upon hearing that I was coming to New York, made reservations all over town, then picked the best place we could get into and took me and two friends to dinner... at Eleven Madison Park. 
The menu looks bizarre and exciting, with just rows of words. Basically, you pick one ingredient from each horizontal column, and then tell them if you don't like any foods, prefer a certain preparation and have any special requests. For example, Dan asked about the foie gras. 
"It's presented as a terrine, Dan." Said Kevin, our server/best friend. "It's served cold with a pineapple chutney."
"You don't have a pan-fried hot version, I take it?" Asked Dan.
"I'm sorry." Replied Kevin. "Tonight's preparations are cold."
Brooke piped up. "So much for being able to do anything."
She was teasing, of course. It was all so over the top. But Kevin ran off, and Brooke put her head in her hands. 
"You and Kevin are in a fight!" I whispered. 
Minutes later, Kevin returned. "Dan, we'd be delighted to do a seared preparation for you."
Oh man. 
As we sat down to our 10pm reservation, Dan "explored" the wine list and ordered something that I'm sure was very fancy. When presented with a wine glass, I apologetically smiled at Kevin and said, "I'm not drinking."
"In that case, Beth." Kevin said, "May I have the bartender pair each of your courses with an appropriate non-alcoholic cocktail?"
"Seriously?" I asked. 
"Seriously." Kevin said.
Our food was amazing, we laughed so much we may have offended other tables and the service was literally the best formal service I have ever experienced. After dessert, Kevin brought over little stone blocks with candies and cookies. In front of each of us, he placed a lovely brandy glass. Coming over to Dan, Kevin said, "Dan, this is a 1992 brandy from the (insert something French and complicated.) It's a perfect finish to your meal, and I'll pour each of you a glass. I leave the bottle here, with our compliments. Please stay as long as you wish."
It was 1am.
Then Kevin came over to me. "Beth, this is a sparkling apple cider from the Loire Valley. It's an (insert something complicated about apples) and a perfect finish to your meal. I'll pour you a glass and I leave the bottle here with our compliments.
All four of us looked at Kevin. And then each other. 
"Well, that's..."
"Pretty f****** classy."
"I'm like, touched."
"I am emotional about your cider."
I have been to lots of places that make me feel perfectly comfortable about not ordering booze. In this day and age, good bars are pretty cool about those of us on the wagon. And some bars, even fancy ones, still give me a look of disdain and say something like, "Well, we have cranberry juice." 
But I mentioned casually and once at the beginning of our three-hour meal at Eleven Madison Park that I would not be drinking. And 10 minutes later, the bartender came over, introduced himself, talked about my order and thoughtfully paired my entire experience with non-alcoholic adult beverages. 
There was no, "Can I get you another Diet Coke." Oh no. Kevin and the other 647 people serving us filed away each of our requests and made sure every single second of our experience was silently considered. 
I got drunk on class. 
So thank you Dan, Kevin, Eleven Madison Park and New York, for showing me how it's done...

I cannot even beggin to describe how AMAZING AND EXCELLENT my whole experience was at 11 Madison Park. I have had the chance to visit several of the top 10 restaurants in the world, and this has been one of the best.

The kindness of the whole staff was beyond anything I have ever experienced, humble and EXTREMELY PROFESSIONAL, and I have only one way of describing good food....It made me smile!! It gave me an involuntary reaction of surprise and happiness!! GOOD JOB

Excellent. Everything was delicious, well presented, and the service was good.  This was a memorable meal.  had the full tasting menu including the wine pairing.   The wines were acceptable and matched the dishes for the most part with a few misses.  The wines weren't great, but acceptable.  The main course, the pork and lamb, was too salty and borderline.  That said, that was two botched dishes out of some 10 or more dishes.  Otherwise the other dishes where excellent, on par with kaiseki Japanese cuisine I've had in Japan, or good nouvelle cuisine Ive had in France.

Came here to celebrate one of my sister's birthdays. 
I was pleasantly surprised to walk in to such a beautiful building w goregous ambience. I say this because I was expecting to walk into a stuffy white table cloth "fancy" restaurant - judging from the pictures I saw on the website. The combination of sensory satisfying food and elegant service made it one of the best fine dining experiences I've ever had. We did the four course which included plenty of complimentary amuses to make a perfect amount of food and drink. I also really love the menu format - where you get to choose a main ingredient for each course, and then be pleasantly surprised w what the chef prepares. A highlight of the evening - was when they rolled out a little cart w all the concoctions to make an egg cream...! One of my most favourite things in the world!! 
Now who can I sweet talk into taking me here again...

I came here last year during the summer of 2010 for lunch so this review has been a long time coming. The executive chef Daniel Humm had very recently won the James Beard award for the best chef in NYC and EMP had a really good prix fixe lunch deal so I was eager to try it out. Even though the meal was almost a year ago, it was memorable enough that I still remember the details to this day.

When you first walk in, you'll notice that the decor is elegant, simple, clean, and beautiful. This philosophy extends to their food - because the dishes are the same way.

After being seated, a plate of amuse bouches were soon brought to our table. It consisted of foie gras and raspberry gelee on a cracker, gougeres, and a carrot marshmallow. Everything was quite delectable but nothing really stood out although I quite enjoyed the gougeres. We were also given a breadbasket with a silver platter of very soft butter.

We ordered some iced teas which were quite good. When we asked a member of the waitstaff to explain how the tea was brewed, he gave such an impressive and lengthy explanation that I don't remember any of it save for the fact that it was very detailed.

Onto the starters:

Tagliotini w/ Alaskan Crab - What a wonderful and simple dish. The pasta was cooked al dente and the flavors were fresh and clean. It had large chunks of crab and a nice lemony tang to it.

Grilled Octopus - I never really liked octopus because it has always been chewy or rubbery. However, the octopus served at EMP was tender on the inside, yet the outside was al dente; no chewiness or rubberiness to be found anywhere. One of the servers later gave us an impressive and lengthy explanation of how it was done (slow cooked for tenderness and then grilled on the outside for al denteness). I will never view octopus the same way again.

While we were waiting for our main courses to arrive, a member of the waitstaff started ironing the tablecloth on the table adjacent to ours. Since I derive great satisfaction from well-pressed fabrics, this pleased me. 

Daniel Humm also stepped out of the kitchen for a bit and decided to chat with some of the patrons. He must have seen us looking at him because he came over to talk to us. We chatted a bit about how he started cooking and his recent award from the James Beard Foundation. Eventually, he had to get back to the kitchen but he would later return to take a picture with us. What a friendly guy!

Mains:

Bone Marrow Crusted Beef Tenderloin - I was very disappointed by this dish as it was cooked medium instead of medium rare. I suppose the blame for the mistake can be partially attributed to me because the waiter never asked me how I wanted the beef cooked and I neglected to tell him. Regardless, it was still pretty good (although it would've been 10x better if cooked properly) and I continued to eat it. The waiter eventually came over on one of his courtesy runs and asked how everything was. I mentioned that everything was delicious but the beef was slightly overcooked and he immediately offered me a replacement. Since I did not want to wait, I declined. When the bill came, I would find that they comped this particular dish. Awesome service :)

Nova Scotia Lobster Lasagna w/ Lemon Verbana & Heirloom Squash - This dish was beautiful! Vibrant and colorful, it looked like a work of art. The lobster was incredibly tender and flavorful. Portion size was very good too. My dining partner commented that this was "the best lobster [she's] ever had." This dish was simply sublime.

Dessert: 

An assortment of macaroons - These were light and delicious, not too sweet either. Some were playful and made me laugh out loud, like the peanut butter and jelly one which was a nod to childhood. Others were delicious combinations, like basil and strawberry - those two aromas just go together so well.

EMP remains the best restaurant experience I've ever had even though I went for lunch. The food was simple and clean with light flavors - perfect for me. The waitstaff was ultra attentive and knowledgeable. Daniel Humm even took a picture with us. They also like to iron tablecloths. In my mind, this place unequivocally deserves more than just one Michelin star.

Great service and wine selection. Had the wine pairing with a semi-large group. Definitely worth the money here. You'll have world class service and an excellent meal. Dining area is also very elegant and quiet. A good place to impress a date! I'd highly likely come back.

Since that initial review I have returned to Eleven Madison Park and sampled most of the other NYC restaurants in its league.  I can say that, with the benefit of experience, my earlier four star review was a mistake.  The food and service continues to improve and this place is really reaching for the top.

Wow I am speechless. This is definitely the BEST restaurant I have ever been to my life. It has the best service, amazing food and crazy atmosphere. Maybe it is because I was proposed to right here? Hehe

Either way, I can't say enough nice things about this place. The menu is simple but the design and flavor of actual dishes are so many layers and excitingly diverse. 

Although our pre-fix only has 4 dishes but they actually come with so many more little dishes on the house and amazing house special egg cream.

The caviar is by far the best I have ever had; it was so smooth and creamy that I couldn't even tell it is caviar! The pork I had was so tender and flavorful too. The dessert I got was chocolate with peanut butter wafer and it was delicate, sweet and peanut buttery! 

Oh they also gave you a jar of house special granola to bring home. Now I have a cute and memorable engagement gift!

One of the best restaurants I have ever experienced. The food is fantastic, and the service is absolutely exemplary. The only downside is the difficulty of making a reservation weeks in advance, but I have to say it only makes sense. This is always the first place I mention when someone asks for a recommendation in the city.

Let me start with the end of the lunch price-fixe meal. We were lucky to be treated to a behind the scenes tour of the kitchen by the restaurant manager who also went further and got a chef to prepare a awesome gin sorbet dessert in the kitchen in our very eyes. If thats not exceeding expectations I don't know what is.

The food was superb to say the least. Fresh, interesting, tasty and beautifully plated. Much appreciate the fine balance and lightness on the palate their food possesses. 

Service struck the optimal balance between attentiveness and discreetness. Staff were knowledgeable and warm - in a word, peerless. The head chef came around to greet guests and asked how we were enjoying the service - no ego, just a chef who likes to keep tabs on the customers which I admire.

The setting is pretty against Madison Park, vaulted ceilings, plenty of natural light and the right amount of noise for a intimate meal without the intimidation.

Lunch is outstanding value at $75 for four courses which doesnt include little treats such as the egg creme made tableside for added drama. This is the refined NYC dining experience. Well done.
I had one of the best meals here. Very creative and modern. Great service. Great atmosphere.  It is a big expensive but well worth it.  I am a fan and hope to come back soon.

Went for lunch again, and everything is really good. What amazes me is their attentive service.

My lunch partner had to step out to take a business call after they served the main course. After she was away for 5 min, they covered the plate and asked if she is going to be back soon. After a further 10 min, they said the plate was sitting longer than what they would like, and said they will bring out a fresh plate when she's back. Then he asked if I would like to taste the lobster anyway and he could bring it out on a small side plate while I was eating my own main course. I politely declined (damn! I should have accepted!).  And out came a fresh plate for her when she's back. Plain brilliant.

I can honestly say this is the best restaurant I have ever been to and enjoyed it from beginning to end each and every time. The food is so good it makes you laugh. It's shockingly wonderful. The flavors are deep, the textures are a spin on tradition and it is all breath taking. 
The service is beyond compare but not stuffy or uptight. Many restaurants like 11 make you feel like you are eating at your grandmother's holiday table but here, you are relaxed and happy. 
The meal won't be cheap but I leave feeling I've paid for an experience and that I've gotten my money's worth.

We ate at the bar since $125 per person is a tad out of our price range...However, the experience was still lovely since the bar has it's own section with tables and couches and candle light.

Dishes ordered:
Crab Tagliolini-absolutely delicious, definitely the prizewinner of the night, light but flavorful and filling

Poached egg and frog legs-very "avant garde", more about the flavor than the substance, don't expect to fill up on this!

Lobster-for sure the best entree that we ordered, I'm not really a lobster fan but I couldn't get enough of this dish

Beef with pecans-not as soft as it looked, interesting dish but a bit underwhelming

Chocolate peanut butter palette and popcorn ice cream-an all around favorite, even to my sister who balked when she first read its description, I didn't think ice cream could taste like popcorn but this one really does, the chocolate peanut butter palette is like a thinner, easier-to-break version of brittle, the chocolate was dark and rich but not too decadent

Overall, I really enjoyed my dinner here! The service was impeccable and always pleasant and attentive. The portions weren't huge but we were completely stuffed after. The inside of the restaurant is also beautifully furnished and elegant. The bill totaled to around $230 for 3 meaning that this will be one of those places I go to for special occasions only, but I'd definitely recommend it to anyone else!

I've been three times and every experience has been mind blowingly amazing.  These guys any Danny Meyer in particular really know how to run a fantastic restaurant from FOH to BOH.  Everyone from the hostess, sommelier, bus boy and maitre d were on point.  It's no wonder his restaurants are always the top rated on Zagat.  I went to EMP before the star and after the extra star and I honestly didn't find that big of a difference--besides the way the menu is planned.  I don't at all mean that as a bad thing, I just don't think they had much improving to do after my first visit.  I look forward to returning and have another wonderful experience.

Was torn between 3 and 4 and had to give it 3 because from the fancy pants restaurants I've been too, it's slightly on the lower end although the price was a little easier to swallow. 

The amuse bouche, especially the egg dish served in the shell, was excellent.

The lobster was tasty, excellently prepared, perfectly cooked. The pickled vegetable gave it the right amount of tart for my palate. 

My friend's halibut was also perfectly cooked as well. Fresh and the texture was creamy. 

Friend's Egg Dish was just okay but she loved her dish. 

If the caliber of the dishes remained the same, then I would have given the restaurant 5 stars. BUT then it went downhill pretty quickly.

The beef dish was good but the beef was overcooked and rubbery. I have to say the side dishes/garnishes were tasty. Maybe it's because I'm Korean but I thought the pickled vegetable along with other garnishes was fantastic with the beef, despite the dense chew. 

The desserts were mediocre. Interesting and beautifully plated but tasteless.

I have to say the complimentary egg cream was a great touch to a tourist visiting NY, which I was.

There are only a handful of restaurants in Manhattan which the New York Times has rated four stars. Eleven Madison Park is perhaps the most "approachable" of all of them. 

The first thing to understand about going to places like this is that you're not just there to fill your stomach. At the risk of sounding cliched, you're there to fill all five of your senses. The chefs are not just cooks, they are artists. Each dish is made up of ingredients which work together to give the dish a distinctive visual appeal, scent, and texture. And of course, a taste where all the ingredients balance each other perfectly. When I was a kid, every time I'd taste something good, I'd shudder with delight. I'm in my middle ages, but Eleven Madison Park brought back that feeling. 

The ordering experience is unique. You're given a menu with sixteen words on it, representing the main ingredients (from pork to chicken to foie gras to black truffles). The menu varies by season. Out of that, you'll either get four courses or a tasting menu (or lunch, you can choose three or four courses). 

The service, of course, was impeccable. The servers were very young, but they were the best of the best. They did talk in a bit of a "heightened" manner (e.g., using fancy words and a slightly fake European accent), but that only added to the atmosphere. They were always friendly and approachable. I did make a "fancy restaurant faux pas" by not asking for the check; my guests and I ended up staying for a very long time after our meal because we didn't realize that the servers were trained to be so polite they'd wait until you asked for the check before offering it to you!

It's been months since I ate dinner there, but certain things linger in my long term memory. The crisp, delicious skin of the pork. The smoothness of the foie gras. I'm someone who can't normally what I ate for breakfast by noon, but this was more than just a meal, it was an exhibition of fine art. This is where culinary art is unique. You can't take a bite out of the Mona Lisa nor Beethoven's Violin Concerto.

This was my first trip to a New York Times four-star restaurant. My wallet did take a bit of a hit (especially since I treated two others to the experience--with the final price I could have bought about 300 Big Macs). But I have no regrets. If you're looking to celebrate a special occasion, there are few places in the City better than here.

In terms of gesalt -- food, wine, service, etc -- EMP is unparalleled. When I walked in the door there was a group of women waiting to greet me. When I said who I was they said "Happy birthday!" -- like, ok how the hell did you remember it was my brithday? When they took my coat I asked for the tag -- I didn't need a tag. Then I sat down at my table. There was a HANDWRITTEN BIRTHDAY CARD. What?!?! The drinks were fantastic. The amuses were abundant and not at all skimpy with the ingredients and just as inventive and delicious as the mains. We had about five courses of amuses. Really really impressive. There was not a single bad dish. If the highs don't match the highs of something like Corton, the lows -- well there are no lows. Everything is beautifully executed and flavorful. It's a bit like Per Se, but I prefer the food and ambience here a hundredfold. The cooking style is a little more loose and less technical and more impulsive, and there's more love in it. Where I would take off half a star: The wait between courses was sometimes too long. And the dessert for the tasting was the generic high -end kit kat that everyone seems to be into these days. (I get this freaking ganache kit kat thing everywhere I go, honestly, and it's profoundly NOT interesting!). The kit kat thing was somewhat counterweighted by a really sweet surprise invitation to the kitchen, where my friend and I were taken around and then treated to an AMAZING nitrogen orange blossom pop-rocks thing with gin sorbet -- which was great and so much fun to eat while hanging out in the kitchen. In any case I felt so happy eating dinner there. Can't wait to go back.

Service and ambience without a doubt deserve 5 stars and beyond.
I'll describe the food shortly to explain where it lost one star.

Reservation was for 9.00 and we were 15 minutes late. But that was no problem to such a gracious restaurant and my friend and I started at the bar with some really delicious and yummy tasting cocktails.

We were seated around 9.30 pm, and did the four course tasting menu - didn't get the wine pairing but got a bottle of wine instead.

Just to put it out there, expect to spend about 4 hours for your meal. We were one of the last two groups of the door that night at 1.30 am. We still got treated like VIPs, in fact even better VIPs since everyone paid attention to the only two tables left - felt like we booked the entire restaurant. 

Anyway, I made the mistake of ordering a 'fatty combination'. Foie gras - which came in three different variations - a stick, brulee, and bread with foie gras between layers (refer to picture). I got the fish for my second course and then for the third course I opted for the Pork. It was a pork belly so you can only imagine by that hour, I was getting abit averse to having so much fat in me. I was expecting maybe pork chop or something else since the chef knew for a fact that I just had tons of foie gras. Hmmm. My final course was the chocolate dessert tasting which was excellent.

Friend got the healthier option - so there was the raddichio, carrot, chicken and then coconut. Everything was great except the chicken - I'm not sure what was up with the chicken (one rectangular block and it was not so tender) so this was where this restaurant lost it's one star. Probably the our least favorite dish of the night (Refer to photos)

Be prepared to have many other mini-appetizers, tasters, goat cheese lollipops and extra desserts come your way. They were all extremely delicious and all ladies get to go home with a little jar of all natural Eleven Madison Park made gronola mix with dried fruits. 

Overall though, had a great night all thanks to the SUPER service, ambience and the majority of the food.

Just had lunch at 11MP and I have to say it was a bit..just a bit...of a let down as compared to my other experiences. I took my mom because she has never been here and I feel so strongly about 11MP that I thought she'd love it..which she did. I p[ersonally was disappointed mainly in the service...not as on point as before. We got shorted an amuse, and I felt cheated on the wine pairings. last time...I got 6 wine pairings with my four course lunch...they gave me champagne with an amuse and a dessert wine with my pre-dessert. This time, I only got four pairings...same price. And my mom didnt get anything to take home either. It might sound silly to hear me complain about these things, but that type of high service and those extras are what puts 11MP in the upper echelon of NYC restaurants, and if there is no consistancy from one visit to the next,,why bother? It's a shame too because the food was outrageously good...my sirloin strip with sweetbreads being one of the best things I have ever had.

I have very mixed feelings about this place. This is a fine dining establishment so really, food, service and the memorability of the dining experience should all score high marks. I'm not sure if I expected too much of this place from the great Yelp and NYT 4 star review as well as their Michelin star. The dining experience started off strong but the food and the service seemed to fade as the evening progressed.

We ordered the 4 course tasting menu ($125) with wine pairing (add on $95). As many reviews have noted already, the menu only states the main ingredient in each course. The concept is pretty unique for diners who like to be surprised by the kitchen but probably not the best place for very picky eaters who want to know every single ingredient that goes into their dish.

- Warm cheese puffs. 
- Amuse: a thyme tied bouquet steeping in the halibut tea served with a side of nori crisps. The soup was subtle and delicious and had a very whimsical presentation.
- Complimentary starters: scallop ceviche with a tangerine gelee on a clam half shell and a raw fluke served on a rice cracker with basil and meyer lemon. Both the scallop and fluke tasted fresh, citrusy and light. Second starter was another whimsical presentation of beet and goat cheese lollipops presented in fake grass container along with goat cheese croquettes and a side of remoulade. 
- Bread served with goat's milk butter and cow's milk butter with side of sea salt. Bread was flakey and buttery. The cow's milk was super smooth and definitely more flavourful than the goat's milk butter. 
- 1st courses: Crab salad with daikon discs - beautiful spring presentation. Foie gras terrine with pineapple served with a toasted brioche - foie tasted very light in texture and super smooth, delicious with the pineapple.
- 2nd courses: Poached egg with frog legs and spring peas - another gorgeous spring like scene (see pic), I hated breaking the egg but it was paired beautifully with the frog legs. Poached halibut with almonds and cauliflower was perfectly poached though flavour was a bit flat compared to the egg dish.
- 3rd courses: Pork loin and belly along with spring peas and mint - perfectly cooked with great flavour. Squab breast and leg served with a piece of foie gras on the side tasted more like a rich winter dish but still delicious.
- Complimentary egg and cream drink. This was made table side so I enjoyed the story behind this traditional NY fountain drink but it was way too sweet since it's made with of chocolate syrup, whole milk, olive oil and soda water.
- 4th courses: chocolate bar served with popcorn and ice cream. The other dessert was a lemon poppyseed dish served with lemon ice cream. The desserts were too sweet for the chocolate and too tart for the lemon - more balance would have ended the meal on a higher note. Every table received port to pair with their desserts and a bottle was set on the table if you wanted more. The port was too sweet along with the already overly sweet desserts but it was nice for EMP to include it.
- Petit Fours - I usually look forward to petit fours but we didn't like any of it, we ate a few because we didn't want to waste it! LOL. But once again, the items were too sweet. 
- Complimentary jar of house made granola - haven't tried it yet but a nice parting gift for each diner.

It was a Thursday evening so the restaurant was not packed, it was probably 85% full. Our server was nice but didn't seem to very proactive in delivering service. Fine dining service staff are usually one step ahead of their diners needs and I just found that our server required us to flag her down to get her attention. There was a lag in taking our orders and she did not explain some of the special offerings that we overheard from other tables. That being said, our sommelier and other wait staff were very professional and on the ball. Water was constantly filled and the service was not snooty as it had more of a laid back friendly vibe to it. After we finished our 4th course, we waited for over 25 mins until we flagged her down because it was nearly 3 hours for 4 courses at this point. Our server just said "oh I thought you two were enjoying the evening so I didn't want to interrupt?" That was an odd explanation considering that you can still complete someone's entire meal and bring the bill without making someone feel rushed. 

Service and timing of dishes were mixed; I really think that 3+ hours is too long for a 4 course meal even t with the addition of a few complimentary dishes. My 6 course meal at Daniel was nowhere near 3 hours as the pacing of the food service did not miss a beat. Here, I felt like we were waiting and waiting for things to happen. Maybe we were here on an off night because it seems like my experience is out of the norm. Would I come back? Probably not but that being said, 80% of the evening was enjoyed but at these price points, you really want to enjoy the entire experience, not just aspects of it.

Service - 5 stars.  Truly astounding sommelier who knew the food, wine and beer menus backwards and forwards.

Food - The 4 of us tried 12 out of the 16 dinner options and the most commonly uttered word was "wow".  Every dish was astounding.  In addition to the 4 ordered courses there were 3 amuses and 1 petit fours, so really 8 courses.  As far as I'm concerned there is no wrong option in ordering, but the squab and pork belly were particularly astounding.  

Truly excellent.

How did I never review this place?!  

We came about a year ago (since then, they've made some service changes - fewer tables, more staff, slightly higher prices) and I kept asking my husband if he'd told them we were famous.  They kept treating us like Hollywood royalty.  We were fed little bites and interludes between every completely delicious course, taken on a tour of the kitchen, and then led to a little lounge area for a complimentary tower of macarons and a bottomless glass of Cognac.  Oh em geeeeeeeeeee.

Honestly, I would give this place five stars even if the food were just okay - the service is that amazing.  But the food is fantastic.  You feel like a decadent pre-Revolution French royal, in the best possible way, utterly relaxed and indulged.

Also, this is a great place to get engaged, because if you do, they immediately produce a bottle of champagne and a saber - they even gave my sister-in-law and her freshly minted fiance the (very nice) glasses to take home.

Even though they've raised prices, $125 a person a steal for this place.  I mean, that's what they charge at Ko, and Ko barely even has waiters.

Love love love love LOVE.

So this 16-course meal is dedicated to three of my ultra special friends who participated in this 4-hour gastronomical marathon with me on my birthday. You know who you are.

Jan 2011:

Hamachi - marinated with fennel, meyer lemon, and horseradish

Radicchio - tardivo with buffalo mozzarella and mango

Langoustine - ceviche with celery, apple, and lime

Foie Gras - torchon with cocoa and quince

Carrot - roasted with dates and wheat berries (RECOMMENDED)

Black Truffle - celery root puree, goat cheese and potato sabayon (RECOMMENDED)

Skate - seared with lemon, bok choy and madras curry

Lobster - with pickled daikon radish, dehydrated citrus, and edamame

Guinea Fowl - roasted with parsnip, grapes, and hen of the wood mushroom

Pork - roasted with sauerkraut, pear and morcilla

Lamb - roasted with vadouvan, lady apples and puntarella

Veal - blanquette with winter vegetables and smoked bone marrow

Hobelchas - variations with country bread

Coconut - vacherin with passion fruit and mango

Lemon - cake with poppy seeds, olives and yogurt

Chocolate - ganache with butternut squash and maple (RECOMMENDED)

and many amuse bouches, intermezzos, drinks, and additional desserts. (RECOMMENDED)

Will C.'s 300th Review.

I had not been to Eleven Madison in a long time, and it really is a beautiful space.  They  meet you at the door, knowing your party's name and whether they are seated.  And the servers - so many, and so much to tell us.  The food was gorgeous...inventive and tasty at the same time.  We all left so full, and with their wonderful gifts of mason jars with granola for morning breakfast.  I highly recommend for any special occasion.

Good place to hang out with friends. I loved it.

Menaka Indrani

I usually don't bother to review places that have 300+ reviews already, but my dinner was so amazing that I had to share.

Ordered a "Union Jack," one of their specialty cocktails.  It smelled like cologne but tasted wonderful.

Whenever I got up to go to the loo and came back to sit down, there was always someone who pulled my seat out and pushed my seat in.  Fancy shmancy.

Everyone who writes that there are a lot more courses that come with the standard 4-course meal is correct.  We got a ton of amuse bouche.  A bread puff thing, goat cheese lollipops and nuggets (meant to look like those tiny Easter eggs?  And the lollipops were presented poking up from a bed of grass.  So, nice touch with the spring theme).  We also got shellfish, warm bread with two kinds of butter.  It was pretty great.

And then our meal started.  The menu changes seasonally so I'm not going to get too much into it, but all the dishes were amazing and we also opted for the wine pairing, which was amazing.  Each dish had a wine that accompanies it (and we definitely got more than 4 glasses of wine...I'm thinking by the end of the night we had all drank at least a bottle of wine each).  And the sommelier (actually, the junior sommelier) was super nice and informative.  We liked her so much we asked how she ended up becoming a sommelier and got some really cool insight.  Same for all the waitstaff.  I believe we bonded with the Captain on the floor...because after we were done with dessert...HE TOOK US ON A TOUR OF THE KITCHEN.  OMG SO COOL.  IT TOTALLY MADE OUR NIGHT.

And they even made a really cook dessert/cocktail thingy with liquid nitrogen while we were on our kitchen tour! SO COOL.
