And then, when we thought we were going to go back to our table, we were whisked to a loungey area with digestifs!  There was a PEAR in the bottle of liquor.  A PEAR.  And they brought all our stuff to our new lounge table!  And, they came back with even MORE sweets.  OMG, I died a little.  And by this time I needed some coffee so ordered an espresso macchiato, which was divine. 

And then they gave us granola to take home.  Amazing.

Best restaurant experience I've had (dare I say...ever).  We had a 6:15 reservation and didn't leave till past 10, but enjoyed every minute of it.

The service was impeccable, the food was amazing.  They really took care of us.  We sat next to a table of regulars.  I want to be a regular now.
One of the best fine dining experiences ever. Food outstanding, decor lively, staff attentive. If you like the long, multiple-course type of dinner you will love it here.

This was the best meal I have had in new York, bar none. Lovely, subdued ambience, amazingly creative and delicious food and e service was over the top. I have eaten in many other places with great reputations, and yet 11 Madison is where I would go back again in a heart beat!

Decor: 5/5
-classy
-large windows and lots of natural light
-long table clothes

Service: 5/5
-where do I begin? This service is impeccable
-I made no reservations and got seated immediately
-We got a corner booth and a server pulled out the table if we needed to get out
-Silverware is carefully placed before each dish
-server to diner ratio is almost 3:1
-Each dish is explained in detail after it is served
-any bread crumbs is cleaned off the table cloth
-water is constantly refilled

Food: 5/5
-I chose the 3 course meal ($56 for lunch): Cod, Veal and Coconut.
-Tiffany D chose Foie Gras, Beef and Lemon
-Don't be misled, this 3 course meal turned into 8 dishes
-Note that dishes are prepared seasonally so you will never have the same dish twice.
-The following are in addition to the three main courses: 
---Cheese puffs 
---Smoked sturgeon in egg yolk
---Bread with cow's milk and goat's milk
French salt
---Tangerine sorbet
---Carrotcake macaroon& Peanut brittle

I'm totally coming here each season. I love the fine dining experience and Eleven Madison Park hits the spot.

I was feeling fancy today so at my request Paul H. and I ventured out to this magnificent gem of a place. At the door, I swapped out my flippy floppies for nude pumps. Gotta look fancy if I'm going to go to a fancy place ;) We didn't have reservations but it wasn't a problem since they weren't packed. We were seated in a corner which was awesome since that's my favorite way to sit since i could still cuddle and hold hands with my honey. I know it's way sappy, you can go ahead and puke, lol

We went for the 3 course meal which ended up being a lot more than 3 courses.
i'm going to dumb things down for the normal people who don't get to indulge in "fine dining" often. :)

-cheese puffs
-seaweed broth with sesame wafers
-sturgeon cream soup in egg shells
-flaky butter rolls with goat butter & cow butter, fleur de sel on the side
-tangerine sorbet
-carrot cake macaron
-pralines

that was in addition to the three main items we chose.
Paul H. went with Cod, Veal, and Coconut. I chose Foie Gras, Beef, and Lemon. 

To avoid writing a book on this place, I'll just say go for it. Your tongue will thank you for a break from instant ramen and pizza. Your mind will be confused (lemon sorbet and olives?!?!) but it will be happy after the experience. 

For lunch we each spent $75, which for a Michelin 1 star rated restaurant & 3 James Beard awards is not bad at all. The service is impeccable here. Be prepared to be pampered. I honestly can't wait to come back. I just have to let my wallet recover a bit. ;)

Tiffany and Paul's 2nd Michelin rated restaurant experience. :)

When I was a child and had the opportunity to dine at a 'fine' restaurant, a rather pedantic soul told me sententiously that you could tell everything about a restaurant by 'the butter' served with the bread. If that's the case, Eleven Madison Park is the best restaurant on the planet. Real goat butter that actually tastes like chevre! It's unbelievable...
Now, if you're not of that school of thought, imagine this: a series of canapes (I lost count), all wonderfully imagined and crafted to perfection, served before your first course with a never-empty glass of blanc des blancs. Follow that with a delicious 4 course meal (you really can't go wrong no matter what you pick), another round of amuses-bouches sized apres-desserts, AND a bottle of 10 year old cognac left on your table for your post-prandial self-medication, and you have my definition of the finest dining currently available in NYC.
Nuff said.

This place is fine dining at its best. 

We got the tasting menu which is what I would recommend over the four course tasting cos if you're going here in the first place you should go all out. 

We started off with some kind of tea appetizer and then four appetizer courses. One was a fingerling potato that was decorated so beautifully it looked like a garden. There is so much detail put into the presentation you almost don't want to eat the food. 

After our four appetizers, we moved onto the main courses which was veal, fish, braised vegetables, and pork. I was so stuffed by this time I thought I was going to burst. There is A LOT of food. I saw many parties take breaks to get up and walk around. I'm not sure where they went but I think they toured the kitchen. 

Our dessert was a chocolate cake (for lack of a better word) that had black sesame oil in it. This was followed with smaller dessert dishes that included macarons, peanut brittle and others I can't remember. When our meal was over we were treated to a French pear brandy that our waitress left at our table and told us we can have as much as we want. Too bad that stuff had an alcohol volume of..um..I dunno 100%. That stuff was so strong I could barely sip it. 

After our bill was paid we were given a parting gift which was granola for the night that we were there. What an experience...

Going to this restaurant is really an experience, the staff is exceptional and you feel extremely taken care of from the moment you walk in the door. The first time I ate at 11 Madison was for my birthday at lunch time and it was one of the best meals I have ever had. I will never forget the linguine pasta with rock crab I ordered, best pasta I have ever had, minimal ingredients put together perfectly, pasta, crab, lemon, butter. The most recent time I went for dinner, and the menu has changed. For each course they list four single ingredients, for example, for your main dish you would choose between veal, lobster, lamb, and bass. But you have no other information unless you specifically ask, it certainly makes for an amazing night of culinary surprises. Choose wisely, there is a chance of ordering all heavy dishes without giving yourself a lighter break, but overall I really love this kind of dining experience, I don't need to know in advance what I'm going to eat to enjoy it!!!

There are celebrity chefs but there aren't enough celebrity restaurantuers.  Danny Meyer has perfected the art of the restaurant and there's no better evidence than emp.  The service is amazing from when they took our coats at entry to bring a birthday candle based on an aside that I made when selecting our wine for the evening.

The food is amazing but emp really speaks to why another rater has three categories...food, service and decor.  EMP is a home run on all fronts.  Although not inexpensive by any measure, the "event" nature of the restaurant makes up for it.  The concept menu is fascinating the wine list has something for everyone and every income.  As close to perfection as could be envisioned.

This was one of the best dining experiences and had near flawless execution.  The service was fantastic, food delish, and room beautiful.  We were there celebrating and were offered a tour of the kitchen, which was a lot of fun.

The food was divine, the service was over the top; actually it was "food theatre and arts."  I was hungry and left hungry, but it was a show of excellence in the kitchen and service overkill. We arrived early for lunch and were overwhelmed by the number of pleasant staffers greeting us. The environs are lovely, the flower arrangements are beyond, and you feel very special as you enter this large elegant space.
The food was spectacularly presented and elegantly prepared, but the service (performance) a bit over to the top (nah, it was WAY over the top).  It took two wait staff to deliver the rolls; one to hold the huge silver tray with two small, yet lovely rolls and one to carefully place the lovely creations and their accompanying butters on the table. AHHHHH Too much fuss and too much theatre for me.  We asked for more rolls--- EEK, I think we threw them a curve ball.  If you want to impress someone with a lovely celebration of food as art and theatre,  yes, take them to Eleven Madison,   you will not be disappointed. But don't go it you are actually hungry in the old fashioned way.
There is no perfection in this earthly plane, which is why I am certain this place must exist in another dimension.  If one day we live inside the Matrix, I will eat here every day.

Life. Changing. From the food to the service, my evening could only be described as 'exemplary.'

I can only recommend that you go to celebrate a special occasion - and make sure the wait staff knows when you make a reservation - and keep an open mind.

You will not be disappointed.

Soooooo, back in August, I had already started my review of Eleven Madison Park ("EMP").

It was titled "Going out with a BANG: New Job Edition" and I was planning to share that (a) my now-former employer gives us a budget for our "going-away" celebration and (b) being the dollar-stretcher that I am, I decided to bifurcate my "going-away" into (1) a relatively cost-efficient SSS cupcake party in one of our conference rooms and (2) a no-holds-barred poshy "associates-who-lunch" lunch at good ol' EMP.

This review, however, was never written. After it gathered dust in my "Finish My Review" queue for quite some time, the statute of limitations expired on finishing it. I remembered vaguely that I vastly enjoyed my experience; however, I wasn't able to pinpoint exactly why.

That said, I recently took myself to EMP for my birthday, and let's just say that my vague recollections now have concrete grounds upon which to be based.

This place deserves five stars. Period. It's fantastic and delicious and set in a beautiful space. Being the risk-averse conservative legal eagle that I am, I am always wary of outright statements (e.g., "this is the best" versus "this is one of the best"), but truly, this is the best.

An understated entrance in the side of the Credit Suisse building (NB: the reason that I recognize the address, i.e. the aforementioned  now-former employer, in and of itself would normally give me reason to shy away from this destination) leads to a spacious and elegant dining room with clean lines, dizzyingly high ceilings, and fresh flowers dangling from bare branches in Spartan test tube-like vases.

I was fifteen minutes late, about which I had called them earlier and for which I now apologized. "Not a problem, Miss J.," the hostess said with a smile as she took my coat, "Thank you for your call earlier - we appreciate your letting us know. Please, right this way."

I was seated at a booth that faced out onto the dining room. It was lunch on a Friday, and I spied any number of different patrons, from two twenty-something likely food-bloggers to a septuagenarian couple celebrating the wife's birthday.

The menu is now a simple sheet of paper with no separate a la carte options or chef's menu. Upon this sheet of paper were 4 rows of 4 words, 16 total. Pricing for lunch is either three courses ($56) or four courses ($74). The waiter explained that, after I chose one "main ingredient" in each row, the chef would create a dish around that ingredient. Thus, there is the surprise element of a chef's tasting menu while still leaving some of it to the diner's choice. After making my selections, I told the waiter that, other than an aversion to onions, I was up for anything the chef could dish out (hardy har har). I also ordered an Up the Alley (a "soft" cocktail), which was apple cider, maple syrup, lemon and sparkling cider.

There were some amuse bouche to start. All were excellent, but the standout in this cast was the hollowed egg shell with smoked sturgeon sabayon and chive oil. The bread was delicious, and the butter was oh-my-stars amazing. I was completely, utterly (udderly?) shameless and asked for some to take home. :D

The experience was divine, the food was delectable and decadent, and I felt like royalty throughout my entire meal (see: my solo diner theory).

I left a 30%+ tip, and I consider this meal the best $130 I've spent in NYC. (I couldn't help comparing it to my $190 spent at Momofuku Ko recently...and finding Ko vastly wanting.)

The meal, inter alia, crossed my place setting as follows:

Halibut dashi poured over a bundle of red seaweed & thyme 
Crisp Nori & sesame lavash flatbread
House smoked sturgeon sabayon served in a hollowed egg shell with chive oil on the bottom
Black truffle beignet with black truffle yogurt sauce 
Hamachi sashimi served with differents types of fennel & horseradish puree 
Coconut stuffed pan seared skate topped with curry foam & served with bok choy & dulce seaweed on the side (Mmmm...skate...)
Pork loin and confit pork belly cooked 72 hours served with apple variations, mustard spaetzle & bacon marmalade
Jasmine sorbet served on a layer of jasmine bavarois (I asked - this is custard that is solidified with gelatin) with cilantro gel, tangerine snow & jasmine foam 
Coconut sorbet and passion fruit sorbet & coconut merengue stuffed w passion fruit, served with fresh papaya & mango and topped with cookie crumbles 
Peanut tulle, violet & chocolate macaron & fruit gellies of tangerine & cassis

Interspersed were the little cheesy Gourges and French and olive breads with goat's mlk and cow's milk butters.

The only slightly disappointing thing was the Up the Alley drink. I didn't think it was all that special, and it reminded me too much of Martinelli's apple cider, which in and of itself was a throwback to birthdays of my childhood.

Overall, I loved my meal here, and I have to say...sorry, Jean-Georges, but I've found a new lover.

EMP...call me. ;)

The food was good, but unfortunately inconsistent. I went with Jurgen J. Some was better, the rest rather disappointing. Maybe my expectation was too high. The only thing that stood out was the truffle and dessert.

We had lunch here whilst on vacation in NYC and loved it. We opted for four courses with matched wines. The room is fantastic, it was a glorious sunny day and the light streaming in made the room look magical.

We opted for four courses, all of which were excellent. The concept of the menu has been explained in plenty of reviews, so I won't go into it in lots of detail. We ordered from the four choices and our waiter then asked us what we did and didn't like to ensure that the food matched our needs. The food was delicious, perfectly balanced flavours and decent sized portions that left you full, but not bursting.

Service was exquisite. Some reviewers have complained that it is over the top but we found that it was perfectly executed. It wasn't intrusive or overly stuffy. My only slight criticism was that when we ordered I explained that I didnt eat pork or shellfish (as I am Jewish) however was given a sturgeon amuse bouche, which I left. Perhaps this was my fault for not being so explicit with my instructions to our waiter.

We had a cocktail each, four courses, matched wines and coffee and the bill after tip came to $390. The following day we had dinner at the Gramercy Tavern and spent about the same and had to say that we thought that EMP was far far better.

As for dress code, my husband wore jeans, shirt and shoes (no trainers) for lunch and was appropriately dressed. We did see a guy there eating in jogging bottoms too!

so i am going to sound like my grandmother, but seriously what a pleasure eleven madison park was!

the restauarant is stunning, the food is magical and the service is beyond. i mentioned to my boyfriend during dinner that i was chilly and one of the waiters was tableside with a BOX of pashminas for me to choose from 30 seconds later.

 i really just can't say enough good things about dinner here. certainly somewhere to go for a special occassion when you want to languish over your meal and be surprised and delighted by each course.
Unbelievably good. To echo others, one of the best meals I have ever had. Totally worth it. Do it. Don't ask questions, just eat what they give you. They are geniuses.

I am a huge foie gras fan and after reading many reviews on certain restaurants Eleven Madison Park was one of my MUST GO TO's. 

For the noobies, how EMP works is by giving you a selection of ingredients (their so-called menu). You pick 1 ingredient for each course and the Chef will make it for you based on what you like and don't like. For me I picked out foie gras, truffle, muschovy duck (to share) and the hobelchas. The food was good, but it wasn't amazing. Overall I think it was a nice once in a life time experience. 

The service was amazing and so was the ambiance. I don't think I will be coming back though since I have had better.

Quite honestly one of the beast meals I have had in NY. I don't eat gluten and they even offered me gluten free substitutes even though I didn't inform them until I arrived. The dishes were all great, especially the pork and the desserts were very inventive and always well plated. 
We also did the wine selection flights with the meal and they were perfect.

Oh man, this is good. I had one of the best meals of my life here. The menu is fascinating, and makes it really exciting when the food arrives, as you know so little about what you're going to get. The service is amazing - knowledgeable and formal without being stuffy, and, in a nice touch, it's the chefs who serve you your canapes, amuse bouches and all the other little titbits you get between courses. The room is beautiful, especially the expansive, high ceilings, so you feel like you're dining in a cathedral :) 

But the food. Oh, the food. The most incredible, melt-in-the-mouth beef. Sole with the perfect, delicate mushroom sauce. An astounding rabbit and fois gras terrine (and I think terrine can be really dull, so all credit to them). A rich chocolate ganache that made me want to lick the plate clean. And my favourite thing of all was a petit four of 'truffled truffle' - truffle-flavoured icecream dipped in dark chocolate and rolled in truffle-flavoured crushed wafers. So it looked like a chocolate truffle and tasted of ACTUAL truffles. Sounds bizarre - tasted amazing.

If only I didn't live in London, I'd be back tomorrow.

We did the VEG tasting Menu for one of my aunt's 50th birthday party in a private room upstairs. The place is awesome. The wait staff was one of the best I have see in the city, they described everything perfectly and put on a show every-time they bought a new dish out. The ambiance of the was very fresh and modern. All the different wines/cocktais were great. The food was excellent.

This place is incredible.  Hands down.  
I work in the restaurant industry and this place was out of control!  Even I was baffled at the sort of "ballet" service you receive and the food is out of this world.  This is a real treat and you should soak in every moment.  I'm still reeling from the wonderful time I had.
One little suggestion to the first time diner: Don't let it intimidate you.  Relax and enjoy the ride.  Think of yourself sitting in a bentley, you probably wont do it every day, but don't forget to have some fun while your there!

My boyfriend and I made reservations for the two of us and his parents one month in advance.  We decided to do the tasting menu and three bottles of wine.  It seemed like we had five or six Amuse Bouche before we started the menu.  We started off with a goat cheese lollipop and a raspberry marshmallow, brioche toast with uni and shaved truffle, monk fish two ways, oysters two ways with caviar and a few more.  Then, the tasting menu dishes arrived.  The first dish was chicken soup thickened with flour and butter. It was amazing!  Then, we had langoustine soup which was great! Very refreshing.  Following these dishes were the foie gras with toast, carrots three ways, sea bass, lamb, and two desserts.  These dishes did not make anyone happy.  Unfortunately, after I had the langoustines, my stomach started to hurt and I had to take all of my dishes home.  Talk about expensive left overs for breakfast!  In all honesty, the food was just okay which was disappointing because up until the langoustine soup, we thought the meal would be pretty promising.  We thought wrong!  Regarding service, our waiter was snooty for most of the evening but he actually asked me if I wanted them to make me anything for my stomach. I asked for pasta with a little olive oil, salt and pepper which was yummy.  My BF's mother thought it was the best dish.  That just shows you how upsetting our meal was.  Maybe we should have tried ordering the four course meal instead.  OH WELL!

Dining at 11 Mad is an experience of a lifetime. If you are an adventurous diner, leave yourself in the hands of the expert chef and be prepared for some amazing and delicious surprises. We went for the tasting menu, which was expensive, but worthwhile. It's hard to remember or describe some of the dishes, but a couple things we experienced and loved were a sea urchin in gelee and en egg shell with a mixture of egg, fish and caviar which we went crazy over. Every night promises totally different dishes. Wine list is immense, but there are some reasonable and wonderful choices. I would go back at least once a year if I was splurging.

My girlfriend and I went here for an anniversary dinner.  The wait staff is second to none and has almost mastered the essential art of service: anticipation without intrusion.  The food was good (we went in the spring and got the spring tasting menu) but to be perfectly honest, I was a bit let down.  Between the reviews, the price and the difficulty in obtaining reservations, I was expecting to taste nirvana in every bite.  Perhaps, however, it was my own fault.  Being lactose intollerant I let that be known prior to ordering and regretted doing so the entire meal.  Where my girlfriend would get a delicious bisque, I would get a so-so borscht.  But the true torture was in the desert.  She received a panoply of delicious and varied miniature macarons (not too dry, not too gooey.  Just perfect, as I found out after...re appropriating one).  I however, got four fruit jelly candies that could have come out of my grandmother's house.  I was just about as disappointed as I could be, considering it was about cookies.

In sum, great service, good food that can't quite live up to its legendary hype, and a poor decision on my part.

My advice:  Go in expecting a great meal and don't mention any food allergies that won't kill you.

To me this place is like Disneyland. I really appreciate all the spectacle and showmanship, it was a lot of fun, I enjoy all the pomp and circumstance, but overall, at least in terms of what foods actually end up in my mouth, it's not for me. While others may be happy spinning around in a tea-cup, I prefer skydiving.

We started off with a cocktail, my friend (it was his birthday) got a Martini and I got a Flyfox (Genever Gin, Blanco Highland Tequila, Cocchi Americano, Mezcal, Concord Grape). His came on a push cart, our waitress nobly poured some Vermouth from a silver dripper, then liberally poured some ice-cold Vodka -- I tasted it, nice and crisp. Mine wasn't bitter or assertive enough to be memorable.

Then came the Gougeres. Which were bland and salty.

Then came the Truffle Toast and Chicken Veloute. Which were salty.

Then came the Sable Sabayon with Chive Oil. Which was salty.

Then came two different kinds of breads, which weren't anything special. They were accompanied by a bowl of Sea Salt and two kinds of Butter (Goat and Cow), which weren't particularly noteworthy.

Hamachi Sashimi with Fennel was nice, but not remarkable. It was nice that they tried to feature so many different components of the whole fennel plant, and also of the Meyer Lemon, but it really could've used some salt. Paired with white wine.

Crab with Tagliolini was salty and the meat was far from tender. It was paired with a terrific white wine, and then another white wine.

Both pieces of my boneless Rack of Lamb were improperly cooked. It was paired with an extremely sediment-heavy glass of red wine, which the Sommelier quickly observed, then gracefully replaced.

The Hobelchas cheese course was quirky, in that it featured four presentations of different textures, but was lacking in overall inspiration. Paired with white wine.

We shared the Coffee Siphon, which required our waitress to bring a large cart, boil water over a flame, blow air (from her mouth) upon the coffee pot, and constantly take temperatures with machines. Basically, it was a $22 science experiment, resulting in great coffee.

The Lemon Dessert was a bit of a mess, but thankfully rather tasty. It came with some ground up cake, some lemon-poppyseed crusts, preserved lemon, lemon ice cream, lemon foam, and green olives? Came with a glass of white wine.

Kir Royale (Creme de Cassis Sorbet with Cotton-Candy Candy-Canes and Lemon Emulsion), which came complimentary, was probably my favorite part of the meal. It was amazingly creative and delicious.

Peanut Butter Tuile and Chocolate-Dipped Banana Ice Cream with Peanut Butter Chunks and Sea Salt. These were just okay.

The last component of my meal, the Blackthorn Monk cocktail (London Dry Gin, Sloe Gin, Yellow Chartreuse, Dolin Dry Vermouth de Chambéry), was my second favorite part of the whole experience, and if I were to return, it will most likely be just to knock down a few of these beautiful babies.

Went here in a group of four and had great time.  Lots of amuse boucheseses (or whatever the plural is) with each one being better than the last. The little pieces of garlic bread with a black truffle butter were unbelievable.  One of the best things about this place is that they ask what things you like and don't like and make a meal tailored to you.  I really like Mac and Cheese, so the chef made a black truffle mac and cheese with linguine that absolutely amazing.

Everything here was off the charts good (other than the fennel, but that's just because I don't like fennel).  There is also a great drink selection including half and quarter cask scotches.  They even had a Cabernet made just for them.  I highly recommend this place as it is one of the best meals I've had in the city.

I have been here multiple times... Is it possible to give a restaurant 10 stars? I would if I could. This is the best restaurant I have ever been to in my life. 

Everything about eleven madison is perfect. The interior is beautiful. High ceilings, simple yet elegant decor that I want to say is in the style of art deco...

The service is amazing. Always and consistently the best I ever had. Danny Meyer has clearly figured out that fine dining is not just about the food (although, at the same time it totally is about the food) but... dining at eleven madison is an EXPERIENCE. The servers are beyond helpful and professional. I personally am not totally accustomed to such wonderful treatment... it almost feels awkward that they're so nice. But they'll definitely make you feel important. There was one waiter here who I especially loved who was also the bar captain (or some other fancy title) and he was so eloquent, although I think he left... the "waiters" here are no average waiters... They are all very well trained and informed and intelligent about their business. We asked one of the "bus girls" about her background and she had gone to the CIA and was an aspiring pastry chef. This might be typical for fine dining restaurants, but I guess this is all to say that Eleven Madison is at the top of it's game in this arena. 

As for the food...

I have never had a bad meal here. 

Last summer in 2009 I came here and ordered a beef medallion course encrusted with bone marrow. Oh god it was amazing. I dream about the courses I've had here. They also used to serve a sort of spring salad with egg, asparagus... 

but, I decided to wait before I reviewed this place because I had heard that they had a new menu. 

My dad was nice enough to take my boyfriend and I here in celebration of birthdays and new jobs...

We came here for lunch to try the new menu.

As you have probably heard -- 3 or 4 course menu in which you select single ingredients from a card... (ie. carrot, scallop, chicken, coconut.) 

We had the three course meal, and I admit that at first I was skeptical about this new menu with the lack of description. However, the truth about eleven madison is you have to go in knowing that you can trust the chef. Pretty much anything sent out is going to be delicious. They also accommodate to any allergies or specific tastes... for example, I'm not a huge fan of seafood.

they came with a series of amuse bouches that were all delicious. i won't do justice to the description of them... or to their deliciousness. this has to be seen and tasted to be believed. there were cheddar bread bites, egg with chive oil, mushroom/egg soup, chicken voulte with the most amazing brioche toast with white truffle butter and chives... 

then our appetizers...

carrots -- amazing roasted carrots with cumin, dates, and a sauce that was out of this world..

prawns -- my boyfriend had these. he loved them. 

we both had the lamb, which was amazing. served with jus... our waiter highly recommended it and he was right to do so. 

for dessert we had the coconut and chocolate... my chocolate was served with a butternut squash sorbet which was great. 

we also had two cocktails, and an alcoholic "hot chocolate" which had a house-made marshmallow that was very large and made with fresh vanilla bean. 

i feel ashamed that i can't describe any of these meals properly. this is genius food. it's beyond comprehension -- just know that whatever you eat will be amazing and worth it. i've listed eleven madison as the last meal i'd want to eat... for a reason.

I want to like 11 madison more than I do. I hadn't been there since Kerry was the chef and recently went back on my birthday. The new menu concept fails to deliver. The food is good but at this point? Nothing game changing. Service was very good, but I hesitate to consider this since I was with someone that people wanted to impress. The wine list also seemed a bit bland and corkage is insane if you don't know someone.

My complaint about the menu was that when I asked for an ingredient to be served a certain way (foie gras, seared with a berry sauce) I was told that it was terrine. So I gave up and just said however it's being done. Also ordered the steak. Guess what that was served with. Seared foie gras. Don't write checks your staff can't cash.

It's a shame because back in the day, I had some really good meals here.

I had the best meal of my life here last year (it was also one of the most expensive, but totally worth it).  I had the tasting menu and the wine pairing.  They actually missed wine pairings for couple amuse bouche courses, but I didn't mind too much because I was blown away by the food.  Everything were amazing, the one dish that I really loved was the cauliflower, cooked three ways, roasted, puree, and with cous cous.  I would like to have that for my last meal, it was perfect.

my girlfriend and i celebrated a one-year anniversary here.  fantastic as usual.  tried the new tasting menu option, which we were told was to be eight courses.  keeping track of this as the meal went on, i only counted six, but i guess they count the parade of canapes and the sorbet intermezzo as courses.  a little disappointed to see that most of the dishes using the ingredients that we'd sampled previously remained the same from our last visit two months ago, but they're all so great that it wasn't too much of a detraction, but a detraction nonetheless.  

highlights include... most of if not the entire meal:

two canapes stood out head and shoulders above all the others, though everything was really great (save for the monkfish on rice cracker.  that was bland.)  sea urchin on brioche toast with lemon gelee and grated foie gras.  combines what are among my absolute favorite things to eat in a two-bite dish.  superb.  also the slow poached egg with white truffle foam was unfair in its deliciousness.

a simple dish of roasted sunchokes with a couple sauces and some greens was astonishing.  i find well-prepared vegetables to be more impressive and indicative of a chef's mettle than meat dishes, as the latter is so intrinsically satisfying -- it takes a considerable amount of skill to make a plate of vegetables exciting to eat.  this was just that.

opted for the white truffle supplement as we were informed that white truffle season was over and what they had in the restaurant was the very last that they'd have for the year.  no regrets, even at $95.  the dish was exceptional.  fontina-stuffed... pasta (i don't remember the name) with chestnut puree, white truffle emulsion of some sort, and a grating of the most aromatic white truffles i've ever smelled in my life.  i've experienced some lackluster truffle preparations where they were simply thrown onto the dish (looking at you, gary danko) but this was such a perfect dish and showcased white truffle in all its great depth and earthy luxuriousness.

poached (?) striped bass with black truffle, artichokes, celery, and a black truffle sauce was worthy of le bernardin.  almost.

rack of lamb was served off the bone, normally an unforgivable offense except this was so beautifully prepared.  seasons and cooked perfectly, served with dandelion greens (i think), garlic confit, and a vadouvan-lamb jus.  very classic, very well executed.

the kir royale is among the best sorbet courses i've had the pleasure of enjoying.

coconut passionfruit vacherin.  gorgeously plated, so refreshing and sweet, a tropical vacation of a dish.  transportive.  the meringues, which i think were coconut flavored, were filled with passionfruit puree.   two sorbets on the plate -- guess which flavors -- as well as an arrangement of tropical fruits including a rather orgasmic brulee'd pineapple.  fucking amazing.

chocolate ganache with butternut squash sorbet and some sort of nut butter.  more in keeping with the season, really delicious.  the pastry team at emp is s o l i d.  i've loved every dessert i've had there.

oh, and the petit fours!  flash frozen banana covered in chocolate, rolled in almond, sprinkled with fleur de sel--my mouth misses it.  fennel macaron with grapefruit cream!  fuuuuuuuuck so good.  housemade peanut brittle was wonderful but eclipsed by the ingenuity and quality of the aforementioned.  then there's that crazy white truffle ice cream truffle that i'm certain will no longer exist, at least not until next white truffle season.  sigh.

there was wine, there was coffee.  and then there was the check.  bah.  as much as i love emp i feel like they slightly overestimate the monetary worth of the experience they provide. it made per se seem like a steal.

in my original review i claimed emp worthy of three michelin stars, and i'm not sure that stands.  (one is definitely not enough.)  i found that there's a lack of any real perspective or personality in the restaurant, which isn't to say it's soulless, but somewhat anonymous.  the cuisine is impeccable and delicious, sure, but there's nothing that ties it to the restaurant or separates it from the general crowd of this echelon of restaurant.  no doubt that this level is very high and that alone is worthy of merit but singularity is what make a restaurant truly special, even if it's as easy as exclusively serving seafood but doing it better than anyone else at le bernardin, or something as abstract as having the philosophy of its chef/owner be a unifying vision that permeates ever facet as it does at per se and the french laundry.  i like feeling as though what i'm experiencing and eating can't be had anywhere else, and i don't think emp quite has that.  but it's a great fucking restaurant and i will be back.  a more focused cuisine and a price adjustment would make me an instant regular, despite my shallow pockets.  then again, i'm just one person.

Class and greatness just pours from this wonferful revelation of a restaurant.
This place is beautiful in every sense of the word.

We were fans of Chef Humm when he was at Campton Place in San Francisco and it seems like he's done nothing but get even better since he came to New York.  Everything, and I do mean everything, was impeccable.  The sommelier was also spectacular.  An amazing experience overall, equal to or better than other restaurants at this price point, even those with more stars from Michelin.

A client brought me here a few months ago, I'm sure they thought I'd be terribly impressed, which I wasn't. Without going into detail, because my last review was yanked, I'll just say this: they serve foie gras. 

In Chicago--as many European countries have-- I believe they have outlawed it. i know it is illegal in California.

So my policy is not to patronize establishments who continue to offer it in light of how it is produced. 

BTW, the food was pretentious and pretty but mediocre.

The meal was simply a revelation.  Every dish was refined and thoughtful.  The flavours were complex yet perfectly balanced.   The food was contemporary and inventive without being overworked.  I love it when chefs make innovative dishes without going molecular and deconstructionist on me.  I can't believe they have only been awarded 1 Michelin star....they have definitely been cheated by the Michelin snobs.  

ATMOSPHERE - It's in the Credit Suisse building and the space occupies what used to be the lobby hence the soaring ceilings and gorgeous details and inlay.  I find the rest of the decor somewhat sterile.  There are wood paneled dividers separating the space, leather seating, and a mosaic floor, but it's not really a warm environment.

SERVICE - Impeccable.  The dishes were well paced and the waiters friendly.  There is a lot of pomp and circumstance.  When the bread comes, there are two waiters - one with a silver tray holding the goods and the other who introduces the two butters (cow and goat) in addition to the two breads (rosemary olive and plain French).  All this chatter over 2 pieces of bread.  It was slightly over the top.

FOOD - The menu contains a card with 4 rows (4 courses), each containing 4 ingredients.  All you get is the main ingredient and absolutely no other details.  This is an interesting concept for adventurous eaters but very few are truly adventurous (with many claiming they are).  The two tables flanking either side of us asked the waiter to describe every dish, probed into all the ingredients, specified what they would or would not eat, before deciding on their course choices 20 minutes later.  If you're going to offer this kind of spartan menu, you need to be a jerk about it.  You should get to clarify your allergies but be forced to entrust the kitchen with the rest of the details.  Otherwise, you might as well print a full menu and save the waiters the aggravation.

Amuse bouche #1 - Celery root soup, chicken soup, and toast with chives and butter.  

Amuse bouche #2 - This is one of those courses that I'll be talking about for the rest of my life.  The eggs have been stored with white truffles, which apparently allows the truffle aroma to infuse into the egg.  The egg is then poached, covered in a layer of foam, which has some truffle oil in it.  This dish was so fragrant and rich.  It was spectacular.

Foie gras - This was a smooth terrine with diced pineapples on top.  The second way it was served was as a foie brulee with a side of brioche.  Both were prepared perfectly.

Scallops - This dish was so light and lovely.  There were raw scallops atop persimmons.  The plating was both colourful and beautiful.

John Dory - Light fish poached in butter with flowers sprinkled on top.

Lobster - Poached in butter and lay atop butternut squash puree. There was also a flavourful demi glace.

Pork - There was a pork tenderloin that was sous vide (this was amazing tender and perfectly medium), the pork belly had a crispy skin with a fatty underside, and there was a lovely pig's head croquette.

Squab - This was so amazingly tender and cooked medium rare.  There was a thin bread crisp on top with chicken liver pate.  The dish also had some cabbage that complemented the squab well.

Amuse bouche #3 - Raspberry puree covered with a champagne foam.  The champagne foam had amazing flavour and was the perfect palate cleanser. The dish was also this interesting ceramic thing that was shaped like a pillow.

Coconut - Coconut and passion fruit sorbet with pieces of passion fruit and melon.  This was very light and perfect ending to the meal.

The plating was incredibly artistic and the food exceeded my expectations for a lunch time meal and $56 price tag. The kitchen is incredibly skilled and every dish was executed with perfection.  This is one of the best meals I've ever had and I would not hesitate to return for dinner.

This is a beautiful restaurant located on the base level of the Credit Suisse building.  My party and I decided to come here on the last minute and were lucky to secure a spot at 9:45 on a Thursday night.  Upon walking in, I noticed and immediately fell in love with the high (and i mean HIGH) ceiling here.  It's a rare sight to come by in NYC's restaurants.  

There are no descriptions on the menu besides the single words spaced out in four by four, so you have to ask your server how each dish comes prepared. We ordered our four-course meal in following combinations:

Foie Gras
White Truffle
Beef
Chocolate

Fennel
John Dory
Pork
Cranberry

I'll state my negatives first.  The amount of detail they put into every entree is amazing. Everything here is really top-notch.  So imagine my dissappointment when one of my favorite dishes of all time, Foie Gras, came TOO salty for my liking.  The taste was overrun by the saltiness that I couldn't help but wonder if it was an accident.  Fennel, on the other hand, was an "interesting" taste, a little intriguing at most, then it lost me. It was forgettable. White Truffle, already small in portion, came out in such a wide plate that I giggled aloud a little when the chef came out to describe our entree. 

Now, to the positives: they bring out one-of-a-kind snacks or appetizers before and in-between your entrees, and these are AMAZING! They were packed with so many different ingredients and textures all in a single bite that I didn't know what to think of the taste, other than that it was heavenly. I think I sat there with my eyes closed for a little bit. They were unique in presentation and taste and perhaps better than the actual course meals.  Also, their chocolate dessert was over the top. I was so full by the end of the meal that I didn't think it was humanly possible to eat any more, but I scraped the every last bit of the plate. I also found my favorite wine of all time here thanks to our sommelier: the David Aurthur wine.  Thank you!

All in all, a good dining experience. 5 for presentation, 4 for food, and 5 for interior aesthetics.
This place should be Michelin 3 stars.  I liked here better than Le Bernardin, Jean Georges or Per Se.  Go with wine pairing.  It's a good deal.

Having read the phrase "EMP has the best vegetarian tasting menu in Manhattan" on Yelp and Chowhound ad nauseum, to say my expectations (and anticipation) were high is not an overstatement. We began at the fanciful gourmand journey at 2:00pm and by 3:30pm, forcing down the final crumb of exquisite macrons, we were the last men standing in the shimmering gold deco dining room at the base of the iconic Met Life Tower.

As expected (I can't decide if it's funny or crass that these "compliments of the kitchen" types of bites are now expected in a tasting menu) we were presented with a square bowl of Gougeres. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=Tyx03v5A9fps9D6Hrk_4vQ The delicately cheesy bread is almost like eating air with carbs... 

While sipping my Blackberry Bramble, we were presented with diminutive duos of Melon with Radish and Chive/ Buttered Radish http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=AaeeOHQ2CAO98CFg57mXVA Though refreshing, they were barely notable... 

Corn Chowder, heaven in a cup! http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=XTJerenXvv8yuVYC8W7Jgw The creamy cold soup coats the mouth, easing the way for the crunchy dehydrated corn kernel and a paper thin slice of radish like a red round window into the bowl. A single stewed cherry tomato sits like an island with a single sprig of the very tip of a young basil plant atop it like a palm. With all my strength, I attempted to dent the porcelain side while digging out every last drop of sweetness from the bowl.

Then, out of the kitchen, came out the famous bread and butter course: A mellow salty Cow's milk from Beurremont of Vermont and grassy white as snow Goat's milk butter from Meyenberg of California. Along side the butters sat a dish of fleur de sel and a set of breads: Olive Ficelle loaf and a triangle of French bread. 

Our next course was a deconstructed Taboli salad. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=m3KCB5QH69wqez-wVGvlrw The dish held a waxing crescent of squash blossom, melon ribbons, radishes, parsley, mozzarella, baked tomato, mint and purslane on a bed of (of course) couscous. Normally these fancy deconstructions seem, at the best, unnecessary - while at the worst, pompous - but this was a strange case of "just right." 

Next came a thick slice of juicy Buffalo Mozzarella http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=QfohQqFugQ8GgdA0w4jtkQ with cherries, thin crisp raisin bread, pistachio, pearl onions, mustard vinaigrette, and a sprinkle of pistachio dust. Although delicious, I wish there had been a bit more cooking involved besides slicing a mozzarella ball... then again, it's not like the chef is back there stuffing corn down a goose's throat for the omnivore's foie gras... like mozzarella, he just bought it, sliced it, tossed it on a plate.

After the delightful fattiness of the previous course, we were presented with a menagerie of summertime memories in a bowl. Fresh sheets of pasta, rolled with herbs and stamped with leafy trademarks, were curled and layered with zucchini, paddy plant, squash blossom, oven roasted tomatoes, viola flowers, parsley, and lemon verbena to make up the Heirloom Squash Lasagna http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=1rr9NMDRYLZA02nQabBGiw The dish is finished with creamy foam, which I'm sure the waiter provided a description for, but which left just the lightest impression, so what does it even matter. 

And for the final (savory) presentation, we received multiple preparations of our respective vegetarian and omnivore ingredients. I received Eggplant 5 ways http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=RVd7gVWGEBGv9nBRUdMuHg - pan fried, breaded, chips, broiled, and er... something else. Served upon mozzarella, a littering of fresh peas, basil tips and other accoutrements, these aubergines barreled into the battle of reestablishing my affections for this commonly over-played "vegetarian" vegetable. Considering EMP makes no explicative gesture to vegetarian other then by reputation, the chef didn't phone this dish in (like most drab vegetarian options). This dish was a playful and intelligent exploration of a vegetable that up until this point, I thought I had eaten every which way... 

Red Velvet Cake http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=mH17XhHw7LK0RXe6fhJi8Q with cream cheese parfait, roasted strawberry ice cream and red currants and freeze-dried fruit bits sprinkled around. This extra fancy post-modern rectangle was a bland and, at moments, sour end to the decadent lunch.   

And to finish it off, in the grand tradition of EMP, Macarons! http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=XIZ93IR3Yrj2GDlhs_Wf8A&select=O6e0UxH9E3Mp0zq71rfE3w

It is as good as they say....especially when you have the ultimate experience.

I go here quite often, especially to the bar for a quick after work cocktail (ask Leo for the "Hot Trolly" haha) and usually this turns into dinner.

We had a pluthera of food. We initially ordered the Duck (which, you will die over) and some salads, but the chef brought out an amazing one-of-a-kind tasting menu. I can't even describe to you the flavors my mouth experienced. Halibut chunks with a warm frothy butter cream sauce, served in an egg shell. Oysters in a kiwi dill sauce, with caviar. Ahhhh diiiiieeee I tell you. 

More small tastes came out, but we were a bottle deep (or two) into Chateau Margaux from '85, so I wasn't listening to what it was...just enjoying.

The service is amazing, the people are young, fresh, efficent, hard working and knowledgable. They always treat you as if you are their only customer, or better yet their friend. 

Okay so the food,.....the menu changes, which I love because it means the chef knows how to go with what is fresh, in season and good rather than forcing hormones into an animal so we can get salmon in the inappropriate season.

Duck: I hate duck, I hate gamey food...gross...it just tastes fatty and nasty. However, THIS DUCK was melt in your mouth amazing. I am salivating over this just thinking about it. It was cooked to perfection and seasoned well. 

The salad was a salad, it was great though.

Desert, awesome choclate cake...i was wasted by this point so I don't recall it. Plus, I was full.

All in all, I try to go here at least once a week for dinner. Amazing. Eleven madison is the epitome of fine dining.

This is a serious foodie paradise.  If you typically order a burger and fries, or couldn't care less about the way food is normally presented.  Then let me give you a tip.... save your credit card a lot of stress and stay home and get Luke's takeout.  Now back to Eleven Madison Park... I've really never tried better food in my life. We decided to do the tasting menu, which ended up being about 8 or 9 courses.  Although really tempting, I decided not to order the wine parings, because I knew if I did that I'd be sleeping 1/2 way though the meal.  The dinner really is a true event.  We arrived at 8:30 and didn't finish dinner until well after midnight.  The dishes the chef chose were just amazing. Wonderful taste combinations, and a beautiful presentation.  My mouth was having a party after every course.  The most inventive dish was probably the goat cheese popsicles.  I've never seen or tried something like that before.  The cocktails were delicious and equally beautifully presented.  The bartender even came out to talk to my boyfriend about what type of drinks he normally likes so that he could prepare him a unique cocktail, came back to pour it, and finally a third time to make sure he was enjoying it.  Wonderful service overall! My water glass never dropped below 1/2 full and everything I could desire the servers took care of. Although Asiate is still tops on my list for ambiance, Eleven Madison park is in a league of its own for food quality and presentation.  I would highly recommend this restaurant for a special night out. Anyone you bring here will be wowed, and if they aren't, they probably would have been fine with a McD's burger :-)

This is one of the best restaurants ever.  The service I had was perfect and exceeded expectations.  The staff was extremely professional without being too stuffy.  I had four courses which included scallops, cauliflower, beef and a chocolate desert. The menu contains no details requiring you to rely on the staff for details and they're very good about making sure you don't get anything you don't like.  The wine and the after-dinner drink (a bottle of scotch, compliments of the restaurant) were amazing as well.  All in all it was a great dinner on a cold winter night in New York City.  This place is for special occasions or business meetings.  It's very special.

I've decided to try as many restaurants as I possibly can named on the S. Pellegrino World's 50 Best Restaurants 2010 list. Two days after I found this list I found out that we were heading to New York for a day. I tried to make a reservation at all the NYC based restaurants on the list, but could only get into one. (Per Se I will be coming back for you!)

Eleven Madison Park is ranked at number 50 on this list. I'm not really sure how it made the cut. I've been to a few restaurants that were not on the list, but were far superior to this one. This restaurant was about a 7 out of 10. I'm happy that I tried it, but will not be revisiting it again anytime soon. It was 11 courses with many very unique dishes. They were all very well presented and looked delicious, but all were lacking flavor (yes even the DESSERT!).

www.anitaeat.com

This place is to die for (at least until you see the bill! ^^ but totally worth it)
The bartender took his time to make each drink with care..and it tasted great...My angus beef and foie gras arrived...it was well presented. The foie gras was very tasty and it melted in my mouth. Beef was tender and yum....I need to go back to try other dishes!

The pinnacle of fine dining.     Bring your Gold card and a very light appetite because your stomach won't be full but your wallet will be empty.

Sit back and enjoy - the food here is really top notch.    Tasting menu satisfies.

If you're not a "foodie" you will probably be disappointed.

I had the best meal of my life at 11 Madison, and that's including all of the amazing food I've had in Paris. Every single course was phenomenal. It was artfully plated and an absolute pleasure to eat. I've never felt more excitement or surprise while consuming a meal. This is now the place to beat in my book. I will gauge all future culinary experiences by this meal. I can't say enough good things about this restaurant. 

In addition to the food the service was also impeccable, operating like a well-oiled machine. Each table was waited on by several servers, not allowing an empty plate or crumb to sit unattended to. I would  highly recommend this restaurant to anyone that is an avid food lover. I will definitely be back here the next time I'm in New York. What a treat!

100% lives up to hype. If you have an occasion for a meal of this caliber (like 10 year wedding anniversary) I cannot more highly recommend EMP. The style of service is a bit hushed for my liking, but leave it to us to pull those servers out of their shells. Also, every dish was phenomenal & the many added courses before dinner, between dinner & dessert & the après course were all something to write home about. Loved it, would rec it to friends and would return in a hot second given the opportunity.
beautiful restaurant, excellent excellent service and awesome food. the amuse bouches were my favorite but all the 4 courses were amazing. pricey but def worth it for a special occasion.

A girl can get use to this! as my best friend said during dinner.  This was a BFF dinner for me on a Friday night. I love the double ceiling place and cozy decor.  The center pieces looked like they are ready for a wedding reception everyday!

Service was amazing, lots of various different servers making switching 8 courses seamless.  They have a very extensive wine list which I couldn't even finish reading.  Overall they had very innovative appetizers, but very traditional entree courses.  Compared to my other new favorite french restaurant recette, think recette was just a star more than eleven madison (even though this place is way more upscale)

We decided to go with the 8 course 3 hour commitment with two half bottles of wine.  It was a great experience overall. I was very amazed at the different texture and ingredients they used. Shaved foie gras, goat cheese ice lollipop, oyster with dill and caviar.. the appetizers were amazing. leading up to the raw lobsters with mangosteen, foie gras dish with sweet garlic and fruit, john dory fish, venison with some amazing cabbage and the best cauliflower I tasted! 

oh i love loved the Kir royale dish of the desert! who wouldn't love deliciousness on a ceramic pillow? champagne emulsion perfection!

Various chocolate, powdered sugar and ice cream followed. I really appreciate the mixed use of texture in one dish.  Final little pieces of macaroons, white trouble and dark chocolate etc. were just over the top but i've never tasted so many different things in one setting.  

I think it was definitely an experience. Considering someone got engaged the same night says a lot about the type of occasions people come here for.  

Last but not least a glass bottle of granolas for the morning. how thoughtful.

If it's your birthday, or 50th wedding anniversary, or you've just won the nobel prize, this is the place to celebrate. Chef Daniel Humm is a tour de force of perfection and GM Will Guidara has created the perfect dining experience. Every detail is equisite, but forget about your diet and don't make plans for afterwards because you may need a few hours to come back to earth.

Prompted by Yelp's spectacular reviews, my wife and I made a reservation and headed over to 11MP after her guitar lesson at The Guitar School.

The place was full of good-looking, conservatively and well-dressed attractive young white people, whose smiles were genuine and welcome was warm.  We were seated at a lovely, comfortable bench appropriate to the romantic evening we had in mind, in a large room elegantly windowed and ceilinged on the cusp of post-classical monumentalism and art deco, where still more nice young white people served us appetizers, drinks, and menus.

My wife had spent much of the day working with Congolese refugee women, and when the menu arrived, with its $120+/person prix fixe options, we asked if we could share one.   This was after I had ordered a double single malt.   The obliging waiter conferred with the head somebody and apologetically reported back that, no; dinners were per person, and could not be shared among plates.   A la carte was not in the cards.

The thought of spending close to $300 on dinner for two, when that amount could probably help four, five, or six Congolese women survive with their families was not something my wife was prepared to do, so we made our own apologies and announced our imminent departure.

The waiter returned and let us know, among other niceties, that:

1.  My drink, which probably cost in the neighborhood of $40, would be on the house.
2.  He hoped we might return for lunch, when the fare was more adaptable and the costs more modest.
3.  Everyone was very glad for our appearance and custom.

I thought their reaction to our moral dismissal of such splendor was pretty classy, not to mention tactful and gracious.

The food?   The drink was really single malt, which most Manhattan bars cheat on.   Nor was it watered down, an almost universal custom on that island, which seems to correlate with cost.  The more money you spend on a single malt, the likelier it is to be watered down,and even more likely a high-year Scotch than single malt.   The appetizers were elegant and tasty.   The service was gracious.

So for those of you who aren't bothered by $300/couple dinners, it comes highly recommended.  Personally, I prefer lower-budget ethnic restaurants, to one of which we repaired.   But for what it is, 11MP is a wonderful place; and we were glad to see how the other .07% lives, or at least eats.

This has been on the top of many professional food ranking lists (as well as my own for a very long time) and it did not disappoint! Service is impeccable, honestly nicest, most accomodating, friendliest staff ever!  Food is very delicious - it changes daily. Essentially you get a bingo like 4x4 card that contains primary ingredient options for you to choose (e.g. Fish, Beef, Venison, White Truffles, Tuna, Apple)- each row represents a course from appetizers to desserts.  We went for the ambitious 5 course (the 5th being a whole duck with huckleberry that the table shared) but I think 4 courses is definitely more than enough food, especially with 3 rounds of amuse bouche and many mignardises - we barely dented the extra 5th course. White truffles was an extra $95 but worth it to at least try once!  Foie gras was very light and creamy, but preferred the raw tuna preparation instead. Lobster was delightful, venison my fave of the meats, followed by the beef (pork was too heavy for me).  Vanilla soufflé was intensely refreshing, chocolate was very rich, and cheeses were a bad choice for how full I was at the end... mignardises were fabulous (white truffle chocolate but with actual mushrooms, candy apple pops, thin wafer-like peanut butter brittle) AND THEN we had some pear brandy to finish plus a take home gift of a glass jar of nutty sweet granola
My favorite restaurant ever! The most tasty and innovative dishes that I have ever had! The tasting menu is worth every penny!

Simply amazing! Deliciously addictive... I won't go into all the details of the courses since you can get that from all the other reviews, but everything from the food (specifically the innovative flavor combinations and textures) to the service, to the whole experience was impeccable. I will say the white truffle dish was utterly orgasmic (hubby agrees). The wait staff made it an unforgettable night. It was as if they could read our minds... They truly take service to the next level here - I'd say this is one of my top restaurant experiences ever (and that's saying a lot)! 

The kitchen tour with the extra dessert at the chef's table was a brilliant touch (pop rocks in my dessert - mouth explosion!!) and every turn was full of surprises. After the kitchen tour, instead of going back to our dining table, they led us to the small lounge area where we were treated to a fiery drink and more amazing little desserts! To top it off, they give you a jar of granola for the next morning - it's all these little touches that make Eleven Madison Park a notch above what you'd expect from any top restaurant. My new favorite restaurant in NYC... i will be back!

Best dinner EVER.  I can't even begin to explain it.  Yes, it's a bit expensive... but it's well worth the price.  All I can say is, you have to experience it to know why everyone RAVES about this place.

I'm having a hard time finding any sort of criticism, except maybe for the price point.  Celebrating a special occasion?  This is your place.  Lovely space, comically efficient waitstaff (at one point it felt like the ratio of staff to patrons was 1:1), very interesting food combinations that were spot-on.  Delicious cocktails, interesting wine list, and the personalization of the menu for your tastes makes you feel like your $ are well spent here.  For the same price ($125) you can go to Momofuku Ko and be disappointed, or come here and be smitten.

Have been here a couple of times when visiting NY and have always enjoyed dining here. Made reservations on a week night for the early bird special with in-laws (both in their 70s) who were visiting from Ireland.

Arrived to a virtually empty restaurant and were made to feel rushed as we had a cocktail in the bar. We were quickly seated in the main dining room with a pretentious 4 course prix fixe for $125.  Ummm...HELLO!!!  All of us glanced at the menu with confusion.  All of the courses had one word next to them them "Beef", "Pork", etc.  WTF?  Imagine my confusion - now imagine my in-laws confusion!!!  Please!  Even the patrons sitting next to us looked at the menu the same way.

Asked if we could order off the ala carte menu to accommodate my father-n-law and was told "yes".  When the rest of us asked if we could order off the ala carte menu, we were told emphatically, "No" (insert attitude) and that we would have to move to the bar for that menu.  So, we did!  Two seconds later, I get an email from Open Table ***CANCELING*** my reservation at Eleven Madison.  Really?  I'm still here...HELLO!

$500+ later for dinner/drinks in the bar was excessive - even by NY standards.  Unfortunately, we will never go back or refer anyone to this restaurant.  What use to be a fun experience has taken a detour and is now a joke.  Save yourself the heartache and dine elsewhere.  NY has so many more better restaurants (without attitude) to experience!!!

A fantastic meal.  If not for one service mishap, it would definitely be 5 stars.

We started with a series of amuse-bouches.  The sturgeon sabayon with chive oil was the best - in that it was mind blowingly good.  The others dishes such as the salmon with melon and potato tea were also great... but they did not blow my mind.

As for the main meal, the waiters comes up and asks you for likes and dislikes, etc.  Our rules were simple... we don't eat pork and we really like avocado.   We chose the 4-course meal and enjoyed pretty much everything.  The sole with hen of wood mushooms, the foie gras, and the short rib were the most memorable.  I was also pleased that they incorporated avocado into our tuna dish.

I must also add that the sommelier was great.  He suggested a very reasonable red wine - the Corison Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon -  it was just perfect.

Now, I know this reads like a 5-star review.  But, I was upset by a service mishap.  We ordered shrimp and it came with a butternut squash puree and two strips of bacon were served over the shrimp.  To me, the fact that a restaurant that encourages a "dialogue" would serve us bacon when we very plainly stipulated that we do not eat pork was unacceptable.  We pointed this out to the waiter and he was extremely apologetic.  We quickly got a new shrimp dish.  It was identical to the last one... except it was now without the bacon.  It seems like a cop-out to make the identical dish minus one ingredient.  Isn't the whole point of the menu to customize the meal?  Couldn't they come up with a more creative way to highlight the shrimp?  Also, I didn't really like the dish - the butternut squash overpowered the shrimp and it was too sweet.

Anyway, great meal marred by one service mishap.  While it did not ruin the meal, it prevents me from giving 5 stars.

Best lunch I have ever had and can't wait to go back! The new menu is very cool, the extra things they bring out are all very innovating, thought provoking, and enjoyable. The wine pairing is amazing. They brought out for one dish a champagne, and mixed it with half ungi blanc, I have never seen something like this formally served. There were 6 wines for a 4 course meal. Way more than I expected. They bring you into the kitchen to see the staff, and make you something while you are in there watching! Not only that but they send you home with a jar full of granola. The experience of the meal lives on after you get home, and it is amazing. Chef Daniel Humm also came by during the meal and introduced himself! This was a very exciting meal on very many levels, thoroughly enjoyed.
Most amazing meal of my life!  Everything was better than I could imagine and the service was perfect.

What can  be said that has not been said? Probably the best meal I have ever had and quite certainly the best lunch. 

Our hosts and waiters were outstanding. When I had a question about a dish, the cook was happy to answer it. 

Also of note was the pairing of a wonderful beer that was selected as part of my "wine" pairing. It went beautifully with my foie gras.

This trip to NYC we visited Graffiti, WD-50 and other heavy hitters. Eleven Madison Park was the real standout. 

Not to be missed!

Awesome!
Beautiful room. Fantastic food and drinks at the bar.

Feels  big time, old school new york.

Only complaint :PRICEY!

but totally worth it

This was hands down one of the most disappointing restaurants I've ever been to.  Each course was worse than the last one.  The restaurat in general was very stuffy and bland and we were hoping that the food would make up for the unimpressive ambiance, but that certainly was NOT the case.  It was painful to pay the bill, which was so atrocious given the quality of the food.  Needless to say, we will NEVER return to this restaurant.

Disappointing meal!

Small Portions! 

Not very flavorful!

Ignore the hype! 

This restaurant emphasizes form over function. In other words, the food is pretty but lacks flavor. The service is efficient but rather robotic.  This restaurant has no soul. If you want delicious food and great service, skip EMP and go to Jean georges instead.  On the bright side, the wine and champagne selection is incredible! And the room is beautiful and comfortable. Also, skip the coffee service. Again, its all show and no taste.

Beautiful place, exquisite and friendly service and really interesting dishes.  I don't eat at many places at this price level so I can't offer much comparison. 

My only criticism is that I thought based on the NYT review on the new menu that the waiters would want to know how you like things prepared.  But other than asking the standard questions for a tasting menu about allergies and things you really don't like to eat, there was no dialogue.  

Still it was a unique and enjoyable dining experience.

This has been our favorite restaurant in NYC, but we were worried about the new menu changes.  We needn't have worried.  It is better than ever.  You choose either a 4 or 5 course tasting menu, pick from one of 4 items for each course and let the chef take it from there.  The staff is amazingly efficient, yet friendly and not pretentious.  The food is really creative and each bite is bursting with flavor.  If you have only one restaurant to try in NYC, this should be it.  The best meal ever.

It's a little hard for me to rate this place. I won't discuss the food as that is gone over in much detail here (and everywhere on the internet), except to say that, naturally, it was some of the best I'd ever had. The service was also notable, and they really excel at the combination of friendliness and great service (unlike, say, the Modern, which veers way on the stuffy side). 

However, the feeling that I "took away" from my dinner was that $500 is a little much to pay for one meal, even if it is the best meal of your life. And this was PRE price hike.

If other places are good, this place 'god.' The entire dinner was not merely food but an experience. Price is high but worth every PENNY(a lot of penny that is). 4 course meal was $125 and 5 course meal is 150 per person. How it works is that you pick the main ingredient of each course from the menu and tell them something you just can't have or don't like. Interesting thing was some of the kitchen staff were serving and explaining the dishes. It was great feeling to have someone who made the dish comes to explain gorgeous dishes one after another. My favorite was the tomato tea. It looks like a clear green tea with herb inside but boy it tasted like tomato soup. Service is amazing: I got my water glass filled every time I drank the water. Plus we did the kitchen tour where we got to go to check out the kitchen. Not only did we get to see how our food was made, we got to stand behind this stand set up facing the kitchen and one of the chef made a frozen liquor dish using liquified nitrogen and pop rocks. How cool is that? My palate was in heaven. Please do try.
Wish places like this existed in Chicago. Loved everything about my experience here. Gotta go back because I heard they've tweaked everything a bit, including only serving one menu.

Alright it's a little hard to review this place. I chose to eat here after hearing and reading amazing things about this place. I came here on New Years Eve for dinner and when I made a reservation, they mentioned a prix fixe NYE menu (which i thought was optional) HAHA, not optional, it was the only thing that night. We were too embarrassed to just get up and leave so we stayed and ate that $$$ meal. With tax and tip, it ended up being $1000 for a party of two, not including any wine. The 7 course dinner was pretty amazing - it consisted of foie gras, lobster, fish, lamb, truffles and desserts. The place is decorated beautifully (like places where Bruce Wayne would host parties in the movies). I enjoyed the food, it had a very umami taste to everything. it was harder to enjoy knowing that my boyfriend and I dished out $1000 on one meal, prior to this, the most we've spent on dinner was $375, a huge difference! I would come here again but when they don't have that NYE menu...ha

Food: 8.5
Decor: 9
Service: 9

*ratings out of 10

Perfect service. The staff cater to your needs and are extremely polite to the guests. The food was beautifully prepared and seasoning was on point. The only negative I have to write is about one of the appetizers- please do not eat the carrot marshmallow. My whole table looked like they were going to be sick.

Wow.... not sure why it took me this long to write a review.

IMPECCABLE SERVICE!

Food was beautifully presented. Everything was delicious, but obviously there are always highlights to every meal. Some dishes were amazing, others were well executed and tasty, but for some reason or another didn't strike a chord with me.

I think when it came down to it, the special touches through out the meal made the experience.

This is definitely the first restaurant that I've been to that offered a purse table hook as an amenity...

Great Service, Great Staff!

We went for lunch and everything was very good.  I had king crab and pasta which was good and the pork for entree.  The pork belly was good but the loin was overcooked.  Overall very good and want to come back and try dinner to get the full experience.

With its high ceilings, huge windows and tasteful decor , Eleven Madison Park has one of most beautiful dining rooms in NYC. 

Unfortunately for us, we got a server who seemed uninterested in serving us. She seemed a lot less friendly than the other servers and we would've really appreciated an explanation as to why there was almost an hour wait between our appetizers and entrees. Thank God we ordered beverages a bit after the appetizers were taken away. Otherwise, we would've been sitting at an empty table for way too long. A 2-3 course lunch should not take two hours. The entire tasting menu at WD-50 only took 2.5 hours, with normal-length breaks between the courses.

The food was all beautifully presented, but taste-wise it fell just a touch short. 

Amuse bouches - Loved the black pepper cracker with foie gras and strawberry jelly. It was such a tasty, creamy, crunchy sweet bite. However, I just couldn't get into the beet marshmallow. It had a weird taste I wasn't fond of.

Spaetzle w/ Numan Ranch Pork Belly, Pommery Mustard and Spinach - If you love mustard, this is the dish for you, as the dish features a lovely mustardy sauce that added some extra kick to the spinach and very yummy pork belly. My only complaint is that I wish there was more than one piece of the delicious pork belly!

Tagliolini w/ Alaskan King Crab, Black Pepper and Lemon - This dish was very lemony with not enough pepper taste to balance it out. At times, it seemed like the lemon overwhelmed the lightness of the crab.

Seared Diver Scallop, with Succotash, Watercress and Red Pepper Nage - I had a taste of this (my friend ordered it) and the scallop was cooked to perfection. 

Coke Float - white tea, licorice, house-made grenadine, egg yolk, and Coca-Cola - This sounds gross, but it's actually quite tasty. It has the creaminess of the ice cream without any actual ice cream in it. It doesn't look like much, but it did taste good!

Orange Julius - orange juice, cream, orange blossom, honey and sparkling mineral water - My friend ordered this and it tastes exactly like the Orange Julius drinks I remembered. If I had ordered a second beverage, I probably would've gotten this.

St. Canut Cochon de Lait with Bing Cherries, Sweet Onion and Mustard - The pork was a little dry in this dish, which was disappointing. However, really loved how all the flavors worked together. The sauce was a little on the salty side though.

Nova Scotia Lobster Lasagna with Lemon Verbena and Heirloom Squash - I stole a bite or two of this and it was quite tasty, although I think it barely looks like a lasagna! Pretty generous on the lobster too. =)

Strawberry Shortcake - I couldn't resist the dessert trolley. The strawberries were tiny, beautiful and oh so sweet. What a great dessert.

Eleven Madison opened 11 years ago.  I ate there shortly after it opened, and I thought it was a pleasant but not exceptional dining experience.
Over the years this Danny Meyer restaurant has evolved into a truly special restaurant. The setting is very dramatic with ceilings at least 40 feet high. With that kind of volume it lacks a certain intimacy.

The service is exceptional without being overly fawning. Area around the table can get pretty crowded with all the servers.

The menu is reasonably broad and there are no weak items. The wine list is extensive with great selections from France and Italy. California is represented but not so much. Strangely, there are no Australian wines. I often get an Australian Shiraz because they can be pretty formidable and much more drinkable at a young age than a Bordeaux or Cabernet.

Everything is bigger in Texas, right? Eleven Madison Park didn't get the memo. Not that I'm really complaining but the portions here are massive. Seriously, massive. So massive and so good that I gorged myself to a tipping point. 

We did the summer lunch menus-- another robbery at around $30 for two courses. I started with a really light, complex big eye tuna tartare which was great. Admittedly, my palate is a little bit of a clusterfuck but this is something I'd start my meal off with any time. She got an amazing taglioni with alaskan king crab. This was the best dish of lunch between both of us. It was really flavorful without being too heavy and there was a wonderful taste of the sea to it-- we both loved it. Again, the portion was huge, though. I thought for sure she'd be full after eating it and to a certain extent she was. 

For our main entrees, I got the marrow-crusted filet ($15 supplement) and she got the lobster ($15 supplement). I think her dish was too heavy. Especially after the heavy pasta first course, it was just difficult to finish the entire thing--again, a huge portion of lobster. My dish was great but huge. To give you an idea how big it was, it was TWO cuts of meat - one marrow-crusted, the other without, TWO portions of mashed potatos, four mushrooms, and then something like pot roast to the side.
