I was stuffed after the first non marrow-crusted piece, and it was one of the best entrees I've had in recent memory... but then I tried to and finished the rest of my plate. Felt like I was going to burst-- sorta uncomfortable for the rest of the day afterward. 

For dessert, we shared a cookie platter which is basically 8-9 bite sized macarons. Each one was an adventure, no joke. Best part of the meal. 

Service was perfect. Seriously perfect. From the hostesses to our two revolving waiter/waitresses. The space was beautiful, with a huge flower arrangement and all sorts of nice pictures, plants, awards. I'm wavering now and think I should give this place five stars but will stick to my rating. Who am I, anyway...

The food was great.  I had the lamb.  It's all good.  Fancy as all get out, shmancier than I remember than a few years ago.  But this is a testament to attentiveness!  Listen:

It's across the street from the Shake Shack. I love me some Shake Shack. As we were ordering, I said that they should just give us milkshakes from across the street. My brother then admitted he had never had Shake Shack, and I spent the next 10 minutes describing in horrific detail everything that makes Shake Shack fantastic. We joke that after dessert we'll go get some.

So we enjoy our dinner. It was great. We order dessert. A few minutes later the wait staff comes by with four covered dishes, all fancy/french, and upon the simultaneous removal of the tops:

Shake Shack Custard. A unique flavor for each of us.

The maître d' then explained that she had walked by our table 3 times over 30 minutes, and each time she overheard us going on about ice cream or Shake Shack. Being a Shake Shack fan herself she dug it, and voila, surprise ice cream.

NOTHING IN THIS GREAT WORLD SURPASSES SURPRISE ICE CREAM.

Nothing.

So here's to 11 Madison and the best maître d' evar.

My hubby and me had outstanding experience here for our engagement announcement to my parents, here.

My hubby was in floods of sweat from the nervousness (meeting my parents of course), but we all enjoyed their elegant service and atmosphere.

Everything taste AMAZING and each meal had wonderful presentations. 
Great champagne we all had as well.

I would give 10 stars if I could.
Great great restaurant!

http://sportsfoodie.tumblr.com/post/977775553/eleven-madison-park-the-miami-heat-of-ducks 

Eleven Madison Park. 

Does that sound like an elegant place to you? Well it is. It oozes elegance like an Alec Baldwin voice over 

Like Goodwill Ambassador Angelina Jolie 

(Not Crazy Angelina Jolie) 

As with most fine establishments, the first thing you notice about Eleven Madison Park is the room itself (pictured above). A high vaulted, two story space...EMP has a Roaring 20's New York feel to it. A throwback vibe and decor that is serious, not overly stuffy, but impressive nonetheless 
The staff is great. Attentive and consistent without being elegantly up in your grill. Just the right balance. 

Lastly, it was my 13th Anniversary, and the menu had a "Happy Anniversary" note on it. Simple, but a nice and appreciated touch. 

The Chef, Daniel Humm, recently won the James Beard award for best new chef of 2010. While he puts a major emphasis on classical French cooking, he is also up on the current gastro-trends and is not afraid to experiment. Boulud meets Dufresne. The amuse-bouche was a strong start and tipped more towards experimental than classic. 
What's that pink square at the end of the plate? That's a beet marshmallow. I cant recall the other 4 items verbatim, but they were equally delicious and a touch odd. Also, who doesn't like cheesy poof balls? 

Next up was a Strawberry Gazpacho. Now, this also sounds more Experimental than Classical, but I'd say that it actually leaned more towards the latter. A highly distinct palette with an emphasis on a perfect flavor balance. You want to try this at home? Have some! 

http://nymag.com/listings/recipe/strawberry-gazpacho/ 

We moved on to salad, where I ordered the Heirloom Tomato with Mozzarella Ice Cream and Basil Granola. The Farmer's market tomatoes were fantastic while the Ice Cream Mozz....hold up! Ice Cream Mozzarella?! Wouldn't regular non-frozen Mozzarella do perfectly ok here? The answer is yes...I think this one instance where the experimentation got in the way of a more pure indulgence. 

Mrs. Foodie had the Goat's Milk ricotta gnocchi with artichoke, olives and bacon. One of the best dishes of the night. Perfect really. 

Speaking of Goat's Milk, one of the pleasures we most enjoyed at EMP was the bread served with a goat's milk butter. Flown in from a mico-distributor in California, this was a minor masterpiece. A great grassy flavor, yet still distinctively butter. 

For the mid course, I tried the Cochon De Lait (suckling pig) with bing cherries, spring onion + ice wine vinegar. Chef Humm is big on the cherries (as they remain in season) and the tartness worked well against the expertly cooked pig. 

Mrs. Foodie went Nova Scotia Lobster - Poached with Young Carrots, Ginger, and Vadouvan Granola. The sauce was decadence defined. One of the strongest dishes of the night. 

As exceptional as the meal had been thus far, all of this was just a long, slow wind-up to the main course. Duck. And not just any duck mind you, but Grimaud Farms Muscovy Duck (from Central Valley, California). It's where all of the best ducks in the country go to hang out together. It's the Miami Heat of ducks. And guess what? You can purchase them here: 

http://www.grimaudfarms.com/purchase.htm 

However, you'll be hard pressed to cook this duck as perfectly as Daniel Humm + Team. The cooked whole duck comes to your table where they prepare it for you at a personal carving station. They serve only the breasts, and garnish with a peach confit. 

Rarely have I had duck that has not been ruined by too much fat (with the notable exception of Momofuku Ko and a few old-school Chinese Peking Duck fests). But this duck blew all competitors away. The skin was incredibly crispy with a salty, crackling rub. However, the inside was moist, tender, lean, and cooked to medium perfection. That juxtaposition of texture and flavor was truly blissful. Melting into our chairs, we ate rather silently, basking in the satisfaction of a perfect plate. The only other tip I would offer here would be to order a glass of Grenache, which offered a wonderful compliment to this incredible dish. 
Lastly, we went with a really fine cheese assortment . A good, but not great chocolate peanut butter palette, and fun mini French macaroons, with flavors like strawberry basil and blueberry melon 

As fine dining goes, Eleven Madison Park proved to be one of NYC's best. However, as gushing as this write up has been, I'd still place the overall experience a shade behind both Daniel and Momofuku Ko. Daniel is, IMHO, the purest and most fully realized French cooking in the city, and Momofuku Ko is like escaping into a magical room that only you and 12 other people get to share. I have also not had the pleasure to dine yet at Per Se, which many critics and friends alike say is the best dining experience in the city and perhaps the planet. 

Still, a 5 star night.

Our recent trip to NY took us back to EMP.  Though this time, the bar.  Since we were on the company tab...we didn't want to go nuts. :o)

We walked in around 6:30PM on a Wednesday evening.  The bar wasn't too busy..we even found a table right away.  It took a good while before a server came to us (perhaps 15 min?) with a cocktail menu.  We were so accustomed to the prompt, attentive service during our first visit, that this was sort of a let down.  

Other than that, we had a fantastic experience.  The bar fare was just as fantastic as the 11 course Gourmand tasting, so they don't take it down just because you're on the other side of the room!  Drinks were also outstanding.  I wasn't feeling up to drinking heavily that night, so I worked my way down the non spirit menu...and let me tell you something....one does not booze to enjoy a cocktail like the ones offered here...every one of them was delicious in their own right!

We decided to just split some plates to start.  First was the heirloom tomato salad with mascarpone ice cream (um..yum!).  Second was the Madison Square "Park Dogs" which were little itty bitty bites of hot dog goodness.  Plus, they were absolutely adorable.  Third was the pizzetta "carbonara" -- it was good, but nothing extraordinary.  Yet, to its credit...it was light, crispy and very flavorable.  Next came the black angus beef burgers...er, sliders.  They were absolutely ridiculous...soo sooo good.  I'm kind of disappointed that they don't put up a regular sized version of these on the menu.  I'd have one every day.  Next to last was the ricotta "gnocchi" -- um, it clearly was not like any other gnocchi I've ever tasted.  To describe it would not do it justice, one would need to experience it.  Lastly, we had the black angus beef to split as our entree.  Absolutely melt in your mouth fabulous.

Although we didn't order dessert (I was pretty stuffed at that point, and I never turn down dessert!), they brought over a plate of the mignardises.

To end our evening, we were offered a tour of the kitchen...which is unlike any other kitchen I've ever seen.  Spotless, cool, and ever so efficient.  It was a lot of fun being in the middle of it all...and the chefs really enjoyed us being in there.  To us, they're like rock stars!  Can't wait to visit again soon!

Eleven Madison Park is one of Manhattan's best restaurants.  I've been here twice now and both times were amazing.  Let me begin by telling you my first experience.  My husband's cousin had just passed her Medical exam after being in lock down for months of studying, this was the celebration dinner and boy did we celebrate.  We had a 9p reservation and began with Bellinis for the ladies and something for the gents( I forget what they had ordered, lol).  Since it's a celebration dinner, we all ordered the gourmand tasting menu..11 courses.  Every dish was amazing to the eye and amazing to the mouth.  They were all so beautifully presented that you almost was too afraid to mess it up by putting your fork in it.  But of course, it would be silly to just stare at it.  Once you make the move of digging your fork in for the first time, you can't stop because of how good it tastes.  Each course is a discovery to me of how creative you can get with making food.  Everything was delicious and perfect.  We ate until 2A and were one of the last people left in the restaurant. Besides the stuff on the menu for dessert, we also got little macarones, chocoate truffles at the end of the meal.  As if....we weren't already stuffed to our throat.  Even though it was so late, the wait staffs patiently served and explained what we were having.  What a memorable night.  

My husband and I had such a great time there, we decided to take his brother here for his birthday.  You know how sometimes experiencing something for the second time, it never meets the expectation or is as good as the first?  Not this place...second time was just as good.  We didn't do the gourmand since none of us want to go into food coma before movie plans.  We did the 5 course tasting instead and it was just as good.  

EMP is definitely on the top of the restaurant list for me.

My husband and I were blown away. We had heard fabulous things and decided not to research it to death because we wanted to be surprised by what came out of the kitchen. (We had heard there were multiple fleets of amuse bouches and hors d'oeuvres. There were. All I'll say is that it was phenomenal.) I think we might do this more often because we were utterly delighted from A-Z. Everything gets an A+ from service to atmosphere to the food itself.

We did the three course tasting menu, the shortest by far, and it was way more food than I could manage. If you're wondering if the short menu is a diluted experience, I assure you it is not.  

Highlights:
-For apps, both the mozzarella ice cream with tomato and basil granola and also the ricotta gnocchi were mind-blowing.
-For entrees, the marrow-crusted steak and suckling pig. 
-Try their custom Cab Sauv from Napa. After ten minutes of breathe time, it was velvet.

Daniel Humm's reputation seems to be growing in leaps and bounds. I don't think you could find a food blog or forum on the Internet that didn't recommend EMP as a dining hot spot in this city. 
I came here for the excellently priced lunch and did not leave disappointed. The amuse bouche were outstanding and my fregola salad with octopus, chickpeas and fennel was fresh and delightful with a playful balance of texture and acidity that seemed to draw inspiration from Spain but put together with a more French elegance. My Bouillabaisse was rich a flavourful and although I probably prefer a bolder interpretation of the dish Humm's creation was none the less excellent. The dining room is a beautiful space and the greenery outside the windows that filters the sunshine also helps you escape from the bustle of Manhattan outside. An elegant oasis that one does not want to leave in a hurry. 

Service was courteous and professional but perhaps lacked the charisma and personality to lift it to the highest level. I would definitely love to return to EMP in the evening to experience a much more involved and extended experience.

Mere days after Chef Daniel Humm won the James Beard Foundation's award for Best NYC Chef 2010, I sat down to dinner at Eleven Madison Park with Felicia C.

I would be hard pressed to choose between EMP and Le Bernardin for my favorite fine dining experience. They rank just about equally in my book. I can honestly say that in 2010, EMP was probably the BEST meal I experienced. I say experienced because eating at a place like this is an experience - it's not just shoveling food into your maw and masticating. You sit and savor and truly take your time eating when you eat here. 

I don't understand how this place has only one Michelin Star. Really? It was probably the largest foodgasm I've had in my life. 
 
 
We both ordered the Gourmand Menu, a multi-course tasting menu designed to melt even the coldest food critics' hearts.

We started off with complimentary gougeres - cheese puffs of puffy deliciousness. Next came the hor d'oeuvres - each distinct in flavor and texture. I wish I could remember what everything was, but what really stood out to me were the foie gras macaroon and the carrot marshmallow. 

The first course was the Sterling Royal Caviar course - tiny Spheres of Smoked Sturgeon and Salmon Cream sat pillowed next to caviar to all pop gently in your mouth. This was probably my 2nd favorite of the courses.

The Santa Barbara Sea Urchin served with Custard with Green Apple and Shellfish Ragoût beautifully presented in an egg shell gave my taste buds something new and different in every bite, yet everything seemed to compliment each other just right. 

Now on to my favorite course of the night - the Garden Pea and Mint Lollipop. It was crisp, cold, and surprisingly refreshing, but not hard to bite into. After exclaiming over the unique lollipop, one of the staff informed us that the chef had just perfected it a week or two prior.

The dish that was explained as their "Spring out of Winter" plate consisted of Variations of Asparagus with Jamón Ibérico. Light and perfectly cooked, I couldn't have asked for anything more. The saltiness of the jamón ibérico paired in a simple, yet elegant way. 

Next up was one of my favorite foods - Foie Gras. It was served as a Tochon with Tête de Cochon, Pickled Spring Vegetables, and Horseradish. If you like foie, then this is the dish for you. No complaints here except that I can't have it every day.

The Atlantic Halibut served with Seared with Smoked Spring Garlic and Crayfish was perfectly cooked. Moist and flavorful, I really enjoyed the crayfish as a flavorful compliment to the fish.

For our 7th course, we were served the Nova Scotia Lobster - Poached with Young Carrots, Ginger, and Vadouvan Granola. The highlight of this dish for me was probably the sauce. I couldn't deconstruct it to save my life, but the flavors kissed my taste buds in a way that I couldn't really describe.

I wasn't too stuffed to eat the Earth and Ocean course, which consisted of Slow Cooked Poussin with Hawaiian Blue Prawns and Seaweed. Presentation-wise, this was the weakest dish to me. Flavor-wise however, it was spot on.

Our Colorado Lamb course came Herb Roasted with Sucrine Lettuce, Garden Peas, and Oregon Morels. It seems that peas are THE accent vegetable for the spring season. Tender and absolutely mouthwatering, I adored the way that the sauce played with the flavor of the lamb. Beautiful.

The selection of three Fromage from the Artisanal Cheese Cart - I wish I could remember which each of them were, but j'adore fromage, so it would have been difficult to choose a favorite anyways. The cheese selection at EMP is extensive. There were 2-3 tiers of cheeses to choose from. 

One of the more amazing desserts that I've ever had, the "Soda Pop" consisted of Tangerine, Grapefruit, Pomelo, and Lemon flavors. A sphere of tangerine soda, frozen with liquid nitrogen and with pop rocks sprinkled throughout it, sat atop various citrus fruit. It was one of the most unique, light flavors that I've had the pleasure of tasting.

For the last course, we were told that it was called the Milk and Chocolate. I was worried that it would be too heavy at the end of such a gregarious meal, but lo and behold - I was surprised again! The milk and chocolate was relatively light and came in Variations of Flavor and Texture. At no point on that plate was there an actual bar of chocolate, it was all deconstructed.

We ended our meal with a selection of Mignardises - macaroons in this case. I particularly enjoyed the lavender and the meyer lemon flavors. We were also provided with a glass of complimentary cognac, which I believe is supposed to help digestion. It's not really my thing, but I still appreciated the gesture. 
 
You might think that our meal ended there - sitting and sipping on cognac while nibbling on macaroons like ladies of importance. Nay... at our request, our gracious waiter gave each of us a print out of our mind-blowing menu as well as some soft fruit jellies in a beautiful little box.

thursday evening, no plans, just done shopping in the flatiron district: this calls for a solo dinner at eleven madison park. 

the bar isn't too crowded when i get there and i manage to snatch a seat immediately.  while the bartender takes a while to warm up to me (my sending back the house cabernet right at the beginning certainly didn't help with building the relationship) i end up having one of the best dinners in nyc yet.  i start out with the rabbit rillettes & foie gras, then move on to heirloom tomatoes with mozzarella ice cream - yes, ice cream.  the rabbit is quite good though not outstanding but the caprese variation can't be described as anything but superb

throw in a delicious 'english milk punch' (rum, scotch, batavia arrack, darjeeling tea, pineapple and spices) and i'm in a happy enough place to not only order dessert but go a little crazy with it, too: i get the haitian vanilla souffle and a tasting flight of exceptional dessert wines on the side. the souffle is out of this world and the wines are beyond compare: a 2000 berthet-bondet vin de paille, the 1999 chateau d'yquem and a 1989 geschwister erhard riesling beerenauslese that i like even better than the chateau d'yquem.

overall: fantastic dinner, i'll be back.

It's probably sacrilege not to give EMP five stars.  It's a beautiful restaurant with delicious (though not particularly inventive) food and lots of nice touches like the extra little tastings and take-home sweets.  The first time I came, I was blown away and declared it my new favorite restaurant.

On this last visit, however, I left feeling a bit fatigued with the place.  A hundred staff people milled around in black outfits smiling cordially, but getting a drink took forty minutes, and there were long delays between courses.  The menu is pretty rigid; it's difficult to stray from the three-course or tasting menu choices.  EMP is a great place, but it just isn't *fun*.  In the future, I'll only eat at the bar, where the atmosphere's a little more friendly, and there are small-plate sharing options.

Wow, what a night!

Fiance made reservations after hearing from multiple sources that Eleven Madison was a must try. 

We loved every minute of the evening!
The service was outstanding. Truly, the best we've had anywhere. 
The food was amazing, and the extras made us feel totally pampered. 

Our meal started with mini popover type bites and then moved on directly to an entire plate of amuse bouche. We're pretty used to getting a little treat from the chef when coming to a restaurant like Eleven, but the entire platter was crazy nice and extravagant looking. Plus, they were ALL tasty. 

My favorite was the foie gras with strawberry, but each little treat was pretty darn awesome. 

We then ordered our meal--peekytoe crab followed by the lamb for me and heirloom tomatoes with mozzarella ice cream followed by the marrow crusted steak for the fiance. 

We thought that would be it for the night until dessert..but not a chance! Out came delicious rolls with 2 kinds of butter (cow and goat), and then a lobster and corn bisque again compliments of the chef. 

After finally finishing the food we had actually ordered (which was all delicious), out came our desserts. The fiance wasn't a huge huge fan of his berries with olive oil gelato, but I loved my souffle. 

The evening, however, continued with an assortment of free macaroons and an after dinner drink. 

Writing it all out, I can't believe we managed to walk out of the restaurant--we should have required a wheelbarrow considering how much we consumed during our almost 3 hour dinner!

Oh, and this afternoon we enjoyed our little fruit treats as a lovely reminder of the dinner!

Amazing service.
Amazing food. 
We'll be back!
I nearly always rate on food quality alone, but: this was good food, great service, but not amazing, especially given the expectation and price. I wouldn't go again. (review of a visit 6 months ago).

This meal/experience was pretty amazing.

My favorite parts about the experience:

1. They put a bottle of cognac on the table (that we didn't order) after the meal. They said "have as much as you like."
2. Because I ordered several cocktails during the meal, they gave me a book about the history of cocktails as well as some recipes.
3. They gave us a box of candy to take home.
4. The service is out of control!!

Jean-Georges is by far my favorite lunch deal in the city, so I was intensely excited to hear that EMP offered a similar deal for lunch: $28 for two-courses, $42 for three. I have no idea why it took me so long to come here, it was definitely worth the money. Before I get into what I ate, I would like to point out that their ice tea comes with three different syrups (simple, ginger honey and pomegranate) and there are unlimited refills so you get to sample them all -- this is amazing. We of course got the 3-course, but we pretty much gorged ourselves, 2 is more than sufficient if you get at least one of the items in the lower section of the menu. 

To start, you get amuse-bouches: we received foie gras and strawberry gelee on a cracker and a carrot marshmallow, both interesting, but I'm not sure I loved either. However, my bouche was certainly amused. As others mentioned you also get little gougeres (baked cheese bread), which are delicious as well as two different kinds of bread (the olive rosemary is fantastic). Here's a run-down of the items I tried:

1) Balik Salmon with Cucumbers, Pickled Pearl Onions and Dill - a take on lox (with no bagel), the salmon comes smoky with a creamy sauce and is served tar-tar style, with a few pieces of sliced salmon on top. A decent starter, but not my favorite.

2) Tagliolini with Alaskan King Crab, Black Pepper and Lemon - nice, large chunks of crab tossed with just cooked right tagliolini came in a rich, buttery sauce, good flavor, and certainly filling.

3) Spaetzle with Niman Ranch Pork Belly, Pommery Mustard and Spinach - my favorite starter that I tried (and filling enough to be an entree), the porkbelly came in a nice big chunk that was tender and moist, and yet firm with dense porky flavor. The spaetzle was decent, with whole mustard grains, as a whole, the dish was very, very rich.

4) St. Canut Farm Cochon de Lait with Bing Cherries, Sweet Onion and Mustard - suckling pig served two ways (loin and belly) arrived with rich porky flavor and was complemented perfectly by the marinated bing cherries which were delicious by themselves. 

5) Bone Marrow Crusted Beef Tenderloin with Swiss Chard and Royal Trumpet Mushrooms ($15 supplement) - This was truly an amazing dish, my favorite that I tried. The beef came meltingly tender with rich beef flavor in a sauce that included little chunks of bone marrow. It was also quite large and included two pieces of tenderloin. Absurdly decadent, but equally delicious, and complemented well by the earthy mushrooms and crisp swiss chard. Would definitely recommend this dish, it is worth the extra 15 bucks. 

6) Kouign Amann with Sour Cherry - Essentially a giant croissant cake dipped in caramel, this was a buttery, flaky and delicious dessert. 

While I still think Jean-Georges is better, this was definitely a meal to remember and I will be adding it to my list of great lunch deals in the city.

i fell in love here over the "summer" seven course tasting menu with wine pairing. what? oh yeah, my date was cool too.

the only thing that ruined our evening was the older woman who wore the most awful, pungent, cloying perfume. she was seated maybe 20 feet away and the stink of it kept punching me in the face.

oh. also, for a tasting menu of seven courses, we probably should not have been done within 90 minutes. we needed a little more time to savor; the starters were seriously clockwork precise in timing.

This dinner was fantastic, definitely a night to remember. (It kills me that my camera broke the DAY BEFORE our dinner here.) When you walk in, you're struck by the gorgeous high ceilings and architecture. There seemed to be a really lovely view of the park along one wall, though we were seated in a more secluded section on the other side of the restaurant--which was also lovely and very intimate.

My beau had landed himself a $200 dinner at his choice of restaurants, and after pouring over reviews for various places, we decided that EMP was exactly what we wanted. Our reservations were for 8:45PM on a Tuesday, but we walked in at about 8:15 and were seated immediately. The service was impeccable. Our main waiter was Kirk, who was fantastic, though various other people appeared throughout the night to bring things to our table, pull out our seats, refold our napkins, etc. Every time I came back from the restroom, I found that my napkin had magically become a triangle again, folded so that my smears of chocolate or mushroom sauce were hidden from delicate eyes.

We started off with cocktails and some delicious puffs of crispy, cheesy bread... apparently these are called gougères. I ordered a Pimm's Cup, which caught my eye for being the oldest recipe in the apéritif section. It was adorable, with a veritable garden of fresh mint sprouting from one side, and colorful sliced fruit settled in the middle of the drink. It's the tastiest cocktail I can ever recall having. (Note that there is a fairly large percentage of cocktails in my past that I do not remember at all, for obvious reasons.)

Next, we moved on to the first set of amuse-bouches, which were five little mouthfuls of heaven. In the order I ate them: Carrot marshmallow cube, which is what I considered the least tasty but most 'interesting'. I described it to my boyf as "science in your mouth" which I think is fairly apt. Tuna and something-I-forget with crispy, thin cracker housing... excellent. Strawberry gelée on a cracker was adorable and I hesitated to destroy it, but for the taste, the destruction was worth it. It was a tie between the fourth, a mushroom tart, and the final amuse, a sweetbread pouch, for most delicious.

Next came a second, larger amuse-bouche that consisted of chilled lobster bisque served over a corn cream, with a few kernels of dried, crispy corn. I can describe it only by slamming my hands against the keyboard in ecstatic remembrance sdkbgkahguhLIHhrl;. The bread came around this time too, with the choice of goat's milk butter or cow's milk butter.

Next we received our appetizers. Michael ordered the gnocchi, while I went with the Arctic char. Being a lover of all things savory, I found his gnocchi to be the best thing I'd ever tasted (a feeling I kept having throughout the night), while the Arctic char was very refreshing. I found the cucumbers a little too vinegar-y, though.

Next came the entrées. The lamb was splendid, I refuse to believe that something so tender, so delicate, so melt-in-your-mouth delicious could have possibly come off an animal, unless this was actually Flank of Unicorn. It fell apart at the lightest touch of my knife, and was complimented perfectly by the curry sauce. Michael's Atlantic Halibut was also fantastic, though it couldn't top the lamb in my opinion. However, the tomatoes he had! I stole a bite of them, and they were what a tomato should be. Perfection.

We moved on to the desserts, with their house coffee. Honestly, I'd give the coffee a 7/10. It was good, but I've had better... not that that stopped me from downing two cups. I ordered the Milk & Chocolate for dessert. Dehydrated milk foam and chocolate mousse. It was a very salty-sweet flavor, which combined perfectly. My boyfriend's bittersweet chocolate crémeux was excellent, too. (We developed a habit of sampling each other's plates all night.) I really liked the mixture of bitter sauce with sweet chocolate and ice cream, maybe even better than the milk & chocolate. 

We also were given a complementary cognac with our dessert... I've never had cognac before and have no way of comparing it's deliciousness to other cognacs, but I really appreciated it.

Finally came the after-dessert mini macarons. I had been anticipating these since I saw them on my way to the ladies' room, and even tried to order them for dessert. I'm running out of room to type this review, but they were AMAZING! All of them. I expressed my joy at their arrival fervently, and devoured them all despite being obscenely full. When it was time to leave, we were given the most darling little boxes of sweet candies, and our waiter Kirk also very kindly gave me a box with a larger macaron inside it.

Eating here was something I'll remember for a long time, and was definitely the best dinner I've ever had--amazing food, amazing service, and amazing atmosphere. I can't recommend it highly enough, and I hope to come back again as soon as I can afford it.

Ohh my Gawwd! That's the first thing that comes to mind when I think about Eleven Madison Park. If I were filthy rich, I'd just come here every day. 

Our experience dining here was divine and it was of course for a very special occasion - to celebrate our engagement. We had the 11-course prix fix with a bunch of wines, I believe (I hope I remember this right as it's been some time) and 5 hours and almost $500 later (for 2 people!) we still thought it was worth it. The service was superb too. We were treated like royalty. 

Can't wait to go back there some day...

Wow...where to begin.  Our experience at EMP was magical, from the minute we entered the room.   Full disclosure: my dear friend used to be a manager here, so she made the reservation and I know we got a few special extras as a result... the evening would have been spectacular regardless.

The scene: the room is quite stunning, with high vaulted ceilings and serene flower arrangements.  Tables don't feel cramped, which is a pleasure in NYC.  High ceilings often make a restaurant feel cold or unwelcoming, but EMP manages to strike the perfect balance between elegance and warmth.  

This dinner was my surprise gift to my parents for their birthdays, and was also a belated anniversary celebration for my husband and I.  I really messed up and booked us for the wrong day, so they had to accomodate us last minute.  They offered us a 9:30pm slot and I gratefully took it, secretly hoping they could seat us earlier.  We arrived early to have a drink, the bar was full, and when I mentioned my dad was older, they immediately found me a perfect table in the lounge where he could sit.  To make matters better, they sat us at our table almost as soon as my parents arrived--probably 45 minutes before our 9:30 reservation.  Our table was perfect, with a single white rose in the middle.  We drank a delicious and unusual glass of champagne carried only by the restaurant.  It seemed to get better with every sip.  I could taste these lovely sherry undertones in it--just loved it.  We opened our menus and were overcome when we saw Happy Birthday, Happy Anniversary, and our names printed on top--wow!  It made us feel like we were the only people in the room, and also gave us a lovely keepsake with which to commemorate the evening.  

A few food highlights: We began with some special amuse/ mini apps which were fabulous and innovative.  The sweetbread pouch is to die for, the carrot marshmallow (you heard that right) was wild; each new taste was a little party in my mouth.  Standout apps were the gnocchi (more traditional, rich, indulgent)  and the crazy watermellon ceviche (fresh, light, totally innovative). Peekytoe crab was the weakest app.  My mom and husband split the duck as an entrée, and we all decided it was hands down the best duck we'd ever tasted (and hubbie is from CT, or 'land of the duck', so he is a tough critic.)  Cochon du lait was well-prepared and delicious, as was the lamb, but the duck trumped them both. The lobster bisque amuse was outstanding, and they sweetly brought my husband a sweet corn chowder with truffle oil because he'd mentioned he didn't love tomatoes.  They surprised us with a Milk and Honey spherical which was unlike anything I've ever tasted... sort of like eating creamy snow with an explosion of orange blossom honey in the center.  Amazing. Desserts, which i often find dissappointing at nice restaurants, were outstanding. Not a single misstep-- order them all!  Best meal any of us have had in a long time.

The service really took the evening to the next level.  Our wine captain came up with fabulous pairings for us to enjoy with our meal.  Our captain, described dishes perfectly, made excellent suggestions, and was just a joy to be around.  Daniel Humm came out and said hi--it was so cool to meet him as we were enjoying his creations!  All the staff defined excellence, and managed to balance warmth and knowledge perfectly.  We felt at home, while at the same time feeling like we were being treated like royalty.        

Bottom line is that the 4 of us walked away feeling like we'd had a once in a lifetime experience--like we'd had a night we'd remember for a very long time.

I came here for lunch and I have to say its a great deal.  You get 2 courses for $28 (or 3 for $42) at one of the top restaurants in NYC (Daniel Humm just won best chef NYC and it got a glowing 4 star review from the NY Times).  While it is certainly not cheap, it is definitely a value as you would easily spend more at comparable high end restaurants.

To start you off they serve a basket of warm gougeres (think warm cheesy pastry puffs) that were delicious.  The amuse bouches were a savory carrot marshmallow which was definitely strange.  I think I liked it but the texture of marshallow was nice with an intense sweet carroty flavor.  This was served nice to foie gras and raspberry gelee on a cracker.  I was pleansantly surprised to see foie in a lunch amuse and it was great.  The rich, fatty foie with the cracker and gelee were tasty.

The bread basket was good as well.  They had an olive bread which I loved and a french roll that was served warm and crispy.

For the main meal, I started with the Big Eye Tuna Tartare with Sorrel, Lemon and Taggiasca Olives.  It was a beautiful looking dish and it was pretty good.  The tuna was nice and fresh and the flavors were clean.  It wasn't the best tuna I've ever had, but it was certainly simple and very good.

Next I had the bouillabaisse of Black Bass, Bouchot Mussels, Manila Clams and Chorizo.  I love seafood and I love soups and stews and I thought this dish was great.  The broth was a vibrant orangey color and had a rich seafood flavor.  The bass was cooked well and the chorizo added a nice and surprising touch, my favorite dish of the meal.

I finished with the pork dish (St. Canut Farm Cochon de Lait with Bing Cherries, Sweet Onion and Mustard ).   This was also a very good dish.  The pork loin was cooked well, but it wasn't especially tender or flavorful.  The pork belly though was just amazing.  The skin was nice and crunchy and the fat was just sooo tasty and smooth and creamy.  The rest of the elements also worked very well with the dish.

To drink, I had the iced tea (with free refills!) which they serve with 3 syrups that you add yourself.  I thought it was pretty cool and I thoroughly enjoyed the drink.

Overall, you get a great meal at a very reasonable price.  EMP is just an incredible restaurant where you get to experience great food as well as Danny Meyer's famous hospitality (they have an army of servers to take care of you and they pride themselves on service).  I definitely recommend it for lunch and I look forward to eating dinner here in the future.  5 stars.

Certain things happen to be unexpectedly perfect. 

Seems like Daniel Humm reach already the best of the best category along a few others. Named best chef in NYC 2010*. The one who recently made Eleven Madison Park be part of of the World's 50 Best Restaurants*, holder of 1 Michelin Star and raised to the top 4 star rating (extraordinary) at the NY times* 

All this awards are almost a 100% warranty of no other than an exceptional meal. You are expecting to be good and it will be better than that. But the assertion mentioned above include an experience where the food is truly the main part but doesn't really make a complete scenario. Chef Humm declare at Eleven Madison Park magazine that he "wants everybody remember delicious and pure flavors, textures and ingredients but, most importantly, enjoy their meal leaving with wonderful memories and hopes of returning soon". And he does. 

It was unexpected to feel completely relaxed in one of the finest dining destinations in the city. Personally, I feel sometimes overwhelmed with upscale service, grandiosity look and anything that indicates "Jacket Preferred". Don't be afraid. That will not happen here. Unexpected as well the fact that there is many Prix Fixe choices. The hopes of returning soon automatically go up as is not easy to beat a $28 Two-Course Prix Fixe or $42 Three-Course Prix Fixe. But its very easy to go there once in a while for that amount. It has to be for lunch. Until 2pm. And any day except during weekends. But still. The possibilities are high to do it a few times. Its also unexpected that you can choose among more than a few choices as usually happen in many other places. 

My choices included Tuna Tartare and Seared Diver Scallop . The food taste amazing, its clean. The combination come along as if it was born to be together. Beautiful and fresh. Just perfect. Mum congrats our servers even if she doesn't know a word in English. But her Fregola Sarda with Veal Sweetbreads and her Slow Cooked Knoll Krest Farm Egg was just so good. Aunt was repeatedly saying "bueno, bueno, bueno" ... a Spanish expression when you just don't know what to say, while she was eating her Tagliolini with Alaskan King Crab. Dad was intrigued with his choice because the combinations of flavors in the Bouillabaisse of Black Bass, Bouchot Mussels, Manila Clams and Chorizo. I order for everyone based in what I know they like. But he likes to discern what he is eating. And pick up everything, the sea flavor. The chorizo. His head was just saying yes all the time; during his main entree but from the beginning with the bouchees served at each table while drinks and food are served. He couldn't stop eating that small balls of savory and tasty pastry. I preferred however the small toast and the green jelly bites while mum was delighted with the orange marshmallows that i didn't really like, but that was a surprising bite, in texture and flavor.   

Out of the menu you can choose among a few desserts that include many house made tarts. We choose Lemon Meringue and Mango Linzer. And on the house we also got a piece of the Toasted Pine Nut & Ricotta. All of them was so good.  The presentation is simple. The cakes looks and taste like the ones that only old ladies can make. Your grandma after a life of experience. The Toasted Pine Nut with Ricotta would have been my favorite without any question according to my taste. But unexpectedly, it was The Lemon Meringue the one I loved the most.  

According to anything else the space is beautiful.Grandiose as consequence of a high ceiling and natural lighting because the giant windows creating the impression of an open space. Perfect again. It was a wonderful meal in all the senses but I have to point out however that I find Daniel Humm's cuisine classic comparing with Degustation or Aldea, that I experienced a few days back. The food was not as surprising as the ones I had in those places. He reach perfection but in my opinion it wasn't as innovative. But it could be just what we choose. It could be that I have to taste more dishes and be more experienced. Perfect excuses for coming back


*http://www.jbfawards.com/winners.html#restaurant
*http://www.theworlds50best.com/awards/1-50-winners
*http://events.nytimes.com/2009/08/12/dining/reviews/12rest.html

I am extremely conflicted about how to review this restaurant, one of the best fine dining experiences I have had, but with food that was not quite as brilliantly flavorful as I had hoped, or at least not in the way I had hoped. Start with the easy stuff. The staff was extremely friendly, professional, and remarkably knowledgeable about the food and wine. The custom construction of the cheese course, based on a discussion of the cheeses we like and don't like, was a treat. The decor is outstanding as well, spacious and exquisitely classy without being stuffy or overly formal. 

For food, in addition to the cheese course, we picked the Summer tasting menu, with roughly eight courses. Highlights included a brilliantly creamy and elegant corn soup with radish and truffle, a beautiful couscous salad with a variety of perfectly-chosen summer greens and vegetables, and a fish course with an amazing summer pepper sauce. On the other hand, some of the later courses didn't quite rise to the same level. In discussions afterward, we tended to think that the dishes lacked the level of savoryness and piquantness that we particularly enjoy, leaning on unctuousness instead of aliums, perhaps. Maybe this is trying to wish qualities upon fine-dining French food that it doesn't have, or perhaps a richer/darker Winter menu would be more our style, or perhaps Chef Humm just prefers a slightly different style of cuisine. Certainly there was nothing incorrectly prepared, or unbalanced, or made from anything but the best ingredients. If we were to return, though, we might take a closer look at the rest of the menu, and focus on particular dishes where the skills of the restaurant more closely match our idiosyncratic palates.

They really know how to treat their diners here.  For such an upscale restaurant, the service is incredibly down to earth while still being able to maintain its professionalism.  

The highlights:

1. Before we even saw a dinner menu, we were presented with gruyère cheese gougères and a sample of 4-5 different bite sized appetizers.

2. They make the most amazing duck here.  They bring out a whole duck but only serve the breast and then take the rest of the carcass back to the kitchen for a second preparation with foie gras.  The duck is infused with lavendar, topped with szchewan peppercorns, and served with grilled strawberries and asparagus.  The sweet and savory flavors went together perfectly and the presentation was so colorful and pretty!  

3. For dessert, I couldn't decide between two so the server brought me both!  

I couldn't give it 5 stars though because the appetizers were sub-par and the desserts were just alright.  My friend had the ricotta stuffed gnocchi, which was too rich and salty.  I had the frogs legs with mushroom assortment, which was kind of mushy and had a strange presentation - all the component ingredients were separated and I didn't know what I was supposed to do with it all.

Overall, great meal!

This was the kind of meal that we'll talk about for years to come. The staff, though seemingly young, went above and beyond for our 5 year anniversary dinner. We did the tasting menu ... each course blended well into the next, while at the same time boldly standing out on their own.

The lamb was a highlight, so were the 8 different macaroons as part of our 3 dessert courses. Their "honey and milk", for instance, is surprising yet comforting, as a mountain of dehydrated milk cracks open to reveal a river of honey. 

I could go on and on, but I don't want to ruin so many surprises that happened along the way (including the take home goodies!). 

Oh, and their mixed drinks are heavenly ... and make sure to call on the sommelier to help you with their dictionary sized wine list!
I just got a HANDWRITTEN card from them, thanking me for my enjoyment of the spring menu and telling me that their summer menu is on it's way.  AMAZING.
Beautiful, cool, impressive space. Great service and the food is breathtaking to look at and downright delicious and creative!

It seems that most people come here wanting to give Eleven Madison at least 4 stars, but I was surprised that this didn't turn out to be the case for me. 3.5 stars. 

Highlights:
- 6 complimentary tastings + 1 amuse bouche. ( I thought the tastings were pretty amazing for being just tastings) 
- Warm baguettes w/ two options for butter (goat and cows milk) 
- Good dessert selection - + complimentary dessert (desserts are gloriously rich, and portions are well-sized.)
- Cochon au lait (the chef's special roast pork that costs an additional $20. I'd never tasted a flavour combination like that before)

Cons: 
I prefer bold flavours in my food, and it seems like the trend here is that the dishes are inventive and the flavours are more subtle so you don't feel like you've eaten alot. I did find the regular menu portions disappointingly small. (thank goodness for all the tastings or i would still be hungry!) 

I liked that our waiter was attentive and he kept giving us complimentary tibbits + a free takehome gift of sugar jellies, but prepare yourself for at least a 3hr dinner.

I would love to come back here, but i do prefer Gramery Tavern, Jean Georges or even La Bernadin.

Although the place was pretty crowded, the tall ceilings made it feel spacious.  And although prices are quite high, it did not feel at all pretentious.  My friend and I went with the 3 course meal (2 savory dishes, 1 sweet) for $95 (we also had the option of a spring tasting menu for $135 with an optional $95 wine pairing, or chef's tasting menu for $175 with an optional $125 wine pairing, but I couldn't really justify paying that much money for a Wednesday night dinner! ...not that I could really justify a $95 weekday dinner either).

We began with a small basket of warm gougeres while we pondered our menu choices, followed by a gorgeous plate of amuses bouche of a savory carrot marshmallow, an interesting and delicious tuna tartare sandwiched between two very thin crispy crackers, a foie gras and aspargus gelee on a cracker, a mini morel mushroom tart, and a sweetbread eggroll.  They were all pretty good, and a great adventure for my taste buds.  My favorite was the tuna tartare, followed by the sweetbread eggroll.

We placed our order with the friendly waiter who was great at helping us make our choices and who made some great wine pairing suggestions for each of our courses (my friend and I both started with a white wine with our appetizer, followed by a red with our entree), and then received a complimentary appetizer of chilled soup that was cool and refreshing.  We also received two warm, crusty fluffy pieces of bread (mini baguette and olive roll) with two kinds of butter:  goat's milk and cow's milk.

For my appetizer I ordered the slow-cooked farm egg with mushrooms, frog legs, and a beautiful foam.  It was a great burst of bright flavor, smooth and creamy but with some good textural contrast from the frog legs and mushrooms.  This was my second favorite dish of the night.

My friend's appetizer was the scallop ceviche with rhubarb, celery and yuzu, which was fruity and very refreshing, but not particularly memorable since I feel like I could probably have gotten it at several other restaurants in the city.

For our entrees, I had the colorado lamb with sucrine lettuce and morel mushrooms, and my friend had the cochon au lait, their signature dish ($20 supp.).  My plate was a celebration of lamb, presenting it in many forms (sausage, tortellini, etc.).  It was perfectly cooked and gave me a wonderful textural adventure from the creaminess of the pasta filling, crispy outer layer of lamb, and sweetness of the crunchy lettuce.  My friend's suckling pig, however, was hands down the best thing I ate all night.  I forget what accompaniments it came with but the pork itself was buttery and melt-in-your-mouth.  It was perfect.

Being a chocolate lover, my friend and I were deciding between three of the chocolate desserts:  the bittersweet chocolate cremeux with caramelized bananas and yuzu, the chocolate peanut butter palette with caramelized popcorn and popcorn ice cream, and the milk & chocolate, a dehydrated milk chocolate mousse.  I ended up getting the chocolate peanut butter palette, which was crunchy and rich and tasted kind of like a Butterfinger candy bar, with a great slightly salty ice cream, and my friend decided on the milk & chocolate, which she loved.  But as a pleasant surprise, they also gave us the bittersweet chocolate cremeux!  It was also rich and delicious, with some nice crunchy elements and brightness from the yuzu.  Our desserts were paired with a madeira, which they were happy to give a splash of to my friend (in addition to the full glass I ordered) even though she didn't want a dessert wine.

As a nice end to the meal, they presented us with a beautiful selection of mini macarons in interesting flavors such as peanut butter & jelly (tasted just like a PB&J sandwich!), pink peppercorn caramel, and lemon chamomile, as well as a complementary glass of cognac as a nightcap.  They even left the bottle of cognac at our table and told us to pour ourselves as much as we wanted (we didn't though, since we were already quite full from the rest of the meal).

While the food was great, I thought the service was wonderful, if a little on the slow side (I think we were there for about 3 hours, but I didn't complain as I was enjoying myself).  Everyone was extremely friendly and helpful, and the chef even stopped by at each table to say hi and make sure everything was going well.  And when we ended the meal, they brought out complementary boxes of pate de fruit for us to take home.  And they weren't stingy with them either:  two pates de fruit each of tangerine, lime, lemon, and grapefruit flavors.

An overall great experience.

I was a bit reluctant to write this review, since I really, really wanted to love Eleven Madison Park... but unfortunately I didn't.

Don't get me wrong -- service is absolutely TOP NOTCH, no question.  We were seated promptly and even greeted each time we would walk to the bathroom.  The server that directed me to the bathroom even made small talk with me as he walked me to the area.  The execution of dishes was super synchronized and my food never came to the table cold when it should hot or hot when it should be cold.  It was perfect.

Now, to the not so great parts.

We ordered the 11 course Gourmand menu, which is really the Spring menu with a few extra dishes added on.  11 is a minomer since it really turned out to be like 15.  The portions were relatively small, but we did get pretty full by the time it was dessert (and there were like 4 courses of dessert).

Daniel Humm did come out towards the beginning to survey the room, but unlike other reviewers, he did not come around each table.  I didn't even know it was him until I saw a really tall man in a white chef's outfit and I Google imaged him hahaha.

I didn't care for many of the dishes, particularly the carrot marshmallow and carrot lollipop.  The rest of the appetizers were only okay; I honestly expected a lot more.  I think the only one I can even remotely say that I enjoyed was the sea urchin.  There was a foie gras plate that was okay for the first 3 bites but after that it just got to be too much.  I almost wanted to puke at how fatty/oily it was.

For the entrees, the seafood dishes were the best -- lobster and crayfish and halibut had to be my absolute faves of the night.  I'm not a fan of lamb so the lamb dish went untouched, unfortunately.

I have no issues with the desserts though!  They were good, although Daniel Humm does use the dehydrated method a bit too much.

There was a cheese course that we turned away.  The whole cheese cart smelled like feet once they opened it -- gross.  I'm not a huge cheese fan, as you can see.  But from the appearance of other diners, it looked like they'd give you a small variety of cheeses.

In the end, we were given a copy of the menu; I think it was freshly printed for us because it did not note the cheese course and it also noted the courses as they came out (we noticed that some diners had their courses come out in different order).

I asked the hostess if it would be an issue to get Daniel Humm to sign the menus, to which she enthusiastically replied, of course, no problem!  She asked another girl to bring them in and a few minutes later, that girl returned, conferred with the hostess and stood around for a few minutes.  Afterwards, she conferred with the hostess again and told us that the chef had left for the night.  That seemed a bit odd to us?  Was he too busy to scribble his signature?  We left disappointed, especially since the hostess said, "maybe next time."

I don't think we'd spend another $500 on dinner here next time since the chef didn't even bother to sign our menus.  :(

I really wanted to like this place but I have to say, course after course after course was totally underwhelming. Granted, I ate their for lunch, not dinner, and perhaps they do better in the evenings, but to be a top restaurant in NYC, I'm sorry, if you're doors open, you need to be bringing the A game.

The sad part is, the food wasn't the only thing that was a let down. Service was slow, and inaccurate. They messed up the dessert order, bringing me something I hadn't even ordered. After even longer wait still, they brought out the correct one, yet all three desserts were lack luster. With so many other fantastic options in the Flatiron/Union Sq. area, this would fall near the bottom of my list.

This is part 1 (lunch) of 2 reviews, otherwise it would be too long...

Let me start from the beginning...My love affair with 11 Madison Park actually began at LUNCH last Thursday, where I limited myself (and my credit card) to 2 courses, dessert, and a couple glasses of wine. Instead of going into depth about every single course I had, let me say now that the dishes weren't just delicious, or even great, but that EVERY dish blew me away. Every. Single. Dish. 

I could go into depth about why this was, and will for my Examiner article, but I'll keep it simple here: Unlike many NYC restaurants, the menu is exceptionally inventive and market-driven, with ingredients that are locally sourced (as much as possible). Therefore, they are buying the freshest, best ingredients possible to create their dishes. And, unlike many NYC restaurants, while the technique used to create a dish may be extremely complicated and advanced, the plate itself is left relatively uncomplicated so that each one of those ingredients can shine - very similar to Coi in SF, but with a bit more metropolitan flare. 

That said, for lunch all of the following would be highly recommended: The BALIK SALMON with white asparagus/tarragon mayonnaise/fava beans, the SLOW COOKED FARM EGG with asparagus veloute and morels, the COCHON DE LAIT (suckling pig, served 3 ways) with rhubarb/spring onion/ice wine vinegar, and the FREGOLA Sarda with veal sweetbreads/pickled ramps/sorrel (almost like risotto, but larger grains). 

And, of course, the wine was expertly chosen and went beautifully with each one of our courses. In fact, I think our sommelier, Jennifer, was the best I have ever encountered in that when she served a wine she didn't just state the name or even what it was going to taste like, but specifically WHY she was pairing it with that particular dish - what it was supposed to bring out in the ingredients. And, at the end of the meal we were given cards with descriptions about each wine we had tasted, so if we ever wanted to find it on our own we had all of the information. It's those type of details that make this restaurant exceptional.

It is also much more than just lunch. You get hors d'oeuvres to start the meal, a little extra dish somewhere before dessert, and mignardises to finish. They do an excellent job of keeping you surprised, and who doesn't love surprises? Especially when they're edible!

Look, I may have a lot of Yelp reviews and do some work for Examiner, but in terms of the food industry, I'm really not that important...yet. But, the staff (specifically the floor manager Robert, and Sofia, our server) treated me like I was queen for the day - extra wine pairings, a complimentary hors d'oeuvre (a pea/mint lollipop cooked in brown butter and then frozen in liquid nitrogen), the best table in the house, a tour of the exquisite (and HUGE) kitchen, and, a VERY special treat...I got to meet the man himself, Daniel Humm. And yes, I have the photo and signed menu to prove it.

Needless to say, after all of that, I was overwhelmed. But, even with all of the perks excluded, the food itself was certainly the best lunch I have had. So good, in fact, that I went back for more the next night...
Quality and class.  This place is beautiful and they go above and beyond to ensure you have an unforgettable experience.

Absolutely delicious. One of my favorite meals of my life.  Definitely worth the price, as far as I'm concerned.

I went for dinner with my mother and father, and we all loved our meals.  First, the space is absolutely beautiful- high ceilings, beautiful flower arrangements, and polished wood.

Second, as in any Danny Meyer restaurant, the service was wonderful- friendly, competent, attentive, unobtrusive, and accommodating.  From the time we were greeted to the time we left, the staff made us feel very comfortable and cared for.

Third, and most important, the food!  We each ordered the three-course prixe fix menu.  The meal started with delicious, warm bread with goat's milk and cow's milk butter.  Great start to the meal.

Our courses were the following:
First course:
Lynnhaven Farms Goat's Milk Ricotta 
Gnocchi with Artichokes, Taggiasca Olives and Bacon

Knoll Krest Farm Egg 
Slow Cooked with Vin Jaune, Winter Mushrooms and Everglades Frogs' Legs

Diver Scallops 
Ceviche with Fennel, Yuzu and Satsuma Tangerine

The gnocchi was my favorite of the three.  Rich but not heavy.  Tiny pillows of tastiness!


Second course: 
John Dory 
Slow Cooked with Pickled Daikon Radish and Winter Citrus 
 
Bouillabaisse 
Atlantic Black Bass with Bouchot Mussels, Bay Scallops, Hawaiian Blue Prawns and Chorizo

Black Angus Beef 
Bone Marrow Crusted with Braised Root Vegetables and Sauce Bordelaise

Balanced flavors, perfectly cooked, tender. 

Dessert:
Milk & Chocolate 
Dehydrated Chocolate Mousse and Dulce de Leche

Sheep's Milk Yogurt Cheesecake 
Blood Orange and Pinenuts 
 
Tahitian Vanilla Soufflé  
Vermont Quark and Passion Fruit Sauce

Chocolate Peanut Butter Palette 
Caramel Popcorn and Popcorn Ice Cream

Our server brought us the Chocolate Peanut Butter Palette as a complimentary dessert.  We had been trying to decide between the Chocolate Peanut Butter Palette and the Milk and Chocolate, and although we ultimately decided on the Mlik and Chocolate, our server brought us the Chocolate Peanut Butter Palette anyway, saying that she was "passionate" about the dessert.

I think our favorite dessert was the cheesecake, which was tangy, sweet, and light.  I am not crazy about souffles, but I could still appreciate the quality of the souffle here.

I loved the extras, especially the macarons brought out at the end.  Plus, we were each given a muffin for the next morning.

All in all, a wonderful dining experience.  Next time, I want to try EMP for lunch!

Class. This place oozes with class. Well crafted, lovely view of Madison Square Park, the interior/layout = fabulous, and you're enjoying well mixed cocktails at a NY Times 4-star restaurant...gets no better!

The manager also came over to check on how we were and struck up a conversation which was a nice touch. I'll def. be back.

This is the best dining experience of my life. The food was truly excellent on every course. I very much enjoyed the amuse bouche of garlic cream with some shrimp concoction and the foie gras appetizer. But it was the duck, carved table-side, that blew my mind. It was undoubtedly the  best duck I've ever had, the skin was perfectly crispy and flavorful, almost all the fat had melted away, and the meat pink, juicy, and bursting with flavor. The red velvet dessert had a delicious cheesecake parfait and rhubarb and strawberry ice cream. Everything was perfectly balanced so I was full but never over-stuffed. 

In my mind what really separated this dining experience from others was the incredibly hospitality provided by the staff. Everyone was incredibly polite and friendly. While we were dining Chef Daniel came out and greeted all the tables. We were also treated to a tour of the kitchen where the magic happens. What we did to deserve this, I had no idea. Our waiter just said that he thought that we were having a really good time and wanted us to enjoy ourselves. Post-dinner we were treated to a bottle of cognac and macaroons at a separate table, all of which added up to be the bets dining experience ever. Definitely for special occasions, and I look forward to having the occasion to return.

Wonderful meal! They deserve all the awards they receive. Great food without being pretentious, good and attentive service. I felt like they really cared and enjoyed having us eat at their establishment. 

Definitely will be back.

Excellent !  
Again in agreement with five star writers.
Experience the tasting menus with the wines that compliment each dish and enjoy.

We arrived 30 minutes early and were promptly seated. They seated us next to each other facing the waiters area. We asked for seating facing each other and were quickly moved.

We went with the Spring Tasting with wine pairing.  Started off with the a mix of small hors d'oeuvres. The sweat potato puff stood out. It was a sweat and salty with marshmallow texture. My partner loved it.

The Spring out of Winter was also very good with white asparagus ice cream standing out.

The Atlantic Halibut was good but had a weird fishy flavor that tasted like the pink lobster innards.

Nova Scotia Lobster was amazing. It was perfect. It was the best dish and it wasn't only because I love lobster.

The Colorado Lamb was the most disappointing dish. The piece of medium rare lamb looked wonderful but was very chewy. The best piece was the sweat breads which were very rich.

The Soda Pop dish was my partners the favorite dish. It included deep freeze (nitro) ice cream and pop rocks.

The Milk Chocolate dessert was very good. There wasn't anything that stood out though.

So overall the food was 4 Stars. The service was 5 Stars. The wine paring was 5 Stars. The atmosphere was 5 Stars.

The food at Per Se was 5 Stars and the wine was 4 Stars maybe even 3 Stars.  (They didn't have a pairing option w/ the tasting).

My expectations were neither exceeded nor disappointed. 

The service is nearly flawless (except for the tray of glasses dropped that stopped the room cold and no cream for coffee, but who's keeping notes? ;-) )   Returning from the rest room, about 5 servers parted like the Red Sea for Charlton Heston making me feel like a feared third word dictator walking past his staff.

The appetizers were breathtaking. Peekytoe crab served between micro-thin translucent radish slices with edible flower petals glowing through.  My fiancee had divers scallops with strawberries (yes, strawberries), and it's incredible. 

Unfortunately the entrees were just alright; nothing earthshaking. My bouillabaisse was fine, but not the best ever. It's a bit too precious. 

My fiancee's lobster was a bit cold, and though the presentation is beautiful, the flavor wasn't much to write about. 

The amuse bouche were very nice, including a wonderful Hawaiian prawns in garlic soup. The bread service was good. They provide two types of butter, cows milk and goats milk. The former is nice but the latter tastes funky--perhaps just my lack of appreciation for goat's milk. 

The initial amuse bouche plate is a work of art, with bite size morsels of everything from sweetbreads to a carrot marshmallow. 

Dessert was lacking a bit. I had the caramel apple. Just ok. 

The cheese selection was good, though accompaniments didn't do the best job complementing the flavor/textures. 

The room is impressive. They inherited what appears to be a 1920s art deco bank lobby. If you like that period and style (as I do), you'll like the interior. Impressive windows look out onto the Flatiron Building and Madison Sq. Park. 

Fortunately, this meal was gifted to me. I probably would not have been so happy dropping north of $300 for the experience. 

Leaving  the restaurant, we walked across the street past another Danny Meyer venue, Shake Shack. I've also experienced Blue Smoke and Gramercy Tavern. I'm a fan of his restaurants, but it sometimes feels he's seeking near perfection, but comes up a bit short. That's the way I feel about Eleven Madison Park. I'm glad I experienced it, but I'll likely not return.

Both EMP is one of the two best lunch deals in the city (the other in Jean George).  Having been to and been disappointed by other Danny Meyer restaurants (Union Square Cafe, The Modern), was really impressed with this one.  Memorable dishes included a fantastic green apple & foie gras amuse, as well as the popcorn ice-cream.  My guest - who wisely followed the waiter's recommendations - had one of the best dishes I've ever had.  At $28 for two courses, it's a must, especially for those on a budget who want to try one of the city's best restaurants.

Epic lunch y'all! I came here and had the $40 three course prix fixe lunch (they also offer a two course for $27). My meal consisted of:

* Slow Cooked Knoll Krest Farm Egg with Asparagus Velouté and Oregon Morels
* Spaetzle with Niman Ranch Pork Belly, Pommery Mustard and Spinach
* Poached Nova Scotia Lobster with Heirloom Carrots, Ginger and Vadouvan Granola

Everything was excellent and very creative (granola on lobster? hell yeah!). I could describe each dish in detail but I don't think it's worth it.. every dish was expertly prepared and all of the flavors came through without overpowering each other. Service was excellent.. the cocktails were amazing. 

All around, possibly the best lunch I've had in my life. They just won the James Beard award for best chef in NY and were recently named the #50 best restaurant in the world. Give this place a try, it's a great deal for lunch.

Only days after my gluttonous dinner at EMP, I came back for lunch with Dolya and Steph - the first two people I met at Brooklyn Law School - for a meal celebrating the completion of our three year journey through what sometimes seemed like academic hell together.  It was actual pure coincidence that EMP was chosen as the venue for our celebratory luncheon.  And apparently, I'm not the only fan as Steph seems to have frequented the restaurant quite often.

Lunch is definitely not as extravagant an experience as dinner, but the service is still impeccable and the food delectable.  They did start us off with some hors d'oeuvres - the carrot marshmallow (which wasn't received well by the table) and foie gras.  For lunch, you have the option of going with a two or three course meal.  Since this was a special occasion, all three of us decided to go with the three course option.

As my starters I had the Big Eye Tuna Tartare with Sweat Peas, Mint, and Sheep's Milk Yogurt followed by the Linguini with Alaskan King Crab, Black Pepper, and Lemon.  The Tuna Tartare might very well be the best I've ever had.  The fish was fresh and perfectly seasoned with just the right amount of acid and salt.  The spring peas had a sweetness and brightness that complimented and balanced all the flavors of the dish.  The Linguini was tossed in a buttery and rich but light dressing.  The lemon worked well with the crab and helped cut through the richness of the sauce.  The pepper gave it a nice kick but wasn't overpowering.

For my entree I had the St. Canut Farm Cochon de Lait with Rhubarb, Spring Onion, and Ice Wine Vinegar.  Other than simply amazing, I'm not sure how else to describe this dish.  There were three different cuts of pork prepared three ways on the plate.  While each was delicious, the small piece of pork belly was absolutely scrumptious.  It has an extremely crispy skin but the meat was rich, moist, and buttery soft underneath - the perfect little bite.  The tartness from the rhubarb and sweetness from the onion and ice win vinegar provided a depth of flavor that makes you just keep wanting more of the dish.

Of course even though we already had our three listed courses, dessert was included.  They bring over a cart full of homemade tarts for you to choose from.  I had the Lemon Meringue Tart which had just enough tartness to cut through the very large, very rich lunch I just had.  Somehow I managed to finish the whole slice.  It was the most perfect ending to an exquisite meal.  Or so I though.  There was no bottle of cognac this time, but not long after I cleaned my plate did the waitress come over with a sampling of macaroons again.  I couldn't help myself but to have one... maybe two... okay, three cookies.  I had to stop because any more food and there was a good chance I wouldn't be able to get up out of my seat.

The lunch menu at EMP is clearly a cheaper alternative than dinner.  There aren't as many frills, but you definitely get a very nice bang for your buck (two-course at $28 or three-courses at $42).  If you still haven't been, there really is no excuse.

We would go again in a heartbeat, and can't think of anything I would rather do with a few hours in Manhattan.  Althought a lot more expensive for lunch than the Shake Shack across the street, the line is a lot shorter, although you really should have a reservation.

We had the 3 course prix fixe menu ($42, without wine) and every thing from the delicious bread and butter to the dessert -- we split the Fuji apple pie, and I'm buying a tart pan tonight so I can make it when I get home (the caramelized flavor made every other apple pie I've ever had a distant second.

We had no wine as we wanted to stay awake the rest of the afternoon, and the cost was $113 plus tip, which I consider a good value considering the great staff, setting, presentation, and taste sensations.

For the reviewer who complained that the restaurant didn't make special vegetarian dishes for her:  Get over yourself.  A restaurant isn't your mother.  If you go to a nice restaurant that doesn't cater to veggies, you need to make due -- it isn't the obligation of the chef to satisfy everyone. -- I think there is enough good veggie fare to satisfy most anyone.

For those who down rate a restaurant, ask where you can get a similar meal in Manhattan at a lesser cost.  If you can be "just as happy" somewhere else for a lot less, go there -- someone will be happy to take your place.  A hamburger joint can get five stars from me if it is really good, and I'll often go there, but I won't measure one against the others.

My wife is a picky eater, and eats no red meat, and very little fish, but she ate her scallops and salmon, claiming they were as good as anything she had ever had in a restaurant.  She raved about her salad and each individual ingredient.  She really doesn't like mint, but somehow loved the mint oil drizzles on her entree.
  
I had the crab linguini, and although I don't like pasta swimming in butter, it was wonderfully buttery.

LOVED IT! Service was excellent!! Really liked all the peeps and soooo knowledgeable!! The wine list was amazing and had very hard to find vintages : ). The food was superb and the special touches were perfection. At the end of the night they left a bottle of Cognac at the table for our leisurely consumption! WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE

I have eaten here twice. Very pricey but that's what happens when you eat gold. Food is top notch and so is the service. I was more than happy to empty my bank account here. Danny Meyer is a restaurant genius. I had a gnocchi in a truffle foam I wanted to take a bubble bath in.

This was a huge disappointment.   I booked a lunch reservation on Opentable and noted that I was a vegetarian.  Also confirmed with the restaurant numerous times that this would not be an issue (they said they would let the kitchen know).  When I got there, they told me that besides the three vegetarian options on the menu, they could do a linguini or roasted vegetables.  Really?  That's ALL you can do after having weeks of notification?  What shocks me is that they do a tasting menu and a gourmand menu that can be entirely vegetarian as well - so what do they serve a different vegetable for each course?  Also, they served our entree about 45 minutes after our appetizer.  The service apologized but it would have been nice to have a dessert comped or something.  The service was very awkward - definitely did not seem like a top restaurant.   The dishes I had were good, but it was disappointing that there was such a limited selection and such poor service.  They didn't even tell us what they were serving like most other restaurants in this tier.  I also sent the restaurant an email expressing my disappointment and haven't heard back.   No excuse for this kind of service at supposedly one of the best restaurants in the city.

this was my first fine-dining experience in nyc, and it's still my favorite, after 6 years! went here for the 2nd time last month for a group birthday celebration. 

food, ambiance and service are impeccable.. i love that the 3-course tasting dinner menu is actually a 7-course menu because of all the amuse bouche -- a couple of which appear as courses in the full tasting menu. 

they started us with tasty little gougères (cheese puffs), then an hors d'oeuvres plate including foie gras macarons & sweetbread dumplings. next up we had a delicious madras curry soup with langoustines. after our prix-fixe appetizers, entrees (standouts were the lobster and black angus beef), and dessert, the final extra course was a plate of assorted macarons (like lemon poppyseed, grapefruit fennel and pb & j) accompanied by a glass of cognac for each of us, and then they left the bottle on our table! 

so even if that $95 3-course tasting menu price seems a bit daunting, think of it more as a 7-course.. the whole experience is well worth it. 

note on the dress code: 
no strict dress code, but male guests may feel more comfortable with jacket (preferred) and shoes instead of sneakers. that being said, i saw plenty of guys in there wearing t-shirts and jeans.. but they definitely looked out of place since even the waitstaff was far more presentable!

EMP probably doesn't need another stellar, raving review, but I just feel compelled to share my experience.

I visited EMP over spring break with two of my college gal pals and we had a 4-hour dining experience of our LIVES (so far). 

FOOD
we ordered the gourmand tasting menu. first came toasted olive bread with both salted and unsalted butter, and some amuse buches. the first course was a frothy sea urchin and crab soup that came plated in a bowl shaped like a pumpkin without its top. the dish was light and decadent at the same time. the second course was salad with buffalo mozzarella, champagne mango, and terre bormand olive oil. such a simple dish but executed perfectly. each ingredient's flavor really come out in this dish and it was a great segue way and palate cleanser for the third course, which was foie gras served with rum-raisin brioche. i've never had foie gras before so i didn't know what to expect. i was full at this point and didn't know if i could eat any more. thankfully EMP seems to get this, and we had a nice break before our 4th course, atlantic halibut, came out. the way they cooked the halibut really highlights the flavor of halibut. the meat was tender and i wanted more!! the 5th course was milk fed veal - the most tender pieces of cow i have ever tasted. the 6th course was a peanut butter palette - caramel popcorn and popcorn ice cream. the saltiness really balanced the sweetness, and it was a great way to finish the tasting menu

SERVICE
our waiter daniel was awesome!! i think he was very amused by our enthusiasm for each course, and our constant picture taking. he also gave us an extra piece of dessert from the dessert cart and sent us home with olive oiil!!! but the very very best part of this meal was meeting the executive chef Daniel!!! He was so modest and shy and humble and I was just awe-struck to meet the man who'd created the dishes we'd just eaten.

We paid $90 including tip and tax, and even though it was a lot of money for our college student budgets, I think it was totally worth it. You can 2 - 3x pay more elsewhere and not get anywhere near the level of service of quality of execution of food that you get at EMP. they totally deserve those 4 NYT stars!

Next time I come to NYC I want to try the dinner tasting menu! I definitely recommend EMP to anybody visiting NY.

I'd like to conserve giving out 5 stars... Ideally, Eleven Madison Park deserves 4.5 stars...

This restaurant is certainly worth trying out at least once.  One of the highlights of the night is the complimentary mignardises and champagne cognac.

In conclusion - highly recommended.

First of all, I strongly believe that Danny Meyer's book Setting the Table ought to be mandatory reading for all restaurateurs who are serious about treating their customers well.  If you want to see what perfect service and treatment of patrons looks like, Eleven Madison will show you.
