I will say that the smoked pork belly was amazing, and possibly one of the best things I've ever eaten.  But otherwise, I totally regret the $500+ we spent on dinner last night between the two of us.

Delicious. Had the Taste of Autumn (5 courses) with the wine pairings. All were unbelievable. Hawaiian prawns were a great start. The crusted dover was fantastic. I have to say, far and away, the best dish was the pig though. Goodness, I'll be honest, I almost killed my date so I could have her plate. True story. Perfect service as well. Not sure if it's possible but I'd suggest the 5 or even 11 course tasting...just ask for all 5 or 11 courses to be the pig.

Have you ever food-gasmed just listening to the description of food?  No?  Well, I nearly did.  And I could not have picked a better (non-Gramercy Tavern) restaurant to patronize for my husband's birthday.

There's not much for me to add to all these great reviews, but if you go during winter '09, you must get the hare and the Dover sole (part of the two seasonal tasting menus).  You'll have to ask for them special if you're not getting those tasting menus, but I promise the reward on your tongue and in your belly will be worth any embarrassment.

We had only been here once, long ago, and I said then that I didn't feel loved.  Well, I felt the love this time.  We spent 5 hours being lavished with food and attention.  My husband actually said, "If you ever happen to meet Danny Meyer again, you tell him we love him and his restaurants."

As a final note, before dessert, while the table was being cleared, we joked with one of the servers about how we wanted our leftover goat's milk butter to go.  Imagine our surprise as we left to find that we had a bag with, in fact, a new serving of butter wrapped up for us with information about the purveyor.

Wow.
For my review, please go to:  http://holypozole.blogspot.com/2008/03/camilles-29th-birthday-eleven-madison_10.html

One of the best dining experiences ever!  I was invited here at the last minute and so was "that person" wearing jeans and sneakers.  Yet the service was impeccable.  I seriously felt like a queen, converse and all.  Our waitress was lovely and explained every single dish in vivid detail.  The servers brought out our food in perfect unison; it could only be described as choreography (see: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kchxqnvQwcI).

The food here is a treat for the eyes and the mouth.  We each ordered the $88/person three-course prix fixe, which actually comes with several tantalizing extras.  I don't think you could go wrong with anything on the menu but we had (and loved): the Hawaiian prawn roulade and heirloom beets to start; loup de mer and halibut; and the summer melon dessert.  And this is just stuff that was on the menu.  I'm not even going to bother describing the extras because the element of surprise was partly what made this meal so fantastic.  If you were at Eleven Madison last week and heard periodic squeals of joy, that was probably our table.

After dessert, we were presented with a huge tray of mini macaroons and were told that we could go to town with it.  To top it all off, we each got a box of jellies to take home by which to remember this awesome meal.  This restaurant should be on everyone's short list!

This place is really elegant with good service and wonderful food.  The 2-course lunch pre-fix is a great deal.  Note that dessert costs extra.

Everything was well-presented, perfectly executed, flavorful but not overly heavy.  I particularly enjoyed my pan-seared skate entree.  For dessert - we were given a choice of a variety of cakes and tarts from a dessert cart.  The waiter would slice it up in front of the table before serving it.  I really enjoyed that.  We tried the raspberry tart and one of the cakes - both were delicious.

We decided to go to Eleven Madison Park for our anniversary after reading the 4 star review they just got in the Times. Made the reservation 3 weeks ahead of time for a Tuesday night. Was able to park right on Madison Ave without a problem.

We had to wait 15-20 minutes for our table but that was the only real negative to the night (besides the price). We waited at the vibrant bar and enjoyed a cocktail before the attentive hostess sat us.

The service is impeccable, this was our first 4 star experience and were surprised how the entire staff seemed to wait on us hand and foot. When my wife asked where the bathroom was the waitress didnt simply point it out, but esorted her there. The restaurant manager introduced himself and seemed very attentive, and even Chef Humm came by to say hello (he spent a considerable amount of time at a table that featured a couple of countrymen).

The food was spectacular from beginning to end. Everything we had was either completely new to us, or prepared in a new manner. We opened with the Knoll Krest Farm Egg (featuring frog legs and truffles, very tasty) and one of the jewels of the meal: the succulant Fois Gras.

I had the Angus Beef Marrow (very good, a little heavy) and my wife had the Suckling Pig (very tender and tasty). 

Even though we were pretty full after about 2 hours of dining, we were pleasantly surprised with the dessert course: she had something sweet and chocolatey, which was okay, but I had the other jewel of the night: the fresh summer melon plate. 

This place is first class and it comes with, unfortunately, a first class price. The dinner service is $88 3-course prix fix (unless you go for one of the seasonal tasting menus which can run you $150-$300 a head), the fois gras was a $20 supplement, we brought our own wine but there is a $35 corking fee, plus the pre-dinner drinks and post-dinner coffee and our bill came to about $350 with taxes and tip. Thats pretty hefty for dinner for two (when you consider what I paid for the wine off-site and it cost us well over $400).

If you can afford it, I recommend it.

Love the bright open dining space, as well as the yellow-green roses at the entrance and in the main room.  Liked that they had a $28 wine menu to go along with their $28 lunch menu.

Octopus Salad with Mizuna, Avocado and Radishes wasn't earth-shattering, but the octopus was well cooked and the salad was superbly dressed.

Tete de Cochon with Pickled Baby Vegetables was higher quality than my friend expected and the assortment of vegetables paired well with the meat.

Poached Snapper with Fennel, Shellfish and Sauce Bouillabaisse had fantastic sauce and the snapper was high quality.  

The star of the lunch was my Lobster with Lemon Verbena and Flavors of Ratatouille.  Huge, succulent lobster tail and claws, cooked to perfection.

Service was excellent, and our waiter gave us an additional complementary desert (Chocolate Peanut Butter Palette, Carmel Popcorn and Popcorn Ice Cream) in addition to the Blueberry & Brown Sugar Crumble and Macarons we ordered.

Just thinking of my meal at Eleven Madison Park right now makes me want to go back asap.  Last year, we celebrated my mom's birthday at Le Bernardin, but our experience at EMP this year was just THAT much better.  What the NYTimes says about Eleven Madison Park getting better and better with the years is spot on.  This is now my favorite fine dining restaurant in NYC.

The five of us decided to get the three course prix fixe for $88/p.  However, what you get is a lot more than three courses.  What you get is also a number of amuse-bouches like gougeres (small, savory, puffy pastries with cheese), sweetbread (that even i enjoyed), small cup of corn and bacon soup (mouth watering), and an assortment of 4 different canapes per person.  We also received complimentary miniature macaroons (they let you choose from a variety of flavors ranging from rose & pistachio to toasted sesame) and my mother and I received a box of jelly candies to go.

I decided to order the ricotta di capra gnocchi for an appetizer.  I am not a huge fan of goat's milk, so I thought the taste was a bit too strong, but for anybody who enjoys that, they would love it.  Instead, I ended up eating half my dad's plate of Hawaiian prawns with avocado, lime, & yogurt... perfect balance of sweetness and zest.  For the main entree, I ordered the Atlantic halibut which practically melted in my mouth.  My brother and Charles ordered the muscovy duck with blueberries, sweet corn, and a lavender honey glaze.  They carved the whole duck right in front of our table.  Smelling it was almost just as good as tasting it.  And my mother ordered the suckling pig.  It was a tiny piece, but well worth it.  I don't think I have ever had such a succulent piece of pork before.  As if everything wasn't already amazing, the desserts blew us all away.  Most popular at the table was the Tahitian vanilla souffle with a passion fruit dressing... heaven.

Beyond the food was spectacular service.  The sommelier was able to recommend two bottles of wine for us that paired very well with our variety of dishes.  They also put the wine in a decanter for us.  When we asked him about the history of the building, he was able to give us a thorough explanation.  Furthermore, our waiter saw me take my camera out and voluntarily asked if we would like him to take a group picture for us.  Also, he joked around very comfortably with my dad who likes to make fun, but sometimes silly comments.  It is the service and ambience of the restaurant that really completed the meal.  Unlike many other top restaurants, EMP is not stuffy at all, but very welcoming and relaxed.

Please don't get me wrong with the three star review. The food at Eleven Madison Park is amazing and my deepest complements and respect go out to the chef. We enjoyed the three course tasting menu and loved every bite. My husband ordered the Foie Gras (amazing) and lamb (also lucious). I had the gnocchi and pork which I cannot rave about enough. It was divine with tender braised suckling pig draped in perfectly crisped skin. Flawless is the only word that suits.

Unfortunately though, the entire experience was undone by the service. Our waiter hovered intrusively when he was not needed and disappeared when he was. Our food was dropped at our table without ceremony or description and we were left to our own devices to decipher what we were served. Our requests to the waiter to explain the preparation and ingredients were met with vague answers in a condescending tone. (before he scurried away) We were not offered wine beyond the very start of our meal, before we even had menus, and had to chase the waiter to request wine after our courses, all of them, were dropped and cooling on the table. 

All in all, given the reputation of Eleven Madison, we were quite disappointed. 

In short, do go for the food. Don't count on being made welcome.

I decided to go the EMP for my birthday dinner, mostly because while I was west-coasting it for the summer I read of its acclaim in the Times. There is nothing like some well-deserved praise - what a remarkable meal. I may just have to say this was the best I've had in New York. 

We opted for the three course prix fixe after learning from Bruni that they will amuse bouche your belly to satiation. He was not joking. Before our food arrived we had: Gougeres, a crazy good mini morsel of sweetbreads, a plate of eight canapes and a tiny bowl of corn soup. Not too mention the two tiny baguettes with choice of butter (the goat's milk butter was the best I've ever had - put it on the olive baguette).

I started my meal with the gnocchi. SO decadent and a serious portion to boot. I had to put a few on my man's plate. Then I moved onto the lobster poached in lemon verbena heaven. It was the best lobster I've ever had, and I grew up summering on Cape Cod. The lemon verbena idea is simply genius, it complements the richness of the lobster perfectly.

The staff here is excellent, never missed a beat, and they even caught on that it was my birthday while overhearing our somewhat alcohol induced conversation with the table next door (it was her birthday too). They brought me a candle and even gave my husband a gratis dessert when he couldn't decide between a cheese course and dessert. He ended up with both the lucky bastard.

I look forward to returning here and seeing what the chef does with the changing seasons. A + +

Went back again for a special meal and what can I say?

Just as terrific as I remember from my first experience. This is truly one of the best restaurants in the entire country. The servive is genuinely warm, professional, and impeccably perfect!

Cuisine is delicious beyond words. Did a customized tasting menu and once again they were very accomodating in allowing me to supplement and add dishes. Standouts were the lobster, rack of pork from the suckling pig tasting, beef tenderloin with bone marrow, and the lamb chop was utterly amazing.

For dessert, you must have the new cornbread pudding dessert with blueberries, blueberry sorbet, corn sabayon. Maybe the best dessert I have put into my mouth. The chocolate peanut butter palette and chocolate symphony no. 2 also awesome.

Go here if you have any respect for yourself lol.

very nice decor; great service, good food.

but, i mean, their food is great, matching against 5-star restaurant standard. they are fresh and of good quality, great presentation and all, but unfortunately, nothing stood out or deemed memorable. maybe it was just me, or maybe my memory was overshadowed by the whole array of desserts we got to sample afterwards.

yes, my sister used to work there as a pastry chef (hence this meal), so we got the goodies FOC.  90% of the desserts we had were fantastic, although some were too sweet to my taste. 

that was a few years ago too; now both my sister and her boss have left, so i can't say for sure what it's like there now.

4 stars for food.
5 for service.
4.5 average!

Service really does enhance a restaurant experience because when you've got great servers, you know that if you're unhappy with your meal they'll do what's possible to make it right.  

For once, in a 5-star restaurant, I was no ashamed to say that I am a pescatarian and no, I am sorry, I will not be participating in your sausage plate.  The server was very sensitive to my dietary needs, and they brought us great amuse-bouches as well as a free dessert tray of french macaroons (my favorite cookies!)

The ravioli blew me away, the salmon-- not so much.  I'm not a fan of dishes with foam.  I think the skate would probably have been the smarter choice.  My boyfriend adored his sausage, and mopped up the sauce with all of our bread.  That all being said, it definitely was above average, nearing excellent, food.

The service, though-- Jeff, our waiter, poured a perfect martini at the table and brought a million little trays of garnishes to top it off with.  He recommended perfect wine, and his associate (a lady) walked me to the restroom when I asked where it was! At first, you feel like you don't deserve to be treated so well but you know what?  Eleven Madison Park is mad expensive.  You do deserve it.  OWN IT.

i'm giving this place 5 stars strictly because of the hot waiter who graced our table with his smiling, dimpled presence. otherwise i found the sea foam or whatever on my salmon incredibly anticlimactic. and the setup of the whole restaurant is bit too stuffy for my tastes. the ceiling's pretty cool though

So last time I had lunch at Jean Georges I decided I would someday become a 'lady who lunches'. Must be in the cards for me because a group of 'ladies who lunch' sat at the table next to us. 

For now I can settle with being a 'girl who lunches' every once in a blue moon. But really $28 for two courses is a great deal. 

They start out by presenting you with a delicious amuse bouche- cucumber with creme fraiche & smoked salmon and a type of radish with salt and butter perhaps? They were both super tasty with wonderful summer flavors and bright colors. 

They give you these cheese puff pastries that are impossible not to devour whole one after the other. The olive bread was also absolutely deliciously warm and tasty. 

1. Sweet Corn Chowder with Nova Scotia Lobster and Bacon
2. Lamb Sausage with Arugula, Tomato Confit and Potato Mousseline

The corn chowder was a beautiful yellow color with perfectly cooked pieces of lobster that were bursting with brightness and flavor. Absolutely a wonderful beginning. Mr. Humm really takes advantage of what the summer has to offer in his menu. Every bite was like enjoying a warm summer day. 

The lamb sausage dish was filled with deep smoky flavors of all kinds with a tomato confit that tasted so sweet and balanced the spicy smoky sausage so well. The potato was also a wonderful component to the dish. This felt like extremely refined comfort food. 

My companion's snapper ala bouillabaisse was absolutely fantastic and perfectly done as well. Her appetizer was a sort of terrine that had pickled vegetables that were so delicious. 

For desert they bring out the desert cart and it is so difficult to choose and impossible to turn away from. I wish we could have had all of them. 

1. Blueberry & Brown Sugar Crumble
2. Lemon Meringue tart

Once again Eleven Madison Park was able to achieve an extremely refined version of a classic comfort dish. The blueberry crumble was light and yet showcased the strong delicious flavors that a blueberry has. Absolutely delectable and as satisfying as any chocolate desert would be. The lemon meringue tart was also light and delicious with a soft meringue as an accompaniment. 

Small yet beautiful space, efficient service, fantastic food and at a wonderful price. What more could you ask for on a beautiful summer day?
Went for lunch and was blown away. Dying to return for a full on dinner - a stalwart classic that is a must for anyone claiming to enjoy superb food and fine dining. Excellent wine list as well.

Went last night for my 1st year anniversary and had the 11 courses.  Everything I want to say has already been said, so I will add that at the end of the meal they left us with a bottle of cognac. Granted, at this point I really couldn't drink much more after having the wine pairing, but it was just another example of the superior service. If you have the money and a special event, go for it.

I've only dined at Eleven Madison Park once, and I am returning next month. 
I started with a glass of their House Champagne. Vinified in a unique manner, similar to the Sherry-making Solera method, it was complex, nuanced and well balanced- the perfect aperitif.
I opted for the 5 course Gourmand menu with wine pairings.  I won't go through course by course, but I will say that every single course was perfectly executed, as far as my palette could tell. A touch of molecular gastronomy was balanced by solid flavor contrasts and compliments, interesting textures, and simply well-done preparation techniques. Presentation was unique and fun without flamboyance.  The wine pairings were of course dead-on. The best, or most interesting, wine was the Gruner Veltliner by Knoll. I have never experienced a Gruner of this complexity- an Austrian Meursault! Service was warm and friendly, professional and hospitable. Neither pretentious nor starchy. Alexandra anticipated our every need. I must mention that it is a real bargain, and now that the restaurant has received its fourth NYT star, I recommend you get there soon before the pricetag goes up!

I go to EMP often for lunch and more rarely for dinner. It is a first-class restaurant in every way. The service is exemplary, attentive but not too pushy. The space is very elegant, quite impressive during the day with the large windows, although it can be a little dull at night. the food is consistently excellent, rich but not too much, and the wine list is solid and has a good amount of choices below $85. 

The prix fixe during lunch at around $25 is amazing value and highly, highly recommended. With that amount you get an appetizer and main course, amuse bouche and their excellent bread and cheese puffs. They even have walk-ins most days at lunch if you go a little late

Now that was $430 well spent.  The food was excellent and the service superb.  I don't think I can think of a place that has better service! One of the few places that I've been where the food that was brought out looks just like the picture on the site.  Even if you don't like French cuisine, the beautiful presentation will make your mouth water.  The wait staff was friendly and knowledgeable, not at all stuck up as one might expect them to be. The two us had plenty of drinks and two different tasting menus to share and the check came to $430 including tax and a 25% tip.  The only downside is that if you are the kind of person who gets restaurant anxiety,  you may not want to get the tasting menu.  After three hours, I finally had to cut outside before dessert to grab a quick cig.  Don't misunderstand, I am not a very patient person, and the wait between courses felt like nothing, and I had no idea 3 hours had gone by. If it weren't for the little internal cigarette clock...  Overall, great experience.  Can't wait for another occasion to go back.  A definite do try, but don't forget that tie...or you might feel a little out of place.
Five delishes on my scale.

This is a 5 star restaurant in every single regard other than the bottom line.  Room: soaring, beautiful.  Service: friendly, meticulous.  Amuse-bouches and petit-fours: generous, creative.  But the apps and mains: tasty, well-executed, but just not exciting. At $140-$150 a person with even the most basic foray into the wine a little more is expected.

Wife and I celebrated our 1 year anniversary a week early by having the Gourmand at EMP on Tuesday night.

Everything was simply perfect from the food to the service to the decor to the company.

I didn't write anything down so this is off the top of my head....

Hors doeuvres.  Approximately six items.  Standouts were the lobster/creme fraiche on small cucumber and the one with foie gras.

Caviar (served in its tin) over panna cotta, sturgeon eggs and lobster gel.  My wife has shellfish allergy so they put the caviar over a creamy avocado something or other.  She said the combo was excellent.

Tomato and mozzarella ala molecular gastronomy served on two white spoons.  See picture above.

Dueling tomatoes...served three ways.  One was tomatoes under a tomato foam another was sorbet-like and the third was tartare.

Sea urchin cappuccino with crab and cauliflower soup.

Foie gras course.

Halibut with freeze dried corn.

Lobster tail poached with lemon verbena and flavors of ratatouille.

Eggshell filled with sabayon, frogs legs and truffle.  AWESOME!

Elysian Fields Farms lamb with goat cheese pie, chick peas, green peas and a very fun picholine olive bubble (molecular gastronomy) served from a jar.  This was develeped in honor of Ferran Adrià's recent visit.

Cheese course.  Three different varieties for each of us depending on our own personal preferences.

Strawberry/champagne foam dessert #1

Raspberry/chocolate dessert #2

Six varieties of macaroons.

Should you eat at 11 Madison? Yes Yes Yes and then go back... I have worked in the top Kitchen's in Portland Oregon and under James Beard award winning chefs.  I have tasted a lot of food and Chef Daniel Hum's food is Amazing.  Everything was spot on.  Flavor profiles perfect, Seasoning perfect, presentation elegant.  Eleven Madison provided everything I want in an upscale meal.  There are very few Chefs who create a meal that you 'taste' the next day and that memory/taste evokes thoughts and flavors that are so real and amazing, 11 Madison is one of those few restaurants that creates food that you will 'taste' the next day.

Such a classy dining experience with excellent food!

My brother and I shared the chicken for two with truffles, and we ordered a plethora of deserts, and everything tasted incredible. I recommend the passion-fruit desert they make!

Also the service is the most incredible in the city and part of the atmosphere is watching the routes that all the servers and waiters have to take to get to the tables.

This place is the epitome of classy, and my whole family loved it and would come back every day if we lived in New York. In fact, we may fly back to new york just to eat here again.

I've just been back to Eleven Madison Park after four months away. Right off the bat, the sommelier's face brightened when she saw me and she asked me how I'd been. One waiter I'd never seen before heard I had 3 Greater Swiss Mountain Dogs (I mentioned this when I was here in March, mind you) and wanted to chat about the breed since his parents in Wisconsin just bought one. This is before the food as well. So at this point I already feel I'm absolutely in the right place.

There follows the best amuses bouches I've ever had, including a foie gras that made me want to lie down accompanied by a Claude Genet blancs de blancs Champagne; a Santa Barbara sea urchin cappuccino with Peekytoe crab and Cauliflower accompanied by a Dewazakura sake; Greenmarket heirloom tomatoes with olive oil and basil accompanied by a Domaine de Deffends Rosé du Nuit, which lays on the grape skins just one night, ergo the name; a tete de cochon with cornichons and baby radishes accompanied by a Niedermenniger Herrenberg Spätlese Trocken from Saar (yes, you're reading that correctly, a sweet dry wine that almost never gets out of Germany without being drunk by the Germans); a Nova Scotia (my peeps!) lobster poached with lemon verbena (yes, the actual shrub) accompanied by a phenomenal dried butterscotch-flavored 2007 Mas de Daumas Gassac blanc from Languedoc, which itself had 20% 'heirloom' grapes you can't find anywhere outside the region; an Elysian Field Farm (PA!) herb-roasted lamb chop with sheep's milk tart, sweet onions and bacon accompanied by a jaw-dropping 2000 Talenti Brunello di Montalcino; a pre-dessert course of summer melons with a citrus tapioca accompanied by a yes-I-was-born-to-taste-this 2008 Elio Perrone Clarté Asti from Piedmont; and finally a chocolate peanut butter 'palette' with caramel popcorn and popcorn ice cream accompanied by a Madeira from the New York Rare Wine Company. And amazing coffee. And a Normandin Mercier cognac. And sweets to bring home. And a rolled copy of the menu tied with gray ribbon.

After which Chef Daniel Humm, a freakishly young Swiss, comes around to my table to ask how everything was. What could I say? I'll tell you what I said: that the closest thing to immortality for we mortals is immersion in the moment, and his food takes me there. That's what I felt. And that's what a world-class restaurant is about: not the snooty treatment at the door (which ain't Eleven Madison by a mile), but both decanting your body from your soul for a few short synaptic moments and being laser-present with the cascade of flavors from a liquid dot of olive or a spoonful of tomato cloud that doesn't just taste, it haunts you. 

So, five stars on everything. Better than Le Bernardin in New York, better than Kommandanten in Copenhagen, better than L'Espalier in Boston and Quince in San Francisco. For warmth, genuineness, gastronomic genius, gorgeousness of room, wine list, service, floral arrangements, sylvan Madison Park surrounds, music (Coltrane, Miles, Mingus, Horace Silver, Bill Evans), value for money, even the quality of tiling in the Men's room for God's sake, I am really having a hard time imagining how Eleven Madison Park as a holistic package can be equaled. 

I am plotting my next visit already. In the meantime, God bless everyone there. I mean that.

Each and every bite creates an explosion of flavor.  The food is so fresh and carefully prepared into small experiences that give dining new meaning.  Each time I dine at EMP it only gets better.  I had the lunch pre fixe--2 course meal, ordered every desert and a bottle of wine, oh yes and the margaritas are even made from fresh ingredients!  Of course they start you off with their amuse bouche which was salmon in cucumber and radishes dipped in salted butter (I like these radishes!!!) and then a lobster bisque which was light and truly full of flavor.  For my meal I started with sweet corn chowder, with lobster and bacon, the corn was cooked perfectly and a few were a bit crunchy, the broth was a perfect blend of spices.  My main course was the black angus beef saute.  The meat melted in your mouth. It was cooked to perfection.  The potatoes left you wanting more and the veggies were crisp and fresh.  The sauce was light but truly enhanced the flavors in the beef.  I cannot begin to say enough about this dish!  The desert tray looked so good we ordered one of each.  The chocolate dish was rich with a blend of spices and a very faint crust that satisfied all chocolate cravings.  The sorbets tasted as if they took ripened fruit and put them in a blender they were so fresh.  I know, I know all of this could add up to be a big bill but go for their lunch pre fixe, it is well worth the splurge!

One word...  Excellent.

The best service I've ever experienced from the moment you walk in.  You have multiple waiters tending to your every need.  The food was amazing.  I've been there on four occasions and I never leave disappointed.

Today I went for lunch ($28 price fixe, how can you beat that?!).  It's a two course meal w/ dessert.  We before our first course they brought a chilled lobster bisque.  I usually like by bisque warm but this was one of my favorite experiences.  Started out with a dollop of cream topped by a few morsels of lobster surrounded by the chilled bisque.

My first course was sweet corn chowder with a frothy pumpkin foam on top.  Inside the chowder were small bits of crisp bacon and some more morsels of lobster!

Main coures I had the famous and suckling pig.  One portion was similar to pulled pork with confit and crisped to perfection.  The other was a moist selection of pork tenderloin roasted just enough to retain it's plump juices.

Whenever I go, I always sample other dishes from my guests so I was able to experience the Black Angus sirloin with sauce bordelaise.  It was quite possibly the best steak I've ever had.

Also had the lamb sausage with potato mousseline.  A must have if you like game.  I'm getting hungry just typing this again.  You have to go if you want the best dining experience and food.  A must visit for all foodies.

I was impressed with everything about Eleven Madison Park.  From the ambiance, service, food presentation, food quality and taste - everything was perfectly executed. I knew it was going to be a great experience based on what I had been told from friends and family - but it exceeded my expectations.  This is a 5 star restaurant, without question.  We had the Spring Chef Tasting menu.  As I do with an experience like this  (i.e. Cyrus, French Laundry) I don't want to get into every dish I had. Please go and experience it for yourself because words cannot describe it.

The distinction of being named part of the Relais-Chateaux says it all.  Every detail for a perfect meal last night was executed with the similar precision of a Marine formation special ceremony without being super rigid.  The staff was amazingly friendly and attentive from the first instance of walking through the door until you leave.  The very lovely sommelier was kind enough to do a glass pairing with our food last evening.  And on top of it, gave us recommendations for our Trip to France in a few months.  And just prior to dessert the Chef, Daniel Humm came around to every table to check on how our meal was that evening.  Only rave reviews came from us.  

The food even topped the service.  We opted for the 2 savory 1 sweet option on the menu (3 course), but you get all the extras of an amuse bouche, bread, hours d'oeuvres (which were awesome little bites of foie gras, salmon on cucumber, fried sweetbreads, etc.) macaroons at the end.  You wind up getting way more than just 2 savory and 1 sweet.  

1st Course:
We opted for the Tomato Salad at the delight of waiter once we mentioned it, there was no turning back. (Paired with a glass of Rose)  And
We also got the FLUKE with uni cream (Paired with a glass of SAKE)

2nd Course:
The 4 story farms suckling pig (Piece of loin and shoulder with crispy skin) FAVORITE (Paired with a delicious burgundy
The Halibut with fresh and dried corn and some mushrooms was light and moist.  (Paired with a delicious white burgundy)

Cheese and Dessert 
The cheeses were awesome, but the stand out was the Triple Creme Goat cheese they have made for them.  WOW!
The chocolate symphony 2 with caramel and sea salt pretty much (To break it down a notch) was the best slice of pie I have had in a long time.  (The fact that I even called it pie is an atrocity, but I didn't know what to call this little sliver of heaven.)

EMP...see you again real soon.  This meal was EXCELLENT and looking forward to many many more.

I visited EMP with my boyfriend a month+ ago to celebrate his birthday.  

We were pretty excited given the overwhelming appreciation for the restaurant on Yelp.  On the service side, the reviews were dead on: As with many restaurants of this caliber, the service and ambiance of EMP was impeccable.  The waiter was clearly watching our experience and checking-in when necessary, without bombarding us throughout our dinner.  Everyone serving us was knowledgeable, friendly and very professional.

I'm only giving the restaurant 3 stars due to our disappointment with the food.  While the presentation was excellent and the plates were creative, it wasn't AS amazing (if that makes sense) as we had anticipated.  My fish was slightly overdone and a month after our dinner, that's about all I can recall about the meal.  We limit our experiences of these amazing restaurants to just a hanfdul a year and this was the first time we walked away slightly disappointed with the food.

One minor hiccup - I had informed the restaurant that we were there to celebrate my boyfriend's birthday.  So it was cute and touching that they had customized his menu to say "happy birthday ____" on the top... except, they put the wrong name!  It was absolutely no big deal, it didn't impact our dinner in anyway, but it might have been better if they didn't try to customize at all.  

We do think that perhaps our experience was different because of the pre-fixe menu and we do plan on going back someday for the "real" EMP experience.  But for a dinner that was expensive even without any alcohol, it's going to be hard for us to decide to go back anytime soon.

Unbelievable experience all around. The foodwas amazing ( had the suckling pig and my wife had the veal with sweetbreads). But what really made the night was the Danny Meyer special...The service. It was like nothing we'd exp before. Down to giving us a hand written recipe for the Pimm's Cup cocktail we briefly mentioned we enjoyed at the start of the meal (highly recommend u try one as well). A++ for any special occassion

My husband and I just celebrated our first anniversary at Eleven Madison Park.  Without a doubt, this is the best restaurant experience we have ever had, hands down.  The level of service left me speechless, and at one point the level of detail and thoughtfulness actually nearly brought me to tears.  

As soon as we entered the restaurant they gave us the impression that they had been looking forward to our arrival, despite being a few minutes early for our reservation. We had let them know that it was our anniversary and they pulled out all the stops to make sure that we had a memorable experience.

The food was amazing and we found ourselves blown away by each course.  Every bite was thoughtful, beautifully presented, and delicious, it is also worth noting that the dishes were delicate, but filling. 

I wish I could give the restaurant a sixth star for the service.  They really made a special effort to meet our every need and provided extras that we could not have even imagined. 

I agree with other reviewers, the price definitely reflects the experience, so I may reserve this for a special occasion. This was the most we had ever paid for a dinner for two, but we were happy to give a very good tip because we felt the experience was worth every penny.

Fantastic Experience. One of the best I have ever had. 

Incredible room (great lighting and ambiance) 
Impeccable service.
Absolutely amazing food. We had the duck for 2. Best I have ever had. 
Super friendly, knowledgeable and helpful Sommelier. She found us exactly what we were looking for. 
Drinks at the bar before were also top notch. 

NYtimes gave it 3 stars? It deserves 4.

Well worth the money.

Update
8/12/2009 Finally, NYtimes gives EMP the 4 stars it deserves!

Eleven Madison Park is the epitome of fine dining.  The food, service, and ambiance are all completely top-notch.  The menu is seasonal so the dishes change up, but this is one of those "whatever you get is going to be good" type places.

The price reflects the experience, so it may be best reserved for special occasions (or expense accounts).

The gourmand tasting menu + wine pairings clocks in at about $300 before tax and tip, but boy is it worth it. 

The service is absolutely top-notch. The decor was grand, but tasteful. The service, decor and the unforgettable foie gras push it to a 5 star review.

This review has nothing to do with dining at the restaurant.  Go to 11 madison park, sit by the bar, look at the kitchen (which is stunning), order a vodka martini with onions (it takes 10 minutes to make, which is an enigma in and of itself) and get the peanut butter jelly sandwich (brioche with foie gras and rhubarb chutney).  If you want to go crazy, get the asparagus with the egg on top.  Out of this world.
Excellent food served in breathtakingly large and bright quarters.

I'll be honest - this was my first dining experience where 10 waiters/servers are at your beckon-call and service is meticulous. this was one of the top of my restaurants-to-try list in NYC, so my sister and i made a reservation (luckily she's a baller-shot-calla and paid).

upon sitting down in the dimly-lit space filled with beautiful flower arrangements, we were given a drink menu and ordered one sweet white wine and a red. both were good, but i forget what they were. in fact, if i didn't have photographs of all the food here, i wouldn't remember anything we ate there, which is really telling about this place.

i believe the dinner here is always pri-fixe, with a bit of wiggle room on what entree you can order. according to my photos, this is what we had:

- encrusted-goat cheese balls: amazing and crisp on outside, rich on inside

- bread & butter: 1 was a fresh goat's milk butter, the other was cow butter w/ sea salt sprinkled atop. these were both amazing

- a plate of hors douvres': they were beautifully presented, but the flavors themselves were a bit bland and not specatular

- a crab-salad rolled in a skin of avocado with a side of creme fraiche sauce. again, beautifully presented, almost like a sushi roll. very tasty, but tasted plain.

- filet mignon slices w/ spinach and garlic cloves: this meat was amazing, tender, and tasty. it was a bit bloody, but i like my meat rare

- pork with an encrusted glaze, asparagus, and some sauce on the side. this dish was very good at first bite but ended up being way too rich. it needed more vegetables on the side to neutralize the fat & salt.

- dessert: umm, i forget. but they were tasty and very unique.

- plate of desserts: these were very beautifully presented. it came with mini-sizes of macaron, peanut butter cup, strawberry cake, lemon tart, dark chocolate truffle.

service was impeccable, but almost to the point where my sister and i had to compliment every dish (with mouths full) to make the waiter go away.

i give this place 4 stars because it just wasn't worth the money to me. it came out to probably over $140 per person, and nothing particularly stood out to me. i really do appreciate how food became art, though.

I remember, long time ago, we had a dinner reservation at Tabla and we instead walked into Eleven Madison Park. They gently directed us to the right location. I looked at the enormous space with the warm lighting and making a mental note to come back to eat here some day. I did, on two separate occasions. 

Dinner date #1: 
Since EMP asks for about 3 days notice to be able to prepare an eleven course vegetarian meal, and since the boyfriend and I are not ones to skimp on the courses, three days notice it was. When we got there, we found that there had been a miscommunication and they didn't have the meal ready for us. WHat! Hrrmph, I said. Minus 3.4 stars. As we got served each of our (tad smaller) 4 course menu, EMP quickly redeemed its reputation as the culinary heaven that it is reputed to be. Notably, the wine pairings were exquisite! I remember mentioning to our waiter that I like whites better, and for the heavier course, he suggested a white wine that tasted like a red wine! It was so unusual and lovely - tragic that I don't remember the name. 

Dinner date #2: 
Hmm.. there's something nagging me. Hmm.. I still hadn't tasted the eleven course menu! So we decided to call for another reservation. Done. Reminder. Done. Second reminder. Done. 

The food was amazing. Every course. Even the bread. Make sure you taste the olive baguette - it's heavenly. My favourite course was the Jerusalem artichokes with grapes - Brilliant flavours exploding in mouth and all that jazz. The chef came in and greeted us, they made personalized menu cards for us, they kept the wine flowing enough that we didn't notice the amount on the check - I fell in love with the place. We had an amazing evening, mostly consisting of oohs and aahs over the food, for about 5 straight hours. 

Oh and you should take some chocolates home for the next day.

Went with Dad, after some agonizing between Tabla and this.  Sat at the bar.  Started with Octopus Salad.  Dad has the Sweetbreads.  Then had gnocci; Dad had the poached loup de mer.  Each was as good as the last.  Octopus was super-tender and the gnocci were the fluffiest I have ever consumed.  For dessert we asked if we could have the roasted pork from the restaurant menu.  After getting approval, ate the porcine deliciousness (which was, I might add, excessive at $45 for a tasty but small portion).    It was very very good.  Interesting:  on a Saturday night, we were the only people eating in the bar -- the other bar patrons had a drink and then each went and took a table in the restaurant.    Best part:  Dad fought for, and then picked up, the check.

Perfection.

From the rousing amuse bouche up to the delicate petit four finale...Eleven Mad scored a perfect 10 on ambience, service, menu, wine list, food quality & presentation. It is literally impossible to highlight just one aspect of this institution because they have it all impeccably perfected (as the other yelpers have divulged with great detail). 

Needless to say, a perfect experience as such comes at a pretty hefty price, Eleven Mad will not be kind to your AMEX. But if ever possible, for even just once, the gastronomical experience here will be one of those that you will remember even when you're 90 with dementia in your rocking chair.
The lunch prixfixe is a great value. Lovely spot for lunch. Was quite empty on Friday due to the downturn I am sure. The trotter terrine and snapper were my choices and was very pleased

You're in for an excellent meal.

Wifey and I have been a fan of Chef Humm since his days of cooking at Campton place in San Francisco.  The man's got style, that's for damn sure.
Then he left us, never to return.

So wifey and I decided to get all 'stalker' on his ass and tracked him all the way to NY.

Well worth the effort.

Chef Humm's doing some great things at Eleven Madison Park.  He's using some fantastic seasonal ingredients and transforming them into nothing short of minor miracles on your plate.  His approach is quite modern, but the food's still accessible... and damn tasty.

I had a slow cooked organic egg appetizer that made me see heavenly lights and angels.
And the papardelle with lamb ragout?  I'm crying tears of joy just thinking about it.

There's no way Chef Humm's getting away from us this time.
Wifey and I plan on waiting for him in his closet.
With a bit of rope.
Just to say "hello", ya know?
And to see if he'd like to be our personal chef for a few years...

I was just kidding about the "stalker" thing.
Fantastic in every single respect. Lunch is relatively quiet, and extraordinary value.

Our first visit to Eleven Madison Park six months ago was excellent but not quite mind-blowing. But we went back for a second visit last night and I can honestly say it was one of the best meals I've ever had in my life. I am completely in love with this restaurant and already scheming for the next visit. We did the summer tasting menu (the first time we went we stuck with the prix-fixe) and EVERY single dish from the menu blew me away. I can't remember ONE dish that I wasn't thoroughly impressed with. Even bread course! That delectable goat-milk cheese! (served at room temperature and perfectly spreadable, a sign of a good restaurant -- don't you HATE it when they give you a cold stick of butter?) I won't even go into the description of each dish because that'd easily be a novel. The summer tasting menu is PHENOMENAL, do it before summer's over! The service is impeccable -- cordial, generous, and genuine. They granted every request we made (substituted desserts, wrote down names of wine from wine pairing, speed up the kitchen, etc.) without hesitation and were eager to please. And the space, well, it's an old bank building with a high, high ceiling, VERY grand, VERY beautiful. My husband said the wine pairing was excellent both times -- I don't drink so I can't comment on it, but he was very impressed with their choice of wine for each dish and he's a total wine snob. They also left a bottle of cognac on our table after all the food so the boys (my husband and his friend) could drink as much as he wanted to! Needless to say they left the restaurant VERY happy and so did I -- the recent four-star review from Frank Bruni is SO well-deserved. Run, don't walk to try this place -- I only wish I could come here more often!

EMP is where I had the best meal of my life.  Everything here is absolutely, breathtakingly perfect.

I came for my birthday dinner earlier this year, and we had the Gourmand tasting menu: eleven courses plus an amuse and mignardises.  

Upon arriving at the restaurant, we were escorted to our table and seated, and passed the next 4 hours in absolute heaven.

The room is large, elegant and surprisingly formal, but it is imbued with warmth by excellent lighting and clever use of sound-absorbing materials.  

The service is seamless, elegant, gracious and attentive, surpassing any other destination restaurant in NYC (including Per Se).  From the moment you arrive to the moment you leave, the entire staff treats you like you are the only diner in the restaurant and they seem personally invested in making sure you have an unforgettable experience.  Case in point: we asked a casual offhand question about the butter (it's fantastic) and our server returned two minutes later with a handwritten index card describing the source and tasting notes of the butter and including contact information for the farm from which it came.

The food: Chef Humm is an absolute mastermind.  Each and every course was a hit.   Every flavor, texture, temperature and plating was spot-on and beyond excellent.  Each dish was unique and inventive and danced right on the knife-edge between haute cuisine and baroque fussiness.  

The quality of the cocktails was on par with any of the big 5 cocktail destinations in NYC, and our sommelier was fantastic with helping us choose wine that suited our Californian taste.

It's tough in this economy, but if you have the opportunity to go to Eleven Madison Park you will almost certainly not be disappointed.

(Also, for anyone who desires further proof that Chef Humm may in fact be superhuman, the guy ran the NY Marathon in under 3 hours this year.)

I was a very lucky person to have one of my closest friends treat me to an amazing meal at Eleven.  This was not just a meal but a true culinary experience.  I still dream of this meal.  The restaurant is amazing.  The front of house makes everyone feel as though they are important.  We got an amazing people watching table too.

We had the tasting menu and were delighted (I think I may have even squealed) with each carefully prepared course.  The amuse bouche was the delicate lobster in a flawless bisque, my beet salad was something I can only dream of replicating.  The atlantic char was cooked perfectly.   My friend also had the wine pairings (I only did one with desert) and was not disappointed.  I did have one of their non alcoholic ginger infusions which was refreshing.

This is definitely a place to go if you are in NYC.

This place really sets the standard for other high end restaurants.

The service is impeccable.  The courses were served with perfect timing, presentation of the food perfect, and waiter was attentive and helpful without all that attitude seen in some other restaurants.

Food portions like many high end restaurants tend to be small, but the quality make up for it.  The dishes were not only delcious.but also inventive.

Danny Meyer restaurants simply never fail to amaze me.  This is absolutely a must try.  If I had more money, I would be here every week.

My favorite restaurant for fine dining.

Decor - Beautifully white. Think church and wedding bells.

Service  - Outrageously attentive. Waiters will reset your napkins, clear plates, push aside tables without being ask. The best service I have ever had and that includes dining at Alinea for their touring menu.

Food - Fresh! Delicious! Quality! The dishes were well prepared and the flavor really came through brilliantly. The octopus salad had lots of octopus and was enhanced by the citrus dressing. The braised pork pasta was so earthy and rich. Portions were huge for Restaurant Week. They definitely know how to win customers back.

Dessert was amazing. The contrast and flavors of the chocolate cake and milkshake ice cream blew my mind.

Eleven Madison Park definitely have that special occasion feel to it. But with their $28 prix fix lunch menu it's also very affordable. I had the best lunch here and I can't wait to go back.

I've been here for dinner with my girlfriend twice - May 2007 and Oct 2008 and it has never disappointed.  It's a beautiful art deco space.  The tables for 2 are generously sized and well spaced from other diners.

The hosts/hostesses and waitstaff are always friendly and helpful.  Everyone is always well dressed but I've showed up in just slacks and a button down shirt.

Portions are small and dinner for 2 can easily pass $200 with little acohol but you always leave fuller and more satisfied than you would have thought.  An amuse + 3 courses in a typical dinner + dessert will leave you plenty satisfied.  The menu changes constantly but always has something interesting.  One of the most creative I've ever encountered.  Check a sample menu online to see for yourself.

Went here for restaurant week lunch last Friday and absolutely loved it!!! The poached egg was so flavorful, rich and delicious.  Octupus salad had an interesting combination of flavors. The cheescake with grapefruit sorbert was to die for.  I can't wait to come back for free next time (thanks to the 28 dollar coupons they gave to both my dining companion and I )

The bright sunlight shining through the huge windows just magnified the high ceilings and made the environment so regal.  The impeccable service and great tasting food made me fall in love with this place. I came here for restaurant week last Monday and it was so worth the frigid treck outside.  The salads portions (octo salad and winter green) were rather large and very tasty.  My companion and I both enjoyed my  entree of roasted artic char.  Her entrée of lobster risotto was a bit under cooked and required TOO much chewing-- call me lazy but my teeth HURT from over mastication -- and that's not normal.  BUT, everything else was great.  Would DEFINITELY return again.  **please note, Almost everyone was dressed up and I believe there is a no shorts, no flip flop rule**

My favorite restaurant in NYC.  

i've been several times.  Once for the dinner tasting menu with wine pairings, which ranks among the top-3 meals of my life.  The suckling pig dish is like a really awesome pork candy bar.  Just wish I wasn't so full by the time we got to it.  Oh, and drunk too. 

Also, I've gone a couple times during lunch, which is a great bargain now that the 2-course prix-fixe is only $28.  

In addition, the service is always friendly and competent, and the room is great.  Nice and airy.  I just miss the gold rimmed coffee/tea set they used to have.  I loved them.  I actually emailed the restaurant to find out the brand so I could buy some for my home.  But they were J.L. Coquet and sooooo far out of my budget.  Oh well

I have been here a few times and I haven't been disappointed yet!  This week and next week are part of the 2009 Resturant Week...and what a bargin!  For $24.07, 3 courses that are delicious.  Yesterday I had, the Octopus Salad with Avocado, Fennel and Satsuma Tangerine, the Boudin Blanc with Savoy Cabbage and Poached Seckel Pear and for dessert...a chocolate mousse with malted ice cream.  All in all a very tasty and appetizing meal.

Don't forget the fantastic olive bread!  I'm sure to go back!

Two course $28 lunch pre-fix specials in an airy, huge space off Gramercy Park. That's a lot cheaper than the average $107 it would cost you for dinner. It's a special treat! Portions may be small but the octopus salad and beef stroganoff is YUM YUM YUM. I wasn't in love with the seafood chowder but I think that's because it needed to be hotter.

There are very few meals, actually this would be the first one, that I would call a culinary revelation.  My meal at Eleven Madison was definitely one of them.

Went here for my third wedding anniversary in July 2008.  I thought the space was roomy, yet romantic; the food inventive, yet understandable; and the service top notch.

We had a four course tasting menu that was superbly executed and presented.  However, the highlight, which I can't stop drooling about, was the honey/lavender duck.  This was the centerpiece of my dining revelation at Eleven Madison.  It was a beautiful assault on all the senses at once that I have rarely experienced.  Saving up savor the duck again...

Did I say the service was top-notch, too?  I ordered a Brachetto d'Aqui that I loved so much, I asked to see the bottle.  At the end of the meal without my asking, a nicely hand written card was handed to me with all the relevant information regarding the Brachetto.  Now I have a lovely souvenir of that anniversary dinner, especially when we savor another bottle of Brachetto...

I went there today for lunch. I have the Meche salad and the seafood chowder for the entree. It wasn't as good as advertised as I asked the server was she recommeneded she told to pick those. Presentation was ok for the chowder, and the salad was just plain salad with bacon under the greens. The wine was ok. The person I went out to lunch with had the lobster risotto which was very good, but not knock your sox off good. Would I come back, maybe, because I can expense the lunch. For dinner using my own money? Doubtful. Also the space seemed very cold, and not that impressive. It reminded me of a houstons, except with high ceilings. Not much personality.

I give this restaurant 4 stars, but I cannot imagine many reasons to patronize Eleven Madison Park.  Danny Meyer is a talented restaurateur of the new self-adulation generation, but the cuisine is a bit supererogatory.  Some people might be impressed by foams and new techniques, but even they would have to concede that there are better restaurants in this genre.  I guess I'd proffer a recommendation only to people who avowed desperation to try "weird" ingredients or "particular" ingredients like seckel pears or Iranian figs.

The service is attentive and fine.  I cannot support claims of its being "pretentious."  

The bottom line, though, is that if you want to spend $88 on a menu before wine and dessert, there are many other places I'd recommend before 11MP.

We had an absolutely oustanding brunch here many years ago - probably 2003.  I never went back though because I did not live nearby and it was cost prohibitive.

This is a great "special occaision" restaurant with flawless service, elegant presentation and above all well-executed, fresh delicious food.

I wish I had been here more than once.

I went to EMP for a special occasion dinner  The service is top-notch but not intrusive.  We had the autumn tasting menu and the presentations of all the dishes were the most artistic I've seen.

The most memorable dishes are the foie gras custard with pineapple foam.  It was an ingenious way to enjoy foei gras.  For the entree I had their signature Suckling Pig.  It's similar to the roasted pork with crispy skin you get in some Chinese restaurant but the meat tastes more tender and delicate!  Even the garnishes on the plate also tasted great.  The executive chef came out and greeted tables midway through our dinner.

On the other hands, not all of the dishes had the wow factors.  The other entree we had, which is lamb with sheep milk yogurt, was not impressive.  We had a milk chocolate cakes for desserts.  It looked cute but its taste was very mediocre.

Overall, it's a great restaurant, but I was expecting the food to be between above avg to exceptional throughout the course.  It was not the case.  However, some dishes were true home-runs so it still well deserved a 4 stars in my book.

A beautiful restaurant with a staff that appears to have been trained in the British butler tradition: serve and get out of the way, but don't inject yourself into the experience.  It's a style.  You either don't mind it or the lack of warmth/friendliness bothers you.  There does seem to be a lot of bustling about by the large staff, but it didn't intrude on our experience...that may be because the people I was dining with were pretty entertaining.

I ordered the Colorado lamb and it was easily the highest quality, best cooked piece of lamb I've ever had.  My husband had the suckling pig confit and was intrigued with the preparation (and enjoyed the flavor).

In some of the accompaniments and a couple of the amuse bouche, someone was a bit too fond of fleur de sel.  It didn't spoil any of the flavors but it definitely seemed a little repetitive.  (And it is part of why I didn't give the restaurant a fifth star.)

Although this is an very good restaurant, there wasn't anything I ate that really blew me away (ok, well, the lamb was really beautfully prepared).  Maybe my expectations were too high...but, I probably won't be returning as there are plenty of other more interesting, innovative restaurants in NYC.  And maybe that's my problem.  I was looking for something a little more innovative.  I guess that's the other reason I couldn't give it the last star.

I went to Eleven Madison Park for an office holiday lunch. It was around noon, and the place was fairly empty and quiet, which was nice. Lovely high-ceilinged atmosphere, lots of interesting fresh flower arrangements. The two-course prix fixe lunch was $28. Food was excellent, though portions were small and some members of our party left a bit hungry. The service was excellent, very formal and fancy, could even be off putting to some. 

For example, if you get up to use the restroom (floor length stall doors, cloth hand towels, fresh flowers) someone will come along and push your chair back in as you sit down. In can be a bit much (Wipers!!) if you're not used to it. Yet there was no snooty vibe at all, it was all very friendly in a professional way.

FYI, we did not get any amuse bouche or post dessert candies with the prix fixe lunch... it was appetizer and main only. I would give this place 5 stars but I am a pretty light eater and still would like to feel a little more full after a meal of that price... not Applebee's style cheese-and-preservatives full, just, you know, pleasantly full.  However, I imagine the dinner tasting menu would be much more satisfying and I would be happy to try it.

Yes, this is the restaurant where Mr. Big told Carrie he was engaged to Natasha. For those who care.

Since I am a devoted yelper, I hit up my favorite site to figure out a good 5 star restaurant for me and my parents to go to tonight. Eleven Madison Park was the only one that could accomadate us on such short notice but when we looked on the site, we were all pretty excited to try it out. The pictures of the food looked especially delicious, so why not try something new?

Honestly the food here was very good. But what we all agreed on and did not like about Eleven Madison Park was that it was so pretentious. There were so many waiters and waitresses walking around, hustling and bustling, we couldn't really enjoy dinner. They were so proper (ie fixing our forks when we moved them slightly, adjusting the position of our water to wine glasses) it just didn't make dinner relaxing or fun. I was somewhat surprised that it had so many positive reviews on yelp since I didn't feel the same way. Yelp has never led me wrong...why now?

They placed us on this round table right in front of the staircase with a station right behind us. So the traffic of servers was just...extremely hectic. They also lacked personality. Everyone was dressed so severely, in the same tie and suits, and we didn't seem to have a set waiter. Every time we needed something, it was a different guy in the same suit helping us. It was service but somewhat mechanical. 

I feel like the best restaurants are the ones that serve you discretely, so that you can enjoy the company of your friends and the food. Eleven Madison Park did not have this quality. Management should think about changing something to make the atmosphere seem less robotic and more friendly. I won't be back.
Had brunch here with a friend visiting from London. Lovely decor and brunch fare. Friend remembered the location to be one of the scenes from SATC and validated that with the waiter.

A truly religious experience between black-truffle poached lobster and yours truly. 

All the hype is true -- top-notch service, top location, wine, food, everything. Even the collection of the wine decanters displayed throughout the restaurant will blow your mind. 

Other reviewers are correct -- 3 course meal is plenty given all the additional courses you will be served. 

Additional tip -- the place has an awesome wine list with a lot of fantastic names you might not have heard of (there, I admit it -- I know some but not much about the wine! But I am Ok with it and so should you). Ask their somelier to do a custom pairing for your courses + maybe an extra for the opening course not listed on the menu. You're likely to discover something new for yourself.

The only course that was not extra-fabulous were little candies served after the official dessert. A couple of them were experimental and not in a good way -- the olive oil gelee tasted just like it sounds. Olive oil jello-type substance  dusted with sugar, meh. But hey, they were complimentary and designed to tease the taste.

You will have soooo much more food than you would have ever thought. Even though it says three courses, you get a lot more stuff -- the amuse-bouche, the sweetbreads, the candy thingies... the food just keeps coming and coming. I was way too stuffed afterward....

Very beautiful decor. However, the fact that my SO and I had to wait close to 20 minutes to being addressed by anyone after being seated left  a sour taste to begin with. Finally the sommelier approached us and asked if anyone had been to 'see us' yet-funny. We went on a cold winter night in Feb. for V. day/7th anniversary. Once we were served, we choose the 3 course menu which frankly were not very memorable. They dishes were executed well with smart presentation but the taste was rather 'meh'. The duck was succulent but I couldn't taste the lavender that everyone has been raving about....I have eaten at  a few fine dining establishments and this is one of the bombs unfortunately-seeing as I had high hopes to begin with, given the numerous recommendations I had received beforehand. I hope this was an off-night but as this place is pretty pricey not willing to go back to find out anytime soon!

Definitely the best dining experience in New York.  I've eaten here twice since Chef Humm came on board and both times were amazing.  The dishes are all executed expertly with a delicate touch, the service was impeccable, and while the decor is a tad cold, it was definitely beautiful.  Fresh flowers everywhere.

I highly highly recommend this restaurant.

Eleven Madison Park is my favorite restaurant in the city.  Daniel Humms cooking and the service in the front of the house combine to make this a truly special place.

I had lunch there this week and we ordered the Gourmand tasting menu - a good deal - $58 for 5 courses plus the amuse at the beginning and the mignardises at the end.  They were very accommodating about a substitution on the menu as one in our party did not eat pork or shellfish.  

The foie gras terrine with golden pineapple and rum raisin broiche was pilgrimage worthy.  So rich and decadent but not too sweet/sugary.  

The garden potatoes dish was also really good.  It came with smoked salmon draped over each potato, which were each different colors.  The presentations are visually beautiful in composition and plating.  Everything looks so good and then you taste it and it exceeds your expectation.

We had exceptional service, which was great.  I am a regular here, so they know me.  I hadn't been to the restaurant in eight months yet several staff welcomed me by name.  It is that kind of place.  Danny Meyer really knows service.  If I had to choose one fine dining restaurant in Manhattan to recommend this would be it.

this place screams "corporate dinner". i wasn't impressed by the food or the service. in fact, i was alittle disappointed. our waiter mixed up my parents dishes -- one filet was medium and the other was medium well. we constantly felt like we were being rushed. dishes were cleared away before we even had a chance to try. for instance the complimentary cheese puffs didn't stand a chance at being on the table for more than 5 minutes.

as for the food itself, nothing spectacular. i had the skate, which as another yelper pointed out, is a relatively inexpensive fish but served at this fine establishment for a pretty penny. i found the fish quite salty. my dad described it as an expensive filet-o-fish (yes that's right as in Mickey Ds).

if you're in the mood for a stuffy business affair then try this place otherwise only come here on a corporate card.

A truly exceptional dining experience that left me floating out of this place. 

Decor: wonderful high ceilings and columns, signature art deco style, lots of space, and beautiful bar. 

Service: Amazing. Everyone was so accommodating and ridiculously polite!

Food: EXQUISITE. In-(insert expletive)- credible!!! We went for my mom's birthday, and ordered the 3-course pre-fixe dinner starting at $88 a person. The pre-appetizers were an accurate preview of the meal that was to follow. All the little tiny pieces of art/food were pretty to look at, perfectly portioned to leave you wanting more, and a wonderful blend of unexpected flavors. Portions were small in general (ie. a proper serving size), but they gave us so many rounds of food that we were all suitably full - in a good way - at the end of the night. 

In my unglamourous lay-man way, let me describe what we ate:
1. Pre-appetizer: gorgeous little bites, and a small creamy thing with shrimp in it
2. Appetizers: Fall 08 menu - the crab meat wrapped in thin slices of avocado and tiny flower petals and a yogurt sauce was divine.. a wonderful blend of flavors. 
3. Main: I ordered the sucking pig dish with plum sauce.. and it was SO good. The black angus steak with swiss chard and oxtail was even better. 
4. Dessert - the chocolate custard with passionfruit and caramelized banana ice-cream was so delicious. 
5. Post-dessert: More little pretty bites

And the wine was great too. I know I'm not doing the food justice with my lame descriptions.. but lets just say that I've found a new favorite spot in the city. And even though they are owned by the same group, Gramercy Tavern ain't got nothing on this spot. My new #1.. too bad it's so bloody expensive.

The decor was beautiful with individual roses hanging from branches of red berries...they made the place so intimate with lots of candles burning everywhere and then finding out it used to be the private conference room to a big company.  We opted for the 11 course tasting menu and by the time the 6th course came, we were soooooooooooo full!!! Couldn't eat another bite but each dish was beautifully presented we just couldn't resist another bite of each upcoming dishes!! If you are ever in need of satisfying a hungry appetite u must get the 11 course tasting menu.  I can't wait to go back!

Service - check.
Top-notch food - check.
Excellent wine with a knowledgeable sommelier - check. 

What put it over the top? Three words: foie gras brulee.

It was really expensive, though.  I've been to top restaurants and done the tasting thing before, but rarely have I seen this.  While the experience was one I'm glad I had, and the food excellent and service amazing, I would choose Gramercy any day.  Same quality service and food, but better value (for the same price at Gramercy we could have gotten the wine pairings, too). Plus, Gramercy throws in a glass of champagne when it's our anniversary and we do the tasting menu.  None of that here, though it was our anniversary.

I had a thoroughly enjoyable meal with multiple highs. For a eleven course meal, I left feeling great, not too stuffed and by no means hungry. 

The amuse was great in that you had an assorted variety from simple to indulgent ( tar tar, fois, etc..). 

The dishes I remember were the fois and suckling pig dish. The fois dish was actually the best I've had in a long time, and that includes my meal at per se. The dish was balanced perfectly between sweet and salty. It also came in 2/3 variations (can't remember, a while ago), all equally delicious. 

It was overall a fantastic meal. The only negative things I can say about it is they seated us in the back room, which I believe is not as grand as the main dining room, and that there were long waits in between courses during peak times. But I guess that's forgivable given the right companions. 

I am definitely going back to get the duck. It looked absolutely amazing, served whole, with lavender sprigs shooting out its cavity.

We went here to celebrate a birthday and it was a wonderful experience.  We started off with two glasses of champagne and then ordered dinner.

The service was top notch.  Couldn't have asked for better.  The food was delicious.  We had the skate and steak.  Both dishes were wonderful but I kept on thinking I should have had the lobster instead.  Decided against because I was in Newport the weekend before and ate lobster everyday.

The presentation and quality was superb.  I was a little disappointed with dessert but overall the dinner was excellent.

Highly recommend coming here for a romantic evening with that special someone.

I love this place, Saturday was my 4th visit and every-time has been fantastic.  The staff was particularly great since my girlfriend and I were completely shit-faced for the entire meal and the staff handled us with complete grace and humor, at least as far as we can remember and we're pretty sure the food was good too.

I made had reservations for a friday night dinner and was taken to the table promptly upon arrival. What did it for me was the gorgeous decor (classy and modern) and fantastic service. I thought the food was just ok but the chocolate souffle dessert was really good. Overall it was good times and worth a try if you haven't been.

Service and ambiance/decoration are the winning points for this review.  I dined here for restaurant week and the service and ambiance left lasting impressions.  The decor is simple and clean but the flower arrangements were gorgeous.

Now to the food.  No complaints on the food.  I actually liked how they asked if we had allergies or if there were any foods we didn't like.  Everything was fresh and cooked just right.

I'm glad I checked this place out.  I guess I'd go back on a special occassion but not anytime soon.  There are too many other top notch restaurants in the city that I have to try.

Everything is just right at EMP. The service is fantastic, but still human and personal, not too stuffy. The food is amazing. The gnocchi was so light and fluffy, loup de mer was great, and the suckling pig was outstanding. You are going to spend a lot, so go for the four courses. You'll leave with a full stomach and very satisfied by everything that has touched your tongue in those 2+ hours. (The atmosphere is also terrific - such a beautiful space!)

I took my girlfriend here for dinner on her birthday. We each enjoyed the prix fix tasting menu and were delighted at the creativity and variety of textures and tastes. We enjoyed both unique ingredients as well as some of the more exotic preparations of traditional ingredients. It was an experience in fine dining that has yet to be matched. Service was attentive and friendly and were accommodating at finding a seat that was somewhat private. The décor felt impressive and felt like a bank more than a restaurant but somehow still managed to pull it off without feeling too cold. The other patrons unfortunately put us off, as we were a pretty young couple in a restaurant that seems frequented by "old money" (in fact, we got looks from other patrons making us feel a little out of place despite us being well dressed and mannered) Nevertheless it was a pleasurable dining experience and we definitely go here again.

the service is extremely friendly and attentive, but i had 2 issues--  
1) the prix fixe lunch is actually on a separate menu that was never given to us, but the price for it was given on the menu we had, leading us to believe we were ordering a prix fixe
2) after an appetizer and an entree, i was hungry again an hour later--and $70 lighter.
went to le cirque the next night and had a meal WORTH the money

I was in New York for business and brought my wife with me. She found the place as it was reviewed in the NY Times. At first I felt intimidated due to:

(1) The price
(2) They have a dress code
(3) The price...

I shouldn't have stressed as when we arrived the staff made every effort to make us feel comfortable and welcome. I am a sucker for good professional service. The wait staff was top notch. Our head server Megan was excellent and knew as much about the food being served as the chef. The Sommolier was patient and extremely helpful in navigating the huge wine list. You are given several choices on a prix-fixe menu. While the portions were fairly small I felt that the service and presentation was top notch and enjoyed the "show" so to speak. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is because I have only been there once so no additional data points. With regards to the price yes--it's a little expensive but well worth it.

Our one experience here was a mixed bag. In some ways excellent, even thrilling, but in some important ways a disappointment. There were two of us; we both ordered the two savory plus one dessert prix fixe, and didn't duplicate any orders. This gave us a total of 6 different dishes, plus a very generous assortment of amuse-type nibbles and surprises, and an extra dessert that came our way (possibly because the waiter knew we weren't thrilled with the restaurant's signature dish. But more on that later).

The meal started at its high point: a tray of gem-like hors d'ouvres, assembled with sushi-like precision, with a mix of local American, traditional French, and Japanese-inspired ingredients. All these single-bite creations were perfectly crafted to melt in your mouth in just the right order (even if they weren't always designed to be picked up without disintegrating). They included perfect cubes of foie gras on on cracker-like pastry, a sushi-like roll of hamachi and bell pepper brunoise wrapped in daikon radish, puff pastry cones filled with rabbit, and at least a couple of others that I've forgotton.

If the meal had been able to sustain this level of surprise and perfection throughout the courses that we ordered, it would have been mindblowing. Unfortunately, the chef tried to sustain the techniques and esthetics that worked so well for the amuses, without continuing to address the issues of how to make a dish inviting and easy to eat. 

We felt that the gem-like, sushi style just didn't work as well for the large plates. This was most evident with the restaurant's most celebrated dish, the suckling pig. In keeping with the chef's esthetic, there was no indication that you were eating a pig, suckling or otherwise. The presentation was a perfectly geometric rectangle of shredded meat, covered on top with a perfectly cut, crispy piece of skin. The sauce was a smear off to the side. The sauce was a work of perfection--perfectly clear, intensely flavored, balanced. But there was too little of it to moisten the meat, and the meat needed a fair amount of sauce. 

Part of our gripe was a stylistic one. We both felt that this style, which works for a sushi piece or an amuse, is misplaced with a suckling pig, where we want to enjoy sights, forms, and textures of the meat itself--not the unsurprising geometric contrivances of the chef. Part of it was a practical one--the food was neither particularly inviting nor easy to eat. We needed more sauce, we needed the meat evenly moistened in it, and it was difficult to make this happen. But the biggest part of our gripe was about execution, and this led us to assume we were there on an off night. The pork was just overcooked. It was dry, and while the flavor was intense it was also one dimensional. When I read Frank Bruni's gushing review of this dish, I didn't recognize anything in his description besides the name and the shape. I was stunned to learn that the pork had been poached in duck fat. How the hell do dry out heritage pork and get dimensionless flavor when you poach it in duck fat? 

Anyway, enough griping. The rest of our dishes fell between the extremes. The arctic char was adequate, but less flavorful that examples of this fish that I've had at much cheaper restaurants (or that I've made myself). The appetizers were better. The sockeye tuna appetizer was interesting and featured excellent fish, although the dish as a whole seemed to lack focus and wasn't especially memorable. The la ratte potato gnocchi was excellent.

The desserts were uniformly great. They maintained the same geometric / constructed / precious esthetic of the rest of the meal, but thanks in part to their small size, they worked. The flavors were vibrant and fresh, the sorbets were perfectly made, and all of it was fun to eat. We left full but not stuffed.
